children.text: yatpadāmbhoruhadhyānavidhvastāśeṣakalmaṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the meditation upon whose lotus feet all sins are completely destroyed,

children.text: vastutām upayāto 'haṃ yāmuneyaṃ namāmi tam //
children.translated_text: I, who have attained true being, bow to that son of <s>Yāmunā</s> (<s>Yāmuneyam</s>). ||

children.text: yat-pada-ambhoruha-dhyāna-vidhvasta-aśeṣa-kalmaṣaḥ /
vastutām upayāto 'haṃ yāmuneyaṃ namāmi tam //

body.text:
śriyaḥ patiḥ, nikhilaheyapratyanīkakalyāṇaikatānaḥ, svetarasamastavastuvilakṣaṇānantajñanānandaikasvarūpaḥ, svābhāvikānavadhikātiśayajñānabalāiśvaryavīryaśaktitejaḥprabhṛtyasaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇamahodadhiḥ, svābhimatānurūpaikarūpācintyadivyādbhutanityaniravadyaniratiśayāujjvalyasaundaryasaugandhyasaukumāryalāvaṇyayauvanādyanantaguṇanidhidivyarūpaḥ, svocitavividhavicitrānantāścaryanityaniravadyāparimitadivyabhūṣaṇaḥ, svānurūpāsaṃkhyeyācintyaśaktinityaniravadyaniratiśayakalyāṇadivyāyudhaḥ, svābhimatānurūpanityaniravadyasvarūparūpaguṇavibhavāiśvaryaśīlādyanavadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇaśrīvallabhaḥ,
svasaṅkalpānuvidhāyisvarūpasthitipravṛttibhedāśeṣaseṣataikaratirūpanityaniravadyaniratiśayajñānakriyāiśvaryādyanantaguṇagaṇāparimitasūribhir anavaratābhiṣṭutacaraṇayugalaḥ, vāṅmanasāparicchedyasvarūpasvabhāvaḥ svocitavividhavicitrānantabhogyabhogopakaraṇabhogasthānasamṛddhānantāścaryānantamahāvibhavānantaparimāṇanityaniravadyākṣaraparamavyomanilayaḥ, vividhavicitrānantabhogyabhoktṛvargaparipūrṇanikhilajagadudayavibhavalayalīlaḥ, paraṃ brahma puruṣottamo nārāyaṇaḥ, brahmādisthāvarāntam akhilaṃ jagat sṛṣṭvā ,svena rūpeṇāvasthito brahmādidevamanuṣyāṇāṃ dhyānārādhanādyagocaraḥ, apārakāruṇyasauśīlyavātsalyāudāryamahodadhiḥ, svam eva rūpaṃ tat tat sajātīyasaṃsthānaṃ svasvabhāvam
ajahad eva kurvan teṣu teṣu lokeṣv avatīryāvatīrya tais tair ārādhitas tat tad iṣṭānurūpaṃ dharmārthakāmamokṣākhyaṃ phalaṃ prayacchan, bhūbhārāvatāraṇāpadeśenāsmadādīnām api samāśrayaṇīyatvāyāvatīryorvyāṃ sakalamanujanayanaviṣayatāṃ gataḥ, parāvaranikhilajanamanonayanahāridivyaceṣṭitāni kurvan, pūtanāśakaṭayamalārjunāriṣṭapralambadhenukakāliyakeśikuvalayāpīḍacāṇūramuṣṭikatosalakaṃsādīn nihatya anavadhikadayāsauhārdānurāgagarbhāvalokanālāpāmṛtair viśvam āpyāyayan, niratiśayasaundaryasauśīlyādiguṇagaṇāviṣkāreṇākrūramālākārādīn paramabhāgavatān kṛtvā, pāṇḍutanayayuddhaprotsāhanavyājena paramapuruṣārthalakṣaṇamokṣasādhanatayā vedāntoditaṃ svaviṣayaṃ
jñānakarmānugṛhītaṃ bhaktiyogam avatārayām āsa / tatra pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca yuddhe prārabdhe sa bhagavān puruṣottamaḥ sarveśvareśvaro jagadupakṛtimartyaḥ āśritavātsalyavivaśaḥ pārthaṃ rathinam ātmānaṃ ca sārathiṃ sarvalokasākṣikaṃ cakāra /
body.translated_text:
The Lord of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Śriyaḥ patiḥ</s>), whose sole tenor is auspiciousness that is the counter-opposite of everything deficient, whose unique essential nature is infinite knowledge and bliss that is utterly distinct from all other entities, who is a great ocean of innumerable auspicious qualities beginning with knowledge, strength, sovereignty, valor, power, and splendor — all natural, unsurpassable, and supreme — whose divine form is a treasure-house of infinite qualities such as inconceivable, divine, wonderful, eternal, flawless, unsurpassable brilliance, beauty, fragrance, tenderness, loveliness, and youth, each of a single form suited to His own desire, who possesses infinitely varied, wonderful, eternal, flawless, immeasurable divine ornaments befitting Him, who possesses innumerable, inconceivably powerful, eternal, flawless, unsurpassable, auspicious divine weapons suited to His nature, who is the beloved of <s>Śrī</s> who possesses innumerable auspicious qualities such as eternal, flawless essential nature, form, qualities, glory, sovereignty, and virtuous character, all unsurpassable and suited to His own desire,
whose twin feet are unceasingly praised by unlimited <s>Sūris</s> (eternally liberated souls) who possess infinite multitudes of qualities such as eternal, flawless, unsurpassable knowledge, activity, and sovereignty, all having the form of sole delight in complete servitude, whose essential nature, form, condition, and activity all conform to His will, whose essential nature and character are beyond the grasp of speech and mind, who abides in the supreme, eternal, flawless, imperishable highest heaven (<s>paramavyoman</s>), replete with infinitely varied, wonderful, infinite objects of enjoyment, instruments of enjoyment, and places of enjoyment, all befitting Him, of infinite, wondrous, infinite great glory and infinite measure, whose sport (<s>līlā</s>) is the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the entire universe filled with infinitely varied classes of enjoyers and objects of enjoyment — this Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, having created the entire universe from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the immovable [beings], established in His own form, being beyond the reach of meditation, worship, and the like of gods from <s>Brahmā</s> downward and of humans, being a great ocean of boundless compassion, graciousness, parental affection, and magnanimity, making His own form take configurations belonging to each respective species while never abandoning His own essential nature,
descending again and again into those various worlds, being worshipped by those [beings] in various ways, granting the fruit called <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> suited to each desired [goal], descended to earth — under the pretext of relieving the earth's burden — so as to become a refuge for us as well, entering the range of vision of all human beings, performing divine deeds that captivate the minds and eyes of all people, high and low, having slain <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Śakaṭa</s>, <s>Yamala-Arjuna</s>, <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, <s>Pralamba</s>, <s>Dhenuka</s>, <s>Kāliya</s>, <s>Keśin</s>, <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>, <s>Cāṇūra</s>, <s>Muṣṭika</s>, <s>Tosala</s>, <s>Kaṃsa</s>, and others, nourishing the entire world with the nectar of glances, speech, and address imbued with boundless compassion, friendship, and love, having made <s>Akrūra</s>, <s>Mālākāra</s>, and others into supreme devotees (<s>paramabhāgavata</s>) through the revelation of His multitude of qualities such as unsurpassable beauty, graciousness, and the like, brought down (<s>avatārayām āsa</s>) — under the pretext of encouraging the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> in battle — <s>Bhaktiyoga</s>, which is taught in the <s>Vedānta</s>, has Himself as its object, is assisted by knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) and action (<s>karma</s>), and is the means of attaining the supreme human goal (<s>paramapuruṣārtha</s>) characterized as liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). | Therein, when the battle between the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> and the <s>Kurus</s> had commenced, that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), the Lord of all lords, who had assumed mortal form for the benefit of the world, overpowered by affection for those who take refuge in Him, made <s>Pārtha</s> (Arjuna) the chariot-warrior and Himself the charioteer, with all the worlds as witnesses. |

children.text:
śriyaḥ patiḥ, nikhila-heya-pratyanīka-kalyāṇa-ekatānaḥ, sva-itara-samasta-vastu-vilakṣaṇa-ananta-jñana-ānanda-eka-sva-rūpaḥ, svābhāvika-anavadhika-atiśaya-jñāna-bala-aiśvarya-vīrya-śakti-tejaḥ-prabhṛty-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-mahā-udadhiḥ, sva-abhimata-anurūpa-eka-rūpa-acintya-divya-adbhuta-nitya-niravadya-niratiśaya-aujjvalya-saundarya-saugandhya-saukumārya-lāvaṇya-yauvana-ādy-ananta-guṇa-nidhi-divya-rūpaḥ, sva-ucita-vividha-vicitra-ananta-āścarya-nitya-niravadya-aparimita-divya-bhūṣaṇaḥ, sva-anurūpa-asaṃkhyeya-acintya-śakti-nitya-niravadya-niratiśaya-kalyāṇa-divya-āyudhaḥ, sva-abhimata-anurūpa-nitya-niravadya-sva-rūpa-rūpa-guṇa-vibhava-aiśvarya-śīla-ādy-anavadhika-atiśaya-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-śrī-vallabhaḥ,
sva-saṅkalpa-anuvidhāyi-sva-rūpa-sthiti-pravṛtti-bheda-aśeṣa-seṣatā-eka-rati-rūpa-nitya-niravadya-niratiśaya-jñāna-kriyā-aiśvarya-ādy-ananta-guṇa-gaṇa-aparimita-sūribhir anavarata-abhiṣṭuta-caraṇa-yugalaḥ, vāṅ-manasā-aparicchedya-sva-rūpa-sva-bhāvaḥ sva-ucita-vividha-vicitra-ananta-bhogya-bhoga-upakaraṇa-bhoga-sthāna-samṛddha-ananta-āścarya-ananta-mahā-vibhava-ananta-parimāṇa-nitya-niravadya-akṣara-parama-vyoma-nilayaḥ, vividha-vicitra-ananta-bhogya-bhoktṛ-varga-paripūrṇa-nikhila-jagad-udaya-vibhava-laya-līlaḥ, paraṃ brahma puruṣa-uttamo nārāyaṇaḥ, brahmā-ādi-sthāvara-antam akhilaṃ jagat sṛṣṭvā ,svena rūpeṇa avasthito brahmā-ādi-deva-manuṣyāṇāṃ dhyāna-ārādhana-ādy-agocaraḥ, apāra-kāruṇya-sauśīlya-vātsalya-audārya-mahā-udadhiḥ, svam eva rūpaṃ tat tat sajātīya-saṃsthānaṃ sva-sva-bhāvam
ajahad eva kurvan teṣu teṣu lokeṣv avatīrya avatīrya tais tair ārādhitas tat tad iṣṭa-anurūpaṃ dharma-artha-kāma-mokṣa-ākhyaṃ phalaṃ prayacchan, bhū-bhāra-avatāraṇa-apadeśena asmad-ādīnām api samāśrayaṇīyatvāya avatīrya urvyāṃ sakala-manuja-nayana-viṣayatāṃ gataḥ, para-avara-nikhila-jana-mano-nayana-hāri-divya-ceṣṭitāni kurvan, pūtanā-śakaṭa-yamala-arjuna-ariṣṭa-pralamba-dhenuka-kāliya-keśi-kuvalaya-āpīḍa-cāṇūra-muṣṭika-tosala-kaṃsa-ādīn nihatya anavadhika-dayā-sauhārda-anurāga-garbha-avalokana-ālāpa-amṛtair viśvam āpyāyayan, niratiśaya-saundarya-sauśīlya-ādi-guṇa-gaṇa-āviṣkāreṇa akrūra-mālā-kāra-ādīn parama-bhāgavatān kṛtvā, pāṇḍu-tanaya-yuddha-protsāhana-vyājena parama-puruṣa-artha-lakṣaṇa-mokṣa-sādhanatayā vedānta-uditaṃ sva-viṣayaṃ
jñāna-karma-anugṛhītaṃ bhakti-yogam avatārayām āsa / tatra pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca yuddhe prārabdhe sa bhagavān puruṣa-uttamaḥ sarva-īśvara-īśvaro jagad-upakṛti-martyaḥ āśrita-vātsalya-vivaśaḥ pārthaṃ rathinam ātmānaṃ ca sārathiṃ sarva-loka-sākṣikaṃ cakāra /
dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ |
children.translated_text: On the field of <s>Dharma</s>, at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, assembled and eager to fight,

children.text: māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva kim akurvata sañjaya ||
children.translated_text: what did my [people] and the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> do, O <s>Sañjaya</s>? ||

children.text: dharma-kṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ |
māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāś ca eva kim akurvata sañjaya ||

body.text: evaṃ jñātvāpi sarvātmanāndho dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ suyodhanavijayabubhutsayā sañjayaṃ papraccha /
body.translated_text: Thus, though knowing [all this], <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, blind in every way, out of desire to hear of <s>Suyodhana</s>'s victory, questioned <s>Sañjaya</s>. |

children.text: evaṃ jñātva āpi sarva-ātmana āndho dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ suyodhana-vijaya-bubhutsayā sañjayaṃ papraccha /
dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanas tadā |
children.translated_text: But seeing the army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> arrayed in formation, <s>Duryodhana</s> then,

children.text: ācāryam upasaṃgamya rājā vacanam abravīt ||
children.translated_text: approaching the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), the king spoke these words: ||

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanas tadā |
ācāryam upasaṃgamya rājā vacanam abravīt ||
paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇām ācārya mahatīṃ camūm |
children.translated_text: Behold this great army of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, O teacher,

children.text: vyūḍhāṃ drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: arrayed by the son of <s>Drupada</s>, your intelligent disciple! ||

children.text: paśya etāṃ pāṇḍu-putrāṇām ācārya mahatīṃ camūm |
vyūḍhāṃ drupada-putreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā ||
atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi |
children.translated_text: Here [are] heroes, great archers, equal to <s>Bhīma</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> in battle:

children.text: yuyudhāno virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca mahārathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yuyudhāna</s>, <s>Virāṭa</s>, and <s>Drupada</s>, the great chariot-warrior; ||

children.text: atra śūrā mahā-īṣvāsā bhīma-arjuna-samā yudhi |
yuyudhāno virāṭaś ca drupadaś ca mahā-rathaḥ ||
dhṛṣṭaketuś cekitānaḥ kāśīrājaś ca vīryavān |
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, <s>Cekitāna</s>, and the valiant king of <s>Kāśī</s>;

children.text: purujitkuntibhojaś ca śaibyaś ca narapuṅgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Purujit</s>, <s>Kuntibhoja</s>, and <s>Śaibya</s>, bull among men; ||

children.text: dhṛṣṭaketuś cekitānaḥ kāśī-rājaś ca vīryavān |
puru-jit-kunti-bhojaś ca śaibyaś ca nara-puṅ-gavaḥ ||
yudhāmanyuś ca vikrānta uttamaujāś ca vīryavān |
children.translated_text: the mighty <s>Yudhāmanyu</s> and the valiant <s>Uttamauja</s>;

children.text: saubhadro draupadeyāś ca sarva eva mahārathāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Subhadrā</s> and the sons of <s>Draupadī</s> — all indeed great chariot-warriors. ||

children.text: yudhāmanyuś ca vikrānta uttama-ojāś ca vīryavān |
saubhadro draupadeyāś ca sarva eva mahā-rathāḥ ||
asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tān nibodha dvijottama |
children.translated_text: But know those who are distinguished among our [side], O best of the twice-born;

children.text: nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tān bravīmi te ||
children.translated_text: the leaders of my army — I name them to you for identification: ||

children.text: asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tān nibodha dvi-ja-uttama |
nāyakā mama sainyasya saṃjñā-arthaṃ tān bravīmi te ||
bhavān bhīṣmaś ca karṇaś ca kṛpaś ca samitiñjayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Your good self, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, and <s>Kṛpa</s>, ever victorious in battle;

children.text: aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca saumadattis tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvatthāmā</s>, <s>Vikarṇa</s>, and <s>Saumadatti</s> likewise; ||

children.text: bhavān bhīṣmaś ca karṇaś ca kṛpaś ca samitiñ-jayaḥ |
aśvatthāmā vikarṇaś ca saumadattis tatha aiva ca ||
anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: and many other heroes who have given up their lives for my sake,

children.text: nānāśastrapraharaṇās sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ ||
children.translated_text: wielding various weapons and missiles, all skilled in warfare. ||

children.text: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā mad-arthe tyakta-jīvitāḥ |
nānā-śastra-praharaṇās sarve yuddha-viśāra-dāḥ ||
aparyāptaṃ tad asmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam |
children.translated_text: Insufficient is that army of ours, protected by <s>Bhīṣma</s>;

children.text: paryāptaṃ tv idam eteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: but sufficient is this army of theirs, protected by <s>Bhīma</s>. ||

children.text: aparyāptaṃ tad asmākaṃ balaṃ bhīṣma-abhirakṣitam |
paryāptaṃ tv idam eteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīma-abhirakṣitam ||
ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgam avasthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, stationed in your respective positions at all the access-points,

children.text: bhīṣmam evābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi ||
children.translated_text: protect <s>Bhīṣma</s> in particular — all of you indeed! ||

children.text: ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathā-bhāgam avasthitāḥ |
bhīṣmam eva abhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi ||

body.text: duryodhanaḥ svayam eva bhīmābhirakṣitaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ balam, ātmīyaṃ ca bhīṣmābhirakṣitaṃ balam avalokya, ātmavijaye tasya balasya paryāptatām ātmīyasya balasya tadvijaye cāparyāptatām ācāryāya nivedya antarviṣaṇṇo 'bhavat //
body.translated_text: <s>Duryodhana</s> himself, surveying the army of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> protected by <s>Bhīma</s> and his own army protected by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, reporting to the teacher the sufficiency of that [enemy] army for defeating his own, and the insufficiency of his own army for defeating them, became inwardly dejected. ||

children.text: duryodhanaḥ svayam eva bhīma-abhirakṣitaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ balam, ātmīyaṃ ca bhīṣma-abhirakṣitaṃ balam avalokya, ātma-vijaye tasya balasya paryāptatām ātmīyasya balasya tad-vijaye ca aparyāptatām ācāryāya nivedya antarviṣaṇṇo 'bhavat //
tasya saṃjanayan harṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, generating joy in him, the elder of the <s>Kurus</s>, the grandsire,

children.text: siṃhanādaṃ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān ||
children.translated_text: roaring a lion's roar loudly, blew his conch — the valiant one. ||

children.text: tasya saṃjanayan harṣaṃ kuru-vṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ |
siṃha-nādaṃ vinadya uccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān ||
tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then conches, kettledrums, tabors, drums, and cow-horns

children.text: sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: were suddenly struck all together, and that sound was tumultuous. ||

children.text: tataḥ śaṅkhāś ca bheryaś ca paṇava-ānaka-go-mukhāḥ |
sahasa aiva abhyahanyanta sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat ||
tataḥ śvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau |
children.translated_text: Then, standing upon a great chariot yoked with white horses,

children.text: mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaś caiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s> and <s>Pāṇḍava</s> too blew their divine conches. ||

children.text: tataḥ śvetair hayair yukte mahati syandane sthitau |
mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaś ca eva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ ||
pāñcajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanañjayaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> [blew] <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, <s>Dhanañjaya</s> [blew] <s>Devadatta</s>;

children.text: pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛkodara</s> of terrible deeds blew the great conch <s>Pauṇḍra</s>; ||

children.text: pāñca-janyaṃ hṛṣī-keśo deva-dattaṃ dhanañjayaḥ |
pauṇḍraṃ dadhmau mahā-śaṅkhaṃ bhīma-karmā vṛka-udaraḥ ||
anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ |
children.translated_text: King <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, son of <s>Kuntī</s>, [blew] <s>Anantavijaya</s>;

children.text: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s> [blew] <s>Sughoṣa</s> and <s>Maṇipuṣpaka</s>. ||

children.text: ananta-vijayaṃ rājā kuntī-putro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ |
nakulaḥ saha-devaś ca sughoṣa-maṇi-puṣpakau ||
kāśyaś ca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ |
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Kāśī</s>, the supreme archer, and <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, the great chariot-warrior,

children.text: dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaś ca sātyakiś cāparājitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, <s>Virāṭa</s>, and the unconquered <s>Sātyaki</s>, ||

children.text: kāśyaś ca parama-īṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahā-rathaḥ |
dhṛṣṭa-dyumno virāṭaś ca sātyakiś ca aparā-jitaḥ ||
drupado draupadeyāś ca sarvataḥ pṛthivīpate |
children.translated_text: <s>Drupada</s> and the sons of <s>Draupadī</s>, on all sides, O lord of the earth,

children.text: saubhadraś ca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuḥ pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and the mighty-armed son of <s>Subhadrā</s> — [they] blew their conches, each separately. ||

children.text: drupado draupadeyāś ca sarvataḥ pṛthivī-pate |
saubhadraś ca mahā-bāhuḥ śaṅkhān dadhmuḥ pṛthak pṛthak ||

body.text: tasya viṣādam ālakṣya bhīṣmas tasya harṣaṃ janayituṃ siṃhanādaṃ śaṅkhadhmānaṃ ca kṛtvā, śaṅkhabherīninādaiś ca vijayābhiśaṃsinaṃ ghoṣaṃ cākārayat // tataḥ -- taṃ ghoṣam ākarṇya sarveśvareśvaraḥ pārthasārathī rathī ca pāṇḍutanayas trailokyavijayopakaraṇabhūte mahati syandane sthitau
body.translated_text: Observing his (<s>Duryodhana</s>'s) despondency, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, in order to generate joy in him, performed a lion's roar and blew his conch, and caused a resounding sound with conch-blasts and kettledrum-sounds that announced victory. || Then — hearing that sound, the Lord of all lords, the charioteer of <s>Pārtha</s>, and the chariot-warrior, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, standing upon the great chariot that was the instrument of the conquest of the three worlds —

children.text: tasya viṣādam ālakṣya bhīṣmas tasya harṣaṃ janayituṃ siṃha-nādaṃ śaṅkha-dhmānaṃ ca kṛtvā, śaṅkha-bherī-ninādaiś ca vijaya-abhiśaṃsinaṃ ghoṣaṃ ca akārayat // tataḥ --- taṃ ghoṣam ākarṇya sarva-īśvara-īśvaraḥ pārtha-sārathī rathī ca pāṇḍu-tanayas trailokya-vijaya-upakaraṇa-bhūte mahati syandane sthitau
sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat |
children.translated_text: that tumultuous sound shattered the hearts of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>'s sons,

children.text: nabhaś ca pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo 'py anunādayan ||
children.translated_text: reverberating through heaven and earth alike. ||

children.text: sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat |
nabhaś ca pṛthivīṃ ca eva tumulo 'py anunādayan ||
atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapidhvajaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> drawn up in formation, [<s>Arjuna</s>] whose banner bore the monkey,

children.text: pravṛtte śastrasaṃpāte dhanur udyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the clash of weapons commenced, raising his bow, the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>,

children.text: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrān kapi-dhvajaḥ |
pravṛtte śastra-saṃpāte dhanur udyamya pāṇḍavaḥ ||
hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyam idam āha mahīpate |
children.translated_text: spoke these words to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> then, O lord of the earth:

children.text: senayor ubhayor madhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me 'cyuta ||
children.translated_text: Station my chariot between the two armies, O <s>Acyuta</s>! ||

children.text: hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyam idam āha mahīpate |
senayor ubhayor madhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me 'cyuta ||

body.text: trailokyaṃ kampayantau śrīmatpāñcajanyadevadattau divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ //
body.translated_text: — [they] blew their two divine conches, the glorious <s>Pāñcajanya</s> and <s>Devadatta</s>, making the three worlds tremble. ||

children.text: trailokyaṃ kampayantau śrīmat-pāñcajanya-deva-dattau divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ //

body.text: tato yudhiṣṭhiro vṛkodarādayaś ca svakīyān śaṅkhān pṛthak pṛthak pradadhmuḥ / sa ghoṣo duryodhanapramukhānāṃ sarveṣām eva bhavatputrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni bibheda / "adyaiva naṣṭaṃ kurūṇāṃ balam" iti dhārtarāṣṭrā menire / evaṃ tadvijayābhikāṅkṣiṇe dhṛtarāṣṭrāya sañjayo 'kathayat //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, <s>Vṛkodara</s>, and the others blew their respective conches, each separately. | That sound shattered the hearts of all your sons, led by <s>Duryodhana</s>. | 'This very day the army of the <s>Kurus</s> is destroyed!' — so the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> thought. | Thus <s>Sañjaya</s> narrated to <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, who was eager for their victory. ||

children.text: tato yudhiṣṭhiro vṛka-udara-ādayaś ca svakīyān śaṅkhān pṛthak pṛthak pradadhmuḥ / sa ghoṣo duryodhana-pramukhānāṃ sarveṣām eva bhavat-putrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni bibheda / "adya eva naṣṭaṃ kurūṇāṃ balam" iti dhārtarāṣṭrā menire / evaṃ tad-vijaya-abhikāṅkṣiṇe dhṛtarāṣṭrāya sañjayo 'kathayat //

body.text: atha yuyutsūn avasthitān dhārtarāṣṭrān dṛṣṭvā laṅkādahanavānaradhvajaḥ pāṇḍutanayo
body.translated_text: Then, seeing the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> arrayed and eager for battle, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, whose banner bore the monkey that burnt <s>Laṅkā</s> —

children.text: atha yuyutsūn avasthitān dhārtarāṣṭrān dṛṣṭvā laṅkā-dahana-vānara-dhvajaḥ pāṇḍu-tanayo
yāvad etān nirīkṣe 'haṃ yoddhukāmān avasthitān |
children.translated_text: While I survey these [warriors], standing eager to fight,

children.text: kair mayā saha yoddhavyam asmin raṇasamudyame ||
children.translated_text: with whom I must fight in this onset of battle, ||

children.text: yāvad etān nirīkṣe 'haṃ yoddhu-kāmān avasthitān |
kair mayā saha yoddhavyam asmin raṇa-samudyame ||
yotsyamānān avekṣe 'haṃ ya ete 'tra samāgatāḥ |
children.translated_text: let me behold those who are about to fight, who have gathered here,

children.text: dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddher yuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: wishing to please the evil-minded <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> in battle. ||

children.text: yotsyamānān avekṣe 'haṃ ya ete 'tra samāgatāḥ |
dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddher yuddhe priya-cikīrṣavaḥ ||
evam ukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata |
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Guḍākeśa</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, O <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: senayor ubhayor madhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam ||
children.translated_text: having stationed the finest chariot between the two armies, ||

children.text: evam ukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata |
senayor ubhayor madhye sthāpayitvā ratha-uttamam ||
bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām |
children.translated_text: in front of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and all the rulers of the earth,

children.text: uvāca pārtha paśyaitān samavetān kurūn iti ||
children.translated_text: said: 'Behold, O <s>Pārtha</s>, these <s>Kurus</s> assembled here.' ||

children.text: bhīṣma-droṇa-pramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām |
uvāca pārtha paśya etān samavetān kurūn iti ||
tatrāpaśyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitQn atha pitāmahān |
children.translated_text: There <s>Pārtha</s> saw, standing [in formation], fathers and grandfathers,

children.text: tatra apaśyat sthitān pārthaḥ pitQn atha pitāmahān |

body.text: jñānaśaktibalāiśvaryavīryatejasāṃ nidhiṃ svasaṅkalpakṛtajagadudayavibhavalayalīlaṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ parāvaranikhilajanāntarabāhyakaraṇānāṃ sarvaprakāraniyamane 'vasthitam āśritavātsalyavivaśatayā svasārathye 'vasthitam, "yuyutsūn yathāvad avekṣituṃ tad īkṣanakṣame sthāne rathaṃ sthāpaya" ity acodayat //
body.translated_text: — [He,] <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, the treasure-house of knowledge, power, strength, sovereignty, valor, and splendor, whose sport is the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the universe accomplished by His own will, who is established in the complete regulation, in every manner, of the inner and outer organs of all beings, high and low — [yet] who, overpowered by parental affection for those who take refuge [in Him], was stationed as His own charioteer — [<s>Arjuna</s>] urged Him: 'Station the chariot in a place fit for viewing, so that I may properly survey those who are eager to fight.' ||

children.text: jñāna-śakti-bala-aiśvarya-vīrya-tejasāṃ nidhiṃ sva-saṅkalpa-kṛta-jagad-udaya-vibhava-laya-līlaṃ hṛṣīkeśaṃ para-avara-nikhila-jana-antara-bāhya-karaṇānāṃ sarva-prakāra-niyamane 'vasthitam āśrita-vātsalya-vivaśatayā sva-sārathye 'vasthitam, "yuyutsūn yathāvad avekṣituṃ tad īkṣana-kṣame sthāne rathaṃ sthāpaya" ity acodayat //
ācāryān mātulān bhrātQn putrān pautrān sakhīṃs tathā ||
children.translated_text: teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends likewise, ||

children.text: ācāryān mātulān bhrātQn putrān pautrān sakhīṃs tathā ||
śvaśurān suhṛdaś caiva senayor ubhayor api |
children.translated_text: fathers-in-law and well-wishers too, in both armies.

children.text: tān samīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūn avasthitān ||
children.translated_text: Surveying them, that son of <s>Kuntī</s>, all his kinsmen arrayed [for battle], ||

children.text: śvaśurān suhṛdaś ca eva senayor ubhayor api |
tān samīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūn avasthitān ||
kṛpayā parayāviṣṭo viṣīdann idam abravīt |
children.translated_text: overcome with profound compassion, despairing, spoke thus:

children.text: dṛṣṭvemaṃ svajanaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this my own people, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, eager to fight, standing before me, ||

children.text: kṛpayā parayā āviṣṭo viṣīdann idam abravīt |
dṛṣṭva īmaṃ sva-janaṃ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṃ samupasthitam ||
sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati |
children.translated_text: my limbs sink, and my mouth dries up,

children.text: vepathuś ca śarīre me romaharṣaś ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: trembling seizes my body, and my hair stands on end. ||

children.text: sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati |
vepathuś ca śarīre me roma-harṣaś ca jāyate ||
gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāt tvak caiva paridahyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Gāṇḍīva</s> slips from my hand, and my skin burns all over;

children.text: na ca śaknomy avasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am unable to stand, and my mind seems to reel. ||

children.text: gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate hastāt tvak ca eva paridahyate |
na ca śaknomy avasthātuṃ bhramati iva ca me manaḥ ||
nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava |
children.translated_text: And I see adverse omens, O <s>Keśava</s>;

children.text: na ca śreyo 'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanam āhave ||
children.translated_text: nor do I foresee any good from slaying my own people in battle. ||

children.text: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava |
na ca śreyo 'nupaśyāmi hatvā sva-janam āhave ||
na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ Kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca |
children.translated_text: I desire not victory, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, nor kingdom, nor pleasures.

children.text: kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogair jīvitena vā ||
children.translated_text: Of what use is kingdom to us, O <s>Govinda</s>, of what use are enjoyments or even life? ||

children.text: na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ Kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca |
kiṃ no rājyena govinda kiṃ bhogair jīvitena vā ||
yeṣām arthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca |
children.translated_text: Those for whose sake we desired kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures —

children.text: ta ime 'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃs tyaktvā dhanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: they stand here in battle, having abandoned their lives and wealth: ||

children.text: yeṣām arthe kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca |
ta ime 'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃs tyaktvā dhanāni ca ||
ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrās tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ |
children.translated_text: teachers, fathers, sons, and grandfathers likewise,

children.text: mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ syālāḥ saṃbandhinas tathā ||
children.translated_text: maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives. ||

children.text: ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrās tatha aiva ca pitāmahāḥ |
mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ syālāḥ saṃbandhinas tathā ||

body.text: sa ca tena coditas tatkṣaṇād eva Bhīṣmaḍroṇādīnāṃ sarveṣām eva mahīkṣitāṃ paśyatāṃ yathācoditam akarot / īdṛśī bhavadīyānāṃ vijayasthitir iti cāvocat //
body.translated_text: And he [<s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>], thus urged by him [<s>Arjuna</s>], immediately did as instructed, in full view of <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and all the rulers of the earth. || And he said: 'Such is the state of affairs regarding the victory of your [enemies]!' ||

children.text: sa ca tena coditas tat-kṣaṇād eva Bhīṣma-ḍroṇa-ādīnāṃ sarveṣām eva mahīkṣitāṃ paśyatāṃ yathā-coditam akarot / īdṛśī bhavadīyānāṃ vijaya-sthitir iti ca avocat //

body.text: sa tu Pārtho mahāmanāḥ paramakāruṇiko dīrghabandhuḥ paramadhārmikaḥ sabhrātṛko
body.translated_text: But that <s>Pārtha</s>, noble-minded, supremely compassionate, a long-standing kinsman, supremely righteous, together with his brothers —

children.text: sa tu Pārtho mahā-manāḥ parama-kāruṇiko dīrgha-bandhuḥ parama-dhārmikaḥ sabhrātṛko
etān na hantum icchāmi ghnato 'pi madhusūdhana |
children.translated_text: I do not wish to slay these, even though they slay [me], O <s>Madhusūdana</s>,

children.text: api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahīkṛte ||
children.translated_text: even for the sovereignty of the three worlds — how much less for the sake of the earth! ||

children.text: etān na hantum icchāmi ghnato 'pi madhu-sūdhana |
api trailokya-rājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ nu mahī-kṛte ||
nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana |
children.translated_text: Having slain the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, what joy would be ours, O <s>Janārdana</s>?

children.text: pāpam evāśrayed asmān hatvaitān ātatāyinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Sin alone would attach to us from slaying these aggressors. ||

children.text: nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrān naḥ kā prītiḥ syāj janārdana |
pāpam evā aśrayed asmān hatva aitān ātatāyinaḥ ||
tasmān nārhā vayaṃ hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrān sabāndhavān |
children.translated_text: Therefore we ought not to slay the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> together with their kinsmen;

children.text: svajanaṃ hi katham hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava ||
children.translated_text: for how could we be happy, O <s>Mādhava</s>, having slain our own people? ||

children.text: tasmān na arhā vayaṃ hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrān sabāndhavān |
sva-janaṃ hi katham hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava ||
yady apy ete na paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even if they, with minds corrupted by greed, do not see

children.text: kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam ||
children.translated_text: the sin caused by the destruction of family, or the crime of treachery to friends, ||

children.text: yady apy ete na paśyanti lobha-upahata-cetasaḥ |
kula-kṣaya-kṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitra-drohe ca pātakam ||
kathaṃ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum |
children.translated_text: how should we not know [enough] to turn away from this sin,

children.text: kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhir ñanārdana ||
children.translated_text: we who clearly see the evil caused by the destruction of family, O <s>Janārdana</s>? ||

children.text: kathaṃ na jñeyam asmābhiḥ pāpād asmān nivartitum |
kula-kṣaya-kṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhir ñanārdana ||
kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ |
children.translated_text: With the destruction of family, the eternal family duties (<s>kuladharma</s>) perish;

children.text: dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnam adharmo 'bhibhavaty uta ||
children.translated_text: when duty is destroyed, lawlessness (<s>adharma</s>) overwhelms the entire family. ||

children.text: kula-kṣaye praṇaśyanti kula-dharmāḥ sanātanāḥ |
dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnam adharmo 'bhibhavaty uta ||
adharmābhibhavāt kṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: From the prevalence of lawlessness, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the women of the family become corrupt;

children.text: strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: when women are corrupt, O <s>Vārṣṇeya</s>, intermixture of castes (<s>varṇasaṅkara</s>) arises. ||

children.text: adharma-abhibhavāt kṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kula-striyaḥ |
strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇa-saṅkaraḥ ||
saṅkaro narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṃ kulasya ca |
children.translated_text: Intermixture [leads] to hell alone for the family-destroyers and for the family;

children.text: patanti pitaro hy eṣāṃ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ancestors of these fall, deprived of the offerings of rice-balls and water. ||

children.text: saṅkaro narakāya eva kula-ghnānāṃ kulasya ca |
patanti pitaro hy eṣāṃ lupta-piṇḍa-udaka-kriyāḥ ||
doṣair etaiḥ kulaghnānāṃ varṇasaṅkarakārakaiḥ |
children.translated_text: By these sins of the family-destroyers, which cause the intermixture of castes,

children.text: utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāś ca śāśvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the eternal duties of caste (<s>jātidharma</s>) and family duties (<s>kuladharma</s>) are destroyed. ||

children.text: doṣair etaiḥ kula-ghnānāṃ varṇa-saṅkara-kārakaiḥ |
utsādyante jāti-dharmāḥ kula-dharmāś ca śāśvatāḥ ||
utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ ñanārdana |
children.translated_text: For men whose family duties are destroyed, O <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: narake niyataṃ vāso bhavatīty anuśuśruma ||
children.translated_text: there will surely be a dwelling in hell — so we have heard.' ||

children.text: utsanna-kula-dharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ ñanārdana |
narake niyataṃ vāso bhavati ity anuśuśruma ||
aho bata mahat pāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam |
children.translated_text: 'Alas! What a great sin we have resolved to commit,

children.text: yad rājyasukhalābhena hantuṃ svajanam udyatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: in that we are prepared to kill our own kinsmen for the sake of the pleasure of a kingdom!' ||

children.text: aho bata mahat pāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam |
yad rājya-sukha-lābhena hantuṃ sva-janam udyatāḥ ||
yadi mām apratīkāram aśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'If the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, weapons in hand, were to kill me in battle,

children.text: dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣemataraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: unarmed and unresisting — that would be more beneficial for me.' ||

children.text: yadi mām apratīkāram aśastraṃ śastra-pāṇayaḥ |
dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyus tan me kṣemataraṃ bhavet ||

body.text: bhavadbhir atighorair māraṇair jatugṛhadāhādibhir asakṛdvañcito 'pi paramapuruṣasahāyenātmanā haniṣya
body.translated_text: 'Though deceived more than once by you through exceedingly cruel acts of killing such as the burning of the lac-house and the like, I shall, with the Supreme Person (<s>Paramapuruṣa</s>) as my ally, destroy' —

children.text: bhavadbhir atighorair māraṇair jatu-gṛha-dāha-ādibhir asakṛd-vañcito 'pi parama-puruṣa-sahāyenā atmanā haniṣya-
evam uktvārjunaḥ saṃkhye rathopastha upāviśat |
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Arjuna</s> sat down on the seat of the chariot in the midst of battle,

children.text: visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: casting aside his bow along with its arrows, his mind overwhelmed with grief. ||

children.text: evam uktva ārjunaḥ saṃkhye ratha-upastha upāviśat |
visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ śoka-saṃvigna-mānasaḥ ||

body.text: māṇān bhavadīyān vilokya bandhusnehena parayā kṛpayā dharmabhayena cātimātrasannasarvagātraḥ sarvathāhaṃ na yotsyāmīty uktvā bandhuviśleṣajanitaśokasaṃvignamānasaḥ saśaraṃ cāpaṃ visṛjya rathopastha upāviśat //
body.translated_text: Seeing your kinsmen, with affection born of the bond of kinship, with supreme compassion, and with fear of <s>adharma</s>, all his limbs excessively weakened — having said 'I shall not fight under any circumstances,' his mind overwhelmed with grief born of separation from kinsmen, he cast aside his bow along with its arrows and sat down on the seat of the chariot. //

children.text: māṇān bhavadīyān vilokya bandhu-snehena parayā kṛpayā dharma-bhayena ca atimātra-sanna-sarva-gātraḥ sarvatha āhaṃ na yotsyāmi ity uktvā bandhu-viśleṣa-janita-śoka-saṃvigna-mānasaḥ saśaraṃ cāpaṃ visṛjya ratha-upastha upāviśat //
taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: To him, thus seized by compassion, his eyes filled and troubled with tears,

children.text: viṣīdantam idaṃ vākyam uvāca madhusūdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: despairing — <s>Madhusūdana</s> spoke these words: ||

children.text: taṃ tathā kṛpayā āviṣṭam aśru-pūrṇa-ākula-īkṣaṇam |
viṣīdantam idaṃ vākyam uvāca madhu-sūdanaḥ ||
kutas tvā kaśmalam idaṃ viṣame samupasthitam |
children.translated_text: 'Whence has this faintheartedness come upon you at this critical juncture,

children.text: anāryajuṣṭam asvargyam akīrtikaram arjuna ||
children.translated_text: unbecoming of a noble person, not leading to heaven, and causing dishonor, O <s>Arjuna</s>?' ||

children.text: kutas tvā kaśmalam idaṃ viṣame samupasthitam |
anārya-juṣṭam asvargyam akīrti-karam arjuna ||
mā klaibyaṃ gaccha kaunteya naitat tvayy upapadyate |
children.translated_text: 'Do not yield to unmanliness, O son of <s>Kuntī</s> — this does not befit you.',

children.text: kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa ||
children.translated_text: 'Abandon this base weakness of heart and arise, O scorcher of foes!' ||

children.text: mā klaibyaṃ gaccha kaunteya na etat tvayy upapadyate |
kṣudraṃ hṛdaya-daurbalyaṃ tyaktva ūttiṣṭha paran-tapa ||

body.text: evam upaviṣṭe pārthe kuto 'yam asthāne samupasthitaḥ śoka ity ākṣipya tam imaṃ viṣamasthaṃ śokam avidvatsevitaṃ paralokavirodhinam akīrtikaram atikṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyakṛtaṃ parityajya yuddhāyottiṣṭheti śrībhagavān uvāca //
body.translated_text: When <s>Pārtha</s> had thus sat down, the blessed Lord (<s>Śrī Bhagavān</s>) spoke — rebuking [him with] 'whence has this grief come upon you at this inappropriate moment?' — [saying:] 'Abandon this grief that is ill-placed, resorted to by the ignorant, opposed to the other world, causing dishonor, exceedingly base, and born of weakness of heart — and arise for battle!' //

children.text: evam upaviṣṭe pārthe kuto 'yam asthāne samupasthitaḥ śoka ity ākṣipya tam imaṃ viṣama-sthaṃ śokam avidvat-sevitaṃ para-loka-virodhinam akīrti-karam atikṣudraṃ hṛdaya-daurbalya-kṛtaṃ parityajya yuddhāya uttiṣṭha iti śrī-bhagavān uvāca //
kathaṃ bhīṣmam ahaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana |
children.translated_text: 'How can I fight against <s>Bhīṣma</s> in battle, and <s>Droṇa</s>, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>,

children.text: iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāv arisūdana ||
children.translated_text: with arrows — they who are worthy of worship, O destroyer of enemies?' ||

children.text: kathaṃ bhīṣmam ahaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ ca madhu-sūdana |
iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjā-arhāv ari-sūdana ||
gurūn ahatvā hi mahānubhāvān śreyaś cartuṃ bhaikṣam apīha loke |
children.translated_text: 'It would be better to live in this world even by begging than to kill teachers of great nobility;

children.text: hatvārthakāmāṃs tu gurūn ihaiva bhuñjīya bhogān rudhirapradigdhān ||
children.translated_text: for having killed teachers who desire wealth and pleasures, I would enjoy pleasures smeared with blood right here.' ||

children.text: gurūn ahatvā hi mahā-anubhāvān śreyaś cartuṃ bhaikṣam api iha loke |
hatva ārtha-kāmāṃs tu gurūn iha eva bhuñjīya bhogān rudhira-pradigdhān ||

body.text: punar api pārthaḥ snehakāruṇyadharmādharmabhayākulo bhagavaduktaṃ hitatamam ajānann idam uvāca -- bhīṣmadroṇādikān gurūn bahumantavyān katham ahaṃ haniṣyāmi? kathaṃtarāṃ bhogeṣv atimātrasaktān tān hatvā tair bhujyamānāṃs tān eva bhogān tadrudhireṇopasicya teṣv āsaneṣūpaviśya bhuñjīya? //
body.translated_text: Again, <s>Pārtha</s>, bewildered by affection, compassion, and the fear of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, not understanding the most beneficial [teaching] spoken by the Lord, said this: 'How can I kill teachers like <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and the others, who are to be highly honored? How indeed could I, having killed them who are excessively attached to pleasures, sprinkle those very pleasures that they were enjoying with their blood, sit upon those very seats, and enjoy [them]?' //

children.text: punar api pārthaḥ sneha-kāruṇya-dharma-adharma-bhaya-ākulo bhagavad-uktaṃ hitatamam ajānann idam uvāca --- bhīṣma-droṇa-ādikān gurūn bahu-mantavyān katham ahaṃ haniṣyāmi? kathaṃtarāṃ bhogeṣv atimātra-saktān tān hatvā tair bhujyamānāṃs tān eva bhogān tad-rudhireṇa upasicya teṣv āsaneṣu upaviśya bhuñjīya? //
na caitad vidmaḥ kataran no garīyo yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Nor do we know which is better for us — whether we should conquer or they should conquer us.',

children.text: yān eva hatvā na jijīviṣāmas te 'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Those very sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> stand before us, having killed whom we would not wish to live.' ||

children.text: na ca etad vidmaḥ kataran no garīyo yad vā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ |
yān eva hatvā na jijīviṣāmas te 'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ ||
kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvā dharmasaṃmūḍhacetāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'My nature overwhelmed by the fault of pity, my mind confused about <s>dharma</s> —

children.text: yac chreyaḥ syān niścitaṃ brūhi tan me śiṣyas te 'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam ||
children.translated_text: I ask you: tell me decisively what is the better [course]. I am your disciple — instruct me, who have taken refuge in you.' ||

children.text: kārpaṇya-doṣa-upahata-sva-bhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvā dharma-saṃmūḍha-cetāḥ |
yac chreyaḥ syān niścitaṃ brūhi tan me śiṣyas te 'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam ||
na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyād yac chokam ucchoṣaṇam indriyāṇām |
children.translated_text: 'For I do not see what could dispel this grief that dries up my senses,

children.text: avāpya bhūmāv asapatnam ṛddhaṃ rājyaṃ surāṇām api cādhipatyam ||
children.translated_text: even if I were to obtain on earth a prosperous kingdom without rivals, or even sovereignty over the gods.' ||

children.text: na hi prapaśyāmi mama apanudyād yac chokam ucchoṣaṇam indriyāṇām |
avāpya bhūmāv asapatnam ṛddhaṃ rājyaṃ surāṇām api cā adhipatyam ||

body.text: evaṃ yuddham ārabhya nivṛttavyāpārān bhavato dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ prasahya hanyur iti cet, astu / tadvadhalabdhavijayād adharmyād asmākaṃ dharmādharmāv ajānadbhiḥ tair hananam eva garīya iti me pratibhātīty uktvā, yan mahyaṃ śreya iti niścitam, tac śaraṇāgatāya tava śiṣyāya me brūhīty atimātrakṛpaṇo bhagavatpādāv upasasāda //
body.translated_text: Thus — if the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, having ceased activity regarding battle, were to forcefully kill you — so be it! For us, who do not know <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, their killing [of us] is weightier than the <s>adharma</s> of victory obtained through their slaughter — this is what appears to me. Having said this, [<s>Arjuna</s> said:] 'Tell me, your disciple who has come for refuge, what you determine to be the better [course] for me' — and, exceedingly pitiable, he approached the feet of the Lord. //

children.text: evaṃ yuddham ārabhya nivṛtta-vyāpārān bhavato dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ prasahya hanyur iti cet, astu / tad-vadha-labdha-vijayād adharmyād asmākaṃ dharma-adharmāv ajānadbhiḥ tair hananam eva garīya iti me pratibhāti ity uktvā, yan mahyaṃ śreya iti niścitam, tac śaraṇā-gatāya tava śiṣyāya me brūhi ity atimātra-kṛpaṇo bhagavat-pādāv upasasāda //
evam uktvā hṛśīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ parantapaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Guḍākeśa</s>, the scorcher of foes,

children.text: na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: having said 'I shall not fight' to <s>Govinda</s>, fell silent. ||

children.text: evam uktvā hṛśīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ paran-tapaḥ |
na yotsya iti govindam uktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha ||

body.text: "evam asthāne samupasthitasnehakāruṇyābhyām aprakṛtiṃ gatam, kṣatriyāṇāṃ yuddhaṃ paramadharmam apy adharmaṃ manvānaṃ dharmabubhutsayā ca śaraṇāgataṃ pārtham uddiśya, ātmayāthātmyajñānena yuddhasya phalābhisandhirahitasyātmaprāptyupāyatājñānena ca vinā asya moho na śāmyati" iti matvā, bhagavatā paramapuruṣeṇa adhyātmaśāstrāvataraṇaṃ kṛtam / taduktam -- "asthānasnehakāruṇyadharmādharmadhiyākulam / pārthaṃ prapannam uddiśya śāstrāvataraṇaṃ kṛtam" // iti // BhGR_2.9 //
body.translated_text: "Seeing <s>Pārtha</s>, who had been brought to an unnatural state by affection and compassion inappropriately arisen, who was regarding as <s>adharma</s> even the supreme <s>dharma</s> of battle for <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and who had taken refuge [in the Lord] out of a desire to know <s>dharma</s> — thinking: 'Without knowledge of the true nature of the self, and without the knowledge that battle performed without attachment to results is a means of attaining the self, his delusion will not be pacified' — the blessed Lord, the Supreme Person (<s>Paramapuruṣa</s>), undertook the descent of the science of the self (<s>adhyātmaśāstra</s>). As stated: 'Seeing <s>Pārtha</s> who had taken refuge, bewildered by affection, compassion, and confused notions of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> inappropriately arisen, the descent of the scripture was undertaken.' // <s>BhGR</s> 2.9 //"

children.text: "evam asthāne samupasthita-sneha-kāruṇyābhyām aprakṛtiṃ gatam, kṣatriyāṇāṃ yuddhaṃ parama-dharmam apy adharmaṃ manvānaṃ dharma-bubhutsayā ca śaraṇā-gataṃ pārtham uddiśya, ātma-yāthātmya-jñānena yuddhasya phala-abhisandhi-rahitasyā atma-prāpty-upāyatā-jñānena ca vinā asya moho na śāmyati" iti matvā, bhagavatā parama-puruṣeṇa adhyātma-śāstra-avataraṇaṃ kṛtam / tad-uktam --- "asthāna-sneha-kāruṇya-dharma-adharma-dhiyā ākulam / pārthaṃ prapannam uddiśya śāstra-avataraṇaṃ kṛtam" // iti // BhGR_2.9 //
tam uvāca hṛśīkeśaḥ prahasann iva bhārata |
children.translated_text: <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> spoke to him, as if smiling, O <s>Bhārata</s>,

children.text: senayor ubhayor madhye sīdamānam idaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the midst of both armies, these words to the despairing one: ||

children.text: tam uvāca hṛśīkeśaḥ prahasann iva bhārata |
senayor ubhayor madhye sīdamānam idaṃ vacaḥ ||

body.text: evaṃ dehātmanor yāthātmyājñānanimittaśokāviṣṭam, dehātiriktātmajñānanimittaṃ ca dharmaṃ bhāṣamāṇam, parasparaviruddhaguṇānvitam, ubhayos senayor yuddhāyodyuktayor madhye akasmān nirudyogaṃ pārtham ālokya paramapuruṣaḥ prahasann ivedam uvāca -- parihāsavākyaṃ vadann iva ātmaparamātmayāthātmyatatprāptyupāyabhūtakarmayogajñānayogabhaktiyogagocaraṃ "na tv evāhaṃ jātu nāsam" ityārabhya "ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ" ityetadantaṃ vacanam uvācetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, to [<s>Arjuna</s>], who was seized by grief caused by ignorance of the true nature of the body and the self, and who was speaking of <s>dharma</s> occasioned by the knowledge of a self distinct from the body — [though] endowed with mutually contradictory qualities — seeing <s>Pārtha</s> suddenly inactive in the midst of both armies arrayed for battle, the Supreme Person (<s>Paramapuruṣa</s>) spoke this, as if smiling — as if speaking words of jest — a discourse encompassing <s>karmayoga</s> (the yoga of action), <s>jñānayoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge), and <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (the yoga of devotion) as means for attaining the true nature of the self and the Supreme Self, beginning with 'Never indeed was there a time when I did not exist' and ending with 'I shall liberate you from all sins — do not grieve.' This is the meaning. //

children.text: evaṃ deha-ātmanor yāthātmya-ajñāna-nimitta-śoka-āviṣṭam, deha-atirikta-ātma-jñāna-nimittaṃ ca dharmaṃ bhāṣamāṇam, paraspara-viruddha-guṇa-anvitam, ubhayos senayor yuddhāya udyuktayor madhye akasmān nirudyogaṃ pārtham ālokya parama-puruṣaḥ prahasann iva idam uvāca --- parihāsa-vākyaṃ vadann iva ātma-parama-ātma-yāthātmya-tat-prāpty-upāya-bhūta-karma-yoga-jñāna-yoga-bhakti-yoga-gocaraṃ "na tv eva ahaṃ jātu nā asam" ity-ārabhya "ahaṃ tvā sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ" ity-etad-antaṃ vacanam uvāca ity-arthaḥ //
aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṃ prajñāvādāṃś ca bhāṣase |
children.translated_text: 'You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, yet you speak words of wisdom;

children.text: gatāsūn agatāsūṃś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.' ||

children.text: aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṃ prajñā-vādāṃś ca bhāṣase |
gata-asūn a-gata-asūṃś ca na anuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ ||

body.text:
aśocyān prati anuśocasi / "patanti pitaro hy eṣāṃ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ" ityādikān dehātmasvabhāvaprajñānimittavādāṃś ca bhāṣase / dehātmasvabhāvajñānavatāṃ nātra kiṃcic chokanimittam asti / gatāsūn dehān agatāsūn; ātmanaś ca prati tatsvabhāvayāthātmyavido na śocanti / atas tvayi vipratiṣiddham idam upalabhyate, yad etān haniṣyāmīty anuśocanam, yac ca dehātiriktātmajñānakṛtaṃ dharmādharmabhāṣaṇam / ato dehasvabhāvaṃ ca na jānāsi, tadatiriktam ātmānaṃ ca nityam, tatprāptyupāyabhūtaṃ yuddhādikaṃ dharmaṃ ca / idaṃ ca yuddhaṃ phalābhisandhirahitam ātmayāthātmyāvāptyupāyabhūtam / ātmā hi na janmādhīnasadbhāvaḥ; na maraṇādhīnavināśaś ca, tasya janmamaraṇayor abhāvāt / ataḥ sa na śokasthānam / dehas tv acetanaḥ pariṇāmasvabhāvaḥ;
tasyotpattivināśayogaḥ svābhāvika iti so 'pi na śokasthānam ityabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: You grieve regarding those who should not be grieved for. You speak statements occasioned by the knowledge that the body is the nature of the self, such as 'for the ancestors of these fall, deprived of the rites of offering food and water,' and the like. For those who know the nature of the body as the self, there is no cause for grief here at all. For the dead — the bodies — and the living — the selves — those who know the true nature of each do not grieve. Therefore, something contradictory is found in you: the grieving that 'I shall kill them,' and the speaking about <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> which is based on the knowledge of a self distinct from the body. Therefore, you know neither the nature of the body, nor the self which is eternal and distinct from it, nor <s>dharma</s> such as battle which is the means for attaining it. And this battle, performed without attachment to results, is a means for attaining the true nature of the self. For the self does not have its existence dependent on birth, nor its destruction dependent on death, since birth and death do not pertain to it. Therefore, it is not a cause for grief. But the body is insentient, with transformation as its nature; its origination and destruction are natural — so it too is not a cause for grief. This is the purport. //

children.text:
aśocyān prati anuśocasi / "patanti pitaro hy eṣāṃ lupta-piṇḍa-udaka-kriyāḥ" ity-ādikān deha-ātma-sva-bhāva-prajñā-nimitta-vādāṃś ca bhāṣase / deha-ātma-sva-bhāva-jñānavatāṃ na atra kiṃcic choka-nimittam asti / gata-asūn dehān a-gata-asūn; ātmanaś ca prati tat-sva-bhāva-yāthātmya-vido na śocanti / atas tvayi vipratiṣiddham idam upalabhyate, yad etān haniṣyāmi ity anuśocanam, yac ca deha-atirikta-ātma-jñāna-kṛtaṃ dharma-adharma-bhāṣaṇam / ato deha-sva-bhāvaṃ ca na jānāsi, tad-atiriktam ātmānaṃ ca nityam, tat-prāpty-upāya-bhūtaṃ yuddha-ādikaṃ dharmaṃ ca / idaṃ ca yuddhaṃ phala-abhisandhi-rahitam ātma-yāthātmya-avāpty-upāya-bhūtam / ātmā hi na janma-adhīna-sad-bhāvaḥ; na maraṇa-adhīna-vināśaś ca, tasya janma-maraṇayor abhāvāt / ataḥ sa na śoka-sthānam / dehas tv acetanaḥ pariṇāma-sva-bhāvaḥ;
tasya utpatti-vināśa-yogaḥ svābhāvika iti so 'pi na śoka-sthānam ity-abhiprāyaḥ //

body.text: prathamaṃ tāvad ātmanāṃ svabhāvam śṛṇu --
body.translated_text: First, hear the nature of the selves:

children.text: prathamaṃ tāvad ātmanāṃ sva-bhāvam śṛṇu ---
na tv evāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Never indeed was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these lords of men;

children.text: na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayam ataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: nor shall any of us cease to exist hereafter.' ||

children.text: na tv eva ahaṃ jātu nā asaṃ na tvaṃ na ime jana-adhipāḥ |
na ca eva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayam ataḥ param ||

body.text: ahaṃ sarveśvaras tāvat, ataḥ vartamānāt pūrvasmin anādau kāle, na nāsam -- api tv āsam / tvanmukhāś caite īśitavyāḥ kṣetrajñāḥ na nāsam; api tv āsan / ahaṃ ca yūyaṃ ca sarve vayam, ataḥ parasmin anante kāle, na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ; api tu bhaviṣyāma eva / yathāhaṃ sarveśvaraḥ paramātmā nitya iti nātra saṃśayaḥ, tathaiva bhavantaḥ kṣetrajñā ātmāno 'pi nityā eveti mantavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: I, the Lord of all (<s>Sarveśvara</s>), first of all — in the beginningless time prior to this present [moment] — did not not exist; rather, I existed. And these individual selves (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), the governed ones, beginning with you — [they] did not not exist; rather, they existed. And I and all of you, all of us — in the endless time after this — we shall certainly not not exist; rather, we shall certainly exist. Just as there is no doubt that I, the Lord of all, the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), am eternal — so too you, the individual selves, must be understood as eternal. //

children.text: ahaṃ sarva-īśvaras tāvat, ataḥ vartamānāt pūrvasmin anādau kāle, na nā asam --- api tv āsam / tvan-mukhāś ca ete īśitavyāḥ kṣetra-jñāḥ na nā asam; api tv āsan / ahaṃ ca yūyaṃ ca sarve vayam, ataḥ parasmin anante kāle, na ca eva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ; api tu bhaviṣyāma eva / yatha āhaṃ sarva-īśvaraḥ parama-ātmā nitya iti na atra saṃśayaḥ, tatha aiva bhavantaḥ kṣetra-jñā ātmāno 'pi nityā eva iti mantavyāḥ //

body.text:
evaṃ bhagavataḥ sarveśvarād atmanām, parasparaṃ ca, bhedaḥ pāramārthika iti bhagavataivoktam iti pratīyate; ajñānamohitaṃ prati tannivṛttaye pārmārthikanityatvopadeśasamaye aham, tvam, ime, sarve, vayam iti vyapadeśāt / aupacārikātmabhedavāde hi ātmabhedasyātāttvikatvena tattvopadeśasamaye bhedanirdeśo na saṃgacchate / bhagavaduktātmabhedaḥ svābhāvika iti śrutir apy āha, "nityo nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān" iti / nityānāṃ bahūnāṃ cetanānāṃ ya eko nityaś cetanas san kāmān vidadhātītyarthaḥ / ajñānakṛtabhedadṛṣṭivāde tu paramapuruṣasya paramārthadṛṣter nirviśeṣakūṭasthanityacaitanyātmayāthātmyasākṣātkārān nivṛttājñānatatkāryatayā ajñānakṛtabhedadarśanaṃ tanmūlopadeśādivyavahārāś ca
na saṃgacchante /
atha paramapuruṣasyādhigatādvaitajñānasya bādhitānuvṛttirūpam idaṃ bhedajñānaṃ dagdhapaṭādivan na bandhakam ity ucyate -- naitad upapadyate; marīcikājalajñānādikaṃ hi bādhitam anuvartamānaṃ na jalāharaṇādipravṛttihetuḥ / evam atrāpy advaitajñānena bādhitaṃ bhedajñānam anuvartamānam api mithyārthaviṣayatvaniścayān nopadeśādipravṛttihetur bhavati / na ceśvarasya pūrvam ajñasya śāstrādhigatatattvajñānatayā bādhitānuvṛttiḥ śakyate vaktum; "yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit", "parāsya śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñānabalakriyā ca", "vedāhaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna / bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana" iti śrutismṛtivirodhāt / kiṃ ca paramapuruṣaś ca idānīṃtanaguruparamparā ca, advitīyātmasvarūpaniścaye
sati anuvartamāne 'pi bhedajñāne, svaniścayānurūpam advitīyātmajñānaṃ kasmā upadiśatīti vaktavyam // pratibimbavatpratīyamānebhyo 'rjunādibhya iti cet -- naitad upapadyate; na hy anunmattaḥ ko 'pi maṇikṛpāṇadarpaṇādiṣu pratīyamāneṣu svātmapratibimbeṣu, teṣāṃ svātmano 'nanyatvaṃ jānan, tebhyaḥ kim apy upadiśati / bādhitānuvṛttir api tair na śakyate vaktum; bādhakenādvitīyātmajñānenātmavyatiriktabhedajñānakāraṇasyānāder vinaṣṭatvāt / dvicandrajñānādau tu candraikatvajñānena pāramārthikatimirādidoṣasya dvicandrajñānahetor avinaṣṭatvād bādhitānuvṛttir yuktā; anuvartamānam api prabalapramāṇabādhitatvenā-kiṃcitkaram / iha tu bhedajñānasya saviṣayasya sakāraṇasyā-pāramārthikatvena vastuyāthātmyajñānavinaṣṭatvān na kathañcid
api bādhitānuvṛttiḥ saṃbhavati / ataḥ sarveśvarasyedānīṃtanaguruparamparāyāś ca tattvajñānam asti cet, bhedadarśanatatkāryopadeśādyasaṃbhavaḥ / nāsti cet, ajñānasya taddhetoḥ sthitatvenājñatvād eva sutarām upadeśo na saṃbhavati //
body.translated_text:
Thus, the difference of the selves from the Lord of all, the blessed Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>), and from one another, is ultimate (<s>pāramārthika</s>) — this is understood as stated by the blessed Lord himself. For when teaching the ultimate eternal nature [of the self] to one deluded by ignorance, for the purpose of removing that [ignorance], the use of the terms 'I,' 'you,' 'these,' 'all,' 'we' [indicates real distinction]. In a doctrine of figurative self-difference, since the difference of selves would be non-ultimate, the indication of difference at the time of teaching the truth would not be consistent. That the difference of selves stated by the Lord is natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>) is also stated by scripture (<s>śruti</s>): 'The Eternal among eternals, the Conscious among conscious beings, the One among many who fulfills [their] desires.' The meaning is: He who, being one, eternal, and conscious, fulfills the desires of the many eternal conscious beings. But in the doctrine that the vision of difference is caused by ignorance, the Supreme Person — who has the ultimate vision — having directly realized the true nature of the self as undifferentiated, immutably eternal consciousness, and having [thereby] destroyed ignorance and its effects — such a vision of difference caused by ignorance and the practical dealings such as teaching based on that [ignorance] would not be consistent.
Now, if it is said that for the Supreme Person who has attained the knowledge of non-duality, this knowledge of difference is in the form of sublated continuation (<s>bādhitānuvṛtti</s>), like a burnt cloth, and is not binding — this is not tenable. For cognition of water in a mirage, and the like, even when continuing after sublation, is not a cause of activity like going to fetch water. Similarly here too, the knowledge of difference, even though continuing after sublation by the knowledge of non-duality, would not be a cause of activity like teaching, since there is the certainty that its content is unreal. And it cannot be said that the Lord was formerly ignorant and that His knowledge of reality was subsequently obtained through scripture, [resulting in] sublated continuation — because of the contradiction with <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> [which declare]: 'He who is omniscient, who knows all,' 'His supreme power is heard to be manifold — His knowledge, strength, and action are inherent,' and 'I know all past, present, and future beings, O <s>Arjuna</s>, but no one knows Me.' Furthermore, it must be explained why the Supreme Person and the current lineage of teachers, when the knowledge of difference continues even after certainty about the undivided self-nature, teach the knowledge of the undivided self in accordance with their own certainty. If [it is said:] to <s>Arjuna</s> and others who appear like reflections — this is not tenable. For no sane person, knowing the non-difference of his own reflections seen in jewels, swords, mirrors, and the like from himself, teaches anything to those [reflections]. Nor can they maintain sublated continuation, because the beginningless cause of the knowledge of difference distinct from the self has been destroyed by the sublating knowledge of the undivided self. But in the case of the cognition of two moons and the like, since the actual defect such as <s>timira</s> (eye-disease) — the cause of the two-moon cognition — has not been destroyed by the knowledge of the moon's oneness, sublated continuation is reasonable; though continuing, it is inefficacious because it is sublated by a stronger <s>pramāṇa</s>. But here, since the knowledge of difference — which has a real object and a real cause — is destroyed by the knowledge of the true nature of reality as being non-ultimate, sublated continuation is in no way possible. Therefore, if the knowledge of reality exists for the Lord of all and the current lineage of teachers, the impossibility of the vision of difference and its effects such as teaching [follows]. And if [that knowledge] does not exist, then since ignorance — the cause of that [difference-vision] — persists, all the more is teaching impossible, since they are ignorant. //

children.text:
evaṃ bhagavataḥ sarva-īśvarād atmanām, parasparaṃ ca, bhedaḥ pāramārthika iti bhagavata aiva uktam iti pratīyate; ajñāna-mohitaṃ prati tan-nivṛttaye pārmārthika-nityatva-upadeśa-samaye aham, tvam, ime, sarve, vayam iti vyapadeśāt / aupacārika-ātma-bheda-vāde hi ātma-bhedasya atāttvikatvena tattva-upadeśa-samaye bheda-nirdeśo na saṃgacchate / bhagavad-ukta-ātma-bhedaḥ svābhāvika iti śrutir apy āha, "nityo nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān" iti / nityānāṃ bahūnāṃ cetanānāṃ ya eko nityaś cetanas san kāmān vidadhāti ity-arthaḥ / ajñāna-kṛta-bheda-dṛṣṭi-vāde tu parama-puruṣasya parama-artha-dṛṣter nirviśeṣa-kūṭa-stha-nitya-caitanya-ātma-yāthātmya-sākṣātkārān nivṛtta-ajñāna-tat-kāryatayā ajñāna-kṛta-bheda-darśanaṃ tan-mūla-upadeśa-ādi-vyavahārāś ca
na saṃgacchante /
atha parama-puruṣasya adhigata-advaita-jñānasya bādhita-anuvṛtti-rūpam idaṃ bheda-jñānaṃ dagdha-paṭa-ādivan na bandhakam ity ucyate --- na etad upapadyate; marīcikā-jala-jñāna-ādikaṃ hi bādhitam anuvartamānaṃ na jalā-haraṇa-ādi-pravṛtti-hetuḥ / evam atra apy advaita-jñānena bādhitaṃ bheda-jñānam anuvartamānam api mithyā-artha-viṣayatva-niścayān na upadeśa-ādi-pravṛtti-hetur bhavati / na cā iśvarasya pūrvam ajñasya śāstra-adhigata-tattva-jñānatayā bādhita-anuvṛttiḥ śakyate vaktum; "yaḥ sarva-jñaḥ sarva-vit", "para āsya śaktir vividha aiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñāna-bala-kriyā ca", "veda ahaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni ca arjuna / bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana" iti śruti-smṛti-virodhāt / kiṃ ca parama-puruṣaś ca idānīṃtana-guru-paramparā ca, advitīya-ātma-sva-rūpa-niścaye
sati anuvartamāne 'pi bheda-jñāne, sva-niścaya-anurūpam advitīya-ātma-jñānaṃ kasmā upadiśati iti vaktavyam // pratibimbavat-pratīyamānebhyo 'rjuna-ādibhya iti cet --- na etad upapadyate; na hy anunmattaḥ ko 'pi maṇi-kṛpāṇa-darpaṇa-ādiṣu pratīyamāneṣu sva-ātma-pratibimbeṣu, teṣāṃ sva-ātmano 'nanyatvaṃ jānan, tebhyaḥ kim apy upadiśati / bādhita-anuvṛttir api tair na śakyate vaktum; bādhakena advitīya-ātma-jñānenā atma-vyatirikta-bheda-jñāna-kāraṇasya anāder vinaṣṭatvāt / dvi-candra-jñāna-ādau tu candra-ekatva-jñānena pāramārthika-timira-ādi-doṣasya dvi-candra-jñāna-hetor avinaṣṭatvād bādhita-anuvṛttir yuktā; anuvartamānam api prabala-pramāṇa-bādhitatvena a-kiṃcit-karam / iha tu bheda-jñānasya sa-viṣayasya sa-kāraṇasya a-pāramārthikatvena vastu-yāthātmya-jñāna-vinaṣṭatvān na kathañcid
api bādhita-anuvṛttiḥ saṃbhavati / ataḥ sarva-īśvarasya idānīṃtana-guru-paramparāyāś ca tattva-jñānam asti cet, bheda-darśana-tat-kārya-upadeśa-ādy-asaṃbhavaḥ / na asti cet, a-jñānasya tad-dhetoḥ sthitatvena ajñatvād eva sutarām upadeśo na saṃbhavati //

body.text: kiṃ ca guror advitīyātmavijñānād eva brahmājñānasya sakāryasya vinaṣṭatvāc śiṣyaṃ praty upadeśo niṣprayojanaḥ / gurus tajjñānaṃ ca kalpitam iti cet, śiṣyatajjñānayor api kalpitatvāt tad apy anivartakam / kalpitatve 'pi pūrvavirodhitvena nivartakam iti cet, tad acāryajñāne 'pi samānam iti tad eva nivartakaṃ bhavatīty upadeśānarthakyam eva -- iti kṛtam asamīcīnavādaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, since from the teacher's knowledge of the undivided self alone, the ignorance of <s>Brahman</s> along with its effects has been destroyed, teaching the student is purposeless. If [one says] the teacher and that knowledge are imagined (<s>kalpita</s>) — since the student and his knowledge are also imagined, that too does not remove [ignorance]. If [one says] even though imagined, it removes [ignorance] because it is contradictory to the prior [ignorance] — that is equally true of the teacher's knowledge, so that alone becomes the remover — and so teaching is purposeless all the same. — Thus, enough with unsound doctrines! //

children.text: kiṃ ca guror advitīya-ātma-vijñānād eva brahma-ajñānasya sa-kāryasya vinaṣṭatvāc śiṣyaṃ praty upadeśo niṣprayojanaḥ / gurus taj-jñānaṃ ca kalpitam iti cet, śiṣya-taj-jñānayor api kalpitatvāt tad apy anivartakam / kalpitatve 'pi pūrva-virodhitvena nivartakam iti cet, tad acārya-jñāne 'pi samānam iti tad eva nivartakaṃ bhavati ity upadeśa-anarthakyam eva --- iti kṛtam asamīcīna-vādaiḥ //
dehino 'smin yathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā |
children.translated_text: 'Just as in this body the embodied [self] [passes through] boyhood, youth, and old age,

children.text: tathā dehāntaraprāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati ||
children.translated_text: so too [does the self] attain another body — the wise person is not deluded about this.' ||

children.text: dehino 'smin yathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā |
tathā deha-antara-prāptir dhīras tatra na muhyati ||

body.text: ekasmin dehe vartamānasya dehinaḥ kaumārāvasthāṃ vihāya yauvanādyavasthāprāptau ātmanaḥ sthiratvabuddhyā yathā ātmā naṣṭa iti na śocati, dehād dehāntaraprāptāv api tathaiva sthira ātmeti buddhimān na śocati / ata ātmanāṃ nityatvād ātmano na śokasthānam //
body.translated_text: Just as the embodied being (<s>dehin</s>) dwelling in a single body, upon leaving the childhood state and attaining the stage of youth and the like, does not grieve thinking 'the self is lost' — due to the firm understanding of the stability of the self — so too, even upon attaining another body from the [present] body, the wise one does not grieve, [knowing] the self is stable. Therefore, since the selves are eternal, the self is not a ground for grief.

children.text: ekasmin dehe vartamānasya dehinaḥ kaumāra-avasthāṃ vihāya yauvana-ādy-avasthā-prāptau ātmanaḥ sthiratva-buddhyā yathā ātmā naṣṭa iti na śocati, dehād deha-antara-prāptāv api tatha aiva sthira ātma īti buddhimān na śocati / ata ātmanāṃ nityatvād ātmano na śoka-sthānam //

body.text: etāvad atra kartavyam -- ātmanāṃ nityānām evānādikarmavaśyatayā tattatkarmocitadehasaṃsṛṣṭānāṃ tair eva dehair bandhanivṛttaye śāstrīyaṃ svavarṇocitaṃ yuddhādikam anabhisaṃhitaphalaṃ karma kurvatām avarjanīyatayā indriyair indriyārthasparśāḥ śītoṣṇādiprayuktasukhaduḥkhadā bhavanti, te tu yāvacchāstrīyakarmasamāpti kṣantavyā iti / imam artham anantaram evāha --
body.translated_text: This much is to be done here: since the selves, being eternally subject to beginningless <s>karma</s>, are conjoined with bodies appropriate to their respective <s>karmas</s> — for those who perform scriptural action appropriate to their own <s>varṇa</s> (social class), such as battle and the like, without attachment to results, for the purpose of removing bondage through those very bodies — the contacts of the senses with sense-objects, which produce pleasure and pain occasioned by cold, heat, and the like, are unavoidable. But these must be endured until the completion of the scriptural action. He states this very meaning immediately after:

children.text: etāvad atra kartavyam --- ātmanāṃ nityānām eva anādi-karma-vaśyatayā tat-tat-karma-ucita-deha-saṃsṛṣṭānāṃ tair eva dehair bandha-nivṛttaye śāstrīyaṃ sva-varṇa-ucitaṃ yuddha-ādikam anabhisaṃhita-phalaṃ karma kurvatām avarjanīyatayā indriyair indriya-artha-sparśāḥ śīta-uṣṇa-ādi-prayukta-sukha-duḥkha-dā bhavanti, te tu yāvac-chāstrīya-karma-samāpti kṣantavyā iti / imam artham anantaram evā aha ---
mātrāsparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The contacts with matter, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, which give cold and heat, pleasure and pain,' |

children.text: āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṃs titikṣasva bhārata ||
children.translated_text: 'they come and go, are impermanent — endure them, O <s>Bhārata</s>.' ||

children.text: mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ |
āgama-apāyino 'nityās tāṃs titikṣasva bhārata ||

body.text: śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ sāśrayāḥ tanmātrākāryatvān mātrā ity ucyante / śrotrādibhis teṣāṃ sparśāḥ śītoṣṇamṛduparuṣādirūpasukhaduḥkhadāḥ bhavanti / śītoṣṇaśabdaḥ pradarśanārthaḥ / tān dhairyeṇa yāvadyuddhādiśāstrīyakarmasamāpti titikṣasva / te cāgamāpāyitvād dhairyavatām kṣantuṃ yogyāḥ / anityāś ca te / bandhahetubhūtakarmanāśe sati āgamāpāyitvenāpi na vartante ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, together with their substrata, are called <s>mātrā</s> because they are effects of the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). Their contacts with the ear and other [sense organs] produce pleasure and pain in the form of cold, heat, soft, hard, and the like. The word 'cold and heat' is illustrative. Endure them with fortitude until the completion of scriptural action such as battle. And since they come and go, they are fit to be endured by those who possess fortitude. And they are impermanent — meaning that when the <s>karma</s> that is the cause of bondage is destroyed, they do not persist even in their coming-and-going nature.

children.text: śabda-sparśa-rūpa-rasa-gandhāḥ sa-āśrayāḥ tanmātrā-kāryatvān mātrā ity ucyante / śrotra-ādibhis teṣāṃ sparśāḥ śīta-uṣṇa-mṛdu-paruṣa-ādi-rūpa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ bhavanti / śīta-uṣṇa-śabdaḥ pradarśana-arthaḥ / tān dhairyeṇa yāvad-yuddha-ādi-śāstrīya-karma-samāpti titikṣasva / te cā agama-apāyitvād dhairyavatām kṣantuṃ yogyāḥ / anityāś ca te / bandha-hetu-bhūta-karma-nāśe sati āgama-apāyitvena api na vartante ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: tatkṣamā kimarthety atrāha --
body.translated_text: To the question 'for what purpose is that endurance?' he says:

children.text: tat-kṣamā kim-artha īty atrā aha ---
yaṃ hi na vyathayanty ete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha |
children.translated_text: 'The person whom these do not afflict, O best of men,' |

children.text: samaduḥkhasukhaṃ dhīraṃ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: 'the wise one who is equal in pain and pleasure — he is fit for immortality.' ||

children.text: yaṃ hi na vyathayanty ete puruṣaṃ puruṣa-rṣabha |
sama-duḥkha-sukhaṃ dhīraṃ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate ||

body.text: yaṃ puruṣaṃ dhairyayuktam avarjanīyaduḥkhaṃ sukhavan manyamānam, amṛtatvasādhanatayā svavarṇocitaṃ yuddhādikarma anabhisaṃhitaphalaṃ kurvāṇaṃ tadantargatāḥ śastrapātādimṛdukrūrasparśāḥ na vyathayanti; sa evāmṛtatvaṃ sādhayati / na tvādṛśo duḥkhāsahiṣṇur ityarthaḥ / ātmanāṃ nityatvād etāvad atra kartavyam ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The person endowed with fortitude, who regards unavoidable pain as [equal to] pleasure, who performs action appropriate to his <s>varṇa</s>, such as battle, as a means to immortality, without attachment to results — whom the contacts of weapons, soft and cruel, included therein, do not afflict — he alone achieves immortality. Not one such as you who cannot bear pain — this is the meaning. Since the selves are eternal, this much alone is to be done here — this is the meaning.

children.text: yaṃ puruṣaṃ dhairya-yuktam avarjanīya-duḥkhaṃ sukhavan manyamānam, amṛtatva-sādhanatayā sva-varṇa-ucitaṃ yuddha-ādi-karma anabhisaṃhita-phalaṃ kurvāṇaṃ tad-antargatāḥ śastra-pāta-ādi-mṛdu-krūra-sparśāḥ na vyathayanti; sa eva amṛtatvaṃ sādhayati / na tva-ādṛśo duḥkha-asahiṣṇur ity-arthaḥ / ātmanāṃ nityatvād etāvad atra kartavyam ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: yat tu ātmanāṃ nityatvaṃ dehānāṃ svābhāvikaṃ nāśitvaṃ ca śokānimittam uktam, "gatāsūn agatāsūṃś ca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ" iti, tad upapādayitum ārabhate --
body.translated_text: But as for the statement that the eternality of the selves and the inherent destructibility of bodies are not grounds for grief — 'the wise do not grieve for those whose life-breaths have departed or for those whose life-breaths have not departed' — he begins to establish this:

children.text: yat tu ātmanāṃ nityatvaṃ dehānāṃ svābhāvikaṃ nāśitvaṃ ca śoka-animittam uktam, "gata-asūn agata-asūṃś ca na anuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ" iti, tad upapādayitum ārabhate ---
nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The unreal has no being; the real has no non-being.' |

children.text: ubhayor api dṛṣṭo 'ntas tv anayos tattvadarśibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The conclusion of both has indeed been seen by the seers of truth.' ||

children.text: na asato vidyate bhāvo na abhāvo vidyate sataḥ |
ubhayor api dṛṣṭo 'ntas tv anayos tattva-darśibhiḥ ||

body.text:
asataḥ dehasya sadbhāvo na vidyate / sataś cātmano nāsadbhāvaḥ / ubhayoḥ -- dehātmanor upalabhyamānayor yathopalabdhi tattvadarśibhir anto dṛṣṭaḥ -- nirṇayāntatvān nirūpaṇasya nirṇaya iha antaśabdenocyate / dehasyācidvastuno 'sattvam eva svarūpam; ātmanaś cetanasya sattvam eva svarūpam iti nirṇayo dṛṣṭa ityarthaḥ / vināśasvabhāvo hy asattvam / avināśasvabhāvaś ca sattvam / yathā uktaṃ bhagavatā parāśareṇa, "tasmān na vijñānam ṛte 'sti kiṃcit kvacit kadācid dvija vastujātam", "sadbhāva evaṃ bhavato mayokto jñānaṃ yathā satyam asatyam anyat", "anāśī paramārthaś ca prājñair abhyupagamyate / tat tu nāśi na saṃdeho nāśidravyopapāditam", "yat tu kālāntareṇāpi nānyasaṃjñām upaiti vai / pariṇāmādisaṃbhūtāṃ tad vastu nṛpa tac ca kim" iti / atrāpi "antavanta
ime dehāḥ", "avināśi tu tad viddhi" iti hy ucyate / tad eva sattvāsattvavyapadeśahetur iti gamyate //
body.translated_text: The unreal — the body — has no coming-into-being. And of the real — the self — there is no coming-into-non-being. Of both — of the body and the self as they are perceived — the conclusion has been seen by the seers of truth as it truly is. Since 'conclusion' (<s>anta</s>) means the end of inquiry, the word <s>anta</s> here denotes determination. The essential nature of the body, which is non-conscious matter (<s>acid-vastu</s>), is precisely non-being (<s>asattva</s>); the essential nature of the self, which is conscious (<s>cetana</s>), is precisely being (<s>sattva</s>) — such is the determination that has been seen. For the nature of destruction is non-being; and the nature of indestructibility is being. As the blessed <s>Parāśara</s> has stated: 'Therefore, without consciousness there is nothing whatsoever, anywhere, at any time, O twice-born, among the classes of entities'; 'Thus has being been declared by me to you — knowledge is real, the other is unreal'; 'The indestructible is accepted by the wise as the ultimate reality; but what is destructible — there is no doubt — is established by destructible substance'; 'But that which, even with the passage of time, does not acquire a different designation, arising from transformation and the like — that is a real entity, O king, and what is that?' And here too, 'these bodies have an end,' 'but know that to be indestructible' — this is indeed said. From this it is understood that this alone is the ground for the designation of being and non-being.

children.text:
asataḥ dehasya sad-bhāvo na vidyate / sataś cā atmano na asad-bhāvaḥ / ubhayoḥ --- deha-ātmanor upalabhyamānayor yathā-upalabdhi tattva-darśibhir anto dṛṣṭaḥ --- nirṇaya-antatvān nirūpaṇasya nirṇaya iha anta-śabdena ucyate / dehasya acid-vastuno 'sattvam eva sva-rūpam; ātmanaś cetanasya sattvam eva sva-rūpam iti nirṇayo dṛṣṭa ity-arthaḥ / vināśa-sva-bhāvo hy asattvam / avināśa-sva-bhāvaś ca sattvam / yathā uktaṃ bhagavatā parāśareṇa, "tasmān na vijñānam ṛte 'sti kiṃ-cit kva-cit kadā-cid dvi-ja vastu-jātam", "sad-bhāva evaṃ bhavato maya ūkto jñānaṃ yathā satyam asatyam anyat", "anāśī parama-arthaś ca prājñair abhyupagamyate / tat tu nāśi na saṃdeho nāśi-dravya-upapāditam", "yat tu kāla-antareṇa api na anya-saṃjñām upaiti vai / pariṇāma-ādi-saṃbhūtāṃ tad vastu nṛ-pa tac ca kim" iti / atra api "antavanta
ime dehāḥ", "avināśi tu tad viddhi" iti hy ucyate / tad eva sattva-asattva-vyapadeśa-hetur iti gamyate //

body.text: atra tu satkāryavādasyāprastutatvān na tatparo 'yaṃ ślokaḥ; dehātmasvabhāvājñānamohitasya tanmohaśāntaye hy ubhayor nāśitvānāśitvarūpasvabhāvaviveka eva vaktavyaḥ / sa eva "gatāsūn agatāsūn" iti ca prastutaḥ / sa eva ca, "avināśi tu tad viddhi", "antavanta ime dehāḥ" iti anantaram upapādyate / ato yathā ukta evārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, since the doctrine of <s>satkāryavāda</s> (pre-existence of the effect in the cause) is not the topic at hand, this verse does not pertain to that. For one deluded by ignorance of the true natures of body and self, in order to dispel that delusion, the discrimination of the essential natures of both — destructibility and indestructibility — alone must be stated. That alone is the topic in 'those whose life-breaths have departed and those whose life-breaths have not departed.' And that alone is established subsequently in 'but know that to be indestructible' and 'these bodies have an end.' Therefore, the meaning is as stated.

children.text: atra tu sat-kārya-vādasya aprastutatvān na tat-paro 'yaṃ ślokaḥ; deha-ātma-sva-bhāva-ajñāna-mohitasya tan-moha-śāntaye hy ubhayor nāśitva-anāśitva-rūpa-sva-bhāva-viveka eva vaktavyaḥ / sa eva "gata-asūn agata-asūn" iti ca prastutaḥ / sa eva ca, "avināśi tu tad viddhi", "antavanta ime dehāḥ" iti anantaram upapādyate / ato yathā ukta eva arthaḥ //

body.text: ātmanas tv avināśitvaṃ katham avagamyata ity atrāha --
body.translated_text: To the question 'how is the indestructibility of the self known?' he says:

children.text: ātmanas tv avināśitvaṃ katham avagamyata ity atrā aha ---
avināśi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaṃ tatam |
children.translated_text: 'But know that to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded.' |

children.text: vināśam avyayasyāsya na kaścit kartum arhati ||
children.translated_text: 'No one is able to cause the destruction of this imperishable [self].' ||

children.text: avināśi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaṃ tatam |
vināśam avyayasya asya na kaś-cit kartum arhati ||

body.text: tad atmatattvam avināśīti viddhi, yena ātmatattvena cetanena tadvyatiriktam idam acetanatattvaṃ sarvaṃ tataṃ vyāptam / vyāpakatvena niratiśayasūkṣmatvād ātmano vināśānarhasya tadvyatirikto na kaścit padārtho vināśam kartum arhati, tadvyāpyatayā tasmāt sthūlatvāt / nāśakaṃ hi śastrajalāgnivāyvādikaṃ nāśyaṃ vyāpya śithilīkaroti / mudrādayo 'pi hi vegavat saṃyogena vāyum utpādya taddvāreṇa nāśayanti / ata ātmatattvam avināśi //
body.translated_text: Know that reality of the self to be indestructible — by which reality of the self, being conscious, all this, which is the non-conscious reality distinct from it, is pervaded, is permeated. Because of being the pervader, due to its surpassing subtlety, the self is unfit for destruction — no entity distinct from it is able to cause its destruction, because of being pervaded by it, and hence being grosser than it. For destructive agents such as weapons, water, fire, wind, and the like destroy the destructible by pervading [it] and loosening [it]. Even hammers and the like produce wind through forceful contact and destroy through that medium. Therefore, the reality of the self is indestructible.
