children.text: tad atma-tattvam avināśi iti viddhi, yena ātma-tattvena cetanena tad-vyatiriktam idam acetana-tattvaṃ sarvaṃ tataṃ vyāptam / vyāpakatvena niratiśaya-sūkṣmatvād ātmano vināśa-anarhasya tad-vyatirikto na kaś-cit pada-artho vināśam kartum arhati, tad-vyāpyatayā tasmāt sthūlatvāt / nāśakaṃ hi śastra-jala-agni-vāyv-ādikaṃ nāśyaṃ vyāpya śithilī-karoti / mudrā-ādayo 'pi hi vegavat saṃyogena vāyum utpādya tad-dvāreṇa nāśayanti / ata ātma-tattvam avināśi //

body.text: dehānāṃ tu vināśitvam eva svabhāva ityāha --
body.translated_text: He says that the destructibility of bodies is indeed their essential nature:

children.text: dehānāṃ tu vināśitvam eva sva-bhāva ity-āha ---
antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'These bodies of the eternal embodied one are said to have an end,' |

children.text: anāśino 'prameyasya tasmād yudhyasva bhārata ||
children.translated_text: '[the embodied one who is] indestructible and immeasurable — therefore fight, O <s>Bhārata</s>.' ||

children.text: antavanta ime dehā nityasya uktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ |
anāśino 'prameyasya tasmād yudhyasva bhārata ||

body.text: "diha upacaye" ityupacayarūpā ime dehā antavantaḥ vināśasvabhāvāḥ / upacayātmakā hi ghaṭādayo 'ntavanto dṛṣṭāḥ / nityasya śarīriṇaḥ karmaphalabhogārthatayā bhūtasaṃghātarūpā dehāḥ, "puṇyaḥ puṇyena" ityādiśāstrair uktāḥ karmāvasānavināśinaḥ / ātmā tv avināśī; kutaḥ ? aprameyatvāt / na hy ātmā prameyatayopalabhyate, api tu pramātṛtayā / tathā ca vakṣyate, "etad yo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ" iti / na cānekopacayātmaka ātmopalabhayate, sarvatra dehe "aham idaṃ jānāmi" iti dehasya cānyasya ca pramātṛtayaikarūpeṇopalabdheḥ / na ca dehāder iva pradeśabhede pramātur ākārabheda upalabhyate / ata ekarūpatvena anupacayātmakatvāt pramātṛtvād vyāpakatvāc ca ātmā nityaḥ / dehas tu upacayātmakatvāt, śarīriṇaḥ karmaphalabhogārthatvāt,
body.translated_text: From '<s>diha upacaye</s>' (the root <s>dih</s> meaning 'to grow/accumulate') — these bodies, whose nature is accumulation, have an end — they are of the nature of destruction. For things composed of accumulation, such as pots and the like, are seen to have an end. The bodies, which are aggregates of elements for the purpose of experiencing the fruits of <s>karma</s>, of the eternal embodied one (<s>śarīrin</s>) — as stated by scriptures such as 'the meritorious [obtains a body] through merit' — are destroyed at the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>. But the self is indestructible. Why? Because it is immeasurable (<s>aprameya</s>). For the self is not apprehended as an object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), but rather as the knower (<s>pramātṛ</s>). And it will be stated: 'One who knows this, the knowers call him the field-knower.' Nor is the self apprehended as composed of multiple accumulations, since in every body [there is] the uniform apprehension 'I know this' — the uniform apprehension of the body and of another as the knower. Nor is there any apprehension of a difference of form in the knower corresponding to difference of location, as there is for the body and the like. Therefore, because of being of uniform nature, because of being not composed of accumulation, because of being the knower, and because of being the pervader — the self is eternal.

children.text: "diha upacaye" ity-upacaya-rūpā ime dehā antavantaḥ vināśa-sva-bhāvāḥ / upacaya-ātmakā hi ghaṭa-ādayo 'ntavanto dṛṣṭāḥ / nityasya śarīriṇaḥ karma-phala-bhoga-arthatayā bhūta-saṃghāta-rūpā dehāḥ, "puṇyaḥ puṇyena" ity-ādi-śāstrair uktāḥ karma-avasāna-vināśinaḥ / ātmā tv avināśī; kutaḥ ? aprameyatvāt / na hy ātmā prameyataya ūpalabhyate, api tu pramātṛtayā / tathā ca vakṣyate, "etad yo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetra-jña iti tad-vidaḥ" iti / na ca aneka-upacaya-ātmaka ātma upalabhayate, sarvatra dehe "aham idaṃ jānāmi" iti dehasya ca anyasya ca pramātṛtaya aika-rūpeṇa upalabdheḥ / na ca deha-āder iva pradeśa-bhede pramātur ākāra-bheda upalabhyate / ata eka-rūpatvena anupacaya-ātmakatvāt pramātṛtvād vyāpakatvāc ca ātmā nityaḥ / dehas tu upacaya-ātmakatvāt, śarīriṇaḥ karma-phala-bhoga-arthatvāt,

body.text: anekarūpatvāt, vyāpyatvāc ca vināśī / tasmād dehasya vināśasvabhāvatvād atmano nityatvāc ca ubhayāv api na śokasthānam iti, śastrapātādipuruṣasparśān avarjanīyān svagatān anyagatāṃś ca ghairyeṇa soḍhvā amṛtatvaprāptaye anabhisaṃhitaphalaṃ yuddhākhyaṃ karmārabhasva //
body.translated_text: But the body, because of being composed of accumulation, because of serving the purpose of the embodied one's experience of the fruits of <s>karma</s>, because of being of manifold form, and because of being the pervaded — is destructible. Therefore, since the body is of the nature of destruction and the self is eternal, both are not grounds for grief. Thus, having endured with fortitude the unavoidable contacts of persons [in battle] — the strikes of weapons and the like, both those affecting oneself and those affecting others — undertake the action called battle, without attachment to results, for the attainment of immortality.

children.text: aneka-rūpatvāt, vyāpyatvāc ca vināśī / tasmād dehasya vināśa-sva-bhāvatvād atmano nityatvāc ca ubhayāv api na śoka-sthānam iti, śastra-pāta-ādi-puruṣa-sparśān avarjanīyān sva-gatān anya-gatāṃś ca ghairyeṇa soḍhvā amṛtatva-prāptaye anabhisaṃhita-phalaṃ yuddha-ākhyaṃ karmā arabhasva //
ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaś cainan manyate hatam |
children.translated_text: 'He who thinks this [self] is a slayer, and he who thinks it is slain' — |

children.text: ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate ||
children.translated_text: 'both of them do not understand — this neither slays nor is slain.' ||

children.text: ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaś ca enan manyate hatam |
ubhau tau na vijānīto na ayaṃ hanti na hanyate ||

body.text: enam -- uktasvabhāvam ātmānaṃ prati, hantāraṃ hananahetuṃ kam api yo manyate; yaś cainaṃ kenāpi hetunā hataṃ manyate; tāv ubhau na vijānītaḥ, uktair hetubhir asya nityatvād eva enam ayaṃ na hanti asyāyaṃ hananahetur na bhavati / ata eva cāyam ātmā na hanyate / hantidhātur apy ātmakarmakaḥ śarīraviyogakaraṇavācī / "na hiṃsyāt sarvā bhūtāni", "brāhmaṇo na hantavyaḥ" ityādīny api
body.translated_text: Regarding the self — whose nature has been described — whoever thinks [there is] a slayer, some cause of killing, and whoever thinks it is slain by some cause — those two do not understand. By the reasons stated, since this [self] is eternal, this does not slay it — this is not the cause of its killing. And for this very reason, this self is not slain. The verb <s>han</s> (to kill), even when having the self as its object, denotes causing the separation from the body. [Scriptural injunctions] such as 'one should not harm any beings' and 'a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should not be killed'

children.text: enam --- ukta-sva-bhāvam ātmānaṃ prati, hantāraṃ hanana-hetuṃ kam api yo manyate; yaś ca enaṃ kena api hetunā hataṃ manyate; tāv ubhau na vijānītaḥ, uktair hetubhir asya nityatvād eva enam ayaṃ na hanti asya ayaṃ hanana-hetur na bhavati / ata eva ca ayam ātmā na hanyate / hanti-dhātur apy ātma-karmakaḥ śarīra-viyoga-karaṇa-vācī / "na hiṃsyāt sarvā bhūtāni", "brāhmaṇo na hantavyaḥ" ity-ādīny api

body.text: śāstrāṇi avihitaśarīraviyogakaraṇaviṣayāṇi //
body.translated_text: are also concerned with causing the separation from the body that is not sanctioned [by scripture].

children.text: śāstrāṇi avihita-śarīra-viyoga-karaṇa-viṣayāṇi //
na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'It is never born, nor does it ever die; nor, having once been, will it again cease to be.' |

children.text: ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||
children.translated_text: 'Unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient — it is not slain when the body is slain.' ||

children.text: na jāyate mriyate vā kadā-cin na ayaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ |
ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre ||

body.text: uktair eva hetubhir nityatvenāpariṇāmitvād ātmano jananamaraṇādayaḥ sarva evācetanadehadharmā na santīty ucyate / tatra jāyate, mriyate iti vartamānatayā sarveṣu deheṣu sarvair anubhūyamāne jananamaraṇe kadācid apy ātmānaṃ na spṛśataḥ / nāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ -- ayaṃ kalpādau bhūtvā
body.translated_text: By the very reasons stated, since the self is eternal and does not undergo transformation — birth, death, and all other [changes] that are properties of the non-conscious body do not belong [to the self]. Therein, 'is born' and 'dies' — birth and death, which are experienced by all in all bodies as present [realities], do not touch the self at any time. 'Nor, having once been, will it again cease to be' — this [self], having existed at the beginning of a cosmic cycle (<s>kalpa</s>),

children.text: uktair eva hetubhir nityatvena apariṇāmitvād ātmano janana-maraṇa-ādayaḥ sarva eva acetana-deha-dharmā na santi ity ucyate / tatra jāyate, mriyate iti vartamānatayā sarveṣu deheṣu sarvair anubhūyamāne janana-maraṇe kadā-cid apy ātmānaṃ na spṛśataḥ / na ayaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ --- ayaṃ kalpa-ādau bhūtvā

body.text: bhūyaḥ kalpānte ca na na bhavitā; keṣucit prajāpatiprabhṛtideheṣv āgamenopalabhyamānaṃ kalpādau jananaṃ kalpānte ca maraṇam ātmānaṃ na spṛśatītyarthaḥ / ataḥ sarvadehagata ātmā ajaḥ, ata eva nityaḥ / śāśvataḥ -- prakṛtivadaviśadasatatapariṇāmair api nānvīyate, purāṇaḥ -- purāpi navaḥ;
body.translated_text: will not fail to exist again at the end of the cosmic cycle. The birth at the beginning of the cycle and death at the end of the cycle, which are apprehended through scripture in certain bodies such as those of <s>Prajāpati</s> and the like, do not touch the self — this is the meaning. Therefore, the self present in all bodies is unborn (<s>aja</s>), and for that very reason eternal. Everlasting (<s>śāśvata</s>) — it is not attended by transformations that are continuous and undifferentiated, like <s>Prakṛti</s> (primal nature). Ancient (<s>purāṇa</s>) — though old, it is [ever] new;

children.text: bhūyaḥ kalpa-ante ca na na bhavitā; keṣu-cit prajā-pati-prabhṛti-deheṣv āgamena upalabhyamānaṃ kalpa-ādau jananaṃ kalpa-ante ca maraṇam ātmānaṃ na spṛśati ity-arthaḥ / ataḥ sarva-deha-gata ātmā ajaḥ, ata eva nityaḥ / śāśvataḥ --- prakṛtivad-aviśada-satata-pariṇāmair api na anvīyate, purāṇaḥ --- pura āpi navaḥ;

body.text: sarvadā apūrvavad anubhāvya ityarthaḥ / ataḥ śarīre hanyamāne na hanyate 'yam ātmā //
body.translated_text: meaning it is always to be experienced as if it were unprecedented. Therefore, when the body is slain, this self is not slain.

children.text: sarvadā apūrvavad anubhāvya ity-arthaḥ / ataḥ śarīre hanyamāne na hanyate 'yam ātmā //
vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enam ajam avyayam |
children.translated_text: 'He who knows this [self] to be indestructible, eternal, unborn, and imperishable' — |

children.text: kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam ||
children.translated_text: 'how does that person, O <s>Pārtha</s>, cause anyone to be slain, or slay anyone?' ||

children.text: veda-avināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enam ajam avyayam |
kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam ||

body.text: evam avināśitvenājatvena vyayānarhatvena ca nityam enam ātmānaṃ yaḥ puruṣo veda, sa puruṣo devamanuṣyatiryaksthāvaraśarīrāvasthiteṣv ātmasu kam apy ātmānaṃ kathaṃ ghātayati ? kaṃ vā kathaṃ hanti / kathaṃ nāśayati; kathaṃ vā tatprayojako bhavatītyarthaḥ / etān ātmano ghātayāmi hanmīty anuśocanam ātmasvarūpayāthātmyājñānamūlam evetyabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The person who thus knows this self to be eternal — by virtue of indestructibility, unborn-ness, and unfitness for decay — that person, regarding the selves established in the bodies of gods, humans, animals, and plants — how does he cause any self whatsoever to be slain? Or how does he slay anyone? How does he destroy [anyone]? Or how does he become the instigator of that? — this is the meaning. The intention is that grief in the form of 'I am slaying them, I am killing them' is rooted in nothing but ignorance of the true nature of the self.

children.text: evam avināśitvena ajatvena vyaya-anarhatvena ca nityam enam ātmānaṃ yaḥ puruṣo veda, sa puruṣo deva-manuṣya-tiryak-sthāvara-śarīra-avasthiteṣv ātmasu kam apy ātmānaṃ kathaṃ ghātayati ? kaṃ vā kathaṃ hanti / kathaṃ nāśayati; kathaṃ vā tat-prayojako bhavati ity-arthaḥ / etān ātmano ghātayāmi hanmi ity anuśocanam ātma-sva-rūpa-yāthātmya-ajñāna-mūlam eva ity-abhiprāyaḥ //

body.text: yady api nityānām ātmanāṃ śarīraviśleṣamātraṃ kriyate -- tathāpi ramaṇīyabhogasādhaneṣu śarīreṣu naśyatsu tadviyogarūpaṃ śokanimittam asty evety atrāha --
body.translated_text: Even if for eternal selves, only separation from the body is effected — still, when the bodies, which are the means of delightful enjoyment, perish, the sorrow that consists in the separation from them is indeed a cause of grief — to this he says:

children.text: yady api nityānām ātmanāṃ śarīra-viśleṣa-mātraṃ kriyate --- tatha āpi ramaṇīya-bhoga-sādhaneṣu śarīreṣu naśyatsu tad-viyoga-rūpaṃ śoka-nimittam asty eva ity atrā aha ---
vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi |
children.translated_text: 'Just as a person discards worn-out garments and takes on other new ones,' |

children.text: tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī ||
children.translated_text: 'so the embodied one, discarding worn-out bodies, takes on other new ones.' ||

children.text: vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi |
tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny anyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī ||

body.text: dharmayuddhe śarīraṃ tyajatāṃ tyaktaśarīrād adhikatarakalyāṇaśarīragrahaṇaṃ śāstrād avagamyata iti jīrṇāni vāsāṃsi vihāya navāni kalyāṇāni vāsāṃsi gṛhṇatām iva harṣanimittam evātropalabhyate //
body.translated_text: From scripture it is understood that for those who give up the body in righteous battle (<s>dharmayuddha</s>), there is the acquisition of a body more auspicious than the body that was given up. Thus, just as for those who discard worn-out garments and take on new auspicious garments, here too only a cause for joy is found.

children.text: dharma-yuddhe śarīraṃ tyajatāṃ tyakta-śarīrād adhikatara-kalyāṇa-śarīra-grahaṇaṃ śāstrād avagamyata iti jīrṇāni vāsāṃsi vihāya navāni kalyāṇāni vāsāṃsi gṛhṇatām iva harṣa-nimittam eva atra upalabhyate //

body.text: punar api "avināśi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaṃ tatam" iti pūrvoktam avināśitvaṃ sukhagrahaṇāya vyañjayan draḍhayati --
body.translated_text: Once again, making vivid and reinforcing the indestructibility stated earlier — 'but know that to be indestructible by which all this is pervaded' — for easy comprehension, [he says]:

children.text: punar api "avināśi tu tad viddhi yena sarvam idaṃ tatam" iti pūrva-uktam avināśitvaṃ sukha-grahaṇāya vyañjayan draḍhayati ---
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it,' |

children.text: na cainaṃ kledayanty āpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'water does not wet it, wind does not dry it.' ||

children.text: na enaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi na enaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ |
na ca enaṃ kledayanty āpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ ||
acchedyo 'yam adāhyo 'yam akledyo 'śoṣya eva ca |
children.translated_text: 'It cannot be cut, it cannot be burnt, it cannot be wetted, and it cannot be dried.' |

children.text: nityas sarvagataḥ sthāṇur acalo 'yaṃ sanātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable — this is primeval.' ||

children.text: acchedyo 'yam adāhyo 'yam akledyo 'śoṣya eva ca |
nityas sarva-gataḥ sthāṇur acalo 'yaṃ sanātanaḥ ||

body.text: śastrāgnyambuvāyavaḥ chedanadahanakledanaśoṣaṇāni ātmānaṃ prati kartuṃ na śaknuvanti, sarvagatatvād ātmanaḥ sarvatattvavyāpanasvabhāvatayā sarvebhyas tattvebhyas sūkṣmatvād asya tair vyāptyanarhatvāt; vyāpyakartavyatvāc ca chedanadahanakledanaśoṣaṇānāṃ / ata ātmā nityaḥ sthāṇur acalo 'yaṃ sanātanaḥ sthirasvabhāvo 'prakampyaḥ purātanaś ca //
body.translated_text: Weapons, fire, water, and wind are unable to perform cutting, burning, wetting, and drying upon the self — because the self, being all-pervading, having the nature of pervading all realities, is subtler than all realities, and hence cannot be pervaded by them; and because cutting, burning, wetting, and drying are to be done to what is pervaded. Therefore, the self is eternal, stable (<s>sthāṇu</s>), immovable (<s>acala</s>) — of firm nature, unshakable — and primeval (<s>sanātana</s>), ancient.

children.text: śastra-agny-ambu-vāyavaḥ chedana-dahana-kledana-śoṣaṇāni ātmānaṃ prati kartuṃ na śaknuvanti, sarva-gatatvād ātmanaḥ sarva-tattva-vyāpana-sva-bhāvatayā sarvebhyas tattvebhyas sūkṣmatvād asya tair vyāpty-anarhatvāt; vyāpya-kartavyatvāc ca chedana-dahana-kledana-śoṣaṇānāṃ / ata ātmā nityaḥ sthāṇur acalo 'yaṃ sanātanaḥ sthira-sva-bhāvo 'prakampyaḥ purātanaś ca //
avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yam avikāryo 'yam ucyate |
children.translated_text: 'This is said to be unmanifest, inconceivable, and immutable.' |

children.text: tasmād evaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, knowing it thus, you should not grieve.' ||

children.text: avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yam avikāryo 'yam ucyate |
tasmād evaṃ viditva ainaṃ na anuśocitum arhasi ||

body.text: chedanādiyogyāni vastūni yaiḥ pramāṇair vyajyante; tair ayam ātmā na vyajyata ity avyaktaḥ; ataḥ chedyādivisajātīyaḥ / acintyaś ca sarvavastuvijātīyatvena tattatsvabhāvayuktatayā cintayitum api nārhaḥ; ataś cāvikāryaḥ vikārānarhaḥ / tasmād uktalakṣaṇam enam ātmānaṃ viditvā tatkṛte nānuśocitum arhasi //
body.translated_text: The <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of knowledge) by which things fit for cutting and the like are made manifest — by those, this self is not made manifest, hence it is 'unmanifest' (<s>avyakta</s>). Therefore it is of a different kind from things that are cuttable and the like. And it is 'inconceivable' (<s>acintya</s>) — being of a kind different from all [other] entities, it is not even fit to be thought of as possessing such-and-such a nature. And therefore it is 'immutable' (<s>avikārya</s>) — unfit for modification. Therefore, knowing this self — whose characteristics have been stated — you should not grieve on account of it.

children.text: chedana-ādi-yogyāni vastūni yaiḥ pramāṇair vyajyante; tair ayam ātmā na vyajyata ity avyaktaḥ; ataḥ chedya-ādi-visajātīyaḥ / acintyaś ca sarva-vastu-vijātīyatvena tat-tat-sva-bhāva-yuktatayā cintayitum api na arhaḥ; ataś ca avikāryaḥ vikāra-anarhaḥ / tasmād ukta-lakṣaṇam enam ātmānaṃ viditvā tat-kṛte na anuśocitum arhasi //
atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam |
children.translated_text: 'Even if you think it is eternally born or eternally dying' —

children.text: tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho! naivaṃ śocitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Even so, O mighty-armed one, you should not grieve thus. ||

children.text: atha ca enaṃ nitya-jātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam |
tatha āpi tvaṃ mahābāho! na evaṃ śocitum arhasi ||

body.text: atha nityajātaṃ nityamṛtaṃ deham evainam ātmānaṃ manuṣe, na dehātiriktam uktalakṣaṇam; tathāpi evam atimātraṃ na śocitum arhasi; pariṇāmasvabhāvasya dehasyotpattivināśayor avarjanīyatvāt //
body.translated_text: But if you think that this self is the body itself, which is ever-born and ever-dying, and not [something] distinct from the body having the characteristics stated [above]; even so, you should not grieve so excessively — because for the body, whose nature is transformation, birth and death are unavoidable. //

children.text: atha nitya-jātaṃ nitya-mṛtaṃ deham eva enam ātmānaṃ manuṣe, na deha-atiriktam ukta-lakṣaṇam; tatha āpi evam atimātraṃ na śocitum arhasi; pariṇāma-sva-bhāvasya dehasya utpatti-vināśayor avarjanīyatvāt //
jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca |
children.translated_text: For one who is born, death is certain; and certain is birth for one who has died. |

children.text: tasmād aparihārye 'rthe na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, with regard to what is unavoidable, you should not grieve. ||

children.text: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur dhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca |
tasmād aparihārye 'rthe na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi ||

body.text:
utpannasya vināśo dhruvaḥ avarjanīya upalabhyate; tathā vinaṣṭasyāpi janma avarjanīyam / katham idam upapadyate vinaṣṭasyotpattir iti; sata evotpattyupalabdheḥ, asataś cānupalabdheḥ / utpattivināśādayaḥ sato dravyasyāvasthāviśeṣāḥ / tantuprabhṛtīni hi dravyāṇi santy eva racanāviśeṣayuktāni paṭādīny ucyante / asatkāryavādināpy etāvad evopalabhyate / na hi tatra tantusaṃsthānaviśeṣātirekeṇa dravyāntaraṃ pratīyate / kārakavyāpāranāmāntarabhajanavyavahāraviśeṣāṇām etāvataivopapatteḥ na dravyāntarakalpanā yuktā / ato utpattivināśādayaḥ sato dravyasyāvasthāviśeṣāḥ / utpattyākhyām avasthām upayātasya dravyasya tadvirodhyavasthāntaraprāptir vināśa ity ucyate / mṛddravyasya piṇḍatvaghaṭatvakapālatvacūrṇatvādivat pariṇāmidravyasya pariṇāmaparamparā
avarjanīyā / tatra pūrvāvasthasya dravyasyottarāvasthāprāptir vināśaḥ / saiva tadavasthasya cotpattiḥ / evam utpattivināśākhyapariṇāmaparamparā pariṇāmino dravyasyāparihāryeti na tatra śocitum arhasi //
body.translated_text:
The destruction of that which has been born is observed to be certain, unavoidable; likewise, the birth of that which has been destroyed is unavoidable. How is this tenable — the arising of what has been destroyed? Because arising is observed only of what exists, and non-arising of what does not exist. Birth, destruction, and the like are particular states (<s>avasthāviśeṣa</s>) of an existing substance (<s>dravya</s>). For substances such as threads and the like, existing as they are, when endowed with a particular arrangement (<s>racanāviśeṣa</s>), are called cloth and the like. Even the proponent of the non-existence of the effect [before its production] (<s>asatkāryavādin</s>) observes just this much. For therein, no other substance is cognized beyond the particular configuration of threads. Since the conventions of different names, the operations of causal agents, and particular usages are all accounted for by just this much, the postulation of another substance is not proper. Therefore, birth, destruction, and the like are particular states of an existing substance. The attainment by a substance that has reached the state called 'birth' of another state contrary to that is called 'destruction.' Just as for clay-substance, [there is] the state of a lump, the state of a pot, the state of potsherds, the state of powder, and so forth — so too, for a substance subject to transformation, an unending succession of transformations
is unavoidable. Therein, the attainment by the substance in a prior state of a subsequent state is destruction. And that very [attainment] is the birth of [the substance] in that [subsequent] state. Thus, the unending succession of transformations called birth and destruction is unavoidable for a substance subject to transformation — therefore you should not grieve over it. //

children.text:
utpannasya vināśo dhruvaḥ avarjanīya upalabhyate; tathā vinaṣṭasya api janma avarjanīyam / katham idam upapadyate vinaṣṭasya utpattir iti; sata eva utpatty-upalabdheḥ, asataś ca anupalabdheḥ / utpatti-vināśa-ādayaḥ sato dravyasya avasthā-viśeṣāḥ / tantu-prabhṛtīni hi dravyāṇi santy eva racana-aviśeṣa-yuktāni paṭa-ādīny ucyante / asat-kārya-vādina āpy etāvad eva upalabhyate / na hi tatra tantu-saṃsthāna-viśeṣa-atirekeṇa dravya-antaraṃ pratīyate / kāraka-vyāpāra-nāma-antara-bhajana-vyavahāra-viśeṣāṇām etāvata aiva upapatteḥ na dravya-antara-kalpanā yuktā / ato utpatti-vināśa-ādayaḥ sato dravyasya avasthā-viśeṣāḥ / utpatty-ākhyām avasthām upayātasya dravyasya tad-virodhy-avasthā-antara-prāptir vināśa ity ucyate / mṛd-dravyasya piṇḍatva-ghaṭatva-kapālatva-cūrṇatva-ādivat pariṇāmi-dravyasya pariṇāma-paramparā
avarjanīyā / tatra pūrva-avasthasya dravyasya uttara-avasthā-prāptir vināśaḥ / sa aiva tad-avasthasya ca utpattiḥ / evam utpatti-vināśa-ākhya-pariṇāma-paramparā pariṇāmino dravyasya aparihārya īti na tatra śocitum arhasi //

body.text: sato dravyasya pūrvāvasthāvirodhyavasthāntaraprāptidarśanena yo 'lpīyān śokaḥ, so 'pi manuṣyādibhūteṣu na saṃbhavatīty āha --
body.translated_text: Showing that even the slight grief [arising] from seeing that an existing substance attains another state contrary to its prior state is not warranted with respect to beings such as humans and the like, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] says:

children.text: sato dravyasya pūrva-avasthā-virodhy-avasthā-antara-prāpti-darśanena yo 'lpīyān śokaḥ, so 'pi manuṣya-ādi-bhūteṣu na saṃbhavati ity āha ---
avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata |
children.translated_text: Beings are unmanifest in their beginnings, manifest in their middles, O <s>Bhārata</s>, |

children.text: avyaktanidhanāny eva tatra kā paridevanā ||
children.translated_text: and unmanifest again in their ends — so what cause is there for lamentation? ||

children.text: avyakta-ādīni bhūtāni vyakta-madhyāni bhārata |
avyakta-nidhanāny eva tatra kā paridevanā ||

body.text: manuṣyādīni bhūtāni santy eva dravyāṇi anupalabdhapūrvāvasthāni upalabdhamanuṣyatvādimadhyamāvasthāni anupalabdhottarāvasthāni sveṣu svabhāveṣu vartanta iti na tatra paridevanānimittam asti //
body.translated_text: Beings such as humans and the like — which are indeed existing substances — having a prior state that is not perceived, having a middle state of human-hood and the like that is perceived, and having a subsequent state that is not perceived — they abide in their own natures. Therefore, there is no cause for lamentation therein. //

children.text: manuṣya-ādīni bhūtāni santy eva dravyāṇi anupalabdha-pūrva-avasthāni upalabdha-manuṣyatva-ādi-madhyama-avasthāni anupalabdha-uttara-avasthāni sveṣu sva-bhāveṣu vartanta iti na tatra paridevanā-nimittam asti //

body.text: evaṃ śarīrātmavāde 'pi nāsti śokanimittam ity uktvā śarīrātirikte āścaryasvarūpe ātmani draṣṭā vaktā śravaṇāyattātmaniścayaś ca durlabha ity āha --
body.translated_text: Having thus said that even on the view that the self is the body, there is no cause for grief, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] says that one who sees, one who speaks about, and one whose ascertainment of the self depends on hearing about the self — which is distinct from the body and marvelous in nature — are all rare:

children.text: evaṃ śarīra-ātma-vāde 'pi na asti śoka-nimittam ity uktvā śarīra-atirikte āścarya-sva-rūpe ātmani draṣṭā vaktā śravaṇa-āyatta-ātma-niścayaś ca durlabha ity āha ---
āścaryavat paśyati kaścid enam āścaryavad vadati tathaiva cānyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Someone sees this [self] as a wonder; likewise another speaks of it as a wonder; |

children.text: āścaryavac cainam anyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvāpy enaṃ veda na caiva kaścit ||
children.translated_text: and yet another hears of it as a wonder; but even having heard, no one truly knows it. ||

children.text: āścaryavat paśyati kaś-cid enam āścaryavad vadati tatha aiva ca anyaḥ |
āścaryavac ca enam anyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutva āpy enaṃ veda na ca eva kaś-cit ||

body.text: evam uktasvabhāvaṃ svetarasamastavastuvisajātīyatayā āścaryavad asthitam ananteṣu jantuṣu mahatā tapasā kṣīṇapāpaḥ upacitapuṇyaḥ kaścit paśyati / tathāvidhaḥ kaścit parasmai vadati / evaṃ kaścid eva śṛṇoti / śrutvāpy enaṃ yathāvad avasthitaṃ tattvato na kaścid veda / cakārād draṣṭṛvaktṛśrotṛṣv api tattvato darśanaṃ tattvato vacanaṃ tattvataś śravaṇaṃ durlabham ityuktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: This [self], having the nature described above, standing like a wonder because it is utterly unlike all other things — among countless beings, someone whose sins have been destroyed and whose merit has been accumulated through great austerity sees it. Likewise, someone of such [attainment] speaks of it to another. Similarly, someone alone hears [of it]. But even having heard, no one truly knows it as it actually is. By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), it is implied that even among those who see, speak, and hear, seeing it in its true nature, speaking of it in its true nature, and hearing of it in its true nature are rare. //

children.text: evam ukta-sva-bhāvaṃ sva-itara-samasta-vastu-visajātīyatayā āścaryavad asthitam ananteṣu jantuṣu mahatā tapasā kṣīṇa-pāpaḥ upacita-puṇyaḥ kaś-cit paśyati / tathā-vidhaḥ kaś-cit parasmai vadati / evaṃ kaś-cid eva śṛṇoti / śrutva āpy enaṃ yathāvad avasthitaṃ tattvato na kaś-cid veda / ca-kārād draṣṭṛ-vaktṛ-śrotṛṣv api tattvato darśanaṃ tattvato vacanaṃ tattvataś śravaṇaṃ durlabham ity-uktaṃ bhavati //
dehī nityam avadhyo 'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata |
children.translated_text: The embodied [self] in the body of every [being] is eternal and indestructible, O <s>Bhārata</s>. |

children.text: tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, you should not grieve for any beings. ||

children.text: dehī nityam avadhyo 'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata |
tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi ||

body.text: sarvasya devādidehino dehe vadhyamāne 'py ayaṃ dehī nityam avadhyo mantavyaḥ / tasmāt sarvāṇi devādisthāvarāntāni bhūtāni viṣamākārāṇy apy uktena svabhāvena svarūpatas samānāni nityāni ca / dehagataṃ tu vaiṣamyam anityatvaṃ ca / tato devādīni sarvāṇi bhūtāny uddiśya na śocitum arhasi; na kevalaṃ bhīṣmādīn prati //
body.translated_text: Even when the body of every embodied being — from gods and the like — is being destroyed, this embodied self should be considered eternal and indestructible. Therefore, all beings — from gods down to immovable things — though diverse in form, are identical in their essential nature as described, and are eternal. But the diversity and impermanence pertain to the body. Therefore, you should not grieve regarding all beings — gods and the like — not merely regarding <s>Bhīṣma</s> and the like. //

children.text: sarvasya deva-ādi-dehino dehe vadhyamāne 'py ayaṃ dehī nityam avadhyo mantavyaḥ / tasmāt sarvāṇi deva-ādi-sthāvara-antāni bhūtāni viṣama-ākārāṇy apy uktena sva-bhāvena sva-rūpatas samānāni nityāni ca / deha-gataṃ tu vaiṣamyam anityatvaṃ ca / tato deva-ādīni sarvāṇi bhūtāny uddiśya na śocitum arhasi; na kevalaṃ bhīṣma-ādīn prati //
svadharmam api cāvekṣya na vikampitum arhasi |
children.translated_text: And considering your own <s>dharma</s> too, you should not waver. |

children.text: dharmyād dhi yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: For a <s>kṣatriya</s>, there is nothing better than a righteous battle. ||

children.text: sva-dharmam api ca avekṣya na vikampitum arhasi |
dharmyād dhi yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat kṣatriyasya na vidyate ||

body.text: api cedaṃ prārabdhaṃ yuddhaṃ prāṇimāraṇam api agnīṣomīyādivat svadharmam avekṣya na vikampitum arhasi / dharmyān nyāyataḥ pravṛttād yuddhād anyan na hi kṣatriyasya śreyo vidyate / "śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpy apalāyanam / dānam īśvarabhāvaś ca kṣātraṃ karma svabhāvajam // " iti hi vakṣyate / agnīṣomīyādiṣu ca na hiṃsā paśoḥ, nihīnataracchāgādidehaparityāgapūrvaka
body.translated_text: Even if this commenced battle involves the killing of living beings, you should not waver, considering [it as] your own <s>dharma</s>, like the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> [sacrifice] and the like. For a <s>kṣatriya</s>, there is nothing better than a battle undertaken righteously, in accordance with justice. For it will be said: 'Valor, splendor, firmness, skill, and also not fleeing in battle, generosity, and lordliness — these are the natural duties of a <s>kṣatriya</s>.' And in [sacrifices like] the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> and the like, there is no [real] harm to the animal, because the scripture declares that the ritual slaying is a means of granting the animal a superior body, heaven, and the like, preceded by the relinquishing of an inferior body such as that of a goat and the like.

children.text: api ca idaṃ prārabdhaṃ yuddhaṃ prāṇi-māraṇam api agnīṣomīya-ādivat sva-dharmam avekṣya na vikampitum arhasi / dharmyān nyāyataḥ pravṛttād yuddhād anyan na hi kṣatriyasya śreyo vidyate / "śauryaṃ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṃ yuddhe ca apy apalāyanam / dānam īśvara-bhāvaś ca kṣātraṃ karma sva-bhāva-jam // " iti hi vakṣyate / agnīṣomīya-ādiṣu ca na hiṃsā paśoḥ, nihīnatara-cchāga-ādi-deha-parityāga-pūrvaka-

body.text: kalyāṇataradehasvargādiprāpakatvaśruteḥ saṃjñapanasya / "na vā u etan mriyase na riṣyasi devāṃ ideṣi pathibhis surebhiḥ / yatra yanti sukṛto nāpi duṣkṛtaḥ tatra tvā devas savitā dadhātu" iti hi śrūyate / iha ca yuddhe mṛtānāṃ kalyāṇataradehaprāptir uktā, "vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti" ityādinā / ataḥ, cikitsakaśalyādikarma āturasyeva, asya rakṣaṇam evāgnīṣomīyādiṣu saṃjñapanam //
body.translated_text: For it is heard [in the Veda]: 'You do not die thereby, nor are you harmed; you go to the gods by auspicious paths. Where the virtuous go, not the wicked — there may the god <s>Savitṛ</s> place you.' And here too, the attainment of a superior body for those who die in battle has been stated: 'Just as one casts off worn-out garments and takes new ones' and so forth. Therefore, just as the work of a physician or surgeon is for the welfare of the patient, so too the ritual slaying in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> and the like is for the protection [of the animal]. //

children.text: kalyāṇatara-deha-svarga-ādi-prāpakatva-śruteḥ saṃjñapanasya / "na vā u etan mriyase na riṣyasi devāṃ ideṣi pathibhis surebhiḥ / yatra yanti sukṛto na api duṣkṛtaḥ tatra tvā devas savitā dadhātu" iti hi śrūyate / iha ca yuddhe mṛtānāṃ kalyāṇatara-deha-prāptir uktā, "vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti" ity-ādinā / ataḥ, cikitsaka-śalya-ādi-karma āturasya iva, asya rakṣaṇam eva agnīṣomīya-ādiṣu saṃjñapanam //
yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāram apāvṛtam |
children.translated_text: And [a battle] that comes of its own accord is an open gate to heaven. |

children.text: sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛśam ||
children.translated_text: Fortunate <s>kṣatriyas</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, obtain such a battle. ||

children.text: yad-ṛcchayā ca upapannaṃ svarga-dvāram apāvṛtam |
sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddham īdṛśam ||

body.text: ayatnopanatam idaṃ niratiśayasukhopāyabhūtaṃ nirvighnam īdṛśaṃ yuddhaṃ sukhinaḥ puṇyavantaḥ kṣatriyā labhante //
body.translated_text: This battle, which has come without effort, which is a means to unsurpassed happiness, and which is unobstructed — fortunate, i.e., meritorious <s>kṣatriyas</s> obtain such [a battle]. //

children.text: ayatna-upanatam idaṃ niratiśaya-sukha-upāya-bhūtaṃ nirvighnam īdṛśaṃ yuddhaṃ sukhinaḥ puṇyavantaḥ kṣatriyā labhante //
atha cet tvam imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi |
children.translated_text: But if you will not undertake this righteous battle, |

children.text: tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi ||
children.translated_text: then, forsaking your own <s>dharma</s> and fame, you will incur sin. ||

children.text: atha cet tvam imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi |
tataḥ sva-dharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpam avāpsyasi ||

body.text: atha kṣatriyasya svadharmabhūtam imam -- ārabdhaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ mohān na kariṣyasi cet -- tataḥ prārabdhasya dharmasyākaraṇāt svadharmaphalaṃ niratiśayasukham, vijayena niratiśayāṃ ca kīrtiṃ hitvā pāpaṃ niratiśayam avāpsyasi //
body.translated_text: But if, out of delusion, you will not undertake this — a battle that is the natural <s>dharma</s> of a <s>kṣatriya</s> — which has [already] been commenced — then, from the non-performance of a <s>dharma</s> [already] commenced, you will forsake the fruit of your own <s>dharma</s> — unsurpassed happiness — and through victory, unsurpassed fame as well, and you will incur unsurpassed sin. //

children.text: atha kṣatriyasya sva-dharma-bhūtam imam --- ārabdhaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ mohān na kariṣyasi cet --- tataḥ prārabdhasya dharmasya akaraṇāt sva-dharma-phalaṃ niratiśaya-sukham, vijayena niratiśayāṃ ca kīrtiṃ hitvā pāpaṃ niratiśayam avāpsyasi //
akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te 'vyayām |
children.translated_text: And beings will speak of your everlasting infamy; |

children.text: saṃbhāvitasya cākīrtiḥ maraṇād atiricyate ||
children.translated_text: and for one who has been honored, infamy is worse than death. ||

children.text: akīrtiṃ ca api bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te 'vyayām |
saṃbhāvitasya ca akīrtiḥ maraṇād atiricyate ||

body.text: na te kevalaṃ niratiśayasukhakīrtihānimātram / "pārtho yuddhe prārabdhe palāyitaḥ" iti avyayāṃ sarvadeśakālavyāpinīm akīrtiṃ ca samarthāni asamarthāny api sarvāṇi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti / tataḥ kim iti cet -- śairyavīryaparākramādibhis sarvasaṃbhāvitasya tadviparyayajā hy akīrtiḥ maraṇād atiricyate / evaṃvidhāyā akīrter maraṇam eva tava śreya ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: It is not merely the loss of unsurpassed happiness and fame for you. All beings, capable and incapable alike, will speak of your everlasting infamy — pervading all places and times — [saying:] '<s>Pārtha</s> fled when the battle had commenced.' And if [you ask] what of it? — for one who has been honored by all for valor, heroism, prowess, and the like, infamy born of the opposite of those is worse than death. The meaning is: for such infamy, death itself would be better for you. //

children.text: na te kevalaṃ niratiśaya-sukha-kīrti-hāni-mātram / "pārtho yuddhe prārabdhe palāyitaḥ" iti avyayāṃ sarva-deśa-kāla-vyāpinīm akīrtiṃ ca samarthāni asamarthāny api sarvāṇi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti / tataḥ kim iti cet --- śairya-vīrya-parākrama-ādibhis sarva-saṃbhāvitasya tad-viparyaya-jā hy akīrtiḥ maraṇād atiricyate / evaṃ-vidhāyā akīrter maraṇam eva tava śreya ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: bandhusnehāt kāruṇyāc ca yuddhān nivṛttasya śūrasya mamākīrtiḥ katham āgamiṣyatīty atrāha --
body.translated_text: To the [possible objection] — 'how can infamy come to a hero who has withdrawn from battle out of affection for kinsmen and compassion?' — to this [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] says:

children.text: bandhu-snehāt kāruṇyāc ca yuddhān nivṛttasya śūrasya mama akīrtiḥ katham āgamiṣyati ity atrā aha ---
bhayād raṇād uparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ |
children.translated_text: The great chariot-warriors will think that you withdrew from battle out of fear. |

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi laughavam ||
children.translated_text: And you, having been held in high esteem by them, will come to be lightly regarded. ||

children.text: bhayād raṇād uparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahā-rathāḥ |
yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahu-mato bhūtvā yāsyasi laughavam ||

body.text: yeṣāṃ karṇaduryodhanādīnāṃ mahārathānām itaḥ pūrvaṃ tvaṃ śūro vairīti bahumato bhūtvā, idānīṃ yuddhe samupasthite nivṛttavyāpāratayā lāghavaṃ -- sugrahatāṃ yāsyasi, te mahārathās tvāṃ bhayād yuddhād uparataṃ maṃsyante / śūrāṇāṃ hi vairiṇāṃ śatrubhayād rte bandhusnehādinā yuddhād uparatir nopapadyate //
body.translated_text: You, who were previously held in high esteem by those great chariot-warriors — <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Duryodhana</s>, and the like — as a hero and a foe, will now, when the battle has arrived, come to be lightly regarded — easily conquerable — because of your cessation of activity. Those great warriors will think that you withdrew from battle out of fear. For heroes and enemies do not withdraw from battle for reasons of affection for kinsmen and the like, except out of fear of the enemy. //

children.text: yeṣāṃ karṇa-duryodhana-ādīnāṃ mahā-rathānām itaḥ pūrvaṃ tvaṃ śūro vairi īti bahu-mato bhūtvā, idānīṃ yuddhe samupasthite nivṛtta-vyāpāratayā lāghavaṃ --- sugrahatāṃ yāsyasi, te mahā-rathās tvāṃ bhayād yuddhād uparataṃ maṃsyante / śūrāṇāṃ hi vairiṇāṃ śatru-bhayād rte bandhu-sneha-ādinā yuddhād uparatir na upapadyate //

body.text: kiṃ ca,
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: kiṃ ca,
avācyavādāṃś ca bahūn vadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ |
children.translated_text: And your enemies will speak many unspeakable words, |

children.text: nindantas tava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim ||
children.translated_text: disparaging your ability — what could be more painful than that? ||

children.text: avācya-vādāṃś ca bahūn vadiṣyanti tava ahitāḥ |
nindantas tava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim ||

body.text: śūrāṇāṃ asmākaṃ sannidhau katham ayaṃ pārthaḥ kṣaṇam api sthātuṃ śaknuyāt, asmatsannidhānād anyatra hy asya sāmarthyam iti tava sāmarthyaṃ nindantaḥ śūrāṇām avācyavādāṃś ca bahūn vadiṣyanti tava śatravo dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ; tato 'dhikataraṃ duḥkhaṃ kiṃ tava ? evaṃvidhāvācyaśravaṇān maraṇam eva śreya iti tvam eva maṃsyase //
body.translated_text: 'How could this <s>Pārtha</s> stand even a moment in our presence? For his ability is [effective] only elsewhere, away from our presence' — thus disparaging your ability, your enemies, the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, being heroes, will speak many words unspeakable [among warriors]. What greater suffering could there be for you than that? You yourself will consider that death is better than hearing such unspeakable [words]. //

children.text: śūrāṇāṃ asmākaṃ sannidhau katham ayaṃ pārthaḥ kṣaṇam api sthātuṃ śaknuyāt, asmat-sannidhānād anyatra hy asya sāmarthyam iti tava sāmarthyaṃ nindantaḥ śūrāṇām avācya-vādāṃś ca bahūn vadiṣyanti tava śatravo dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ; tato 'dhikataraṃ duḥkhaṃ kiṃ tava ? evaṃ-vidha-avācya-śravaṇān maraṇam eva śreya iti tvam eva maṃsyase //

body.text: ataḥ śūrasya ātmanā pareṣāṃ hananam, ātmano vā parair hananam ubhayam api śreyase bhavatīty āha --
body.translated_text: Therefore, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] says that for a hero, both killing others by oneself and being killed by others are conducive to the highest good:

children.text: ataḥ śūrasya ātmanā pareṣāṃ hananam, ātmano vā parair hananam ubhayam api śreyase bhavati ity āha ---
hato vā prāpsyase svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm |
children.translated_text: Slain, you will attain heaven; or victorious, you will enjoy the earth. |

children.text: tasmād uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, arise, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, resolved for battle. ||

children.text: hato vā prāpsyase svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm |
tasmād uttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛta-niścayaḥ ||

body.text: dharmayuddhe parair hataś cet, tata eva paramaniḥśreyasaṃ prāpsyasi; parān vā hatvā akaṇṭakaṃ rājyaṃ bhokṣyase; anabhisaṃhitaphalasya yuddhākhyasya dharmasya paramaniḥśreyasopāyatvāt tac ca paramaniḥśreyasaṃ prāpsyasi; tasmād yuddhāyodyogaḥ paramapuruṣārthalakṣaṇamokṣasādhanam iti niścitya tadartham uttiṣṭha / kuntīputrasya tavaitad eva yuktam ityabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: If slain in a righteous battle by others, you will attain the supreme good (<s>paramaniḥśreyasa</s>) from that very [death]. Or, having slain the others, you will enjoy an unobstructed kingdom. And since battle — when its fruit is not [selfishly] intended — as a <s>dharma</s> called 'war' is a means to the supreme good, you will also attain that supreme good. Therefore, resolve that exertion for battle is a means to liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) — the supreme goal of human life — and arise for that purpose. The implication is: this alone is fitting for you, the son of <s>Kuntī</s>. //

children.text: dharma-yuddhe parair hataś cet, tata eva parama-niḥśreyasaṃ prāpsyasi; parān vā hatvā akaṇṭakaṃ rājyaṃ bhokṣyase; anabhisaṃhita-phalasya yuddha-ākhyasya dharmasya parama-niḥśreyasa-upāyatvāt tac ca parama-niḥśreyasaṃ prāpsyasi; tasmād yuddhāya udyogaḥ parama-puruṣa-artha-lakṣaṇa-mokṣa-sādhanam iti niścitya tad-artham uttiṣṭha / kuntī-putrasya tava etad eva yuktam ity-abhiprāyaḥ //

body.text: mumukṣor yuddhānuṣṭhānaprakāram āha --
body.translated_text: He states the manner of performing battle for one who seeks liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>):

children.text: mumukṣor yuddha-anuṣṭhāna-prakāram āha ---
sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau |
children.translated_text: Treating alike pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, |

children.text: tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpam avāpsyasi ||
children.translated_text: then engage in battle — thus you will not incur sin. ||

children.text: sukha-duḥkhe same kṛtvā lābha-alābhau jaya-ajayau |
tato yuddhāya yujyasva na evaṃ pāpam avāpsyasi ||

body.text: evaṃ dehātiriktam aspṛṣṭasamastadehasvabhāvaṃ nityam ātmānaṃ jñātvā yuddhe cāvarjanīyaśastrapātādinimittasukhaduḥkhārthalābhālābhajayaparājayeṣv avikṛtabuddhiḥ svargādiphalābhisandhirahitaḥ kevalakāryabuddhyā yuddham ārabhasva / evaṃ kurvāṇo na pāpam avāpsyasi -- pāpaṃ duḥkharūpaṃ saṃsāraṃ nāvāpsyasi; saṃsārabandhān mokṣyase ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Having thus known the self — which is distinct from the body, untouched by the nature of any body, and eternal — and with an undisturbed mind regarding pleasure and pain caused by unavoidable blows of weapons and the like in battle, gains and losses of wealth, and victory and defeat — free from the desire for fruits such as heaven and the like — undertake battle with the mere understanding of duty. Acting thus, you will not incur sin — you will not incur <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is of the nature of suffering; you will be freed from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is the meaning. //

children.text: evaṃ deha-atiriktam aspṛṣṭa-samasta-deha-sva-bhāvaṃ nityam ātmānaṃ jñātvā yuddhe ca avarjanīya-śastra-pāta-ādi-nimitta-sukha-duḥkha-artha-lābha-alābha-jaya-parā-jayeṣv avikṛta-buddhiḥ svarga-ādi-phala-abhisandhi-rahitaḥ kevala-kārya-buddhyā yuddham ārabhasva / evaṃ kurvāṇo na pāpam avāpsyasi --- pāpaṃ duḥkha-rūpaṃ saṃsāraṃ na avāpsyasi; saṃsāra-bandhān mokṣyase ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: evam ātmayāthātmyajñānam upadiśya tatpūrvakaṃ mokṣasādhanabhūtaṃ karmayogaṃ vaktum ārabhate --
body.translated_text: Having thus taught the true knowledge of the self, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] begins to state <s>karmayoga</s> — the discipline of action — which is a means to liberation preceded by that [knowledge]:

children.text: evam ātma-yāthātmya-jñānam upadiśya tat-pūrvakaṃ mokṣa-sādhana-bhūtaṃ karma-yogaṃ vaktum ārabhate ---
eṣā te 'bhihitā sāṅkhye buddhir yoge tv imāṃ śṛṇu |
children.translated_text: This understanding has been declared to you according to <s>Sāṅkhya</s>; now hear it according to <s>Yoga</s>. |

children.text: buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi ||
children.translated_text: Endowed with which understanding, O <s>Pārtha</s>, you will cast off the bondage of <s>karma</s>. ||

children.text: eṣā te 'bhihitā sāṅkhye buddhir yoge tv imāṃ śṛṇu |
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karma-bandhaṃ prahāsyasi ||

body.text: saṅkhyā buddhiḥ; buddhyāvadhāraṇīyam ātmatattvaṃ sāṅkhyam / jñātavye ātmatattve tajjñānāya yā buddhir abhidheyā -- "na tv evāham" ity ārabhya "tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi" ityantena saiṣā te 'bhihitā / ātmajñānapūrvakamokṣasādhanabhūtakarmānuṣṭhāne yo buddhiyogo vaktavyaḥ, sa iha yogaśabdenocyate / "dūreṇa hy avaraṃ karma buddhiyogāt" iti hi vakṣyate / tatra yoge yā buddhir vaktavyā, tām imām abhidhīyamānāṃ śṛṇu, yayā buddhyā yuktaḥ karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi / karmaṇā bandhaḥ karmabandhaḥ; saṃsārabandha ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Saṅkhyā</s> means 'understanding' (<s>buddhi</s>); that which is to be ascertained by the understanding — the true nature of the self — is <s>sāṅkhya</s>. Regarding the self as the object to be known, the understanding that is to be stated for knowing it — that which was declared from 'But I have never not existed' up to 'therefore you should not grieve for any beings' — this is what has been declared to you. The <s>buddhiyoga</s> — the discipline of understanding — which is to be stated regarding the performance of action that is a means to liberation preceded by knowledge of the self — that is here referred to by the word <s>yoga</s>. For it will be said: 'Action is far inferior to the discipline of understanding.' Now hear this understanding that is to be stated regarding <s>yoga</s> — this [understanding] that is being declared. Endowed with which understanding, you will cast off the bondage of <s>karma</s>. Bondage by <s>karma</s> is <s>karmabandha</s>; the meaning is the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. //

children.text: saṅkhyā buddhiḥ; buddhya āvadhāraṇīyam ātma-tattvaṃ sāṅkhyam / jñātavye ātma-tattve taj-jñānāya yā buddhir abhidheyā --- "na tv eva aham" ity ārabhya "tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi" ity-antena sa aiṣā te 'bhihitā / ātma-jñāna-pūrvaka-mokṣa-sādhana-bhūta-karma-anuṣṭhāne yo buddhi-yogo vaktavyaḥ, sa iha yoga-śabdena ucyate / "dūreṇa hy avaraṃ karma buddhi-yogāt" iti hi vakṣyate / tatra yoge yā buddhir vaktavyā, tām imām abhidhīyamānāṃ śṛṇu, yayā buddhyā yuktaḥ karma-bandhaṃ prahāsyasi / karmaṇā bandhaḥ karma-bandhaḥ; saṃsāra-bandha ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: vakṣyamāṇabuddhiyuktasya karmaṇo māhātmyam āha --
body.translated_text: [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] states the greatness of action endowed with the understanding to be described:

children.text: vakṣyamāṇa-buddhi-yuktasya karmaṇo māhātmyam āha ---
nehābhikramanāśo 'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate |
children.translated_text: In this [path], there is no loss of the undertaking, nor is there any adverse consequence. |

children.text: svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt ||
children.translated_text: Even a little of this <s>dharma</s> protects from great fear. ||

children.text: na iha abhikrama-nāśo 'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate |
sv-alpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt ||

body.text: iha karmayoge nābhikramanāśo 'sti / abhikramaḥ -- ārambhaḥ / nāśaḥ phalasādhanabhāvanāśaḥ / ārabdhasyāsamāptasya vicchinnasyāpi na niṣphalatvam /ārabdhasya vicchede pratyavāyo 'pi na vidyate / asya karmayogākhyasya dharmasya svalpāṃśo 'pi mahato bhayāt -- saṃsārabhayāt trāyate / ayam arthaḥ; "pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśas tasya vidyate" iti uttaratra prapañcayiṣyate / anyāni hi laukikāni vaidikāni ca sādhanāni vicchinnāni na phalāya bhavanti; pratyavāyāya ca bhavanti //
body.translated_text: In this <s>karmayoga</s>, there is no loss of the undertaking. Undertaking means commencement. Loss means the destruction of its status as a means to the fruit. Even when what has been commenced is not completed and is interrupted, it does not become fruitless. And when what has been commenced is interrupted, there is no adverse consequence either. Even a small portion of this <s>dharma</s> called <s>karmayoga</s> protects from great fear — from the fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>. This is the meaning: 'For him, O <s>Pārtha</s>, there is no destruction either here or hereafter' — this will be elaborated upon later. For other means — whether worldly or Vedic — when interrupted, do not lead to their fruit; and they lead to adverse consequences. //

children.text: iha karma-yoge na abhikrama-nāśo 'sti / abhikramaḥ --- ārambhaḥ / nāśaḥ phala-sādhana-bhāva-nāśaḥ / ārabdhasya asamāptasya vicchinnasya api na niṣphalatvam /ārabdhasya vicchede pratyavāyo 'pi na vidyate / asya karma-yoga-ākhyasya dharmasya sv-alpa-aṃśo 'pi mahato bhayāt --- saṃsāra-bhayāt trāyate / ayam arthaḥ; "pārtha na eva iha na amutra vināśas tasya vidyate" iti uttaratra prapañcayiṣyate / anyāni hi laukikāni vaidikāni ca sādhanāni vicchinnāni na phalāya bhavanti; pratyavāyāya ca bhavanti //

body.text: kāmyakarmaviṣayāyā buddher mokṣasādhanabhūtakarmaviṣayāṃ buddhiṃ viśinaṣṭi --
body.translated_text: He distinguishes the <s>buddhi</s> (understanding) directed toward action that is the means of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) from the <s>buddhi</s> directed toward desire-motivated action (<s>kāmyakarma</s>) —

children.text: kāmya-karma-viṣayāyā buddher mokṣa-sādhana-bhūta-karma-viṣayāṃ buddhiṃ viśinaṣṭi ---
vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekeha kurunandana |
children.translated_text: The <s>buddhi</s> that is of the nature of determination is one alone here, O son of <s>Kuru</s>;

children.text: bahuśākhā hy anantāś ca buddhayo 'vyavasāyinām ||
children.translated_text: But the <s>buddhis</s> of the irresolute are many-branched and endless. ||

children.text: vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhir eka īha kuru-nandana |
bahu-śākhā hy anantāś ca buddhayo 'vyavasāyinām ||

body.text:
iha -- śāstrīye sarvasmin karmaṇi vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekā / mumukṣuṇānuṣṭheye karmaṇi buddhir vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ / vyavasāyaḥ niścayaḥ / sā hi buddhir ātmayāthātmyaniścayapūrvikā /
kāmyakarmaviṣayā tu buddhir avyavasāyātmikā / tatra hi kāmādhikāre dehātiriktātmāstitvajñānamātram apekṣitam, nātmasvarūpayāthātmyaniścayaḥ / svarūpayāthātmyāniścaye 'pi svargādiphalārthitvatatsādhanānuṣṭhānatatphalānubhavānāṃ saṃbhavāt, avirodhāc ca / seyaṃ vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ ekaphalasādhanaviṣayatayaikā; ekasmai mokṣākhyaphalāya hi mumukṣoḥ sarvāṇi karmāṇi vidhīyante / ataḥ śāstrārthasyaikatvāt sarvakarmaviṣayā buddhir ekaiva; yathaikaphalasādhanatayā āgneyādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ setikartavyatākānām ekaśāstrārthatayā tadviṣayā buddhir ekā, tadvad ityarthaḥ / avyavasāyināṃ tu svargaputrapaśvannādiphalasādhanakarmādhikṛtānāṃ buddhayaḥ phalānantyād anantāḥ / tatrāpi bahuśākhāḥ;
body.translated_text: 'Here' — in all action pertaining to scripture, the <s>buddhi</s> that is of the nature of determination is one. The <s>buddhi</s> regarding action to be performed by one who desires liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>) is the <s>buddhi</s> of determination. Determination means firm resolve. For that <s>buddhi</s> is preceded by the ascertainment of the true nature of the self (<s>ātman</s>). But the <s>buddhi</s> directed toward desire-motivated action is of the nature of non-determination. For in the domain of desire, only the mere knowledge that the self exists beyond the body is required, not the ascertainment of the true nature of the self's essential form. Because even without the ascertainment of the true nature of one's essential form, the desire for fruits such as heaven and the like, the performance of the means thereto, and the experience of those fruits are possible and not contradictory. This <s>buddhi</s> of determination is one, because its object is the means to a single fruit; for all actions are enjoined for one who desires liberation for the single fruit called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). Therefore, because the meaning of scripture is one, the <s>buddhi</s> directed toward all actions is one alone — just as the <s>buddhi</s> directed toward the six [rites] beginning with the <s>Āgneya</s> offering, together with their accessories, is one because they have a single scriptural meaning as means to a single fruit — such is the meaning. But for those of non-determination — those who are engaged in actions that are means to fruits such as heaven, sons, cattle, food, and the like — the <s>buddhis</s> are endless because the fruits are endless. And therein too, they are many-branched;

children.text:
iha --- śāstrīye sarvasmin karmaṇi vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhir ekā / mumukṣuṇa ānuṣṭheye karmaṇi buddhir vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhiḥ / vyavasāyaḥ niścayaḥ / sā hi buddhir ātma-yāthātmya-niścaya-pūrvikā /
kāmya-karma-viṣayā tu buddhir avyavasāya-ātmikā / tatra hi kāma-adhikāre deha-atirikta-ātma-astitva-jñāna-mātram apekṣitam, nā atma-sva-rūpa-yāthātmya-niścayaḥ / sva-rūpa-yāthātmya-aniścaye 'pi svarga-ādi-phala-arthitva-tat-sādhana-anuṣṭhāna-tat-phala-anubhavānāṃ saṃbhavāt, avirodhāc ca / sa īyaṃ vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhiḥ eka-phala-sādhana-viṣayataya aikā; ekasmai mokṣa-ākhya-phalāya hi mumukṣoḥ sarvāṇi karmāṇi vidhīyante / ataḥ śāstra-arthasya ekatvāt sarva-karma-viṣayā buddhir eka aiva; yatha aika-phala-sādhanatayā āgneya-ādīnāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ sa-iti-kartavyatākānām eka-śāstra-arthatayā tad-viṣayā buddhir ekā, tadvad ity-arthaḥ / avyavasāyināṃ tu svarga-putra-paśv-anna-ādi-phala-sādhana-karma-adhikṛtānāṃ buddhayaḥ phala-ānantyād anantāḥ / tatra api bahu-śākhāḥ;

body.text: ekasmai phalāya codite 'pi darśapūrṇamāsādau karmaṇi, "āyur āśās te" ityādyavagatāvāntaraphalabhedena bahuśākhatvaṃ ca vidyate / ataḥ avyavasāyināṃ buddhayo 'nantā bahuśākhāś ca / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- nityeṣu naimittikeṣu karmasu pradhānaphalāni avāntaraphalāni ca yāni śrūyamāṇāni, tāni sarvāṇi parityajya mokṣaikaphalatayā sarvāṇi karmāṇy ekaśāstrārthatayānuṣṭheyāni; kāmyāni ca svavarṇāśramocitāni, tattatphalāni parityajya mokṣasādhanatayā nityanaimittikair ekīkṛtya yathābalam anuṣṭheyāni -- iti //
body.translated_text: even in an action such as the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> (new-and-full-moon sacrifice) and the like, though enjoined for a single fruit, through the differentiation of subsidiary fruits understood from [statements like] 'May you obtain long life,' there is many-branchedness. Therefore the <s>buddhis</s> of the irresolute are endless and many-branched. What is meant is this: in obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) and occasional (<s>naimittika</s>) actions, all the primary fruits and subsidiary fruits that are heard of — abandoning all of those, all actions are to be performed as having the single scriptural meaning of the single fruit of liberation; and desire-motivated actions (<s>kāmya</s>) too, those appropriate to one's own <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, abandoning their respective fruits and unifying them with the obligatory and occasional [actions] as means to liberation, are to be performed according to one's capacity — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: ekasmai phalāya codite 'pi darśa-pūrṇa-māsa-ādau karmaṇi, "āyur āśās te" ity-ādy-avagata-avāntara-phala-bhedena bahu-śākhatvaṃ ca vidyate / ataḥ avyavasāyināṃ buddhayo 'nantā bahu-śākhāś ca / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- nityeṣu naimittikeṣu karmasu pradhāna-phalāni avāntara-phalāni ca yāni śrūyamāṇāni, tāni sarvāṇi parityajya mokṣa-eka-phalatayā sarvāṇi karmāṇy eka-śāstra-arthataya ānuṣṭheyāni; kāmyāni ca sva-varṇa-āśrama-ucitāni, tat-tat-phalāni parityajya mokṣa-sādhanatayā nitya-naimittikair ekī-kṛtya yathā-balam anuṣṭheyāni --- iti //

body.text: atha kāmyakarmādhikṛtān nindati --
body.translated_text: Now he censures those who are engaged in desire-motivated actions —

children.text: atha kāmya-karma-adhikṛtān nindati ---
yām imām puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadanty avipaścitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those of limited wisdom (<s>avipaścitaḥ</s>) proclaim this flowery speech,

children.text: vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyad astīti vādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Pārtha</s>, delighting in the pronouncements of the <s>Vedas</s>, declaring 'There is nothing else'; ||

children.text: yām imām puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadanty avipaścitaḥ |
veda-vāda-ratāḥ pārtha na anyad asti iti vādinaḥ ||
kāmātmānaḥ svargaparāḥ janmakarmaphalapradām |
children.translated_text: Full of desire, with heaven as their highest goal, [this speech] which grants rebirth as the fruit of actions,

children.text: kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogāiśvaryagatiṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: Abounding in specific rituals, directed toward enjoyment and lordship; ||

children.text: kāma-ātmānaḥ svarga-parāḥ janma-karma-phala-pradām |
kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulāṃ bhoga-aiśvarya-gatiṃ prati ||
bhogāiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām |
children.translated_text: For those attached to enjoyment and lordship, whose minds are carried away by that [speech],

children.text: vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: The <s>buddhi</s> of determination is not ordained in the mind (<s>samādhi</s>). ||

children.text: bhoga-aiśvarya-prasaktānāṃ taya āpahṛta-cetasām |
vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate ||

body.text:
yām imāṃ puṣpitāṃ -- puṣpamātraphalām, āpātaramaṇīyāṃ vācam avipaścitaḥ -- alpajñāḥ bhogāiśvaryagatiṃ prati vartamānāṃ pravadanti, vedavādaratāḥ -- vedeṣu ye svargādiphalavādāḥ teṣu saktāḥ, nānyad astīti vādinaḥ -- tatsaṅgātirekeṇa svargāder adhikaṃ phalaṃ nānyad astīti vadantaḥ, kām ātmānaḥ kām apravaṇamanasaḥ, svargaparāḥ -- svargaparāyaṇāḥ, svargādiphalāvasāne punarjanmakarmākhyaphalapradāṃ, kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ -- tattvajñānarahitatayā kriyāviśeṣapracurām / bhogāiśvaryagatiṃ prati vartamānāṃ yām imāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ ye pravadantīti saṃbandhaḥ / teṣāṃ bhogāiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayā -- vācā bhogāiśvaryaviṣayayā apahṛtajñānānāṃ yathoditavyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ,
samādhau manasi na vidhīyate, notpadyate, samādhīyate 'sminn ātmajñānam iti samādhir manaḥ / teṣāṃ manasy ātmayāthātmyaniścayapūrvakamokṣasādhanabhūtakarmaviṣayā buddhiḥ kadācid api notpadyate ityarthaḥ / ataḥ kāmyeṣu karmasu mumukṣuṇā na saṅgaḥ kartavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'This flowery' — having only flowers as fruit, i.e., attractive at first sight — 'speech,' those of limited wisdom (<s>avipaścitaḥ</s>) — those of little knowledge — proclaim it, [this speech] which is directed toward enjoyment and lordship. 'Delighting in the pronouncements of the <s>Vedas</s>' — attached to those pronouncements in the <s>Vedas</s> that speak of fruits such as heaven. 'Declaring there is nothing else' — declaring that beyond attachment to those, there is no other fruit higher than heaven and the like. 'Full of desire' — those whose minds are inclined toward desire. 'With heaven as their highest goal' — those for whom heaven is the supreme aim. [This speech] which grants, at the end of the fruits such as heaven and the like, the fruit called rebirth and [new] actions; 'abounding in specific rituals' — abundant in specific rituals due to the absence of true knowledge. 'Directed toward enjoyment and lordship' — the connection is: those who proclaim this flowery speech, which is directed toward enjoyment and lordship. For those who are attached to enjoyment and lordship, whose knowledge has been carried away by that speech concerning enjoyment and lordship — the <s>buddhi</s> of determination as described, regarding the mind (<s>samādhi</s>), 'is not ordained,' does not arise. '<s>Samādhi</s>' means the mind, because it is in this that self-knowledge is settled. The meaning is: in their minds, the <s>buddhi</s> directed toward action that is the means of liberation, preceded by the ascertainment of the true nature of the self, never arises at all. Therefore, one who desires liberation should not have attachment to desire-motivated actions. ||

children.text:
yām imāṃ puṣpitāṃ --- puṣpa-mātra-phalām, āpāta-ramaṇīyāṃ vācam avipaścitaḥ --- alpa-jñāḥ bhoga-aiśvarya-gatiṃ prati vartamānāṃ pravadanti, veda-vāda-ratāḥ --- vedeṣu ye svarga-ādi-phala-vādāḥ teṣu saktāḥ, na anyad asti iti vādinaḥ --- tat-saṅga-atirekeṇa svarga-āder adhikaṃ phalaṃ na anyad asti iti vadantaḥ, kām ātmānaḥ kām apravaṇa-manasaḥ, svarga-parāḥ --- svarga-parāyaṇāḥ, svarga-ādi-phala-avasāne punar-janma-karma-ākhya-phala-pradāṃ, kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulāṃ --- tattva-jñāna-rahitatayā kriyā-viśeṣa-pracurām / bhoga-aiśvarya-gatiṃ prati vartamānāṃ yām imāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ ye pravadanti iti saṃbandhaḥ / teṣāṃ bhoga-aiśvarya-prasaktānāṃ tayā --- vācā bhoga-aiśvarya-viṣayayā apahṛta-jñānānāṃ yathā-udita-vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhiḥ,
samādhau manasi na vidhīyate, na utpadyate, samādhīyate 'sminn ātma-jñānam iti samādhir manaḥ / teṣāṃ manasy ātma-yāthātmya-niścaya-pūrvaka-mokṣa-sādhana-bhūta-karma-viṣayā buddhiḥ kadācid api na utpadyate ity-arthaḥ / ataḥ kāmyeṣu karmasu mumukṣuṇā na saṅgaḥ kartavyaḥ //

body.text: evam atyalpaphalāni punarjanmaprasavāni karmāṇi mātāpitṛsahasrebhyo 'pi vatsalataratayā ātmojjīvane pravṛttā vedāḥ kim arthaṃ vadanti, kathaṃ vā vedoditaṃ tyājyatayocyate ity ata āha --
body.translated_text: Thus, actions that have extremely meager fruits and produce rebirth — why do the <s>Vedas</s>, which are more loving than even a thousand mothers and fathers in their care for the self's welfare, teach them? And how can what is taught by the <s>Vedas</s> be said to be abandonable? — to this he says —

children.text: evam atyalpa-phalāni punar-janma-prasavāni karmāṇi mātā-pitṛ-sahasrebhyo 'pi vatsalataratayā ātma-ujjīvane pravṛttā vedāḥ kim arthaṃ vadanti, kathaṃ vā veda-uditaṃ tyājyataya ūcyate ity ata āha ---
traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna |
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s> have the three <s>guṇas</s> as their subject matter; be free from the three <s>guṇas</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>;

children.text: nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān ||
children.translated_text: Be free from the pairs of opposites, ever established in <s>sattva</s>, free from [concern for] acquisition and preservation, self-possessed. ||

children.text: traiguṇya-viṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavā arjuna |
nirdvandvo nitya-sattva-stho niryoga-kṣema ātmavān ||

body.text:
trayo guṇās traiguṇyaṃ sattvarajastamāṃsi / sattvarajastamaḥpracurāḥ puruṣās traiguṇyaśabdenocyante; tadviṣayā vedāḥ tamaḥpracurāṇāṃ rajaḥpracurāṇāṃ sattvapracurāṇāṃ ca vatsalataratayaiva hitam avabodhayanti vedāḥ / yady eṣāṃ svaguṇānuguṇyena svargādisādhanam eva hitaṃ nāvabodhayanti, tadaite rajastamaḥpracuratayā sāttvikaphalamokṣavimukhāḥ svāpekṣitaphalasādhanam ajānantaḥ kāmaprāvaṇyavivaśā anupādeyeṣu upādeyabhrāntyā praviṣṭāḥ pranaṣṭā bhaveyuḥ / atas traiguṇyaviṣayā vedāḥ, tvaṃ tu nistraiguṇyo bhava -- idānīṃ sattvapracuras tvaṃ tad eva vardhaya; nānyonyasaṅkīrṇaguṇatrayapracuro bhava; na tatprācuryaṃ vardhayetyarthaḥ / nirdvandvaḥ -- nirgatasakalasāṃsārikasvabhāvaḥ; nityasattvasthaḥ --
guṇadvayarahitanityapravṛddhasattvastho bhava / katham iti cet, niryogakṣemaḥ ātmasvarūpatatprāptyupāyabahirbhūtānām arthānāṃ yogaṃ prāptānāṃ ca kṣemaṃ parityajya ātmavān bhava -- ātmasvarūpān veṣaṇaparo bhava / aprāptasya prāptir yogaḥ prāptasya parikṣaṇaṃ kṣemaḥ / evaṃ vartamānasya te rajastamaḥpracuratā naśyati, sattvaṃ ca vardhate //
body.translated_text: The three <s>guṇas</s> are <s>traiguṇya</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. Persons predominated by <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> are referred to by the word '<s>traiguṇya</s>'; the <s>Vedas</s> have them as their subject — with even greater loving care, the <s>Vedas</s> teach what is beneficial to those predominated by <s>tamas</s>, those predominated by <s>rajas</s>, and those predominated by <s>sattva</s>. If the <s>Vedas</s> did not teach what is beneficial in accordance with their respective <s>guṇas</s> — namely, the means to heaven and the like — then these persons, predominated by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, averse to the <s>sāttvika</s> fruit of liberation, not knowing the means to the fruit they seek, helplessly driven by the inclination toward desire, having entered what should not be taken up through the delusion that it should be taken up, would be destroyed. Therefore, the <s>Vedas</s> have the three <s>guṇas</s> as their subject. But you should be free from the three <s>guṇas</s> — you are now predominated by <s>sattva</s>; cultivate that alone. Do not be predominated by the three <s>guṇas</s> intermixed with one another; do not cultivate their predominance — this is the meaning. 'Free from the pairs of opposites' — free from the entire nature of worldly existence (<s>saṃsāra</s>). 'Ever established in <s>sattva</s>' — be established in <s>sattva</s> that is ever-growing, free from the other two <s>guṇas</s>. How? — 'Free from acquisition and preservation' — abandoning the acquisition (<s>yoga</s>) of things not yet obtained and the preservation (<s>kṣema</s>) of things already obtained, which are external to the essential nature of the self and the means of attaining it, be self-possessed (<s>ātmavān</s>) — be devoted to the investigation of the essential nature of the self. '<s>Yoga</s>' is the obtaining of what is not yet obtained; '<s>kṣema</s>' is the guarding of what has been obtained. For you who live thus, the predominance of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> perishes, and <s>sattva</s> increases. ||

children.text:
trayo guṇās traiguṇyaṃ sattva-rajas-tamāṃsi / sattva-rajas-tamaḥ-pracurāḥ puruṣās traiguṇya-śabdena ucyante; tad-viṣayā vedāḥ tamaḥ-pracurāṇāṃ rajaḥ-pracurāṇāṃ sattva-pracurāṇāṃ ca vatsalatarataya aiva hitam avabodhayanti vedāḥ / yady eṣāṃ sva-guṇa-ānuguṇyena svarga-ādi-sādhanam eva hitaṃ na avabodhayanti, tada aite rajas-tamaḥ-pracuratayā sāttvika-phala-mokṣa-vimukhāḥ sva-apekṣita-phala-sādhanam ajānantaḥ kāma-prāvaṇya-vivaśā anupādeyeṣu upādeya-bhrāntyā praviṣṭāḥ pranaṣṭā bhaveyuḥ / atas traiguṇya-viṣayā vedāḥ, tvaṃ tu nistraiguṇyo bhava --- idānīṃ sattva-pracuras tvaṃ tad eva vardhaya; na anyonya-saṅkīrṇa-guṇa-traya-pracuro bhava; na tat-prācuryaṃ vardhaya ity-arthaḥ / nirdvandvaḥ --- nirgata-sakala-sāṃsārika-sva-bhāvaḥ; nitya-sattva-sthaḥ ---
guṇa-dvaya-rahita-nitya-pravṛddha-sattva-stho bhava / katham iti cet, niryoga-kṣemaḥ ātma-sva-rūpa-tat-prāpty-upāya-bahir-bhūtānām arthānāṃ yogaṃ prāptānāṃ ca kṣemaṃ parityajya ātmavān bhava --- ātma-sva-rūpān veṣaṇa-paro bhava / aprāptasya prāptir yogaḥ prāptasya parikṣaṇaṃ kṣemaḥ / evaṃ vartamānasya te rajas-tamaḥ-pracuratā naśyati, sattvaṃ ca vardhate //
yāvān artha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃplutodake |
children.translated_text: Whatever purpose is served by a well when water floods on all sides,

children.text: tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just that much [purpose is served] in all the <s>Vedas</s> for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows. ||

children.text: yāvān artha udapāne sarvataḥ saṃpluta-udake |
tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ ||

body.text: na ca vedoditaṃ sarvaṃ sarvasyopādeyam; yathā sarvārthaparikalpite sarvataḥ saṃplutodake udapāne pipāsor yāvān arthaḥ -- yāvad eva prayojanam, tāvad eva tenopādīyate, na sarvam; evaṃ sarveṣu ca vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ -- vaidikasya mumukṣoḥ yad eva mokṣasādhanaṃ tad evo=
body.translated_text: And not everything taught in the <s>Vedas</s> is to be taken up by everyone. Just as for one who thirsts, the purpose in a well designed for all purposes, when water floods on all sides, is just as much as the need — only that much is taken up, not everything — likewise, in all the <s>Vedas</s>, for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows — for the Vedic person who desires liberation — only what is the means to liberation is to be taken up;

children.text: na ca veda-uditaṃ sarvaṃ sarvasya upādeyam; yathā sarva-artha-parikalpite sarvataḥ saṃpluta-udake udapāne pipāsor yāvān arthaḥ --- yāvad eva prayojanam, tāvad eva tena upādīyate, na sarvam; evaṃ sarveṣu ca vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ --- vaidikasya mumukṣoḥ yad eva mokṣa-sādhanaṃ tad eva u=

body.text: pādeyam; nānyat //
body.translated_text: nothing else. ||

children.text: pādeyam; na anyat //

body.text: ataḥ sattvasthasya mumukṣor etāvad evopādeyam ity āha --
body.translated_text: Therefore, for one established in <s>sattva</s> who desires liberation, only this much is to be taken up — he says —

children.text: ataḥ sattva-sthasya mumukṣor etāvad eva upādeyam ity āha ---
karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana |
children.translated_text: Your right is to action alone, never to the fruits;

children.text: mā karmaphalahetur bhūḥ mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: Do not be the cause of the fruit of action; let there be no attachment to inaction in you. ||

children.text: karmaṇy eva adhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadā-cana |
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūḥ mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi ||

body.text: nitye naimittike kāmye ca kenacit phalaviśeṣeṇa saṃbandhitayā śrūyamāṇe karmaṇi nityasattvasthasya mumukṣos te karmamātre 'dhikāraḥ / tatsaṃbandhitayāvagateṣu phaleṣu na kadācid apy adhikāraḥ / saphalasya bandharūpatvāt phalarahitasya kevalasya madārādhanarūpasya mokṣahetutvāc ca / mā ca karmaphalayor hetubhūḥ / tvayānuṣṭhīyamāne 'pi karmaṇi nityasattvasthasya mumukṣos tava
body.translated_text: In action — whether obligatory, occasional, or desire-motivated — that is heard as connected with some specific fruit, for you who are ever established in <s>sattva</s> and desire liberation, the right is to action alone. In the fruits that are understood as connected with those [actions], there is never any right. Because action with fruit has the form of bondage, while action alone, devoid of fruit, being in the form of worship of Me [the Lord], is the cause of liberation. And do not be the cause of the fruit of action. Even when action is being performed by you, who are ever established in <s>sattva</s> and desire liberation —

children.text: nitye naimittike kāmye ca kena-cit phala-viśeṣeṇa saṃbandhitayā śrūyamāṇe karmaṇi nitya-sattva-sthasya mumukṣos te karma-mātre 'dhikāraḥ / tat-saṃbandhitaya āvagateṣu phaleṣu na kadā-cid apy adhikāraḥ / sa-phalasya bandha-rūpatvāt phala-rahitasya kevalasya mad-ārādhana-rūpasya mokṣa-hetutvāc ca / mā ca karma-phalayor hetu-bhūḥ / tvaya ānuṣṭhīyamāne 'pi karmaṇi nitya-sattva-sthasya mumukṣos tava

body.text: akartṛtvam apy anusandheyam / phalasyāpi kṣunnivṛttyāder na tvaṃ hetur ity anusandheyam / tadubhayaṃ guṇeṣu vā sarveśvare mayi vānusandheyam ity uttaratra vakṣyate / evam anusandhāya karma kuru / akarmaṇi -- ananuṣṭhāne, na yotsyāmīti yat tvayābhihitam, na tatra te saṅgo 'stu; uktena prakāreṇa yuddhādikarmaṇy eva saṅgo 'stv ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: the sense of non-agency too should be contemplated. 'I am not the cause even of the fruit, such as the alleviation of hunger and the like' — this should be contemplated. Both of those [non-agency and non-causation of fruit] should be contemplated as [belonging to] the <s>guṇas</s> or as [belonging to] Me, the Lord of all — this will be stated later. Having contemplated thus, perform action. 'In inaction' — in non-performance. That which was declared by you — 'I shall not fight' — let there be no attachment to that. The meaning is: let there be attachment to action such as battle in the manner described. ||

children.text: akartṛtvam apy anusandheyam / phalasya api kṣun-nivṛtty-āder na tvaṃ hetur ity anusandheyam / tad-ubhayaṃ guṇeṣu vā sarva-īśvare mayi va ānusandheyam ity uttaratra vakṣyate / evam anusandhāya karma kuru / akarmaṇi --- ananuṣṭhāne, na yotsyāmi iti yat tvaya ābhihitam, na tatra te saṅgo 'stu; uktena prakāreṇa yuddha-ādi-karmaṇy eva saṅgo 'stv ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: etad eva sphuṭīkaroti --
body.translated_text: He makes this very thing clear —

children.text: etad eva sphuṭī-karoti ---
yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya |
children.translated_text: Established in <s>yoga</s>, perform actions, abandoning attachment, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>;

children.text: siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Having become equal in success and failure — [this] equanimity is called <s>yoga</s>. ||

children.text: yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañ-jaya |
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate ||

body.text: rājyabandhuprabhṛtiṣu saṅgaṃ tyaktvā yuddhādīni karmāṇi yogasthaḥ kuru, tadantarbhūtavijayādisiddhyasiddhyos samo bhūtvā kuru / tad idaṃ siddhyasiddhyos samatvaṃ yogastha ity atra yogaśabdenocyate / yogaḥ -- siddhyasiddhiyos samatvarūpaṃ cittasamādhānam //
body.translated_text: Abandoning attachment to kingdom, kinsmen, and the like, perform actions such as battle established in <s>yoga</s>, having become equal in success and failure — including victory and the like contained therein. This equanimity in success and failure is what is referred to by the word '<s>yoga</s>' in 'established in <s>yoga</s>.' <s>Yoga</s> — the composure of mind (<s>cittasamādhāna</s>) in the form of equanimity in success and failure. ||

children.text: rājya-bandhu-prabhṛtiṣu saṅgaṃ tyaktvā yuddha-ādīni karmāṇi yoga-sthaḥ kuru, tad-antar-bhūta-vijaya-ādi-siddhy-asiddhyos samo bhūtvā kuru / tad idaṃ siddhy-asiddhyos samatvaṃ yoga-stha ity atra yoga-śabdena ucyate / yogaḥ --- siddhy-asiddhiyos samatva-rūpaṃ citta-samādhānam //

body.text: kim artham idam asakṛd ucyata ity ata āha --
body.translated_text: Why is this said repeatedly? — to this he says —

children.text: kim artham idam asakṛd ucyata ity ata āha ---
dūreṇa hy avaraṃ karma buddhiyogād dhanañjaya |
children.translated_text: For action is far inferior to <s>buddhiyoga</s> (the discipline of understanding), O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>;

children.text: buddhau śaraṇam anviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seek refuge in the understanding; wretched are those who are motivated by fruits. ||

children.text: dūreṇa hy avaraṃ karma buddhi-yogād dhanañ-jaya |
buddhau śaraṇam anviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ ||

body.text: yo 'yaṃ pradhānaphalatyāgaviṣayo 'vāntaraphalasiddhyasiddhyos samatvaviṣayaś ca buddhiyogaḥ; tadyuktāt karmaṇa itarat karma dūreṇāvaram / mahad idaṃ dvayor utkarṣāpakarṣarūpaṃ vairūpyam / uktabuddhiyogayuktaṃ karma nikhilasāṃsārikaduḥkhaṃ vinivartya paramapuruṣārthalakṣaṇaṃ ca mokṣaṃ prāpayati / itarad aparimitaduḥkharūpaṃ saṃsāram iti / ataḥ karmaṇi kriyamāṇe uktāyāṃ buddhau śaraṇam anviccha / śaraṇaṃ -- vāsasthānam / tasyām eva buddhau vartasvetyarthaḥ / kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ -- phalasaṅgādinā karma kurvāṇāḥ kṛpaṇāḥ -- saṃsāriṇo bhaveyuḥ //
body.translated_text: This <s>buddhiyoga</s> — which has as its object the abandonment of the primary fruit and equanimity regarding the success and failure of subsidiary fruits — action endowed with that is [superior]; other action is far inferior to it. Great is this disparity in the form of superiority and inferiority between the two. Action endowed with the described <s>buddhiyoga</s> removes all the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> and leads to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which is the supreme human goal. The other [kind of action leads to] <s>saṃsāra</s>, which has the form of unlimited suffering. Therefore, while performing action, seek refuge in the described <s>buddhi</s>. 'Refuge' means dwelling-place. The meaning is: abide in that <s>buddhi</s> alone. 'Wretched are those who are motivated by fruits' — those who perform action with attachment to fruits are wretched — they would become beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>. ||

children.text: yo 'yaṃ pradhāna-phala-tyāga-viṣayo 'vāntara-phala-siddhy-asiddhyos samatva-viṣayaś ca buddhi-yogaḥ; tad-yuktāt karmaṇa itarat karma dūreṇa avaram / mahad idaṃ dvayor utkarṣa-apakarṣa-rūpaṃ vairūpyam / ukta-buddhi-yoga-yuktaṃ karma nikhila-sāṃsārika-duḥkhaṃ vinivartya parama-puruṣa-artha-lakṣaṇaṃ ca mokṣaṃ prāpayati / itarad aparimita-duḥkha-rūpaṃ saṃsāram iti / ataḥ karmaṇi kriyamāṇe uktāyāṃ buddhau śaraṇam anviccha / śaraṇaṃ --- vāsa-sthānam / tasyām eva buddhau vartasva ity-arthaḥ / kṛpaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ --- phala-saṅga-ādinā karma kurvāṇāḥ kṛpaṇāḥ --- saṃsāriṇo bhaveyuḥ //
buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte |
children.translated_text: One endowed with <s>buddhi</s> abandons here both merit and demerit;

children.text: tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore devote yourself to <s>yoga</s>; <s>yoga</s> is skill in actions. ||

children.text: buddhi-yukto jahāti iha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte |
tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam ||

body.text: buddhiyogayuktas tu karma kurvāṇaḥ ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte anādikālasañcite anante bandhahetubhūte jahāti / tasmād uktāya buddhiyogāya yujyasva / yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam -- karmasu kriyamāṇeṣv ayaṃ buddhiyogaḥ kauśalam -- atisāmarthyam / atisāmarthyasādhya ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: But one who performs action endowed with <s>buddhiyoga</s> abandons both merit (<s>sukṛta</s>) and demerit (<s>duṣkṛta</s>) — accumulated from beginningless time, infinite, constituting the cause of bondage. Therefore devote yourself to the described <s>buddhiyoga</s>. '<s>Yoga</s> is skill in actions' — when actions are being performed, this <s>buddhiyoga</s> is skill — supreme capability. The meaning is: [something] to be accomplished by supreme capability. ||

children.text: buddhi-yoga-yuktas tu karma kurvāṇaḥ ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte anādi-kāla-sañcite anante bandha-hetu-bhūte jahāti / tasmād uktāya buddhi-yogāya yujyasva / yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam --- karmasu kriyamāṇeṣv ayaṃ buddhi-yogaḥ kauśalam --- atisāmarthyam / atisāmarthya-sādhya ity-arthaḥ //
karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: For the wise, endowed with <s>buddhi</s>, having abandoned the fruit born of action,

children.text: janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchanty anāmayam ||
children.translated_text: Freed from the bondage of birth, they go to the state that is free from affliction. ||

children.text: karma-jaṃ buddhi-yuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ |
janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchanty anāmayam ||

body.text: buddhiyogayuktāḥ karmajaṃ phalaṃ tyaktvā karma kurvantaḥ, tasmāj janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ anāmayaṃ padaṃ gacchanti hi -- prasiddhaṃ hy etat sarvāsūpaniṣatsv ityarthaḥ //
