body.translated_text: Those endowed with <s>buddhiyoga</s>, having abandoned the fruit born of action, performing action — thereby freed from the bondage of birth, they go to the state free from affliction (<s>anāmaya</s>). 'For' — for this is well-known in all the <s>Upaniṣads</s> — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: buddhi-yoga-yuktāḥ karma-jaṃ phalaṃ tyaktvā karma kurvantaḥ, tasmāj janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ anāmayaṃ padaṃ gacchanti hi --- prasiddhaṃ hy etat sarvāsu upaniṣatsv ity-arthaḥ //
yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhir vyatitariṣyati |
children.translated_text: When your <s>buddhi</s> will cross beyond the mire of delusion,

children.text: tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Then you will attain indifference toward what is to be heard and what has been heard. ||

children.text: yadā te moha-kalilaṃ buddhir vyatitariṣyati |
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca ||

body.text: uktaprakāreṇa karmaṇi vartamānasya tayā vṛttyā nirdhūtakalmaṣasya te buddhir yadā mohakalilam atyalpaphalasaṅgahetubhūtaṃ moharūpaṃ kaluṣaṃ vyatitariṣyati, tadā asmattaḥ itaḥ pūrvaṃ tyājyatayā śrutasya phalādeḥ itaḥ paścāc chrotavyasya ca kṛte svayam eva nirvedaṃ gantāsi -- gamiṣyasi //
body.translated_text: For you who live in the manner described in performing action, whose impurities have been cleansed by that practice — when your <s>buddhi</s> will cross beyond the mire of delusion, the impurity in the form of delusion that is the cause of attachment to extremely meager fruits, then you will of your own accord attain indifference toward the fruits and the like that have been heard from us as worthy of abandonment, and toward what is yet to be heard — you will attain [indifference]. ||

children.text: ukta-prakāreṇa karmaṇi vartamānasya tayā vṛttyā nirdhūta-kalmaṣasya te buddhir yadā moha-kalilam atyalpa-phala-saṅga-hetu-bhūtaṃ moha-rūpaṃ kaluṣaṃ vyatitariṣyati, tadā asmattaḥ itaḥ pūrvaṃ tyājyatayā śrutasya phala-ādeḥ itaḥ paścāc chrotavyasya ca kṛte svayam eva nirvedaṃ gantāsi --- gamiṣyasi //

body.text: "yoge tv imāṃ śṛṇu" ityādinoktasyātmayāthātmyajñānapūrvakasya buddhiviśeṣasaṃskṛtasya dharmānuṣṭhānasya lakṣabhūtaṃ yogākhyaṃ phalam āha --
body.translated_text: The fruit called <s>yoga</s>, which is the goal of the practice of <s>dharma</s> refined by the specific <s>buddhi</s> preceded by the knowledge of the true nature of the self, as stated beginning with 'But hear this regarding <s>yoga</s>' — he states —

children.text: "yoge tv imāṃ śṛṇu" ity-ādina ūktasyā atma-yāthātmya-jñāna-pūrvakasya buddhi-viśeṣa-saṃskṛtasya dharma-anuṣṭhānasya lakṣa-bhūtaṃ yoga-ākhyaṃ phalam āha ---
śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā |
children.translated_text: When your <s>buddhi</s>, perplexed by what has been heard, will stand firm,

children.text: samādhāv acalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasi ||
children.translated_text: Immovable in <s>samādhi</s> — then you will attain <s>yoga</s>. ||

children.text: śruti-vipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā |
samādhāv acalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasi ||

body.text: śrutiḥ śravaṇam / asmattaḥ śravaṇena viśeṣataḥ pratipannā sakaletaravisajātīyanityaniratiśayasūkṣmatattvātmaviṣayā, svayam acalā ekarūpā buddhiḥ asaṅgakarmānuṣṭhānena nirmalīkṛte manasi yadā niścalā sthāsyati, tadā yogam ātmāvalokanam avāpsyasi / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- śāstrajanyātmajñānapūrvakakarmayogaḥ sthitaprajñatākhyajñānaniṣṭhām āpādayati; jñānaniṣṭhārūpā
body.translated_text: '<s>Śruti</s>' means hearing. Through hearing from us, [your <s>buddhi</s>], having specifically understood — having as its object the eternal, unsurpassed, subtle reality of the self, which is dissimilar from all else — your <s>buddhi</s>, immovable, of a single form, when [the mind] has been purified through the performance of action without attachment — when [it] will stand firm in <s>samādhi</s>, then you will attain <s>yoga</s> — the vision of the self (<s>ātmāvalokana</s>). What is meant is this: <s>karmayoga</s> preceded by knowledge of the self born of scripture brings about the state of steady wisdom (<s>sthitaprajñatā</s>), which is the state of being established in knowledge; the state of being established in knowledge, in its form —

children.text: śrutiḥ śravaṇam / asmattaḥ śravaṇena viśeṣataḥ pratipannā sakala-itara-visajātīya-nitya-niratiśaya-sūkṣma-tattva-ātma-viṣayā, svayam acalā eka-rūpā buddhiḥ asaṅga-karma-anuṣṭhānena nirmalīkṛte manasi yadā niścalā sthāsyati, tadā yogam ātma-avalokanam avāpsyasi / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- śāstra-janya-ātma-jñāna-pūrvaka-karma-yogaḥ sthita-prajñatā-ākhya-jñāna-niṣṭhām āpādayati; jñāna-niṣṭhā-rūpā

body.text: sthitaprajñatā tu yogākhyam ātmāvalokanaṃ sādhayati iti //
body.translated_text: But the state of being established in wisdom (<s>sthitaprajñatā</s>) is the means for accomplishing the contemplation of the self called <s>yoga</s>. //

children.text: sthita-prajñatā tu yoga-ākhyam ātma-avalokanaṃ sādhayati iti //

body.text: etad uktaḥ pārtho 'saṅgakarmānuṣṭhānarūpakarmayogasādhyasthitaprajñatāyā yogasādhanabhūtāyāḥ svarūpam, sthitaprajñasyānuṣṭhānaprakāraṃ ca pṛcchati --
body.translated_text: <s>Pārtha</s>, having been told this, asks about the nature of the state of established wisdom — which is achieved through <s>karmayoga</s> consisting in the performance of action without attachment — and which serves as a means for <s>yoga</s>, and about the manner of conduct of one established in wisdom:

children.text: etad uktaḥ pārtho 'saṅga-karma-anuṣṭhāna-rūpa-karma-yoga-sādhya-sthita-prajñatāyā yoga-sādhana-bhūtāyāḥ sva-rūpam, sthita-prajñasya anuṣṭhāna-prakāraṃ ca pṛcchati ---
sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava |
children.translated_text: 'What is the description of one established in wisdom who is absorbed in <s>samādhi</s>, O <s>Keśava</s>?'

children.text: sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣate kim āsīta vrajeta kim ||
children.translated_text: 'How does one established in wisdom speak? How does he sit? How does he move?' ||

children.text: sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhi-sthasya keśava |
sthita-dhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣate kim āsīta vrajeta kim ||

body.text: samādhisthasya sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā ko vācakaś śabdaḥ ? tasya svarūpaṃ kīdṛśam ityarthaḥ / sthitaprajñaḥ kiṃ ca bhāṣādikaṃ karoti ? //
body.translated_text: What is the description — what is the designating term — for one established in wisdom who is absorbed in <s>samādhi</s>? The meaning is: what is his essential nature like? And what speaking and other activities does the one established in wisdom perform? //

children.text: samādhi-sthasya sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣā ko vācakaś śabdaḥ ? tasya sva-rūpaṃ kīdṛśam ity-arthaḥ / sthita-prajñaḥ kiṃ ca bhāṣā-ādikaṃ karoti ? //

body.text: vṛttiviśeṣakathanena svarūpam apy uktaṃ bhavatīti vṛttiviśeṣa ucyate --
body.translated_text: Since by stating the specific mode of conduct, the essential nature too is conveyed, the specific mode of conduct is stated:

children.text: vṛtti-viśeṣa-kathanena sva-rūpam apy uktaṃ bhavati iti vṛtti-viśeṣa ucyate ---
prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha manogatān |
children.translated_text: 'When a person abandons all desires that arise in the mind, O <s>Pārtha</s>,'

children.text: ātmany evātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñas tadocyate ||
children.translated_text: 'satisfied in the self alone by the self — then he is said to be one of established wisdom.' ||

children.text: prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha mano-gatān |
ātmany evā atmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthita-prajñas tada ūcyate ||

body.text: ātmany evātmanā manasā ātmaikāvalambanena tuṣṭaḥ tena toṣeṇa tadvyatiriktān sarvān manogatān kāmān yadā prakarṣeṇa jahāti, tadāyaṃ sthitaprajña ity ucyate / jñānaniṣṭhākāṣṭheyam //
body.translated_text: Satisfied in the self alone, by the self — that is, by the mind — through the self being the sole support, when through that satisfaction he thoroughly abandons all desires that arise in the mind, other than the self, then he is said to be one of established wisdom. This is the highest stage of the practice of knowledge (<s>jñānaniṣṭhā</s>). //

children.text: ātmany evā atmanā manasā ātma-eka-avalambanena tuṣṭaḥ tena toṣeṇa tad-vyatiriktān sarvān mano-gatān kāmān yadā prakarṣeṇa jahāti, tada āyaṃ sthita-prajña ity ucyate / jñāna-niṣṭhā-kāṣṭha īyam //

body.text: anantaraṃ jñānaniṣṭhasya tato 'rvācīnādūraviprakṛṣṭāvasthocyate --
body.translated_text: Next, the state of the practitioner of knowledge that is earlier and not far removed from that [highest stage] is stated:

children.text: anantaraṃ jñāna-niṣṭhasya tato 'rvācīna-adūra-viprakṛṣṭa-avastha ūcyate ---
duḥkheṣv anudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One whose mind is not distressed in sorrows, who is free from longing in pleasures,'

children.text: vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīr munir ucyate ||
children.translated_text: 'free from attachment, fear, and anger — he is called a sage of established wisdom.' ||

children.text: duḥkheṣv anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣu vigata-spṛhaḥ |
vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ sthita-dhīr munir ucyate ||

body.text: priyaviśleṣādiduḥkhanimitteṣu upasthiteṣu anudvignamanāḥ -- na duḥkhī bhavati; sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ -- priyeṣu sannihiteṣv api vigataspṛhaḥ, vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ -- anāgateṣu spṛhā rāgaḥ, tadrahitaḥ; priyaviśleṣāpriyāgamanahetudarśananimittaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhayam, tadrahitaḥ; priyaviśleṣāpriyāgamanahetubhūtacetanāntaragataduḥkhahetubhūtasvamanovikāraḥ krodhaḥ, tadrahitaḥ; evaṃbhūtaḥ muniḥ -- ātmamananaśīlaḥ sthitadhīr ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: When occasions of sorrow, such as separation from the beloved and the like, present themselves, his mind is not distressed — he does not become sorrowful. Free from longing in pleasures — even when beloved [objects] are near, he is free from longing. Free from attachment, fear, and anger: longing for things not yet attained is attachment — he is free from that. The suffering that is fear, caused by seeing the cause of separation from the beloved and the approach of the unpleasant — he is free from that. Anger is the mental agitation that is the cause of suffering directed toward other sentient beings who are the causes of separation from the beloved and the approach of the unpleasant — he is free from that. One of this nature is a sage (<s>muni</s>) — one given to contemplating the self — and is said to be of established wisdom. //

children.text: priya-viśleṣa-ādi-duḥkha-nimitteṣu upasthiteṣu anudvigna-manāḥ --- na duḥkhī bhavati; sukheṣu vigata-spṛhaḥ --- priyeṣu sannihiteṣv api vigata-spṛhaḥ, vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ --- anāgateṣu spṛhā rāgaḥ, tad-rahitaḥ; priya-viśleṣa-apriya-āgamana-hetu-darśana-nimittaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhayam, tad-rahitaḥ; priya-viśleṣa-apriya-āgamana-hetu-bhūta-cetana-antara-gata-duḥkha-hetu-bhūta-sva-mano-vikāraḥ krodhaḥ, tad-rahitaḥ; evaṃ-bhūtaḥ muniḥ --- ātma-manana-śīlaḥ sthita-dhīr ity ucyate //

body.text: tato 'rvācīnadaśā procyate --
body.translated_text: A still earlier stage is stated:

children.text: tato 'rvācīna-daśā procyate ---
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śubhāśubham |
children.translated_text: 'He who is without affection everywhere, who, encountering this or that, pleasant or unpleasant,'

children.text: nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||
children.translated_text: 'neither rejoices nor hates — his wisdom is established.' ||

children.text: yaḥ sarvatra anabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śubha-aśubham |
na abhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||

body.text: yaḥ sarvatra priyeṣu anabhisnehaḥ udāsīnaḥ; priyasaṃśleṣaviśleṣarūpaṃ śubhāśubhaṃ prāpyābhinandanadveṣarahitaḥ, so 'pi sthitaprajñaḥ //
body.translated_text: He who is everywhere without affection toward beloved [objects], who is indifferent; who, encountering the pleasant and unpleasant in the form of union with and separation from the beloved, is free from rejoicing and hatred — he too is one of established wisdom. //

children.text: yaḥ sarvatra priyeṣu anabhisnehaḥ udāsīnaḥ; priya-saṃśleṣa-viśleṣa-rūpaṃ śubha-aśubhaṃ prāpya abhinandana-dveṣa-rahitaḥ, so 'pi sthita-prajñaḥ //

body.text: tato 'rvācīnadaśām āha --
body.translated_text: A still earlier stage is stated:

children.text: tato 'rvācīna-daśām āha ---
yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo 'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'When this one withdraws the senses from the sense-objects on all sides, as a tortoise [withdraws] its limbs,'

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||
children.translated_text: 'his wisdom is established.' ||

children.text: yadā saṃharate ca ayaṃ kūrmo 'ṅgāni iva sarvaśaḥ |
indriyāṇi indriya-arthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||

body.text: yadendriyāṇīndriyārthān spṛṣṭum udyuktāni, tadaiva kūrmo 'ṅgānīva, indriyārthebhyaḥ sarvaśaḥ pratisaṃhṛtya mana ātmany avasthāpayati, so 'pi sthitaprajñaḥ / evaṃ caturvidhā jñānaniṣṭhā / pūrvapūrvā uttarottraniṣpādyā //
body.translated_text: When the senses, being eager to touch the sense-objects, at that very moment — as a tortoise [withdraws] its limbs — having withdrawn [them] from the sense-objects on all sides, he establishes the mind in the self — he too is one of established wisdom. Thus, the practice of knowledge is fourfold. Each earlier [stage] is to be accomplished by the subsequent one. //

children.text: yada īndriyāṇi indriya-arthān spṛṣṭum udyuktāni, tada aiva kūrmo 'ṅgāni iva, indriya-arthebhyaḥ sarvaśaḥ pratisaṃhṛtya mana ātmany avasthāpayati, so 'pi sthita-prajñaḥ / evaṃ catur-vidhā jñāna-niṣṭhā / pūrva-pūrvā uttara-uttra-niṣpādyā //

body.text: idānīṃ jñānaniṣṭhāyā duṣprāpatāṃ tatprāptyupāyaṃ cāha --
body.translated_text: Now he states the difficulty of attaining the practice of knowledge and the means for attaining it:

children.text: idānīṃ jñāna-niṣṭhāyā duṣprāpatāṃ tat-prāpty-upāyaṃ cā aha ---
viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Sense-objects cease for the embodied one who abstains from feeding [the senses],'

children.text: rasavarjaṃ raso 'py asya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate ||
children.translated_text: 'but the taste remains. Even that taste ceases upon seeing the Supreme.' ||

children.text: viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ |
rasa-varjaṃ raso 'py asya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate ||

body.text: indriyāṇām āhārā viṣayāḥ; nirāhārasya viṣayebhyaḥ pratyāhṛtendriyasya dehino viṣayā vinivartamānā rasavarjaṃ vinivartante; rasaḥ rāgaḥ / viṣayarāgo na nivartata ityarthaḥ / rāgo 'py ātmasvarūpaṃ viṣayebhyaḥ paraṃ sukhataraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate //
body.translated_text: The foods of the senses are the sense-objects. For the embodied one who abstains from feeding [the senses] — one who has withdrawn the senses from the objects — the sense-objects, though ceasing, cease except for the taste (<s>rasa</s>). The taste is attachment (<s>rāga</s>). The meaning is: the attachment to sense-objects does not cease. But even the attachment ceases upon seeing the Supreme — the self's own nature, which is more blissful than the sense-objects. //

children.text: indriyāṇām āhārā viṣayāḥ; nirāhārasya viṣayebhyaḥ pratyāhṛta-indriyasya dehino viṣayā vinivartamānā rasa-varjaṃ vinivartante; rasaḥ rāgaḥ / viṣaya-rāgo na nivartata ity-arthaḥ / rāgo 'py ātma-sva-rūpaṃ viṣayebhyaḥ paraṃ sukhataraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate //
yatato hy api kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The turbulent senses, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, even of a striving, wise person,'

children.text: indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'forcefully carry away the mind.' ||

children.text: yatato hy api kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ |
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ ||

body.text: ātmadarśanena vinā viṣayarāgo na nivartate, anivṛtte viṣayarāge vipaścito yatamānasyāpi puruṣasyendriyāṇi pramāthīni balavanti, manaḥ prasahya haranti / evam indriyajayaḥ ātmadarśanādhīnaḥ, ātmadarśanam indriyajayādhīnam iti jñānaniṣṭhā duṣprāpā //
body.translated_text: Without the vision of the self, the attachment to sense-objects does not cease. When the attachment to sense-objects has not ceased, the senses — which are turbulent, powerful — of even a wise and striving person forcefully carry away the mind. Thus, the conquest of the senses depends on the vision of the self, and the vision of the self depends on the conquest of the senses — therefore, the practice of knowledge is difficult to attain. //

children.text: ātma-darśanena vinā viṣaya-rāgo na nivartate, anivṛtte viṣaya-rāge vipaścito yatamānasya api puruṣasya indriyāṇi pramāthīni balavanti, manaḥ prasahya haranti / evam indriya-jayaḥ ātma-darśana-adhīnaḥ, ātma-darśanam indriya-jaya-adhīnam iti jñāna-niṣṭhā duṣprāpā //
tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having restrained all of them, let one sit, disciplined, intent on Me;'

children.text: vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||
children.translated_text: 'for one whose senses are under control, his wisdom is established.' ||

children.text: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ |
vaśe hi yasya indriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||

body.text: asya sarvasya parijihīrṣayā viṣayānurāgayuktatayā durjayānīndriyāṇi saṃyamya, cetasaś śubhāśrayabhūte mayi mano 'vasthāpya samāhita āsīta / manasi madviṣaye sati nirdagdhāśeṣakalmaṣatayā nirmalīkṛtaṃ viṣayānurāgarahitaṃ mana indriyāṇi svavaśāni karoti / tato vaśyendriyaṃ mana ātmadarśanāya prabhavati / yathoktam, "yathāgnir uddhataśikhaḥ kakṣaṃ dahati sānilaḥ / tathā cittasthito viṣṇur yogināṃ sarvakilbiṣam // BhGR_2." iti / tadāha "vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā"+iti //
body.translated_text: With the desire to overcome all of this — restraining the senses, which are difficult to conquer due to being yoked to attachment to sense-objects, and fixing the mind on Me, the auspicious refuge for the mind — let one sit, concentrated. When the mind is directed toward Me as its object, being purified by the complete burning away of all impurities, the mind — made pure and free from attachment to sense-objects — brings the senses under its control. Then the mind, having its senses under control, becomes capable of the vision of the self. As stated: 'Just as fire, when fanned into blazing flames, burns the forest, so <s>Viṣṇu</s>, established in the mind, [burns away] all the sins of the <s>yogins</s>.' // <s>BhGR</s> 2 // Therefore he says: 'for one whose senses are under control, his wisdom is established.' //

children.text: asya sarvasya parijihīrṣayā viṣaya-anurāga-yuktatayā durjayāni indriyāṇi saṃyamya, cetasaś śubha-āśraya-bhūte mayi mano 'vasthāpya samāhita āsīta / manasi mad-viṣaye sati nirdagdha-aśeṣa-kalmaṣatayā nirmalīkṛtaṃ viṣaya-anurāga-rahitaṃ mana indriyāṇi sva-vaśāni karoti / tato vaśya-indriyaṃ mana ātma-darśanāya prabhavati / yatha ūktam, "yatha āgnir uddhata-śikhaḥ kakṣaṃ dahati sa-anilaḥ / tathā citta-sthito viṣṇur yogināṃ sarva-kilbiṣam // BhGR_2." iti / tadā āha "vaśe hi yasya indriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā"+iti //

body.text: evaṃ mayy aniveśya manaḥ svayatnagauraveṇendriyajaye pravṛtto vinaṣṭo bhavatīty āha --
body.translated_text: Thus, one who, without fixing the mind on Me, proceeds to conquer the senses by his own self-effort, is destroyed — he says:

children.text: evaṃ mayy aniveśya manaḥ sva-yatna-gauraveṇa indriya-jaye pravṛtto vinaṣṭo bhavati ity āha ---
dhyāyato viṣayān puṃsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate |
children.translated_text: 'For a person who contemplates sense-objects, attachment to them is born;'

children.text: saṅgāt saṃjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate ||
children.translated_text: 'from attachment arises desire; from desire, anger is born.' ||

children.text: dhyāyato viṣayān puṃsaḥ saṅgas teṣu upajāyate |
saṅgāt saṃjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate ||
krodhād bhavati saṃmohaḥ saṃmohāt smṛtivibhramaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'From anger arises delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory;'

children.text: smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśo buddhināśāt praṇaśyati ||
children.translated_text: 'from confusion of memory, destruction of discernment; from destruction of discernment, one perishes.' ||

children.text: krodhād bhavati saṃmohaḥ saṃmohāt smṛti-vibhramaḥ |
smṛti-bhraṃśād buddhi-nāśo buddhi-nāśāt praṇaśyati ||

body.text:
anirastaviṣayānurāgasya hi mayy aniveśitamanasa indriyāṇi saṃyamyāvasthitasyāpi anādipāpavāsanayā viṣayadhyānam avarjanīyaṃ syāt / dhyāyato viṣayān puṃsaḥ punar api saṅgo 'tipravṛddho jāyate / saṅgāt saṃjāte kāmaḥ / kāmo nāma saṅgasya vipākadaśā / puruṣo yāṃ daśām āpanno viṣayān abhuktvā sthātuṃ na śaknoti, sa kāmaḥ // kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate / kāme vartamāne, viṣaye cāsannihite, sannihitān puruṣān prati, ebhir asmadiṣṭaṃ vihitam iti krodho bhavati / krodhād bhavati saṃmohaḥ / saṃmohaḥ kṛtyākṛtyavivekaśūnyatā / tayā sarvaṃ karoti / tataś ca prārabdhe indriyajayādike prayatne smṛtibhraṃśo bhavati / smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśaḥ ātmajñāne yo vyavasāyaḥ kṛtaḥ, tasya nāśaḥ syāt / buddhināśāt punar api saṃsāre nimagno
vinaṣṭo bhavati //
body.translated_text: For one whose mind has not been fixed on Me, whose attachment to sense-objects has not been removed — even though established in restraining the senses — contemplation of sense-objects would be unavoidable due to the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions) of beginningless sin. For the person contemplating sense-objects, attachment, exceedingly intensified, is again born. From attachment, desire (<s>kāma</s>) is born. Desire is the mature stage of attachment — the state in which a person, having reached it, cannot remain without enjoying the sense-objects. // From desire, anger is born. When desire is present but the sense-object is not at hand, anger arises toward persons who are nearby, [thinking] 'these have obstructed what I desire.' From anger, delusion (<s>saṃmoha</s>) arises. Delusion is the absence of discrimination between what should and should not be done. Due to that, one does everything. And from that, when the endeavor already undertaken toward the conquest of the senses and the like is [disrupted], confusion of memory arises. From confusion of memory, destruction of discernment — the resolution that was made regarding self-knowledge is destroyed. From destruction of discernment, one perishes — once again plunged into <s>saṃsāra</s>, one is destroyed. //

children.text:
anirasta-viṣaya-anurāgasya hi mayy aniveśita-manasa indriyāṇi saṃyamya avasthitasya api anādi-pāpa-vāsanayā viṣaya-dhyānam avarjanīyaṃ syāt / dhyāyato viṣayān puṃsaḥ punar api saṅgo 'tipravṛddho jāyate / saṅgāt saṃjāte kāmaḥ / kāmo nāma saṅgasya vipāka-daśā / puruṣo yāṃ daśām āpanno viṣayān abhuktvā sthātuṃ na śaknoti, sa kāmaḥ // kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate / kāme vartamāne, viṣaye ca asannihite, sannihitān puruṣān prati, ebhir asmad-iṣṭaṃ vihitam iti krodho bhavati / krodhād bhavati saṃmohaḥ / saṃmohaḥ kṛtya-akṛtya-viveka-śūnyatā / tayā sarvaṃ karoti / tataś ca prārabdhe indriya-jaya-ādike prayatne smṛti-bhraṃśo bhavati / smṛti-bhraṃśād buddhi-nāśaḥ ātma-jñāne yo vyavasāyaḥ kṛtaḥ, tasya nāśaḥ syāt / buddhi-nāśāt punar api saṃsāre nimagno
vinaṣṭo bhavati //
rāgadveṣaviyuktais tu viṣayān indriyaiś caran |
children.translated_text: 'But one who moves among sense-objects with senses free from attachment and aversion,'

children.text: ātmavaśyair vidheyātmā prasādam adhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: 'with self-controlled [senses], the self-disciplined one attains serenity.' ||

children.text: rāga-dveṣa-viyuktais tu viṣayān indriyaiś caran |
ātma-vaśyair vidheya-ātmā prasādam adhigacchati ||

body.text: uktena prakāreṇa mayi sarveśvare cetasaś śubhāśrayabhūte nyastamanāḥ nirdagdhāśeṣakalmaṣatayā rāgadveṣaviyuktair ātmavaśyair indriyaiḥ viṣayāṃś caran viṣayāṃs tiraskṛtya vartamānaḥ vidheyātmā vidheyamanāḥ prasādam adhigacchati nirmalāntaḥkaraṇo bhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: One who, in the manner stated, has placed his mind on Me — the Lord of all, the auspicious refuge for the mind — and who moves among sense-objects with senses free from attachment and aversion, under the control of the self, through the complete burning away of all impurities — passing through sense-objects while disregarding them — the self-disciplined one (<s>vidheyātmā</s>), one whose mind is disciplined, attains serenity — the meaning is: he becomes one of pure inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>). //

children.text: uktena prakāreṇa mayi sarva-īśvare cetasaś śubha-āśraya-bhūte nyasta-manāḥ nirdagdha-aśeṣa-kalmaṣatayā rāga-dveṣa-viyuktair ātma-vaśyair indriyaiḥ viṣayāṃś caran viṣayāṃs tiraskṛtya vartamānaḥ vidheya-ātmā vidheya-manāḥ prasādam adhigacchati nirmala-antaḥkaraṇo bhavati ity-arthaḥ //
prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānir asyopajāyate |
children.translated_text: 'Upon [the attainment of] serenity, the cessation of all his sorrows comes about;'

children.text: prasannacetaso hy āśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: 'for the discernment of one whose mind is serene quickly becomes firmly established.' ||

children.text: prasāde sarva-duḥkhānāṃ hānir asya upajāyate |
prasanna-cetaso hy āśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate ||

body.text: asya puruṣasya manaḥprasāde sati prakṛtisaṃsargaprayuktasarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānir upajāyate / prasannacetasaḥ ātmāvalokanavirodhidoṣarahitamanasaḥ tadānīm eva hi viviktātmaviṣayā buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate / ato manaḥprasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānir bhavaty eva /65//
body.translated_text: When this person attains serenity of mind, the cessation of all sorrows occasioned by the contact with <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature) comes about. For one whose mind is serene — whose mind is free from the defects that obstruct the contemplation of the self — at that very moment, the discernment directed toward the distinct self becomes firmly established. Therefore, upon serenity of mind, the cessation of all sorrows indeed comes about. //

children.text: asya puruṣasya manaḥ-prasāde sati prakṛti-saṃsarga-prayukta-sarva-duḥkhānāṃ hānir upajāyate / prasanna-cetasaḥ ātma-avalokana-virodhi-doṣa-rahita-manasaḥ tadānīm eva hi vivikta-ātma-viṣayā buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate / ato manaḥ-prasāde sarva-duḥkhānāṃ hānir bhavaty eva /65//
nāsti buddhir ayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā |
children.translated_text: 'There is no discernment for the undisciplined, nor for the undisciplined is there meditation;'

children.text: na cābhāvayataḥ śāntir aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham ||
children.translated_text: 'for one who does not meditate, there is no peace; for the peaceless, whence happiness?' ||

children.text: na asti buddhir ayuktasya na ca ayuktasya bhāvanā |
na ca abhāvayataḥ śāntir aśāntasya kutaḥ sukham ||

body.text: mayi sannyastamanorahitasya svayatnenendriyaniyamane pravṛttasya kadācid api viviktātmaviṣayā buddhir na setsyati/ ata eva tasya tadbhāvanā ca na saṃbhavati / viviktātmānam abhāvayato viṣayaspṛhāśāntir na bhavati / aśāntasya viṣayaspṛhāyuktasya kuto nityaniratiśayasukhaprāptiḥ //
body.translated_text: For one who has not surrendered his mind to Me and who is engaged in controlling the senses by his own effort alone — the discernment directed toward the distinct self will never succeed. And for that very reason, his meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) on that [self] is also impossible. For one who does not meditate upon the distinct self, the cessation of longing for sense-objects does not occur. And for one who is not at peace — who is still endowed with longing for sense-objects — whence the attainment of eternal, unsurpassable happiness? //

children.text: mayi sannyasta-mano-rahitasya sva-yatnena indriya-niyamane pravṛttasya kadācid api vivikta-ātma-viṣayā buddhir na setsyati/ ata eva tasya tad-bhāvanā ca na saṃbhavati / vivikta-ātmānam abhāvayato viṣaya-spṛha-aśāntir na bhavati / aśāntasya viṣaya-spṛha-ayuktasya kuto nitya-niratiśaya-sukha-prāptiḥ //

body.text: punar apy uktena prakāreṇendriyaniyamanam akurvato 'nartham āha --
body.translated_text: He states again the misfortune for one who does not control the senses in the manner described:

children.text: punar apy uktena prakāreṇa indriya-niyamanam akurvato 'nartham āha ---
indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yan mano 'nuvidhīyate |
children.translated_text: 'The mind that follows in the wake of the wandering senses'

children.text: tad asya harati prajñāṃ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi ||
children.translated_text: 'carries away his wisdom, as wind [carries away] a ship on water.' ||

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yan mano 'nuvidhīyate |
tad asya harati prajñāṃ vāyur nāvam iva ambhasi ||

body.text: indriyāṇāṃ viṣayeṣu caratāṃ vartamānānāṃ vartanam anu yan mano vidhīyate puruṣeṇānuvartyate, tan mano 'sya viviktātmapravaṇāṃ prajñāṃ harati viṣayapravaṇāṃ karotītyarthaḥ; yathāmbhasi nīyamānāṃ nāvaṃ pratikūlo vāyuḥ prasahya harati //
body.translated_text: Of the senses that are wandering — moving — among the sense-objects, the mind that follows in their wake — that is made to follow by the person — that mind carries away his wisdom inclined toward the distinct self and makes it inclined toward sense-objects. This is the meaning. Just as a contrary wind forcefully carries away a ship being propelled on water. //

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ viṣayeṣu caratāṃ vartamānānāṃ vartanam anu yan mano vidhīyate puruṣeṇa anuvartyate, tan mano 'sya vivikta-ātma-pravaṇāṃ prajñāṃ harati viṣaya-pravaṇāṃ karoti ity-arthaḥ; yatha āmbhasi nīyamānāṃ na avaṃ pratikūlo vāyuḥ prasahya harati //
tasmād yasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, O mighty-armed one, one whose senses are completely restrained'

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||
children.translated_text: 'from the sense-objects — his wisdom is established.' ||

children.text: tasmād yasya mahā-bāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ |
indriyāṇi indriya-arthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||

body.text: tasmād uktena prakāreṇa śubhāśraye mayi niviṣṭamanaso yasyendriyāṇi indriyārthebhyaḥ sarvaśo nigṛhītāni, tasyaivātmani prajñā pratiṣṭhitā bhavati //
body.translated_text: Therefore, only for one whose mind is fixed on Me — the auspicious refuge — in the manner stated, and whose senses are completely restrained from the sense-objects — for him alone, wisdom directed toward the self becomes established. //

children.text: tasmād uktena prakāreṇa śubha-āśraye mayi niviṣṭa-manaso yasya indriyāṇi indriya-arthebhyaḥ sarvaśo nigṛhītāni, tasya evā atmani prajñā pratiṣṭhitā bhavati //

body.text: evaṃ niyatendriyasya prasannamanasaḥ siddhim āha --
body.translated_text: Thus, he states the attainment of one whose senses are controlled and whose mind is serene:

children.text: evaṃ niyata-indriyasya prasanna-manasaḥ siddhim āha ---
yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī |
children.translated_text: 'What is night for all beings, in that the self-restrained one is awake;'

children.text: yasyāṃ jāgarti bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'that in which beings are awake — that is night for the seeing sage.' ||

children.text: yā niśā sarva-bhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī |
yasyāṃ jāgarti bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ ||

body.text: yā ātmaviṣayā buddhiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ niśā niśevāprakāśā, tasyām ātmaviṣayāyāṃ buddhau indriyasaṃyamī prasannamanāḥ jāgarti ātmānam avalokayan āsta ityarthaḥ / yasyāṃ śabdādiviṣayāyāṃ buddhau sarvāṇi bhūtāni jāgrati prabuddhāni bhavanti,; sā śabdādiviṣayā buddhir ātmānaṃ paśyato muner niśevāprakāśā bhavati //
body.translated_text: That which is discernment directed toward the self — which is like night, i.e., darkness, for all beings — in that discernment directed toward the self, the one who has restrained the senses, whose mind is serene, is awake — he abides contemplating the self. This is the meaning. That discernment directed toward sound and other sense-objects, in which all beings are awake — are wakeful — that discernment directed toward sound and the like is like night, i.e., darkness, for the sage who sees the self. //

children.text: yā ātma-viṣayā buddhiḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ niśā niśa īva aprakāśā, tasyām ātma-viṣayāyāṃ buddhau indriya-saṃyamī prasanna-manāḥ jāgarti ātmānam avalokayan āsta ity-arthaḥ / yasyāṃ śabda-ādi-viṣayāyāṃ buddhau sarvāṇi bhūtāni jāgrati prabuddhāni bhavanti,; sā śabda-ādi-viṣayā buddhir ātmānaṃ paśyato muner niśa īva aprakāśā bhavati //
āpūryamāṇam acalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat |
children.translated_text: 'Just as the ocean, which is being filled, remains unmoved and firm, [and] the waters enter into it,'

children.text: tadvat kāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntim āpnoti na kāmakāmī ||
children.translated_text: 'so too one into whom all desires enter attains peace — not the desirer of desires.' ||

children.text: āpūryamāṇam acala-pratiṣṭhaṃ samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat |
tadvat kāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī ||

body.text: yathā svenaivāpūryamāṇam ekarūpaṃ samudraṃ nādeyya āpaḥ praviśanti, āsām apāṃ praveśe 'py apraveśe ca samudro na kañcana viśeṣam āpadyate -- evaṃ sarve kāmāḥ śabdādayo viṣayāḥ yaṃ saṃyaminaṃ praviśanti indriyagocaratāṃ yānti, sa śāntim āpnoti / śabdādiṣv indriyagocaratām āpanneṣv anāpanneṣu ca svātmāvalokanatṛptyaiva yo na vikāram āpnoti, sa eva śāntim āpnotītyarthaḥ / na kāmakāmī / yaḥ śabdādibhir vikriyate, sa kadācid api na śāntim āpnoti //
body.translated_text: Just as the ocean, being filled by its own nature and being of one form, [receives] the river waters that enter it — and upon the entering or non-entering of these waters, the ocean undergoes no change whatsoever — so too, all desires — sense-objects such as sound and the like — enter into the self-restrained one, come within the range of his senses; and he attains peace. The meaning is: one who, when sound and the like come within the range of his senses or do not come, undergoes no change whatsoever, due to being satisfied by the contemplation of his own self alone — he alone attains peace. Not the desirer of desires — one who is agitated by sound and the like never attains peace. //

children.text: yathā svena evā apūryamāṇam eka-rūpaṃ samudraṃ nādeyya āpaḥ praviśanti, āsām apāṃ praveśe 'py apraveśe ca samudro na kañcana viśeṣam āpadyate --- evaṃ sarve kāmāḥ śabda-ādayo viṣayāḥ yaṃ saṃyaminaṃ praviśanti indriya-gocaratāṃ yānti, sa śāntim āpnoti / śabda-ādiṣv indriya-gocaratām āpanneṣv anāpanneṣu ca sva-ātma-avalokana-tṛptya aiva yo na vikāram āpnoti, sa eva śāntim āpnoti ity-arthaḥ / na kāma-kāmī / yaḥ śabda-ādibhir vikriyate, sa kadācid api na śāntim āpnoti //
vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumāṃś carati nisspṛhaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The person who abandons all desires and moves about free from longing,'

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntim adhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: 'free from possessiveness and ego — he attains peace.' ||

children.text: vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumāṃś carati nisspṛhaḥ |
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntim adhigacchati ||

body.text: kāmyanta iti kāmāḥ śabdādayaḥ / yaḥ pumān śabdādīn sarvān viṣayān vihāya
body.translated_text: That which is desired is a desire (<s>kāma</s>) — sound and the like. The person who, abandoning all sense-objects such as sound and the like,

children.text: kāmyanta iti kāmāḥ śabda-ādayaḥ / yaḥ pumān śabda-ādīn sarvān viṣayān vihāya

body.text: tatra nisspṛhaḥ tatra mamatārahitaś ca, anātmani dehe ātmābhimānarahitaś carati; sa ātmānaṃ dṛṣṭvā śāntim adhigacchati //
body.translated_text: is free from longing for them, free from the sense of 'mine' regarding them, and free from the identification of the self with the non-self, the body — he moves about; having seen the self, he attains peace. //

children.text: tatra nisspṛhaḥ tatra mamatā-rahitaś ca, anātmani dehe ātma-abhimāna-rahitaś carati; sa ātmānaṃ dṛṣṭvā śāntim adhigacchati //
eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati |
children.translated_text: 'This is the <s>Brāhmī</s> state, O <s>Pārtha</s> — having attained this, one is not deluded.'

children.text: sthitvāsyām antakāle 'pi brahmanirvāṇam ṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: 'Established in this even at the time of death, one attains <s>brahmanirvāṇa</s>.' ||

children.text: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha na enāṃ prāpya vimuhyati |
sthitva āsyām anta-kāle 'pi brahma-nirvāṇam ṛcchati ||

body.text: eṣā nityātmajñānapūrvikā asaṅgakarmaṇi sthitiḥ sthitadhīlakṣā brāhmī brahmaprāpikā / īdṛśīṃ karmaṇi sthitiṃ prāpya na vimuhyati punaḥ saṃsāraṃ nāpnoti, asyāḥ sthityām antime 'pi vayasi sthitvā brahmanirvāṇam ṛcchati nirvāṇamayaṃ brahma gacchati; sukhaikatānam ātmānam avāpnotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: This state — consisting in action without attachment, preceded by the knowledge of the eternal self — characterized by established wisdom, is the <s>Brāhmī</s> [state], leading to <s>Brahman</s>. Having attained such a state in action, one is not deluded — one does not again attain <s>saṃsāra</s>. Even established in this state in the final period of life, one attains <s>brahmanirvāṇa</s> — one reaches <s>Brahman</s> that consists in <s>nirvāṇa</s>; the meaning is: one attains the self whose nature is solely bliss. //

children.text: eṣā nitya-ātma-jñāna-pūrvikā asaṅga-karmaṇi sthitiḥ sthita-dhī-lakṣā brāhmī brahma-prāpikā / īdṛśīṃ karmaṇi sthitiṃ prāpya na vimuhyati punaḥ saṃsāraṃ nā apnoti, asyāḥ sthityām antime 'pi vayasi sthitvā brahma-nirvāṇam ṛcchati nirvāṇa-mayaṃ brahma gacchati; sukha-ekatānam ātmānam avāpnoti ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: evam ātmayāthātmyaṃ yuddhākhyasya ca karmaṇas tatprāptisādhanatām ajānataḥ śarīrātmajñānena mohitasya, tena ca mohena yuddhān nivṛttasya mohaśāntaye nityātmaviṣayā sāṅkhyabuddhiḥ, tatpūrvikā ca asaṅgakarmānuṣṭhānarūpakarmayogaviṣayā buddhiḥ sthitaprajñatāyogasādhanabhūtā dvitīye adhyāye proktā; tad uktam, "nityātmāsaṅgakarmehāgocarā sāṅkhyayogadhīḥ / dvitīye sthitadhīlakṣā proktā tanmohaśāntaye" iti //
body.translated_text: Thus, for one who did not know the true nature of the self, the instrumentality of the action called battle as a means of attaining it, and who was deluded by the identification of the self with the body, and who had turned away from battle due to that delusion — for the calming of that delusion, in the second chapter was taught: the <s>sāṅkhya</s>-understanding concerning the eternal self, and the understanding of <s>karmayoga</s> (the discipline of action) in the form of performing action without attachment, preceded by that [self-knowledge], which serves as a means to the state of steady wisdom (<s>sthitaprajñatā</s>). As stated: 'The <s>sāṅkhya</s> and <s>yoga</s> understanding, pertaining to the eternal self and to desireless action, was taught in the second chapter, characterized by steady wisdom, for the calming of that delusion.' ||

children.text: evam ātma-yāthātmyaṃ yuddha-ākhyasya ca karmaṇas tat-prāpti-sādhanatām ajānataḥ śarīra-ātma-jñānena mohitasya, tena ca mohena yuddhān nivṛttasya moha-śāntaye nitya-ātma-viṣayā sāṅkhya-buddhiḥ, tat-pūrvikā ca asaṅga-karma-anuṣṭhāna-rūpa-karma-yoga-viṣayā buddhiḥ sthita-prajñatā-yoga-sādhana-bhūtā dvitīye adhyāye proktā; tad uktam, "nitya-ātma-asaṅga-karma-īhā-gocarā sāṅkhya-yoga-dhīḥ / dvitīye sthita-dhī-lakṣā proktā tan-moha-śāntaye" iti //

body.text:
tad evaṃ mumukṣubhiḥ prāpyatayā vedāntoditanirastanikhilāvidyādidoṣagandhānavadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇaparabrahmapuruṣottamaprāptyupāyabhūtavedanopāsanadhyānādiśabdavācyatadaikāntikātyantikabhaktiṃ vaktuṃ tadaṅgabhūtaṃ "ya ātmāpahatapāpmā" ityādiprajāpativākyoditaṃ prāptur ātmano yāthātmyadarśanaṃ tannityatājñānapūrvakāsaṅgakarmaniṣpādyajñānayogasādhyam uktam /
prajāpativākye hi daharavākyoditaparavidyāśeṣatayā prāptur ātmanas svarūpadarśanam, "yas tam ātmānam anuvidya vijānāti" ity uktvā jāgaritasvapnasuṣuptyatītaṃ pratyagātmasvarūpam aśarīraṃ pratipādya, "evam evaiṣa saṃprasādo 'smāc charīrāt samutthāya paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate" iti daharavidyāphalenopasaṃhṛtam / anyatrāpi, "adhyātmayogādhigamena devaṃ matvā dhīro harṣaśokau jahāti" ity evam ādiṣu, devaṃ matveti vidhīyamānaparavidyāṅgatayā adhyātmayogādhigameneti pratyagātmajñānam api vidhāya, "na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit" ityādinā pratyagātmasvarūpaṃ viśodhya, "aṇor aṇīyān", ity ārabhya, "mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati", "nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena / yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām // BhGR_3." ityādibhiḥ parasvarūpaṃ tadupāsanam upāsanasya ca bhaktirūpatāṃ pratipādya, "vijñānasārathir yas tu manaḥpragrahavān naraḥ / so 'dhvanaḥ pāram āpnoti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam // iti paravidyāphalenopasaṃhṛtam
body.translated_text:
Thus, in order to teach the exclusive and ultimate devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) — which is to be attained by seekers of liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>), which is designated by the words <s>vedana</s> (knowledge), <s>upāsana</s> (worship), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and the like, and which is the means of attaining the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), taught in the <s>Vedānta</s>, who is free from even the slightest trace of all defects such as ignorance, and who is an inexhaustible treasure of unsurpassable, innumerable auspicious qualities — as an ancillary to that [devotion], the true vision of the nature of the self that is to attain [<s>Brahman</s>], as taught in the <s>Prajāpati</s>-passage beginning with 'The self that is free from evil,' was stated as achievable through the discipline of knowledge (<s>jñānayoga</s>), which is to be accomplished by desireless action accompanied by the knowledge of the eternity [of the self]. |
For in the <s>Prajāpati</s>-passage, as a subsidiary to the supreme knowledge (<s>paravidyā</s>) taught in the <s>dahara</s>-passage, [there is] the vision of the true nature of the self that is to attain [<s>Brahman</s>]. Having stated 'he who finds and knows that self,' having taught the nature of the inner self — beyond waking, dream, and deep sleep — as disembodied, [the passage] concludes with the fruit of the <s>dahara</s>-meditation: 'Thus indeed, this serene one, rising from this body, attaining the supreme light, appears in his own form.' Elsewhere too, in passages such as 'By the attainment of the <s>adhyātmayoga</s> (meditation on the inner self), knowing the God, the wise one abandons joy and sorrow' — as an ancillary to the supreme knowledge enjoined by 'knowing the God,' the knowledge of the inner self is also enjoined by 'by the attainment of the <s>adhyātmayoga</s>'; and having purified the nature of the inner self through passages such as 'It is never born, nor does it die — the wise one,' and then beginning with 'Subtler than the subtle,' through 'knowing the self that is great and all-pervading, the wise one does not grieve,' and 'This self cannot be attained through discourse, nor through intellect, nor through much learning; / He whom this [self] chooses, by him alone it is attained — to him this self reveals its own form' — [these passages] establish the nature of the Supreme, the worship of Him, and the devotional character of that worship, and conclude with the fruit of the supreme knowledge: 'The person who has discrimination as his charioteer and the mind as the reins — he reaches the end of the journey, that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'

children.text:
tad evaṃ mumukṣubhiḥ prāpyatayā veda-anta-udita-nirasta-nikhila-avidyā-ādi-doṣa-gandha-anavadhika-atiśaya-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-para-brahma-puruṣa-uttama-prāpty-upāya-bhūta-vedanā-upāsana-dhyāna-ādi-śabda-vācya-tad-aikāntika-ātyantika-bhaktiṃ vaktuṃ tad-aṅga-bhūtaṃ "ya ātma āpahata-pāpmā" ity-ādi-prajāpati-vākya-uditaṃ prāptur ātmano yāthātmya-darśanaṃ tan-nityatā-jñāna-pūrvaka-asaṅga-karma-niṣpādya-jñāna-yoga-sādhyam uktam /
prajāpati-vākye hi dahara-vākya-udita-para-vidyā-aśeṣatayā prāptur ātmanas sva-rūpa-darśanam, "yas tam ātmānam anuvidya vijānāti" ity uktvā jāgarita-svapna-suṣupty-atītaṃ pratyag-ātma-sva-rūpam aśarīraṃ pratipādya, "evam eva eṣa saṃprasādo 'smāc charīrāt samutthāya paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇa abhiniṣpadyate" iti dahara-vidyā-phalena upasaṃhṛtam / anyatra api, "adhyātma-yoga-adhigamena devaṃ matvā dhīro harṣa-śokau jahāti" ity evam ādiṣu, devaṃ matva īti vidhīyamāna-para-vidyā-aṅgatayā adhyātma-yoga-adhigamena iti pratyag-ātma-jñānam api vidhāya, "na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit" ity-ādinā pratyag-ātma-sva-rūpaṃ viśodhya, "aṇor aṇīyān", ity ārabhya, "mahā-antaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati", "na ayam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena / yam eva eṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasya eṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām // BhGR_3." ity-ādibhiḥ para-sva-rūpaṃ tad-upāsanam upāsanasya ca bhakti-rūpatāṃ pratipādya, "vijñāna-sārathir yas tu manaḥ-pragrahavān naraḥ / so 'dhvanaḥ pāram āpnoti tad-viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam // iti para-vidyā-phalena upasaṃhṛtam

body.text: ataḥ param adhyāyacatuṣṭayena idam eva prāptuḥ pratyagātmano darśanaṃ sasādhanaṃ prapañcayati --
body.translated_text: Henceforth, through a tetrad of chapters, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] elaborates this very vision of the nature of the inner self that is to attain [<s>Brahman</s>], together with its means —

children.text: ataḥ param adhyāya-catuṣṭayena idam eva prāptuḥ pratyag-ātmano darśanaṃ sasādhanaṃ prapañcayati ---
jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana |
children.translated_text: If understanding (<s>buddhi</s>) is deemed by you to be superior to action, O <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: tat kiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava ||
children.translated_text: then why do you engage me in this terrible action, O <s>Keśava</s>? ||

children.text: jyāyasī cet karmaṇas te matā buddhir jana-ardana |
tat kiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava ||
vyāmiśreṇaiva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasīva me |
children.translated_text: With what seems a contradictory statement, you confuse my understanding, as it were.

children.text: tad ekaṃ vada, niścitya yena śreyo 'ham āpnuyām ||
children.translated_text: Tell me the one [path] with certainty, by which I may attain the highest good. ||

children.text: vyāmiśreṇa eva vākyena buddhiṃ mohayasi iva me |
tad ekaṃ vada, niścitya yena śreyo 'ham āpnuyām ||

body.text:
yadi karmaṇo buddhir eva jyāyasīti te matā, kim arthaṃ tarhi ghore karmaṇi māṃ niyojayasi / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- jñānaniṣṭhaivātmāvalokanasādhanam; karmaniṣṭhā tu tasyāḥ niṣpādikā; ātmāvalokanasādhanabhūtā ca jñānaniṣṭhā sakalendriyamanasāṃ śabdādiviṣayavyāpāroparatiniṣpādyety abhihitā / indriyavyāpāroparatiniṣpādyam ātmāvalokanaṃ cet siṣādhayiṣitam, sakalakarmanivṛttipūrvakajñānaniṣṭhāyām evāhaṃ niyojayitavyaḥ / kim arthaṃ ghore karmaṇi sarvendriyavyāpārarūpe ātmāvalokanavirodhini karmaṇi māṃ niyojayasīti // ato miśravākyena māṃ mohayasīva -- pratibhāti / tathā hy ātmāvalokanasādhanabhūtāyāḥ sarvendriyavyāpāroparatirūpāyāḥ jñānaniṣṭhāyāḥ tadviparyayarūpaṃ karma sādhanam, tad eva kurv
iti vākyaṃ viruddhaṃ vyāmiśram eva / tasmād ekam amiśrarūpaṃ vākyaṃ vada, yena vākyenāham anuṣṭheyarūpaṃ niścitya śreyaḥ prāpnuyām //
body.translated_text: If understanding alone is deemed by you to be superior to action, then for what purpose do you engage me in terrible action? What is being said is this: the discipline of knowledge (<s>jñānaniṣṭhā</s>) alone is the means of the vision of the self; the discipline of action (<s>karmaniṣṭhā</s>) is what accomplishes that [knowledge-discipline]; and the knowledge-discipline that is the means of self-vision was said to be accomplished through the cessation of the engagement of all sense organs and mind in objects such as sound and the like. If the self-vision to be accomplished requires the cessation of the engagement of the senses, then I should be directed to the knowledge-discipline preceded by the complete cessation of all actions. For what purpose do you engage me in terrible action — action consisting of the engagement of all sense organs, which is opposed to self-vision? || Therefore, you seem to confuse me with a mixed statement. For the statement 'perform that very action which is the means of the knowledge-discipline — whose form is the cessation of all sense-engagement — when [action is] of a form contrary to that' — [such a statement] is indeed contradictory and mixed. Therefore, tell me a single, unmixed statement, by which statement, having determined what is to be done, I may attain the highest good. ||

children.text:
yadi karmaṇo buddhir eva jyāyasi īti te matā, kim arthaṃ tarhi ghore karmaṇi māṃ niyojayasi / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- jñāna-niṣṭha aivā atma-avalokana-sādhanam; karma-niṣṭhā tu tasyāḥ niṣpādikā; ātma-avalokana-sādhana-bhūtā ca jñāna-niṣṭhā sakala-indriya-manasāṃ śabda-ādi-viṣaya-vyāpāra-uparati-niṣpādya īty abhihitā / indriya-vyāpāra-uparati-niṣpādyam ātma-avalokanaṃ cet siṣādhayiṣitam, sakala-karma-nivṛtti-pūrvaka-jñāna-niṣṭhāyām eva ahaṃ niyojayitavyaḥ / kim arthaṃ ghore karmaṇi sarva-indriya-vyāpāra-rūpe ātma-avalokana-virodhini karmaṇi māṃ niyojayasi iti // ato miśra-vākyena māṃ mohayasi iva --- pratibhāti / tathā hy ātma-avalokana-sādhana-bhūtāyāḥ sarva-indriya-vyāpāra-uparati-rūpāyāḥ jñāna-niṣṭhāyāḥ tad-viparyaya-rūpaṃ karma sādhanam, tad eva kurv
iti vākyaṃ viruddhaṃ vyāmiśram eva / tasmād ekam amiśra-rūpaṃ vākyaṃ vada, yena vākyena aham anuṣṭheya-rūpaṃ niścitya śreyaḥ prāpnuyām //
loke 'smin dvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha |
children.translated_text: In this world, a twofold discipline has been taught by me of old, O sinless one:

children.text: jñānayogena sāṅkhyānāṃ karmayogena yoginām ||
children.translated_text: the discipline of knowledge for the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>, and the discipline of action for the <s>Yogins</s>. ||

children.text: loke 'smin dvi-vidhā niṣṭhā purā proktā maya ānagha |
jñāna-yogena sāṅkhyānāṃ karma-yogena yoginām ||

body.text:
pūrvoktaṃ na samyagavadhṛtaṃ tvayā / purā hy asmin loke vicitrādhikāripūrṇe, dvividhā niṣṭhā jñānakarmaviṣayā yathādhikāram asaṅkīrṇaiva mayoktā / na hi sarvo laukikaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃjātamokṣābhilāṣas tadānīm eva jñānayogādhikāre prabhavati, api tv anabhisaṃhitaphalena kevalaparamapuruṣārādhanaveṣeṇānuṣṭhitena karmaṇā vidhvastasvāntamalaḥ, avyākulendriyo jñānaniṣṭhāyām adhikaroti / "yataḥ pravṛttir bhūtānāṃ yena sarvam idaṃ tatam / svakarmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ" iti paramapuruṣārādhanaikaveṣatā karmaṇāṃ vakṣyate / ihāpi, "karmaṇy evādhikāras te" ityādinā anabhisaṃhitaphalaṃ karma anuṣṭheyaṃ vidhāya, tena viṣayavyākulatārūpamohād uttīrṇabuddheḥ "prajahāti yadā kāmān" ityādinā
jñānayoga uditaḥ / ataḥ sāṅkhyānām eva jñānayogena sthitir uktā / yogināṃ tu karmayogena / saṅkhyā buddhiḥ tadyuktāḥ sāṅkhyāḥ -- ātmaikaviṣayayā buddhyā saṃbandhinaḥ sāṅkhyāḥ; atadarhāḥ karmayogādhikāriṇo yoginaḥ / viṣayavyākulabuddhiyuktānāṃ karmayoge 'dhikāraḥ; avyākulabuddhīnāṃ tu jñānayoge 'dhikāra ukta iti na kiṃcid iha viruddhaṃ vyāmiśram abhihitam //
body.translated_text:
What was previously said was not properly grasped by you. For of old, in this world filled with persons of diverse qualifications, the twofold discipline — pertaining to knowledge and action — was taught by me according to [each person's] qualification, without intermixture. For not every worldly person, the moment the desire for liberation arises, is capable of [undertaking] the discipline of knowledge. Rather, one whose inner impurities have been destroyed through action performed solely in the spirit of worshipping the Supreme Person, without desire for results, becomes qualified for the knowledge-discipline with unagitated senses. 'By worshipping Him through one's own actions — Him from whom beings come forth, by whom all this is pervaded — a person attains perfection' — thus the exclusively worshipful character of actions toward the Supreme Person will be stated. Here too, having enjoined action without attachment to results through 'you have a right to action alone' and the like, for one whose understanding has crossed beyond the delusion characterized by agitation toward sense-objects through that [action], the discipline of knowledge is taught through 'when one completely abandons desires' and the like. |
Therefore, the established discipline through the <s>jñānayoga</s> was stated only for the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>. But for the <s>Yogins</s>, through <s>karmayoga</s>. <s>Saṅkhyā</s> is understanding (<s>buddhi</s>); those endowed with that are <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> — those who have a relationship with understanding focused solely on the self; those unfit for that are <s>Yogins</s>, who are qualified for <s>karmayoga</s>. For those endowed with understanding agitated by sense-objects, the right is to <s>karmayoga</s>; but for those with unagitated understanding, the right to <s>jñānayoga</s> has been stated — so nothing contradictory or mixed has been stated here. ||

children.text:
pūrva-uktaṃ na samyag-avadhṛtaṃ tvayā / purā hy asmin loke vicitra-adhikāri-pūrṇe, dvi-vidhā niṣṭhā jñāna-karma-viṣayā yathā-adhikāram asaṅkīrṇa aiva maya ūktā / na hi sarvo laukikaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃjāta-mokṣa-abhilāṣas tadānīm eva jñāna-yoga-adhikāre prabhavati, api tv anabhisaṃhita-phalena kevala-parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-veṣeṇa anuṣṭhitena karmaṇā vidhvasta-sva-anta-malaḥ, avyākula-indriyo jñāna-niṣṭhāyām adhikaroti / "yataḥ pravṛttir bhūtānāṃ yena sarvam idaṃ tatam / sva-karmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ" iti parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-eka-veṣatā karmaṇāṃ vakṣyate / iha api, "karmaṇy eva adhikāras te" ity-ādinā anabhisaṃhita-phalaṃ karma anuṣṭheyaṃ vidhāya, tena viṣaya-vyākulatā-rūpa-mohād uttīrṇa-buddheḥ "prajahāti yadā kāmān" ity-ādinā
jñāna-yoga uditaḥ / ataḥ sāṅkhyānām eva jñāna-yogena sthitir uktā / yogināṃ tu karma-yogena / saṅkhyā buddhiḥ tad-yuktāḥ sāṅkhyāḥ --- ātma-eka-viṣayayā buddhyā saṃbandhinaḥ sāṅkhyāḥ; atad-arhāḥ karma-yoga-adhikāriṇo yoginaḥ / viṣaya-vyākula-buddhi-yuktānāṃ karma-yoge 'dhikāraḥ; avyākula-buddhīnāṃ tu jñāna-yoge 'dhikāra ukta iti na kiṃcid iha viruddhaṃ vyāmiśram abhihitam //

body.text: sarvasya laukikasya puruṣasya mokṣecchāyāṃ jātāyāṃ sahasaiva jñānayogo duṣkara ity āha --
body.translated_text: He says that for every worldly person, when the desire for liberation has arisen, the discipline of knowledge is immediately difficult [to undertake] —

children.text: sarvasya laukikasya puruṣasya mokṣa-icchāyāṃ jātāyāṃ sahasa aiva jñāna-yogo duṣkara ity āha ---
na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo 'śnute |
children.translated_text: Not by the non-performance of actions does a person attain the state of freedom from action (<s>naiṣkarmya</s>);

children.text: na ca saṃnyasanād eva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: nor does one attain perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) by renunciation alone. ||

children.text: na karmaṇām anārambhān naiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo 'śnute |
na ca saṃnyasanād eva siddhiṃ samadhigacchati ||

body.text: na śāstrīyāṇāṃ karmaṇām anārambhād eva, puruṣo naiṣkarmyaṃ -- jñānaniṣṭhāṃ prāpnoti / na cārabdhasya śāstrīyasya tyāgāt; yato 'nabhisaṃhitaphalasya paramapuruṣārādhanaveṣasya karmaṇaḥ siddhiḥ sā / atas tena vinā tāṃ na prāpnoti / anabhisaṃhitaphalaiḥ karmabhir anārādhitagovindair avinaṣṭānādikālapravṛttānantapāpasañcayair avyākulendriyatāpūrvikā ātmaniṣṭhā dussaṃpādā //
body.translated_text: Not by the mere non-performance of scriptural actions does a person attain <s>naiṣkarmya</s> — the discipline of knowledge. Nor by the abandonment of scriptural action already undertaken — because the perfection [called <s>naiṣkarmya</s>] is [the fruit of] action performed without attachment to results, in the spirit of worshipping the Supreme Person. Therefore, without that [action], one does not attain it. For those who have not worshipped <s>Govinda</s> through actions performed without desire for results, for whom the accumulated mass of sins from beginningless time has not been destroyed — the discipline focused on the self, preceded by the non-agitation of the senses, is difficult to accomplish. ||

children.text: na śāstrīyāṇāṃ karmaṇām anārambhād eva, puruṣo naiṣkarmyaṃ --- jñāna-niṣṭhāṃ prāpnoti / na cā arabdhasya śāstrīyasya tyāgāt; yato 'nabhisaṃhita-phalasya parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-veṣasya karmaṇaḥ siddhiḥ sā / atas tena vinā tāṃ na prāpnoti / anabhisaṃhita-phalaiḥ karmabhir anārādhita-govindair avinaṣṭa-anādi-kāla-pravṛtta-ananta-pāpa-sañcayair avyākula-indriyatā-pūrvikā ātma-niṣṭhā dussaṃpādā //

body.text: etad evopapādayati --
body.translated_text: He establishes this very [point] —

children.text: etad eva upapādayati ---
na hi kaścit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhaty akarmakṛt |
children.translated_text: Indeed, no one ever remains even for a single moment without performing action;

children.text: kāryate hy avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijair guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: for everyone is made to act, helplessly, by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) born of <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature). ||

children.text: na hi kaścit kṣaṇam api jātu tiṣṭhaty akarma-kṛt |
kāryate hy avaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛti-jair guṇaiḥ ||

body.text: na hy asmin loke vartamānaḥ puruṣaḥ kaścit kadācid api karmākurvāṇas tiṣṭhati; na kiṃcit karomīti vyavasito 'pi sarvaḥ puruṣaḥ prakṛtisaṃbhavaiḥ sattvarajastamobhiḥ prācīnakarmānuguṇaṃ pravṛddhair guṇaiḥ svocitaṃ karma prati avaśaḥ kāryate - pravartyate / ata uktalakṣaṇena karmayogena prācīnaṃ pāpasaṃcayaṃ nāśayitvā guṇāṃś ca sattvādīn vaśe kṛtvā nirmalāntaḥkaraṇena saṃpādyo jñānayogaḥ //
body.translated_text: For no person existing in this world ever remains without performing any action at all. Even one who has resolved 'I am doing nothing at all' — every person is helplessly made to act, is impelled, toward action appropriate to himself by the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — born of <s>Prakṛti</s>, which have grown in accordance with prior <s>karma</s>. Therefore, having destroyed the accumulated mass of prior sins through <s>karmayoga</s> of the stated character, and having brought the <s>guṇas</s> such as <s>sattva</s> and the like under control, the discipline of knowledge is to be accomplished with a purified inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>). ||

children.text: na hy asmin loke vartamānaḥ puruṣaḥ kaścit kadācid api karma-akurvāṇas tiṣṭhati; na kiṃcit karomi iti vyavasito 'pi sarvaḥ puruṣaḥ prakṛti-saṃbhavaiḥ sattva-rajas-tamobhiḥ prācīna-karma-anuguṇaṃ pravṛddhair guṇaiḥ sva-ucitaṃ karma prati avaśaḥ kāryate -- pravartyate / ata ukta-lakṣaṇena karma-yogena prācīnaṃ pāpa-saṃcayaṃ nāśayitvā guṇāṃś ca sattva-ādīn vaśe kṛtvā nirmala-antaḥkaraṇena saṃpādyo jñāna-yogaḥ //

body.text: anyathā jñānayogāya pravṛtto mithyācāro bhavatīty āha --
body.translated_text: He says that otherwise, one who undertakes the discipline of knowledge becomes a hypocrite (<s>mithyācāra</s>) —

children.text: anyathā jñāna-yogāya pravṛtto mithyā-ācāro bhavati ity āha ---
karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran |
children.translated_text: He who, restraining the organs of action, sits remembering mentally

children.text: indriyārthān vimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: the objects of the senses — that deluded person is called a hypocrite. ||

children.text: karma-indriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran |
indriya-arthān vimūḍha-ātmā mithyā-ācāraḥ sa ucyate ||

body.text: avinaṣṭapāpatayā ajitāntaḥkaraṇaḥ ātmajñānāya pravṛtto viṣayapravaṇatayā ātmani vimukhīkṛtamanāḥ viṣayān eva smaran ya āste, anyathā saṃkalpya anyathā caratīti sa mithyācāra ucyate / ātmajñānāyodyukto viparīto vinaṣṭo bhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: One whose sins are not destroyed, whose inner instrument is not conquered, who has set out toward self-knowledge but whose mind, due to inclination toward sense-objects, has turned away from the self — he who sits merely remembering sense-objects, having resolved one thing and doing another — he is called a hypocrite. The meaning is that one who is engaged in self-knowledge but [acts] contrarily is destroyed. ||

children.text: avinaṣṭa-pāpatayā ajita-antaḥkaraṇaḥ ātma-jñānāya pravṛtto viṣaya-pravaṇatayā ātmani vimukhīkṛta-manāḥ viṣayān eva smaran ya āste, anyathā saṃkalpya anyathā carati iti sa mithyā-ācāra ucyate / ātma-jñānāya udyukto viparīto vinaṣṭo bhavati ity-arthaḥ //
yas tv indriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate 'rjuna |
children.translated_text: But he who, controlling the senses with the mind, undertakes, O <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: karmendriyaiḥ karmayogam asaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>karmayoga</s> (the discipline of action) with the organs of action, without attachment — he excels. ||

children.text: yas tv indriyāṇi manasā niyamyā arabhate 'rjuna |
karma-indriyaiḥ karma-yogam asaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate ||

body.text: ataḥ pūrvābhyastaviṣayasajātīye śāstrīye karmaṇi indriyāṇy ātmāvalokanapravṛttena manasā niyamya taiḥ svata eva karmapravaṇair indriyair asaṅgapūrvakaṃ yaḥ karmayogam ārabhate, so 'saṃbhāvyamānapramādatvena jñānaniṣṭhād api puruṣād viśiṣyate //
body.translated_text: Therefore, controlling the senses — in scriptural action of the same kind as the previously practiced sense-objects — with the mind that is directed toward the vision of the self, one who undertakes <s>karmayoga</s> without attachment, with those very organs that are naturally inclined toward action — he excels even over the person established in the knowledge-discipline, because of the impossibility of negligence [in his case]. ||

children.text: ataḥ pūrva-abhyasta-viṣaya-sajātīye śāstrīye karmaṇi indriyāṇy ātma-avalokana-pravṛttena manasā niyamya taiḥ svata eva karma-pravaṇair indriyair asaṅga-pūrvakaṃ yaḥ karma-yogam ārabhate, so 'saṃbhāvyamāna-pramādatvena jñāna-niṣṭhād api puruṣād viśiṣyate //
niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karmaṃ jyāsayo hy akarmaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Perform your prescribed action, for action is superior to inaction;

children.text: śarīrayātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even the maintenance of your body would not be accomplished through inaction. ||

children.text: niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karmaṃ jyāsayo hy akarmaṇaḥ |
śarīra-yātra āpi ca te na prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ ||

body.text:
niyataṃ vyāptam; prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭena hi vyāptaṃ karma, anādivāsanayā prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭas tvaṃ niyatatvena suśakatvād asaṃbhāvitapramādatvāc ca karmaṇaḥ, karmaiva kuru; akarmaṇaḥ jñānaniṣṭhāyā api karmaiva jyāyaḥ / "naiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo 'śunute" iti prakramād akarmaśabdena jñānaniṣṭhaivocyate / jñānaniṣṭhādhikāriṇo 'py anabhyastapūrvatayā hy aniyatatvena duḥśakatvāt sapramādatvāc ca jñānaniṣṭhāyāḥ, karmaniṣṭhaiva jyāyasī; karmaṇi kriyamāṇe ca ātmayāthātmyajñānenātmano 'kartṛtvānusandhānam anantaram eva vakṣyate / ata ātmajñānasyāpi karmayogāntargatatvāt sa eva jyāyān ityarthaḥ / karmaṇo jñānaniṣṭhāyā jyāyastvavacanaṃ jñānaniṣṭhāyām adhikāre saty evopapadyate /
yadi sarvaṃ karma parityajya kevalaṃ jñānaniṣṭhāyām adhikāro 'pi, tarhi akarmaṇaḥ jñānaniṣṭhasya jñānaniṣṭhopakāriṇī śarīrayātrāpi na setsyati / yāvat sādhanasamāpti śarīradhāraṇaṃ cāvaśyaṃ kāryam / nyāyārjitadhanena mahāyajñādikaṃ kṛtvā tacchiṣṭāśanenaiva śarīradhāraṇaṃ kāryam, "āhāraśuddhau sattvaśuddhiḥ sattvaśuddhau dhrutvā smṛtiḥ" ityādiśruteḥ / "te tv aghaṃ bhuñjate pāpā ye pacanty ātmakāraṇāt" iti vakṣyate / ato jñānaniṣṭhasyāpi karmākurvato dehayātrāpi na setsyati / yato jñānaniṣṭhasyāpi dhriyamāṇaśarīrasya yāvatsādhanasamāpti mahāyajñādi nityanaimittikaṃ karma avaśyaṃ kartavyam, yataś ca karmayoge 'py ātmano 'kartṛtvabhāvanayātmayāthātmyānusandhānam antarbhūtam, yataś ca prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭasya
karmayogaḥ suśako 'pramādaś ca, ato jñānaniṣṭhāyogyasyāpi jñānayogāt karmayogo jyāyān / tasmāt tvaṃ karmayogam eva kurv ityabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text:
'Prescribed' means 'pervaded'; for one conjoined with material nature (<s>Prakṛti</s>), action is pervaded [i.e., pervasive]. Since you, being conjoined with <s>Prakṛti</s> through beginningless <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions), [should perform] only action — because it is prescribed and hence easy to perform, and because negligence is impossible for it — action itself is superior even to the discipline of knowledge. From the context of 'a person does not attain <s>naiṣkarmya</s>,' the word 'inaction' (<s>akarma</s>) denotes the discipline of knowledge itself. For even one who is qualified for the knowledge-discipline — because of not having been previously practiced, the knowledge-discipline is not prescribed, is difficult to perform, and is subject to negligence — therefore the discipline of action is superior. And when action is being performed, the contemplation of the non-agency of the self through the knowledge of the true nature of the self will be stated immediately after. Therefore, since even self-knowledge is included within <s>karmayoga</s>, that alone is superior — this is the meaning. The statement of the superiority of the knowledge-discipline over action is applicable only when there is [actual] qualification for the knowledge-discipline. |
But if all action is abandoned and one is qualified solely for the knowledge-discipline, then for one in the knowledge-discipline, even the maintenance of the body — which supports the knowledge-discipline — will not be accomplished through inaction. For the maintenance of the body until the completion of the means [of liberation] must necessarily be done. The body must be sustained by eating the remnants of the great sacrifices (<s>mahāyajña</s>) and the like, performed with justly acquired wealth, in accordance with the <s>śruti</s>: 'From the purity of food [comes] purity of <s>sattva</s>; from purity of <s>sattva</s> [comes] firm memory.' And it will be stated: 'But those sinners who cook only for themselves eat sin.' Therefore, even for one in the knowledge-discipline, if one does not perform action, even the maintenance of the body will not be accomplished. Since even for one in the knowledge-discipline who maintains the body, the obligatory and occasional actions such as the great sacrifices must necessarily be performed until the completion of the means; since in <s>karmayoga</s> too, the contemplation of the true nature of the self through the meditation on the non-agency of the self is included within it; and since for one conjoined with material nature, <s>karmayoga</s> is easy to perform and free from negligence — therefore, even for one qualified for the knowledge-discipline, <s>karmayoga</s> is superior to <s>jñānayoga</s>. Therefore, you should perform <s>karmayoga</s> alone — this is the purport. ||

children.text:
niyataṃ vyāptam; prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭena hi vyāptaṃ karma, anādi-vāsanayā prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭas tvaṃ niyatatvena suśakatvād asaṃbhāvita-pramādatvāc ca karmaṇaḥ, karma eva kuru; akarmaṇaḥ jñāna-niṣṭhāyā api karma eva jyāyaḥ / "naiṣkarmyaṃ puruṣo 'śunute" iti prakramād akarma-śabdena jñāna-niṣṭha aiva ucyate / jñāna-niṣṭhā-adhikāriṇo 'py anabhyasta-pūrvatayā hy aniyatatvena duḥśakatvāt sapramādatvāc ca jñāna-niṣṭhāyāḥ, karma-niṣṭha aiva jyāyasī; karmaṇi kriyamāṇe ca ātma-yāthātmya-jñānenā atmano 'kartṛtva-anusandhānam anantaram eva vakṣyate / ata ātma-jñānasya api karma-yoga-antargatatvāt sa eva jyāyān ity-arthaḥ / karmaṇo jñāna-niṣṭhāyā jyāyastva-vacanaṃ jñāna-niṣṭhāyām adhikāre saty eva upapadyate /
yadi sarvaṃ karma parityajya kevalaṃ jñāna-niṣṭhāyām adhikāro 'pi, tarhi akarmaṇaḥ jñāna-niṣṭhasya jñāna-niṣṭhā-upakāriṇī śarīra-yātra āpi na setsyati / yāvat sādhana-samāpti śarīra-dhāraṇaṃ ca avaśyaṃ kāryam / nyāya-arjita-dhanena mahā-yajña-ādikaṃ kṛtvā tac-chiṣṭa-āśanena eva śarīra-dhāraṇaṃ kāryam, "āhāra-śuddhau sattva-śuddhiḥ sattva-śuddhau dhrutvā smṛtiḥ" ity-ādi-śruteḥ / "te tv aghaṃ bhuñjate pāpā ye pacanty ātma-kāraṇāt" iti vakṣyate / ato jñāna-niṣṭhasya api karma-akurvato deha-yātra āpi na setsyati / yato jñāna-niṣṭhasya api dhriyamāṇa-śarīrasya yāvat-sādhana-samāpti mahā-yajña-ādi nitya-naimittikaṃ karma avaśyaṃ kartavyam, yataś ca karma-yoge 'py ātmano 'kartṛtva-bhāvanayā ātma-yāthātmya-anusandhānam antarbhūtam, yataś ca prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭasya
karma-yogaḥ suśako 'pramādaś ca, ato jñāna-niṣṭhā-yogyasya api jñāna-yogāt karma-yogo jyāyān / tasmāt tvaṃ karma-yogam eva kurv ity-abhiprāyaḥ //

body.text: evaṃ tarhi dravyārjanādeḥ karmaṇo 'haṅkāramamakārādisarvendriyavyakulatāgarbhatvenāsya puruṣasya karmavāsanayā bandhanaṃ bhaviṣyatīty atrāha --
body.translated_text: If so, since the action of acquiring wealth and the like carries within it the agitation of all senses through egoism (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), possessiveness (<s>mamakāra</s>), and the like — this person will become bound by the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions) of action — to this he says —

children.text: evaṃ tarhi dravya-arjana-ādeḥ karmaṇo 'haṅkāra-mamakāra-ādi-sarva-indriya-vyakulatā-garbhatvena asya puruṣasya karma-vāsanayā bandhanaṃ bhaviṣyati ity atrā aha ---
yajñārthāt karmaṇo 'nyatra loko 'yaṃ karmabandhanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Action other than that performed for the sake of sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>) is the cause of bondage in this world;

children.text: tadarthaṃ karma kaunteya muktasaṅgas samācara ||
children.translated_text: perform action for that purpose, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, free from attachment! ||

children.text: yajña-arthāt karmaṇo 'nyatra loko 'yaṃ karma-bandhanaḥ |
tad-arthaṃ karma kaunteya mukta-saṅgas samācara ||

body.text: yajñādiśāstrīyakarmaśeṣabhūtād dravyārjanādeḥ karmaṇo 'nyatra ātmīyaprayojanaśeṣabhūte karmaṇi kriyamāṇe ayaṃ lokaḥ karmabandhano bhavati / atas tvaṃ yajñārthaṃ dravyārjanādikaṃ karma samācara / tatrātmaprayojanasādhanatayā yaḥ saṅgaḥ tasmāt saṅgān muktas tam samācara / evaṃ muktasaṅgena yajñādyarthatayā karmaṇi kriyamāṇe yajñādibhiḥ karmabhir ārādhitaḥ paramapuruṣo 'syānādikālapravṛttakarmavāsanām ucchidya avyākulātmāvalokanaṃ dadātītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: When action is performed for the purpose of one's own benefit — in an action that is a subsidiary to one's own purpose, other than the acquisition of materials and the like that form a subsidiary to scriptural action such as sacrifice — this world becomes bound by <s>karma</s>. Therefore, perform action such as the acquisition of materials for the purpose of sacrifice. Perform it free from the attachment that takes the form of regarding it as a means for one's own purpose. When action is performed in this way, as a subsidiary to sacrifice and the like, by one free from attachment — the Supreme Person (<s>Paramapuruṣa</s>), propitiated by such actions as sacrifice, cuts off the latent impression of <s>karma</s> accumulated since beginningless time and grants the undisturbed vision of the self — this is the meaning.

children.text: yajña-ādi-śāstrīya-karma-śeṣa-bhūtād dravya-arjana-ādeḥ karmaṇo 'nyatra ātmīya-prayojana-śeṣa-bhūte karmaṇi kriyamāṇe ayaṃ lokaḥ karma-bandhano bhavati / atas tvaṃ yajña-arthaṃ dravya-arjana-ādikaṃ karma samācara / tatrā atma-prayojana-sādhanatayā yaḥ saṅgaḥ tasmāt saṅgān muktas tam samācara / evaṃ mukta-saṅgena yajña-ādy-arthatayā karmaṇi kriyamāṇe yajña-ādibhiḥ karmabhir ārādhitaḥ parama-puruṣo 'sya-anādi-kāla-pravṛtta-karma-vāsanām ucchidya avyākula-ātma-avalokanaṃ dadāti ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: yajñaśiṣṭenaiva sarvapuruṣārthasādhananiṣṭhānāṃ śarīradhāraṇakartavyatām, ayajñaśiṣṭena śarīradhāraṇaṃ kurvatāṃ doṣaṃ cāha --
body.translated_text: He states the obligation of those established in the pursuit of all human goals to maintain the body through the remnants of sacrifice alone, and the fault of those who maintain the body through what is not the remnant of sacrifice:

children.text: yajña-śiṣṭena eva sarva-puruṣa-artha-sādhana-niṣṭhānāṃ śarīra-dhāraṇa-kartavyatām, ayajña-śiṣṭena śarīra-dhāraṇaṃ kurvatāṃ doṣaṃ cā aha ---
saha yajñaiḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having created beings together with sacrifices, <s>Prajāpati</s> (the Lord of beings) said of old:' |

children.text: anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣa vo 'stv iṣṭakāmadhuk ||
children.translated_text: 'By this [sacrifice] may you prosper — may this be your wish-fulfilling cow.' ||

children.text: saha yajñaiḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā pura ūvāca prajāpatiḥ |
anena prasaviṣyadhvam eṣa vo 'stv iṣṭa-kāma-dhuk ||

body.text: "patiṃ viśvasya" ityādiśruter nirupādhikaḥ prajāpatiśabdaḥ sarveśvaraṃ viśvasya sraṣṭāraṃ viśvātmānaṃ parāyaṇaṃ nārāyaṇam āha / purā -- sargakāle sa bhagavān prajāpatir anādikālapravṛttācitsaṃsargavivaśāḥ upasaṃhṛtanāmarūpavibhāgāḥ svasmin pralīnāḥ sakalapuruṣārthānarhāḥ cetanetarakalpāḥ prajāḥ samīkṣya paramakāruṇikas tadujjīvayiṣayā svārādhanabhūtayajñanirvṛttaye yajñaiḥ saha tāḥ sṛṣṭvaivam uvāca -- anena yajñena prasaviṣyadhvam, ātmano vṛddhiṃ kurudhvam; eṣa vo yajñaḥ paramapuruṣārthalakṣaṇamokṣākhyasya kāmasya tadanuguṇānāaṃ ca kāmānāṃ prapūrayitā bhavatu // BhGR_3.10 //
body.translated_text: From the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) 'the Lord of the universe' and the like, the word <s>Prajāpati</s> without any limiting adjunct denotes <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — the Lord of all, the creator of the universe, the self of the universe, the supreme refuge. Of old — at the time of creation, that blessed <s>Prajāpati</s>, seeing beings who were helpless due to their association with non-conscious matter accumulated since beginningless time, whose differentiation of names and forms had been withdrawn, who had dissolved into him, who were unfit for any human goal, and who were like non-conscious matter — being supremely compassionate, with the desire to revive them, for the accomplishment of sacrifice which is his worship, having created them together with sacrifices, said thus: by this sacrifice may you prosper, may you bring about your own growth; may this sacrifice be the fulfiller of your desire called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which is the supreme human goal, and of the desires conducive to it.

children.text: "patiṃ viśvasya" ity-ādi-śruter nirupādhikaḥ prajāpati-śabdaḥ sarva-īśvaraṃ viśvasya sraṣṭāraṃ viśva-ātmānaṃ parāyaṇaṃ nārāyaṇam āha / purā --- sarga-kāle sa bhagavān prajāpatir anādi-kāla-pravṛtta-acit-saṃsarga-vivaśāḥ upasaṃhṛta-nāma-rūpa-vibhāgāḥ svasmin pralīnāḥ sakala-puruṣa-artha-anarhāḥ cetana-itara-kalpāḥ prajāḥ samīkṣya parama-kāruṇikas tad-ujjīvayiṣayā sva-ārādhana-bhūta-yajña-nirvṛttaye yajñaiḥ saha tāḥ sṛṣṭva aivam uvāca --- anena yajñena prasaviṣyadhvam, ātmano vṛddhiṃ kurudhvam; eṣa vo yajñaḥ parama-puruṣa-artha-lakṣaṇa-mokṣa-ākhyasya kāmasya tad-anuguṇānāaṃ ca kāmānāṃ prapūrayitā bhavatu // BhGR_3.10 //

body.text: katham?
body.translated_text: How?

children.text: katham?
devān bhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Cherish the gods by this [sacrifice], and may those gods cherish you.' |

children.text: parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha ||
children.translated_text: 'Cherishing one another, you shall attain the supreme good.' ||

children.text: devān bhāvayata anena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ |
parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ param avāpsyatha ||

body.text: anena devatārādhanabhūtena devān maccharīrabhūtān madātmakān ārādhayata / "ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca" iti hi vakṣyate / yajñenārādhitās te devā madātmakāḥ svārādhanāpekṣitānnapānādikair yuṣmān puṣṇantu / evaṃ parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ paraṃ śreyo mokṣākhyam avāpsyatha //
body.translated_text: By this [sacrifice], which is the worship of the gods, propitiate the gods who are my body, who have me as their inner self. 'For I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices' — this will be stated [later]. Those gods who have me as their inner self, propitiated by sacrifice, may nourish you with food, drink, and the like that are needed for their worship. Thus, cherishing one another, you shall attain the supreme good called <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text: anena devatā-ārādhana-bhūtena devān mac-charīra-bhūtān mad-ātmakān ārādhayata / "ahaṃ hi sarva-yajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca" iti hi vakṣyate / yajñenā arādhitās te devā mad-ātmakāḥ sva-ārādhana-apekṣita-anna-pāna-ādikair yuṣmān puṣṇantu / evaṃ parasparaṃ bhāvayantaḥ paraṃ śreyo mokṣa-ākhyam avāpsyatha //
iṣṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The gods, nourished by sacrifice, will indeed bestow upon you the desired enjoyments.' |

children.text: tair dattān apradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'He who enjoys what is given by them without offering [back] to them is indeed a thief.' ||

children.text: iṣṭān bhogān hi vo devā dāsyante yajña-bhāvitāḥ |
tair dattān apradāya ebhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ ||

body.text: yajñabhāvitāḥ -- yajñenārādhitāḥ madātmakā devāḥ iṣṭān vo dāsyante uttamapuruṣārthalakṣaṇaṃ mokṣaṃ sādhayatāṃ ye iṣṭā bhogās tān pūrvapūrvayajñabhāvitā devā dāsyante uttarottarārādhanopekṣitān sarvān bhogān vo dāsyante ityarthaḥ / svārādhanārthatayā tair dattān bhogān tebhyo 'pradāya yo bhuṅkte cora eva saḥ / couryaṃ hi nāma anyadīye tatprayojanāyaiva parikḷpte vastuni svakīyatābuddhiṃ kṛtvā tena svātmapoṣaṇam / ato 'sya na paramapuruṣārthānarhatāmātram; api tu nirayagāmitvaṃ ca bhaviṣyatītyabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The gods who have me as their inner self, nourished by sacrifice — i.e., propitiated by sacrifice — will bestow upon you the desired [enjoyments]. For those who are accomplishing <s>mokṣa</s>, which is the supreme human goal, the desired enjoyments — the gods, nourished by previous successive sacrifices, will bestow all the enjoyments needed for successive further worship — this is the meaning. He who enjoys the enjoyments given by them for the purpose of their own worship without offering [back] to them is indeed a thief. For theft is precisely this: having assumed the notion of ownership over a thing belonging to another that was arranged for that other's purpose, using it for the nourishment of one's own self. Therefore, for such a person, it is not merely unfitness for the supreme human goal; but he will also go to hell — this is the intention.

children.text: yajña-bhāvitāḥ --- yajñenā arādhitāḥ mad-ātmakā devāḥ iṣṭān vo dāsyante uttama-puruṣa-artha-lakṣaṇaṃ mokṣaṃ sādhayatāṃ ye iṣṭā bhogās tān pūrva-pūrva-yajña-bhāvitā devā dāsyante uttara-uttara-ārādhana-upekṣitān sarvān bhogān vo dāsyante ity-arthaḥ / sva-ārādhana-arthatayā tair dattān bhogān tebhyo 'pradāya yo bhuṅkte cora eva saḥ / couryaṃ hi nāma anyadīye tat-prayojanāya eva parikḷpte vastuni svakīyatā-buddhiṃ kṛtvā tena sva-ātma-poṣaṇam / ato 'sya na parama-puruṣa-artha-anarhatā-mātram; api tu niraya-gāmitvaṃ ca bhaviṣyati ity-abhiprāyaḥ //

body.text: tad eva vivṛṇoti -
body.translated_text: He elaborates on this very [point]:

children.text: tad eva vivṛṇoti --
yajñaśiṣṭāśinas santo mucyante sarvakilviṣaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The good who eat the remnants of sacrifice are freed from all sins.' |

children.text: te tv aghaṃ bhuñjate pāpā ye pacanty ātmakāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: 'But the wicked who cook for their own sake — they eat sin.' ||

children.text: yajña-śiṣṭa-āśinas santo mucyante sarva-kilviṣaiḥ |
te tv aghaṃ bhuñjate pāpā ye pacanty ātma-kāraṇāt ||

body.text: indrādyātmanāvasthitaparamapuruṣārādhanārthatayaiva dravyāṇy upādāya vipacya tair yathāvasthitaṃ paramapuruṣam ārādhya tacchiṣṭāśanena ye śarīrayātrāṃ kurvate, te tv anādikālopārjitaiḥ kilbiṣaiḥ ātmayāthātmyāvalokanavirodhibhiḥ sarvair mucyante / ye tu paramapuruṣeṇendrādyātmanā svārādhanāya dattāni ātmārthatyopādāya vipacyāśnanti, te pāpātmano 'gham eva bhuñjate / aghapariṇāmitvād agham ity ucyate / ātmāvalokanavimukhāḥ narakāyaiva pacante //
body.translated_text: Those who, having acquired materials for the purpose of worshipping the Supreme Person established in the form of <s>Indra</s> and other [gods], having cooked them, having worshipped the Supreme Person in his proper form thereby, maintain their bodily existence by eating the remnants of that [sacrifice] — they are freed from all sins accumulated since beginningless time that obstruct the vision of the true nature of the self. But those who, having acquired [materials] given by the Supreme Person in the form of <s>Indra</s> and the like for his own worship, and having cooked and eaten them for their own sake — those sinful ones eat nothing but sin. It is called sin (<s>agha</s>) because it transforms into sin. Those who are averse to the vision of the self cook [themselves] for hell alone.
