children.text: indra-ādy-ātmana āvasthita-parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-arthataya aiva dravyāṇy upādāya vipacya tair yathā-avasthitaṃ parama-puruṣam ārādhya tac-chiṣṭa-āśanena ye śarīra-yātrāṃ kurvate, te tv anādi-kāla-upārjitaiḥ kilbiṣaiḥ ātma-yāthātmya-avalokana-virodhibhiḥ sarvair mucyante / ye tu parama-puruṣeṇa indra-ādy-ātmanā sva-ārādhanāya dattāni ātma-arthatya ūpādāya vipacya aśnanti, te pāpā-ātmano 'gham eva bhuñjate / agha-pariṇāmitvād agham ity ucyate / ātma-avalokana-vimukhāḥ narakāya eva pacante //

body.text: punar api lokadṛṣṭyā śāstradṛṣṭyā ca sarvasya yajñamūlatvaṃ darśayitvā yajñānuvartanasyāvaśyakāryatām ananuvartane doṣaṃ cāha --
body.translated_text: Once again, having shown from the standpoint of worldly observation and scriptural authority that everything is rooted in sacrifice, he states the necessity of following sacrifice and the fault of not following it:

children.text: punar api loka-dṛṣṭyā śāstra-dṛṣṭyā ca sarvasya yajña-mūlatvaṃ darśayitvā yajña-anuvartanasya avaśya-kāryatām ananuvartane doṣaṃ cā aha ---
annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād annasaṃbhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'From food beings come into being, from rain comes the production of food.' |

children.text: yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'From sacrifice comes rain, and sacrifice is born from action.' ||

children.text: annād bhavanti bhūtāni parjanyād anna-saṃbhavaḥ |
yajñād bhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karma-samudbhavaḥ ||
karma brahmodbhavaṃ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam |
children.translated_text: 'Know that action arises from <s>Brahman</s>, and <s>Brahman</s> arises from the Imperishable.' |

children.text: tasmāt sarvagataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, the all-pervading <s>Brahman</s> is eternally established in sacrifice.' ||

children.text: karma brahma-udbhavaṃ viddhi brahma akṣara-samudbhavam |
tasmāt sarva-gataṃ brahma nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam ||
evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He who does not follow the wheel thus set in motion here,' |

children.text: aghāyur indriyārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: 'living sinfully, delighting in the senses — he lives in vain, O <s>Pārtha</s>.' ||

children.text: evaṃ pravartitaṃ cakraṃ na anuvartayati iha yaḥ |
agha-āyur indriya-ārāmo moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati ||

body.text: "annāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhavanti parjanyāc cānnasaṃbhavaḥ" iti sarvalokasākṣikam / yajñāt parjanyo bhavatīti ca śāstreṇāvagamyate, "agnau prāstāhutiḥ samyagādityam upatiṣṭhate / ādityāj jāyate vṛṣṭiḥ" ityādinā / yajñaś ca dravyārjanādikartṛvyāpārarūpakarmasamudbhavaḥ, karma ca brahmodbhavam / atra ca brahmaśabdanirdiṣṭaṃ prakṛtipariṇāmarūpaṃ śarīram / "tasmād etad brahma nāma rūpam annaṃ ca jāyate" iti hi brahmaśabdena prakṛtinirdiṣṭā / ihāpi "mama yonir mahad brahma" iti vakṣyate / ataḥ karma brahmodbhavam iti prakṛtipariṇāmarūpaśarīrodbhavaṃ karmetyuktaṃ bhavati / brahmākṣarasamudbhavam ity atrākṣaraśabdanirdiṣṭo jīvātmā, annapānādinā tṛptākṣarādhiṣṭhitaṃ śarīraṃ karmaṇe prabhavatīti karmasādhanabhūtaṃ
body.translated_text: 'From food all beings come into being, and from rain comes the production of food' — this is witnessed by the entire world. That rain comes from sacrifice is understood through scripture: 'The oblation properly offered in the fire reaches the sun; from the sun rain is born' — and the like. Sacrifice arises from action in the form of the agent's effort such as the acquisition of materials. And action arises from <s>Brahman</s>. Here, what is denoted by the word <s>Brahman</s> is the body, which is a transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primal nature). For 'from that, this <s>Brahman</s> — name, form, and food — is born' — here, by the word <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s> is denoted. And here too, 'my womb is the great <s>Brahman</s>' will be stated. Therefore, 'action arises from <s>Brahman</s>' means that action arises from the body, which is a transformation of <s>Prakṛti</s>. '<s>Brahman</s> arises from the Imperishable' — here, what is denoted by the word 'Imperishable' (<s>akṣara</s>) is the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>). The body superintended by the satisfied imperishable [self], [satisfied] through food, drink, and the like, is capable of action — thus the body, which is the instrument of action,

children.text: "annāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhavanti parjanyāc ca anna-saṃbhavaḥ" iti sarva-loka-sākṣikam / yajñāt parjanyo bhavati iti ca śāstreṇa avagamyate, "agnau prāsta-āhutiḥ samyag-ādityam upatiṣṭhate / ādityāj jāyate vṛṣṭiḥ" ity-ādinā / yajñaś ca dravya-arjana-ādi-kartṛ-vyāpāra-rūpa-karma-samudbhavaḥ, karma ca brahma-udbhavam / atra ca brahma-śabda-nirdiṣṭaṃ prakṛti-pariṇāma-rūpaṃ śarīram / "tasmād etad brahma nāma rūpam annaṃ ca jāyate" iti hi brahma-śabdena prakṛti-nirdiṣṭā / iha api "mama yonir mahad brahma" iti vakṣyate / ataḥ karma brahma-udbhavam iti prakṛti-pariṇāma-rūpa-śarīra-udbhavaṃ karma ity-uktaṃ bhavati / brahma-akṣara-samudbhavam ity atra akṣara-śabda-nirdiṣṭo jīva-ātmā, anna-pāna-ādinā tṛpta-akṣara-adhiṣṭhitaṃ śarīraṃ karmaṇe prabhavati iti karma-sādhana-bhūtaṃ

body.text:
śarīram akṣarasamudbhavam; tasmāt sarvagataṃ brahma sarvādhikārigataṃ śarīraṃ nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitaṃ -- yajñamūlam ityarthaḥ / evaṃ paramapuruṣeṇa pravartitam idaṃ cakram annād bhūtaśabdanirdiṣṭāni sajīvāni śarīrāṇi, paryjanyād annam, yajñāt parjanyaḥ, yajñaś ca kartṛvyāpārarūpāt karmaṇaḥ, karma ca sajīvāc charīrāt, sajīvaṃ śarīraṃ punar apy annād ity anyonyakāryakāraṇabhāvena cakravat parivartamānam iha sādhane vartamāno yaḥ karmayogādhikārī jñānayogādhikārī vā nānuvartayati na pravartayati, yajñaśiṣṭena dehadhāraṇam akurvan so 'ghāyur bhavati / aghārambhāyaiva yasyāyuḥ, aghapariṇataṃ vā, ubhayarūpaṃ vā so 'ghāyuḥ / ata evendriyārāmo bhavati, nātmārāmaḥ; indriyāṇy evāsyodyānāni bhavanti;
ayajñaśiṣṭavardhitadehamanastvenodriktarajastamaskaḥ ātmāvalokanavimukhatayā viṣayabhogaikaratir bhavati / ato jñānayogādau yatamāno 'pi niṣphalaprayatnatayā moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati //
body.translated_text: arises from the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading <s>Brahman</s> — the body that pertains to all eligible persons — is eternally established in sacrifice — meaning that sacrifice is its root. This wheel set in motion by the Supreme Person — from food come the bodies designated by the word 'beings,' endowed with life; from rain comes food; from sacrifice comes rain; sacrifice [arises] from action in the form of the agent's effort; action from the body endowed with life; and the body endowed with life again from food — revolving like a wheel through mutual cause-and-effect relationship: he who, being established in this practice, being eligible for <s>karmayoga</s> or <s>jñānayoga</s>, does not follow it, does not set it in motion, not maintaining the body through the remnants of sacrifice — he lives sinfully. One whose life is for the undertaking of sin, or whose [life] has transformed into sin, or both — he is 'one who lives sinfully.' For this very reason he delights in the senses, not in the self; the senses alone become his pleasure-gardens. His body and mind, nourished by what is not the remnant of sacrifice, become excessively dominated by <s>rajas</s> (passion) and <s>tamas</s> (darkness), and he becomes averse to the vision of the self and devoted solely to the enjoyment of sense-objects. Therefore, even though striving for <s>jñānayoga</s> and the like, his effort being fruitless, he lives in vain, O <s>Pārtha</s>.

children.text:
śarīram akṣara-samudbhavam; tasmāt sarva-gataṃ brahma sarva-adhikāri-gataṃ śarīraṃ nityaṃ yajñe pratiṣṭhitaṃ --- yajña-mūlam ity-arthaḥ / evaṃ parama-puruṣeṇa pravartitam idaṃ cakram annād bhūta-śabda-nirdiṣṭāni sajīvāni śarīrāṇi, paryjanyād annam, yajñāt parjanyaḥ, yajñaś ca kartṛ-vyāpāra-rūpāt karmaṇaḥ, karma ca sajīvāc charīrāt, sajīvaṃ śarīraṃ punar apy annād ity anyonya-kārya-kāraṇa-bhāvena cakravat parivartamānam iha sādhane vartamāno yaḥ karma-yoga-adhikārī jñāna-yoga-adhikārī vā na anuvartayati na pravartayati, yajña-śiṣṭena deha-dhāraṇam akurvan so 'gha-āyur bhavati / agha-ārambhāya eva yasyā ayuḥ, agha-pariṇataṃ vā, ubhaya-rūpaṃ vā so 'gha-āyuḥ / ata eva indriya-ārāmo bhavati, nā atma-ārāmaḥ; indriyāṇy eva asya udyānāni bhavanti;
ayajña-śiṣṭa-vardhita-deha-manastvena udrikta-rajas-tamaskaḥ ātma-avalokana-vimukhatayā viṣaya-bhoga-eka-ratir bhavati / ato jñāna-yoga-ādau yatamāno 'pi niṣphala-prayatnatayā moghaṃ pārtha sa jīvati //

body.text: asādhanāyattātmadarśanasya muktasyeva mahāyajñādivarṇāśramocitakarmānārambha ity āha
body.translated_text: He says that for one whose vision of the self is not dependent on [any] means — like one who is already liberated — there is no undertaking of the actions appropriate to one's <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, such as the great sacrifices:

children.text: asādhana-āyatta-ātma-darśanasya muktasya iva mahā-yajña-ādi-varṇa-āśrama-ucita-karma-anārambha ity āha
yas tv ātmaratir eva syād ātmatṛptaś ca mānavaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'But the person who delights in the self alone, who is satisfied in the self,' |

children.text: ātmany eva ca saṃtuṣṭas tasya kāryaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: 'and who is content in the self alone — for him there is no duty to perform.' ||

children.text: yas tv ātma-ratir eva syād ātma-tṛptaś ca mānavaḥ |
ātmany eva ca saṃtuṣṭas tasya kāryaṃ na vidyate ||
naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana |
children.translated_text: 'For him there is no purpose in what is done, nor any [loss] in what is not done here.' |

children.text: na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaścid arthavyapāśrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Nor is there for him any dependence on any being for any purpose.' ||

children.text: na eva tasya kṛtena artho na akṛtena iha kaścana |
na ca asya sarva-bhūteṣu kaścid artha-vyapāśrayaḥ ||

body.text: yas tu jñānayogakarmayogasādhananirapekṣaḥ svata evātmaratiḥ ātmābhimukhaḥ, ātmanaiva tṛptaḥ nānnapānādibhir ātmavyatiriktaiḥ, ātmany eva ca santuṣṭaḥ, nodyānasrakcandanagītavāditranṛttādau, dhāraṇapoṣaṇabhogyādikaṃ sarvam atmaiva yasya, tasyātmadarśanāya kartavyaṃ na vidyate, svata eva sarvadā dṛṣṭātmasvarūpatvāt / ata eva tasyātmadarśanāya kṛtena tatsādhanena nārthaḥ na kiṃcit prayojanam; akṛtenātmadarśanasādhanena na kaścid anarthaḥ; asādhanāyattātmadarśanatvāt / svata evātmavyatiriktasakalācidvastuvimukhasyāsya sarveṣu prakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣeṣv ākāśādiṣu sakāryeṣu na kaścit prayojanatayā sādhanatayā vā vyapāśrayaḥ; yatas tadvimukhīkaraṇāya sādhanārambhaḥ; sa hi mukta eva //
body.translated_text: But he who, independent of the means of <s>jñānayoga</s> and <s>karmayoga</s>, delights in the self spontaneously — is inclined toward the self — is satisfied by the self alone, not by food, drink, and other things external to the self — and is content in the self alone, not in gardens, garlands, sandal-paste, songs, musical instruments, dance, and the like — for whom the self alone is everything: what is to be sustained, nourished, and enjoyed — for him there is no duty to perform for the vision of the self, because the essential nature of the self is always directly seen by him spontaneously. For this very reason, for him there is no purpose — no benefit — in what is done, in any means for the vision of the self; nor any detriment from what is not done, from the absence of any means for the vision of the self — because the vision of the self for him is not dependent on any means. For him who is spontaneously averse to all non-conscious entities external to the self, there is no dependence on anything among all the specific transformations of <s>Prakṛti</s> — ether and the like, together with their effects — either as a purpose or as a means; since the undertaking of means is for the purpose of turning away from those [external objects]. For he is already liberated.

children.text: yas tu jñāna-yoga-karma-yoga-sādhana-nirapekṣaḥ svata evā atma-ratiḥ ātma-abhimukhaḥ, ātmana aiva tṛptaḥ na anna-pāna-ādibhir ātma-vyatiriktaiḥ, ātmany eva ca santuṣṭaḥ, na udyāna-srak-candana-gīta-vāditra-nṛtta-ādau, dhāraṇa-poṣaṇa-bhogya-ādikaṃ sarvam atma aiva yasya, tasyā atma-darśanāya kartavyaṃ na vidyate, svata eva sarvadā dṛṣṭa-ātma-sva-rūpatvāt / ata eva tasyā atma-darśanāya kṛtena tat-sādhanena na arthaḥ na kiṃcit prayojanam; akṛtenā atma-darśana-sādhanena na kaścid anarthaḥ; asādhana-āyatta-ātma-darśanatvāt / svata evā atma-vyatirikta-sakala-acid-vastu-vimukhasya asya sarveṣu prakṛti-pariṇāma-viśeṣeṣv ākāśa-ādiṣu sakāryeṣu na kaścit prayojanatayā sādhanatayā vā vyapāśrayaḥ; yatas tad-vimukhīkaraṇāya sādhana-ārambhaḥ; sa hi mukta eva //
tasmād asaktas satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, always perform the action that is to be done, without attachment.' |

children.text: asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti puruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'For a person who performs action without attachment attains the Supreme.' ||

children.text: tasmād asaktas satataṃ kāryaṃ karma samācara |
asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti puruṣaḥ ||

body.text: yasmād asādhanāyattātmadarśanasyaiva sādhanāpravṛttiḥ, yasmāc ca sādhane pravṛttasyāpi suśakatvāc ca apramādatvād antargatātmayāthātmyānusandhānatvāc ca jñānayogino 'pi mātrayā karmānuvṛttyapekṣatvāc ca karmayoga evātmadarśananirvṛttau śreyān, tasmād asaṅgapūrvakaṃ kāryam ity eva satataṃ yāvadātmaprāpti karmaiva samācara / asaktaḥ, kāryam iti vakṣyamāṇākartṛtvānusandhānapūrvakaṃ ca karmācaran puruṣaḥ karmayogenaiva param āpnoti ātmānaṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Since abstention from the means [of spiritual practice] is only for one whose vision of the self is not dependent on means; and since even for one engaged in the means, the practice of <s>karmayoga</s> alone is superior for the attainment of the vision of the self — because of its being easy to perform, because of its being free from the danger of error, and because even for the <s>jñānayogin</s>, who internally investigates the true nature of the self, there is a need for at least a measure of engagement in action — therefore, always perform action preceded by non-attachment, regarding it as 'duty,' preceded by the contemplation of non-agency that will be described — until the attainment of the self. A person performing action without attachment, [regarding it] as duty, attains the Supreme — attains the self — through <s>karmayoga</s> alone — this is the meaning.

children.text: yasmād asādhana-āyatta-ātma-darśanasya eva sādhana-apravṛttiḥ, yasmāc ca sādhane pravṛttasya api suśakatvāc ca apramādatvād antargata-ātma-yāthātmya-anusandhānatvāc ca jñāna-yogino 'pi mātrayā karma-anuvṛtty-apekṣatvāc ca karma-yoga evā atma-darśana-nirvṛttau śreyān, tasmād asaṅga-pūrvakaṃ kāryam ity eva satataṃ yāvad-ātma-prāpti karma eva samācara / asaktaḥ, kāryam iti vakṣyamāṇa-akartṛtva-anusandhāna-pūrvakaṃ ca karma acaran puruṣaḥ karma-yogena eva param āpnoti ātmānaṃ prāpnoti ity-arthaḥ //
karmaṇaiva hi saṃsiddhim āsthitā janakādayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'For by action alone, <s>Janaka</s> and others attained perfection.' |

children.text: karmaṇa aiva hi saṃsiddhim āsthitā janaka-ādayaḥ |

body.text: yato jñānayogādhikāriṇo 'pi karmayoga evātmadarśane śreyān; ata eva hi janakādayo rājarṣayo jñāninām agresarāḥ karmayogenaiva saṃsiddhim āsthitāḥ ātmānaṃ prāptavantaḥ // evaṃ prathamaṃ mumukṣor jñānayogānarhatayā karmayogādhikāriṇaḥ karmayoga eva kārya ity uktvā jñānayogādhikāriṇo 'pi jñānayogāt karmayoga eva śreyān iti sahetukam uktam / idānīṃ śiṣṭatayā vyapadeśyasya sarvathā karmayoga eva kārya ity ucyate --
body.translated_text: Since even for one eligible for <s>jñānayoga</s>, <s>karmayoga</s> alone is superior for the vision of the self — for this very reason, <s>Janaka</s> and other royal sages, who were the foremost among the wise, attained perfection through <s>karmayoga</s> alone — they attained the self. Thus, having first stated that for the aspirant to liberation who is not eligible for <s>jñānayoga</s> and is eligible only for <s>karmayoga</s>, <s>karmayoga</s> alone is to be practiced, he has then stated with reasons that even for one eligible for <s>jñānayoga</s>, <s>karmayoga</s> is superior to <s>jñānayoga</s>. Now he states that for one renowned as exemplary, <s>karmayoga</s> alone is to be practiced in all circumstances:

children.text: yato jñāna-yoga-adhikāriṇo 'pi karma-yoga evā atma-darśane śreyān; ata eva hi janaka-ādayo rāja-rṣayo jñāninām agresarāḥ karma-yogena eva saṃsiddhim āsthitāḥ ātmānaṃ prāptavantaḥ // evaṃ prathamaṃ mumukṣor jñāna-yoga-anarhatayā karma-yoga-adhikāriṇaḥ karma-yoga eva kārya ity uktvā jñāna-yoga-adhikāriṇo 'pi jñāna-yogāt karma-yoga eva śreyān iti sahetukam uktam / idānīṃ śiṣṭatayā vyapadeśyasya sarvathā karma-yoga eva kārya ity ucyate ---
lokasaṃgraham evāpi saṃpaśyan kartum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: 'Even with a view to the welfare of the world, you should act.' ||

children.text: loka-saṃgraham eva api saṃpaśyan kartum arhasi ||
yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Whatever the best person does, that alone other people also do.' |

children.text: sa yat pramāṇaṃ kurute lokas tad anuvartate ||
children.translated_text: 'Whatever standard he sets, the world follows that.' ||

children.text: yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad eva itaro janaḥ |
sa yat pramāṇaṃ kurute lokas tad anuvartate ||

body.text: lokasaṃgrahaṃ paśyann api karmaiva kartum arhasi / śreṣṭhaḥ kṛtsnaśāstrajñātayānuṣṭhātṛtayā ca prathito yad yad ācarati, tat tad evākṛtsnavij jano 'py ācarati; anuṣṭhīyamānam api karma śreṣṭho yat pramāṇaṃ yadaṅgayuktam anutiṣṭhati tadaṅgayuktam evākṛtsnavilloko 'py anutiṣṭhati / ato lokarakṣārthaṃ śiṣṭatayā prathitena śreṣṭhena svavarṇāśramocitaṃ karma sakalaṃ sarvadā anuṣṭheyam; anyathā lokanāśajanitaṃ pāpaṃ jñānayogād apy enaṃ pracyāvayet //
body.translated_text: Even with a view to the welfare of the world, you should perform action alone. The best person — renowned as one who knows the entire scripture and as one who practices it — whatever he does, that very thing the common person, even though not knowing the whole [scripture], also does. Even the action being performed — whatever the best person performs with the proper ancillaries, and [sets as] the standard — the common person, even though not knowing the whole, performs it with those very ancillaries. Therefore, for the sake of protecting the world, the best person renowned as exemplary should always perform all the action appropriate to his <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>. Otherwise, the sin generated by the destruction of the world would cause him to fall even from <s>jñānayoga</s>.

children.text: loka-saṃgrahaṃ paśyann api karma eva kartum arhasi / śreṣṭhaḥ kṛtsna-śāstra-jñātaya ānuṣṭhātṛtayā ca prathito yad yad ācarati, tat tad eva akṛtsna-vij jano 'py ācarati; anuṣṭhīyamānam api karma śreṣṭho yat pramāṇaṃ yad-aṅga-yuktam anutiṣṭhati tad-aṅga-yuktam eva akṛtsna-vil-loko 'py anutiṣṭhati / ato loka-rakṣā-arthaṃ śiṣṭatayā prathitena śreṣṭhena sva-varṇa-āśrama-ucitaṃ karma sakalaṃ sarvadā anuṣṭheyam; anyathā loka-nāśa-janitaṃ pāpaṃ jñāna-yogād apy enaṃ pracyāvayet //
na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiṃcana |
children.translated_text: 'For me, O <s>Pārtha</s>, there is nothing to be done in the three worlds,' |

children.text: nānavāptam avāptavyaṃ varta eva ca karmaṇi ||
children.translated_text: 'nor is there anything unattained that is to be attained — yet I engage in action.' ||

children.text: na me pārtha asti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiṃcana |
na anavāptam avāptavyaṃ varta eva ca karmaṇi ||

body.text: na me sarveśvarasyāptakāmasya sarvajñasya satyasaṅkalpasya triṣu lokeṣu devamanuṣyādirūpeṇa svacchandato vartamānasya kiṃcid api kartavyam asti, yato 'navāptaṃ karmaṇāvāptavyaṃ na kiṃcid apy asti / athāpi lokarakṣāyai karmaṇy eva varte //
body.translated_text: For me — the Lord of all, whose desires are all fulfilled, who is omniscient, whose will is unfailingly true, who abides in the three worlds in the form of gods, humans, and the like at my own will — there is nothing whatsoever to be done. Because there is nothing whatsoever unattained that is to be attained through action. Yet, for the protection of the world, I engage in action alone.

children.text: na me sarva-īśvarasyā apta-kāmasya sarva-jñasya satya-saṅkalpasya triṣu lokeṣu deva-manuṣya-ādi-rūpeṇa svacchandato vartamānasya kiṃcid api kartavyam asti, yato 'navāptaṃ karmaṇa āvāptavyaṃ na kiṃcid apy asti / atha api loka-rakṣāyai karmaṇy eva varte //
yadi hy ahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇy atandritaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'For if I were not to engage in action, ever unwearied,' |

children.text: mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'human beings, O <s>Pārtha</s>, would follow my path in every way.' ||

children.text: yadi hy ahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇy atandritaḥ |
mama vartma anuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ ||
utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṃ karma ced aham |
children.translated_text: 'These worlds would perish if I did not perform action.' |

children.text: saṃkarasya ca kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'I would be the author of confusion and would destroy these beings.' ||

children.text: utsīdeyur ime lokā na kuryāṃ karma ced aham |
saṃkarasya ca kartā syām upahanyām imāḥ prajāḥ ||

body.text:
ahaṃ sarveśvaraḥ satyasaṅkalpaḥ svasaṅkalpakṛtajagadudayavibhavalayalīlaḥ chandato jagadupakṛtimartyo jāto 'pi manuṣyeṣu śiṣṭajanāgresaravasudevagṛhe 'vatīrṇas tatkulocite karmaṇy atandritas sarvadā yadi na varteya, mama śiṣṭajanāgresaravasudevasūnor vartma akṛtsnavidaḥ śiṣṭāḥ sarvaprakāreṇāyam eva dharma ity anuvartante; te ca svakartavyānanuṣṭhānena akaraṇe pratyavāyena ca ātmānam alabdhvā nirayagāmino bhaveyuḥ / ahaṃ kulocitaṃ karma na cet kuryām, evam eva sarve śiṣṭalokā madācarāyattadharmaniścayāḥ akaraṇād evotsīdeyuḥ naṣṭā bhaveyuḥ / śāstrīyācārānanupālanāt sarveṣāṃ śiṣṭakulānāṃ saṃkarasya ca kartā syām / ata evemāḥ prajāḥ upahanyām / evam eva tvam api śiṣṭajanāgresarapāṇḍutanayo
yudhiṣṭhirānujo 'rjunas san yadi jñānaniṣṭhāyām adhikaroṣi; tatas tvadācārānuvartino 'kṛtsnavidaḥ śiṣṭā mumukṣavaḥ svādhikāram ajānantaḥ karmaniṣṭhāyāṃ nādhikurvanto vinaśyeyuḥ / ato vyapadeśyena viduṣā karmaiva kartavyam //
body.translated_text:
I am the Lord of all, of infallible will, whose sport is the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe brought about by My own will. Though born by My own choice in human form for the benefit of the world, having descended into the house of <s>Vasudeva</s> — the foremost among the virtuous — if I were not always diligently engaged in action befitting that family, then the virtuous — those of incomplete knowledge — following the path of Me, the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>, the foremost among the virtuous, would follow [Me thinking:] 'This alone is the <s>dharma</s> in every respect.' And they, through non-performance of their own duties and the adverse consequences of non-performance, not having attained the self, would become bound for hell. If I were not to perform the actions befitting My family, in just the same way all the virtuous people — whose determination of <s>dharma</s> depends on My conduct — would perish, would be destroyed, through non-performance alone. And I would be the cause of the intermixture of all virtuous families due to non-observance of the conduct prescribed by scripture.
Thus I would destroy these people. In just this way, you too — <s>Arjuna</s>, son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> who is the foremost among the virtuous, younger brother of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> — if you claim authority in the discipline of knowledge (<s>jñānaniṣṭhā</s>), then the virtuous who are seekers of liberation, following your conduct, being of incomplete knowledge, not knowing their own proper authority, and not establishing themselves in the discipline of action (<s>karmaniṣṭhā</s>), would perish. Therefore, the wise person who is a model for others must perform action alone. //

children.text:
ahaṃ sarva-īśvaraḥ satya-saṅkalpaḥ sva-saṅkalpa-kṛta-jagad-udaya-vibhava-laya-līlaḥ chandato jagad-upakṛti-martyo jāto 'pi manuṣyeṣu śiṣṭa-jana-agresara-vasu-deva-gṛhe 'vatīrṇas tat-kula-ucite karmaṇy atandritas sarvadā yadi na varteya, mama śiṣṭa-jana-agresara-vasu-deva-sūnor vartma akṛtsna-vidaḥ śiṣṭāḥ sarva-prakāreṇa ayam eva dharma ity anuvartante; te ca sva-kartavya-ananuṣṭhānena akaraṇe pratyavāyena ca ātmānam alabdhvā niraya-gāmino bhaveyuḥ / ahaṃ kula-ucitaṃ karma na cet kuryām, evam eva sarve śiṣṭa-lokā mad-ācara-āyatta-dharma-niścayāḥ akaraṇād eva utsīdeyuḥ naṣṭā bhaveyuḥ / śāstrīya-ācāra-ananupālanāt sarveṣāṃ śiṣṭa-kulānāṃ saṃkarasya ca kartā syām / ata eva imāḥ prajāḥ upahanyām / evam eva tvam api śiṣṭa-jana-agresara-pāṇḍu-tanayo
yudhiṣṭhira-anujo 'rjunas san yadi jñāna-niṣṭhāyām adhikaroṣi; tatas tvad-ācāra-anuvartino 'kṛtsna-vidaḥ śiṣṭā mumukṣavaḥ sva-adhikāram ajānantaḥ karma-niṣṭhāyāṃ na adhikurvanto vinaśyeyuḥ / ato vyapadeśyena viduṣā karma eva kartavyam //
saktāḥ karmaṇy avidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata |
children.translated_text: The ignorant, attached to action, perform [it] as they do, O <s>Bhārata</s>; |

children.text: kuryād vidvāṃs tathāsaktaś cikīrṣur lokasaṃgraham ||
children.translated_text: so should the wise person, unattached, perform [action], desiring the welfare of the world. ||

children.text: saktāḥ karmaṇy avidvāṃso yathā kurvanti bhārata |
kuryād vidvāṃs tatha āsaktaś cikīrṣur loka-saṃgraham ||
na buddhibhedaṃ janayed ajñānāṃ karmasaṅginām |
children.translated_text: Let not [the wise person] create confusion of understanding in the ignorant who are attached to action; |

children.text: joṣayet sarvakarmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran ||
children.translated_text: the wise person, being disciplined, performing all actions, should cause [them] to delight [in action]. ||

children.text: na buddhi-bhedaṃ janayed ajñānāṃ karma-saṅginām |
joṣayet sarva-karmāṇi vidvān yuktaḥ samācaran ||

body.text:
avidvāṃsaḥ ātmany akṛtsnavidaḥ, karmaṇi saktāḥ karmaṇy avarjanīyasaṃbandhāḥ ātmany akṛtsnavittayā tadabhyāsarūpajñānayoge 'nadhikṛtāḥ karmayogādhikāriṇaḥ karmayogam eva yathā ātmadarśanāya kurvate, tathā ātmani kṛtsnavittayā karmaṇy asaktaḥ jñānayogādhikārayogyo 'pi vyapadeśyaḥ śiṣṭo lokarakṣārthaṃ svācāreṇa śiṣṭalokānāṃ dharmaniścayaṃ cikīrṣuḥ karmayogam eva kuryāt / ajñānām ātmany akṛtsnavittayā jñānayogopādānāśaktānāṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ karmasaṅginām anādikarmavāsanayā karmaṇy eva niyatatvena karmayogādhikāriṇāṃ karmayogād anyad ātmāvalokanasādhanam astīti na buddhibhedaṃ janayet / kiṃ tarhi? ātmani kṛtsnavittayā jñānayogaśakto 'pi pūrvoktarītyā, "karmayoga eva jñānayoganirapekṣaḥ
ātmāvalokanasādhanam" iti buddhyā yuktaḥ karmaivācaran
body.translated_text:
The ignorant — those of incomplete knowledge regarding the self — are attached to action, i.e., have an unavoidable connection with action. Because of their incomplete knowledge of the self, not being qualified for the discipline of knowledge in the form of the practice [of self-realization], they are qualified for <s>karmayoga</s>. Just as they perform <s>karmayoga</s> alone for the vision of the self, so too the wise person who is a model for others — though qualified for the discipline of knowledge because of complete knowledge of the self — unattached to action, desiring to establish the determination of <s>dharma</s> for the virtuous through his own conduct for the protection of the world, should perform <s>karmayoga</s> alone. Let him not create confusion of understanding in the ignorant — those who, because of incomplete knowledge of the self, are unable to take up the discipline of knowledge, who are seekers of liberation, who are attached to action because of being bound to action by beginningless latent impressions (<s>karmasaṅgin</s>) and thus qualified for <s>karmayoga</s> — [thinking:] 'there exists a means of self-realization other than <s>karmayoga</s>.' Rather, the wise person, though capable of the discipline of knowledge because of complete knowledge of the self, endowed with the understanding that '<s>karmayoga</s> alone, independent of the discipline of knowledge,
is the means of self-realization' — in the manner previously stated — performing action alone,

children.text:
avidvāṃsaḥ ātmany akṛtsna-vidaḥ, karmaṇi saktāḥ karmaṇy avarjanīya-saṃbandhāḥ ātmany akṛtsna-vittayā tad-abhyāsa-rūpa-jñāna-yoge 'nadhikṛtāḥ karma-yoga-adhikāriṇaḥ karma-yogam eva yathā ātma-darśanāya kurvate, tathā ātmani kṛtsna-vittayā karmaṇy asaktaḥ jñāna-yoga-adhikāra-yogyo 'pi vyapadeśyaḥ śiṣṭo loka-rakṣā-arthaṃ sva-ācāreṇa śiṣṭa-lokānāṃ dharma-niścayaṃ cikīrṣuḥ karma-yogam eva kuryāt / ajñānām ātmany akṛtsna-vittayā jñāna-yoga-upādāna-aśaktānāṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ karma-saṅginām anādi-karma-vāsanayā karmaṇy eva niyatatvena karma-yoga-adhikāriṇāṃ karma-yogād anyad ātma-avalokana-sādhanam asti iti na buddhi-bhedaṃ janayet / kiṃ tarhi? ātmani kṛtsna-vittayā jñāna-yoga-śakto 'pi pūrva-ukta-rītyā, "karma-yoga eva jñāna-yoga-nirapekṣaḥ
ātma-avalokana-sādhanam" iti buddhyā yuktaḥ karma evā acaran

body.text: sakalakarmasu akṛtsnavidāṃ prītiṃ janayet //
body.translated_text: should generate delight in all actions among those of incomplete knowledge. //

children.text: sakala-karmasu akṛtsna-vidāṃ prītiṃ janayet //

body.text: karmayogam anutiṣṭhato viduṣo 'viduṣaś ca viśeṣaṃ pradarśayan karmayogāpekṣitam ātmano 'kartṛtvānusandhānaprakāram upadiśati --
body.translated_text: Showing the difference between the wise and the unwise in performing <s>karmayoga</s>, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] teaches the manner of contemplating the non-agency of the self, which is required for <s>karmayoga</s>:

children.text: karma-yogam anutiṣṭhato viduṣo 'viduṣaś ca viśeṣaṃ pradarśayan karma-yoga-apekṣitam ātmano 'kartṛtva-anusandhāna-prakāram upadiśati ---
prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāṇi guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: All actions are performed by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s> in every way. |

children.text: ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā kartāham iti manyate ||
children.translated_text: One whose self is deluded by the ego thinks 'I am the doer.' ||

children.text: prakṛteḥ kriyamāṇāṇi guṇaiḥ karmāṇi sarvaśaḥ |
ahaṅkāra-vimūḍha-ātmā karta āham iti manyate ||
tattvavit tu mahābāho guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ |
children.translated_text: But one who knows the truth, O mighty-armed one, of the division of <s>guṇas</s> and actions, |

children.text: guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate ||
children.translated_text: [thinking:] '<s>guṇas</s> operate among <s>guṇas</s>' — does not become attached. ||

children.text: tattva-vit tu mahā-bāho guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ |
guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate ||

body.text: prakṛter guṇaiḥ sattvādibhiḥ svānurūpaṃ kriyamāṇāni karmāṇi prati ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā, ahaṃ karteti manyate; ahaṅkāreṇa vimūḍha ātmā yasyāsāv ahaṅkāravimūḍhātmā; ahaṅkāro nāma anahamarthe prakṛtāv ahamabhimānaḥ; tena ajñātasvarūpo guṇakarmasu ahaṃ karteti manyata ityarthaḥ / guṇakarmavibhāgayoḥ sattvādiguṇavibhāge tattatkarmavibhāge ca tattvavit, guṇās sattvādayaḥ guṇeṣu sveṣu kāryeṣu vartanta iti matvā guṇakarmasu ahaṃ karteti na sajjate //
body.translated_text: Regarding the actions being performed in accordance with [one's nature] by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the like — one whose self is deluded by the ego thinks 'I am the doer.' One whose self (<s>ātmā</s>) is deluded by the ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) is called 'one whose self is deluded by the ego.' The ego (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>) is the conceit of 'I' with respect to <s>Prakṛti</s>, which is not the [true] self. Through that [ego], one whose true nature is unknown thinks 'I am the doer' regarding the actions of the <s>guṇas</s> — this is the meaning. One who knows the truth regarding the division of the <s>guṇas</s> and actions — the division of <s>guṇas</s> such as <s>sattva</s> and the like, and the division of their respective actions — thinking '<s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the like — operate among <s>guṇas</s>, i.e., in their own products,' does not become attached [thinking] 'I am the doer' regarding the actions of the <s>guṇas</s>. //

children.text: prakṛter guṇaiḥ sattva-ādibhiḥ sva-anurūpaṃ kriyamāṇāni karmāṇi prati ahaṅkāra-vimūḍha-ātmā, ahaṃ karta īti manyate; ahaṅkāreṇa vimūḍha ātmā yasya asāv ahaṅkāra-vimūḍha-ātmā; ahaṅkāro nāma anaham-arthe prakṛtāv aham-abhimānaḥ; tena ajñāta-sva-rūpo guṇa-karmasu ahaṃ karta īti manyata ity-arthaḥ / guṇa-karma-vibhāgayoḥ sattva-ādi-guṇa-vibhāge tat-tat-karma-vibhāge ca tattva-vit, guṇās sattva-ādayaḥ guṇeṣu sveṣu kāryeṣu vartanta iti matvā guṇa-karmasu ahaṃ karta īti na sajjate //
prakṛter guṇasaṃmūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇakarmasu |
children.translated_text: Those who are deluded by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s> become attached to the actions of the <s>guṇas</s>. |

children.text: tān akṛtsnavido mandān kṛtsnavin na vicālayet ||
children.translated_text: The one who knows the whole should not unsettle those dull ones of incomplete knowledge. ||

children.text: prakṛter guṇa-saṃmūḍhāḥ sajjante guṇa-karmasu |
tān akṛtsna-vido mandān kṛtsna-vin na vicālayet ||

body.text:
akṛtsnavidaḥ svātmadarśanāya pravṛttāḥ prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭatayā prakṛter guṇair yathāvasthitātmani saṃmūḍhāḥ guṇakarmasu kriyāsv eva sajjante, na tadviviktātmasvarūpe / atas te jñānayogāya na prabhavantīti karmayoga eva teṣām adhikāraḥ / evaṃbhūtāṃs tān mandān akṛtsnavidaḥ kṛtsnavit svayaṃ jñānayogāvasthānena na vicālayet / te kila mandāḥ śreṣṭhajanācārānuvartinaḥ karmayogād utthitam enaṃ dṛṣṭvā karmayogāt pracalitamanaso bhaveyuḥ / ataḥ śreṣṭhaḥ svayam api karmayoge tiṣṭhan ātmayāthātmyajñānenātmano 'kartṛtvam anusandhānaḥ, karmayoga evātmāvalokane nirapekṣasādhanam iti darśayitvā tān akṛtsnavido joṣayed ityarthaḥ / jñānayogādhikāriṇo 'pi jñānayogād asyaiva jyāyastvaṃ pūrvam evoktam / ato
vyapadeśyo lokasaṃgrahāyaitam eva kuryāt //
body.translated_text:
Those of incomplete knowledge, engaged in the vision of their own self, being deluded regarding the self as it truly is because of [its] conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s>, by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s>, become attached to the actions of the <s>guṇas</s> — to activities alone — not to the essential nature of the self distinct from those [<s>guṇas</s>]. Therefore, since they are not capable of the discipline of knowledge, <s>karmayoga</s> alone is their proper domain. Such dull ones of incomplete knowledge — the one who knows the whole should not unsettle them by himself standing in the discipline of knowledge. For those dull ones, who follow the conduct of eminent persons, upon seeing this [wise one] risen from <s>karmayoga</s>, would become unsettled in mind regarding <s>karmayoga</s>. Therefore, the eminent person, himself also remaining in <s>karmayoga</s>, contemplating the non-agency of the self through the true knowledge of the self, having shown that <s>karmayoga</s> alone is an independent means for the vision of the self, should cause those of incomplete knowledge to delight [in it] — this is the meaning. The superiority of this [<s>karmayoga</s>] over the discipline of knowledge, even for one qualified for the latter, has been previously stated.
Therefore, the model person should perform this alone for the welfare of the world. //

children.text:
akṛtsna-vidaḥ sva-ātma-darśanāya pravṛttāḥ prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭatayā prakṛter guṇair yathā-avasthita-ātmani saṃmūḍhāḥ guṇa-karmasu kriyāsv eva sajjante, na tad-vivikta-ātma-sva-rūpe / atas te jñāna-yogāya na prabhavanti iti karma-yoga eva teṣām adhikāraḥ / evaṃ-bhūtāṃs tān mandān akṛtsna-vidaḥ kṛtsna-vit svayaṃ jñāna-yoga-avasthānena na vicālayet / te kila mandāḥ śreṣṭha-jana-ācāra-anuvartinaḥ karma-yogād utthitam enaṃ dṛṣṭvā karma-yogāt pracalita-manaso bhaveyuḥ / ataḥ śreṣṭhaḥ svayam api karma-yoge tiṣṭhan ātma-yāthātmya-jñānenā atmano 'kartṛtvam anusandhānaḥ, karma-yoga evā atma-avalokane nirapekṣa-sādhanam iti darśayitvā tān akṛtsna-vido joṣayed ity-arthaḥ / jñāna-yoga-adhikāriṇo 'pi jñāna-yogād asya eva jyāyastvaṃ pūrvam eva uktam / ato
vyapadeśyo loka-saṃgrahāya etam eva kuryāt //

body.text: prakṛtiviviktātmasvabhāvanirūpaṇena guṇeṣu kartṛtvam āropya karmānuṣṭhānaprakāra uktaḥ -- guṇeṣu kartṛtvānusandhānaṃ cedam eva -- ātmano na svarūpaprayuktam idaṃ kartṛtvam, api tu guṇasamparkakṛtam iti prāptāprāptavivekena guṇakṛtam ity anusandhānam -- idānīm ātmanāṃ paramapuruṣaśarīratayā tanniyāmyatvasvarūpanirūpaṇena bhagavati puruṣottame sarvātmabhūte guṇakṛtaṃ ca kartṛtvam āropya karmakartavyatocyate --
body.translated_text: Through the determination of the essential nature of the self as distinct from <s>Prakṛti</s>, the manner of performing action by attributing agency to the <s>guṇas</s> has been stated. And this contemplation of agency in the <s>guṇas</s> is this alone: 'This agency of mine is not inherent in my essential nature, but rather is produced by the conjunction with the <s>guṇas</s>' — the contemplation that [agency] is produced by the <s>guṇas</s>, through the discrimination of what is [truly] attained and what is not. Now, through the determination of the essential nature of all selves as having the Supreme Person as their body (<s>paramapuruṣaśarīratā</s>) and being controlled by Him, by attributing both the agency produced by the <s>guṇas</s> to the Blessed <s>Puruṣottama</s> — who is the self of all — the obligatory nature of action is stated:

children.text: prakṛti-vivikta-ātma-sva-bhāva-nirūpaṇena guṇeṣu kartṛtvam āropya karma-anuṣṭhāna-prakāra uktaḥ --- guṇeṣu kartṛtva-anusandhānaṃ ca idam eva --- ātmano na sva-rūpa-prayuktam idaṃ kartṛtvam, api tu guṇa-samparka-kṛtam iti prāpta-aprāpta-vivekena guṇa-kṛtam ity anusandhānam --- idānīm ātmanāṃ parama-puruṣa-śarīratayā tan-niyāmyatva-sva-rūpa-nirūpaṇena bhagavati puruṣa-uttame sarva-ātma-bhūte guṇa-kṛtaṃ ca kartṛtvam āropya karma-kartavyata ūcyate ---
mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā |
children.translated_text: Surrendering all actions to Me, with a mind fixed on the self, |

children.text: nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigatajvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: free from desire, free from possessiveness, fight, freed from [inner] fever. ||

children.text: mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya adhyātma-cetasā |
nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā yudhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ ||

body.text:
mayi sarveśvare sarvabhūtāntarātmabhūte sarvāṇi karmāṇy adhyātmacetasā saṃnyasya, nirāśīr nirmamaś ca vigatajvaro yuddhādikaṃ sarvaṃ coditaṃ karma kuruṣva / ātmani yac cetaḥ tad adhyātmacetaḥ / ātmasvarūpaviṣayeṇa śrutiśatasiddhena jñānenetyarthaḥ / "antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānāṃ sarvātmā ..... antaḥ praviṣṭaṃ kartāram etam" "ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyātmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati, sa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ" ity evam ādyāḥ śrutayaḥ paramapuruṣapravartyaṃ taccharīrabhūtam enam ātmānam, paramapuruṣaṃ ca pravartayitāram ācakṣate / smṛtayaś ca "praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām" ityādyāḥ / "sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca", "īśvaras sarvabhūtānāṃ
hṛddeśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati / bhrāmayan sarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā // BhGR_3." iti vakṣyate / ato maccharīratayā matpravartyātmasvarūpānusandhānena sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayaiva kriyamāṇānīti mayi paramapuruṣe saṃnyasya, tāni ca kevalaṃ madārādhanānīti kṛtvā tatphale nirāśīḥ, tata eva tatra karmaṇi mamatārahito bhūtvā vigatajvaro yuddhādikaṃ kuruṣva -  svakīyenātmanā kartrā svakīyaiś copakaraṇaiḥ svārādhanaikaprayojanāya paramapuruṣaḥ sarvaśeṣī sarveśvaraḥ svayam eva svakarmāṇi kārayatīty anusandhāya, karmas mamatārahitaḥ, prācīnenānādikālapravṛttānantapāpasañcayena katham ahaṃ bhaviṣyāmīty evaṃbhūtāntarjvaravinirmuktaḥ, paramapuruṣa eva karmabhir ārādhito bandhān mocayiṣyatīti sukhena karmayogam eva
kuruṣv ityarthaḥ / "tam īśvarāṇāṃ paramaṃ maheśvaraṃ taṃ daivatānāṃ paramaṃ ca daivatam", "patiṃ viśvasya" , "patiṃ patīnām" ityādiśrutisiddhiṃ hi sarveśvaratvaṃ sarvaśeṣitvaṃ ca / īśvaratvam niyantṛtvam, śeṣitvaṃ patitvam //
body.translated_text:
Surrendering all actions to Me — the Lord of all, the inner self of all beings — with a mind fixed on the self (<s>adhyātmacetas</s>), free from desire, free from possessiveness, and freed from [inner] fever, perform battle and all other enjoined actions. 'A mind fixed on the self' (<s>adhyātmacetas</s>) means a mind directed toward the self — i.e., with the knowledge established by hundreds of <s>Śruti</s> texts concerning the essential nature of the self. 'He who has entered within, the ruler of all people, the self of all..... the agent who has entered within'; 'He who stands in the self, who is inner to the self, whom the self does not know, whose body is the self, who controls the self from within — He is your inner controller, the immortal self' — such <s>Śrutis</s> declare this self to be the body of the Supreme Person, set in motion by Him, and the Supreme Person to be the initiator. And <s>Smṛtis</s> too: 'the ruler of all' and the like. 'And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me come memory, knowledge, and their removal';
'The Lord, O <s>Arjuna</s>, dwells in the heart-region of all beings, causing all beings to revolve as if mounted on a machine, by [His] <s>māyā</s>.' — thus it will be said. Therefore, through the contemplation that the essential nature of the self, being My body and set in motion by Me, [entails that] all actions are being performed by Me, the Supreme Person, alone — surrendering [all actions] to Me, and regarding those [actions] as solely for My worship (<s>ārādhana</s>), free from desire regarding their fruit, and for that very reason free from the sense of 'mine' regarding those actions, freed from [inner] fever — perform battle and the like. The Supreme Person, the master of all, the Lord of all, Himself causes His own actions to be performed, through the agent which is His own self, and through His own instruments, for the sole purpose of His own worship — contemplating thus, free from possessiveness regarding action, freed from the inner fever [of thinking:] 'How shall I fare, burdened by the beginningless accumulated mass of sins committed since time without beginning?' — [knowing that] the Supreme Person Himself, worshipped through actions, will liberate [you] from bondage — happily perform <s>karmayoga</s> alone — this is the meaning. For 'Him, the supreme great Lord among lords, Him, the supreme deity among deities,' 'the Lord of the universe,' 'the Lord of lords' — these <s>Śruti</s> texts establish His Lordship over all and His being the master of all. Lordship is the power to control; mastership is sovereignty. //

children.text:
mayi sarva-īśvare sarva-bhūta-antara-ātma-bhūte sarvāṇi karmāṇy adhyātma-cetasā saṃnyasya, nirāśīr nirmamaś ca vigata-jvaro yuddha-ādikaṃ sarvaṃ coditaṃ karma kuruṣva / ātmani yac cetaḥ tad adhyātma-cetaḥ / ātma-sva-rūpa-viṣayeṇa śruti-śata-siddhena jñānena ity-arthaḥ / "antaḥ praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānāṃ sarva-ātmā ..... antaḥ praviṣṭaṃ kartāram etam" "ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyā atmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati, sa ta ātma āntaryāmy-amṛtaḥ" ity evam ādyāḥ śrutayaḥ parama-puruṣa-pravartyaṃ tac-charīra-bhūtam enam ātmānam, parama-puruṣaṃ ca pravartayitāram ācakṣate / smṛtayaś ca "praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām" ity-ādyāḥ / "sarvasya ca ahaṃ hṛdi san-niviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca", "īśvaras sarva-bhūtānāṃ
hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati / bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantra-ārūḍhāni māyayā // BhGR_3." iti vakṣyate / ato mac-charīratayā mat-pravarty-ātma-sva-rūpa-anusandhānena sarvāṇi karmāṇi maya aiva kriyamāṇāni iti mayi parama-puruṣe saṃnyasya, tāni ca kevalaṃ mad-ārādhanāni iti kṛtvā tat-phale nirāśīḥ, tata eva tatra karmaṇi mamatā-rahito bhūtvā vigata-jvaro yuddha-ādikaṃ kuruṣva -- - svakīyenā atmanā kartrā svakīyaiś ca upakaraṇaiḥ sva-ārādhana-eka-prayojanāya parama-puruṣaḥ sarva-śeṣī sarva-īśvaraḥ svayam eva sva-karmāṇi kārayati ity anusandhāya, karmas mamatā-rahitaḥ, prācīnena anādi-kāla-pravṛtta-ananta-pāpa-sañcayena katham ahaṃ bhaviṣyāmi ity evaṃ-bhūta-antarjvara-vinirmuktaḥ, parama-puruṣa eva karmabhir ārādhito bandhān mocayiṣyati iti sukhena karma-yogam eva
kuruṣv ity-arthaḥ / "tam īśvarāṇāṃ paramaṃ mahā-īśvaraṃ taṃ daivatānāṃ paramaṃ ca daivatam", "patiṃ viśvasya" , "patiṃ patīnām" ity-ādi-śruti-siddhiṃ hi sarva-īśvaratvaṃ sarva-śeṣitvaṃ ca / īśvaratvam niyantṛtvam, śeṣitvaṃ patitvam //

body.text: ayam eva sākṣād upaniṣatsārabhūto 'rtha ityāha --
body.translated_text: Saying that this alone is the directly stated essence of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>:

children.text: ayam eva sākṣād upaniṣat-sāra-bhūto 'rtha ity-āha ---
ye me matam idaṃ nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who always follow this teaching of Mine, |

children.text: śraddhāvanto 'nasūyanto mucyante te 'pi karmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: faithful and free from envy — they too are freed from [the bondage of] actions. ||

children.text: ye me matam idaṃ nityam anutiṣṭhanti mānavāḥ |
śraddhāvanto 'nasūyanto mucyante te 'pi karmabhiḥ ||

body.text: ye mānavāḥ śāstrādhikāriṇaḥ ayam eva śāstrārtha iti etan me mataṃ niścitya tathānutiṣṭhanti, ye cānanutiṣṭhanto 'py asmin śāstrārthe śraddadhānā bhavanti, ye cāśraddadhānā api evaṃ śāstrārtho na saṃbhavatīti nābhyasūyanti -- asmin mahāguṇe śāstrārthe doṣam anāviṣkurvanto bhavantītyarthaḥ -- te sarve bandhahetubhir anādikālārabdhais sarvaiḥ karmabhir mucyante; te 'pi ity apiśabdād eṣāṃ pṛthakkaraṇam / idānīm ananutiṣṭhanto 'py asmin śāstrārthe śraddadhānā anabhyasūyavaś ca śraddhayā cānasūyayā ca kṣīṇapāpāḥ acireṇemam eva śāstrārtham anuṣṭhāya mucyanta ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Those humans qualified for [following] scripture who, having ascertained that this is the meaning of scripture and that this is My teaching, follow accordingly; and those who, even without following [it], have faith in this meaning of scripture; and those who, even without faith, do not cavil — i.e., do not impute faults to this most excellent meaning of scripture — they are all freed from all actions that have been the cause of bondage since beginningless time. By the word 'too' (<s>api</s>), these [three groups] are distinguished separately. The meaning is: those who presently, even without following [it], have faith in this meaning of scripture and are free from envy — they, with their sins destroyed through faith and non-envy, will soon follow this very meaning of scripture and be freed. //

children.text: ye mānavāḥ śāstra-adhikāriṇaḥ ayam eva śāstra-artha iti etan me mataṃ niścitya tatha ānutiṣṭhanti, ye ca ananutiṣṭhanto 'py asmin śāstra-arthe śraddadhānā bhavanti, ye ca aśraddadhānā api evaṃ śāstra-artho na saṃbhavati iti na abhyasūyanti --- asmin mahā-guṇe śāstra-arthe doṣam anāviṣkurvanto bhavanti ity-arthaḥ --- te sarve bandha-hetubhir anādi-kāla-ārabdhais sarvaiḥ karmabhir mucyante; te 'pi ity api-śabdād eṣāṃ pṛthak-karaṇam / idānīm ananutiṣṭhanto 'py asmin śāstra-arthe śraddadhānā anabhyasūyavaś ca śraddhayā ca anasūyayā ca kṣīṇa-pāpāḥ acireṇa imam eva śāstra-artham anuṣṭhāya mucyanta ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: bhagavadabhimatam aupaniṣadam artham ananutiṣṭhatām aśraddadhānānām abhyasūyatāṃ ca doṣam āha --
body.translated_text: [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] states the fault of those who do not follow the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> meaning that is approved by the Lord, who lack faith, and who cavil:

children.text: bhagavad-abhimatam aupaniṣadam artham ananutiṣṭhatām aśraddadhānānām abhyasūyatāṃ ca doṣam āha ---
ye tv etad abhyasūyanto nānutiṣṭhanti me matam |
children.translated_text: But those who, caviling, do not follow this teaching of Mine — |

children.text: sarvajñānavimūḍhāṃs tān viddhi naṣṭān acetasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: know them to be deluded in all knowledge, lost, and senseless. ||

children.text: ye tv etad abhyasūyanto na anutiṣṭhanti me matam |
sarva-jñāna-vimūḍhāṃs tān viddhi naṣṭān acetasaḥ ||

body.text: ye tv etat sarvam ātmavastu maccharīratayā madādhāraṃ maccheṣabhūtaṃ madekapravartyam iti me mataṃ nānutiṣṭhanti naivam anusandhāya sarvāṇi karmāṇi kurvate, ye ca na śraddadhate, ye cābhyasūyanto vartante -- tān sarveṣu jñāneṣu viśeṣeṇa mūḍhān tata eva naṣṭān, acetaso viddhi; cetaḥkāryaṃ hi vastuyāthātmyaniścayaḥ; tadabhāvād acetasaḥ; viparītajñānāḥ sarvatra vimūḍhāś ca //
body.translated_text: But those who do not follow My teaching — that all this — the self-substance — has Me as its body, is supported by Me, exists as My accessory, and is set in motion by Me alone — [those who] do not thus contemplate and perform all actions; and those who do not have faith; and those who cavil — know them to be especially deluded regarding all forms of knowledge, hence lost, and senseless. For the function of the mind is the ascertainment of the true nature of things; in its absence, [they are] senseless; [they are] those of perverted knowledge and deluded everywhere. //

children.text: ye tv etat sarvam ātma-vastu mac-charīratayā mad-ādhāraṃ mac-cheṣa-bhūtaṃ mad-eka-pravartyam iti me mataṃ na anutiṣṭhanti na evam anusandhāya sarvāṇi karmāṇi kurvate, ye ca na śraddadhate, ye ca abhyasūyanto vartante --- tān sarveṣu jñāneṣu viśeṣeṇa mūḍhān tata eva naṣṭān, acetaso viddhi; cetaḥ-kāryaṃ hi vastu-yāthātmya-niścayaḥ; tad-abhāvād acetasaḥ; viparīta-jñānāḥ sarvatra vimūḍhāś ca //

body.text: evaṃ prakṛtisaṃsargiṇas tadguṇodrekakṛtaṃ kartṛtvam, tac ca paramapuruṣāyattam ity anusandhāya karmayogayogyena jñānayogayogyena ca karmayogasya suśakatvād apramādatvād antargatātmajñānatayā nirapekṣatvāt, itarasya duśśakatvāt sapramādatvāc śarīradhāraṇādyarthatayā karmāpekṣatvāt karmayoga eva kartavyaḥ; vyapadeśyasya tu viśeṣataḥ sa eva kartavyaḥ iti coktam / ataḥ param adhyāyaśeṣeṇa jñānayogasya duśśakatayā sapramādatocyate --
body.translated_text: Thus, [it has been stated that] agency belongs to one conjoined with <s>Prakṛti</s> and is produced by the predominance of its <s>guṇas</s>, and that too is dependent on the Supreme Person — contemplating thus, because of the ease of <s>karmayoga</s>, its freedom from error, and its independence due to incorporating knowledge of the self, versus the difficulty of the discipline of knowledge, its liability to error, and its dependence on action for the maintenance of the body and the like — both for one qualified for <s>karmayoga</s> and for one qualified for the discipline of knowledge, <s>karmayoga</s> alone is to be performed. But for the model person especially, that alone is to be performed — this too has been stated. Hereafter, in the remainder of the chapter, the difficulty and liability to error of the discipline of knowledge are stated:

children.text: evaṃ prakṛti-saṃsargiṇas tad-guṇa-udreka-kṛtaṃ kartṛtvam, tac ca parama-puruṣa-āyattam ity anusandhāya karma-yoga-yogyena jñāna-yoga-yogyena ca karma-yogasya suśakatvād apramādatvād antargata-ātma-jñānatayā nirapekṣatvāt, itarasya duśśakatvāt sapramādatvāc śarīra-dhāraṇa-ādy-arthatayā karma-apekṣatvāt karma-yoga eva kartavyaḥ; vyapadeśyasya tu viśeṣataḥ sa eva kartavyaḥ iti ca uktam / ataḥ param adhyāya-śeṣeṇa jñāna-yogasya duśśakatayā sapramādata ūcyate ---
sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛter jñānavān api |
children.translated_text: Even a person of knowledge acts in conformity with his own nature (<s>Prakṛti</s>). |

children.text: prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Beings follow [their] nature — what can restraint accomplish? ||

children.text: sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate svasyāḥ prakṛter jñānavān api |
prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati ||

body.text: prakṛtiviviktam īdṛśam ātmasvarūpam, tad eva sarvadānusandheyam iti ca śāstrāṇi pratipādayantīti jñānavān api svasyāḥ prakṛteḥ prācīnavāsanāyās sadṛśaṃ prākṛtaviṣayeṣv eva ceṣṭate; kutaḥ? prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni -- acitsaṃsṛṣṭā jantavo 'nādikālapravṛttavāsanām evānuyānti; tāni vāsanānuyāyīni bhūtāni śāstrakṛto nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati //
body.translated_text: The essential nature of the self is such — distinct from <s>Prakṛti</s> — and that alone is to be always contemplated: thus the scriptures teach. Yet even a person of knowledge acts in conformity with his own nature (<s>Prakṛti</s>) — with past latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). Why? Because beings follow [their] nature — beings conjoined with unconscious matter follow the latent impressions accumulated since beginningless time. What can the restraint imposed by scripture accomplish upon those beings that follow [their] latent impressions? //

children.text: prakṛti-viviktam īdṛśam ātma-sva-rūpam, tad eva sarvada ānusandheyam iti ca śāstrāṇi pratipādayanti iti jñānavān api svasyāḥ prakṛteḥ prācīna-vāsanāyās sadṛśaṃ prākṛta-viṣayeṣv eva ceṣṭate; kutaḥ? prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni --- acit-saṃsṛṣṭā jantavo 'nādi-kāla-pravṛtta-vāsanām eva anuyānti; tāni vāsanā-anuyāyīni bhūtāni śāstra-kṛto nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati //

body.text: prakṛtyanuyāyitvaprakāram āha --
body.translated_text: He states the manner in which [beings] follow [their] nature:

children.text: prakṛty-anuyāyitva-prakāram āha ---
indriyasyendriyasyārthe rāgadveṣau vyavasthitau |
children.translated_text: Attachment and aversion are established with respect to each sense organ's object. |

children.text: tayor na vaśam āgacchet tau hy asya paripanthinau ||
children.translated_text: Let one not come under the sway of those two, for they are one's adversaries. ||

children.text: indriyasya indriyasya arthe rāga-dveṣau vyavasthitau |
tayor na vaśam āgacchet tau hy asya paripanthinau ||

body.text: śrotrādijñānendriyasyārthe śabdādau vāgādikarmendriyasya cārthe vacanādau prācīnavāsanājanitatadanububhūṣārūpo yo rāgo 'varjanīyo vyavasthitaḥ; tadanubhave pratihate cāvarjanīyo yo dveṣo vyavasthitaḥ, tāv evaṃ jñānayogāya yatamānaṃ niyamitasarvendriyaṃ svavaśe kṛtvā prasahya svakāryeṣu saṃyojayataḥ / tataś cāyam ātmasvarūpānubhavavimukho vinaṣṭo bhavati / jñānayogārambheṇa rāgadveṣavaśam āgamya na vinaśyet / tau hi rāgadveṣau asya durjayau śatrū -- jñānābhyāsaṃ vārayataḥ //
body.translated_text: The attachment (<s>rāga</s>) in the form of the desire to experience [sense-objects], born of prior latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), that is inescapably established with respect to the objects — sound and the like — of the sense-faculties of knowledge such as hearing and the like, and with respect to the objects — speech and the like — of the organs of action such as the voice and the like; and the aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) that is inescapably established when that experience is obstructed — these two, overpowering one who is striving toward the practice of knowledge (<s>jñānayoga</s>) and who has restrained all the senses, forcefully bring him under their control and yoke him to their own operations. And consequently, he, having turned away from the experience of the self's essential nature, is destroyed. Through embarking upon the practice of knowledge, he comes under the sway of attachment and aversion and is destroyed. For these two — attachment and aversion — are his enemies that are difficult to conquer — they obstruct the practice of knowledge. //

children.text: śrotra-ādi-jñāna-indriyasya arthe śabda-ādau vāg-ādi-karma-indriyasya ca arthe vacana-ādau prācīna-vāsanā-janita-tad-anububhūṣā-rūpo yo rāgo 'varjanīyo vyavasthitaḥ; tad-anubhave pratihate ca avarjanīyo yo dveṣo vyavasthitaḥ, tāv evaṃ jñāna-yogāya yatamānaṃ niyamita-sarva-indriyaṃ sva-vaśe kṛtvā prasahya sva-kāryeṣu saṃyojayataḥ / tataś ca ayam ātma-sva-rūpa-anubhava-vimukho vinaṣṭo bhavati / jñāna-yoga-ārambheṇa rāga-dveṣa-vaśam āgamya na vinaśyet / tau hi rāga-dveṣau asya durjayau śatrū --- jñāna-abhyāsaṃ vārayataḥ //
śreyān svadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt |
children.translated_text: One's own <s>dharma</s>, though imperfect, is better than another's <s>dharma</s> well-performed;

children.text: svadharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ paradharmo bhayāvahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Death in one's own <s>dharma</s> is better; another's <s>dharma</s> is fraught with danger. ||

children.text: śreyān sva-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt |
sva-dharme nidhanaṃ śreyaḥ para-dharmo bhaya-āvahaḥ ||

body.text: ataḥ suśakatayā svadharmabhūtaḥ karmayogo viguṇo 'py apramādagarbhaḥ prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭasya duśśakatayā paradharmabhūtāj jñānayogāt saguṇād api kiṃcit kālam anuṣṭhitāt sapramādāc chreyān; svenaivopādātuṃ yogyatayā svadharmabhūte karmayoge vartamānasyaikasmin janmany aprāptaphalatayā nidhanam api śreyaḥ, anantarāyahatatayānantarajanmany api avyākulakarmayogārambhasaṃbhavāt / prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭasya svenaivopādātum aśakyatayā paradharmabhūto jñānayogaḥ pramādagarbhatayā bhayāvahaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>karmayoga</s>, which is one's own <s>dharma</s> because it is easily within one's capability, even though imperfect — i.e., containing [the possibility of] heedlessness — is better than <s>jñānayoga</s>, which is another's <s>dharma</s> because it is difficult for one who is associated with <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature), even though it is well-performed — i.e., having [good] qualities — even if practiced for some time, [but] attended by heedlessness. Even death while abiding in <s>karmayoga</s>, which is one's own <s>dharma</s> because it is fit to be undertaken by oneself, is better — [meaning] even if the fruit is not attained in a single lifetime — because, being unobstructed by obstacles, the commencement of untroubled <s>karmayoga</s> is possible even in the next life. <s>Jñānayoga</s>, which is another's <s>dharma</s> because it cannot be undertaken by oneself when associated with <s>Prakṛti</s>, is fraught with danger because it is attended by heedlessness. //

children.text: ataḥ suśakatayā sva-dharma-bhūtaḥ karma-yogo viguṇo 'py apramāda-garbhaḥ prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭasya duśśakatayā para-dharma-bhūtāj jñāna-yogāt saguṇād api kiṃcit kālam anuṣṭhitāt sapramādāc chreyān; svena eva upādātuṃ yogyatayā sva-dharma-bhūte karma-yoge vartamānasya ekasmin janmany aprāpta-phalatayā nidhanam api śreyaḥ, anantara-āya-hatataya ānantara-janmany api avyākula-karma-yoga-ārambha-saṃbhavāt / prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭasya svena eva upādātum aśakyatayā para-dharma-bhūto jñāna-yogaḥ pramāda-garbhatayā bhaya-āvahaḥ //
atha kena prayukto 'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then by what is this person impelled to commit sin,

children.text: anicchann api vārṣṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even unwilling, O <s>Vārṣṇeya</s>, as if driven by force? ||

children.text: atha kena prayukto 'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ |
anicchann api vārṣṇeya balād iva niyojitaḥ ||

body.text: athāyaṃ jñānayogāya pravṛttaḥ puruṣaḥ svayaṃ viṣayān anubhavitum anicchann api kena prayukto viṣayānubhavarūpaṃ pāpaṃ balān niyojita iva carati //
body.translated_text: Now this person who has set out toward the practice of knowledge — by what is he impelled to commit the sin in the form of experiencing sense-objects, even though he himself does not wish to experience sense-objects, as if driven by force? //

children.text: atha ayaṃ jñāna-yogāya pravṛttaḥ puruṣaḥ svayaṃ viṣayān anubhavitum anicchann api kena prayukto viṣaya-anubhava-rūpaṃ pāpaṃ balān niyojita iva carati //
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of <s>rajas</s>,

children.text: mahāśano mahāpāpmā viddhy enam iha vairiṇam ||
children.translated_text: All-devouring, greatly sinful — know this to be the enemy here. ||

children.text: kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ |
mahā-aśano mahā-pāpmā viddhy enam iha vairiṇam ||

body.text: asyodbhavābhibhavarūpeṇa vartamānaguṇamayaprakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭasya jñānāyārabdhasya rajoguṇasamudbhavaḥ prācīnavāsanājanitaḥ śabdādiviṣayaḥ kāmo mahāśanaḥ śatruḥ viṣayeṣv enam ākarṣati / eṣa eva pratihatagatiḥ pratihatihetubhūtacetanān prati krodharūpeṇa pariṇato mahāpāpmā parahiṃsādiṣu pravartayati / enaṃ rajoguṇasamudbhavaṃ sahajaṃ jñānayogavirodhinaṃ vairiṇaṃ viddhi //
body.translated_text: For one who is associated with <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature), which consists of the <s>guṇas</s> and is present in the form of arising and dominating — for one who has set out toward knowledge — the desire directed toward sense-objects such as sound and the like, born of the quality of <s>rajas</s>, generated by prior latent impressions, the all-devouring enemy, drags him toward sense-objects. This very [desire], when its course is obstructed, transforming into the form of anger toward those conscious beings who are the cause of the obstruction, greatly sinful, impels [one] toward harming others and the like. Know this enemy, born of the quality of <s>rajas</s>, innate, antagonistic to the practice of knowledge. //

children.text: asya udbhava-abhibhava-rūpeṇa vartamāna-guṇa-maya-prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭasya jñānāyā arabdhasya rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ prācīna-vāsanā-janitaḥ śabda-ādi-viṣayaḥ kāmo mahā-āśanaḥ śatruḥ viṣayeṣv enam ākarṣati / eṣa eva pratihata-gatiḥ pratihati-hetu-bhūta-cetanān prati krodha-rūpeṇa pariṇato mahā-pāpmā para-hiṃsā-ādiṣu pravartayati / enaṃ rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaṃ saha-jaṃ jñāna-yoga-virodhinaṃ vairiṇaṃ viddhi //
dhūmenāvriyate vahnir yathādarśo malena ca |
children.translated_text: As fire is covered by smoke, as a mirror by dust,

children.text: yatholbenāvṛto garbhas tathā tenedam āvṛtam ||
children.translated_text: As an embryo is enveloped by the membrane — so is this covered by that. ||

children.text: dhūmenā avriyate vahnir yathā ādarśo malena ca |
yatha ūlbenā avṛto garbhas tathā tena idam āvṛtam ||

body.text: yathā dhūmena vahnir āvriyate, yathā ādarśo malena, yathā ca ulbenāvṛto garbhaḥ, tathā tena kāmena idaṃ jantujātam āvṛtam //
body.translated_text: Just as fire is covered by smoke, just as a mirror [is covered] by dust, and just as an embryo is enveloped by the membrane — so by that desire, this mass of living beings is covered. //

children.text: yathā dhūmena vahnir āvriyate, yathā ādarśo malena, yathā ca ulbenā avṛto garbhaḥ, tathā tena kāmena idaṃ jantu-jātam āvṛtam //

body.text: āvaraṇaprakāram āha --
body.translated_text: He states the mode of covering:

children.text: āvaraṇa-prakāram āha ---
āvṛtaṃ jñānam etena jñānino nityavairiṇā |
children.translated_text: Knowledge is covered by this eternal enemy of the knower,

children.text: kāmarūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca ||
children.translated_text: In the form of desire, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, an insatiable fire. ||

children.text: āvṛtaṃ jñānam etena jñānino nitya-vairiṇā |
kāma-rūpeṇa kaunteya duṣpūreṇa analena ca ||

body.text: asya jantoḥ jñāninaḥ jñānasvabhāvasyātmaviṣayaṃ jñānam etena -- kāmakāreṇa viṣayavyāmohajananena nityavairiṇā āvṛtam; duṣpūreṇa -- prāptyanarhaviṣayeṇa, analena ca -- paryāptirahitena //
body.translated_text: Of this living being — the knower, one whose essential nature is knowledge — the knowledge directed toward the self is covered by this — by the operation of desire, which generates delusion regarding sense-objects, and which is an eternal enemy; 'insatiable' — having sense-objects that are not fit to be attained; 'and a fire' — without satiety. //

children.text: asya jantoḥ jñāninaḥ jñāna-sva-bhāvasyā atma-viṣayaṃ jñānam etena --- kāma-kāreṇa viṣaya-vyāmoha-jananena nitya-vairiṇā āvṛtam; duṣpūreṇa --- prāpty-anarha-viṣayeṇa, analena ca --- paryāpti-rahitena //

body.text: kair upakaraṇair ayaṃ kāma ātmānam adhiṣṭhitīty atrāha --
body.translated_text: By what instruments does this desire occupy the self? — regarding this he says:

children.text: kair upakaraṇair ayaṃ kāma ātmānam adhiṣṭhiti ity atrā aha ---
indriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣṭhānam ucyate |
children.translated_text: The senses, the mind, and the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) are said to be its seat;

children.text: etair vimohayaty eṣa jñānam āvṛtya dehinam ||
children.translated_text: Through these, it deludes the embodied one, covering knowledge. ||

children.text: indriyāṇi mano buddhir asya adhiṣṭhānam ucyate |
etair vimohayaty eṣa jñānam āvṛtya dehinam ||

body.text: adhitiṣṭhaty ebhir ayaṃ kāma ātmānam itīndriyāṇi mano buddhir asyādhiṣṭhānam; etair indriyamanobuddhibhiḥ kāmo 'dhiṣṭhānabhūtair viṣayapravaṇair dehinaṃ prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭaṃ jñānam āvṛtya vimohayati -- vividhaṃ mohayati, ātmajñānavimukhaṃ viṣayānubhavaparaṃ karotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: This desire occupies the self through these — therefore the senses, the mind, and the <s>buddhi</s> are its seat. Through these — the senses, the mind, and the <s>buddhi</s>, which are its seats and which are inclined toward sense-objects — desire, covering knowledge, deludes the embodied one who is associated with <s>Prakṛti</s> — deludes in various ways; the meaning is: it makes him averse to self-knowledge and devoted to the experience of sense-objects. //

children.text: adhitiṣṭhaty ebhir ayaṃ kāma ātmānam iti indriyāṇi mano buddhir asya adhiṣṭhānam; etair indriya-mano-buddhibhiḥ kāmo 'dhiṣṭhāna-bhūtair viṣaya-pravaṇair dehinaṃ prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭaṃ jñānam āvṛtya vimohayati --- vividhaṃ mohayati, ātma-jñāna-vimukhaṃ viṣaya-anubhava-paraṃ karoti ity-arthaḥ //
tasmāt tvam indriyāṇy ādau niyamya bharatarṣabha |
children.translated_text: Therefore, O best of the <s>Bharatas</s>, having first restrained the senses,

children.text: pāpmānaṃ prajahi hy enaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam ||
children.translated_text: Slay this sinful [enemy] that destroys knowledge and discernment. ||

children.text: tasmāt tvam indriyāṇy ādau niyamya bharata-rṣabha |
pāpmānaṃ prajahi hy enaṃ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam ||

body.text: yasmāt sarvendriyavyāpāroparatirūpe jñānayoge pravṛttasyāyaṃ kāmarūpaḥ śatruḥ viṣayābhimukhyakaraṇena ātmani vaimukhyaṃ karoti, tasmāt prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭatayendriyavyāpārapravaṇastvam ādau -- mokṣopāyārambhasamaya eva, indriyavyāpārarūpe karmayoge indriyāṇi niyamya, enaṃ jñānavijñānanāśanam -- ātmasvarūpaviṣayasya jñānasya tadvivekaviṣayasya ca nāśanaṃ pāpmānaṃ kāmarūpaṃ vairiṇaṃ prajahi -- nāśaya //
body.translated_text: Since this enemy in the form of desire, for one who has embarked upon the practice of knowledge (<s>jñānayoga</s>) — which is in the form of the cessation of all sense-activity — makes him averse to the self by directing the senses toward objects, therefore you — who, being associated with <s>Prakṛti</s>, are inclined toward sense-activity — at the very outset, i.e., at the very time of commencing the means to liberation, having restrained the senses through <s>karmayoga</s>, which is in the form of sense-activity, slay this sinful enemy in the form of desire, which destroys knowledge and discernment — i.e., which destroys knowledge directed toward the essential nature of the self and the discernment of that [self]. //

children.text: yasmāt sarva-indriya-vyāpāra-uparati-rūpe jñāna-yoge pravṛttasya ayaṃ kāma-rūpaḥ śatruḥ viṣaya-abhimukhya-karaṇena ātmani vaimukhyaṃ karoti, tasmāt prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭataya īndriya-vyāpāra-pravaṇastvam ādau --- mokṣa-upāya-ārambha-samaya eva, indriya-vyāpāra-rūpe karma-yoge indriyāṇi niyamya, enaṃ jñāna-vijñāna-nāśanam --- ātma-sva-rūpa-viṣayasya jñānasya tad-viveka-viṣayasya ca nāśanaṃ pāpmānaṃ kāma-rūpaṃ vairiṇaṃ prajahi --- nāśaya //

body.text: jñānavirodhiṣu pradhānam āha --
body.translated_text: He states what is primary among the opponents of knowledge:

children.text: jñāna-virodhiṣu pradhānam āha ---
indriyāṇi parāṇy āhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: The senses are said to be superior; superior to the senses is the mind;

children.text: manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Superior to the mind is the <s>buddhi</s>; but that which is superior to the <s>buddhi</s> is he [desire]. ||

children.text: indriyāṇi parāṇy āhur indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ |
manasas tu parā buddhir yo buddheḥ paratas tu saḥ ||

body.text: jñānavirodhe pradhānānīndriyāṇy āhuḥ, yata indriyeṣu viṣayavyāpṛteṣu ātmani jñānaṃ na pravartate / indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ -- indriyeṣu uparateṣv api manasi viṣayapravaṇe ātmajñānaṃ na saṃbhavati / manasas tu parā buddhiḥ -- manasi vṛttyantaravimukhe 'pi viparītādhyavasāyapravṛttau satyāṃ jñānaṃ na pravartate / sarveṣu buddhiparyanteṣu uparateṣv apīcchāparyāyaḥ kāmo rajassamudbhavo vartate cet, sa evaitānīndriyādīny api svaviṣaye vartayitvā ātmajñānaṃ niruṇaddhi / tad idam ucyate, yo buddheḥ paras tu saḥ iti / buddher api yaḥ paras sa kāma ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The senses are said to be primary in opposing knowledge, because when the senses are engaged with objects, knowledge of the self does not operate. The mind is superior to the senses — even when the senses have ceased, if the mind is inclined toward objects, self-knowledge is not possible. The <s>buddhi</s> is superior to the mind — even when the mind is free from other activities, if there is the operation of false determination, knowledge does not operate. Even when everything up to and including the <s>buddhi</s> has ceased, if desire — which is another name for <s>icchā</s> (volition) — born of <s>rajas</s>, continues to operate, it alone, having directed these very senses and the like toward their objects, obstructs self-knowledge. This is what is stated as 'that which is superior to the <s>buddhi</s> is he.' The meaning is: that which is superior even to the <s>buddhi</s> is desire. //

children.text: jñāna-virodhe pradhānāni indriyāṇy āhuḥ, yata indriyeṣu viṣaya-vyāpṛteṣu ātmani jñānaṃ na pravartate / indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ manaḥ --- indriyeṣu uparateṣv api manasi viṣaya-pravaṇe ātma-jñānaṃ na saṃbhavati / manasas tu parā buddhiḥ --- manasi vṛtty-antara-vimukhe 'pi viparīta-adhyavasāya-pravṛttau satyāṃ jñānaṃ na pravartate / sarveṣu buddhi-paryanteṣu uparateṣv api icchā-paryāyaḥ kāmo rajas-samudbhavo vartate cet, sa eva etāni indriya-ādīny api sva-viṣaye vartayitvā ātma-jñānaṃ niruṇaddhi / tad idam ucyate, yo buddheḥ paras tu saḥ iti / buddher api yaḥ paras sa kāma ity-arthaḥ //
evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyātmānam ātmanā |
children.translated_text: Having thus known [desire] to be superior to the <s>buddhi</s>, steadying the self by the self,

children.text: jahi śatruṃ mahābāho kāmarūpaṃ durāsadam ||
children.translated_text: O mighty-armed one, slay the enemy in the form of desire, which is difficult to overcome. ||

children.text: evaṃ buddheḥ paraṃ buddhvā saṃstabhyā atmānam ātmanā |
jahi śatruṃ mahā-bāho kāma-rūpaṃ durāsadam ||

body.text: evaṃ buddher api paraṃ kāmaṃ jñānayogavirodhinaṃ vairiṇaṃ buddhvā ātmānaṃ -- manaḥ ātmanā -- buddhyā karmayoge 'vasthāpya enaṃ kāmarūpaṃ durāsadaṃ śatruṃ jahi -- nāśayeti //
body.translated_text: Having thus known desire to be superior even to the <s>buddhi</s> and to be the enemy antagonistic to the practice of knowledge, steadying the self — the mind — by the self, i.e., by the <s>buddhi</s>, establishing it in <s>karmayoga</s>, slay this enemy in the form of desire, which is difficult to overcome. //

children.text: evaṃ buddher api paraṃ kāmaṃ jñāna-yoga-virodhinaṃ vairiṇaṃ buddhvā ātmānaṃ --- manaḥ ātmanā --- buddhyā karma-yoge 'vasthāpya enaṃ kāma-rūpaṃ durāsadaṃ śatruṃ jahi --- nāśaya iti //

body.text: tṛtīye 'dhyāye -- prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭasya mumukṣoḥ sahasā jñānayoge 'nadhikārāt karmayoga eva kāryaḥ, jñānayogādhikāriṇo 'py akartṛtvānusandhānapūrvakakarmayoga eva śreyān iti -- sahetukam uktam; śiṣṭatayā vyapadeśyasya tu viśeṣataḥ karmayoga eva kārya iti coktam / caturthenedānīm -- asyaiva karmayogasya nikhilajagaduddharaṇāya manvantarādāv evopadiṣṭatayā kartavyatāṃ draḍhayitvā antargatajñānatayāsyaiva jñānayogākaratāṃ pradarśya, karmayogasvarūpam, tadbhedāḥ, karmayoge jñānāṃśasyaiva prādhānyaṃ cocyate / prasaṅgāc ca bhagavadavatārayāthātmyam ucyate /
body.translated_text: In the third chapter, it has been stated with reasons that <s>karmayoga</s> alone is to be performed by one who desires liberation and is associated with <s>Prakṛti</s>, since one is not qualified for the sudden [practice of] <s>jñānayoga</s>; and that even for one qualified for <s>jñānayoga</s>, <s>karmayoga</s> preceded by the contemplation of non-agency is better. It has also been stated that especially for one who is to be designated as a model (<s>śiṣṭa</s>), <s>karmayoga</s> alone is to be performed. Now in the fourth [chapter] — having strengthened the claim that this very <s>karmayoga</s> is to be performed, by [showing that] it was taught at the very beginning of a <s>manvantara</s> for the upliftment of the entire world; having shown that this very [<s>karmayoga</s>] has the character of <s>jñānayoga</s> because knowledge is internal to it; the essential nature of <s>karmayoga</s>, its varieties, and the primacy of the knowledge-aspect within <s>karmayoga</s> are stated. And incidentally, the true nature of the Lord's incarnation (<s>avatāra</s>) is stated.

children.text: tṛtīye 'dhyāye --- prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭasya mumukṣoḥ sahasā jñāna-yoge 'nadhikārāt karma-yoga eva kāryaḥ, jñāna-yoga-adhikāriṇo 'py akartṛtva-anusandhāna-pūrvaka-karma-yoga eva śreyān iti --- sahetukam uktam; śiṣṭatayā vyapadeśyasya tu viśeṣataḥ karma-yoga eva kārya iti ca uktam / caturthena idānīm --- asya eva karma-yogasya nikhila-jagad-uddharaṇāya manv-antara-ādāv eva upadiṣṭatayā kartavyatāṃ draḍhayitvā antargata-jñānataya āsya eva jñāna-yoga-ākaratāṃ pradarśya, karma-yoga-sva-rūpam, tad-bhedāḥ, karma-yoge jñāna-aṃśasya eva prādhānyaṃ ca ucyate / prasaṅgāc ca bhagavad-avatāra-yāthātmyam ucyate /
imaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavān aham avyayam |
children.translated_text: I taught this imperishable <s>yoga</s> to <s>Vivasvat</s>;

children.text: vivasvān manave prāha manur īkṣavākave 'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vivasvat</s> communicated it to <s>Manu</s>; <s>Manu</s> told it to <s>Ikṣvāku</s>. ||

children.text: imaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavān aham avyayam |
vivasvān manave prāha manur īkṣavākave 'bravīt ||
evaṃ paramparāprāptam imaṃ rājarṣayo 'viduḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus received through succession, the royal sages knew it;

children.text: sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa ||
children.translated_text: This <s>yoga</s>, through great [lapse of] time, has been lost here, O scorcher of foes. ||

children.text: evaṃ paramparā-prāptam imaṃ rājarṣayo 'viduḥ |
sa kālena iha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ paran-tapa ||
sa evāyaṃ mayā te 'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ |
children.translated_text: This very same ancient <s>yoga</s> has been taught by Me to you today;

children.text: bhakto 'sti me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hy etad uttamam ||
children.translated_text: For you are My devotee and friend — for this is the supreme secret. ||

children.text: sa eva ayaṃ mayā te 'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purā-tanaḥ |
bhakto 'sti me sakhā ca iti rahasyaṃ hy etad uttamam ||

body.text: yo 'yaṃ tavodito yogaḥ sa kevalaṃ yuddhaprotsāhanāyedānīm udita iti na mantavyam / manvantarādāv eva nikhilajagaduddharaṇāya paramapuruṣārthalakṣaṇamokṣasādhanatayā imaṃ yogam aham eva vivasvate proktavān, vivasvāṃś ca manave, manur ikṣvakave / ity evaṃ saṃpradāyaparamparayā prāptam imaṃ yogaṃ pūrve rājarṣayo 'viduḥ / sa mahatā kālena tattacchrotṛbuddhimāndyād vinaṣṭaprāyo 'bhūt / sa evāyam askhalitasvarūpaḥ purātano yogaḥ sakhyenātimātrabhaktyā ca mām eva prapannāya te mayā proktaḥ -- saparikaras savistaram ukta ityarthaḥ / madanyena kenāpi jñātuṃ vaktuṃ cāśakyam, yata idaṃ vedāntoditam uttamaṃ rahasyaṃ jñānam //
body.translated_text: This <s>yoga</s> that has been taught to you — it should not be thought that it has been taught now merely for the purpose of encouraging you to fight. At the very beginning of the <s>manvantara</s>, as the means of liberation — which is the supreme human goal — for the upliftment of the entire world, I Myself taught this <s>yoga</s> to <s>Vivasvat</s>; and <s>Vivasvat</s> [taught it] to <s>Manu</s>; <s>Manu</s> to <s>Ikṣvāku</s>. Thus, this <s>yoga</s>, received through the succession of the tradition, was known by the royal sages of old. Through the great [passage of] time, due to the dullness of intellect of successive hearers, it became nearly lost. This very same ancient <s>yoga</s>, with its true form unimpaired, has been taught by Me to you — who have taken refuge in Me alone through friendship and supreme devotion — [taught] with all its accessories and in detail — this is the meaning. It cannot be known or spoken by anyone other than Me, because this is the supreme secret knowledge taught in the <s>Vedānta</s>. //

children.text: yo 'yaṃ tava udito yogaḥ sa kevalaṃ yuddha-protsāhanāya idānīm udita iti na mantavyam / manv-antara-ādāv eva nikhila-jagad-uddharaṇāya parama-puruṣa-artha-lakṣaṇa-mokṣa-sādhanatayā imaṃ yogam aham eva vivasvate proktavān, vivasvāṃś ca manave, manur ikṣvakave / ity evaṃ saṃpradāya-paramparayā prāptam imaṃ yogaṃ pūrve rāja-rṣayo 'viduḥ / sa mahatā kālena tat-tac-chrotṛ-buddhi-māndyād vinaṣṭa-prāyo 'bhūt / sa eva ayam askhalita-sva-rūpaḥ purā-tano yogaḥ sakhyena atimātra-bhaktyā ca mām eva prapannāya te mayā proktaḥ --- saparikaras savistaram ukta ity-arthaḥ / mad-anyena kena api jñātuṃ vaktuṃ ca aśakyam, yata idaṃ veda-anta-uditam uttamaṃ rahasyaṃ jñānam //

attributes.n: asmin prasaṅge bhagavad-avatāra-yāthātmyaṃ yathāvaj jñātum arjuna uvāca ---

children.text: avaraṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ |
children.translated_text: Your birth is recent; the birth of <s>Vivasvat</s> is ancient;

children.text: katham etad vijānīyāṃ tvam ādau proktavān iti ||
children.translated_text: How am I to understand this — that You taught [it] in the beginning? ||

children.text: avaraṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ |
katham etad vijānīyāṃ tvam ādau proktavān iti ||

body.text:
kālasaṅkhyayā avaram asmajjanmasamakālaṃ hi bhavato janma / vivasvataś ca janma kālasaṅkhyayā param -- aṣṭāviṃśaticaturyugasaṅkhyāsaṅkhyātam / tvam evādau proktavān iti katham etad asaṃbhāvanīyaṃ yathārthaṃ jānīyām ? nanu janmāntareṇāpi vaktuṃ śakyam, janmāntarakṛtasya mahatāṃ smṛtiś ca yujyata iti nātra kaścid virodhaḥ / na cāsau vaktāram enaṃ vasudevatanayaṃ sarveśvaraṃ na jānāti, yata evaṃ vakṣyati, "paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān / puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyam ādidevam ajaṃ vibhum // āhus tvām ṛṣayas sarve devarṣir nāradas tathā / asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṃ caiva bravīṣi me" iti / yudhiṣṭhirarājasūyādiṣu bhīṣmādibhyaś cāsakṛcchrutam, "kṛṣṇa eva hi lokānām utpattir api cāpyayaḥ / kṛṣṇasya
hi kṛte bhūtam idaṃ viśvaṃ carācaram" ityevamādiṣu / kṛṣṇasya hi kṛte iti, kṛṣṇasya śeṣabhūtam idaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagad ityarthaḥ // atrocyate jānāty evāyaṃ bhagavantaṃ vasudevasūnaṃ pārthaḥ / jānato 'py ajānata iva pṛcchato 'yam āśayaḥ -- nikhilaheyapratyanīkakalyāṇaikatānasya sarveśvarasya sarvajñasya satyasaṅkalpasyāvāptasamastakāmasya karmaparavaśadevamanuṣyādisajātīyaṃ janma kim indrajālādivan mithyā, uta satyam? satyatve ca kathaṃ janmaprakāraḥ? kim ātmako 'yaṃ dehaḥ? kaś ca janmahetuḥ? kadā ca janma? kim arthaṃ ca janmeti / parihāraprakāreṇa praśnārtho vijñāyate //
body.translated_text: In terms of the reckoning of time, Your birth is recent — of the same time as our birth. And the birth of <s>Vivasvat</s> is ancient in terms of the reckoning of time — incalculable in the count of twenty-eight four-<s>yuga</s> cycles. How am I to know this seemingly impossible thing as true — that You Yourself taught [it] in the beginning? Now, it might be said that one can teach even through another birth, and the memory of great beings of what was done in another birth is reasonable — so there is no contradiction here. And he [<s>Arjuna</s>] does not fail to know this speaker, the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>, to be the Lord of all, for he will say: 'You are the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier; the eternal, divine Person, the primal God, unborn, all-pervading. All the sages declare You thus — the divine sage <s>Nārada</s>, as well as <s>Asita</s>, <s>Devala</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, and You Yourself tell me.' And it has been heard repeatedly from <s>Bhīṣma</s> and others at <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>'s <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice and the like: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone is the origin and also the dissolution of the worlds; for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s sake this entire universe, moving and unmoving, has come into being' — and such [statements].
