'For <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s sake' means: this entire universe is the subordinate (<s>śeṣa</s>) of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — this is the meaning. // Here it is said: <s>Pārtha</s> does indeed know the Lord, the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>. Even though knowing, the purport of his question as if not knowing is: Is the birth of the Lord of all — who is the sole abode of all auspicious qualities, opposed to everything base, omniscient, of true resolve, and who has attained all desires — a birth resembling that of <s>devas</s>, humans, and the like who are subject to <s>karma</s>, false like magic, or is it real? And if real, what is the manner of birth? Of what nature is this body? And what is the cause of the birth? When is the birth? And for what purpose is the birth? The meaning of the question is understood from the manner of the answer. //

children.text:
kāla-saṅkhyayā avaram asmaj-janma-sama-kālaṃ hi bhavato janma / vivasvataś ca janma kāla-saṅkhyayā param --- aṣṭā-viṃśati-catur-yuga-saṅkhyā-saṅkhyātam / tvam evā adau proktavān iti katham etad asaṃbhāvanīyaṃ yathā-arthaṃ jānīyām ? nanu janma-antareṇa api vaktuṃ śakyam, janma-antara-kṛtasya mahatāṃ smṛtiś ca yujyata iti na atra kaścid virodhaḥ / na ca asau vaktāram enaṃ vasu-deva-tanayaṃ sarva-īśvaraṃ na jānāti, yata evaṃ vakṣyati, "paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān / puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyam ādi-devam ajaṃ vibhum // āhus tvām ṛṣayas sarve deva-rṣir nāradas tathā / asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṃ ca eva bravīṣi me" iti / yudhiṣṭhira-rāja-sūya-ādiṣu bhīṣma-ādibhyaś ca asakṛc-chrutam, "kṛṣṇa eva hi lokānām utpattir api ca apyayaḥ / kṛṣṇasya
hi kṛte bhūtam idaṃ viśvaṃ cara-acaram" ity-evam-ādiṣu / kṛṣṇasya hi kṛte iti, kṛṣṇasya śeṣa-bhūtam idaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagad ity-arthaḥ // atra ucyate jānāty eva ayaṃ bhagavantaṃ vasu-deva-sūnaṃ pārthaḥ / jānato 'py ajānata iva pṛcchato 'yam āśayaḥ --- nikhila-heya-pratyanīka-kalyāṇa-eka-tānasya sarva-īśvarasya sarva-jñasya satya-saṅkalpasya avāpta-samasta-kāmasya karma-para-vaśa-deva-manuṣya-ādi-sajātīyaṃ janma kim indra-jāla-ādivan mithyā, uta satyam? satyatve ca kathaṃ janma-prakāraḥ? kim ātmako 'yaṃ dehaḥ? kaś ca janma-hetuḥ? kadā ca janma? kim arthaṃ ca janma iti / parihāra-prakāreṇa praśna-artho vijñāyate //
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna |
children.translated_text: Many births of Mine have passed, and of yours too, O <s>Arjuna</s>;

children.text: tāny ahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa ||
children.translated_text: All of them I know; you do not know them, O scorcher of foes. ||

children.text: bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cā arjuna |
tāny ahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha paran-tapa ||

body.text: anena janmanas satyatvam uktam, bahūni me vyatītāni janmānīti vacanāt, tava ceti dṛṣṭāntatayopādānāc ca //
body.translated_text: By this, the reality of the births is stated — because of the statement 'many births of Mine have passed,' and because of the mention of 'and of yours too' as an analogy. //

children.text: anena janmanas satyatvam uktam, bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni iti vacanāt, tava ca iti dṛṣṭāntataya ūpādānāc ca //

body.text: avatāraprakāram, dehayāthātmyam, janmahetuṃ cāha --
body.translated_text: He states the manner of the incarnation, the true nature of the body, and the cause of the birth:

children.text: avatāra-prakāram, deha-yāthātmyam, janma-hetuṃ cā aha ---
ajo 'pi san avyayātmā bhūtānām īśvaro 'pi san |
children.translated_text: Though unborn and of imperishable self, though being the Lord of all beings,

children.text: prakṛtiṃ svām adhiṣṭhāya saṃbhavāmy ātmamāyayā ||
children.translated_text: Governing My own <s>Prakṛti</s>, I come into being through My own <s>māyā</s>. ||

children.text: ajo 'pi san avyaya-ātmā bhūtānām īśvaro 'pi san |
prakṛtiṃ svām adhiṣṭhāya saṃbhavāmy ātma-māyayā ||

body.text:
ajatvāvyayatvasarveśvaratvādi sarvaṃ pārameśvaraṃ prakāram ajahad eva svāṃ prakṛtim adhiṣṭhāya ātmamāyayā saṃbhavāmi / prakṛtiḥ -- svabhāvaḥ svam eva svabhāvam adhiṣṭhāya svenaiva rūpeṇa svecchayā saṃbhavāmītyarthaḥ / svasvarūpaṃ hi, "ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt", "kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāke", "ya eṣo 'ntarāditye hiraṇyamayaḥ puruṣaḥ", "tasminn ayaṃ puruṣo manomayaḥ; amṛto hiraṇmayaḥ", "sarve nimeṣā jajñire vidyutaḥ puruṣād adhi" , "bhārūpas satyasaṅkalpa ākāśātmā sarvakāmā sarvakāmas sarvagandhas sarvarasaḥ", "māhārajanaṃ vāsaḥ" ityādiśrutisiddham / ātmamāyayā -- ātmīyayā māyayā / "māyā vayunaṃ jñānam" iti jñānaparyāyo 'tra māyāśabdaḥ / tathā cābhiyuktaprayogaḥ, "māyayā satataṃ vetti
prāṇināṃ ca śubhāśubham" iti / ātmīyena jñānena ātmasaṅkalpenetyarthaḥ / ato 'pahatapāpmatvādisamastakalyāṇaguṇātmakatvaṃ sarvam aiśaṃ svabhāvam ajahat svam eva rūpaṃ devamanuṣyādisajātīyasaṃsthānaṃ kurvan ātmasaṅkalpena devādirūpaḥ saṃbhavāmi / tad idam āha, "ajāyamāno bahudhā vijāyate" iti śrutiḥ / itarapuruṣasādhāraṇaṃ janma akurvan devādirūpeṇa svasaṅkalpenoktaprakriyayā jāyata ityarthaḥ / "bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna / tāny ahaṃ veda sarvāṇi", "tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham" "janma karma ca me divyam evaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ" iti pūrvāparāvirodhāc ca // janmakālam āha -
body.translated_text: Retaining all divine attributes such as unborn-ness, imperishability, lordship over all, and the like — all the divine modes (<s>prakāra</s>) — presiding over My own <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), I come into being through My own <s>Māyā</s>. <s>Prakṛti</s> means 'own nature'; presiding over My own nature, I come into being in My own form, by My own will — this is the meaning. For My own form is established by <s>śruti</s> texts such as: 'Of the color of the sun, beyond darkness,' 'shining beyond the darkness of this [world],' 'that golden person who is within the sun,' 'in him is this person made of mind, immortal, golden,' 'all flashes of lightning were born from the Person,' 'whose form is light, whose will is true, whose nature is space, who possesses all desires, all fragrances, all tastes,' 'whose garment is of great splendor,' and the like. 'Through My own <s>Māyā</s>' — through My own <s>Māyā</s>. '<s>Māyā</s> [means] plan, knowledge' — here the word <s>Māyā</s> is a synonym for knowledge. And so the usage of the learned: 'Through <s>Māyā</s> he constantly knows the auspicious and inauspicious of living beings.' The meaning is: through My own knowledge, through My own will. Therefore, not abandoning the entire divine nature consisting of being free from evil, and all auspicious qualities, — making My own form into a configuration of the same class as gods, humans, and the like — I come into being in the form of a god and the like, through My own will. This is stated by <s>śruti</s>: 'Being unborn, he is born in many ways.' The meaning is: not undergoing birth common to other persons, he is born in the form of gods and the like, through his own will, in the manner stated. 'Many are the births of mine that have passed, and yours too, O <s>Arjuna</s>; I know all of them,' 'I create myself,' 'My birth and action are divine — one who thus knows them in truth' — there is no contradiction with the earlier and later [statements]. // He states the time of birth:

children.text:
ajatva-avyayatva-sarva-īśvaratva-adi sarvaṃ pārameśvaraṃ prakāram ajahad eva svāṃ prakṛtim adhiṣṭhāya ātma-māyayā saṃbhavāmi / prakṛtiḥ --- sva-bhāvaḥ svam eva sva-bhāvam adhiṣṭhāya svena eva rūpeṇa sva-icchayā saṃbhavāmi ity-arthaḥ / sva-sva-rūpaṃ hi, "āditya-varṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt", "kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāke", "ya eṣo 'ntara-āditye hiraṇya-mayaḥ puruṣaḥ", "tasminn ayaṃ puruṣo mano-mayaḥ; amṛto hiraṇ-mayaḥ", "sarve nimeṣā jajñire vidyutaḥ puruṣād adhi" , "bhā-rūpas satya-saṅkalpa ākāśa-ātmā sarva-kāmā sarva-kāmas sarva-gandhas sarva-rasaḥ", "māhārajanaṃ vāsaḥ" ity-ādi-śruti-siddham / ātma-māyayā --- ātmīyayā māyayā / "māyā vayunaṃ jñānam" iti jñāna-paryāyo 'tra māyā-śabdaḥ / tathā ca abhiyukta-prayogaḥ, "māyayā satataṃ vetti
prāṇināṃ ca śubha-aśubham" iti / ātmīyena jñānena ātma-saṅkalpena ity-arthaḥ / ato 'pahata-pāpmatva-ādi-samasta-kalyāṇa-guṇa-ātmakatvaṃ sarvam aiśaṃ sva-bhāvam ajahat svam eva rūpaṃ deva-manuṣya-ādi-sajātīya-saṃsthānaṃ kurvan ātma-saṅkalpena deva-ādi-rūpaḥ saṃbhavāmi / tad idam āha, "ajāyamāno bahudhā vijāyate" iti śrutiḥ / itara-puruṣa-sādhāraṇaṃ janma akurvan deva-ādi-rūpeṇa sva-saṅkalpena ukta-prakriyayā jāyata ity-arthaḥ / "bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cā arjuna / tāny ahaṃ veda sarvāṇi", "tadā ātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham" "janma karma ca me divyam evaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ" iti pūrva-apara-avirodhāc ca // janma-kālam āha --
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata |
children.translated_text: 'Whenever there is a decline of <s>dharma</s>, O <s>Bhārata</s>,'

children.text: abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: 'and a rise of <s>adharma</s>, then I create Myself.' ||

children.text: yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata |
abhyutthānam adharmasya tadā ātmānaṃ sṛjāmy aham ||

body.text: na kālaniyamo 'smatsaṃbhavasya / yadā yadā hi dharmasya vedoditasya cāturvarṇyacāturāśramyavyavasthayāvasthitasya kartavyayasya glānir bhavati, yadā yadā ca tadviparyayasyādharmasyābhyutthānam tadāham eva svasaṅkalpenoktaprakāreṇātmānaṃ sṛjāmi //
body.translated_text: There is no restriction of time for My incarnation. Whenever there is a decline of <s>dharma</s> — [that <s>dharma</s>] which is taught in the <s>Veda</s>, established in the arrangement of the four <s>varṇas</s> and the four <s>āśramas</s>, and which is to be performed — whenever there is a decline; and whenever there is a rise of <s>adharma</s>, which is the opposite of that — then I Myself, through My own will, in the manner stated, create Myself. //

children.text: na kāla-niyamo 'smat-saṃbhavasya / yadā yadā hi dharmasya veda-uditasya cāturvarṇya-cāturāśramya-vyavasthaya āvasthitasya kartavyayasya glānir bhavati, yadā yadā ca tad-viparyayasya adharmasya abhyutthānam tada āham eva sva-saṅkalpena ukta-prakāreṇā atmānaṃ sṛjāmi //

body.text: janmanaḥ prayojanam āha --
body.translated_text: He states the purpose of the birth:

children.text: janmanaḥ prayojanam āha ---
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām |
children.translated_text: 'For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of the wicked,'

children.text: dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya saṃbhavāmi yuge yuge ||
children.translated_text: 'and for the establishment of <s>dharma</s>, I come into being age after age.' ||

children.text: paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām |
dharma-saṃsthāpana-arthāya saṃbhavāmi yuge yuge ||

body.text: sādhavaḥ uktalakṣaṇadharmaśīlāḥ vaiṣṇavāgresarā matsamāśrayaṇe pravṛttā mannāmakarmasvarūpāṇāṃ vāṅmanasāgocaratayā maddarśanena vinā svātmadhāraṇapoṣaṇādikm alabhamānāḥ kṣaṇamātrakālaṃ kalpasahasraṃ manvānāḥ pratiśithilasarvagātrā bhaveyur iti matsvarūpaceṣṭitāvalokanālāpādidānena teṣāṃ paritrāṇāya tadviparītānāṃ vināśāya ca kṣīṇasya vaidikasya dharmasya madārādhanarūpasyārādhyasvarūpapradarśanena sthāpanāya ca devamanuṣyādirūpeṇa yuge yuge saṃbhavāmi / kṛtatretādiyugaviśeṣaniyamo 'pi nāstītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The righteous (<s>sādhu</s>) — those devoted to <s>dharma</s> of the stated character, foremost among the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, engaged in taking refuge in Me, for whom My name, actions, and form are beyond the reach of speech and mind, and who, without seeing Me, are unable to sustain, nourish, or support themselves, and who regard even a single moment as a thousand <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic cycles), and whose every limb grows feeble — for the protection of those, by granting them the sight, converse, activities, and the like of My own form and deeds; for the destruction of those who are the opposite [of the righteous]; and for the establishment — through the display of the nature of the one to be worshipped — of the Vedic <s>dharma</s>, which has the character of worshipping Me and which has declined — I come into being in the form of gods, humans, and the like, age after age. The meaning is that there is no restriction even to a specific <s>yuga</s> such as <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, and the like. //

children.text: sādhavaḥ ukta-lakṣaṇa-dharma-śīlāḥ vaiṣṇava-agresarā mat-samāśrayaṇe pravṛttā man-nāma-karma-sva-rūpāṇāṃ vāṅ-manasa-agocaratayā mad-darśanena vinā sva-ātma-dhāraṇa-poṣaṇa-ādikm alabhamānāḥ kṣaṇa-mātra-kālaṃ kalpa-sahasraṃ manvānāḥ pratiśithila-sarva-gātrā bhaveyur iti mat-sva-rūpa-ceṣṭita-avalokana-ālāpa-ādi-dānena teṣāṃ paritrāṇāya tad-viparītānāṃ vināśāya ca kṣīṇasya vaidikasya dharmasya mad-ārādhana-rūpasyā arādhya-sva-rūpa-pradarśanena sthāpanāya ca deva-manuṣya-ādi-rūpeṇa yuge yuge saṃbhavāmi / kṛta-treta-ādi-yuga-viśeṣa-niyamo 'pi na asti ity-arthaḥ //
janma karmaṃ ca me divyam evaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'My birth and action are divine — one who knows this in truth,'

children.text: tyaktvā dehaṃ punarjanma naiti mām eti so 'rjuna ||
children.translated_text: 'having left the body, does not come to rebirth — he comes to Me, O <s>Arjuna</s>.' ||

children.text: janma karmaṃ ca me divyam evaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ |
tyaktvā dehaṃ punar-janma na eti mām eti so 'rjuna ||

body.text: evaṃ karmamūlaheyatriguṇaprakṛtisaṃsargarūpajanmarahitasya sarvesvaratvasārvajñyasatyasaṅkalpatvādisamastakalyāṇaguṇopetasya sādhuparitrāṇamatsamāśrayaṇaikaprayojanaṃ divyam -- aprākṛtaṃ madasādhāraṇaṃ mama janma ceṣṭitaṃ ca tattvato yo vetti, sa vartamānaṃ dehaṃ parityajya punarjanma naiti, mām eva prāpnoti / madīyadivyajanmaceṣṭitayāthātmyavijñānena vidhvastasamastamatsamāśryaṇavirodhipāpaḥ asminn eva janmani yathoditaprakāreṇa mām āśritya madekapriyo madekacitto mām eva prāpnoti //
body.translated_text: Thus, one who knows in truth My divine — supernatural, unique to Me — birth and action: [that I am] one who is free from birth occasioned by contact with the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) of <s>Prakṛti</s>, which is to be eliminated and which is the root of <s>karma</s>; who is endowed with all auspicious qualities such as lordship over all, omniscience, truthfulness of will, and the like; and whose sole purpose is the protection of the righteous and the taking of refuge in Me — having abandoned the present body, does not come to rebirth. He comes to Me alone. Through the knowledge of the true nature of My divine birth and deeds, having destroyed all sins that obstruct the taking of refuge in Me, in this very life, having taken refuge in Me in the manner stated, having Me alone as his beloved and Me alone as the object of his thought — he attains Me alone. //

children.text: evaṃ karma-mūla-heya-tri-guṇa-prakṛti-saṃsarga-rūpa-janma-rahitasya sarva-īsvaratva-sārvajñya-satya-saṅkalpatva-ādi-samasta-kalyāṇa-guṇa-upetasya sādhu-paritrāṇamat-samāśrayaṇa-eka-prayojanaṃ divyam --- aprākṛtaṃ mad-asādhāraṇaṃ mama janma ceṣṭitaṃ ca tattvato yo vetti, sa vartamānaṃ dehaṃ parityajya punar-janma na eti, mām eva prāpnoti / madīya-divya-janma-ceṣṭita-yāthātmya-vijñānena vidhvasta-samasta-mat-samāśryaṇa-virodhi-pāpaḥ asminn eva janmani yathā-udita-prakāreṇa mām āśritya mad-eka-priyo mad-eka-citto mām eva prāpnoti //

body.text: tad āha --
body.translated_text: He states this:

children.text: tad āha ---
vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā mām upāśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Free from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me,'

children.text: bahavo jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvan āgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'many, purified by the austerity of knowledge, have attained My nature.' ||

children.text: vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhā man-mayā mām upāśritāḥ |
bahavo jñāna-tapasā pūtā mad-bhāvan āgatāḥ ||

body.text: madīyajanmakarmatattvajñānākhyena tapasā pūtā bahava evaṃ saṃvṛttāḥ / tathā ca śrutiḥ, "tasya dhīrāḥ parijānanti yonim" iti / dhīrāḥ -- dhīmatām agresarā evaṃ tasya janmaprakāraṃ jānantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Purified by the austerity called the knowledge of the true nature of My birth and actions — many have thus become [liberated]. And so the <s>śruti</s>: 'the wise ones know his birth.' The meaning is: the wise — the foremost among the intelligent — thus know the manner of his birth. //

children.text: madīya-janma-karma-tattva-jñāna-ākhyena tapasā pūtā bahava evaṃ saṃvṛttāḥ / tathā ca śrutiḥ, "tasya dhīrāḥ parijānanti yonim" iti / dhīrāḥ --- dhīmatām agresarā evaṃ tasya janma-prakāraṃ jānanti ity-arthaḥ //
ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃs tathaiva bhajāmy aham |
children.translated_text: 'In whatever way people approach Me, I favor them accordingly, O <s>Pārtha</s>;'

children.text: mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'people follow My path in all ways.' ||

children.text: ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃs tatha aiva bhajāmy aham |
mama vartma anuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ ||

body.text: na kevalaṃ devamanuṣyādirūpeṇāvatīrya matsamāśrayaṇāpekṣāṇāṃ paritrāṇaṃ karomi, api tu ye matsamāśrayaṇāpekṣā yathā -- yena prakāreṇa svāpekṣānurūpaṃ māṃ saṃkalpya prapadyante -- samāśrayante; tān prati tathaiva tanmanīṣitaprakāreṇa bhajāmi -- māṃ darśayāmi / kim atra bahunā, sarve manuṣyāḥ madanuvartanaikamanorathā mama vartma -- matsvabhāvaṃ sarvaṃ yogināṃ vāṅmanasāgocaram api svakīyāiś cakṣurādikaraṇaiḥ sarvaśaḥ svāpekṣitaiḥ sarvaprakārair anubhūyānuvartnte //
body.translated_text: Not only do I protect those who seek refuge in Me by descending in the form of gods, humans, and the like, but those who seek refuge in Me — in whatever manner, conceiving of Me in accordance with their own aspirations, they approach Me — take refuge in Me; toward them, in that very manner, in accordance with what they desire, I favor them — I reveal Myself to them. What more needs to be said? All people, whose sole desire is to follow Me — My path, My nature — though beyond the reach of the speech and mind of even <s>yogins</s>, by their own senses such as the eyes and the like, they experience and follow [Me] in all ways, through all means in accordance with their aspirations. //

children.text: na kevalaṃ deva-manuṣya-ādi-rūpeṇa avatīrya mat-samāśrayaṇa-apekṣāṇāṃ paritrāṇaṃ karomi, api tu ye mat-samāśrayaṇa-apekṣā yathā --- yena prakāreṇa sva-apekṣa-anurūpaṃ māṃ saṃkalpya prapadyante --- samāśrayante; tān prati tatha aiva tan-manīṣita-prakāreṇa bhajāmi --- māṃ darśayāmi / kim atra bahunā, sarve manuṣyāḥ mad-anuvartana-eka-mano-rathā mama vartma --- mat-sva-bhāvaṃ sarvaṃ yogināṃ vāṅ-manasa-agocaram api svakīyāiś cakṣur-ādi-karaṇaiḥ sarvaśaḥ sva-apekṣitaiḥ sarva-prakārair anubhūya anuvartnte //

body.text: idānīṃ prāsaṅgikaṃ parisamāpya prakṛtasya karmayogasya jñānākāratāprakāraṃ vaktuṃ tathāvidhakarmayogādhikāriṇo durlabhatvam āha --
body.translated_text: Now, having concluded the incidental [topic], in order to state the nature of the knowledge-form of the <s>karmayoga</s> under discussion, he states the rarity of those qualified for such <s>karmayoga</s>:

children.text: idānīṃ prāsaṅgikaṃ parisamāpya prakṛtasya karma-yogasya jñāna-ākāratā-prakāraṃ vaktuṃ tathā-vidha-karma-yoga-adhikāriṇo durlabhatvam āha ---
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Desiring the success of actions, they worship the gods here;'

children.text: kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhir bhavati karmajā ||
children.translated_text: 'for in the human world, success born of action comes quickly.' ||

children.text: kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ |
kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhir bhavati karma-jā ||

body.text: sarva eva puruṣāḥ karmaṇāṃ phalaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇāḥ indrādidevatāmātraṃ yajante -- ārādhayanti, na tu kaścid anabhisaṃhitaphalaḥ indrādidevatātmabhūtaṃ sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktāraṃ māṃ yajate / kuta etat? yataḥ kṣiprasminn eva mānuṣe loke karmajā putrapaśvannādysiddhir bhavati / manuṣyalokaśabdaḥ svargādīnām api pradarśanārthaḥ / sarvaṃ eva laukikāḥ puruṣā akṣīṇānādikālapravṛttānantapāpasaṃcayatayā avivekinaḥ kṣipraphalākāṅkṣiṇaḥ putrapaśvannādyasvargādyarthatayā sarvāṇi karmāṇīndrādidevatārādhanamātrāṇi kurvate; na tu kaścit saṃsārodvignahṛdayo mumukṣuḥ uktalakṣaṇaṃ karmayogaṃ madārādhanabhūtam ārabhata ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: All persons, desiring the fruit of actions, worship — propitiate — merely the gods such as <s>Indra</s> and the like; but no one, without attachment to results, worships Me, the enjoyer of all sacrifices, who is the inner self of all the gods such as <s>Indra</s> and the like. Why is this? Because in this very human world, the success born of action — in the form of offspring, cattle, food, and the like — comes quickly. The word 'human world' is meant to indicate heaven and the like as well. All worldly persons, being without discrimination due to the accumulation of infinite sins that has been in progress from beginningless time, desirous of quick results, perform all actions merely as the worship of gods such as <s>Indra</s> and the like, for the sake of offspring, cattle, food, heaven, and the like. But no one — one whose heart is weary of <s>saṃsāra</s>, a seeker of liberation — undertakes <s>karmayoga</s> of the stated character, which has the nature of worshipping Me. This is the meaning. //

children.text: sarva eva puruṣāḥ karmaṇāṃ phalaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇāḥ indra-ādi-devatā-mātraṃ yajante --- ārādhayanti, na tu kaścid anabhisaṃhita-phalaḥ indra-ādi-devatā-ātma-bhūtaṃ sarva-yajñānāṃ bhoktāraṃ māṃ yajate / kuta etat? yataḥ kṣiprasminn eva mānuṣe loke karma-jā putra-paśv-anna-ādy-siddhir bhavati / manuṣya-loka-śabdaḥ svarga-ādīnām api pradarśana-arthaḥ / sarvaṃ eva laukikāḥ puruṣā akṣīṇa-anādi-kāla-pravṛtta-ananta-pāpa-saṃcayatayā avivekinaḥ kṣipra-phala-ākāṅkṣiṇaḥ putra-paśv-anna-ādy-asvarga-ādy-arthatayā sarvāṇi karmāṇi indra-ādi-devatā-ārādhana-mātrāṇi kurvate; na tu kaścit saṃsāra-udvigna-hṛdayo mumukṣuḥ ukta-lakṣaṇaṃ karma-yogaṃ mad-ārādhana-bhūtam ārabhata ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: yathoktakarmayogārambhavirodhipāpakṣayahetum āha --
body.translated_text: He states the cause for the destruction of sins that obstruct the commencement of <s>karmayoga</s> of the stated character:

children.text: yathā-ukta-karma-yoga-ārambha-virodhi-pāpa-kṣaya-hetum āha ---
cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The four-<s>varṇa</s> system was created by Me, distributed according to <s>guṇas</s> and <s>karmas</s>;'

children.text: tasya kartāram api māṃ viddhy akartāram avyayam ||
children.translated_text: 'though I am the author of that, know Me as the non-author, the imperishable.' ||

children.text: cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaḥ |
tasya kartāram api māṃ viddhy akartāram avyayam ||

body.text: cāturvarṇyapramukhaṃ brahmādistambaparyantaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagat sattvādiguṇavibhāgena tadanuguṇaśamādikarmavibhāgena ca vibhaktaṃ mayā sṛṣṭam / sṛṣṭigrahaṇaṃ pradarśanārtham / mayaiva rakṣyante, mayaiva copasaṃhriyate / tasya -- vicitrasṛṣtyādeḥ kartāram apy akartāraṃ māṃ viddhi // katham ity atrāha -
body.translated_text: The entire universe, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, beginning with the four-<s>varṇa</s> system, was created by Me, distributed according to the division of <s>guṇas</s> such as <s>sattva</s> and the like, and the division of <s>karmas</s> such as self-control and the like that correspond to those [<s>guṇas</s>]. The use of the word 'creation' is illustrative — [the universe] is also sustained by Me and dissolved by Me. Though I am the author of that — of the diverse creation and the like — know Me as the non-author. // How so? He says:

children.text: cāturvarṇya-pramukhaṃ brahmā-ādi-stamba-paryantaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagat sattva-ādi-guṇa-vibhāgena tad-anuguṇa-śama-ādi-karma-vibhāgena ca vibhaktaṃ mayā sṛṣṭam / sṛṣṭi-grahaṇaṃ pradarśana-artham / maya aiva rakṣyante, maya aiva ca upasaṃhriyate / tasya --- vicitra-sṛṣty-ādeḥ kartāram apy akartāraṃ māṃ viddhi // katham ity atrā aha --
na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karmaphale spṛhā |
children.translated_text: 'Actions do not taint Me, nor do I have any desire for the fruit of action;'

children.text: iti māṃ yo 'bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badhyate ||
children.translated_text: 'one who knows Me thus is not bound by actions.' ||

children.text: na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karma-phale spṛhā |
iti māṃ yo 'bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badhyate ||

body.text:
yata imāni vicitrasṛṣṭyādīni karmāṇi māṃ na limpanti -- na māṃ saṃbadhnanti / na matprayuktāni tāni devamanuṣyādivaicitryāṇi / sṛjyānāṃ puṇyapāparūpakarmaviśeṣaprayuktānītyarthaḥ / ataḥ prāptāprāptavivekena vicitrasṛṣṭyāder nāhaṃ kartā; yataś ca sṛṣṭāḥ kṣetrajñāḥ sṛṣṭilabdhakaraṇakalebarāḥ sṛṣṭilabdhaṃ bhogyajātaṃ phalasaṅgādihetusvakarmānuguṇaṃ bhuṅjate; sṛṣṭyādkarmaphale ca teṣām eva spṛheti ne me spṛhā / tathāha sūtrakāraḥ -- vaiṣamyanairghṛṇye na sāpekṣatvād iti / tathā ca bhagavān parāśaraḥ -- "nimittamātram evāsau sṛjyānāṃ sargakarmaṇi / pradhānakāraṇībhūtā yato vai sṛjyaśaktayaḥ // nimittamātraṃ muktvedaṃ nānyat kiṃcid apekṣate / nīyate tapatāṃ
śreṣṭha svaśaktyā vastu vastutām // BhGR_4." iti / sṛjyānāṃ devādīnāṃ kṣetrajñānāṃ sṛṣṭeḥ kāraṇamātram evāyaṃ paramapuruṣaḥ; devādivaicitrye tu pradhānakāraṇaṃ sṛjyabhūtakṣetrajñānāṃ prācīnakarmaśaktaya eva / ato nimittamātraṃ muktvā -- sṛṣṭeḥ kartāraṃ paramapuruṣaṃ muktvā idaṃ kṣetrajñavastu devādivicitrabhāve nānyad apekṣate; svagataprācīnakarmaśaktyā eva hi devādivastubhāvaṃ nīyata ityarthaḥ / evam uktena prakāreṇa sṛṣtyādeḥ kartāram apy akartāraṃ sṛṣṭyādikarmaphalasaṅgarahitaṃ ca yo mām abhijānāti, sa karmayogārambhavirodhibhiḥ phalasaṅgādihetubhiḥ prācīnakarmabhir na saṃbadhyate / mucyata ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because these actions of diverse creation and the like do not taint Me — do not bind Me. Those diversities of gods, humans, and the like are not caused by Me. The meaning is: they are caused by the specific <s>karmas</s> — of the nature of merit and demerit — of the beings being created. Therefore, through the discrimination of the deserving and undeserving, I am not the author of diverse creation and the like; and because the created individual selves (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), having obtained instruments and bodies through creation, enjoy the class of enjoyable objects obtained through creation in accordance with their own <s>karmas</s> that are the causes of attachment to results and the like — and the desire for the fruit of the actions of creation and the like belongs to them alone — it is not Mine. Thus the <s>sūtra</s>-maker states: 'Partiality and cruelty [do not attach to God,] because [creation] depends [on <s>karma</s>].' And so the blessed <s>Parāśara</s> says: 'He is merely the efficient cause in the act of creation of the created; for the powers of the created are the principal cause — from which indeed the powers of the created [derive]. | Except for being the efficient cause, this [creation] requires nothing else — O best of ascetics, the thing is brought into its thingness by its own power.' // The meaning is: this Supreme Person is merely the efficient cause of the creation of the created — the individual selves of gods and the like. But the principal cause of the diversity of gods and the like is the power of prior <s>karma</s> belonging to the individual selves being created. Therefore, except for the efficient cause — except for the Supreme Person as the author of creation — this individual-self-reality, in its becoming diverse as gods and the like, requires nothing else; for it is brought into the state of being a thing such as a god by its own inherent prior <s>karma</s>-power. Thus, one who knows Me — the author of creation and the like in the manner stated, yet a non-author, free from attachment to the fruit of actions of creation and the like — is not bound by prior <s>karmas</s> that are the causes of attachment to results and the like, which obstruct the commencement of <s>karmayoga</s>. The meaning is: he is liberated. //

children.text:
yata imāni vicitra-sṛṣṭy-ādīni karmāṇi māṃ na limpanti --- na māṃ saṃbadhnanti / na mat-prayuktāni tāni deva-manuṣya-ādi-vaicitryāṇi / sṛjyānāṃ puṇya-pāpa-rūpa-karma-viśeṣa-prayuktāni ity-arthaḥ / ataḥ prāpta-aprāpta-vivekena vicitra-sṛṣṭy-āder na ahaṃ kartā; yataś ca sṛṣṭāḥ kṣetra-jñāḥ sṛṣṭi-labdha-karaṇa-kalebarāḥ sṛṣṭi-labdhaṃ bhogya-jātaṃ phala-saṅga-ādi-hetu-sva-karma-anuguṇaṃ bhuṅjate; sṛṣṭy-ād-karma-phale ca teṣām eva spṛha īti ne me spṛhā / tathā āha sūtra-kāraḥ --- vaiṣamya-nairghṛṇye na sa-apekṣatvād iti / tathā ca bhagavān parāśaraḥ --- "nimitta-mātram eva asau sṛjyānāṃ sarga-karmaṇi / pradhāna-kāraṇībhūtā yato vai sṛjya-śaktayaḥ // nimitta-mātraṃ muktva īdaṃ na anyat kiṃcid apekṣate / nīyate tapatāṃ
śreṣṭha sva-śaktyā vastu vastutām // BhGR_4." iti / sṛjyānāṃ deva-ādīnāṃ kṣetra-jñānāṃ sṛṣṭeḥ kāraṇa-mātram eva ayaṃ parama-puruṣaḥ; deva-ādi-vaicitrye tu pradhāna-kāraṇaṃ sṛjya-bhūta-kṣetra-jñānāṃ prācīna-karma-śaktaya eva / ato nimitta-mātraṃ muktvā --- sṛṣṭeḥ kartāraṃ parama-puruṣaṃ muktvā idaṃ kṣetra-jña-vastu deva-ādi-vicitra-bhāve na anyad apekṣate; sva-gata-prācīna-karma-śaktyā eva hi deva-ādi-vastu-bhāvaṃ nīyata ity-arthaḥ / evam uktena prakāreṇa sṛṣty-ādeḥ kartāram apy akartāraṃ sṛṣṭy-ādi-karma-phala-saṅga-rahitaṃ ca yo mām abhijānāti, sa karma-yoga-ārambha-virodhibhiḥ phala-saṅga-ādi-hetubhiḥ prācīna-karmabhir na saṃbadhyate / mucyata ity-arthaḥ //
evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvair api mumukṣubhiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having known [Me] thus, action was performed even by the ancients who sought liberation.'

children.text: kuru karmaiva tasmāt tvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, you too perform that very action, performed by the ancients from the most ancient times.' ||

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvair api mumukṣubhiḥ |
kuru karma eva tasmāt tvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam ||

body.text: evaṃ māṃ jñātvā vimuktapāpaiḥ pūrvair api mumukṣubhir uktalakṣaṇaṃ karma kṛtam / tasmāt tvam uktaprakāramadviṣayajñānavidhūtapāpaḥ pūrvair vivasvanmanvādibhiḥ kṛtaṃ pūrvataraṃ -- purātanaṃ tadānīm eva mayoktaṃ vakṣyamāṇākāraṃ karvaiva kuru //
body.translated_text: Having known Me thus, even by the ancients — who had been freed from sin — who were seekers of liberation, action of the stated character was performed. Therefore, you too, your sins having been removed by knowledge of Me of the stated character, perform that very action — performed by the ancients such as <s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Manu</s>, and the like — that most ancient [action], which was taught by Me at that very time, and whose form will be described. //

children.text: evaṃ māṃ jñātvā vimukta-pāpaiḥ pūrvair api mumukṣubhir ukta-lakṣaṇaṃ karma kṛtam / tasmāt tvam ukta-prakāra-mad-viṣaya-jñāna-vidhūta-pāpaḥ pūrvair vivasvan-manv-ādibhiḥ kṛtaṃ pūrvataraṃ --- purātanaṃ tadānīm eva maya ūktaṃ vakṣyamāṇa-ākāraṃ karva eva kuru //

body.text: vakṣyamāṇasya karmaṇo durjñānatām āha --
body.translated_text: He states the difficulty of understanding the action that will be described:

children.text: vakṣyamāṇasya karmaṇo durjñānatām āha ---
kiṃ karma kim akarmeti kavayo 'py atra mohitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'What is action? What is inaction? — even the wise are confused about this.'

children.text: tat te karma pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt ||
children.translated_text: 'I shall declare to you that action, knowing which you shall be freed from evil.' ||

children.text: kiṃ karma kim akarma iti kavayo 'py atra mohitāḥ |
tat te karma pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvā mokṣyase 'śubhāt ||

body.text: mumukṣuṇānuṣṭheyaṃ karma kiṃrūpam, akarma ca kim / akarmeti kartur ātmano yāthātmyajñānam ucyate; anuṣṭheyaṃ karma tadantargataṃ jñānaṃ ca kiṃrūpam ity ubhayatra kavayaḥ -- vidvāṃso 'pi mohitāḥ -- yathāvan na jānanti / evam antargatajñānaṃ yat karma, tat te pravakṣyāmi, yaj jñātvānuṣṭhāya aśubhāt -- saṃsārabandhān mokṣyase / kartavyakarmajñānaṃ hy anuṣṭhānaphalam //
body.translated_text: What is the form of the action to be performed by the seeker of liberation? And what is inaction? — <s>akarma</s> refers to the knowledge of the true nature of the agent, the self. What is the form of the action to be performed, and the knowledge included within it? — regarding both of these, even the wise — even the learned — are confused, i.e., they do not know them properly. I shall declare to you that action which includes knowledge within it, knowing and performing which, you shall be freed from evil — from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. For the knowledge of the action to be performed has its fruit in performance. //

children.text: mumukṣuṇa ānuṣṭheyaṃ karma kiṃ-rūpam, akarma ca kim / akarma iti kartur ātmano yāthātmya-jñānam ucyate; anuṣṭheyaṃ karma tad-antargataṃ jñānaṃ ca kiṃ-rūpam ity ubhayatra kavayaḥ --- vidvāṃso 'pi mohitāḥ --- yathāvan na jānanti / evam antargata-jñānaṃ yat karma, tat te pravakṣyāmi, yaj jñātva ānuṣṭhāya aśubhāt --- saṃsāra-bandhān mokṣyase / kartavya-karma-jñānaṃ hy anuṣṭhāna-phalam //

body.text: kuto 'sya durjñānatety āha --
body.translated_text: Why is it difficult to know? He says:

children.text: kuto 'sya durjñānata īty āha ---
karmaṇo hy api boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'For of action, there is much to be understood; of prohibited action (<s>vikarma</s>) too, much to be understood;'

children.text: akarmaṇaś ca boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'and of inaction, much to be understood — the course of action is deep.' ||

children.text: karmaṇo hy api boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ |
akarmaṇaś ca boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ ||

body.text: yasmān mokṣasādhanabhūte karmasvarūpe boddhavyam asti; vikarmaṇi ca / nityanaimittikakāmyarūpeṇa, tatsādhanadravyārjanādyākāreṇa ca vividhatāpannaṃ karma vikarma / akarmaṇi -- jñāne ca boddhavyam asti / gahanā -- durvijñānā mumukṣoḥ karmaṇo gatiḥ //
body.translated_text: Because in the true nature of the action that is the means of liberation, there is much to be understood; and in <s>vikarma</s> too. <s>Vikarma</s> is action that has become manifold in the forms of obligatory (<s>nitya</s>), occasional (<s>naimittika</s>), and desire-motivated (<s>kāmya</s>) [rites], and in the form of acquiring materials and the like that serve as means for those [rites]. And in inaction — in knowledge — there is much to be understood. Deep — difficult to comprehend — is the course of action for the seeker of liberation. //

children.text: yasmān mokṣa-sādhana-bhūte karma-sva-rūpe boddhavyam asti; vikarmaṇi ca / nitya-naimittika-kāmya-rūpeṇa, tat-sādhana-dravya-arjana-ādy-ākāreṇa ca vividhatā-āpannaṃ karma vikarma / akarmaṇi --- jñāne ca boddhavyam asti / gahanā --- durvijñānā mumukṣoḥ karmaṇo gatiḥ //

body.text: vikarmaṇi boddhavyaṃ nityanaimittikakāmyadravyārjanādau karmaṇi phalabhedakṛtaṃ vaividhyaṃ parityajya mokṣaikaphalatayaikaśāstrārthatvānusandhānam / tad etat "vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekā" ity atraivoktam iti neha prapañcyate / karmākarmaṇor boddhavyam āha --
body.translated_text: What is to be understood regarding <s>vikarma</s> is: in the actions of obligatory, occasional, desire-motivated, and material-acquisition [categories], abandoning the diversity produced by the difference of fruits, the investigation that [all these] serve a single scriptural purpose — that of liberation alone. This was already stated in 'the resolute understanding is one' — so it is not elaborated here. He states what is to be understood regarding action and inaction:

children.text: vikarmaṇi boddhavyaṃ nitya-naimittika-kāmya-dravya-arjana-ādau karmaṇi phala-bheda-kṛtaṃ vaividhyaṃ parityajya mokṣa-eka-phalataya aika-śāstra-arthatva-anusandhānam / tad etat "vyavasāya-ātmikā buddhir ekā" ity atra eva uktam iti na iha prapañcyate / karma-akarmaṇor boddhavyam āha ---
karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyed akarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction —'

children.text: sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt ||
children.translated_text: 'he is wise among people, he is disciplined, he is the performer of all actions.' ||

children.text: karmaṇy akarma yaḥ paśyed akarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ |
sa buddhimān manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsna-karma-kṛt ||

body.text: akarmaśabdenātra karmetarāt prastutam ātmajñānam ucyate / karmaṇi kriyamāṇa evātmajñānaṃ yaḥ paśyet, akarmaṇi cātmajñāne vartamāna eva yaḥ karma paśyet / kim uktaṃ bhavati? kriyamāṇam eva karma ātmayāthātmyānusandhānena jñānākāraṃ yaḥ paśyet, tac ca jñānaṃ karmayogāntaragatatayā karmākāraṃ yaḥ paśyed ity uktaṃ bhavati / kriyamāṇe hi karmaṇi kartṛbhūtātmayāthātmyānusandhāne sati tadubhayaṃ saṃpannaṃ bhavati / evam ātmayāthātmyānusandhānāntargarbhaṃ karma yaḥ paśyet, sa buddhimān -- kṛtsnaśāstrārthavit,manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ -- mokṣāyārhaḥ, sa eva kṛtsnakarmakṛt kṛtsnaśāstrārthakṛt //
body.translated_text: By the word <s>akarma</s> (non-action), what is denoted here is the knowledge of the self, which is the topic at hand, as distinct from action. He who, while action is being performed, sees knowledge of the self — and he who, while established in <s>akarma</s>, i.e., knowledge of the self, sees action. What is being said? He who sees the very action being performed as having the form of knowledge through the contemplation of the true nature of the self as agent — and he who sees that knowledge, by virtue of being included within <s>karmayoga</s>, as having the form of action — that is what is being said. For when action is being performed and there is contemplation of the true nature of the self as agent, both of those are accomplished. Thus, he who sees action as containing the contemplation of the true nature of the self within it — he is the wise one, the knower of the entire meaning of the scriptures; among humans he is the one who is fit — fit for liberation; he alone is the doer of all action, the accomplisher of the entire meaning of scripture.

children.text: akarma-śabdena atra karma-itarāt prastutam ātma-jñānam ucyate / karmaṇi kriyamāṇa evā atma-jñānaṃ yaḥ paśyet, akarmaṇi cā atma-jñāne vartamāna eva yaḥ karma paśyet / kim uktaṃ bhavati? kriyamāṇam eva karma ātma-yāthātmya-anusandhānena jñāna-ākāraṃ yaḥ paśyet, tac ca jñānaṃ karma-yoga-antaragatatayā karma-ākāraṃ yaḥ paśyed ity uktaṃ bhavati / kriyamāṇe hi karmaṇi kartṛ-bhūta-ātma-yāthātmya-anusandhāne sati tad-ubhayaṃ saṃpannaṃ bhavati / evam ātma-yāthātmya-anusandhāna-antargarbhaṃ karma yaḥ paśyet, sa buddhimān --- kṛtsna-śāstra-artha-vit,manuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ --- mokṣāya arhaḥ, sa eva kṛtsna-karma-kṛt kṛtsna-śāstra-artha-kṛt //

body.text: pratyakṣeṇa kriyamāṇasya karmaṇo jñanākāratā katham upapadyata ity atrāha --
body.translated_text: To the question 'how is the form of knowledge tenable for action that is being performed perceptibly?' he says:

children.text: pratyakṣeṇa kriyamāṇasya karmaṇo jñana-ākāratā katham upapadyata ity atrā aha ---
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṃkalpavarjitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He whose every undertaking is free from desire and intention,' |

children.text: jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tam āhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'whose <s>karma</s> has been burnt by the fire of knowledge — the wise call him a sage.' ||

children.text: yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāma-saṃkalpa-varjitāḥ |
jñāna-agni-dagdha-karmāṇaṃ tam āhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ ||

body.text: yasya mumukṣoḥ sarve dravyārjanādilaukikakarmapūrvakanityanaimittikakāmyarūpakarmasamārambhāḥ kāmārjitāḥ phalasaṅgarahitāḥ / saṅkalpavarjitāś ca / prakṛtyā tadguṇaiś cātmānam ekīkṛtyānusandhānaṃ saṅkalpaḥ; prakṛtiviyuktātmasvarūpānusandhānayuktatayā tadrahitāḥ / tam evaṃ karma kurvāṇaṃ paṇḍitaṃ karmāntargatātmayāthātmyajñānāgninā dagdhaprācīnakarmāṇam āhus tattvajñāḥ / ataḥ karmaṇo jñānākāratvam upapadyate //
body.translated_text: He who is an aspirant to liberation (<s>mumukṣu</s>), whose every undertaking — all actions beginning with the worldly action of acquiring materials, along with the regular, occasional, and desire-prompted ritual actions — is free from desire, free from attachment to results; and free from intention (<s>saṅkalpa</s>). Intention (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) means contemplating the self as identical with <s>Prakṛti</s> and its <s>guṇas</s>. Free from that — because of being endowed with the contemplation of the essential nature of the self as separated from <s>Prakṛti</s>. Him — who thus performs action, a sage whose prior <s>karma</s> has been burnt by the fire of knowledge of the true nature of the self contained within action — the knowers of reality call [a sage]. Therefore, the form of knowledge in action is tenable.

children.text: yasya mumukṣoḥ sarve dravya-arjana-ādi-laukika-karma-pūrvaka-nitya-naimittika-kāmya-rūpa-karma-samārambhāḥ kāma-arjitāḥ phala-saṅga-rahitāḥ / saṅkalpa-varjitāś ca / prakṛtyā tad-guṇaiś cā atmānam ekīkṛtya-anusandhānaṃ saṅkalpaḥ; prakṛti-viyukta-ātma-sva-rūpa-anusandhāna-yuktatayā tad-rahitāḥ / tam evaṃ karma kurvāṇaṃ paṇḍitaṃ karma-antargata-ātma-yāthātmya-jñāna-agninā dagdha-prācīna-karmāṇam āhus tattva-jñāḥ / ataḥ karmaṇo jñāna-ākāratvam upapadyate //

body.text: etad eva vivṛṇoti --
body.translated_text: He elaborates on this very [point]:

children.text: etad eva vivṛṇoti ---
tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, ever content, without dependence,' |

children.text: karmaṇy abhipravṛtto 'pi naiva kiṃcit karoti saḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'though fully engaged in action, he does nothing at all.' ||

children.text: tyaktvā karma-phala-asaṅgaṃ nitya-tṛpto nirāśrayaḥ |
karmaṇy abhipravṛtto 'pi na eva kiṃcit karoti saḥ ||

body.text: karmaphalasaṅgaṃ tyaktvā nityatṛptaḥ -- nitye svātmny eva tṛptaḥ, nirāśrayaḥ -- asthiraprakṛtau āśrayabuddhirahito yaḥ karmāṇi karoti, sa karmaṇy ābhimukhyena pravṛtto 'pi naiva kiṃcit karma karoti -- karmāpadeśena jñānābhyāsam eva karotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Having abandoned attachment to the fruits of action, ever content — content in the eternal self alone, without dependence — free from the notion of dependence on unstable <s>Prakṛti</s>, he who performs actions — though fully engaged in action, he does nothing at all — meaning: under the designation of action, he is practicing knowledge alone.

children.text: karma-phala-saṅgaṃ tyaktvā nitya-tṛptaḥ --- nitye sva-ātmny eva tṛptaḥ, nirāśrayaḥ --- asthira-prakṛtau āśraya-buddhi-rahito yaḥ karmāṇi karoti, sa karmaṇy ābhimukhyena pravṛtto 'pi na eva kiṃcit karma karoti --- karma-apadeśena jñāna-abhyāsam eva karoti ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: punar api karmaṇo jñānākārataiva viśodhyate --
body.translated_text: Once again, the very form of knowledge in action is being clarified:

children.text: punar api karmaṇo jñāna-ākārata aiva viśodhyate ---
nirāśīr yatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Free from expectation, with mind and self restrained, having abandoned all possessions,' |

children.text: śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam ||
children.translated_text: 'performing merely bodily action alone, he incurs no sin.' ||

children.text: nirāśīr yata-citta-ātmā tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ |
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvan nā apnoti kilbiṣam ||

body.text: nirāśīḥ -- nirgataphalābhisandhiḥ yatacittātmā -- yatacittamanāḥ tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ -- ātmaikaprayojanatayā prakṛtiprākṛtavastuni mamatārahitaḥ, yāvajjīvaṃ kevalaṃ śārīram eva karma kurvan kilbiṣaṃ -- saṃsāraṃ nāpnoti jñānaniṣṭhāvyavadhānarahitakevalakarmayogenaivaṃrūpeṇātmānaṃ paśyatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Free from expectation — free from intention regarding results; with mind and self restrained — with mind and thought controlled; having abandoned all possessions — free from possessiveness regarding <s>Prakṛti</s> and its products, since the self alone is the purpose. Performing merely bodily action alone throughout life, he incurs no sin — no <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth). Meaning: through <s>karmayoga</s> alone, without the interruption of a separate establishment in knowledge (<s>jñānaniṣṭhā</s>), of this very form, he sees the self.

children.text: nirāśīḥ --- nirgata-phala-abhisandhiḥ yata-citta-ātmā --- yata-citta-manāḥ tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ --- ātma-eka-prayojanatayā prakṛti-prākṛta-vastuni mamatā-rahitaḥ, yāvaj-jīvaṃ kevalaṃ śārīram eva karma kurvan kilbiṣaṃ --- saṃsāraṃ nā apnoti jñāna-niṣṭhā-vyavadhāna-rahita-kevala-karma-yogena evaṃ-rūpeṇā atmānaṃ paśyati ity-arthaḥ //
yadṛcchālābhasaṃtuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Content with whatever comes by chance, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy,' |

children.text: samaḥ siddhāv asiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate ||
children.translated_text: 'equal in success and failure — even acting, he is not bound.' ||

children.text: yadṛcchā-lābha-saṃtuṣṭo dvandva-atīto vimatsaraḥ |
samaḥ siddhāv asiddhau ca kṛtva āpi na nibadhyate ||

body.text: yadṛcchopanataśarīradhāraṇahetuvastusantuṣṭaḥ, dvandvātītaḥ -- yāvatsādhanasamāptyavarjanīyaśītoṣṇādisahaḥ, vimatsaraḥ -- aniṣṭopanipātahetubhūtasvakarmanirūpaṇena pareṣu vigatamatsaraḥ, samas siddhāv asiddau ca -- yuddhādikarmasu jayādisiddhyasiddhyoḥ samacittaḥ, karmaiva kṛtvāpi -- jñānaniṣṭhāṃ vināpi na nibadhyate -- na saṃsāraṃ pratipadyate //
body.translated_text: Content with whatever comes by chance for sustaining the body; beyond the pairs of opposites — enduring heat, cold, and the like that are unavoidable until the completion of the spiritual practice; free from envy — free from envy toward others by understanding that one's own <s>karma</s> is the cause of undesirable occurrences; equal in success and failure — of even mind regarding success and failure in victory and the like in actions such as battle; even performing action alone — even without a separate establishment in knowledge — he is not bound — he does not enter <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: yadṛcchā-upanata-śarīra-dhāraṇa-hetu-vastu-santuṣṭaḥ, dvandva-atītaḥ --- yāvat-sādhana-samāpty-avarjanīya-śīta-ūṣṇa-ādi-sahaḥ, vimatsaraḥ --- aniṣṭa-upanipāta-hetu-bhūta-sva-karma-nirūpaṇena pareṣu vigata-matsaraḥ, samas siddhāv asiddau ca --- yuddha-ādi-karmasu jaya-ādi-siddhy-asiddhyoḥ sama-cittaḥ, karma eva kṛtva āpi --- jñāna-niṣṭhāṃ vina āpi na nibadhyate --- na saṃsāraṃ pratipadyate //
gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Of one free from attachment, liberated, whose mind is established in knowledge,' |

children.text: yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate ||
children.translated_text: 'performing action for the sake of sacrifice — his <s>karma</s> dissolves entirely.' ||

children.text: gata-saṅgasya muktasya jñāna-avasthita-cetasaḥ |
yajñāyā acarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate ||

body.text: ātmaviṣayajñānāvasthitamanastvena nirgatataditarasaṅgasya tata eva nikhilaparigrahavinirmuktasya uktalakṣaṇayajñādikarmanirvṛttaye vartamānasya puruṣasya bandhahetubhūtaṃ prācīnaṃ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate -- niśśeṣaṃ kṣīyate //
body.translated_text: Of the person whose mind is established in knowledge concerning the self, and who is therefore free from attachment to everything else, who is for that very reason completely freed from all possessions, and who is engaged in performing sacrifice and other actions of the described character — the prior <s>karma</s> that is the cause of bondage dissolves entirely — is completely exhausted.

children.text: ātma-viṣaya-jñāna-avasthita-manastvena nirgata-tad-itara-saṅgasya tata eva nikhila-parigraha-vinirmuktasya ukta-lakṣaṇa-yajña-ādi-karma-nirvṛttaye vartamānasya puruṣasya bandha-hetu-bhūtaṃ prācīnaṃ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate --- niśśeṣaṃ kṣīyate //

body.text: prakṛtiviyuktātmasvarūpānusandhānayuktatayā karmaṇo jñānākāratvam uktam; idānīṃ sarvasya saparikarasya karmaṇaḥ parabrahmabhūtaparamapuruṣātmakatvānusandhānayuktatayā jñānākāratvam āha --
body.translated_text: The form of knowledge in action due to the contemplation of the essential nature of the self as separated from <s>Prakṛti</s> has been stated. Now he states the form of knowledge in action due to the contemplation that all action, together with its accessories, has the Supreme Person — who is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — as its inner self:

children.text: prakṛti-viyukta-ātma-sva-rūpa-anusandhāna-yuktatayā karmaṇo jñāna-ākāratvam uktam; idānīṃ sarvasya saparikarasya karmaṇaḥ para-brahma-bhūta-parama-puruṣa-ātmakatva-anusandhāna-yuktatayā jñāna-ākāratvam āha ---
brahmārpaṇaṃ brahma havir brahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam |
children.translated_text: 'The offering is <s>Brahman</s>, the oblation is <s>Brahman</s>, offered by <s>Brahman</s> into the fire that is <s>Brahman</s>.' |

children.text: brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Brahman</s> alone is to be reached by him who contemplates action as <s>Brahman</s>.' ||

children.text: brahma arpaṇaṃ brahma havir brahma-agnau brahmaṇā hutam |
brahma eva tena gantavyaṃ brahma-karma-samādhinā ||

body.text: brahmārpaṇam iti havir viśeṣyate / arpyate 'nenety arpaṇaṃ srugādi / tadbrahmakāryatvād brahma / brahma yasya haviṣo 'rpaṇaṃ tad brahmārpaṇam, brahma haviḥ brahmārpaṇaṃ haviḥ / svayaṃ ca brahmabhūtam, brahmāgnau -- brahmabhūte agnau brahmaṇā kartrā hutam iti sarvaṃ karma brahmātmakatayā brahmamayam iti yaḥ samādhatte, sa brahmakarmasamādhiḥ, tena brahmakarmasamādhinā brahmaiva gantavyam -- brahmātmakatayā brahmabhūtam ātmasvarūpaṃ gantavyam / mumukṣuṇā kriyamāṇaṃ karma parabrahmātmakam evety anusandhānayuktatayā jñānākāraṃ sākṣādātmāvalokanasādhanam; na jñānaniṣṭhāvyadhānenetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Brahman</s>-offering' qualifies the oblation (<s>havis</s>). That by which [the oblation] is offered is the <s>arpaṇa</s> (instrument of offering) — the ladle and the like. Because it is an effect of <s>Brahman</s>, it is <s>Brahman</s>. That oblation whose instrument of offering is <s>Brahman</s> — that is '<s>brahmārpaṇam</s>,' the <s>Brahman</s>-offering oblation. It is itself <s>Brahman</s>. Offered into the fire that is <s>Brahman</s>, by the agent who is <s>Brahman</s> — he who thus contemplates all action as pervaded by <s>Brahman</s>, as consisting of <s>Brahman</s> by virtue of having <s>Brahman</s> as its inner self — that is the <s>brahmakarmasamādhi</s> (contemplation of action as <s>Brahman</s>). By that contemplation of action as <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Brahman</s> alone is to be reached — the essential nature of the self, which is <s>Brahman</s>-natured by virtue of having <s>Brahman</s> as its inner self, is to be attained. The action performed by the aspirant to liberation is of the nature of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> — by virtue of this contemplation, it has the form of knowledge and is a direct means for the vision of the self; not with the interruption of a separate establishment in knowledge — this is the meaning.

children.text: brahma-arpaṇam iti havir viśeṣyate / arpyate 'nena ity arpaṇaṃ srug-ādi / tad-brahma-kāryatvād brahma / brahma yasya haviṣo 'rpaṇaṃ tad brahma-arpaṇam, brahma haviḥ brahma-arpaṇaṃ haviḥ / svayaṃ ca brahma-bhūtam, brahma-agnau --- brahma-bhūte agnau brahmaṇā kartrā hutam iti sarvaṃ karma brahma-ātmakatayā brahma-mayam iti yaḥ samādhatte, sa brahma-karma-samādhiḥ, tena brahma-karma-samādhinā brahma eva gantavyam --- brahma-ātmakatayā brahma-bhūtam ātma-sva-rūpaṃ gantavyam / mumukṣuṇā kriyamāṇaṃ karma para-brahma-ātmakam eva ity anusandhāna-yuktatayā jñāna-ākāraṃ sākṣād-ātma-avalokana-sādhanam; na jñāna-niṣṭhā-vyadhānena ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: evaṃ karmaṇo jñānākāratāṃ pratipādya karmayogabhedān āha --
body.translated_text: Having thus established the form of knowledge in action, he states the varieties of <s>karmayoga</s>:

children.text: evaṃ karmaṇo jñāna-ākāratāṃ pratipādya karma-yoga-bhedān āha ---
daivam evāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: 'Some <s>yogins</s> devote themselves to sacrifice to the gods alone,' |

children.text: brahmāgnāv apare yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati ||
children.translated_text: 'while others offer sacrifice into the fire of <s>Brahman</s> by means of sacrifice itself.' ||

children.text: daivam eva apare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate |
brahma-agnāv apare yajñaṃ yajñena eva upajuhvati ||

body.text: daivaṃ -- devārcanarūpaṃ yajñam apare karmayoginaḥ paryupāsate -- sevante / tatraiva niṣṭhāṃ kurvantītyarthaḥ / apare brahmāgnau yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati; atra yajñaśabdo havis srugādiyajñasādhane vartate; "brahmārpaṇaṃ brahma haviḥ" iti nyāyena yāgahomayor niṣṭhāṃ kurvanti //
body.translated_text: Some <s>karmayogins</s> devote themselves — engage — in sacrifice that takes the form of worship of the gods. They establish themselves exclusively in that — this is the meaning. Others offer sacrifice into the fire of <s>Brahman</s> by means of sacrifice itself. Here the word 'sacrifice' refers to the instruments of sacrifice — the oblation, ladle, and the like. By the principle 'the offering is <s>Brahman</s>, the oblation is <s>Brahman</s>,' they establish themselves in ritualistic worship (<s>yāga</s>) and fire-offerings (<s>homa</s>).

children.text: daivaṃ --- deva-arcana-rūpaṃ yajñam apare karma-yoginaḥ paryupāsate --- sevante / tatra eva niṣṭhāṃ kurvanti ity-arthaḥ / apare brahma-agnau yajñaṃ yajñena eva upajuhvati; atra yajña-śabdo havis srug-ādi-yajña-sādhane vartate; "brahma-arpaṇaṃ brahma haviḥ" iti nyāyena yāga-homayor niṣṭhāṃ kurvanti //
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇy anye saṃyamāgniṣu juhvati |
children.translated_text: 'Others offer the senses — hearing and the like — into the fires of restraint.' |

children.text: śabdādīn viṣayān anye indriyāgniṣu juhvati ||
children.translated_text: 'Others offer the sense-objects — sound and the like — into the fires of the senses.' ||

children.text: śrotra-ādīni indriyāṇy anye saṃyama-agniṣu juhvati |
śabda-ādīn viṣayān anye indriya-agniṣu juhvati ||

body.text: anye śrotrādīnām indriyāṇāṃ saṃyamane prayatante / anye yoginaḥ indriyāṇāṃ śabdādipravaṇatānivāraṇe prayatante //
body.translated_text: Others strive in the restraint of the senses — hearing and the like. Other <s>yogins</s> strive in preventing the senses from inclining toward sound and the like.

children.text: anye śrotra-ādīnām indriyāṇāṃ saṃyamane prayatante / anye yoginaḥ indriyāṇāṃ śabda-ādi-pravaṇatā-nivāraṇe prayatante //
sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi cāpare |
children.translated_text: 'Others offer all the activities of the senses and the activities of the vital breath' |

children.text: ātmasaṃyamayogāgnau juhvati jñānadīpite ||
children.translated_text: 'into the fire of the <s>yoga</s> of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.' ||

children.text: sarvāṇi indriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi ca apare |
ātma-saṃyama-yoga-agnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite ||

body.text: anye jñānadīpite manassaṃyanayogāgnau sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi ca juhvati / manasa indriyaprāṇakarmaprvaṇatānivāraṇe prayatanta ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Others offer all the activities of the senses and the activities of the vital breath into the fire of the <s>yoga</s> of mind-restraint, kindled by knowledge. They strive in preventing the mind from inclining toward the activities of the senses and the vital breath — this is the meaning.

children.text: anye jñāna-dīpite manas-saṃyana-yoga-agnau sarvāṇi indriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi ca juhvati / manasa indriya-prāṇa-karma-prvaṇatā-nivāraṇe prayatanta ity-arthaḥ //
dravyayajñās tapoyajñā yogayajñās tathāpare |
children.translated_text: 'Some [perform] sacrifice through material offerings, some through austerity, some through <s>yoga</s>,' |

children.text: svādhyāyajñānayajñāś ca yatayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'and others through study and knowledge — [all being] strivers of firm vows.' ||

children.text: dravya-yajñās tapo-yajñā yoga-yajñās tatha āpare |
sva-adhyāya-jñāna-yajñāś ca yatayaḥ saṃśita-vratāḥ ||

body.text: kecit karmayogino dravyayajñāḥ nyāyato dravyāṇy upādāya devatārcane prayatante, kecic ca dāneṣu, kecic ca yāgeṣu, kecic ca homeṣu / ete sarve dravyayajñāḥ / kecit tapoyajñāḥ kṛcchracāndrāyaṇopavāsādiṣu niṣṭhāṃ kurvanti / yogayajñāś cāpare puṇyatīrthapuṇyasthānaprāptiṣu niṣṭhāṃ kurvanti / iha yogaśabdaḥ karmaniṣṭhābhedaprakaraṇāt tadviṣayaḥ / kecit svādhyāyābhyāsaparāḥ / kecit tadarthajñānābhyāsaparāḥ / yatayaḥ yatanaśīlāḥ, saṃśitavratāḥ dṛḍhasaṅkalpāḥ //
body.translated_text: Some <s>karmayogins</s>, being performers of material-sacrifice, strive in the worship of deities by properly acquiring materials; some [strive] in gifts; some in ritualistic worship; some in fire-offerings. All of these are material-sacrificers. Some, being performers of austerity-sacrifice, establish themselves in <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, fasting, and the like. Others, being <s>yoga</s>-sacrificers, establish themselves in reaching holy pilgrimage sites and sacred places. Here, the word <s>yoga</s> refers to these, being in the context of varieties of action-practice. Some are devoted to the practice of self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>). Some are devoted to the practice of knowledge of its meaning. [They are] strivers — of a striving disposition; of firm vows — of resolute determination.

children.text: kecit karma-yogino dravya-yajñāḥ nyāyato dravyāṇy upādāya devatā-arcane prayatante, kecic ca dāneṣu, kecic ca yāgeṣu, kecic ca homeṣu / ete sarve dravya-yajñāḥ / kecit tapo-yajñāḥ kṛcchra-cāndrāyaṇa-upavāsa-ādiṣu niṣṭhāṃ kurvanti / yoga-yajñāś ca apare puṇya-tīrtha-puṇya-sthāna-prāptiṣu niṣṭhāṃ kurvanti / iha yoga-śabdaḥ karma-niṣṭhā-bheda-prakaraṇāt tad-viṣayaḥ / kecit sva-adhyāya-abhyāsa-parāḥ / kecit tad-artha-jñāna-abhyāsa-parāḥ / yatayaḥ yatana-śīlāḥ, saṃśita-vratāḥ dṛḍha-saṅkalpāḥ //
apāne juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe 'pānaṃ tathāpare |
children.translated_text: 'Others offer the out-breath into the in-breath, and the in-breath into the out-breath,' |

children.text: prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'having arrested the paths of the in-breath and the out-breath — devoted to breath-control (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>).' ||

children.text: apāne juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe 'pānaṃ tatha āpare |
prāṇa-apāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇa-āyāma-parāyaṇāḥ ||
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati |
children.translated_text: 'Others, of regulated diet, offer the vital breaths into the vital breaths.' |

children.text: apare niyata-āhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati |

body.text: apare karmayoginaḥ prāṇāyāmeṣu niṣṭhāṃ kurvanti / te ca trividhāḥ pūrakarecakakumbhakabhedena; apāne juhvati prāṇam iti pūrakaḥ, prāṇe 'pānam iti recakaḥ, prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā ..... prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati iti kumbhakaḥ / prāṇāyāmapareṣu triṣv apy anuṣajyate niyatāhārā iti //
body.translated_text: Other <s>karmayogins</s> establish themselves in breath-control (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>). And these are of three kinds, according to the distinction of <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation), <s>recaka</s> (exhalation), and <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention). 'They offer the out-breath into the in-breath' — this is <s>pūraka</s>. 'The in-breath into the out-breath' — this is <s>recaka</s>. 'Having arrested the paths of the in-breath and out-breath... they offer the vital breaths into the vital breaths' — this is <s>kumbhaka</s>. 'Of regulated diet' applies to all three of those devoted to breath-control.

children.text: apare karma-yoginaḥ prāṇa-āyāmeṣu niṣṭhāṃ kurvanti / te ca tri-vidhāḥ pūraka-recaka-kumbhaka-bhedena; apāne juhvati prāṇam iti pūrakaḥ, prāṇe 'pānam iti recakaḥ, prāṇa-apāna-gatī ruddhvā ..... prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati iti kumbhakaḥ / prāṇa-āyāma-pareṣu triṣv apy anuṣajyate niyata-āhārā iti //
sarve 'py ete yajñavido yajñakṣapitakalmaṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'All of these are knowers of sacrifice, whose sins have been destroyed by sacrifice.' ||

children.text: sarve 'py ete yajña-vido yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ ||
yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujo yānti brahma sanātanam |
children.translated_text: 'Eating the immortal remnants of sacrifice, they go to the eternal <s>Brahman</s>.' |

children.text: yajña-śiṣṭa-amṛta-bhujo yānti brahma sanātanam |

body.text: daivayajñaprabhṛtiprāṇāyāmaparyanteṣu karmayogabhedeṣu svasamīhiteṣu pravṛttā ete sarve "saha yajñaiḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā" ityabhihitamahāyajñapūrvakanityanaimittikakarmarūpayajñavidaḥ tanniṣṭhāḥ tata eva kṣapitakalmaṣāḥ yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtena śarīradhāraṇaṃ kurvanta eva karmayoga vyāpṛtāḥ sanātanaṃ brahma yānti //
body.translated_text: These — all who are engaged in their chosen [practices] among the varieties of <s>karmayoga</s> from the sacrifice to the gods through to breath-control — all of them are knowers of sacrifice in the form of the regular and occasional actions preceded by the great sacrifice, as stated in 'having created beings together with sacrifices.' Established in that [practice], their sins have been thereby destroyed. Sustaining the body through the immortal remnant of sacrifice, they — engaged in <s>karmayoga</s> — go to the eternal <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: daiva-yajña-prabhṛti-prāṇa-āyāma-paryanteṣu karma-yoga-bhedeṣu sva-samīhiteṣu pravṛttā ete sarve "saha yajñaiḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā" ity-abhihita-mahā-yajña-pūrvaka-nitya-naimittika-karma-rūpa-yajña-vidaḥ tan-niṣṭhāḥ tata eva kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ yajña-śiṣṭa-amṛtena śarīra-dhāraṇaṃ kurvanta eva karma-yoga vyāpṛtāḥ sanātanaṃ brahma yānti //
nāyaṃ loko 'sty ayajñasya kuto 'nyaḥ kurusattama ||
children.translated_text: 'There is no world for one who does not sacrifice — how then the other, O best of <s>Kurus</s>?' ||

children.text: na ayaṃ loko 'sty ayajñasya kuto 'nyaḥ kuru-sattama ||

body.text: ayajñasya mahāyajñādipūrvakanityamaimittikakarmarahitasya nāyaṃ lokaḥ na prākṛtalokaḥ, prākṛtalokasaṃbandhidharmārthakāmākhyaḥ puruṣārtho na sidhyati / kuta ito 'nyo mokṣākhyaḥ puruṣārthaḥ? paramapuruṣārthatayā mokṣasya prastutatvāt taditarapuruṣārthaḥ ayaṃ lokaḥ iti nirdiśyate / sa hi prākṛtaḥ //
body.translated_text: For one who does not sacrifice — who is devoid of regular and occasional action preceded by the great sacrifices — there is not this world, not the worldly realm — the human goal called <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>, pertaining to the worldly realm, is not accomplished. How much less the other human goal called <s>mokṣa</s>? Since <s>mokṣa</s> is the topic as the supreme human goal, the other human goal is denoted as 'this world.' For it is worldly.

children.text: ayajñasya mahā-yajña-ādi-pūrvaka-nitya-maimittika-karma-rahitasya na ayaṃ lokaḥ na prākṛta-lokaḥ, prākṛta-loka-saṃbandhi-dharma-artha-kāma-ākhyaḥ puruṣa-artho na sidhyati / kuta ito 'nyo mokṣa-ākhyaḥ puruṣa-arthaḥ? parama-puruṣa-arthatayā mokṣasya prastutatvāt tad-itara-puruṣa-arthaḥ ayaṃ lokaḥ iti nirdiśyate / sa hi prākṛtaḥ //
evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe |
children.translated_text: 'Thus, many kinds of sacrifices are spread out at the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>.' |

children.text: karmajān viddhi tān sarvān evaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase ||
children.translated_text: 'Know them all to be born of action — thus knowing, you shall be liberated.' ||

children.text: evaṃ bahu-vidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe |
karma-jān viddhi tān sarvān evaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase ||

body.text: evaṃ hi bahuprakārāḥ karmayogāḥ brahmaṇo mukhe vitatāḥ ātmayāthātmyāvāptisādhanatayā sthitāḥ; tān uktalakṣaṇān uktabhedān karmayogān sarvān karmajān viddhi aharaharanuṣṭhīyamānanityanaimittikakarmajān viddhi / evaṃ jñātvā yathoktaprakāreṇānuṣṭhāya mokṣyase //
body.translated_text: Thus, indeed, the many varieties of <s>karmayoga</s> are spread out — established — at the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>, as means for attaining the true nature of the self. Know all those <s>karmayogas</s> — of the described characteristics and varieties — as born of action; know them to be born of the regular and occasional actions performed day by day. Thus knowing, and practicing in the described manner, you shall be liberated.

children.text: evaṃ hi bahu-prakārāḥ karma-yogāḥ brahmaṇo mukhe vitatāḥ ātma-yāthātmya-avāpti-sādhanatayā sthitāḥ; tān ukta-lakṣaṇān ukta-bhedān karma-yogān sarvān karma-jān viddhi ahar-ahar-anuṣṭhīyamāna-nitya-naimittika-karma-jān viddhi / evaṃ jñātvā yathā-ukta-prakāreṇa anuṣṭhāya mokṣyase //

body.text: antargatajñānatayā karmaṇo jñānākāratvam uktam; tatrāntargatajñāne karmaṇi jñānāṃśasyaiva prādhānyam āha --
body.translated_text: It has been stated that action has the form of knowledge because knowledge is contained within it. Now he states that in action containing knowledge, it is the knowledge-component alone that is predominant:

children.text: antargata-jñānatayā karmaṇo jñāna-ākāratvam uktam; tatra antargata-jñāne karmaṇi jñāna-aṃśasya eva prādhānyam āha ---
śreyān dravyamayād yajñāj jñānayajñaḥ parantapa |
children.translated_text: 'The sacrifice of knowledge is superior to the sacrifice of materials, O scorcher of foes.' |

children.text: sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate ||
children.translated_text: 'All action in its entirety, O <s>Pārtha</s>, culminates in knowledge.' ||

children.text: śreyān dravya-mayād yajñāj jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa |
sarvaṃ karma-akhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate ||

body.text: ubhayākāre karmaṇi dravyamayād aṃśāj jñānamayāṃśaḥ śreyān; sarvasya karmaṇaḥ taditarasya cākhilasyopādeyasya jñāne parisamāpteḥ tad eva sarvais sādhanaiḥ prāpyabhūtaṃ jñānaṃ karmāntargatatvenābhyasyate / tad eva abhyasyamānaṃ krameṇa prāpyadaśāṃ pratipadyate //
body.translated_text: In the action that has both forms, the knowledge-component is superior to the material-component. Because all action — and everything else besides, that is worthy of being pursued — culminates in knowledge. That very knowledge, which is what is to be attained through all means, is practiced as contained within action. That very [knowledge], being practiced, gradually reaches the stage of attainment.

children.text: ubhaya-ākāre karmaṇi dravya-mayād aṃśāj jñāna-maya-aṃśaḥ śreyān; sarvasya karmaṇaḥ tad-itarasya ca akhilasya upādeyasya jñāne parisamāpteḥ tad eva sarvais sādhanaiḥ prāpya-bhūtaṃ jñānaṃ karma-antargatatvena abhyasyate / tad eva abhyasyamānaṃ krameṇa prāpya-daśāṃ pratipadyate //
tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā |
children.translated_text: 'Know that by prostration, by inquiry, and by service.' |

children.text: upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninas tattvadarśinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The wise who see the truth will teach you knowledge.' ||

children.text: tad viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā |
upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninas tattva-darśinaḥ ||

body.text: tad atmaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ "avināśi tu tad viddhi" ityārabhya "eṣā te 'bhihitā" ityantena mayopadiṣṭam, "tadyuktakarmaṇi vartamānatvaṃ vipākānuguṇaṃ kāle kāle praṇipātaparipraśnasevādibhir viśadākāraṃ jñānibhyo viddhi / sākṣātkṛtātmasvarūpās tu jñāninaḥ praṇipātādibhyas sevitāḥ jñānabubhutsayā paritaḥ pṛcchatas tavāśayam ālakṣya jñānam upadekṣyanti //
body.translated_text: That knowledge concerning the self, taught by me from 'but know that to be indestructible' through to 'this has been declared to you' — know it, as you engage in the described action, in vivid form, from the wise, at the appropriate times, through prostration, inquiry, service, and the like. The wise — those who have directly realized the essential nature of the self — when served through prostration and the like, and when questioned all around by you who desire to know — discerning your disposition, they will teach you knowledge.

children.text: tad atma-viṣayaṃ jñānaṃ "avināśi tu tad viddhi" ity-ārabhya "eṣā te 'bhihitā" ity-antena maya ūpadiṣṭam, "tad-yukta-karmaṇi vartamānatvaṃ vipāka-anuguṇaṃ kāle kāle praṇipāta-paripraśna-sevā-ādibhir viśada-ākāraṃ jñānibhyo viddhi / sākṣāt-kṛta-ātma-sva-rūpās tu jñāninaḥ praṇipāta-ādibhyas sevitāḥ jñāna-bubhutsayā paritaḥ pṛcchatas tavā aśayam ālakṣya jñānam upadekṣyanti //

body.text: ātmayāthātmyaviṣayasya jñānasya sākṣātkārarūpasya lakṣaṇam āha --
body.translated_text: He states the characteristic of knowledge concerning the true nature of the self, in its form of direct realization:

children.text: ātma-yāthātmya-viṣayasya jñānasya sākṣātkāra-rūpasya lakṣaṇam āha ---
yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava |
children.translated_text: 'Knowing which, you will not again fall into such delusion, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>,' |

children.text: yena bhūtāny aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasy ātmany atho mayi ||
children.translated_text: 'and by which you will see all beings without exception in the self, and then in me.' ||

children.text: yaj jñātvā na punar moham evaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava |
yena bhūtāny aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasy ātmany atho mayi ||

body.text:
yaj jñānaṃ jñātvā punar evaṃ devādyātmābhimānarūpaṃ tatkṛtaṃ mamatādyāspadaṃ ca mohaṃ na yāsyasi, yena ca devamanuṣyādyākāreṇānusanhitāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni svātmany eva drakṣyasi, yatas tavānyeṣāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ prakṛtiviyuktānāṃ jñānaikākāratayā sāmyam / prakṛtisaṃsargadoṣavinirmuktam ātmarūpaṃ sarvaṃ samam iti ca vakṣyate, "nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ" iti / atho mayi sarvabhūtāny aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasi, matsvarūpasāmyāt pariśuddhasya sarvasyātmavastunaḥ / "idaṃ jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ" iti hi vakṣyate / tathā, "tadā vidvān puṇyapāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyam upaiti" ityevamādiṣu nāmarūpavinirmuktasyātmavastunaḥ parasvarūpasāmyam avagamyate / ataḥ
prakṛtivinirmuktaṃ sarvam ātmavastu parasparaṃ samaṃ sarveśvareṇa ca samam //
body.translated_text:
Knowing which knowledge, you will not again undergo such delusion in the form of the false identification of the self with gods and the like, and the possessiveness and the like caused by it; and by which [knowledge] you will see all beings — apprehended in the forms of gods, humans, and the like — in your own self alone, since there is equality of your self and the selves of other beings, when separated from material nature (<s>Prakṛti</s>), in having the single form of knowledge alone. That the form of the self, freed from the defect of conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s>, is entirely equal — this will be stated: 'For <s>Brahman</s> is flawless and equal; therefore they are established in <s>Brahman</s>.' And then you will see all beings entirely in Me, because of the equality of the purified self-reality with My own essential nature. For it will be stated: 'Having taken refuge in this knowledge, they have attained likeness to My nature.' Likewise, in passages such as 'Then the wise one, having shaken off merit and demerit, becomes stainless and attains supreme equality' — the equality of the self-reality, freed from name and form, with the Supreme's essential nature is understood. Therefore,
all self-reality, separated from <s>Prakṛti</s>, is mutually equal and equal with the Lord of all. ||

children.text:
yaj jñānaṃ jñātvā punar evaṃ deva-ādy-ātma-abhimāna-rūpaṃ tat-kṛtaṃ mamatā-ādy-āspadaṃ ca mohaṃ na yāsyasi, yena ca deva-manuṣya-ādy-ākāreṇa anusanhitāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni sva-ātmany eva drakṣyasi, yatas tava anyeṣāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ prakṛti-viyuktānāṃ jñāna-eka-ākāratayā sāmyam / prakṛti-saṃsarga-doṣa-vinirmuktam ātma-rūpaṃ sarvaṃ samam iti ca vakṣyate, "nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ" iti / atho mayi sarva-bhūtāny aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasi, mat-sva-rūpa-sāmyāt pariśuddhasya sarvasyā atma-vastunaḥ / "idaṃ jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ" iti hi vakṣyate / tathā, "tadā vidvān puṇya-pāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyam upaiti" ity-evam-ādiṣu nāma-rūpa-vinirmuktasyā atma-vastunaḥ para-sva-rūpa-sāmyam avagamyate / ataḥ
prakṛti-vinirmuktaṃ sarvam ātma-vastu parasparaṃ samaṃ sarva-īśvareṇa ca samam //
api ced asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even if you are the worst sinner among all sinners,

children.text: sarvaṃ jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṃ saṃtariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: you shall cross over all sin by the raft of knowledge alone. ||

children.text: api ced asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛttamaḥ |
sarvaṃ jñāna-plavena eva vṛjinaṃ saṃtariṣyasi ||

body.text: yady api sarvebhyaḥ pāpebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamo 'si, sarvaṃ pūrvārjitaṃ vṛjinarūpaṃ samudram ātmaviṣayajñānarūpaplavenaiva saṃtariṣyasi //
body.translated_text: Even if you are the worst sinner among all sinners, you shall cross over the entire ocean of sin accumulated previously, in the form of transgression, by the raft that is knowledge pertaining to the self. ||

children.text: yady api sarvebhyaḥ pāpebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛttamo 'si, sarvaṃ pūrva-arjitaṃ vṛjina-rūpaṃ samudram ātma-viṣaya-jñāna-rūpa-plavena eva saṃtariṣyasi //
yathaidhāṃsi samiddho 'gnir bhasmasāt kurute 'rjuna |
children.translated_text: Just as a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, O <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā ||
children.translated_text: so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes. ||

children.text: yatha aidhāṃsi samiddho 'gnir bhasmasāt kurute 'rjuna |
jñāna-agniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā ||

body.text: samyakpravṛddho 'gnir indhanasañcayam iva, ātmayāthātmyajñānarūpo 'gnir jīvātmagatam anādikālapravṛttānantakarmasañcayaṃ bhasmīkaroti //
body.translated_text: Just as a well-kindled fire [reduces] a heap of firewood [to ashes], the fire that is the knowledge of the true nature of the self reduces to ashes the infinite accumulation of <s>karma</s> pertaining to the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>), which has been accumulated since beginningless time. ||

children.text: samyak-pravṛddho 'gnir indhana-sañcayam iva, ātma-yāthātmya-jñāna-rūpo 'gnir jīva-ātma-gatam anādi-kāla-pravṛtta-ananta-karma-sañcayaṃ bhasmī-karoti //
na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitram iha vidyate |
children.translated_text: Indeed, no purifier equal to knowledge exists in this [world].

children.text: tat svayaṃ yogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati ||
children.translated_text: That [knowledge], the one perfected in <s>yoga</s> finds in the self, in time, by himself. ||

children.text: na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitram iha vidyate |
tat svayaṃ yoga-saṃsiddhaḥ kālenā atmani vindati ||

body.text: yasmād ātmajñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitraṃ śuddhikaram iha jagati vastvantaraṃ na vidyate, tasmād ātmajñānaṃ sarvapāpaṃ nāśayatītyarthaḥ / tat tathāvidhaṃ jñānaṃ yathopadeśam aharaharanuṣṭhīyamānajñānākārakarmayogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālena svātmani svayam eva labhate //
body.translated_text: Since no other entity in this world exists as a purifier — a cleanser — equal to self-knowledge, therefore self-knowledge destroys all sins — this is the meaning. That knowledge of such a kind — one who is perfected through <s>karmayoga</s> in the form of knowledge-natured [action], practiced day after day as instructed — [such a person] in time finds [it] in his own self, by himself. ||

children.text: yasmād ātma-jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitraṃ śuddhi-karam iha jagati vastv-antaraṃ na vidyate, tasmād ātma-jñānaṃ sarva-pāpaṃ nāśayati ity-arthaḥ / tat tathā-vidhaṃ jñānaṃ yathā-upadeśam ahar-ahar-anuṣṭhīyamāna-jñāna-ākāra-karma-yoga-saṃsiddhaḥ kālena sva-ātmani svayam eva labhate //

body.text: tad eva vispaṣṭam āha --
body.translated_text: He states this very [thing] clearly —

children.text: tad eva vispaṣṭam āha ---
śraddhāvān labhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: The faithful one obtains knowledge, devoted to it, with senses controlled;

children.text: jñānaṃ labdhvā parām śāntim acireṇādhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: having obtained knowledge, one quickly attains supreme peace. ||

children.text: śraddhāvān labhate jñānaṃ tat-paraḥ saṃyata-indriyaḥ |
jñānaṃ labdhvā parām śāntim acireṇa adhigacchati ||

body.text: evam upadeśāj jñānaṃ labdhvā copadiṣṭajñānavṛddhau śraddhāvān tatparaḥ tatraiva niyatamanāḥ taditaraviṣayāt saṃyatendriyo 'cireṇa kālenoktalakṣaṇavipākadaśāpannaṃ jñānaṃ labhate, tathāvidhaṃ jñānaṃ labdhvā parām śāntim acireṇādhigacchati paraṃ nirvāṇam āpnoti //
body.translated_text: Thus, having obtained knowledge from instruction, one who has faith in the growth of the instructed knowledge, who is devoted to it, whose mind is fixed on that alone, whose senses are controlled from objects other than that — in a short time obtains knowledge that has reached the stage of maturity as described, and having obtained such knowledge, quickly attains supreme peace — reaches supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s>. ||

children.text: evam upadeśāj jñānaṃ labdhvā ca upadiṣṭa-jñāna-vṛddhau śraddhāvān tat-paraḥ tatra eva niyata-manāḥ tad-itara-viṣayāt saṃyata-indriyo 'cireṇa kālena ukta-lakṣaṇa-vipāka-daśā-āpannaṃ jñānaṃ labhate, tathā-vidhaṃ jñānaṃ labdhvā parām śāntim acireṇa adhigacchati paraṃ nirvāṇam āpnoti //
ajñaś cāśraddadhānaś ca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati |
children.translated_text: The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting self perishes.

children.text: nāyaṃ loko 'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness is for the doubting self. ||

children.text: ajñaś ca aśraddadhānaś ca saṃśaya-ātmā vinaśyati |
na ayaṃ loko 'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśaya-ātmanaḥ ||

body.text: ajñaḥ evam upadeśalabdhajñānarahitaḥ, upadiṣṭajñānavṛddhyupāye cāśraddhadhānaḥ atvaramāṇaḥ, upadiṣṭe ca jñāne saṃśayātmā saṃśayamanāḥ vinaśyati vinaṣṭo bhavati / asminn upadiṣṭe ātmayāthātmyaviṣaye jñāne saṃśayātmano 'yam api prākṛto loko nāsti, na ca paraḥ / dharmārthakāmarūpapuruṣārthāś ca na sidhyanti, kuto mokṣa ityarthaḥ; śāstrīyakarmasiddhirūpatvāt sarveṣāṃ puruṣārthānām, śāstrīyakarmajanyasiddheś ca dehātiriktātmaniścayapūrvakatvāt / ataḥ sukhalavabhāgitvam ātmani saṃśayātmano na saṃbhavati //
body.translated_text: The ignorant — one devoid of the knowledge obtained from such instruction; and the faithless — one who is not earnest regarding the means for the growth of the instructed knowledge; and the doubting self — one whose mind is doubtful about the instructed knowledge — perishes, is destroyed. For one whose mind is doubtful about this instructed knowledge pertaining to the true nature of the self: neither this ordinary world nor the next [exists for him]. The human goals in the form of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s> are not accomplished — how much less <s>mokṣa</s>? — this is the meaning. Because all human goals are of the nature of accomplishment through scriptural action, and because the accomplishment arising from scriptural action is preceded by the certainty that the self exists beyond the body. Therefore, it is not possible for one who doubts the self to have even a share of happiness. ||

children.text: ajñaḥ evam upadeśa-labdha-jñāna-rahitaḥ, upadiṣṭa-jñāna-vṛddhy-upāye ca aśraddhadhānaḥ atvaramāṇaḥ, upadiṣṭe ca jñāne saṃśaya-ātmā saṃśaya-manāḥ vinaśyati vinaṣṭo bhavati / asminn upadiṣṭe ātma-yāthātmya-viṣaye jñāne saṃśaya-ātmano 'yam api prākṛto loko na asti, na ca paraḥ / dharma-artha-kāma-rūpa-puruṣa-arthāś ca na sidhyanti, kuto mokṣa ity-arthaḥ; śāstrīya-karma-siddhi-rūpatvāt sarveṣāṃ puruṣa-arthānām, śāstrīya-karma-janya-siddheś ca deha-atirikta-ātma-niścaya-pūrvakatvāt / ataḥ sukha-lava-bhāgitvam ātmani saṃśaya-ātmano na saṃbhavati //
yogasaṃnyastakarmāṇaṃ jñānasaṃcchinnasaṃśayam |
children.translated_text: One whose actions are renounced through <s>yoga</s>, whose doubts are cut asunder by knowledge,

children.text: ātmavantaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya ||
children.translated_text: who is self-possessed — actions do not bind him, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>. ||

children.text: yoga-saṃnyasta-karmāṇaṃ jñāna-saṃcchinna-saṃśayam |
ātmavantaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya ||

body.text: yathopadiṣṭayogena saṃnyastakarmāṇam jñānākāratāpannakarmāṇaṃ yathopadiṣṭena cātmajñānena ātmani saṃcchinnasaṃśayam, ātmavantaṃ manasvinam -- upadiṣṭārthe dṛḍhāvasthitamanasaṃ bandhahetubhūtaprācīnānantakarmāṇi na nibadhnanti //
body.translated_text: One whose actions are renounced through <s>yoga</s> as instructed — whose actions have assumed the character of knowledge — and whose doubts regarding the self are cut asunder by self-knowledge as instructed; who is self-possessed — resolute of mind, firmly established in the meaning taught — the infinite prior actions that were causes of bondage do not bind him. ||

children.text: yathā-upadiṣṭa-yogena saṃnyasta-karmāṇam jñāna-ākāratā-āpanna-karmāṇaṃ yathā-upadiṣṭena cā atma-jñānena ātmani saṃcchinna-saṃśayam, ātmavantaṃ manasvinam --- upadiṣṭa-arthe dṛḍha-avasthita-manasaṃ bandha-hetu-bhūta-prācīna-ananta-karmāṇi na nibadhnanti //
tasmād ajñānasaṃbhūtaṃ hṛtsthaṃ jñānāsinātmanaḥ |
