children.translated_text: Therefore, with the sword of self-knowledge, cutting this doubt

children.text: chittvainaṃ saṃśayaṃ yogam ātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata ||
children.translated_text: born of ignorance, seated in the heart — take up <s>yoga</s>! Arise, O <s>Bhārata</s>! ||

children.text: tasmād ajñāna-saṃbhūtaṃ hṛt-sthaṃ jñāna-asinā ātmanaḥ |
chittva ainaṃ saṃśayaṃ yogam ātiṣṭha uttiṣṭha bhārata ||

body.text: tasmād anādyajñānasaṃbhūtaṃ hṛtstham ātmaviṣayaṃ saṃśayaṃ mayopadiṣṭenātmajñānāsinā chittvā mayopadiṣṭaṃ karmayogam ātiṣṭha; tadartham uttiṣṭha bhārateti //
body.translated_text: Therefore, having cut this doubt regarding the self, seated in the heart, born of beginningless ignorance, with the sword of self-knowledge instructed by Me — take up the <s>karmayoga</s> instructed by Me; arise for that purpose, O <s>Bhārata</s>! ||

children.text: tasmād anādy-ajñāna-saṃbhūtaṃ hṛt-stham ātma-viṣayaṃ saṃśayaṃ maya ūpadiṣṭenā atma-jñāna-asinā chittvā maya ūpadiṣṭaṃ karma-yogam ātiṣṭha; tad-artham uttiṣṭha bhārata iti //

body.text: caturthe 'dhyāye karmayogasya jñānākāratāpūrvakasvarūpabhedo jñānāṃśasya ca prādhānyam uktam; jñānayogādhikāriṇo 'pi karmayogasyāntargatātmajñānatvād apramādatvāt sukaratvān nirapekṣatvāc ca jyāyastvaṃ tṛtīya evoktam / idānīṃ karmayogasyātmaprāptisādhanatve jñānaniṣṭhāyāś śaighryaṃ karmayogāntargatākarṭrtvānusandhānaprakāraṃ ca pratipādya tanmūlaṃ jñānaṃ ca viśodhyate //
body.translated_text: In the fourth chapter, the specific nature of <s>karmayoga</s> — preceded by its knowledge-natured character — and the predominance of the knowledge-aspect were stated. That <s>karmayoga</s> is superior even for one qualified for <s>jñānayoga</s> — because self-knowledge is included within it, because it is free from the danger of error, because it is easy to perform, and because it is self-sufficient — was stated already in the third [chapter]. Now, having demonstrated the swiftness of <s>jñānaniṣṭhā</s> (the knowledge-discipline) as a means of attaining the self through <s>karmayoga</s>, and the manner of the contemplation of non-agency (<s>akartṛtva</s>) included within <s>karmayoga</s>, the knowledge that is its root is also purified. ||

children.text: caturthe 'dhyāye karma-yogasya jñāna-ākāratā-pūrvaka-sva-rūpa-bhedo jñāna-aṃśasya ca prādhānyam uktam; jñāna-yoga-adhikāriṇo 'pi karma-yogasya antargata-ātma-jñānatvād apramādatvāt sukaratvān nirapekṣatvāc ca jyāyastvaṃ tṛtīya eva uktam / idānīṃ karma-yogasyā atma-prāpti-sādhanatve jñāna-niṣṭhāyāś śaighryaṃ karma-yoga-antargata-akarṭrtva-anusandhāna-prakāraṃ ca pratipādya tan-mūlaṃ jñānaṃ ca viśodhyate //
saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punar yogaṃ ca śaṃsasi |
children.translated_text: You praise the renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) of actions, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and again <s>yoga</s> (discipline of action) too;

children.text: yac chreya etayor ekaṃ tan me brūhi suniścitam ||
children.translated_text: tell me decisively which one of these two is the better. ||

children.text: saṃnyāsaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṛṣṇa punar yogaṃ ca śaṃsasi |
yac chreya etayor ekaṃ tan me brūhi suniścitam ||

body.text: karmaṇāṃ saṃnyāsaṃ jñānayogam punaḥ karmayogaṃ ca śaṃsasi / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- dvitīye 'dhyāye mumukṣoḥ prathamaṃ karmayoga eva kāryaḥ, karmayogena mṛditāntaḥkaraṇakaṣāyasya jñānayogenātmadarśanaṃ kāryam iti pratipādya punas tṛtīyacaturthayoḥ jñānayogādhikāradaśāpannasyāpi karmaniṣṭhaiva jyāyasī, saiva jñānaniṣṭhānirapekṣā ātmaprāptau sādhanam iti karmaniṣṭhāṃ praśaṃśasi iti / tatraitayor jñānayogakarmayogayor ātmaprāptisādhanabhāve yad ekaṃ saukāryac chaighryāc ca śreyaḥ śreṣṭham iti suniścitam, tan me brūhi //
body.translated_text: You praise the renunciation of actions — <s>jñānayoga</s> — and again <s>karmayoga</s> too. What is being said is this: In the second chapter, having established that for the seeker of liberation, <s>karmayoga</s> alone must first be practiced, and that through <s>karmayoga</s>, when the impurities of the inner instrument are worn away, the vision of the self is to be achieved through <s>jñānayoga</s> — then again in the third and fourth [chapters], you praise the discipline of action, [saying] that even for one who has reached the stage of qualification for <s>jñānayoga</s>, the discipline of action alone is superior, and that it alone, without dependence on the knowledge-discipline, is the means of attaining the self. In that case, of these two — <s>jñānayoga</s> and <s>karmayoga</s> — as means of attaining the self, tell me which single one is the best, the most excellent, in terms of ease and swiftness, with full certainty. ||

children.text: karmaṇāṃ saṃnyāsaṃ jñāna-yogam punaḥ karma-yogaṃ ca śaṃsasi / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- dvitīye 'dhyāye mumukṣoḥ prathamaṃ karma-yoga eva kāryaḥ, karma-yogena mṛdita-antaḥkaraṇa-kaṣāyasya jñāna-yogenā atma-darśanaṃ kāryam iti pratipādya punas tṛtīya-caturthayoḥ jñāna-yoga-adhikāra-daśā-āpannasya api karma-niṣṭha aiva jyāyasī, sa aiva jñāna-niṣṭhā-nirapekṣā ātma-prāptau sādhanam iti karma-niṣṭhāṃ praśaṃśasi iti / tatra etayor jñāna-yoga-karma-yogayor ātma-prāpti-sādhana-bhāve yad ekaṃ saukāryac chaighryāc ca śreyaḥ śreṣṭham iti suniścitam, tan me brūhi //
saṃnyāsaḥ karmayogaś ca niśśreyasakarāv ubhau |
children.translated_text: Both renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) and the discipline of action (<s>karmayoga</s>) lead to the highest good.

children.text: tayos tu karmasaṃnyāsāt karmayogo viśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: But of the two, the discipline of action excels over the renunciation of actions. ||

children.text: saṃnyāsaḥ karma-yogaś ca niśśreyasa-karāv ubhau |
tayos tu karma-saṃnyāsāt karma-yogo viśiṣyate ||

body.text: saṃnyāsaḥ jñānayogaḥ, karmayogaś ca jñānayogaśaktasyāpy ubhau nirapekṣau niśśreyasakarau / tayos tu karmasaṃnyāsāj jñānayogāt karmayoga eva viśiṣyate //
body.translated_text: Renunciation is <s>jñānayoga</s>, and <s>karmayoga</s> too — even for one capable of <s>jñānayoga</s> — both independently lead to the highest good. But of the two, <s>karmayoga</s> alone excels over the renunciation of actions, i.e., over <s>jñānayoga</s>. ||

children.text: saṃnyāsaḥ jñāna-yogaḥ, karma-yogaś ca jñāna-yoga-śaktasya apy ubhau nirapekṣau niśśreyasa-karau / tayos tu karma-saṃnyāsāj jñāna-yogāt karma-yoga eva viśiṣyate //

body.text: kuta ity atrāha --
body.translated_text: As to why — he says:

children.text: kuta ity atrā aha ---
jñeyaḥ sa nityasaṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati |
children.translated_text: He should be known as a perpetual renunciant (<s>nityasaṃnyāsī</s>) who neither hates nor desires;

children.text: nirdvandvo hi mahābāho sukhaṃ bandhāt pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: free from the pairs of opposites, O mighty-armed, he is easily freed from bondage. ||

children.text: jñeyaḥ sa nitya-saṃnyāsī yo na dveṣṭi na kāṅkṣati |
nirdvandvo hi mahābāho sukhaṃ bandhāt pramucyate ||

body.text: yaḥ karmayogī tadantargatātmānubhavatṛptas tadvyatiriktaṃ kim api na kāṅkṣati, tata eva kim api na dveṣṭi, tata eva dvandvasahaś ca; sa nityasaṃnyāsī nityajñānaniṣṭha iti jñeyaḥ / sa hi sukarakarmayoganiṣṭhatayā sukhaṃ bandhāt pramucyate //
body.translated_text: The <s>karmayogin</s> who, being satisfied by the experience of the self included within [<s>karmayoga</s>], does not desire anything other than that, and for that very reason does not hate anything, and for that very reason endures the pairs of opposites — he should be known as a perpetual renunciant, one perpetually established in the knowledge-discipline. For he, by being established in the easy-to-perform discipline of action, is easily freed from bondage. ||

children.text: yaḥ karma-yogī tad-antargata-ātma-anubhava-tṛptas tad-vyatiriktaṃ kim api na kāṅkṣati, tata eva kim api na dveṣṭi, tata eva dvandva-sahaś ca; sa nitya-saṃnyāsī nitya-jñāna-niṣṭha iti jñeyaḥ / sa hi sukara-karma-yoga-niṣṭhatayā sukhaṃ bandhāt pramucyate //

body.text: jñānayogakarmayogayor ātmaprāptisādhanabhāve 'nyonyanairapekṣyam āha --
body.translated_text: He states the mutual independence of <s>jñānayoga</s> and <s>karmayoga</s> as means of attaining the self —

children.text: jñāna-yoga-karma-yogayor ātma-prāpti-sādhana-bhāve 'nyonya-nairapekṣyam āha ---
sāṃkhyayogau pṛthag bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ |
children.translated_text: The childish speak of <s>Sāṅkhya</s> (knowledge-discipline) and <s>Yoga</s> (action-discipline) as different, not the wise.

children.text: ekam apy āsthitas samyag ubhayor vindante phalam ||
children.translated_text: One who is properly established in even one of the two obtains the fruit of both. ||

children.text: sāṃkhya-yogau pṛthag bālāḥ pravadanti na paṇḍitāḥ |
ekam apy āsthitas samyag ubhayor vindante phalam ||

body.text: jñānayogakarmayogau phalabhedāt pṛthag bhūtau ye pravadanti, te bālāḥ aniṣpannajñānāḥ na paṇḍitāḥ akṛtsnavidaḥ / karmayogo jñānayogam eva sādhayati; jñānayogas tv eka ātmāvalokanaṃ sādhayatīti tayoḥ phalabhedena pṛthaktvaṃ vadanto na paṇḍitā ityarthaḥ / ubhayor ātmāvalokanaikaphalayor ekaphalatvena ekam apy āsthitas tad eva phalaṃ labhate //
body.translated_text: Those who say that <s>jñānayoga</s> and <s>karmayoga</s> are different because of a difference of fruit — they are childish, of immature knowledge; not wise, not knowing the whole [truth]. <s>Karmayoga</s> accomplishes <s>jñānayoga</s> itself; but <s>jñānayoga</s> alone accomplishes the vision of the self — so those who speak of their separation due to a difference of fruit are not wise — this is the meaning. One who is properly established in even one of the two — which have a single fruit in the vision of the self — obtains that very fruit. ||

children.text: jñāna-yoga-karma-yogau phala-bhedāt pṛthag bhūtau ye pravadanti, te bālāḥ aniṣpanna-jñānāḥ na paṇḍitāḥ akṛtsna-vidaḥ / karma-yogo jñāna-yogam eva sādhayati; jñāna-yogas tv eka ātma-avalokanaṃ sādhayati iti tayoḥ phala-bhedena pṛthaktvaṃ vadanto na paṇḍitā ity-arthaḥ / ubhayor ātma-avalokana-eka-phalayor eka-phalatvena ekam apy āsthitas tad eva phalaṃ labhate //

body.text: etad eva vivṛṇoti --
body.translated_text: He elaborates on this very [point] —

children.text: etad eva vivṛṇoti ---
yat sāṃkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tad yogair api gamyate |
children.translated_text: The state attained by the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> (practitioners of knowledge) is reached also by the <s>Yogins</s> (practitioners of action).

children.text: ekaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||
children.translated_text: He who sees <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> as one — he [truly] sees. ||

children.text: yat sāṃkhyaiḥ prāpyate sthānaṃ tad yogair api gamyate |
ekaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||

body.text: sāṃkhyaiḥ jñānaniṣṭhaiḥ / yad atmāvalokanarūpaṃ phalaṃ prāpyate, tad eva karmayoganiṣṭhair api prāpyate / evam ekaphalatvena ekaṃ vaikalpikaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati, sa paśyati sa eva paṇḍita ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: By the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> — those established in the knowledge-discipline: the fruit that is attained, in the form of the vision of the self — that very [fruit] is attained also by those established in <s>karmayoga</s>. Thus, he who sees <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> as one — as alternative [means] with a single fruit — he [truly] sees; he alone is wise — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: sāṃkhyaiḥ jñāna-niṣṭhaiḥ / yad atma-avalokana-rūpaṃ phalaṃ prāpyate, tad eva karma-yoga-niṣṭhair api prāpyate / evam eka-phalatvena ekaṃ vaikalpikaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati, sa paśyati sa eva paṇḍita ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: iyān viśeṣa ity āhā --
body.translated_text: He states the extent of the difference —

children.text: iyān viśeṣa ity āhā ---
saṃnyāsas tu mahābāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ |
children.translated_text: But renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>), O mighty-armed, is difficult to attain without <s>Yoga</s>;

children.text: yogayukto munir brahma na cireṇādhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: the sage established in <s>Yoga</s> quickly attains <s>Brahman</s>. ||

children.text: saṃnyāsas tu mahābāho duḥkham āptum ayogataḥ |
yoga-yukto munir brahma na cireṇa adhigacchati ||

body.text: saṃnyāsaḥ jñānayogas tu ayogataḥ karmayogād rte prāptum aśakyaḥ; yogayuktaḥ karmayogayuktaḥ svayam eva muniḥ ātmamananaśīlaḥ sukhena karmayogaṃ sādhayitvā na cireṇa alpenaiva kālena brahmādhigacchati ātmānaṃ prāpnoti / jñānayogayuktas tu mahatā duḥkhena jñānayogaṃ sādhayati; duḥkhasādhyatvād ātmānaṃ cireṇa prāpnotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Renunciation — <s>jñānayoga</s> — without <s>Yoga</s>, i.e., without <s>karmayoga</s>, is impossible to attain. One established in <s>Yoga</s> — established in <s>karmayoga</s> — spontaneously becomes a <s>muni</s> (sage), one given to self-contemplation; having easily accomplished <s>karmayoga</s>, he quickly, in a very short time, attains <s>Brahman</s> — attains the self. But one established in <s>jñānayoga</s> accomplishes <s>jñānayoga</s> with great difficulty; since it is difficult to accomplish, he attains the self after a long time — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: saṃnyāsaḥ jñāna-yogas tu ayogataḥ karma-yogād rte prāptum aśakyaḥ; yoga-yuktaḥ karma-yoga-yuktaḥ svayam eva muniḥ ātma-manana-śīlaḥ sukhena karma-yogaṃ sādhayitvā na cireṇa alpena eva kālena brahma adhigacchati ātmānaṃ prāpnoti / jñāna-yoga-yuktas tu mahatā duḥkhena jñāna-yogaṃ sādhayati; duḥkha-sādhyatvād ātmānaṃ cireṇa prāpnoti ity-arthaḥ //
yogayukto viśuddhātmā vijitātmā jitendriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Established in <s>yoga</s>, purified in self, self-conquered, sense-conquered,

children.text: sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā kurvann api na lipyate ||
children.translated_text: whose self has become the self of all beings — even while acting, he is not tainted. ||

children.text: yoga-yukto viśuddha-atmā vijita-ātmā jita-indriyaḥ |
sarva-bhūta-ātma-bhūta-ātmā kurvann api na lipyate ||

body.text:
karmayogayuktas tu śāstrīye paramapuruṣārādhanarūpe viśuddhe karmaṇi vartamānaḥ tena viśuddhamanāḥ vijitātmā svābhyaste te karmaṇi vyāpṛtamanastvena sukhena vijitamanāḥ , tata eva jitendiyaḥ kartur ātmano yāthātmyānusandhānaniṣṭhatayā sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā sarveṣāṃ devādibhūtānām ātmabhūta ātmā yasyāsau sarvabhūtātmabhūtātmā / ātmayāthātmyam anusandhānasya hi devādīnāṃ svasya caikākāra ātmā; devādibhedānāṃ prakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣarūpatayātmākāratvāsaṃbhavāt / prakṛtiviyuktaḥ sarvatra devādideheṣu jñānaikākāratayā samānākāra iti "nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma" iti anantaram eva vakṣyate / sa evaṃbhūtaḥ karma kurvann api anātmany ātmābhimānena na lipyate -- na saṃbadhyate / ato 'cireṇātmānaṃ
prāpnotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: One established in <s>karmayoga</s>, engaged in scriptural action in the form of worshipping the Supreme Person, which is pure — by that, purified in mind; self-conquered — easily conquered in mind because the mind is engaged in that habitual action; and for that very reason, sense-conquered; established in the contemplation of the true nature of the self that is the agent — whose self has become the self of all beings: 'whose self has become the self of the selves of all beings' — i.e., one whose self is the self of the selves of all beings such as gods and the like. For in the contemplation of the true nature of the self, the self of gods and the like and of oneself is of a single form — since the differentiations of gods and the like, being specific transformations of <s>Prakṛti</s>, cannot possibly be of the form of the self. Separated from <s>Prakṛti</s>, [the self] in all bodies of gods and the like is of uniform form as having the single nature of knowledge — thus 'for <s>Brahman</s> is flawless and equal' will be stated immediately after. Being of such a nature, even while performing action, he is not tainted by sin in the form of the false identification of the self with the non-self — he is not bound. Therefore, he quickly attains the self — this is the meaning. ||

children.text:
karma-yoga-yuktas tu śāstrīye parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-rūpe viśuddhe karmaṇi vartamānaḥ tena viśuddha-manāḥ vijita-ātmā sva-abhyaste te karmaṇi vyāpṛta-manastvena sukhena vijita-manāḥ , tata eva jita-indiyaḥ kartur ātmano yāthātmya-anusandhāna-niṣṭhatayā sarva-bhūta-ātma-bhūta-ātmā sarveṣāṃ deva-ādi-bhūtānām ātma-bhūta ātmā yasya asau sarva-bhūta-ātma-bhūta-ātmā / ātma-yāthātmyam anusandhānasya hi deva-ādīnāṃ svasya ca eka-ākāra ātmā; deva-ādi-bhedānāṃ prakṛti-pariṇāma-viśeṣa-rūpatayā ātma-ākāratva-asaṃbhavāt / prakṛti-viyuktaḥ sarvatra deva-ādi-deheṣu jñāna-eka-ākāratayā samāna-ākāra iti "nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma" iti anantaram eva vakṣyate / sa evaṃ-bhūtaḥ karma kurvann api anātmany ātma-abhimānena na lipyate --- na saṃbadhyate / ato 'cireṇā atmānaṃ
prāpnoti ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: yataḥ saukaryāc chaighryāc ca karmayoga eva śreyān, atas tadapekṣitaṃ śṛṇu --
body.translated_text: Since, due to ease and swiftness, <s>karmayoga</s> alone is superior, therefore hear what is required for it —

children.text: yataḥ saukaryāc chaighryāc ca karma-yoga eva śreyān, atas tad-apekṣitaṃ śṛṇu ---
naiṣa kiñcit karomīti yukto manyeta tattvavit |
children.translated_text: The knower of truth, established [in <s>yoga</s>], should think 'I do nothing at all,'

children.text: paśyan śṛṇvan spṛśan jighran aśnan gacchan svapan śvasan ||
children.translated_text: while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, breathing, ||

children.text: na eṣa kiñcit karomi iti yukto manyeta tattva-vit |
paśyan śṛṇvan spṛśan jighran aśnan gacchan svapan śvasan ||
pralapan visṛjan gṛhṇan unmiṣan nimiṣann api |
children.translated_text: talking, releasing, grasping, opening the eyes, and closing the eyes —

children.text: indriyāṇīndriyārtheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan ||
children.translated_text: holding [the thought] that the senses alone engage with the sense-objects. ||

children.text: pralapan visṛjan gṛhṇan unmiṣan nimiṣann api |
indriyāṇi indriya-artheṣu vartanta iti dhārayan ||

body.text: evam ātmatattvavic śrotrādīni jñānendriyāṇi, vāgādīni ca karmendriyāṇi, praṇāś ca svaviṣayeṣu vartanta iti dhārayan anusandhānaḥ nāhaṃ kiṃcit karomīti manyeta -- jñānaikasvabhāvasya mama karmamūlendriyaprāṇasaṃbandhakṛtam īdṛśaṃ kartṛtvam; na svarūpaprayuktam iti manyetetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, one who knows the truth of the self, holding the thought — contemplating — that the sense-organs of knowledge such as the ear and the like, the sense-organs of action such as speech and the like, and the vital breaths engage with their respective objects, should think 'I do nothing at all' — [meaning:] 'For me, whose sole essential nature is knowledge, this agency is caused by the connection with sense-organs, the mind, and vital breaths, which are rooted in <s>karma</s>; it is not produced by my own essential nature' — this is what he should think — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: evam ātma-tattva-vic śrotra-ādīni jñāna-indriyāṇi, vāg-ādīni ca karma-indriyāṇi, praṇāś ca sva-viṣayeṣu vartanta iti dhārayan anusandhānaḥ na ahaṃ kiṃcit karomi iti manyeta --- jñāna-eka-sva-bhāvasya mama karma-mūla-indriya-prāṇa-saṃbandha-kṛtam īdṛśaṃ kartṛtvam; na sva-rūpa-prayuktam iti manyeta ity-arthaḥ //
brahmaṇy ādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, offering actions to <s>Brahman</s>, performs [them] having abandoned attachment,

children.text: lipyate na sa pāpena padmapatram ivāmbhasā ||
children.translated_text: is not tainted by sin, like a lotus leaf by water. ||

children.text: brahmaṇy ādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ |
lipyate na sa pāpena padma-patram iva ambhasā ||

body.text: brahmaśabdena prakṛtir ihocyate / "mama yonir mahad brahma" iti hi vakṣyate / indriyāṇāṃ prakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣarūpatvena indriyākāreṇāvasthitāyāṃ prakṛtau "paśyañ chṛṇvan" ityādyuktaprakāreṇa karmāṇy ādhāya, phalasaṅgaṃ tyaktvā, naiva kiṃcit karomīti yaḥ karmāṇi karoti, sa prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭatayā vartamāno 'pi prakṛtyātmābhimānarūpeṇa bandhahetunā pāpena na lipyate / padmapatram ivāmbhasā -- yathā padmapatram ambhasā saṃsṛṣṭam api na lipyate, tathā na lipyata ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Here, by the word <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature) is denoted. For it will be stated: 'My womb is the great <s>Brahman</s>.' Since the sense-organs are specific transformations of <s>Prakṛti</s>, having offered actions to <s>Prakṛti</s> — established in the form of the sense-organs — in the manner stated as 'seeing, hearing' and the like, having abandoned attachment to results, one who performs actions [thinking] 'I do nothing at all' — he, even though existing in conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s>, is not tainted by sin that is the cause of bondage in the form of the false identification of <s>Prakṛti</s> with the self. Like a lotus leaf by water — just as a lotus leaf, even though in contact with water, is not tainted [by it], so he is not tainted — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: brahma-śabdena prakṛtir iha ucyate / "mama yonir mahad brahma" iti hi vakṣyate / indriyāṇāṃ prakṛti-pariṇāma-viśeṣa-rūpatvena indriya-ākāreṇa avasthitāyāṃ prakṛtau "paśyañ chṛṇvan" ity-ādy-ukta-prakāreṇa karmāṇy ādhāya, phala-saṅgaṃ tyaktvā, na eva kiṃcit karomi iti yaḥ karmāṇi karoti, sa prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭatayā vartamāno 'pi prakṛty-ātma-abhimāna-rūpeṇa bandha-hetunā pāpena na lipyate / padma-patram iva ambhasā --- yathā padma-patram ambhasā saṃsṛṣṭam api na lipyate, tathā na lipyata ity-arthaḥ //
kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalair indriyair api |
children.translated_text: <s>Yogins</s> perform action with body, mind, intellect, and the senses alone, |

children.text: yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvātmaśuddhaye ||
children.translated_text: abandoning attachment, for the purification of the self. ||

children.text: kāyena manasā buddhyā kevalair indriyair api |
yoginaḥ karma kurvanti saṅgaṃ tyaktvā ātma-śuddhaye ||

body.text: kāyamanobuddhīndriyasādhyaṃ karma svargādiphalasaṅgaṃ tyaktvā yogina ātmaviśuddhaye kuranti; ātmagataprācīnakarmabandhavināśāya kurvantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Yogins</s> perform action — accomplished through body, mind, intellect, and senses — abandoning attachment to fruits such as heaven and the like, for the purification of the self; the meaning is: they perform [action] for the destruction of the bondage of prior <s>karma</s> pertaining to the self. //

children.text: kāya-mano-buddhi-indriya-sādhyaṃ karma svarga-ādi-phala-saṅgaṃ tyaktvā yogina ātma-viśuddhaye kuranti; ātma-gata-prācīna-karma-bandha-vināśāya kurvanti ity-arthaḥ //
yuktaḥ karmaphalaṃ tyaktvā śāntim āpnoti naiṣṭhikīm |
children.translated_text: The disciplined one, abandoning the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. |

children.text: ayuktaḥ kāmakāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate ||
children.translated_text: The undisciplined one, attached to the fruit through desire, is bound. ||

children.text: yuktaḥ karma-phalaṃ tyaktvā śāntim āpnoti naiṣṭhikīm |
ayuktaḥ kāma-kāreṇa phale sakto nibadhyate ||

body.text: yuktaḥ -- ātmavyatiriktaphaleṣv acapalaḥ ātmaikapravaṇaḥ, karmaphalaṃ tyaktvā kevalam ātmaśuddhaye karmānuṣṭhāya naiṣṭhikīṃ śāntim āpnoti -- sthirām ātmānubhavarūpāṃ nirvṛtim āpnoti / ayuktaḥ -- ātmavyatiriktaphaleṣu capalaḥ ātmāvalokanavimukhaḥ kāmakāreṇa phale saktaḥ karmāṇi kurvan nityaṃ karmabhir badhyate -- nityasaṃsārī bhavati / ataḥ phalasaṅgarahitaḥ indriyākāreṇa pariṇatāyāṃ prakṛtau karmāṇi saṃnyasya ātmano bandhamocanāyaiva karmāṇi kurvītetyuktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: The disciplined one (<s>yukta</s>) — one who is not fickle regarding fruits other than the self, [and is] solely inclined toward the self — abandoning the fruit of action, performing action solely for the purification of the self, attains lasting peace — attains a stable bliss in the form of the experience of the self. The undisciplined one (<s>ayukta</s>) — one who is fickle regarding fruits other than the self, averse to the vision of the self — attached to the fruit through desire, performing actions, is always bound by actions — becomes an eternal transmigrator. Therefore, it has been said that one free from attachment to fruits, surrendering actions to <s>Prakṛti</s> that has transformed into the form of the senses, should perform actions solely for the liberation of the self from bondage. //

children.text: yuktaḥ --- ātma-vyatirikta-phaleṣv acapalaḥ ātma-eka-pravaṇaḥ, karma-phalaṃ tyaktvā kevalam ātma-śuddhaye karma-anuṣṭhāya naiṣṭhikīṃ śāntim āpnoti --- sthirām ātma-anubhava-rūpāṃ nirvṛtim āpnoti / ayuktaḥ --- ātma-vyatirikta-phaleṣu capalaḥ ātma-avalokana-vimukhaḥ kāma-kāreṇa phale saktaḥ karmāṇi kurvan nityaṃ karmabhir badhyate --- nitya-saṃsārī bhavati / ataḥ phala-saṅga-rahitaḥ indriya-ākāreṇa pariṇatāyāṃ prakṛtau karmāṇi saṃnyasya ātmano bandha-mocanāya eva karmāṇi kurvīta ity-uktaṃ bhavati //

body.text: atha dehākāreṇa pariṇatāyāṃ prakṛtau kartṛtvasaṃnyāsa ucyate --
body.translated_text: Now the surrender of agency to <s>Prakṛti</s> that has transformed into the form of the body is stated:

children.text: atha deha-ākāreṇa pariṇatāyāṃ prakṛtau kartṛtva-saṃnyāsa ucyate ---
sarvakarmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyāste sukhaṃ vaśī /
children.translated_text: Renouncing all actions mentally, the self-controlled embodied one dwells happily, |

children.text: navadvāre pure dehī naiva kurvan na kārayan //
children.translated_text: in the city of nine gates, neither acting nor causing [others] to act. //

children.text: sarva-karmāṇi manasā saṃnyasyā aste sukhaṃ vaśī /
nava-dvāre pure dehī na eva kurvan na kārayan //

body.text: ātmanaḥ prācīnakarmamūladehasaṃbandhaprayuktam idaṃ karmaṇāṃ kartṛtvam; na svarūpaprayuktam iti vivekaviṣayeṇa manasā sarvāṇi karmāṇi navadvāre pure saṃnyasya dehī svayaṃ vaśī dehādhiṣṭhānaprayatnam akurvan dehaṃ ca naiva kārayan sukham āste //
body.translated_text: This agency regarding actions is caused by the connection with the body, which is rooted in prior <s>karma</s> — it is not inherent in the essential nature [of the self]. Through a mind whose domain is this discrimination, the embodied one, surrendering all actions in the city of nine gates, being self-controlled, not himself exerting effort to govern the body, and not causing the body to act — dwells happily. //

children.text: ātmanaḥ prācīna-karma-mūla-deha-saṃbandha-prayuktam idaṃ karmaṇāṃ kartṛtvam; na sva-rūpa-prayuktam iti viveka-viṣayeṇa manasā sarvāṇi karmāṇi nava-dvāre pure saṃnyasya dehī svayaṃ vaśī deha-adhiṣṭhāna-prayatnam akurvan dehaṃ ca na eva kārayan sukham āste //

body.text: sākṣād ātmanaḥ svābhāvikaṃ rūpam āha --
body.translated_text: He states the direct, natural form of the self:

children.text: sākṣād ātmanaḥ svābhāvikaṃ rūpam āha ---
na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ |
children.translated_text: The lord [self] does not create agency, nor actions for beings, |

children.text: na karmaphalasaṃyogaṃ svabhāvas tu pravartate ||
children.translated_text: nor the conjunction with the fruit of action — rather, nature operates. ||

children.text: na kartṛtvaṃ na karmāṇi lokasya sṛjati prabhuḥ |
na karma-phala-saṃyogaṃ sva-bhāvas tu pravartate ||

body.text: asya devatiryaṅmanuṣyasthāvarātmanā prakṛtisaṃsargeṇa vartamānasya lokasya devādyasādhāraṇaṃ kartṛtvaṃ tattadasādhāraṇāni karmāṇi tattatkarmajanyadevādiphalasaṃyogaṃ ca, ayaṃ prabhuḥ akarmavaśyaḥ svābhāvikasvarūpeṇāvasthita ātmā na sṛjati notpādayati / kas tarhi? svabhāvas tu pravartate / svabhāvaḥ prakṛtivāsanā / anādikālapravṛttapūrvapūrvakarmajanitadevādyākāraprakṛtisaṃsargakṛtatattadātmābhimānajanitavāsanākṛtam īdṛśaṃ kartṛtvādikaṃ sarvam; na svarūpaprayuktam ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: For this world (<s>loka</s>), which exists through conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s> in the form of gods, animals, humans, and immovable things — the agency specific to gods and the like, the actions specific to each, and the conjunction with the fruits born of those respective actions — this lord (<s>prabhu</s>), the self, not subject to <s>karma</s>, established in its natural essential form, does not create, does not produce [these]. What then? Rather, nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) operates. Nature means the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of <s>Prakṛti</s>. All such agency and the like is produced by the latent impressions generated by the conceit of self-identity with the respective forms of gods and the like — which [conceit is itself] produced by the conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s> in the form of gods and the like, generated by prior <s>karmas</s> accumulated since beginningless time — [all this] is not inherent in the essential nature [of the self] — this is the meaning. //

children.text: asya deva-tiryaṅ-manuṣya-sthāvara-ātmanā prakṛti-saṃsargeṇa vartamānasya lokasya deva-ādy-asādhāraṇaṃ kartṛtvaṃ tat-tad-asādhāraṇāni karmāṇi tat-tat-karma-janya-deva-ādi-phala-saṃyogaṃ ca, ayaṃ prabhuḥ akarma-vaśyaḥ svābhāvika-sva-rūpeṇa avasthita ātmā na sṛjati na utpādayati / kas tarhi? sva-bhāvas tu pravartate / sva-bhāvaḥ prakṛti-vāsanā / anādi-kāla-pravṛtta-pūrva-pūrva-karma-janita-deva-ādy-ākāra-prakṛti-saṃsarga-kṛta-tat-tad-ātma-abhimāna-janita-vāsanā-kṛtam īdṛśaṃ kartṛtva-ādikaṃ sarvam; na sva-rūpa-prayuktam ity-arthaḥ //
nādatte kasyacit pāpaṃ na caiva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ |
children.translated_text: The all-pervading [self] does not take on the sin of anyone, nor indeed the merit. |

children.text: ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge is covered by ignorance — by that, beings are deluded. ||

children.text: nā adatte kasyacit pāpaṃ na ca eva sukṛtaṃ vibhuḥ |
ajñānenā avṛtaṃ jñānaṃ tena muhyanti jantavaḥ ||

body.text: kasyacit svasaṃbandhitayābhimatasya putrādeḥ pāpaṃ duḥkhaṃ nādatte nāpanudati / kasyacit pratikūlatayābhimatasya sukṛtaṃ sukhaṃ ca nādatte nāpanudati / yato 'yaṃ vibhuḥ; na kvācitkaḥ, na devādidehādyasādhāraṇadeśaḥ, ata eva na kasyacit saṃbandhī, na kasyacit pratikūlaś ca / sarvam idaṃ vāsanākṛtam / evaṃsvabhāvasya katham iyaṃ viparītavāsanā utpadyate? ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jñānam jñānavirodhinā pūrvapūrvakarmaṇā svaphalānubhavayogyatvāya asya jñānam āvṛtaṃ saṃkucitam / tena jñānāvaraṇarūpeṇa karmaṇā devādidehasaṃyogas tattadātmābhimānarūpamohaś ca jāyate / tataś ca tathāvidhātmābhimānavāsanā, taducitakarmavāsanā ca; vāsanāto viparītātmābhimānaḥ, karmārambhaś copapadyate //
body.translated_text: It does not take on, does not remove, the sin, i.e., the suffering, of anyone regarded as related to it — such as a son and the like. Nor does it take on, nor remove, the merit, i.e., the happiness, of anyone regarded as opposed to it. Because this [self] is all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>) — not limited, not confined to a particular place such as the body of a god and the like. Therefore it is not related to anyone, nor opposed to anyone. All this is produced by latent impressions. How does this perverted latent impression arise for one of such a nature? Knowledge is covered by ignorance — by prior <s>karma</s> that opposes knowledge, for the purpose of [bringing about] the fitness for experiencing its own fruit, the knowledge [of the self] is covered, contracted. Through that <s>karma</s>, which has the form of covering knowledge, there arises conjunction with bodies such as those of gods and the like, and the delusion in the form of the conceit of self-identity with those respective [bodies]. And from that arise the latent impressions of such perverted self-conceit, and the latent impressions for actions appropriate to that [conceit]. And from the latent impressions arise the perverted self-conceit and the undertaking of actions. //

children.text: kasyacit sva-saṃbandhitaya ābhimatasya putra-ādeḥ pāpaṃ duḥkhaṃ nā adatte na apanudati / kasyacit pratikūlataya ābhimatasya sukṛtaṃ sukhaṃ ca nā adatte na apanudati / yato 'yaṃ vibhuḥ; na kvācitkaḥ, na deva-ādi-deha-ādy-asādhāraṇa-deśaḥ, ata eva na kasyacit saṃbandhī, na kasyacit pratikūlaś ca / sarvam idaṃ vāsanā-kṛtam / evaṃ-sva-bhāvasya katham iyaṃ viparīta-vāsanā utpadyate? ajñānenā avṛtaṃ jñānam jñāna-virodhinā pūrva-pūrva-karmaṇā sva-phala-anubhava-yogyatvāya asya jñānam āvṛtaṃ saṃkucitam / tena jñāna-āvaraṇa-rūpeṇa karmaṇā deva-ādi-deha-saṃyogas tat-tad-ātma-abhimāna-rūpa-mohaś ca jāyate / tataś ca tathā-vidha-ātma-abhimāna-vāsanā, tad-ucita-karma-vāsanā ca; vāsanāto viparīta-ātma-abhimānaḥ, karma-ārambhaś ca upapadyate //

body.text: "sarvaṃ jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṃ saṃtariṣyati", "jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā", "na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitram" iti pūrvoktaṃ svakāle saṃgamayati --
body.translated_text: The previously stated [verses] — 'By the raft of knowledge alone one will cross over all evil,' 'The fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes,' 'For there is nothing as purifying as knowledge' — [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] now connects them with the present context:

children.text: "sarvaṃ jñāna-plavena eva vṛjinaṃ saṃtariṣyati", "jñāna-agniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasmasāt-kurute tathā", "na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitram" iti pūrva-uktaṃ sva-kāle saṃgamayati ---
jñānena tu tad ajñānaṃ yeṣāṃ nāśitam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: But those whose ignorance regarding the self has been destroyed by knowledge — |

children.text: teṣām ādityavaj jñānaṃ prakāśayati tat param ||
children.translated_text: for them, knowledge, like the sun, illuminates that Supreme. ||

children.text: jñānena tu tad ajñānaṃ yeṣāṃ nāśitam ātmanaḥ |
teṣām ādityavaj jñānaṃ prakāśayati tat param ||

body.text:
evaṃ vartamāneṣu sarveṣv ātmasu yeṣām ātmanām uktalakṣaṇena ātmayāthātmyopadeśajanitena ātmaviṣayeṇa aharaharabhyāsādheyātiśayena niratiśayapavitreṇa jñānena tat -- jñānāvaraṇam anādikālapravṛttānantakarmasaṃcayarūpam ajñānaṃ nāśitam, teṣāṃ tat svābhāvikaṃ paraṃ jñānam aparimitam asaṃkucitam ādityavat sarvaṃ yathāvasthitaṃ prakāśayati / teṣām iti vinaṣṭājñānānāṃ bahutvābhimānād ātmasvarūpabahutvam, "na tv evāhaṃ jātu nāsam" ityupakramāvagatam atra spaṣṭataram uktam / na cedaṃ bahutvam upādhikṛtam; vinaṣṭājñānānām upādhigandhābhāvāt / "teṣām ādityavaj jñānam" iti vyatirekanirdeśāj jñānasya svarūpānubandhidharmatvam uktam / ādityadṛṣṭāntena ca jñātṛjñānayoḥ prabhāprabhāvator
ivāvasthānaṃ ca / tata eva saṃsāradaśāyāṃ jñānasya karmaṇā saṃkoco mokṣadaśāyāṃ vikāsaś copapannaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Among all selves existing in this manner, those selves whose ignorance — in the form of the accumulated mass of beginningless <s>karma</s> that covers knowledge — has been destroyed by knowledge regarding the self, generated by the instruction on the true nature of the self as described, directed toward the self, augmented by daily practice, and supremely purifying — for them, that natural, supreme knowledge — unlimited, uncontracted — illuminates everything as it truly is, like the sun. The plural 'for them' [<s>teṣām</s>] — indicating the multiplicity of those whose ignorance has been destroyed — clearly states here the multiplicity of the essential nature of the self, [already] understood from the opening 'But I have never not existed.' This multiplicity is not produced by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), since for those whose ignorance has been destroyed, there is not the slightest trace of limiting adjuncts. The expression 'for them, knowledge like the sun' — by the distinction indicated by 'for them' — states that knowledge is a property that follows the essential nature [of the self]. And by the analogy of the sun, the abiding of the knower and knowledge like the sun and its radiance
[is shown]. And from this, the contraction of knowledge in the state of transmigration through <s>karma</s>, and its expansion in the state of liberation, are both accounted for. //

children.text:
evaṃ vartamāneṣu sarveṣv ātmasu yeṣām ātmanām ukta-lakṣaṇena ātma-yāthātmya-upadeśa-janitena ātma-viṣayeṇa ahar-ahar-abhyāsa-ādheya-atiśayena niratiśaya-pavitreṇa jñānena tat --- jñāna-āvaraṇam anādi-kāla-pravṛtta-ananta-karma-saṃcaya-rūpam ajñānaṃ nāśitam, teṣāṃ tat svābhāvikaṃ paraṃ jñānam aparimitam asaṃkucitam ādityavat sarvaṃ yathā-avasthitaṃ prakāśayati / teṣām iti vinaṣṭa-ajñānānāṃ bahutva-abhimānād ātma-sva-rūpa-bahutvam, "na tv eva ahaṃ jātu nāsam" ity-upakrama-avagatam atra spaṣṭataram uktam / na ca idaṃ bahutvam upādhi-kṛtam; vinaṣṭa-ajñānānām upādhi-gandha-abhāvāt / "teṣām ādityavaj jñānam" iti vyatireka-nirdeśāj jñānasya sva-rūpa-anubandhi-dharmatvam uktam / āditya-dṛṣṭāntena ca jñātṛ-jñānayoḥ prabhā-prabhāvator
iva avasthānaṃ ca / tata eva saṃsāra-daśāyāṃ jñānasya karmaṇā saṃkoco mokṣa-daśāyāṃ vikāsaś ca upapannaḥ //
tadbuddhayas tadātmanas tanniṣṭhās tatparāyaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Their understanding fixed on that, their selves [centered] on that, established in that, devoted to that as the supreme goal — |

children.text: gacchanty apunarāvṛttiṃ jñānanirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they go to the state of non-return, their impurities cleansed by knowledge. ||

children.text: tad-buddhayas tad-ātmanas tan-niṣṭhās tat-parāyaṇāḥ |
gacchanty apunar-āvṛttiṃ jñāna-nirdhūta-kalmaṣāḥ ||

body.text: tadbuddhayaḥ tathāvidhātmadarśanādhyavasāyāḥ, tadātmānaḥ tadviṣayamanasaḥ, tanniṣṭhāḥ tadabhyāsaniratāḥ, tatparāyaṇāḥ tad eva paramaprayojanam iti manvānāḥ, evam abhyasyamānena jñānena nirdhūtaprācīnakalmaṣāḥ tathāvidham ātmanam apunarāvṛttiṃ gacchanti / yad avasthād ātmanaḥ punarāvṛttir na vidyate, sa ātmā apunarāvṛttiḥ / svena rūpeṇāvasthitam ātmānaṃ gacchantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Their understanding fixed on that' — their resolution [set] on the vision of such a self; 'their selves [centered] on that' — their minds directed toward that; 'established in that' — devoted to the practice of that; 'devoted to that as the supreme goal' — regarding that alone as the ultimate purpose. Their prior impurities having been cleansed by knowledge practiced in this manner, they go to the state of non-return — that state of the self from which there is no return. They reach the self established in its own form — this is the meaning. //

children.text: tad-buddhayaḥ tathā-vidha-ātma-darśana-adhyavasāyāḥ, tad-ātmānaḥ tad-viṣaya-manasaḥ, tan-niṣṭhāḥ tad-abhyāsa-niratāḥ, tat-parāyaṇāḥ tad eva parama-prayojanam iti manvānāḥ, evam abhyasyamānena jñānena nirdhūta-prācīna-kalmaṣāḥ tathā-vidham ātmanam apunar-āvṛttiṃ gacchanti / yad avasthād ātmanaḥ punar-āvṛttir na vidyate, sa ātmā apunar-āvṛttiḥ / svena rūpeṇa avasthitam ātmānaṃ gacchanti ity-arthaḥ //
vidyāvinayasaṃpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini |
children.translated_text: In a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> endowed with learning and humility, in a cow, in an elephant, |

children.text: śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in a dog, and in a dog-cooker — the wise see the same. ||

children.text: vidyā-vinaya-saṃpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini |
śuni ca eva śva-pāke ca paṇḍitāḥ sama-darśinaḥ ||

body.text: vidyāvinayasaṃpanne, kevalabrāhmaṇe, gohastiśvaśvapacādiṣu atyantaviṣamākāratayā pratīyamāneṣu ātmasu paṇḍitāḥ ātmayāthātmyavidaḥ, jñānaikākāratayā sarvatra samadarśinaḥ -- viṣamākāras tu prakṛteḥ, nātmanaḥ; ātmā tu sarvatra jñānaikākāratayā sama iti paśyantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: In [a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>] endowed with learning and humility, in an ordinary <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, in cows, elephants, dogs, dog-cookers (<s>śvapaca</s>), and the like — in selves perceived as being of utterly diverse forms — the wise (<s>paṇḍita</s>), those who know the true nature of the self, see the same everywhere through the uniform nature of knowledge. The diversity of form belongs to <s>Prakṛti</s>, not to the self; the self is everywhere the same through its uniform nature of knowledge — thus they see. This is the meaning. //

children.text: vidyā-vinaya-saṃpanne, kevala-brāhmaṇe, go-hasti-śva-śva-paca-ādiṣu atyanta-viṣama-ākāratayā pratīyamāneṣu ātmasu paṇḍitāḥ ātma-yāthātmya-vidaḥ, jñāna-eka-ākāratayā sarvatra sama-darśinaḥ --- viṣama-ākāras tu prakṛteḥ, nā atmanaḥ; ātmā tu sarvatra jñāna-eka-ākāratayā sama iti paśyanti ity-arthaḥ //
ihaiva tair jitas svargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even here, <s>saṃsāra</s> is conquered by those whose mind is established in equality. |

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For <s>Brahman</s> is flawless and equal — therefore they are established in <s>Brahman</s>. ||

children.text: iha eva tair jitas svargo yeṣāṃ sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ |
nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma tasmād brahmaṇi te sthitāḥ ||

body.text: ihaiva -- sādhanānuṣṭhānadaśāyām eva taiḥ sargo jitaḥ saṃsāro jitaḥ; yeṣām uktarītyā sarveṣv ātmasu sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ / nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma / prakṛtisaṃsargadoṣaviyuktatayā samam ātmavastu hi bramha / ātmasāmye sthitāś ced brahmaṇi sthitā eva te; brahmaṇi sthitir eva hi sṃsārajayaḥ / ātmasu jñānaikākāratayā sāmyam evānusandhānā muktā evetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Even here — in the very stage of practicing the means — <s>saṃsāra</s> is conquered by them, whose mind is established in the equality of all selves in the manner described. 'For <s>Brahman</s> is flawless and equal' — the self-substance, free from the defect of conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s>, is equal, and is <s>Brahman</s>. If established in the equality of selves, they are established in <s>Brahman</s> indeed; for establishment in <s>Brahman</s> is itself the conquest of <s>saṃsāra</s>. The meaning is: through the very contemplation of the equality of selves through their uniform nature of knowledge, they are liberated. //

children.text: iha eva --- sādhana-anuṣṭhāna-daśāyām eva taiḥ sargo jitaḥ saṃsāro jitaḥ; yeṣām ukta-rītyā sarveṣv ātmasu sāmye sthitaṃ manaḥ / nirdoṣaṃ hi samaṃ brahma / prakṛti-saṃsarga-doṣa-viyuktatayā samam ātma-vastu hi bramha / ātma-sāmye sthitāś ced brahmaṇi sthitā eva te; brahmaṇi sthitir eva hi sṃsāra-jayaḥ / ātmasu jñāna-eka-ākāratayā sāmyam eva anusandhānā muktā eva ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: yena prakāreṇāvathitasya karmayoginaḥ samadarśanarūpo jñanavipāko bhavati, taṃ prakāram upadiśati --
body.translated_text: He teaches the manner in which the <s>karmayogin</s>, thus established, attains the maturation of knowledge in the form of equal vision:

children.text: yena prakāreṇa avathitasya karma-yoginaḥ sama-darśana-rūpo jñana-vipāko bhavati, taṃ prakāram upadiśati ---
na prahṛṣyet priyaṃ prāpya nodvijet prāpya cāpriyam |
children.translated_text: Let one not rejoice upon obtaining what is pleasant, nor be agitated upon obtaining what is unpleasant. |

children.text: sthirabuddhir asaṃmūḍho brahmavid brahmaṇi sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Of steady intellect, undeluded, the knower of <s>Brahman</s> is established in <s>Brahman</s>. ||

children.text: na prahṛṣyet priyaṃ prāpya na udvijet prāpya ca apriyam |
sthira-buddhir asaṃmūḍho brahma-vid brahmaṇi sthitaḥ ||

body.text: yādṛśadehasthasya yadavasthasya prācīnakarmavāsanayā yat priyaṃ bhavati, yac cāpriyam, tadubhayaṃ prāpya harṣodvegau na kuryāt / katham? sthirabuddhiḥ -- sthire ātmani buddhir yasya saḥ sthirabuddhiḥ, asaṃmūḍho asthieṇa śarīreṇa sthiram ātmānam ekīkṛtya mohaḥ saṃmohaḥ; tadrahitaḥ / tac ca katham? brahmavid brahmaṇi sthitaḥ / upadeśena brahmavit san tasmin brahmaṇy abhyāsayuktaḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- tattvavidām upadeśena ātmayāthātmyavid bhūtvā tatraiva yatamāno dehātmābhimānaṃ parityajya sthirarūpātmāvalokanapriyānubhave vyavasthitaḥ asthire prākṛte priyāpriye prāpya harṣodevegau na kuryād iti //
body.translated_text: Whatever is pleasant and whatever is unpleasant — [determined by] the latent impressions of prior <s>karma</s> — for one abiding in whatever type of body and in whatever condition: upon obtaining both, one should not experience elation or agitation. How? 'Of steady intellect' — one whose understanding is fixed on the stable self; 'undeluded' — delusion (<s>saṃmoha</s>) is identifying the stable self with the unstable body; free from that. And how [is that possible]? 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s>, established in <s>Brahman</s>' — being a knower of <s>Brahman</s> through instruction, being engaged in practice regarding that <s>Brahman</s>. What has been said amounts to this: having become a knower of the true nature of the self through the instruction of those who know reality, striving toward that very [self], abandoning the conceit of identifying the self with the body, established in the joyful experience of beholding the self of stable form — upon obtaining the unstable, material pleasant and unpleasant, one should not experience elation or agitation. //

children.text: yādṛśa-deha-sthasya yad-avasthasya prācīna-karma-vāsanayā yat priyaṃ bhavati, yac ca apriyam, tad-ubhayaṃ prāpya harṣa-udvegau na kuryāt / katham? sthira-buddhiḥ --- sthire ātmani buddhir yasya saḥ sthira-buddhiḥ, asaṃmūḍho asthieṇa śarīreṇa sthiram ātmānam ekīkṛtya mohaḥ saṃmohaḥ; tad-rahitaḥ / tac ca katham? brahma-vid brahmaṇi sthitaḥ / upadeśena brahma-vit san tasmin brahmaṇy abhyāsa-yuktaḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- tattva-vidām upadeśena ātma-yāthātmya-vid bhūtvā tatra eva yatamāno deha-ātma-abhimānaṃ parityajya sthira-rūpa-ātma-avalokana-priya-anubhave vyavasthitaḥ asthire prākṛte priya-apriye prāpya harṣa-udevegau na kuryād iti //
bāhyasparśeṣv asaktātmā vindaty ātmani yaḥ sukham |
children.translated_text: One whose self is unattached to external contacts finds happiness in the self. |

children.text: sa brahmayogayuktātmā sukham akṣayam aśnute ||
children.translated_text: That one, whose self is united with <s>Brahman</s> in <s>yoga</s>, enjoys imperishable happiness. ||

children.text: bāhya-sparśeṣv asakta-ātmā vindaty ātmani yaḥ sukham |
sa brahma-yoga-yukta-ātmā sukham akṣayam aśnute ||

body.text: evamuktena prakāreṇa bāhyasparśeṣu ātmavyatiriktaviṣayānubhaveṣu, asaktātmā asaktamanāḥ antarātmany eva yaḥ sukhaṃ vindati labhate, sa prakṛtyabhyāsaṃ vihāya brahmayogayuktātmā -- brahmābhyāsayuktamanāḥ brahmānubhavarūpam akṣayaṃ sukhaṃ prāpnoti //
body.translated_text: In the manner described, one whose self — i.e., mind — is unattached to external contacts, i.e., to the experiences of objects other than the self, who finds, i.e., obtains, happiness in the inner self alone — that one, abandoning the practice of [attachment to] material nature, whose mind is united with the practice of <s>Brahman</s> — attains imperishable happiness in the form of the experience of <s>Brahman</s>. //

children.text: evam-uktena prakāreṇa bāhya-sparśeṣu ātma-vyatirikta-viṣaya-anubhaveṣu, asakta-ātmā asakta-manāḥ antar-ātmany eva yaḥ sukhaṃ vindati labhate, sa prakṛty-abhyāsaṃ vihāya brahma-yoga-yukta-ātmā --- brahma-abhyāsa-yukta-manāḥ brahma-anubhava-rūpam akṣayaṃ sukhaṃ prāpnoti //

body.text: prākṛtasya bhogasya sutyajatām āha --
body.translated_text: He states the ease of renouncing material enjoyment:

children.text: prākṛtasya bhogasya su-tyajatām āha ---
ye hi saṃsparśajā bhogā duḥkhayonaya eva te |
children.translated_text: Those pleasures that are born of contact are indeed sources of suffering. |

children.text: ādyantavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: They have a beginning and an end, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>; the wise one does not delight in them. ||

children.text: ye hi saṃsparśa-jā bhogā duḥkha-yonaya eva te |
ādy-antavantaḥ kaunteya na teṣu ramate budhaḥ ||

body.text: viṣayendriyasparśajāḥ ye bhogāḥ duḥkhayonayas te -- duḥkhodarkāḥ / ādyantavantaḥ alpakālavartino hi upalabhyante / na teṣu tadyāthātmyavid ramate //
body.translated_text: Those pleasures born from the contact of senses and objects are sources of suffering — they lead to suffering in their aftermath. They have a beginning and an end — they are observed to be of brief duration. The one who knows their true nature does not delight in them. //

children.text: viṣaya-indriya-sparśa-jāḥ ye bhogāḥ duḥkha-yonayas te --- duḥkha-udarkāḥ / ādy-antavantaḥ alpa-kāla-vartino hi upalabhyante / na teṣu tad-yāthātmya-vid ramate //
śaknotīhaiva yaḥ soḍhuṃ prāk śarīravimokṣaṇāt |
children.translated_text: One who is able, even here, before the release from the body, |

children.text: kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: to endure the impulse born of desire and anger — that one is disciplined, that one is happy. ||

children.text: śaknoti iha eva yaḥ soḍhuṃ prāk śarīra-vimokṣaṇāt |
kāma-krodha-udbhavaṃ vegaṃ sa yuktaḥ sa sukhī naraḥ ||

body.text: śarīravimokṣaṇāt prāk ih+eva sādhanānuṣṭhānadaśāyam eva ātmānubhavaprītyā kāmakrodhodbhavaṃ vegaṃ soḍhuṃ niroddhuṃ yaḥ śaknoti, sa yuktaḥ ātmānubhavāyārhaḥ / sa eva śarīravimokṣottarakālam ātmānubhavaikasukhas saṃpatsyate //
body.translated_text: Before the release from the body, even here — in the very stage of practicing the means — one who is able to endure, i.e., to restrain, the impulse born of desire and anger, through the joy of the experience of the self — that one is disciplined (<s>yukta</s>), worthy of the experience of the self. That very one, after the time of release from the body, will become one whose sole happiness is the experience of the self. //

children.text: śarīra-vimokṣaṇāt prāk ih+eva sādhana-anuṣṭhāna-daśāyam eva ātma-anubhava-prītyā kāma-krodha-udbhavaṃ vegaṃ soḍhuṃ niroddhuṃ yaḥ śaknoti, sa yuktaḥ ātma-anubhavāya arhaḥ / sa eva śarīra-vimokṣa-uttara-kālam ātma-anubhava-eka-sukhas saṃpatsyate //
yo 'ntassukho 'ntarārāmas tathāntarjyotir eva yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One whose happiness is within, whose delight is within, and also whose light is within — |

children.text: sa yogī brahma nirvāṇaṃ brahmabhūto 'dhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: that <s>yogin</s>, having become <s>Brahman</s>, attains the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>. ||

children.text: yo 'ntas-sukho 'ntar-ārāmas tatha āntar-jyotir eva yaḥ |
sa yogī brahma nirvāṇaṃ brahma-bhūto 'dhigacchati ||

body.text: yo bāhyaviṣayānubhavaṃ sarvaṃ vihāya antassukhaḥ ātmānubhavaikasukhaḥ, antarārāmaḥ ātmaikodyānaḥ svaguṇair ātmaiva sukhavardhako yasya sa tathoktaḥ, tathāntarjyotiḥ ātmaikajñāno yo vartate, sa brahmabhūto yogī brahmanirvāṇam ātmānubhavasukhaṃ prāpnoti //
body.translated_text: One who, abandoning all experience of external objects, has happiness within — whose sole happiness is the experience of the self; whose delight is within — whose sole garden is the self, i.e., one for whom the self alone, through its own qualities, is the increaser of happiness — is so called; likewise, whose light is within — whose sole knowledge is of the self — who lives thus — that <s>yogin</s>, having become <s>Brahman</s>, attains the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmanirvāṇa</s>) — the happiness of the experience of the self. //

children.text: yo bāhya-viṣaya-anubhavaṃ sarvaṃ vihāya antas-sukhaḥ ātma-anubhava-eka-sukhaḥ, antar-ārāmaḥ ātma-eka-udyānaḥ sva-guṇair ātma aiva sukha-vardhako yasya sa tathā-uktaḥ, tatha āntar-jyotiḥ ātma-eka-jñāno yo vartate, sa brahma-bhūto yogī brahma-nirvāṇam ātma-anubhava-sukhaṃ prāpnoti //
labhante brahmanirvāṇam ṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: The sages, whose impurities are destroyed, obtain the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> — |

children.text: chinnadvaidhā yatātmānas sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those whose doubts are cut asunder, whose selves are controlled, who delight in the welfare of all beings. ||

children.text: labhante brahma-nirvāṇam ṛṣayaḥ kṣīṇa-kalmaṣāḥ |
chinna-dvaidhā yata-ātmānas sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ ||

body.text: cchinnadvaidhāḥ śītoṣṇādidvandvair vimuktāḥ, yatātmānaḥ ātmany eva niyamitamanasaḥ, sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ ātmavat sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ hiteṣv eva niratāḥ, ṛṣayaḥ draṣṭāraḥ ātmāvalokanaparāḥ, ya evambhūtās te kṣīṇāśeṣātmaprāptivirodhikalmaṣāḥ brahmanirvāṇaṃ labhante //
body.translated_text: 'Whose doubts are cut asunder' — freed from the pairs of opposites such as cold and heat; 'whose selves are controlled' — whose minds are restrained upon the self alone; 'who delight in the welfare of all beings' — devoted to the welfare of all beings as [they would be] to their own self; 'sages' — seers, those devoted to the vision of the self — those who are of such a nature, whose every impurity that obstructs the attainment of the self is destroyed — they obtain the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>. //

children.text: cchinna-dvaidhāḥ śīta-uṣṇa-ādi-dvandvair vimuktāḥ, yata-ātmānaḥ ātmany eva niyamita-manasaḥ, sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ ātmavat sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ hiteṣv eva niratāḥ, ṛṣayaḥ draṣṭāraḥ ātma-avalokana-parāḥ, ya evam-bhūtās te kṣīṇa-aśeṣa-ātma-prāpti-virodhi-kalmaṣāḥ brahma-nirvāṇaṃ labhante //

body.text: uktalakṣaṇānāṃ brahma atyantasulabham ity āha --
body.translated_text: [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] says that for those of the described characteristics, <s>Brahman</s> is extremely easy to attain:

children.text: ukta-lakṣaṇānāṃ brahma atyanta-sulabham ity āha ---
kāmakrodhaviyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yatacetasām |
children.translated_text: For those who are free from desire and anger, who are ascetics of controlled minds, |

children.text: abhito brahmanirvāṇaṃ vartate vijitātmanām ||
children.translated_text: the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> exists on every side, for those who have conquered the self. ||

children.text: kāma-krodha-viyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yata-cetasām |
abhito brahma-nirvāṇaṃ vartate vijita-ātmanām ||

body.text: kāmakrodhviyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yatanaśīlānāṃ yatacetasāṃ niyamitamanasāṃ vijitātmanāṃ vijitamanasāṃ, brahmanirvāṇam abhito vartate / evaṃbhūtānāṃ hastasthaṃ brahmanirvāṇam ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: For those who are free from desire and anger, who are ascetics — of striving nature — of controlled minds, who have conquered the self, i.e., conquered the mind — the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> exists on every side. The meaning is: for those of such a nature, the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> is within hand's reach. //

children.text: kāma-krodh-viyuktānāṃ yatīnāṃ yatana-śīlānāṃ yata-cetasāṃ niyamita-manasāṃ vijita-ātmanāṃ vijita-manasāṃ, brahma-nirvāṇam abhito vartate / evaṃ-bhūtānāṃ hasta-sthaṃ brahma-nirvāṇam ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: uktaṃ karmayogaṃ svalakṣyabhūtayogaśiraskam upasaṃharati --
body.translated_text: [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] concludes the <s>karmayoga</s> that has been described, crowned by <s>yoga</s> as its goal:

children.text: uktaṃ karma-yogaṃ sva-lakṣya-bhūta-yoga-śiraskam upasaṃharati ---
sparśān kṛtvā bahir bāhyāṃś cakṣuś caivāntare bhruvoḥ |
children.translated_text: Shutting out external contacts, fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, |

children.text: prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā nāsābhyantaracāriṇau ||
children.translated_text: equalizing the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> breaths moving within the nostrils, ||

children.text: sparśān kṛtvā bahir bāhyāṃś cakṣuś ca eva antare bhruvoḥ |
prāṇa-apānau samau kṛtvā nāsa-abhyantara-cāriṇau ||
yatendriyamanobuddhir munir mokṣaparāyaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: the sage whose senses, mind, and intellect are controlled, devoted to liberation, |

children.text: vigatecchābhayakrodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: who is free from desire, fear, and anger — that one is forever liberated. ||

children.text: yata-indriya-mano-buddhir munir mokṣa-parāyaṇaḥ |
vigata-icchā-bhaya-krodho yaḥ sadā mukta eva saḥ ||

body.text: bāhyān viṣayasparśān bahiḥ kṛtvā bāhyendriyavyāpāraṃ sarvam upasaṃhṛtya, yogayogyāsane ṛjukāya upaviśya cakṣuṣī bhruvor antare nāsāgre vinyasya nāsābhyantaracāriṇau prāṇāpānau samau kṛtvā ucchvāsaniśvāsau samagatī kṛtvā ātmāvalokanād anyatra pravṛttyanarhendriyamanobuddhiḥ, tata eva vigatecchābhayakrodhaḥ, mokṣaparāyaṇaḥ mokṣaikaprayojanaḥ, muniḥ ātmāvalokanaśīlaḥ yaḥ, saḥ sadā mukta eva sādhyadaśāyām iva sādhanadaśāyām api mukta evetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Making the external sense-contacts outside — completely withdrawing all activity of the external senses — sitting in a posture suitable for <s>yoga</s> with an erect body, placing the eyes between the eyebrows, i.e., at the tip of the nose, making the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> that move within the nose equal — making the inhalation and exhalation of equal course — with senses, mind, and <s>buddhi</s> unfit to operate anywhere other than the vision of the self, and thereby free from desire, fear, and anger; devoted to liberation — having liberation as his sole aim; a <s>muni</s> — one whose disposition is the contemplation of the self — such a person is ever liberated; the meaning is: even in the stage of practice, he is liberated just as in the stage of attainment. //

children.text: bāhyān viṣaya-sparśān bahiḥ kṛtvā bāhya-indriya-vyāpāraṃ sarvam upasaṃhṛtya, yoga-yogya-āsane ṛju-kāya upaviśya cakṣuṣī bhruvor antare nāsa-agre vinyasya nāsa-abhyantara-cāriṇau prāṇa-apānau samau kṛtvā ucchvāsa-niśvāsau sama-gatī kṛtvā ātma-avalokanād anyatra pravṛtty-anarha-indriya-mano-buddhiḥ, tata eva vigata-icchā-bhaya-krodhaḥ, mokṣa-parāyaṇaḥ mokṣa-eka-prayojanaḥ, muniḥ ātma-avalokana-śīlaḥ yaḥ, saḥ sadā mukta eva sādhya-daśāyām iva sādhana-daśāyām api mukta eva ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: uktasya nityanaimittikakarmetikartavyatākasya karmayogasya yogaśiraskasya suśakatām āha --
body.translated_text: He states the easy performability of the <s>karmayoga</s> described — which has obligatory and occasional actions as its accessories and which has <s>yoga</s> (the vision of the self) as its culmination:

children.text: uktasya nitya-naimittika-karma-itikartavyatākasya karma-yogasya yoga-śiraskasya suśakatām āha ---
bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram |
children.translated_text: Knowing Me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all worlds,

children.text: suhṛdaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ jñātvā mām śāntim ṛcchati ||
children.translated_text: The friend of all beings — one attains peace. ||

children.text: bhoktāraṃ yajña-tapasāṃ sarva-loka-mahā-īśvaram |
suhṛdaṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ jñātvā mām śāntim ṛcchati ||

body.text: yajñatapasāṃ bhoktāraṃ sarvalokamaheśvaraṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ suhṛdaṃ māṃ jñātvā śāntim ṛcchati, karmayogakaraṇa eva sukham ṛcchati / sarvalokamaheśvaraṃ sarveṣāṃ lokeśvarāṇām apīśvaram; "tam īśvarāṇāṃ paramaṃ maheśvaram" iti hi śrūyate / māṃ sarvalokamaheśvaraṃ sarvasuhṛdaṃ jñātvā madārādhanarūpaḥ karmayoga iti sukhena tatra pravartata ityarthaḥ; suhṛda ārādhanāya hi sarve pravartante //
body.translated_text: Having known Me as the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, the great Lord of all worlds, the friend of all beings — one attains peace; one attains happiness in the very performance of <s>karmayoga</s>. 'The great Lord of all worlds' — the Lord even of all the rulers of the worlds; as the <s>śruti</s> declares: 'the supreme great Lord of lords.' Having known Me as the great Lord of all worlds and the friend of all, [the practitioner understands that] <s>karmayoga</s> is in the form of worship of Me — and thus engages in it with ease. This is the meaning; for all people devote themselves to the worship of a friend. //

children.text: yajña-tapasāṃ bhoktāraṃ sarva-loka-mahā-īśvaraṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ suhṛdaṃ māṃ jñātvā śāntim ṛcchati, karma-yoga-karaṇa eva sukham ṛcchati / sarva-loka-mahā-īśvaraṃ sarveṣāṃ loka-īśvarāṇām apī iśvaram; "tam īśvarāṇāṃ paramaṃ mahā-īśvaram" iti hi śrūyate / māṃ sarva-loka-mahā-īśvaraṃ sarva-suhṛdaṃ jñātvā mad-ārādhana-rūpaḥ karma-yoga iti sukhena tatra pravartata ity-arthaḥ; suhṛda ārādhanāya hi sarve pravartante //
anāśritaḥ karmaphalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who performs action that is duty, without depending on the fruit of action —

children.text: sa saṃnyasī ca yogī ca na niragnir na cākriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is the <s>saṃnyāsin</s> and the <s>yogin</s> — not one who is without fire and without ritual activities. ||

children.text: anāśritaḥ karma-phalaṃ kāryaṃ karma karoti yaḥ |
sa saṃnyasī ca yogī ca na niragnir na ca akriyaḥ ||

body.text: uktaḥ karmayogaḥ saparikaraḥ, idānīṃ jñānayogakarmayogasādhyātmāvalokanarūpayogābhyāsavidhir ucyate / tatra karmayogasya nirapekṣayogasādhanatvaṃ draḍhayituṃ jñānākāraḥ karmayogo yogaśirasko 'nūdyate / karmaphalaṃ svargādikam anāśritaḥ, kāryaṃ karmānuṣṭhānam eva kāryam, sarvātmanāsmatsuhṛdbhūtaparamapuruṣārādhanarūpatayā karmaiva mama prayojanam, na tatsādhyaṃ kiṃcid iti yaḥ karma karoti; sa saṃnyāsī ca jñānayoganiṣṭhaś ca; yogī ca karmayoganiṣṭhaś ca; ātmāvalokanarūpayogasādhanabhūtobhayaniṣṭha ityarthaḥ / na niragnir na cākriyaḥ na coditayajñādikarmasv apravṛttaḥ, na ca kevalajñānaniṣṭhaḥ / tasya hi jñananiṣṭhaiva, karmayoganiṣṭhasya tūbhayam astītyabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>karmayoga</s> has been stated with all its accessories. Now the rule for the practice of <s>yoga</s> — in the form of the vision of the self, to be attained through <s>jñānayoga</s> and <s>karmayoga</s> — is stated. There, in order to firmly establish that <s>karmayoga</s> is independently the means to <s>yoga</s>, <s>karmayoga</s> in its knowledge-form, with <s>yoga</s> as its culmination, is reiterated. One who, not depending on the fruit of action such as heaven and the like, performs action — [thinking] 'the performance of action alone is my duty' — [thinking] 'action alone, as worship of the Supreme Person who is the friend of all beings, is my purpose, and there is nothing to be attained through it' — he is the <s>saṃnyāsin</s> — one established in the practice of <s>jñānayoga</s>; and the <s>yogin</s> — one established in the practice of <s>karmayoga</s>; the meaning is: he is established in both, which are the means to <s>yoga</s> in the form of the vision of the self. Not 'one without fire' or 'one without ritual activities' — not one who does not engage in the enjoined sacrifices and the like; and not one established in mere <s>jñānayoga</s> alone. The purport is: the one established in <s>jñānayoga</s> alone has only <s>jñānayoga</s>, but the one established in <s>karmayoga</s> has both. //

children.text: uktaḥ karma-yogaḥ saparikaraḥ, idānīṃ jñāna-yoga-karma-yoga-sādhya-ātma-avalokana-rūpa-yoga-abhyāsa-vidhir ucyate / tatra karma-yogasya nirapekṣa-yoga-sādhanatvaṃ draḍhayituṃ jñāna-ākāraḥ karma-yogo yoga-śirasko 'nūdyate / karma-phalaṃ svarga-ādikam anāśritaḥ, kāryaṃ karma-anuṣṭhānam eva kāryam, sarva-ātmana āsmat-suhṛd-bhūta-parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-rūpatayā karma eva mama prayojanam, na tat-sādhyaṃ kiṃcid iti yaḥ karma karoti; sa saṃnyāsī ca jñāna-yoga-niṣṭhaś ca; yogī ca karma-yoga-niṣṭhaś ca; ātma-avalokana-rūpa-yoga-sādhana-bhūta-ubhaya-niṣṭha ity-arthaḥ / na niragnir na ca akriyaḥ na ca udita-yajña-ādi-karmasv apravṛttaḥ, na ca kevala-jñāna-niṣṭhaḥ / tasya hi jñana-niṣṭha eva, karma-yoga-niṣṭhasya tu ubhayam asti ity-abhiprāyaḥ //

body.text: uktalakṣaṇakarmayoge jñānam apy astīty āha --
body.translated_text: He says that knowledge too is present in <s>karmayoga</s> of the described characteristics:

children.text: ukta-lakṣaṇa-karma-yoge jñānam apy asti ity āha ---
yaṃ saṃnyāsa iti prāhur yogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava |
children.translated_text: What they call <s>saṃnyāsa</s>, know that to be <s>yoga</s>, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>;

children.text: na hy asaṃnyastasaṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana ||
children.translated_text: For no one ever becomes a <s>yogin</s> without having renounced <s>saṅkalpa</s> (desire-born resolve). ||

children.text: yaṃ saṃnyāsa iti prāhur yogaṃ taṃ viddhi pāṇḍava |
na hy asaṃnyasta-saṅkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana ||

body.text: yaṃ saṃnyāsa iti jñānayoga iti, ātmayāthātmyajñānam iti prāhuḥ, taṃ karmayogam eva viddhi / tad upapādayati na hy asaṃnyastasaṃkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana / ātmayāthātmyānusandhānena anātmani prakṛtau ātmasaṅkalpaḥ saṃnyastaḥ parityakto yena sa saṃnyastasaṅkalpaḥ; anevaṃbhūtaḥ asaṃnyastasaṅkalpaḥ / na hy ukteṣu karmayogiṣv anevaṃbhūtaḥ kaścana karmayogī bhavati; "yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ" iti hy uktam //
body.translated_text: What they call <s>saṃnyāsa</s>, i.e., <s>jñānayoga</s>, i.e., the knowledge of the true nature of the self — know that to be <s>karmayoga</s> itself. He substantiates this: for no one who has not renounced <s>saṅkalpa</s> ever becomes a <s>yogin</s>. One in whom the identification of the self with the non-self — with <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature) — has been renounced, abandoned, through the contemplation of the true nature of the self, is one who has renounced <s>saṅkalpa</s>; one who is not of this kind is one who has not renounced <s>saṅkalpa</s>. For among the described <s>karmayogins</s>, no one who is not of this kind is ever a <s>karmayogin</s>; for it has been stated: 'whose every undertaking is devoid of desire and [desire-born] resolve.' //

children.text: yaṃ saṃnyāsa iti jñāna-yoga iti, ātma-yāthātmya-jñānam iti prāhuḥ, taṃ karma-yogam eva viddhi / tad upapādayati na hy asaṃnyasta-saṃkalpo yogī bhavati kaścana / ātma-yāthātmya-anusandhānena anātmani prakṛtau ātma-saṅkalpaḥ saṃnyastaḥ parityakto yena sa saṃnyasta-saṅkalpaḥ; anevaṃ-bhūtaḥ asaṃnyasta-saṅkalpaḥ / na hy ukteṣu karma-yogiṣv anevaṃ-bhūtaḥ kaścana karma-yogī bhavati; "yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāma-saṅkalpa-varjitāḥ" iti hy uktam //

body.text: karmayoga evāpramādena yogaṃ sādhayatīty āha --
body.translated_text: <s>Karmayoga</s> alone, without deviation, brings about <s>yoga</s> — he says:

children.text: karma-yoga eva apramādena yogaṃ sādhayati ity āha ---
ārurukṣor muner yogaṃ karma kāraṇam ucyate |
children.translated_text: For a <s>muni</s> (sage) who wishes to ascend to <s>yoga</s>, action is said to be the means;

children.text: yogārūḍhasya tasyaiva śamaḥ kāraṇam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: For that very person who has ascended to <s>yoga</s>, quiescence is said to be the means. ||

children.text: ārurukṣor muner yogaṃ karma kāraṇam ucyate |
yoga-ārūḍhasya tasya eva śamaḥ kāraṇam ucyate ||

body.text: yogam ātmāvalokanaṃ prāptum icchor mumukṣoḥ karmayoga eva kāraṇam ucyate / tasyaiva yogārūḍhasya pratiṣṭhitayogasyaiva, śamaḥ karmanivṛttiḥ kāraṇam ucyate / yāvad ātmāvalokanarūpamokṣāvāpti karma kāryam ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: For one who desires liberation and who wishes to attain <s>yoga</s> — the vision of the self — <s>karmayoga</s> alone is said to be the means. For that very person who has ascended to <s>yoga</s> — who is established in <s>yoga</s> — quiescence (<s>śama</s>), the cessation of action, is said to be the means. The meaning is: action is to be performed until the attainment of liberation in the form of the vision of the self. //

children.text: yogam ātma-avalokanaṃ prāptum icchor mumukṣoḥ karma-yoga eva kāraṇam ucyate / tasya eva yoga-ārūḍhasya pratiṣṭhita-yogasya eva, śamaḥ karma-nivṛttiḥ kāraṇam ucyate / yāvad ātma-avalokana-rūpa-mokṣa-avāpti karma kāryam ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: kadā pratiṣṭhitayogo bhavatīty atrāha --
body.translated_text: When does one become established in <s>yoga</s>? — regarding this he says:

children.text: kadā pratiṣṭhita-yogo bhavati ity atrā aha ---
yadā hi nendriyārtheṣu na karmasv anuṣajjate |
children.translated_text: When one is attached neither to sense-objects nor to actions,

children.text: sarvasaṅkalpasaṃnyāsī yogārūḍhas tadocyate ||
children.translated_text: Having renounced all <s>saṅkalpa</s> — then one is said to have ascended to <s>yoga</s>. ||

children.text: yadā hi na indriya-artheṣu na karmasv anuṣajjate |
sarva-saṅkalpa-saṃnyāsī yoga-ārūḍhas tada ūcyate ||

body.text: yadāyaṃ yogī tv ātmaikānubhavasvabhāvatayā indriyārtheṣu -- ātmavyatiriktaprākṛtaviṣayeṣu, tatsaṃbandhiṣu ca karmasu nānuṣajjate na saṅgam arhati, tadā hi sarvasaṅkalpasamnyāsī yogārūḍha ity ucyate / tasmād ārurukṣor viṣayānubhavārhatayā tadananuṣaṅgābhyāsarūpaḥ karmayoga eva yoganiṣpattikāraṇam / ato viṣayānanuṣaṅgābhyāsarūpaṃ karmayogam eva ārurukṣuḥ kuryāt //
body.translated_text: When this <s>yogin</s>, due to having the essential nature of experiencing the self alone, is not attached — does not merit attachment — to sense-objects, i.e., to the objects of <s>Prakṛti</s> other than the self, or to the actions related to them — then he is said to have renounced all <s>saṅkalpa</s> and to have ascended to <s>yoga</s>. Therefore, for one who wishes to ascend, <s>karmayoga</s> alone — in the form of the practice of non-attachment to sense-objects, though being fit for sense-experience — is the means of the accomplishment of <s>yoga</s>. Therefore, one who wishes to ascend should perform <s>karmayoga</s> alone, in the form of the practice of non-attachment to sense-objects. //

children.text: yada āyaṃ yogī tv ātma-eka-anubhava-sva-bhāvatayā indriya-artheṣu --- ātma-vyatirikta-prākṛta-viṣayeṣu, tat-saṃbandhiṣu ca karmasu na anuṣajjate na saṅgam arhati, tadā hi sarva-saṅkalpa-samnyāsī yoga-ārūḍha ity ucyate / tasmād ārurukṣor viṣaya-anubhava-arhatayā tad-ananuṣaṅga-abhyāsa-rūpaḥ karma-yoga eva yoga-niṣpatti-kāraṇam / ato viṣaya-ananuṣaṅga-abhyāsa-rūpaṃ karma-yogam eva ārurukṣuḥ kuryāt //

body.text: tad evāha --
body.translated_text: He says this very thing:

children.text: tad evā aha ---
uddhared ātmanātmānaṃ nātmānam avasādayet |
children.translated_text: One should raise the self by the self; one should not let the self sink;

children.text: ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the self alone is the friend of the self; the self alone is the enemy of the self. ||

children.text: uddhared ātmanā ātmānaṃ nā atmānam avasādayet |
ātma aiva hy ātmano bandhur ātma aiva ripur ātmanaḥ ||

body.text: ātmanā manasā; viṣayānanuṣaktena ātmānam uddharet / tadviparītena manasā ātmānaṃ nāvasādayet / ātmaiva mana eva hy ātmano bandhuḥ; tad evātmano ripuḥ //
body.translated_text: 'By the self' means: by the mind. One should raise the self by a mind that is not attached to sense-objects. One should not let the self sink by a mind that is of the opposite kind. The self alone — the mind alone — is the friend of the self; that very [mind] is the enemy of the self. //

children.text: ātmanā manasā; viṣaya-ananuṣaktena ātmānam uddharet / tad-viparītena manasā ātmānaṃ na avasādayet / ātma aiva mana eva hy ātmano bandhuḥ; tad evā atmano ripuḥ //
bandhur ātmātmanas tasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The self is the friend of the self for him by whom the self has been conquered by the self;

children.text: anātmanas tu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatruvat ||
children.translated_text: But for one who has not conquered the self, the very self, like an enemy, would persist in enmity. ||

children.text: bandhur ātmā ātmanas tasya yenā atma aivā atmanā jitaḥ |
anātmanas tu śatrutve vartetā atma aiva śatruvat ||

body.text: yena puruṣeṇa svenaiva svamano viṣayebhyo jitam, tanmanas tasya bandhuḥ / anātmanaḥ ajitamanasaḥ svakīyam eva manaḥ svasya śatruvac śatrutve varteta -- svaniśśreyasaviparīte vartetetyarthaḥ / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā parāśareṇāpi, "mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandhamokṣayoḥ / bandhāya viṣayāsaṅgi muktyaiva nirviṣayaṃ manaḥ //  iti //
body.translated_text: For the person who has conquered his own mind from sense-objects by himself, that mind is his friend. For one whose self is unconquered — whose mind is not conquered — his own mind would persist in enmity like an enemy — the meaning is: it would operate in what is contrary to his own highest good. As the blessed <s>Parāśara</s> too has stated: 'The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings. The mind attached to sense-objects [leads to] bondage; [the mind] free from sense-objects alone [leads to] liberation.' //

children.text: yena puruṣeṇa svena eva sva-mano viṣayebhyo jitam, tan-manas tasya bandhuḥ / anātmanaḥ ajita-manasaḥ svakīyam eva manaḥ svasya śatruvac śatrutve varteta --- sva-niśśreyasa-viparīte varteta ity-arthaḥ / yatha ūktaṃ bhagavatā parāśareṇa api, "mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandha-mokṣayoḥ / bandhāya viṣaya-asaṅgi muktya aiva nirviṣayaṃ manaḥ //  iti //

body.text: yogārambhayogyā avasthocyate --
body.translated_text: The state suitable for the commencement of <s>yoga</s> is stated:

children.text: yoga-ārambha-yogyā avastha ūcyate ---
jitātmanaḥ praśāntasya paramātmā samāhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: For one who has conquered the self and who is tranquil, the Supreme Self is settled;

children.text: śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu tathā mānāvamānayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: In cold and heat, happiness and sorrow, as also in honor and dishonor. ||

children.text: jita-ātmanaḥ praśāntasya parama-ātmā samāhitaḥ |
śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu tathā māna-avamānayoḥ ||

body.text: śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu mānāvamānayoś ca jitātmanaḥ jitamanasaḥ vikārarahitamanasaḥ praśāntasya manasi paramātmā samāhitaḥ samyagāhitaḥ / svarūpeṇāvasthitaḥ pratyagātmātra paramātmety ucyate; tasyaiva prakṛtatvāt / tasyāpi pūrvapūrvāvasthāpekṣayā paramātmatvāt / ātmā paraṃ samāhita iti vānvayaḥ //
body.translated_text: For one who has conquered the self — conquered the mind — in cold and heat, happiness and sorrow, honor and dishonor — one whose mind is free from agitation, who is tranquil — in his mind, the Supreme Self is settled, i.e., well-established, i.e., abiding in its own essential form. Here the inner self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) is called the Supreme Self (<s>paramātmā</s>); because that [self] is what is under discussion. And because it too is the Supreme Self relative to the earlier and earlier stages. Or the construction may be: the self is supremely settled. //

children.text: śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu māna-avamānayoś ca jita-ātmanaḥ jita-manasaḥ vikāra-rahita-manasaḥ praśāntasya manasi parama-ātmā samāhitaḥ samyag-āhitaḥ / sva-rūpeṇa avasthitaḥ pratyag-ātma ātra parama-ātma īty ucyate; tasya eva prakṛtatvāt / tasya api pūrva-pūrva-avasthā-apekṣayā parama-ātmatvāt / ātmā paraṃ samāhita iti va ānvayaḥ //
jñānavijñānatṛptātmā kūṭastho vijitendriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: One whose self is satisfied with knowledge and discernment, who is immovable, who has conquered the senses —

children.text: yukta ity ucyate yogī samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>yogin</s> is called 'disciplined' — one for whom a clod, a stone, and gold are equal. ||

children.text: jñāna-vijñāna-tṛpta-ātmā kūṭa-stho vijita-indriyaḥ |
yukta ity ucyate yogī sama-loṣṭa-aśma-kāñcanaḥ ||

body.text: jñānavijñānatṛptātmā ātmasvarūpaviṣayeṇa jñānena, tasya ca prakṛtivisajātīyākāraviṣayeṇa jñānena ca tṛptamanāḥ kūṭasthaḥ devādyavasthāsv anuvartamānasarvasādhāraṇajñānaikākārātmani sthitaḥ, tata eva vijitendriyaḥ, samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ prakṛtiviviktasvarūpaniṣṭhatayā prākṛtavastuviśeṣeṣu bhogyatvābhāvāl loṣṭāśmakāñcaneṣu samaprayojanaḥ yaḥ karmayogī, sa yukta ity ucyate ātmāvalokanarūpayogābhyāsārha ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: 'One whose self is satisfied with knowledge and discernment' — one whose mind is satisfied with knowledge directed toward the essential nature of the self, and with knowledge directed toward its nature as dissimilar from <s>Prakṛti</s>. 'Immovable (<s>kūṭastha</s>)' — established in the self, which has the nature of a single form of common knowledge persisting through the states of gods and the like. Thereby 'one who has conquered the senses.' 'For whom a clod, a stone, and gold are equal' — one who, due to being established in his own essential nature as distinct from <s>Prakṛti</s>, has no desire for enjoyment in particular objects of <s>Prakṛti</s>, and therefore regards clods, stones, and gold as serving equal purpose. The <s>karmayogin</s> who is such is called 'disciplined' — i.e., is said to be fit for the practice of <s>yoga</s> in the form of the vision of the self. //

children.text: jñāna-vijñāna-tṛpta-ātmā ātma-sva-rūpa-viṣayeṇa jñānena, tasya ca prakṛti-visajātīya-ākāra-viṣayeṇa jñānena ca tṛpta-manāḥ kūṭa-sthaḥ deva-ādy-avasthāsv anuvartamāna-sarva-sādhāraṇa-jñāna-eka-ākāra-ātmani sthitaḥ, tata eva vijita-indriyaḥ, sama-loṣṭa-aśma-kāñcanaḥ prakṛti-vivikta-sva-rūpa-niṣṭhatayā prākṛta-vastu-viśeṣeṣu bhogyatva-abhāvāl loṣṭa-aśma-kāñcaneṣu sama-prayojanaḥ yaḥ karma-yogī, sa yukta ity ucyate ātma-avalokana-rūpa-yoga-abhyāsa-arha ity ucyate //

body.text: tathā ca
body.translated_text: And also:

children.text: tathā ca
suhṛnmitrāryudāsīnamadhyasthadveṣyabandhuṣu |
children.translated_text: Among well-wishers, friends, enemies, neutrals, mediators, the hateful, and kinsmen,

children.text: sādhuṣv api ca pāpeṣu samabuddhir viśiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Among the righteous and even among the sinful — one who has equal discernment excels. ||

children.text: suhṛn-mitra-ary-udāsīna-madhya-stha-dveṣya-bandhuṣu |
sādhuṣv api ca pāpeṣu sama-buddhir viśiṣyate ||

body.text:
vayoviśeṣānaṅgīkāreṇa svahitaiṣiṇaḥ suhṛdaḥ; savayaso hitaiṣiṇo mitrāṇi, arayo nimittato 'narthecchavaḥ; ubhayahetvabhāvād ubhayarahitā udāsīnāḥ; janmata evobhayarahitā madhyasthāḥ; janmata evānicchecchavo dveṣyāḥ; janmata eva hitaiṣiṇo bandhavaḥ, sādhavo dharmaśīlāḥ; pāpāḥ pāpaśīlāḥ; ātmaikaprayojanatayā suhṛnmitrādibhiḥ prayojanābhāvād virodhābhāvāc ca teṣu
samabuddhir yogābhyāsārhatve viśiṣyate //
body.translated_text: 'Well-wishers (<s>suhṛd</s>)' — those who desire one's welfare without regard to differences of age. 'Friends (<s>mitra</s>)' — those of equal age who desire one's welfare. 'Enemies (<s>ari</s>)' — those who, from some cause, desire one's misfortune. 'Neutrals (<s>udāsīna</s>)' — those who are free from both [friendliness and enmity] due to the absence of both causes. 'Mediators (<s>madhyastha</s>)' — those free from both by birth. 'The hateful (<s>dveṣya</s>)' — those who are ill-disposed by birth. 'Kinsmen (<s>bandhava</s>)' — those who are well-disposed by birth. 'The righteous' — those devoted to <s>dharma</s>. 'The sinful' — those devoted to sin. Because the self alone is his purpose, since there is no purpose to be served by well-wishers, friends, and the like, and no opposition [from enemies] — one who has equal discernment toward them excels in fitness for the practice of <s>yoga</s>. //

children.text:
vayo-viśeṣa-anaṅgīkāreṇa sva-hita-eṣiṇaḥ suhṛdaḥ; savayaso hita-eṣiṇo mitrāṇi, arayo nimittato 'nartha-icchavaḥ; ubhaya-hetv-abhāvād ubhaya-rahitā udāsīnāḥ; janmata eva ubhaya-rahitā madhya-sthāḥ; janmata eva anicchā-icchavo dveṣyāḥ; janmata eva hita-eṣiṇo bandhavaḥ, sādhavo dharma-śīlāḥ; pāpāḥ pāpa-śīlāḥ; ātma-eka-prayojanatayā suhṛn-mitra-ādibhiḥ prayojana-abhāvād virodha-abhāvāc ca teṣu
sama-buddhir yoga-abhyāsa-arhatve viśiṣyate //
yogī yuñjīta satatam ātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s> should constantly concentrate the mind, dwelling in a secluded place,

children.text: ekākī yatacittātmā nirāśīr aparigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Alone, with mind and body controlled, free from expectations, without possessiveness. ||

children.text: yogī yuñjīta satatam ātmānaṃ rahasi sthitaḥ |
ekākī yata-citta-ātmā nirāśīr aparigrahaḥ ||

body.text: yogī uktaprakārakarmayoganiṣṭhaḥ, satatam aharaharyogakāle ātmānaṃ yuñjīta ātmānaṃ yuktaṃ kurvīta / svadarśananiṣṭhaṃ kurvītetyarthaḥ; rahasi janavarjite niśśabde deśe sthitaḥ, ekākī tatrāpi na sadvitīyaḥ, yatacittātmā yatacittamanaskaḥ, nirāśīḥ ātmavyatirikte kṛtsne vastuni nirapekṣaḥ aparigrahaḥ tadvyatirikte kasmiṃścid api mamatārahitaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s> — one established in <s>karmayoga</s> of the described kind — should constantly, every day at the time of <s>yoga</s>, concentrate the mind — make the mind disciplined, i.e., establish it in the contemplation of the self. Dwelling in a secluded place — a place devoid of people and noise. Alone — even there, without a companion. With mind and body controlled — with mind and consciousness subdued. Free from expectations — without any dependence on anything whatsoever other than the self. Without possessiveness — devoid of the sense of 'mine' regarding anything whatsoever other than [the self]. //

children.text: yogī ukta-prakāra-karma-yoga-niṣṭhaḥ, satatam ahar-ahar-yoga-kāle ātmānaṃ yuñjīta ātmānaṃ yuktaṃ kurvīta / sva-darśana-niṣṭhaṃ kurvīta ity-arthaḥ; rahasi jana-varjite niśśabde deśe sthitaḥ, ekākī tatra api na sadvitīyaḥ, yata-citta-ātmā yata-citta-manaskaḥ, nirāśīḥ ātma-vyatirikte kṛtsne vastuni nirapekṣaḥ aparigrahaḥ tad-vyatirikte kasmiṃścid api mamatā-rahitaḥ //
śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiram āsanam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having established a firm seat for oneself in a clean place,

children.text: nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ celājinakuśottaram ||
