children.translated_text: Neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, skin, and <s>kuśa</s> grass; ||

children.text: śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiram āsanam ātmanaḥ |
na atyucchritaṃ na atinīcaṃ cela-ajina-kuśa-uttaram ||
tatraikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: There, having made the mind one-pointed, with the activities of the mind and senses restrained,

children.text: upaviśyāsane yuñjyād yogam ātmaviśuddhaye ||
children.translated_text: Seated on the seat, one should practice <s>yoga</s> for the purification of the self. ||

children.text: tatra eka-agraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yata-citta-indriya-kriyaḥ |
upaviśyā asane yuñjyād yogam ātma-viśuddhaye ||

body.text: śucau deśe aśucibhiḥ puruṣair anadhiṣṭhite aparigṛhīte ca aśucibhir vastubhir aspṛṣṭe ca pavitrabhūte deśe, dārvādinirmitaṃ nātyucchritaṃ nātinīcaṃ celājinakuśottaraṃ āsanaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tasmin manaḥprasādakare sāpāśraye upaviśya yogaikāgraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yatacittendriyakriyaḥ sarvātmanopasaṃhṛtacittendriyakriyaḥ ātmaviśuddhaye bandhanivṛttaye yogaṃ yuñjyād atmāvalokanaṃ kurvīta //
body.translated_text: In a clean place — a place not occupied by impure persons, not claimed [by others], not touched by impure things, and which is sacred — having established a seat made of wood and the like, neither too high nor too low, covered with cloth, skin, and <s>kuśa</s> grass on top, and having sat down on that seat — which is pleasing to the mind and has support — having made the mind one-pointed on <s>yoga</s>, with the activities of the mind and senses restrained — having completely withdrawn all activities of the mind and senses — for the purification of the self, i.e., for the removal of bondage, one should practice <s>yoga</s> — one should perform the contemplation of the self. //

children.text: śucau deśe aśucibhiḥ puruṣair anadhiṣṭhite aparigṛhīte ca aśucibhir vastubhir aspṛṣṭe ca pavitra-bhūte deśe, dārva-ādi-nirmitaṃ na atyucchritaṃ na atinīcaṃ cela-ajina-kuśa-uttaraṃ āsanaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tasmin manaḥ-prasāda-kare sa-apāśraye upaviśya yoga-eka-agraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā yata-citta-indriya-kriyaḥ sarva-ātmana ūpasaṃhṛta-citta-indriya-kriyaḥ ātma-viśuddhaye bandha-nivṛttaye yogaṃ yuñjyād atma-avalokanaṃ kurvīta //
samaṃ kāyaśirogrīvaṃ dhārayan acalaṃ sthiram |
children.translated_text: Holding the body, head, and neck evenly, motionlessly, and firmly,

children.text: saṃprekṣya nāsikāgraṃ svaṃ deśaś cānavalokayan ||
children.translated_text: Looking at the tip of one's own nose and not looking at the directions; ||

children.text: samaṃ kāya-śiro-grīvaṃ dhārayan acalaṃ sthiram |
saṃprekṣya nāsika-agraṃ svaṃ deśaś ca anavalokayan ||
praśāntātmā vigatabhīḥ brahmacārivrate sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: With a tranquil self, free from fear, established in the vow of celibacy,

children.text: manaḥ saṃyamya maccitto yukta āsīta matparaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having restrained the mind, with the mind fixed on Me — one should sit, disciplined, intent on Me. ||

children.text: praśānta-ātmā vigata-bhīḥ brahma-cāri-vrate sthitaḥ |
manaḥ saṃyamya mac-citto yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ ||

body.text: kāyaśirogrīvaṃ samam acalaṃ sāpāśrayatayā sthiraṃ dhārayan, diśaś cānavaloakayan, svanāsikāgraṃ saṃprekṣya, praśāntātmā atyantanirvṛtamanāḥ, vigatabhīr brahmacaryayukto manaḥ saṃyamya maccitto yuktaḥ avahito matpara āsīta mām eva cintyan āsīta //
body.translated_text: Holding the body, head, and neck evenly, motionlessly, and firmly due to the support, not looking at the directions, looking at the tip of one's own nose, with a tranquil self — with an exceedingly serene mind — free from fear, endowed with celibacy, having restrained the mind, with the mind fixed on Me, disciplined, attentive — one should sit intent on Me, contemplating Me alone. //

children.text: kāya-śiro-grīvaṃ samam acalaṃ sa-apāśrayatayā sthiraṃ dhārayan, diśaś ca anavaloakayan, sva-nāsika-agraṃ saṃprekṣya, praśānta-ātmā atyanta-nirvṛta-manāḥ, vigata-bhīr brahma-carya-yukto manaḥ saṃyamya mac-citto yuktaḥ avahito mat-para āsīta mām eva cintyan āsīta //
yuñjann evaṃ sadātmānaṃ yogī niyatamānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus constantly concentrating the mind, the <s>yogin</s> of controlled mind

children.text: śāntiṃ nirvāṇaparamāṃ matsaṃsthām adhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: Attains peace — the supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s> that abides in Me. ||

children.text: yuñjann evaṃ sadā ātmānaṃ yogī niyata-mānasaḥ |
śāntiṃ nirvāṇa-paramāṃ mat-saṃsthām adhigacchati ||

body.text: evaṃ mayi parasmin brahmaṇi puruṣottame manasaś śubhāśraye sadā ātmānaṃ manaḥ yuñjan niyatamānasaḥ matsparśavitrīkṛtamānasatayā niścalamānasaḥ, mām eva cintayan matsaṃsthāṃ nirvāṇaparamāṃ śāntim adhigacchati nirvāṇakāṣṭhārūpāṃ matsaṃsthāṃ mayi saṃsthitāṃ śāntim adhigacchati //
body.translated_text: Thus constantly concentrating the mind on Me — the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), the auspicious refuge for the mind — the <s>yogin</s> of controlled mind, whose mind has been purified by the touch of Me, with unwavering mind, contemplating Me alone, attains the peace that is the supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s> and that abides in Me — he attains the peace that abides in Me and has the form of the ultimate stage of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. //

children.text: evaṃ mayi parasmin brahmaṇi puruṣa-uttame manasaś śubha-āśraye sadā ātmānaṃ manaḥ yuñjan niyata-mānasaḥ mat-sparśa-vitrīkṛta-mānasatayā niścala-mānasaḥ, mām eva cintayan mat-saṃsthāṃ nirvāṇa-paramāṃ śāntim adhigacchati nirvāṇa-kāṣṭhā-rūpāṃ mat-saṃsthāṃ mayi saṃsthitāṃ śāntim adhigacchati //

body.text: evam ātmayogam ārabhamāṇasya manonairmalyahetubhūtāṃ manaso bhagavati śubhāśraye sthitim abhidhāya anyad api yogopakaraṇam āha --
body.translated_text: Thus, having stated that the mind's abiding in the Lord — the auspicious refuge — is the cause of the purity of mind for one who is commencing the <s>yoga</s> of the self, he states yet another accessory of <s>yoga</s>:

children.text: evam ātma-yogam ārabhamāṇasya mano-nairmalya-hetu-bhūtāṃ manaso bhagavati śubha-āśraye sthitim abhidhāya anyad api yoga-upakaraṇam āha ---
nātyaśnatas tu yogo 'sti na caikāntam anaśnataḥ |
children.translated_text: For one who eats too much, <s>yoga</s> is not [possible]; nor for one who does not eat at all;

children.text: na cātisvapnaśīlasya jāgrato naiva cārjuna ||
children.translated_text: Nor for one who is given to excessive sleep, nor indeed for one who is always awake, O <s>Arjuna</s>. ||

children.text: na atyaśnatas tu yogo 'sti na ca ekāntam anaśnataḥ |
na ca atisvapna-śīlasya jāgrato na eva ca arjuna ||
yuktāhāravihārasya yuktaceṣṭasya karmasu |
children.translated_text: For one whose food and recreation are regulated, whose effort in actions is regulated,

children.text: yuktasvapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkhahā ||
children.translated_text: Whose sleep and waking are regulated — <s>yoga</s> becomes the destroyer of sorrow. ||

children.text: yukta-āhāra-vihārasya yukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu |
yukta-svapna-avabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkha-hā ||

body.text: atyaśanānaśane yogavirodhinī; ativihārāvihārau ca tathātimātrasvapnajāgarye; tathā cātyāyāsānāyāsau / mitāhāravihārasya mitāyāsasya mitasvapnāvabodhasya sakaladuḥkhahā bandhanāśanaḥ yogaḥ saṃpanno bhavati //
body.translated_text: Overeating and not eating are obstacles to <s>yoga</s>; likewise excessive recreation and no recreation; likewise excessive sleep and wakefulness; and likewise excessive exertion and no exertion. For one whose food and recreation are moderate, whose effort is moderate, and whose sleep and waking are moderate — <s>yoga</s>, which destroys all sorrow and removes bondage, becomes fully accomplished. //

children.text: atyaśana-anaśane yoga-virodhinī; ativihāra-avihārau ca tatha ātimātra-svapna-jāgarye; tathā ca atyāyāsa-anāyāsau / mita-āhāra-vihārasya mita-āyāsasya mita-svapna-avabodhasya sakala-duḥkha-hā bandha-nāśanaḥ yogaḥ saṃpanno bhavati //
yadā viniyataṃ cittam ātmany evāvatiṣṭhate |
children.translated_text: When the thoroughly restrained mind abides in the self alone,

children.text: nisspṛhaḥ sarvakāmebhyo yukta ity ucyate tadā ||
children.translated_text: Free from longing for all desires — then one is called 'disciplined.' ||

children.text: yadā viniyataṃ cittam ātmany eva avatiṣṭhate |
nisspṛhaḥ sarva-kāmebhyo yukta ity ucyate tadā ||

body.text: yadā prayojanaviṣayaṃ cittam ātmany eva viniyatam -- viśeṣeṇa niyataṃ niratiśayaprayojanatayā tatraiva niyataṃ niścalam avatiṣṭhate, tadā sarvakāmebhyo nisspṛhas san yukta ity ucyate -- yogārha ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: When the mind — whose object is its purpose — is thoroughly restrained, i.e., especially restrained, in the self alone, and abides there motionlessly because of the unsurpassed purposefulness [of the self], then being free from longing for all desires, one is called 'disciplined' — i.e., fit for <s>yoga</s>. //

children.text: yadā prayojana-viṣayaṃ cittam ātmany eva viniyatam --- viśeṣeṇa niyataṃ niratiśaya-prayojanatayā tatra eva niyataṃ niścalam avatiṣṭhate, tadā sarva-kāmebhyo nisspṛhas san yukta ity ucyate --- yoga-arha ity ucyate //
yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā |
children.translated_text: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker — this simile is recalled ||

children.text: yogino yatacittasya yuñjato yogam ātmanaḥ ||
yathā dīpo nivāta-stho na iṅgate sa ūpamā smṛtā |
yogino yata-cittasya yuñjato yogam ātmanaḥ ||

body.text: nivātastho dīpo yathā neṅgate na calati; acalas saprabhas tiṣṭhati; yatacittasya nivṛttasakaletaramanovṛtteḥ yoginaḥ ātmani yogaṃ yuñjataḥ ātmasvarūpasya sopamā; nivātasthatayā niścalasaprabhadīpavan nivṛttasakalamanovṛttitayā niścalo jñānaprabha ātmā tiṣṭhaītyarthaḥ //

children.text: nivāta-stho dīpo yathā na iṅgate na calati; acalas sa-prabhas tiṣṭhati; yata-cittasya nivṛtta-sakala-itara-mano-vṛtteḥ yoginaḥ ātmani yogaṃ yuñjataḥ ātma-sva-rūpasya sa-upamā; nivāta-sthatayā niścala-sa-prabha-dīpavan nivṛtta-sakala-mano-vṛttitayā niścalo jñāna-prabha ātmā tiṣṭhai ity-arthaḥ //

body.text:
yatroparamate cittaṃ niruddhaṃ yogasevayā /
yatra caivātmanātmānaṃ paśyan ātmani tuṣyati /20//

children.text:
yatra uparamate cittaṃ niruddhaṃ yoga-sevayā /
yatra ca evā atmanā ātmānaṃ paśyan ātmani tuṣyati /20//
sukham ātyantikaṃ yat tad buddhigrāhyam atīndriyam |
vetti yatra na caivāyaṃ sthitaś calati tattvataḥ ||
sukham ātyantikaṃ yat tad buddhi-grāhyam atīndriyam |
vetti yatra na ca eva ayaṃ sthitaś calati tattvataḥ ||
yaṃ labdhvā cāparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate nādhikaṃ tataḥ |
yasmin sthito na duḥkhena guruṇāpi vicālyate ||
yaṃ labdhvā ca aparaṃ lābhaṃ manyate na adhikaṃ tataḥ |
yasmin sthito na duḥkhena guruṇa āpi vicālyate ||
taṃ vidyād duḥkhasaṃyogaviyogaṃ yogasaṃjñitam |
sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo 'nirviṇṇacetasā ||
taṃ vidyād duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyogaṃ yoga-saṃjñitam |
sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo 'nirviṇṇa-cetasā ||

body.text: yogasevayā hetunā sarvatra niruddhaṃ cittaṃ yatra yoge uparamate atiśayitasukham idam iti ramate, yatra ca yoge ātmanā manasā ātmānaṃ paśyan anyanirapekṣam ātmany eva tuṣyati, yat tad atīndriyam ātmabuddhyekagrāhyam ātyantikaṃ sukhaṃ yatra ca yoge vetti anubhavati, yatra ca yoge sthitaḥ sukhātirekeṇa tattvataḥ tadbhāvān na calati, yaṃ yogaṃ labdhvā yogād viratas tam eva kāṅkṣamāṇo nāparaṃ lābhaṃ tato 'dhikaṃ manyate, yasmiṃś ca yoge sthito virato 'pi guṇavat putraviyogādinā guruṇāpi duḥkhena na vicālyate, taṃ duḥkhasaṃyogaviyogaṃ duḥkhasaṃyogapratyanīkākāraṃ yogaśabdābhidheyaṃ vidyāt / sa evaṃrūpo yoga iti ārambhadaśāyāṃ niścayena anirviṇṇacetasā hṛṣṭacetasā yogo yoktavyaḥ //

children.text: yoga-sevayā hetunā sarvatra niruddhaṃ cittaṃ yatra yoge uparamate atiśayita-sukham idam iti ramate, yatra ca yoge ātmanā manasā ātmānaṃ paśyan anya-nirapekṣam ātmany eva tuṣyati, yat tad atīndriyam ātma-buddhy-eka-grāhyam ātyantikaṃ sukhaṃ yatra ca yoge vetti anubhavati, yatra ca yoge sthitaḥ sukha-atirekeṇa tattvataḥ tad-bhāvān na calati, yaṃ yogaṃ labdhvā yogād viratas tam eva kāṅkṣamāṇo na aparaṃ lābhaṃ tato 'dhikaṃ manyate, yasmiṃś ca yoge sthito virato 'pi guṇavat putra-viyoga-ādinā guruṇa āpi duḥkhena na vicālyate, taṃ duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyogaṃ duḥkha-saṃyoga-pratyanīka-ākāraṃ yoga-śabda-abhidheyaṃ vidyāt / sa evaṃ-rūpo yoga iti ārambha-daśāyāṃ niścayena anirviṇṇa-cetasā hṛṣṭa-cetasā yogo yoktavyaḥ //
saṅkalpaprabhavān kāmāṃs tyaktvā sarvān aśeṣataḥ |
manasaivendriyagrāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ ||
saṅkalpa-prabhavān kāmāṃs tyaktvā sarvān aśeṣataḥ |
manasa aiva indriya-grāmaṃ viniyamya samantataḥ ||
śanaiś śanair uparamed buddhyā dhṛtigṛhītayā |
ātmasaṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiṃcid api cintayet ||
śanaiś śanair uparamed buddhyā dhṛti-gṛhītayā |
ātma-saṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiṃcid api cintayet ||

body.text: sparśajāḥ saṅkalpajāś ceti dvividhāḥ kāmāḥ, sparśajāḥ śītoṣṇādayaḥ, saṅkalpajāḥ putrakṣetrādayaḥ / tatra saṅkalpaprabhavāḥ svarūpeṇaiva tyaktuṃ śakyāḥ / tān sarvān manasaiva tadanvayānusandhānena tyaktvā sparśajeṣv avarjanīyeṣu tannimittaharṣodvegau tyaktvā samantataḥ sarvasmād viṣayāt sarvam indriyagrāmaṃ viniyamya śanaiś śanair dhṛtigṛhītayā vivekaviṣayayā buddhyā sarvasmād ātmavyatiriktād uparamya ātmasaṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcid api cintayet //

children.text: sparśa-jāḥ saṅkalpa-jāś ca iti dvi-vidhāḥ kāmāḥ, sparśa-jāḥ śīta-uṣṇa-ādayaḥ, saṅkalpa-jāḥ putra-kṣetra-ādayaḥ / tatra saṅkalpa-prabhavāḥ sva-rūpeṇa eva tyaktuṃ śakyāḥ / tān sarvān manasa aiva tad-anvaya-anusandhānena tyaktvā sparśa-jeṣv avarjanīyeṣu tan-nimitta-harṣa-udvegau tyaktvā samantataḥ sarvasmād viṣayāt sarvam indriya-grāmaṃ viniyamya śanaiś śanair dhṛti-gṛhītayā viveka-viṣayayā buddhyā sarvasmād ātma-vyatiriktād uparamya ātma-saṃsthaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā na kiñcid api cintayet //
yato yato niścarati manaś cañcalam asthiram |
tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmany eva vaśaṃ nayet ||
yato yato niścarati manaś cañcalam asthiram |
tatas tato niyamya etad ātmany eva vaśaṃ nayet ||

body.text: calasvabhāvatayātmany asthiraṃ manaḥ yato yato viṣayaprāvaṇyahetoḥ bahiḥ niścarati, tatas tato yatnena mano niyamya ātmany eva atiśayitasukhabhāvanayā vaśaṃ nayet //

children.text: cala-sva-bhāvatayā ātmany asthiraṃ manaḥ yato yato viṣaya-prāvaṇya-hetoḥ bahiḥ niścarati, tatas tato yatnena mano niyamya ātmany eva atiśayita-sukha-bhāvanayā vaśaṃ nayet //
praśāntamanasaṃ hy enaṃ yoginaṃ sukham uttamam |
upaiti śāntarajasaṃ brahmabhūtam akalmaṣam ||

body.text:
yoginām iti pañcamyarthe ṣaṣṭhī / "sarvabhūtastham ātmānam" ityādinā caturvidhā yoginaḥ pratipāditāḥ / teṣv anantargatatvād vakṣyamāṇasya yoginaḥ na nirdhāraṇe ṣaṣṭhī saṃbhavati / api sarveṣām iti sarvaśabdanirdiṣṭās tapasviprabhṛtayaḥ / tatrāpy uktena nyāyena pañcamyartho grahītavyaḥ / yogibhyaḥ, api sarvebhyo vakṣyamāṇo yogī yuktatamaḥ / tadapekṣayā avaratve tapasviprabhṛtīnāṃ yogināṃ ca na kaścidviśeṣa ityarthaḥ; mervapekṣayā sarṣapāṇām iva / yady api sarṣapeṣu anyonyanyūnādhikabhāvo vidyate -- tathāpi mervapekṣayā avaratvanirdeśaḥ samānaḥ / matpriyatvātirekena ananyadhāraṇasvabhāvatayā madgatena antarātmanā manasā, śraddhāvān atyarthamatpriyatvena kṣaṇamātraviśleṣāsahatayā matprāptipravṛttau tvarāvān
yo māṃ bhajate -- māṃ vicitrānantabhogyabhoktṛvargabhogopakaraṇabhogasthānaparipūrṇanikhilajagadudayavibhavalayalīlam, aspṛṣṭāśeṣadoṣānavadhikātiśayajñānabalāiśvaryavīryaśaktitejaḥprabhṛtyasaṅkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇanidhim, svābhimatānurūpaikarūpācintyadivyādbhutanityaniravadyaniratiśayāujjvalyasaundaryasaugandhyasaukumāryalāvaṇyayauvanādyanantaguṇanidhidivyarūpam, vāṅmanasāparicchedyasvarūpasvabhāvam, apārakāruṇyasauśīlyavātsalyodāryamahodadhim, anālocitaviśeṣāśeṣalokaśaraṇyam, praṇatārtiharam, āśritavātsalyaikajaladhim, akhilam anujanayanaviṣayatāṃ gatam, ajahatsvasvabhāvam, vasudevagṛhe 'vatīrṇam, anavadhikātiśayatejasā nikhilaṃ jagad bhāsayantam, ātmakāntyā viśvam āpyāyayantam, bhajate
sevate, upāsta ityarthaḥ -- sa me yuktatamo mataḥ -- sa sarvebhyaś śreṣṭatamaḥ iti sarvaṃ sarvadā yathāvasthitaṃ svata eva sākṣātkurvan ahaṃ manye //

body.text: prathamenādhyāyaṣaṭkena -- paramaprāpyabhūtasya parasya brahmaṇo niravadhasya nikhilajagadekakāraṇasya sarvajñasya sarvabhūtasya satyasaṅkalpasya mahāvibhūteḥ śrīmato nārāyaṇasya prāptyupāyabhūtaṃ tadupāsanaṃ vaktuṃ tadaṅgabhūtam -- ātmajñānapūrvakakarmānuṣṭhānasādhyaṃ prāptuḥ pratyagātmano yāthātmyadārśanam uktam / idānīṃ madhyamena ṣaṭkena parabrahmabhūtaparamapuruṣasvarūpaṃ tadupāsanaṃ ca bhaktiśabdavācyam ucyate / tad etad uttaratra, "yataḥ pravṛttir bhūtānāṃ yena sarvam idaṃ tatam / svakarmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ // BhGR_1." ity ārabhya, "vimucya nirmamaś śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate / brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati / samas sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām // iti saṃkṣipya vakṣyate /

children.text: prathamena adhyāya-ṣaṭkena --- parama-prāpya-bhūtasya parasya brahmaṇo niravadhasya nikhila-jagad-eka-kāraṇasya sarva-jñasya sarva-bhūtasya satya-saṅkalpasya mahā-vibhūteḥ śrīmato nārāyaṇasya prāpty-upāya-bhūtaṃ tad-upāsanaṃ vaktuṃ tad-aṅga-bhūtam --- ātma-jñāna-pūrvaka-karma-anuṣṭhāna-sādhyaṃ prāptuḥ pratyag-ātmano yāthātmya-dārśanam uktam / idānīṃ madhyamena ṣaṭkena para-brahma-bhūta-parama-puruṣa-sva-rūpaṃ tad-upāsanaṃ ca bhakti-śabda-vācyam ucyate / tad etad uttaratra, "yataḥ pravṛttir bhūtānāṃ yena sarvam idaṃ tatam / sva-karmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ // BhGR_1." ity ārabhya, "vimucya nirmamaś śānto brahma-bhūyāya kalpate / brahma-bhūtaḥ prasanna-ātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati / samas sarveṣu bhūteṣu mad-bhaktiṃ labhate parām // iti saṃkṣipya vakṣyate /

body.text:
upānasaṃ tu bhaktirūpāpannam eva paraprāptyupāyabhūtam iti vedāntavākyasiddham / "tam eva viditvātimṛtyum eti", "tam evaṃ vidvān amṛta iha bhavati" ityādinā abhihitaṃ vedanam, "ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ ..... nididhyāsitavyaḥ", "ātmānam eva lokam upāsīta", "sattvaśuddhau dhruvā smṛtiḥ; smṛtilambhe sarvagranthīnāṃ vipramokṣaḥ", "bhidyate hṛdayagranthiś chidyante sarvasaṃśayāḥ / kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmin dṛṣṭe parāvare" ityādibhir aikārthyāt smṛtisantānarūpaṃ darśanasamānākāraṃ dhyānopāsanaśabdavācyam ity avagamyate / punaś ca, "nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena / yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām" iti viśeṣaṇāt pareṇātmanā varaṇīyatāhetubhūtaṃ smaryamāṇātyarthapriyatvena
svayam apy atyarthapriyarūpaṃ smṛtisantānam evopāsanaśabdavācyam iti hi niścīyate / tad eva hi bhaktir ity ucyate, "snehapūrvam anudhyānaṃ bhaktir ity abhidhīyate" ityādivacanāt / ataḥ "tam evaṃ vidvān amṛta iha bhavati, nānyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyate", "nāhaṃ vedair na tapasā na dānena na cejyayā / śakya evaṃvidho draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavān asi mām yathā // bhaktyā tv ananyayā śakya aham evaṃvidho 'rjuna / jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca parantapa" ity anayor ekārthatvaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati /

svayam apy atyartha-priya-rūpaṃ smṛti-santānam eva upāsana-śabda-vācyam iti hi niścīyate / tad eva hi bhaktir ity ucyate, "sneha-pūrvam anudhyānaṃ bhaktir ity abhidhīyate" ity-ādi-vacanāt / ataḥ "tam evaṃ vidvān amṛta iha bhavati, na anyaḥ panthā ayanāya vidyate", "na ahaṃ vedair na tapasā na dānena na ca ijyayā / śakya evaṃ-vidho draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavān asi mām yathā // bhaktyā tv ananyayā śakya aham evaṃ-vidho 'rjuna / jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca paran-tapa" ity anayor eka-arthatvaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati /

body.text: tatra saptame tāvad upāsyabhūtaparamapuruṣayāthātmyaṃ prakṛtyā tattirodhānaṃ tannivṛttaye bhagavatprapattiḥ, upāsakavidhābhedaḥ, jñāninaś śraiṣṭhyaṃ cocyate //

body.text: mayy ābhimukhyena asaktamanāḥ matpriyatvātirekeṇa matsvarūpeṇa guṇaiś ca ceṣṭitena madvibhūtyā viśleṣe sati tatkṣaṇād eva viśīryamāṇasvarūpatayā mayi sugāḍhaṃ baddhamanāḥ tathā madaśrayaḥ svayaṃ ca mayā vinā viśīryamāṇatayā madāśrayaḥ madekādhāraḥ, madyogaṃ yuñjan yoktuṃ pravṛttaḥ yogaviṣayabhūtaṃ mām asaṃśayaṃ nissaṃśayam, samagraṃ sakalaṃ yathā jñāsyasi yna jñānenoktena jñāsyasi, taj jñānam avahitamanāḥ tvaṃ śṛṇu //

manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣu kaścid yatati siddhaye |
yatatām api siddhānāṃ kaścin māṃ vetti tattvataḥ ||

body.text: manuṣyāḥ śāstrādhikārayogyāḥ / teṣāṃ sahasreṣu kaścid eva siddhiparyantaṃ yatate / siddhiparyantaṃ yatamānānāṃ sahasreṣu kaścid eva māṃ viditvā mattas siddhaye yatate / madvidāṃ sahasreṣu kaścid eva tattvataḥ yathāvasthitaṃ māṃ vetti / na kaścid ityabhiprāyaḥ; "sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ", "māṃ tu veda na kaścana" iti hi vakṣyate //

children.text: manuṣyāḥ śāstra-adhikāra-yogyāḥ / teṣāṃ sahasreṣu kaścid eva siddhi-paryantaṃ yatate / siddhi-paryantaṃ yatamānānāṃ sahasreṣu kaścid eva māṃ viditvā mattas siddhaye yatate / mad-vidāṃ sahasreṣu kaścid eva tattvataḥ yathā-avasthitaṃ māṃ vetti / na kaścid ity-abhiprāyaḥ; "sa mahā-ātmā sudurlabhaḥ", "māṃ tu veda na kaścana" iti hi vakṣyate //
bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhir eva ca |
ahaṅkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā ||
bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhir eva ca |
ahaṅkāra iti iyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā ||

body.text: asya vicitrānantabhogyabhogopakaraṇabhogasthānarūpeṇāvasthitasya jagataḥ prakṛtir iyaṃ gandhādiguṇakapṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśādirūpeṇa manaḥprabhṛtīndriyarūpeṇa mahadahaṃkārarūpeṇa cāṣṭadhā bhinnā madīyeti viddhi //
body.translated_text: Know that this <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature) of this universe — established in the form of infinitely varied objects of enjoyment, instruments of enjoyment, and places of enjoyment — divided eightfold as earth endowed with the quality of smell and the like, water, fire, air, space, and the like, as well as in the form of the mind and other sense-organs, and in the form of <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) and <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) — is Mine. ||

children.text: asya vicitra-ananta-bhogya-bhoga-upakaraṇa-bhoga-sthāna-rūpeṇa avasthitasya jagataḥ prakṛtir iyaṃ gandha-ādi-guṇaka-pṛthivy-ap-tejo-vāyv-ākāśa-ādi-rūpeṇa manaḥ-prabhṛti-indriya-rūpeṇa mahad-ahaṃkāra-rūpeṇa ca aṣṭadhā bhinnā madīya īti viddhi //
apareyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām |
children.translated_text: This is the lower [nature]; but know My other, higher <s>Prakṛti</s>,

children.text: jīvabhūtāṃ mahābāho yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat ||
children.translated_text: which has become the living beings (<s>jīvabhūtā</s>), O mighty-armed, by which this world is sustained. ||

children.text: apara īyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām |
jīva-bhūtāṃ mahā-bāho yaya īdaṃ dhāryate jagat ||

body.text: iyaṃ mamāparā prakṛtiḥ; itas tv anyām ito 'cetanāyāś cetanabhogyabhūtāyāḥ prakṛter visajātīyākārāṃ jīvabhūtāṃ parāṃ tasyāḥ bhoktṛtvena pradhānabhūtāṃ cetanarūpāṃ madīyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi; yayedam acetanaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagad dhāryate //
body.translated_text: This is My lower <s>Prakṛti</s>; but know My other [nature] — different from this, different from this non-conscious [nature] which serves as the object of enjoyment for the conscious [selves], of a form dissimilar to [that non-conscious nature], which has become the living beings, which is higher — being predominant as the enjoyer of that [non-conscious nature] — of the nature of consciousness, and Mine; by which this entire non-conscious world is sustained. ||

children.text: iyaṃ mama aparā prakṛtiḥ; itas tv anyām ito 'cetanāyāś cetana-bhogya-bhūtāyāḥ prakṛter visajātīya-ākārāṃ jīva-bhūtāṃ parāṃ tasyāḥ bhoktṛtvena pradhāna-bhūtāṃ cetana-rūpāṃ madīyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi; yaya īdam acetanaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagad dhāryate //
etadyonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇīty upadhāraya |
children.translated_text: Know that all beings have these two [natures] as their source.

children.text: ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā ||
children.translated_text: I am the origin and dissolution of the entire universe. ||

children.text: etad-yonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇi ity upadhāraya |
ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā ||

body.text:
etadcetanācetanasamaṣṭirūpamadīyaprakṛtidvayayonīni brahmādistambaparyantāni uccāvacabhāvenāvasthitāni cidacinmiśrāṇi madīyāni sarvāṇi bhūtānīty upadhāraya / madīyaprakṛtidvayayonīni hi tāni madīyāny eva / tathā prakṛtidvayayonitvena kṛtsnasya jagataḥ, tayor dvayor api madyonitvena madīyatvena ca, kṛtsnasya jagataḥ aham eva prabhavo 'ham eva ca pralayo 'ham eva ca śeṣīty upadhāraya / tayoḥ cidacitsamaṣṭibhūtayoḥ prakṛtipuruṣayor api paramapuruṣayonitvaṃ śrutismṛtisiddham / "mahān avyakte līyate / avyaktam akṣare līyate / akṣaraṃ tamasi līyate / tamaḥ pare deva ekībhavati", "viṣṇos svarūpāt paratodite dve rūpe prdhānaṃ puruṣaś ca vipra", "prakṛtir yā mayākhyātā vyaktāvyaktasvarūpiṇī / puruṣaś cāpy ubhāv etau līyate paramātmani /
paramātmā ca sarveṣām ādhāraḥ parameśvaraḥ / viṣṇunāmā sa vedeṣu vedānteṣu ca gīyate // BhGR_1." ityādikā hi śrutismṛtayaḥ //
body.translated_text: Know that all beings, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, established in the forms of high and low, consisting of a mixture of the conscious and the non-conscious, and being Mine, have as their source this My dual <s>Prakṛti</s> in the form of the aggregate of the conscious and the non-conscious. For since they have My dual <s>Prakṛti</s> as their source, they are indeed Mine. Likewise, know that since the dual <s>Prakṛti</s> is the source of the entire universe, and since both of those [<s>Prakṛtis</s>] have Me as their source and are Mine, I alone am the origin of the entire universe, I alone am the dissolution, and I alone am the Master (<s>śeṣin</s>). That the Supreme Person is the source of both <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, which are the aggregate of the conscious and the non-conscious, is established in <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>: 'The Great [principle] is dissolved into the Unmanifest; the Unmanifest is dissolved into the Imperishable; the Imperishable is dissolved into Darkness; Darkness becomes one in the Supreme God'; 'From the essential nature of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O sage, two forms arose beyond [it]: <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (conscious self)'; 'The <s>Prakṛti</s> declared by Me, having manifest and unmanifest forms, / and <s>Puruṣa</s> as well — both of these are dissolved in the Supreme Self. / And the Supreme Self is the support of all, the Supreme Lord, / He is sung in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedānta</s> by the name <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' — such are the <s>Śrutis</s> and <s>Smṛtis</s>. ||

children.text:
etad-cetana-acetana-samaṣṭi-rūpa-madīya-prakṛti-dvaya-yonīni brahmā-ādi-stamba-paryantāni uccā-vaca-bhāvena avasthitāni cid-acin-miśrāṇi madīyāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni ity upadhāraya / madīya-prakṛti-dvaya-yonīni hi tāni madīyāny eva / tathā prakṛti-dvaya-yonitvena kṛtsnasya jagataḥ, tayor dvayor api mad-yonitvena madīyatvena ca, kṛtsnasya jagataḥ aham eva prabhavo 'ham eva ca pralayo 'ham eva ca śeṣi īty upadhāraya / tayoḥ cid-acit-samaṣṭi-bhūtayoḥ prakṛti-puruṣayor api parama-puruṣa-yonitvaṃ śruti-smṛti-siddham / "mahān avyakte līyate / avyaktam akṣare līyate / akṣaraṃ tamasi līyate / tamaḥ pare deva ekī-bhavati", "viṣṇos sva-rūpāt paratā-udite dve rūpe prdhānaṃ puruṣaś ca vipra", "prakṛtir yā mayā ākhyātā vyakta-avyakta-sva-rūpiṇī / puruṣaś ca apy ubhāv etau līyate parama-ātmani /
parama-ātmā ca sarveṣām ādhāraḥ parama-īśvaraḥ / viṣṇu-nāmā sa vedeṣu veda-anteṣu ca gīyate // BhGR_1." ity-ādikā hi śruti-smṛtayaḥ //
mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyat kiñcid asti dhanañjaya |
children.translated_text: There is nothing whatsoever higher than Me, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>.

children.text: mattaḥ parataraṃ na anyat kiñcid asti dhanañjaya |

body.text: yathā sarvakāraṇasyāpi prakṛtidvayasya kāraṇatvena, sarvācetanavastuśeṣiṇaś cetanasyāpi śeṣitvena kāraṇatayā śeṣitayā cāhaṃ parataraḥ -- tathā jñānaśaktibalādiguṇayogena cāham eva parataraḥ / matto 'nyan madvyatiriktaṃ jñānabalādiguṇāntarayogi kiṃcid api parataraṃ nāsti //
body.translated_text: Just as by being the cause even of the dual <s>Prakṛti</s> which is the cause of everything, and by being the Master (<s>śeṣin</s>) even of the conscious [selves] who are the master of all non-conscious entities — by causality and by being the Master — I am the highest; so too by the possession of qualities such as knowledge, power, strength, and the like, I alone am the highest. Other than Me — anything distinct from Me, possessing any other set of qualities such as knowledge, strength, and the like — nothing whatsoever is higher. ||

children.text: yathā sarva-kāraṇasya api prakṛti-dvayasya kāraṇatvena, sarva-acetana-vastu-śeṣiṇaś cetanasya api śeṣitvena kāraṇatayā śeṣitayā ca ahaṃ parataraḥ --- tathā jñāna-śakti-bala-ādi-guṇa-yogena ca aham eva parataraḥ / matto 'nyan mad-vyatiriktaṃ jñāna-bala-ādi-guṇa-antara-yogi kiṃcid api parataraṃ na asti //
mayi sarvam idaṃ protaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva ||
children.translated_text: All this is strung on Me, like clusters of gems on a thread. ||

children.text: mayi sarvam idaṃ protaṃ sūtre maṇi-gaṇā iva ||

body.text: sarvam idaṃ cidacidvastujātaṃ kāryāvasthaṃ kāraṇāvasthaṃ ca maccharīrabhūtaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇavad atmatayāvasthite mayi protam āśritam / "yasya pṛthivī śarīram", "yasyātmā śarīram", "eṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmāpahatapāpmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ" iti, ātmaśarīrabhāvenāvasthānaṃ ca jagadbrahmaṇor antaryāmibrāhmaṇādiṣu siddham //
body.translated_text: All this — the totality of conscious and non-conscious entities, in both their effect-state and their causal state — being My body, is strung on, is dependent on, Me who abide as their inner self, like clusters of gems on a thread. 'He of whom the earth is the body'; 'He of whom the self is the body'; 'He is the inner self of all beings, free from evil, divine, the one God <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' — thus the relationship of self and body between <s>Brahman</s> and the universe is established in the <s>Antaryāmibrāhmaṇa</s> and other [scriptural passages]. ||

children.text: sarvam idaṃ cid-acid-vastu-jātaṃ kārya-avasthaṃ kāraṇa-avasthaṃ ca mac-charīra-bhūtaṃ sūtre maṇi-gaṇavad atmataya āvasthite mayi protam āśritam / "yasya pṛthivī śarīram", "yasyā atmā śarīram", "eṣa sarva-bhūta-antara-ātma āpahata-pāpmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇaḥ" iti, ātma-śarīra-bhāvena avasthānaṃ ca jagad-brahmaṇor antaryāmi-brāhmaṇa-ādiṣu siddham //

body.text: ataḥ sarvasya paramapuruṣaśarīratvenātmabhūtaparamapuruṣaprakārarvāt sarvaprakāraḥ paramapuruṣa evāvasthita iti sarvaiś śabdais tasyaivābhidhānam iti tat tat sāmānādhikaraṇyena āha --
body.translated_text: Therefore, since everything, being the body of the Supreme Person, has the Supreme Person — who is the self — as its mode (<s>prakāra</s>), the Supreme Person alone abides as the possessor of all modes; and therefore all words denote Him alone — [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] states this through co-referential predication (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) —

children.text: ataḥ sarvasya parama-puruṣa-śarīratvenā atma-bhūta-parama-puruṣa-prakārarvāt sarva-prakāraḥ parama-puruṣa eva avasthita iti sarvaiś śabdais tasya eva abhidhānam iti tat tat sāmānādhikaraṇyena āha ---
raso 'ham apsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśisūryayoḥ |
children.translated_text: I am the taste in waters, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>; I am the radiance in the moon and sun;

children.text: praṇavas sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Praṇava</s> in all the <s>Vedas</s>; sound in space; manliness in men. ||

children.text: raso 'ham apsu kaunteya prabha āsmi śaśi-sūryayoḥ |
praṇavas sarva-vedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu ||
puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca tejaś cāsmi vibhāvasau |
children.translated_text: I am the pure fragrance in earth, and the brilliance in fire;

children.text: jīvanaṃ sarvabhūteṣu tapaś cāsmi tapasviṣu ||
children.translated_text: the life-force in all beings, and the austerity in the austere. ||

children.text: puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca tejaś ca asmi vibhā-vasau |
jīvanaṃ sarva-bhūteṣu tapaś ca asmi tapasviṣu ||
bījaṃ māṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam |
children.translated_text: Know Me as the eternal seed of all beings, O <s>Pārtha</s>;

children.text: buddhir buddhimatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham ||
children.translated_text: I am the intelligence of the intelligent, the splendor of the splendid. ||

children.text: bījaṃ māṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam |
buddhir buddhimatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham ||
balaṃ balavantāñ cāhaṃ kāmarāgavivarjitam |
children.translated_text: I am the strength of the strong, free from desire and passion;

children.text: dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo 'smi bharatarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: I am the desire in beings that is not opposed to <s>dharma</s>, O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>. ||

children.text: balaṃ balavantāñ ca ahaṃ kāma-rāga-vivarjitam |
dharma-aviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo 'smi bharata-rṣabha ||

body.text: ete sarve vilakṣaṇā bhāvā matta evotpannāḥ, maccheṣabhūtāḥ maccharīratayā mayy evāvasthitāḥ; atas tattatprakāro 'ham evāvathitaḥ //
body.translated_text: All these diverse entities have arisen from Me alone, are subordinate to Me (<s>macceṣabhūta</s>), and abide in Me alone as My body. Therefore, I alone abide as the one possessing all those modes. ||

children.text: ete sarve vilakṣaṇā bhāvā matta eva utpannāḥ, mac-cheṣa-bhūtāḥ mac-charīratayā mayy eva avasthitāḥ; atas tat-tat-prakāro 'ham eva avathitaḥ //
ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāś ca ye |
children.translated_text: And whatever states of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> there are —

children.text: matta eveti tān viddhi na tv ahaṃ teṣu te mayi ||
children.translated_text: know them as being from Me alone; but I am not in them — they are in Me. ||

children.text: ye ca eva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāś ca ye |
matta eva iti tān viddhi na tv ahaṃ teṣu te mayi ||

body.text: kiṃ viśiṣya abhidhīyate? sāttvikā rājasās tāmasāś ca jagati dehatvenendriyatvena bhogyatvena tattaddhtetutvena cāvasthitā ye bhavāḥ, tān sarvān matta evotpannān viddhi; te maccharīratayā mayy evāvasthitā iti ca / na tv ahaṃ teṣu -- nāhaṃ kadācid api tadāyattasthitiḥ; anyatrātmāyattasthititve 'pi śarīrasya, śarīreṇātmanaḥ sthitāv apy upakāro vidyate; mama tu tair na kaścit tathāvidha upakāraḥ, kevalalīlaiva prayojanam ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: What is being stated in particular? Whatever entities established in the world as bodies, sense-organs, objects of enjoyment, and causes of each of those — whether of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, or <s>tamas</s> — know all of them as arisen from Me alone; and [know that] they abide in Me alone as My body. 'But I am not in them' — I am never dependent on them for My existence. Elsewhere, even though the self's existence may depend on the body, and even though the body may be of benefit for the self's existence — for Me, however, no such benefit [accrues] from them. Sport (<s>līlā</s>) alone is the purpose — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: kiṃ viśiṣya abhidhīyate? sāttvikā rājasās tāmasāś ca jagati dehatvena indriyatvena bhogyatvena tat-tad-dhtetutvena ca avasthitā ye bhavāḥ, tān sarvān matta eva utpannān viddhi; te mac-charīratayā mayy eva avasthitā iti ca / na tv ahaṃ teṣu --- na ahaṃ kadācid api tad-āyatta-sthitiḥ; anyatra-ātma-āyatta-sthititve 'pi śarīrasya, śarīreṇā atmanaḥ sthitāv apy upakāro vidyate; mama tu tair na kaścit tathā-vidha upakāraḥ, kevala-līla aiva prayojanam ity-arthaḥ //
tribhir guṇamayair bhāvair ebhiḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat |
children.translated_text: By these threefold states consisting of the <s>guṇas</s>, this entire world,

children.text: mohitaṃ nābhijānāti mām ebhyaḥ param avyayam ||
children.translated_text: deluded, does not know Me, who am beyond these [<s>guṇas</s>], imperishable. ||

children.text: tribhir guṇa-mayair bhāvair ebhiḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat |
mohitaṃ na abhijānāti mām ebhyaḥ param avyayam ||

body.text:
tad evaṃ cetanācetanātmakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagan madīyaṃ kāle kāle matta evotpadyate, mayi ca pralīyate, mayy evāvasthitam, maccharīrabhūtam, madātmakaṃ cety aham eva kāraṇāvasthāyāṃ kāryāvathāyāṃ ca sarvaśarīratayā sarvaprakāro 'vasthitaḥ / ataḥ kāraṇatvena śeṣitvena ca jñānādyasaṅkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇaiś cāham eva sarvaiḥ prakāraiḥ parataraḥ, matto 'nyat kenāpi kalyāṇaguṇagaṇena parataraṃ na vidyate / evaṃbhūtaṃ māṃ tribhyaḥ sāttvikarājasatāmasaguṇamayebhyo bhāvebhyaḥ paraṃ madasādhāraṇaiḥ kalyāṇaguṇagaṇais tattadbhogyatāprakāraiś ca param utkṛṣṭatamam, avyayaṃ sadaikarūpam api tair eva tribhir guṇamayair nihīnataraiḥ kṣaṇadhvaṃsibhiḥ pūrvakarmānuguṇadehendriyabhogyatvenāvasthitaiḥ padārthair mohitaṃ
devatiryaṅmanuṣyasthāvarātmanāvasthitaṃ sarvam idaṃ jagan nābhijānāti //
body.translated_text: Thus, the entire universe consisting of the conscious and the non-conscious is Mine; it arises from Me alone at each [appointed] time, dissolves in Me, abides in Me, is My body, and has Me as its self — thus I alone, in both the causal state and the effect-state, abide as the possessor of all modes by being the self of all bodies. Therefore, by causality, by being the Master, and by innumerable auspicious qualities such as knowledge and the like, I alone am the highest in every respect; nothing other than Me, possessing any set of auspicious qualities, is higher. Me, who is such — [Me who is] beyond the three states consisting of <s>sāttvika</s>, <s>rājasa</s>, and <s>tāmasa</s> <s>guṇas</s>, [Me who is] supreme by auspicious qualities unique to Me and by modes of enjoyability [unique to Me], supremely exalted, imperishable, ever of one form — [Me] this entire universe, established in the forms of gods, animals, humans, and plants, deluded by those very three <s>guṇa</s>-constituted entities, which are utterly inferior, momentarily perishable, and established as bodies, sense-organs, and objects of enjoyment in accordance with prior <s>karma</s>, does not know. ||

children.text:
tad evaṃ cetana-acetana-ātmakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagan madīyaṃ kāle kāle matta eva utpadyate, mayi ca pralīyate, mayy eva avasthitam, mac-charīra-bhūtam, mad-ātmakaṃ ca ity aham eva kāraṇa-avasthāyāṃ kārya-avathāyāṃ ca sarva-śarīratayā sarva-prakāro 'vasthitaḥ / ataḥ kāraṇatvena śeṣitvena ca jñāna-ādy-asaṅkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇaiś ca aham eva sarvaiḥ prakāraiḥ parataraḥ, matto 'nyat kena api kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇena parataraṃ na vidyate / evaṃ-bhūtaṃ māṃ tribhyaḥ sāttvika-rājasa-tāmasa-guṇa-mayebhyo bhāvebhyaḥ paraṃ mad-asādhāraṇaiḥ kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇais tat-tad-bhogyatā-prakāraiś ca param utkṛṣṭatamam, avyayaṃ sada aika-rūpam api tair eva tribhir guṇa-mayair nihīnataraiḥ kṣaṇa-dhvaṃsibhiḥ pūrva-karma-anuguṇa-deha-indriya-bhogyatvena avasthitaiḥ pada-arthair mohitaṃ
deva-tiryaṅ-manuṣya-sthāvara-ātmana āvasthitaṃ sarvam idaṃ jagan na abhijānāti //

body.text: kathaṃ svata evānavadhikātiśayānande nitye sadaikarūpe laukikavastubhogyatatprakāraiś cotkṛṣṭatame tvayi sthite 'py atyantanihīneṣu guṇamayeṣv asthireṣu bhāveṣu sarvasya bhoktṛvargasya bhogyatvabuddhir upajāyata ity atrāha --
body.translated_text: How is it that the entire class of enjoyers develops the cognition of enjoyability in utterly inferior, <s>guṇa</s>-constituted, unstable entities, when You — of an essential nature of unsurpassable, infinite bliss, eternal, ever of one form, and supremely exalted by worldly objects of enjoyment and their modes — are present? To this [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] says —

children.text: kathaṃ svata eva anavadhika-atiśaya-ānande nitye sada aika-rūpe laukika-vastu-bhogya-tat-prakāraiś ca utkṛṣṭatame tvayi sthite 'py atyanta-nihīneṣu guṇa-mayeṣv asthireṣu bhāveṣu sarvasya bhoktṛ-vargasya bhogyatva-buddhir upajāyata ity atrā aha ---
daivī hy eṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā |
children.translated_text: For this divine <s>māyā</s> of Mine, consisting of the <s>guṇas</s>, is hard to overcome.

children.text: daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā |

body.text:
mamaiṣā guṇamayī sattvarajastamomayī māyā yasmād daivī devena krīḍhāpravṛttena mayaiva nirmitā, tasmāt sarvair duratyayā duratikramā / asyāḥ māyāśabdavācyatvam āsurarākṣasāstrādīnām iva vicitrakāryakaratvena, yathā ca "tato bhagavatā tasya rakṣārthaṃ cakram uttamam / ājagāma samājñaptaṃ jvālāmāli sudarśanam / tena māyāsahasraṃ tacchambarasyāśugāminā / bālasya rakṣatā deham aikāikaśyena sūditam" ity ādau / ato māyāśabdo na mithyārthavācī / aindrajālikādiṣv api kenacin mantrāuṣadhādinā mithyārthaviṣayāyāḥ pāramārthikyā eva buddher utpādakatvena māyāvīti prayogaḥ / tathā mantrāuṣadhādir eva tatra māyā; sarvaprayogeṣv anugatasyaikasyaiva śabdārthatvāt / tatra mithyārtheṣu māyāśabdaprayogo māyākāryabuddhiviṣayatvenāupacārikaḥ,
mañcāḥ krośantītivat / eṣā guṇamayī pāramārthikī bhagavanmāyaiva, "māyām tu prakṛtiṃ vidyān māyinaṃ tu maheśvaram" ityādiṣv abhidhīyate / asyāḥ kāryaṃ bhagavatsvarūpatirodhānam, svasvarūpabhogyatvabuddhiś ca / ato bhagavanmāyayā mohitaṃ sarvaṃ jagad bhagavantam anavadhikātiśayānandasvarūpaṃ nābhijānāti //
body.translated_text: This <s>māyā</s> of Mine, consisting of the <s>guṇas</s> — made of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — since it is 'divine' (<s>daivī</s>), i.e., fashioned by Me, the God who has set [it] in motion as sport, therefore it is hard to overcome, hard to cross beyond, for all. Its being denoted by the word <s>māyā</s> is because of its capacity to produce wonderful effects, like the weapons of <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and the like. As [seen in the passage]: 'Then, for the protection of that [child], the supreme discus came, summoned by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, flaming, <s>Sudarśana</s>; by it, the thousand <s>māyās</s> of that swift-moving <s>Śambara</s> were destroyed one by one while protecting the child's body' — and so forth. Therefore, the word <s>māyā</s> does not denote something false or illusory. Even in the case of conjurers and the like, the usage '<s>māyāvī</s>' (possessor of <s>māyā</s>) is because [they are] the producers, by some mantra or herb and the like, of an entirely real cognition that has a false object. Likewise, the mantra or herb and the like itself is the <s>māyā</s> there; since in all usages, one and the same meaning of the word is the denotation. There, the usage of the word <s>māyā</s> with respect to false objects is figurative, because the object of the cognition that is the effect of <s>māyā</s> [is false], like 'the platforms are crying.' This <s>guṇa</s>-constituted, entirely real <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>māyā</s> itself is referred to in passages such as 'Know <s>māyā</s> to be <s>Prakṛti</s>, and the wielder of <s>māyā</s> to be the Great Lord.' Its effect is the concealment of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s true nature, and the cognition of enjoyability with respect to one's own nature. Therefore, the entire universe, deluded by the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>māyā</s>, does not know the <s>Bhagavān</s>, whose essential nature is unsurpassable, infinite bliss. ||

children.text:
mama eṣā guṇa-mayī sattva-rajas-tamo-mayī māyā yasmād daivī devena krīḍhā-pravṛttena maya aiva nirmitā, tasmāt sarvair duratyayā duratikramā / asyāḥ māyā-śabda-vācyatvam āsura-rākṣasa-astra-ādīnām iva vicitra-kārya-karatvena, yathā ca "tato bhagavatā tasya rakṣā-arthaṃ cakram uttamam / ājagāma samājñaptaṃ jvālā-māli sudarśanam / tena māyā-sahasraṃ tac-chambarasya aśu-gāminā / bālasya rakṣatā deham aika-aikaśyena sūditam" ity ādau / ato māyā-śabdo na mithyā-artha-vācī / aindrajālika-ādiṣv api kenacin mantra-auṣadha-ādinā mithyā-artha-viṣayāyāḥ pāramārthikyā eva buddher utpādakatvena māyāvi īti prayogaḥ / tathā mantra-auṣadha-ādir eva tatra māyā; sarva-prayogeṣv anugatasya ekasya eva śabda-arthatvāt / tatra mithyā-artheṣu māyā-śabda-prayogo māyā-kārya-buddhi-viṣayatvena aupacārikaḥ,
mañcāḥ krośanti itivat / eṣā guṇa-mayī pāramārthikī bhagavan-māya aiva, "māyām tu prakṛtiṃ vidyān māyinaṃ tu mahā-īśvaram" ity-ādiṣv abhidhīyate / asyāḥ kāryaṃ bhagavat-sva-rūpa-tirodhānam, sva-sva-rūpa-bhogyatva-buddhiś ca / ato bhagavan-māyayā mohitaṃ sarvaṃ jagad bhagavantam anavadhika-atiśaya-ānanda-sva-rūpaṃ na abhijānāti //

body.text: māyāvimocanopāyam āha --
body.translated_text: He states the means of liberation from <s>māyā</s> —

children.text: māyā-vimocana-upāyam āha ---
mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṃ taranti te ||
children.translated_text: Those who take refuge in Me alone cross beyond this <s>māyā</s>. ||

children.text: mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṃ taranti te ||

body.text: mām eva satyasaṅkalpaṃ paramakāruṇikam anālocitaviśeṣāśeṣalokaśaraṇyam ye śaraṇaṃ prapadyante, te etāṃ madīyāṃ guṇamayīṃ māyāṃ taranti māyām utsṛjya mām evopāsata ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Those who take refuge in Me alone — in Me whose will is true, who is supremely compassionate, who is the refuge of all the worlds without exception and without regard to any distinction — they cross beyond this <s>māyā</s> of Mine consisting of the <s>guṇas</s>; meaning they cast off <s>māyā</s> and worship Me alone. ||

children.text: mām eva satya-saṅkalpaṃ parama-kāruṇikam anālocita-viśeṣa-aśeṣa-loka-śaraṇyam ye śaraṇaṃ prapadyante, te etāṃ madīyāṃ guṇa-mayīṃ māyāṃ taranti māyām utsṛjya mām eva upāsata ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: kim iti bhagavadupāsanāpādinīṃ bhagavatprapattiṃ sarve na kurvata ity atrāha -
body.translated_text: Why do not all undertake the taking of refuge in the <s>Bhagavān</s>, which leads to the worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s>? — to this [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] says —

children.text: kim iti bhagavad-upāsana-āpādinīṃ bhagavat-prapattiṃ sarve na kurvata ity atrā aha --
na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ |
children.translated_text: The evil-doers, the deluded, the lowest of men, do not take refuge in Me,

children.text: māyayāpahṛtajñānā āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those whose knowledge has been stolen by <s>māyā</s>, who have resorted to a demonic (<s>āsura</s>) disposition. ||

children.text: na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante nara-adhamāḥ |
māyaya āpahṛta-jñānā āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ ||

body.text:
duṣkṛtinaḥ pāpakarmāṇaḥ māṃ na prapadyate / duṣkṛtatāratamyena te caturvidhā bhavanti mūḍhāḥ, narādhamāḥ, māyayāpahṛtajñānāḥ, āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ iti / mūḍhāḥ viparītajñānāḥ; pūrvoktaprakāreṇa bhagavaccheṣataikarasam ātmānaṃ bhogyajātaṃ ca svaśeṣatayā manyamānāḥ / narādhamāḥ sāmānyena jñāte 'pi matsvarūpe madaunmukhyānarhāḥ / māyayāpahṛtajñānāḥ madviṣayaṃ madaiśvaryaviṣayaṃ ca jñānaṃ yeṣāṃ tadasaṃbhāvanāpādinībhiḥ kūṭayuktibhir apahṛtam, te tathā uktāḥ / āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ madviṣayaṃ madaiśvaryaviṣayaṃ ca jñānaṃ sudṛḍham upapannaṃ yeṣāṃ dvaiṣāyaiva bhavati; te āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ / uttarottarāḥ pāpiṣṭhatamāḥ
//
body.translated_text: The evil-doers — those of sinful actions — do not take refuge in Me. By the gradation of evil deeds, they are of four kinds: the deluded (<s>mūḍha</s>), the lowest of men (<s>narādhama</s>), those whose knowledge has been stolen by <s>māyā</s>, and those who have resorted to a demonic disposition. The deluded — those of perverted knowledge; who regard the self, whose sole essence is being subsidiary to the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the manner stated above, and all the objects of enjoyment as being subsidiary to themselves. The lowest of men — those who, even though they know My essential nature in general, are unfit to turn their faces toward Me. Those whose knowledge has been stolen by <s>māyā</s> — those whose knowledge pertaining to Me and to My sovereignty has been stolen by sophistical reasonings that produce the conviction of [My] impossibility. Those who have resorted to a demonic disposition — those whose well-established and well-supported knowledge pertaining to Me and My sovereignty serves only for hatred [of Me]. Each succeeding [category] is more sinful than the last. ||

children.text:
duṣkṛtinaḥ pāpa-karmāṇaḥ māṃ na prapadyate / duṣkṛta-tāratamyena te catur-vidhā bhavanti mūḍhāḥ, nara-adhamāḥ, māyaya āpahṛta-jñānāḥ, āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ iti / mūḍhāḥ viparīta-jñānāḥ; pūrva-ukta-prakāreṇa bhagavac-cheṣatā-eka-rasam ātmānaṃ bhogya-jātaṃ ca sva-śeṣatayā manyamānāḥ / nara-adhamāḥ sāmānyena jñāte 'pi mat-sva-rūpe mad-aunmukhya-anarhāḥ / māyaya āpahṛta-jñānāḥ mad-viṣayaṃ mad-aiśvarya-viṣayaṃ ca jñānaṃ yeṣāṃ tad-asaṃbhāvana-āpādinībhiḥ kūṭa-yuktibhir apahṛtam, te tathā uktāḥ / āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ mad-viṣayaṃ mad-aiśvarya-viṣayaṃ ca jñānaṃ sudṛḍham upapannaṃ yeṣāṃ dvaiṣāya eva bhavati; te āsuraṃ bhāvam āśritāḥ / uttara-uttarāḥ pāpiṣṭhatamāḥ
//
caturvidhā bhajante mām janāḥ sukṛtino 'rjuna |
children.translated_text: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me, O <s>Arjuna</s>:

children.text: ārto jijñāsur arthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise one, O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>. ||

children.text: catur-vidhā bhajante mām janāḥ sukṛtino 'rjuna |
ārto jijñāsur artha-arthī jñānī ca bharata-rṣabha ||

body.text: sukṛtinaḥ puṇyakarmāṇo māṃ śaraṇam upagamya mām eva bhajante / te ca sukṛtatāratamyena caturvidhāḥ, sukṛtagarīyastvena pratipattivaiśeṣyād uttarottarā adhikatamā bhavanti / ārtaḥ pratiṣṭhāhīnaḥ bhraṣṭāiśvaryaḥ punar tatprāptikāmaḥ / arthārthī aprāptāiśvaryatayā aiśvaryakāmaḥ / tayor mukhabhedamātram / aiśvaryaviṣayatayāikyād eka evādhikāraḥ / jijñāsuḥ prakṛtiviyuktātmasvarūpāvāptīcchuḥ / jñānam evāsya svarūpam iti jijñāsur ity uktam / jñānī ca, "itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām" ityādinābhihitabhagavaccheṣataikarasātmasvarūpavit; prakṛtiviyuktakevalātmani aparyavasyan bhagavantaṃ prepsuḥ bhagavantam eva paramaprāpyaṃ manvānaḥ //
body.translated_text: The virtuous ones — those of meritorious deeds — having approached Me as their refuge, worship Me alone. And they, by the gradation of meritorious deeds, are of four kinds; by the superiority of their merit, they become progressively higher due to the distinction of their understanding. The distressed (<s>ārta</s>) — one who has lost his position, whose sovereignty has been destroyed, who desires to regain it. The seeker of wealth (<s>arthārthī</s>) — one who, not having attained sovereignty, desires sovereignty. The difference between these two is merely nominal. Since both have sovereignty as their object, they constitute a single class. The seeker of knowledge (<s>jijñāsu</s>) — one who desires to attain the true nature of the self separated from <s>Prakṛti</s>. He is called '<s>jijñāsu</s>' because knowledge alone is its [the self's] essential nature. And the wise one (<s>jñānī</s>) — one who knows the true nature of the self, whose sole essence is being subsidiary to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, as stated in 'but know My other, higher <s>Prakṛti</s>' and the like; who, not resting in the mere self separated from <s>Prakṛti</s>, desires to attain the <s>Bhagavān</s>, considering the <s>Bhagavān</s> alone as the supreme object of attainment. ||

children.text: sukṛtinaḥ puṇya-karmāṇo māṃ śaraṇam upagamya mām eva bhajante / te ca sukṛta-tāratamyena catur-vidhāḥ, sukṛta-garīyastvena pratipatti-vaiśeṣyād uttara-uttarā adhikatamā bhavanti / ārtaḥ pratiṣṭhā-hīnaḥ bhraṣṭa-aiśvaryaḥ punar tat-prāpti-kāmaḥ / artha-arthī aprāpta-aiśvaryatayā aiśvarya-kāmaḥ / tayor mukha-bheda-mātram / aiśvarya-viṣayataya āikyād eka eva adhikāraḥ / jijñāsuḥ prakṛti-viyukta-ātma-sva-rūpa-avāpti-icchuḥ / jñānam eva asya sva-rūpam iti jijñāsur ity uktam / jñānī ca, "itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām" ity-ādina ābhihita-bhagavac-cheṣatā-eka-rasa-ātma-sva-rūpa-vit; prakṛti-viyukta-kevala-ātmani aparyavasyan bhagavantaṃ prepsuḥ bhagavantam eva parama-prāpyaṃ manvānaḥ //
teṣāṃ jñānī nityayuktaḥ ekabhaktir viśiṣyate |
children.translated_text: Among these, the wise one, ever united [with Me], devoted to the One alone, excels.

children.text: priyo hi jñānino 'tyartham ahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For I am exceedingly dear to the wise one, and he is dear to Me. ||

children.text: teṣāṃ jñānī nitya-yuktaḥ eka-bhaktir viśiṣyate |
priyo hi jñānino 'tyartham ahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ ||

body.text:
teṣāṃ jñānī viśiṣyate / kutaḥ? nityayukta ekabhaktir iti ca / jñānino hi
madekaprāpyasya mayā yogo nityaḥ; itarayos tu yāvatsvābhilaṣitaprāpti mayā yogaḥ / tathā jñānino mayy ekasminn eva bhaktiḥ; itarayos tu svābhilaṣite tatsādhanatvena mayi ca / ataḥ sa eva viśiṣyate / kiñ ca, priyo hi jñānino 'tyartham aham / arthaśabdo 'bhidheyavacanaḥ; jñānino 'haṃ yathā priyaḥ, tathā mayā sarvajñena sarvaśaktināpy abhidhātuṃ na śakyata ityarthaḥ; priyatvasyeyattārahitatvāt / yathā jñāninām agresarasya prahlādasya, "sa tv āsaktamatiḥ kṛṣṇe daśyamāno mahoragaiḥ / na vivedātmano gātraṃ tatsmṛtyāhlādasaṃsthitaḥ" iti / tathaiva so 'pi mama priyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>jñānī</s> (knower) is distinguished among them. Why? Because he is ever-disciplined and single in devotion. For the <s>jñānī</s>, whose sole object of attainment is Me, the connection with Me is eternal; but for the other two, the connection with Me lasts only until the attainment of their desired object. Likewise, the <s>jñānī</s>'s devotion is to Me alone; but for the other two, it is to their desired object and to Me as the means for it. Therefore, he alone is distinguished. Moreover, I am exceedingly dear to the <s>jñānī</s>. The word <s>artha</s> here means 'that which is expressed'; the meaning is: how dear I am to the <s>jñānī</s> cannot be expressed even by Me, who am omniscient and omnipotent — because the extent of that dearness is limitless. As in the case of <s>Prahlāda</s>, the foremost among the <s>jñānīs</s>: 'He, with his mind attached to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, being bitten by great serpents, did not feel his own body, being established in the joy of remembering Him.' And he too is equally dear to Me. //

children.text:
teṣāṃ jñānī viśiṣyate / kutaḥ? nitya-yukta eka-bhaktir iti ca / jñānino hi
mad-eka-prāpyasya mayā yogo nityaḥ; itarayos tu yāvat-sva-abhilaṣita-prāpti mayā yogaḥ / tathā jñānino mayy ekasminn eva bhaktiḥ; itarayos tu sva-abhilaṣite tat-sādhanatvena mayi ca / ataḥ sa eva viśiṣyate / kiñ ca, priyo hi jñānino 'tyartham aham / artha-śabdo 'bhidheya-vacanaḥ; jñānino 'haṃ yathā priyaḥ, tathā mayā sarva-jñena sarva-śaktina āpy abhidhātuṃ na śakyata ity-arthaḥ; priyatvasya iyattā-rahitatvāt / yathā jñāninām agresarasya prahlādasya, "sa tv āsakta-matiḥ kṛṣṇe daśyamāno mahā-uragaiḥ / na vivedā atmano gātraṃ tat-smṛty-āhlāda-saṃsthitaḥ" iti / tatha aiva so 'pi mama priyaḥ //
udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tv ātmaiva me matam |
children.translated_text: 'All of these are noble, but the <s>jñānī</s> is My very self — such is My view.'

children.text: āsthitas sa hi yuktātmā mām evānuttamāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: 'For he, with disciplined self, is established [in the conviction that] I alone am the unsurpassed goal.' ||

children.text: udārāḥ sarva eva ete jñānī tv ātma aiva me matam |
āsthitas sa hi yukta-ātmā mām eva anuttamāṃ gatim ||

body.text: sarva evaite mām evopāsata iti udārāḥ vadānyāḥ / ye matto yat kiṃcid api gṛhṇanti, te hi mama sarvasvadāyinaḥ / jñānī tv ātmaiva me matam -- tadāyattadhāraṇo 'ham iti manye / kasmād evam? yasmād ayaṃ mayā vinātmadhāraṇāsaṃbhāvanayā mām evānuttamaṃ prāpyam āsthitaḥ, atas tena vinā mamāpy ātmadhāraṇaṃ na saṃbhavati / tato mamātmā hi saḥ //
body.translated_text: All of these worship Me alone, [so they are] noble — generous. For whoever accepts even the slightest thing from Me — they are givers of all that is mine. But the <s>jñānī</s> is My very self — such is My view: I consider that My sustenance depends on him. Why so? Because this one, considering the sustenance of his own self impossible without Me, is established in [the conviction that] I alone am the unsurpassed object of attainment; therefore, without him, the sustenance of My own self too is not possible. Hence he is indeed My self. //

children.text: sarva eva ete mām eva upāsata iti udārāḥ vadānyāḥ / ye matto yat kiṃcid api gṛhṇanti, te hi mama sarva-sva-dāyinaḥ / jñānī tv ātma aiva me matam --- tad-āyatta-dhāraṇo 'ham iti manye / kasmād evam? yasmād ayaṃ mayā vinā ātma-dhāraṇa-asaṃbhāvanayā mām eva anuttamaṃ prāpyam āsthitaḥ, atas tena vinā mama apy ātma-dhāraṇaṃ na saṃbhavati / tato mamā atmā hi saḥ //
bahūnāṃ janmanām ante jñānavān māṃ prapadyate |
children.translated_text: 'At the end of many births, the knower takes refuge in Me,'

children.text: vāsudevas sarvam iti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: '[saying] "<s>Vāsudeva</s> is everything" — such a great soul is extremely rare.' ||

children.text: bahūnāṃ janmanām ante jñānavān māṃ prapadyate |
vāsu-devas sarvam iti sa mahā-ātmā sudurlabhaḥ ||

body.text:
nālpasaṃkhyāsaṅkhyātānāṃ puṇyajanmanāṃ phalam idam, yan maccheṣataikarasātmayāthātmyajñānapūrvakaṃ matprapadanam; api tu bahūnāṃ janmanāṃ puṇyajanmanām ante avasāne, vāsudevaśeṣataikaraso 'haṃ tadāyattasvarūpasthitipravṛttiś ca; sa cāsaṅkhyeyaiḥ kalyāṇaguṇagaṇaiḥ parataraḥ iti jñānavān bhūtvā, vāsudeva eva mama paramaprāpyaṃ prāpakaṃ ca, anyad api yan manorathavartiṃ sa eva mama tat sarvam iti māṃ prapadyate mām upāste; sa mahātmā mahāmanāḥ sudurlabhaḥ durlabhataro loke / vāsudevas sarvam ity asyāyam evārthaḥ, "priyo hi jñānino 'tyartham aham", "āsthitas sa hi yuktātmā mām evānuttamāṃ gatim" iti prakramāt / jñānavāṃś cāyam uktalakṣaṇa eva, asyaiva pūrvoktajñānitvāt, bhūmir āpaḥ" ity ārabhya, "ahaṅkāra itīyaṃ
me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā / apareyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām / jīvabhūtām" iti hi cetanācetanaprakṛtidvayasya paramapuruṣaśeṣataikarasatoktā; "ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā / mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyat kiñcid asti dhanañjaya" ity ārabhya, "ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāś ca ye / matta eveti tān viddhi na tv ahaṃ teṣu te mayi // iti prakṛtidvayasya kāryakāraṇobhayāvasthasya paramapuruṣāyattasvarūpasthitipravṛttitvaṃ paramapuruṣasya ca sarvaiḥ prakāraiḥ sarvasmāt parataratvam uktam; ataḥ sa evātra jñānīty ucyate //
body.translated_text: This — the taking refuge in Me preceded by the knowledge of the true nature of the self whose sole essence is being a dependent (<s>śeṣa</s>) of Me — is not the fruit of meritorious births of a small or countable number; rather, at the end of many meritorious births — at the conclusion [of them] — having become a knower, [understanding:] 'I am of the sole essence of being a dependent of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and my existence, nature, and activity depend on Him; and He is the highest, with innumerable hosts of auspicious qualities'; [knowing:] '<s>Vāsudeva</s> alone is my supreme object of attainment and the means of attainment; whatever else even enters my thought — He alone is all that to me' — he takes refuge in Me, he worships Me. Such a great soul — one of great mind — is exceedingly rare, rarer than rare in the world. The meaning of '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is everything' is precisely this, as established by the context: 'I am exceedingly dear to the <s>jñānī</s>,' 'For he, with disciplined self, is established [in the conviction that] I alone am the unsurpassed goal.' And this knower is of the character described above, since his being a <s>jñānī</s> was stated earlier. For, beginning with 'Earth, water,' and [continuing with] 'ego — this is My <s>Prakṛti</s>, eightfold divided. This is the lower; but know My other <s>Prakṛti</s>, the higher one — which has become the individual souls' — the sole essence of both the sentient and non-sentient <s>Prakṛtis</s> as being dependents of the Supreme Person was stated. Beginning with 'I am the origin and dissolution of the entire universe; there is nothing higher than Me, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>' and [continuing with] 'And whatever states are of <s>sattva</s>, of <s>rajas</s>, and of <s>tamas</s> — know them as being from Me alone; I am not in them, but they are in Me' — the dependence of the existence, nature, and activity of both <s>Prakṛtis</s> in both their causal and effectual states on the Supreme Person, and the supreme superiority of the Supreme Person over all in every way, was stated. Therefore, it is he alone who is here called the <s>jñānī</s>. //

children.text:
na alpa-saṃkhyā-saṅkhyātānāṃ puṇya-janmanāṃ phalam idam, yan mac-cheṣatā-eka-rasa-ātma-yāthātmya-jñāna-pūrvakaṃ mat-prapadanam; api tu bahūnāṃ janmanāṃ puṇya-janmanām ante avasāne, vāsu-deva-śeṣatā-eka-raso 'haṃ tad-āyatta-sva-rūpa-sthiti-pravṛttiś ca; sa ca asaṅkhyeyaiḥ kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇaiḥ parataraḥ iti jñānavān bhūtvā, vāsu-deva eva mama parama-prāpyaṃ prāpakaṃ ca, anyad api yan mano-ratha-vartiṃ sa eva mama tat sarvam iti māṃ prapadyate mām upāste; sa mahā-ātmā mahā-manāḥ sudurlabhaḥ durlabhataro loke / vāsu-devas sarvam ity asya ayam eva arthaḥ, "priyo hi jñānino 'tyartham aham", "āsthitas sa hi yukta-ātmā mām eva anuttamāṃ gatim" iti prakramāt / jñānavāṃś ca ayam ukta-lakṣaṇa eva, asya eva pūrva-ukta-jñānitvāt, bhūmir āpaḥ" ity ārabhya, "ahaṅkāra iti iyaṃ
me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā / apara īyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām / jīva-bhūtām" iti hi cetana-acetana-prakṛti-dvayasya parama-puruṣa-śeṣatā-eka-rasata ūktā; "ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā / mattaḥ parataraṃ na anyat kiñcid asti dhanañjaya" ity ārabhya, "ye ca eva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasās tāmasāś ca ye / matta eva iti tān viddhi na tv ahaṃ teṣu te mayi // iti prakṛti-dvayasya kārya-kāraṇa-ubhaya-avasthasya parama-puruṣa-āyatta-sva-rūpa-sthiti-pravṛttitvaṃ parama-puruṣasya ca sarvaiḥ prakāraiḥ sarvasmāt parataratvam uktam; ataḥ sa eva atra jñāni īty ucyate //

body.text: tasya jñānino durlabhatvam evopapādayati --
body.translated_text: He establishes the very rarity of that <s>jñānī</s> —

children.text: tasya jñānino durlabhatvam eva upapādayati ---
kāmais tais tair hṛtajñānāḥ prapadyante 'nyadevatāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those whose knowledge has been stolen by various desires resort to other deities,'

children.text: taṃ taṃ niyamam āsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā ||
children.translated_text: 'adopting this or that observance, constrained by their own nature.' ||

children.text: kāmais tais tair hṛta-jñānāḥ prapadyante 'nya-devatāḥ |
taṃ taṃ niyamam āsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā ||

body.text: sarva eva hi laukikāḥ puruṣāḥ svayā prakṛtyā pāpavāsanayā guṇamayabhāvaviṣayayā niyatāḥ nityānvitāḥ tais taiḥ svavāsanānurūpair guṇamayair eva kāmaiḥ icchāviṣayabhūtaiḥ hṛtamatsvarūpaviṣayajñānāḥ tattatkāmasiddhyartham anyadevatāḥ madvyatiriktāḥ kevalendrādidevatāḥ taṃ taṃ niyamaṃ āsthāya tattaddevatāviśeṣamātraprīṇanāsādhāraṇaṃ niyamam āsthyāya prapadyante tā evāśrityārcayante //
body.translated_text: Indeed, all worldly persons, constrained — perpetually connected — by their own nature (<s>prakṛti</s>), which is the latent impression of sin and has the qualities of material nature as its object, by those various desires — objects of wish conforming to their own latent impressions, consisting merely of the <s>guṇas</s> — their knowledge of My true nature having been stolen, for the sake of fulfilling those various desires, resort to other deities — deities other than Me, mere deities like <s>Indra</s> and the like — adopting this or that observance, a specific discipline exclusive to the gratification of each particular deity, they take refuge in and worship them alone. //

children.text: sarva eva hi laukikāḥ puruṣāḥ svayā prakṛtyā pāpa-vāsanayā guṇa-maya-bhāva-viṣayayā niyatāḥ nitya-anvitāḥ tais taiḥ sva-vāsanā-anurūpair guṇa-mayair eva kāmaiḥ icchā-viṣaya-bhūtaiḥ hṛtamat-sva-rūpa-viṣaya-jñānāḥ tat-tat-kāma-siddhy-artham anya-devatāḥ mad-vyatiriktāḥ kevala-indra-ādi-devatāḥ taṃ taṃ niyamaṃ āsthāya tat-tad-devatā-viśeṣa-mātra-prīṇana-asādhāraṇaṃ niyamam āsthyāya prapadyante tā evā aśritya arcayante //
yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitum icchati |
children.translated_text: 'Whatever form a devotee with faith wishes to worship,'

children.text: tasya tasyācalāṃ śraddhāṃ tām eva vidadhāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: 'I make his faith in that [form] unwavering.' ||

children.text: yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhaya ārcitum icchati |
tasya tasya acalāṃ śraddhāṃ tām eva vidadhāmy aham ||

body.text: tā api devatā madīyās tanavaḥ, "ya āditye tiṣṭhan ... yam ādityo na veda yasyādityaś śarīram" ityādiśrutibhiḥ pratipāditāḥ / madīyās tanava ity ajānann api yo yo yāṃ yāṃ madīyām ādityādikāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitum icchati; tasya tasyājānato 'pi mattanuviṣayaiṣā śraddhety anusandhāya tām evācalāṃ nirvighnāṃ vidadhāmy aham //
body.translated_text: Those deities too are My embodiments (<s>tanu</s>), as established by <s>śruti</s> texts such as: 'He who stands in the sun... whom the sun does not know, whose body the sun is,' and the like. Even one who does not know [them to be] My embodiments — whatever devotee wishes with faith to worship whatever embodiment of Mine, such as <s>Āditya</s> and the like — reflecting that 'this faith of his, though unknowing, is directed toward My embodiment' — I make that [faith] of his unwavering, free from obstacles. //

children.text: tā api devatā madīyās tanavaḥ, "ya āditye tiṣṭhan ... yam ādityo na veda yasyā adityaś śarīram" ity-ādi-śrutibhiḥ pratipāditāḥ / madīyās tanava ity ajānann api yo yo yāṃ yāṃ madīyām āditya-ādikāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhaya ārcitum icchati; tasya tasya ajānato 'pi mat-tanu-viṣaya aiṣā śraddha īty anusandhāya tām eva acalāṃ nirvighnāṃ vidadhāmy aham //
sa tayā śraddhayā yuktas tasyārādhanam īhate |
children.translated_text: 'Endowed with that faith, he engages in the worship of that [deity],'

children.text: labhate ca tataḥ kāmān mayaiva vihitān hi tān ||
children.translated_text: 'and from that he obtains his desires, which are indeed ordained by Me alone.' ||

children.text: sa tayā śraddhayā yuktas tasyā arādhanam īhate |
labhate ca tataḥ kāmān maya aiva vihitān hi tān ||

body.text: sa tayā nirvighnayā śraddhayā yuktas tasya indrāder ārādhanaṃ pratīhate / tataḥ mattanubhūtendrādidevatārādhanāt tān eva hi svābhilaṣitān kāmān mayaiva vihitān labhate / yady apy ārādhanakāle, "ārādhyendrādayo madīyās tanavaḥ, tata eva tadarcanaṃ ca madārādhanam" iti na jānāti -- tathāpi tasya vastuno madārādhanatvād ārādhakābhilaṣitam aham eva vidadhāmi //
body.translated_text: He, endowed with that unobstructed faith, engages in the worship of that <s>Indra</s> and the like. From that — from the worship of deities like <s>Indra</s> who are My embodiments — he obtains those very desires of his own wish, which are indeed ordained by Me alone. Even though at the time of worship he does not know that 'the deities being worshipped, <s>Indra</s> and the like, are My embodiments, and therefore their worship too is My worship' — nevertheless, since the thing [being done] is in reality My worship, I alone ordain the desired [fruit] of the worshipper. //

children.text: sa tayā nirvighnayā śraddhayā yuktas tasya indra-āder ārādhanaṃ pratīhate / tataḥ mat-tanu-bhūta-indra-ādi-devatā-ārādhanāt tān eva hi sva-abhilaṣitān kāmān maya aiva vihitān labhate / yady apy ārādhana-kāle, "ārādhya-indra-ādayo madīyās tanavaḥ, tata eva tad-arcanaṃ ca mad-ārādhanam" iti na jānāti --- tatha āpi tasya vastuno mad-ārādhanatvād ārādhaka-abhilaṣitam aham eva vidadhāmi //
antavat tu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tad bhavaty alpamedhasām |
children.translated_text: 'But the fruit of those of small intelligence is finite;'

children.text: devān devayajño yānti madbhaktā yānti mām api ||
children.translated_text: 'the worshippers of the gods go to the gods; My devotees come to Me.' ||

children.text: antavat tu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tad bhavaty alpa-medhasām |
devān deva-yajño yānti mad-bhaktā yānti mām api ||

body.text: teṣām alpamedhasām alpabuddhīnām indrādimātrayājināṃ tadārādhanaphalam alpam, antavac ca bhavati / kutaḥ? devān devayajo yānti -- yata indrādīn devān tadyājino yānti / indrādayo 'pi hi paricchinnabhogāḥ parimitakālavartinaś ca / tatas tatsāyujyaṃ prāptāḥ tais saha pracyavante / madbhaktā api teṣām eva karmaṇāṃ madārādhanarūpatāṃ jñātvā paricchinnaphalasaṅgaṃ tyaktvā matprīṇanaikaprayojanāḥ māṃ prāpnuvanti; na ca punar nivartante / "mām upetya tu kaunteya punar janma na vidyate" iti hi vakṣyate //
body.translated_text: The fruit of worship of <s>Indra</s> and the like for those of small intelligence — of limited understanding — is meager and finite. Why? 'The worshippers of the gods go to the gods' — because those who sacrifice to the gods such as <s>Indra</s> go to <s>Indra</s> and the other gods. For even <s>Indra</s> and the other [gods] have limited enjoyments and exist for a limited time. Therefore, those who have attained union with them fall along with them. But My devotees too — having known those very same actions to be in the form of My worship, having abandoned attachment to limited results, with the sole purpose of pleasing Me — they attain Me; and they never return. For it will be stated: 'Having come to Me, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, there is no rebirth.' //

children.text: teṣām alpa-medhasām alpa-buddhīnām indra-ādi-mātra-yājināṃ tad-ārādhana-phalam alpam, antavac ca bhavati / kutaḥ? devān deva-yajo yānti --- yata indra-ādīn devān tad-yājino yānti / indra-ādayo 'pi hi paricchinna-bhogāḥ parimita-kāla-vartinaś ca / tatas tat-sāyujyaṃ prāptāḥ tais saha pracyavante / mad-bhaktā api teṣām eva karmaṇāṃ mad-ārādhana-rūpatāṃ jñātvā paricchinna-phala-saṅgaṃ tyaktvā mat-prīṇana-eka-prayojanāḥ māṃ prāpnuvanti; na ca punar nivartante / "mām upetya tu kaunteya punar janma na vidyate" iti hi vakṣyate //

body.text: itare tu sarvasamāśrayaṇīyatvāya mama manuṣyādiṣv avatāram apy akiñcitkaraṃ kurvantīty āha --
body.translated_text: But the others render even My incarnation in human and other forms — undertaken for the sake of being accessible to all — ineffective. He says —

children.text: itare tu sarva-samāśrayaṇīyatvāya mama manuṣya-ādiṣv avatāram apy akiñcitkaraṃ kurvanti ity āha ---
avyaktaṃ vyaktim āpannaṃ manyante mām abuddhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The unintelligent think of Me, the unmanifest, as having come into manifestation,'

children.text: paraṃ bhāvam ajānanto mama avyayam anuttamam ||
children.translated_text: 'not knowing My supreme nature, which is imperishable and unsurpassed.' ||

children.text: avyaktaṃ vyaktim āpannaṃ manyante mām abuddhayaḥ |
paraṃ bhāvam ajānanto mama avyayam anuttamam ||

body.text: sarvaiḥ karmabhir ārādhyo 'haṃ sarveśvaro vāṅmanasāparicchedyasvarūpasvabhāvaḥ paramakāruṇyād aśrityavātsalyāc ca sarvasamāśrayaṇīyatvāyājahatsvabhāva eva vasudevasūnur avarīrṇa iti mamaivaṃ paraṃ bhāvam avyayam anuttamam ajānantaḥ prākṛtarājasūnusamānam itaḥ pūrvam anabhivyaktam idānīṃ karmavaśāj janmaviśeṣaṃ prāpya vyaktim āpannam prāptaṃ mām buddhayo manyante / ato māṃ nāśrayante; na karmabhir ārādhayanti ca //
body.translated_text: I — who am to be worshipped by all actions, the Lord of all, whose essential nature and characteristics are beyond the grasp of speech and mind — out of supreme compassion and affection for those who have taken refuge, for the sake of being accessible to all, have descended as the son of <s>Vasudeva</s> without abandoning My own nature. Not knowing this supreme nature of Mine — imperishable and unsurpassed — the unintelligent think of Me as one who was previously unmanifest and who has now, through the force of <s>karma</s>, obtained manifestation by attaining a particular birth, considering Me equal to an ordinary prince. Therefore they do not take refuge in Me, nor do they worship Me through their actions. //

children.text: sarvaiḥ karmabhir ārādhyo 'haṃ sarva-īśvaro vāṅ-manasā-aparicchedya-sva-rūpa-sva-bhāvaḥ parama-kāruṇyād aśritya-vātsalyāc ca sarva-samāśrayaṇīyatvāya ajahat-sva-bhāva eva vasu-deva-sūnur avarīrṇa iti mama evaṃ paraṃ bhāvam avyayam anuttamam ajānantaḥ prākṛta-rāja-sūnu-samānam itaḥ pūrvam anabhivyaktam idānīṃ karma-vaśāj janma-viśeṣaṃ prāpya vyaktim āpannam prāptaṃ mām buddhayo manyante / ato māṃ nā aśrayante; na karmabhir ārādhayanti ca //

body.text: kuta evaṃ na prakāśyata ity atrāha --
body.translated_text: As to why He is not thus revealed, he says —

children.text: kuta evaṃ na prakāśyata ity atrā aha ---
nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I am not manifest to all, veiled by My <s>yogamāyā</s>;'

children.text: mūḍho 'yaṃ nābhijānāti loko mām ajam avyayam ||
children.translated_text: 'this deluded world does not know Me, the unborn and imperishable.' ||

children.text: na ahaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yoga-māyā-samāvṛtaḥ |
mūḍho 'yaṃ na abhijānāti loko mām ajam avyayam ||

body.text: kṣetrajñāsādhāraṇamanuṣyatvādisaṃsthānayogākhyamāyayā samāvṛto 'haṃ na sarvasya prakāśaḥ / mayi manuṣyatvādisaṃsthānadarśanamātreṇa mūḍho 'yaṃ loko mām ativāyvindrakarmāṇam atisūryāgnitejasam upalabhyamānam api ajam avyayaṃ nikhilajagadekakāraṇaṃ sarveśvaraṃ māṃ sarvasamāśrayaṇīyatvāya manuṣyatvasaṃsthānam āsthitaṃ nābhijānāti //
body.translated_text: Veiled by the <s>māyā</s> called <s>yoga</s> — the configuration of a human form and the like, which is unique to the Lord of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) — I am not manifest to all. By merely seeing My configuration as a human and the like, this deluded world — even though perceiving [Me as] one whose deeds surpass those of <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Indra</s>, whose splendor surpasses that of the sun and fire — does not know Me — the unborn, the imperishable, the sole cause of the entire universe, the Lord of all — who has assumed the configuration of a human form for the sake of being accessible to all. //

children.text: kṣetra-jña-asādhāraṇa-manuṣyatva-ādi-saṃsthāna-yoga-ākhya-māyayā samāvṛto 'haṃ na sarvasya prakāśaḥ / mayi manuṣyatva-ādi-saṃsthāna-darśana-mātreṇa mūḍho 'yaṃ loko mām ativāyv-indra-karmāṇam atisūrya-agni-tejasam upalabhyamānam api ajam avyayaṃ nikhila-jagad-eka-kāraṇaṃ sarva-īśvaraṃ māṃ sarva-samāśrayaṇīyatvāya manuṣyatva-saṃsthānam āsthitaṃ na abhijānāti //
vedāhaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna |
children.translated_text: 'I know the past, the present, O <s>Arjuna</s>,'

children.text: bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana ||
children.translated_text: 'and the future beings; but no one knows Me.' ||

children.text: veda ahaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni ca arjuna |
bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana ||

body.text: atītāni vartamānāni anāgatāni ca sarvāṇi bhūtāny ahaṃ veda jānāmi / māṃ tu veda na kaścana mayānusaṃdhīyamāneṣu kālatrayavartiṣu bhūteṣu mām evaṃvidhaṃ vāsudevaṃ sarvasamāśrayṇīyatvāyāvatīrṇaṃ viditvā mām eva samāśrayan na kaścid upalabhyata ityarthaḥ / ato jñānī sudurlabha eva //
body.translated_text: All beings — past, present, and future — I know. But no one knows Me — among the beings of the three times that I contemplate, no one is found who, having known Me, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, of such a nature, who has incarnated for the sake of being accessible to all, takes refuge in Me alone. This is the meaning. Therefore, the <s>jñānī</s> is exceedingly rare indeed. //

children.text: atītāni vartamānāni anāgatāni ca sarvāṇi bhūtāny ahaṃ veda jānāmi / māṃ tu veda na kaścana maya ānusaṃdhīyamāneṣu kāla-traya-vartiṣu bhūteṣu mām evaṃ-vidhaṃ vāsu-devaṃ sarva-samāśrayṇīyatvāya avatīrṇaṃ viditvā mām eva samāśrayan na kaścid upalabhyata ity-arthaḥ / ato jñānī sudurlabha eva //

body.text: tathā hi --
body.translated_text: For thus —

children.text: tathā hi ---
icchādveṣasamutthena dvandvamohena bhārata |
children.translated_text: 'By the delusion of the pairs of opposites arising from desire and aversion, O <s>Bhārata</s>,'

children.text: sarvabhūtāni saṃmohaṃ sarge yānti parantapa ||
children.translated_text: 'all beings fall into delusion at birth, O <s>Parantapa</s>.' ||

children.text: icchā-dveṣa-samutthena dvandva-mohena bhārata |
sarva-bhūtāni saṃmohaṃ sarge yānti paran-tapa ||

body.text: icchādveṣābhyāṃ samutthitena śītoṣṇādidvandvākhyena mohena sarvabhūtāni sarge janmakāla eva saṃmohaṃ yānti / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- guṇamayeṣu sukhaduḥkhādidvandveṣu pūrvapūrvajanmani yadviṣayau icchādveṣau abhyastau, tadvāsanayā punar api janmakāla eva tad eva dvandvākhyam icchādveṣaviṣayatvena samutthitaṃ bhūtānāṃ mohanaṃ bhavati; tena mohena sarvabhūtāni saṃmohaṃ yānti; tadviṣayecchādveṣasvabhāvāni bhavanti, na matsamśleṣaviyogasukhaduḥkhasvabhāvāni, jñānī tu matsaṃśleṣaviyogaikasukhaduḥkhasvabhāvaḥ; na tatsvabhāvaṃ kim api bhūtaṃ jāyate iti //
body.translated_text: By the delusion called the pairs of opposites — cold and heat and the like — arising from desire and aversion, all beings fall into delusion at the very time of birth. What is being said is this: regarding the pairs of opposites consisting of the <s>guṇas</s> — such as pleasure and pain — the desire and aversion whose objects [were determined] in each previous birth, being habitually cultivated, by the force of that latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>), at the very time of birth again, that very pair of opposites, having arisen as the object of desire and aversion, becomes the cause of delusion for beings. By that delusion, all beings fall into confusion — they become of the nature of desire and aversion directed toward those [worldly objects], and not of the nature of [experiencing] happiness and sorrow through union with and separation from Me. But the <s>jñānī</s> is of the nature of [experiencing] happiness and sorrow solely through union with and separation from Me. No being whatsoever is born with such a nature. //

children.text: icchā-dveṣābhyāṃ samutthitena śīta-uṣṇa-ādi-dvandva-ākhyena mohena sarva-bhūtāni sarge janma-kāla eva saṃmohaṃ yānti / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- guṇa-mayeṣu sukha-duḥkha-ādi-dvandveṣu pūrva-pūrva-janmani yad-viṣayau icchā-dveṣau abhyastau, tad-vāsanayā punar api janma-kāla eva tad eva dvandva-ākhyam icchā-dveṣa-viṣayatvena samutthitaṃ bhūtānāṃ mohanaṃ bhavati; tena mohena sarva-bhūtāni saṃmohaṃ yānti; tad-viṣaya-icchā-dveṣa-sva-bhāvāni bhavanti, na mat-samśleṣa-viyoga-sukha-duḥkha-sva-bhāvāni, jñānī tu mat-saṃśleṣa-viyoga-eka-sukha-duḥkha-sva-bhāvaḥ; na tat-sva-bhāvaṃ kim api bhūtaṃ jāyate iti //
yeṣāṃ tv antagataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām |
children.translated_text: 'But those people of meritorious deeds whose sin has come to an end,'

children.text: te dvandvamohanirmuktāḥ bhajante māṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites, they worship Me with firm resolve.' ||

children.text: yeṣāṃ tv anta-gataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇya-karmaṇām |
te dvandva-moha-nirmuktāḥ bhajante māṃ dṛḍha-vratāḥ ||

body.text: yeṣāṃ tv anekajanmārjitenotkṛṣṭapuṇyasaṃcayena guṇamayadvandveccchādveṣahetubhūtaṃ madaunmukhyavirodhi ca anādikālapravṛttaṃ pāpam antagatam kṣīṇam; te pūrvoktena sukṛtatāratamyena māṃ śaraṇam anuprapadya guṇamayān mohād vinirmuktāḥ jarāmaraṇamokṣāya, mahate cāiśvaryāya, matprāptaye ca dṛḍhavratāḥ dṛḍhasaṅkalpāḥ mām eva bhajante //
body.translated_text: But those whose sin — which has been accumulated from beginningless time, which opposes the turning toward Me, and which is the cause of desire and aversion for the pairs of opposites consisting of the <s>guṇas</s> — has come to an end, has been exhausted, through the accumulation of eminent merit earned over many births; they, taking refuge in Me in accordance with the gradation of merit described earlier, freed from delusion caused by the <s>guṇas</s>, worship Me alone with firm resolve — firm determination — for the sake of liberation from old age and death, for great sovereignty, and for the attainment of Me. //

children.text: yeṣāṃ tv aneka-janma-arjitena utkṛṣṭa-puṇya-saṃcayena guṇa-maya-dvandva-iccchā-dveṣa-hetu-bhūtaṃ mad-aunmukhya-virodhi ca anādi-kāla-pravṛttaṃ pāpam anta-gatam kṣīṇam; te pūrva-uktena sukṛta-tāratamyena māṃ śaraṇam anuprapadya guṇa-mayān mohād vinirmuktāḥ jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya, mahate ca aiśvaryāya, mat-prāptaye ca dṛḍha-vratāḥ dṛḍha-saṅkalpāḥ mām eva bhajante //

body.text: atra trayāṇāṃ bhagavantaṃ bhajamānānāṃ jñātavyaviśeṣān upādeyāṃś ca prastauti --
body.translated_text: Here he introduces the specific objects of knowledge and the things to be acquired by the three [types] who worship the Lord —

children.text: atra trayāṇāṃ bhagavantaṃ bhajamānānāṃ jñātavya-viśeṣān upādeyāṃś ca prastauti ---
jarāmaraṇamokṣāya mām āśritya yatanti ye |
children.translated_text: 'Those who, taking refuge in Me, strive for liberation from old age and death —'

children.text: te brahma tad viduḥ kṛtsnam adhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam ||
children.translated_text: 'they know that <s>Brahman</s> in its entirety, the <s>adhyātma</s>, and all <s>karma</s>.' ||

children.text: jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya mām āśritya yatanti ye |
te brahma tad viduḥ kṛtsnam adhyātmaṃ karma ca akhilam ||

body.text: jarāmaraṇamokṣāya prakṛtiviyuktātmasvarūpadarśanāya mām āśritya ye yatante, te tadbrahma viduḥ, adhyātmaṃ tu kṛtsnaṃ viduḥ, karma cākhilaṃ viduḥ //
