body.translated_text: Those who, taking refuge in Me, strive for the vision of the self's true nature separated from <s>Prakṛti</s> — for the sake of liberation from old age and death — they know that <s>Brahman</s>; they know <s>adhyātma</s> in its entirety; and they know <s>karma</s> completely. //

children.text: jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya prakṛti-viyukta-ātma-sva-rūpa-darśanāya mām āśritya ye yatante, te tad-brahma viduḥ, adhyātmaṃ tu kṛtsnaṃ viduḥ, karma ca akhilaṃ viduḥ //
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those who know Me together with <s>adhibhūta</s>, <s>adhidaiva</s>, and <s>adhiyajña</s> —'

children.text: prayāṇakāle 'pi ca māṃ te vidur yuktacetasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'they, with disciplined minds, know Me even at the time of departure.' ||

children.text: sa-adhibhūta-adhidaivaṃ māṃ sa-adhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ |
prayāṇa-kāle 'pi ca māṃ te vidur yukta-cetasaḥ ||

body.text: atra ya iti punar nirdeśāt pūrvanirdiṣṭavyo 'nye adhikāriṇo jñāyante; sādhibhūtaṃ sādhidaivaṃ mām aiśvaryārthino ye viduḥ ity etad anuvādasarūpam apy aprāptārthatvād vidhāyakam eva; tathā sādhiyajñam ity api trayāṇām adhikāriṇām aviśeṣeṇa vidhīyate; arthasvabhāvyāt / trayāṇāṃ hi nityanaimittikarūpamahāyajñādyanuṣṭhānam avarjanīyam / te ca prayāṇakāle 'pi svaprāpyānuguṇaṃ māṃ viduḥ / te ceti cakārāt pūrve jarāmaraṇamokṣāya yatamānāś ca prayāṇakāle vidur iti samuccīyante; anena jñānino 'py arthasvābhāvyāt sādhiyajñaṃ māṃ viduḥ, prayāṇakāle 'pi svaprāpyānuguṇaṃ māṃ vidur ity uktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: Here, from the renewed use of the word 'those who,' persons different from those previously mentioned are understood as being the qualified ones. 'Those who know Me together with <s>adhibhūta</s> and <s>adhidaiva</s>' — [said] regarding those who seek sovereignty — though this has the form of a restatement, it is actually prescriptive since it conveys a not-yet-obtained meaning. Likewise, 'together with <s>adhiyajña</s>' is prescribed without distinction for all three categories of qualified persons, due to the nature of the subject matter. For all three, the performance of the great sacrifices and the like, which are of the nature of obligatory and occasional [rites], is unavoidable. And they know Me at the time of departure in a manner corresponding to their respective objects of attainment. By the word 'and' [in 'they too'], those previously mentioned — those striving for liberation from old age and death — are also included as knowing [Me] at the time of departure. By this, it is also stated that the <s>jñānīs</s> too, due to the nature of the subject matter, know Me together with <s>adhiyajña</s>, and know Me at the time of departure in a manner corresponding to their own object of attainment. //

children.text: atra ya iti punar nirdeśāt pūrva-nirdiṣṭavyo 'nye adhikāriṇo jñāyante; sa-adhibhūtaṃ sa-adhidaivaṃ mām aiśvarya-arthino ye viduḥ ity etad anuvāda-sa-rūpam apy aprāpta-arthatvād vidhāyakam eva; tathā sa-adhiyajñam ity api trayāṇām adhikāriṇām aviśeṣeṇa vidhīyate; artha-sva-bhāvyāt / trayāṇāṃ hi nitya-naimittika-rūpa-mahā-yajña-ādy-anuṣṭhānam avarjanīyam / te ca prayāṇa-kāle 'pi sva-prāpya-anuguṇaṃ māṃ viduḥ / te ca iti ca-kārāt pūrve jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya yatamānāś ca prayāṇa-kāle vidur iti samuccīyante; anena jñānino 'py artha-svābhāvyāt sa-adhiyajñaṃ māṃ viduḥ, prayāṇa-kāle 'pi sva-prāpya-anuguṇaṃ māṃ vidur ity uktaṃ bhavati //

body.text: saptame -- parasya brahmaṇo vāsudevasyopāsyatvam nikhilacetanācetanavastuśeṣitvam, kāraṇatvam, ādhāratvam, sarvaśarīratayā sarvaprakāratvena sarvaśabdavācyatvam, sarvaniyantṛtvam, sarvaiś ca kalyāṇaguṇagaṇais tasyaiva parataratvam, sattvarajastamomayair dehendriyatvena bhogyatvena cāvasthitair bhāvair anādikālapravṛttaduṣkṛtapravāhahetukais tasya tirodhānam, atyutkṛṣṭasukṛtahetukabhagavatprapattyā sukṛtatāratamyena ca pratipattivaiśeṣyād aiśvaryākṣarayāthātmyabhagavatprāptyapekṣayopāsakabhedam, bhagavantaṃ prepsor nityayuktatayaikabhaktitayā cātyarthaparamapuruṣapriyatvena ca śraiṣṭhyam durlabhatvaṃ ca pratipādya eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ jñātavyopādeyabhedāṃś ca prāstauṣīt / idānīm aṣṭame prastutān jñātavyopādeyabhedān vivinakti //
body.translated_text: In the seventh [chapter]: the worthiness of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, to be worshipped; His being the principal of all conscious and non-conscious entities; His being the cause, the support; His being expressible by all words in every manner by virtue of being the inner self of all; His being the controller of all; and His supreme transcendence over all through His host of auspicious qualities — [all this was stated]. Also [stated was]: His concealment by the dispositions of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, which subsist as body, senses, and objects of enjoyment, caused by the stream of sinful deeds accumulated since beginningless time; and the distinction of worshippers — in relation to the attainment of sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), the imperishable self (<s>akṣara</s>), the true nature of the self (<s>yāthātmya</s>), and the attainment of the Lord — according to the grades of their meritorious deeds, [whose devotion is] caused by the supremely excellent meritorious deeds that lead to surrender to the Lord; and the pre-eminence and rarity of one who desires to attain the Lord, by virtue of being perpetually devoted, of single-minded devotion, and of being supremely dear to the Supreme Person. Having established [all this], He introduced the distinctions of what is to be known and what is to be adopted by these three [types of aspirants]. Now, in the eighth [chapter], He distinguishes the objects to be known and adopted that were introduced. ||

children.text: saptame --- parasya brahmaṇo vāsu-devasya upāsyatvam nikhila-cetana-acetana-vastu-śeṣitvam, kāraṇatvam, ādhāratvam, sarva-śarīratayā sarva-prakāratvena sarva-śabda-vācyatvam, sarva-niyantṛtvam, sarvaiś ca kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇais tasya eva parataratvam, sattva-rajas-tamo-mayair deha-indriyatvena bhogyatvena ca avasthitair bhāvair anādi-kāla-pravṛtta-duṣkṛta-pravāha-hetukais tasya tirodhānam, atyutkṛṣṭa-sukṛta-hetuka-bhagavat-prapattyā sukṛta-tāratamyena ca pratipatti-vaiśeṣyād aiśvarya-akṣara-yāthātmya-bhagavat-prāpty-apekṣaya ūpāsaka-bhedam, bhagavantaṃ prepsor nitya-yuktataya aika-bhaktitayā ca atyartha-parama-puruṣa-priyatvena ca śraiṣṭhyam durlabhatvaṃ ca pratipādya eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ jñātavya-upādeya-bhedāṃś ca prāstauṣīt / idānīm aṣṭame prastutān jñātavya-upādeya-bhedān vivinakti //
kiṃ tad brahma kim adhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣottama |
children.translated_text: 'What is that <s>Brahman</s>? What is <s>adhyātma</s>? What is <s>karma</s>, O Supreme Person?' |

children.text: adhibhūtaṃ ca kiṃ proktam adhidaivaṃ kim ucyate ||
children.translated_text: 'And what is declared as <s>adhibhūta</s>? What is called <s>adhidaiva</s>?' ||

children.text: kiṃ tad brahma kim adhyātmaṃ kiṃ karma puruṣa-uttama |
adhibhūtaṃ ca kiṃ proktam adhidaivaṃ kim ucyate ||
adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko 'tra dehe 'smin madhusūdanam |
children.translated_text: 'Who is <s>adhiyajña</s> here, and how, in this body, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>?' |

children.text: prayāṇakāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo 'si niyatātmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'And how are You to be known at the time of departure by those of controlled selves?' ||

children.text: adhiyajñaḥ kathaṃ ko 'tra dehe 'smin madhusūdanam |
prayāṇa-kāle ca kathaṃ jñeyo 'si niyata-ātmabhiḥ ||

body.text: jarāmaraṇamokṣāya bhagavantam āśritya yatamānānāṃ jñātavyatayoktaṃ tad brahma adhyātmaṃ ca kim iti vaktavyam / aiśvaryārthīnāṃ jñātavyam adhibhūtam adhidaivaṃ ca kim? trayāṇāṃ jñātavyo 'dhiyajñaśabdanirdiṣṭaś ca kaḥ? tasya cādhiyajñabhāvaḥ katham? prayāṇakāle ca ebhis tribhir niyatātmabhiḥ kathaṃ jñeyo 'si? //
body.translated_text: That which has been stated as to be known under the designation of <s>Brahman</s> and <s>adhyātma</s> for those who strive having taken refuge in the Lord for liberation from old age and death — what is it? What are <s>adhibhūta</s> and <s>adhidaiva</s> that are to be known by those desiring sovereignty? And who is the one designated by the word <s>adhiyajña</s>, to be known by all three? And how is His nature as <s>adhiyajña</s>? And at the time of departure, how are You to be known by these three who are of controlled selves? ||

children.text: jarā-maraṇa-mokṣāya bhagavantam āśritya yatamānānāṃ jñātavyataya ūktaṃ tad brahma adhyātmaṃ ca kim iti vaktavyam / aiśvarya-arthīnāṃ jñātavyam adhibhūtam adhidaivaṃ ca kim? trayāṇāṃ jñātavyo 'dhiyajña-śabda-nirdiṣṭaś ca kaḥ? tasya ca adhiyajña-bhāvaḥ katham? prayāṇa-kāle ca ebhis tribhir niyata-ātmabhiḥ kathaṃ jñeyo 'si? //
akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ svabhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate |
children.translated_text: 'The supreme imperishable is <s>Brahman</s>; one's own nature is called <s>adhyātma</s>.' |

children.text: bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasaṃjñitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The creative act that brings about the origination of the states of beings is designated as <s>karma</s>.' ||

children.text: akṣaraṃ brahma paramaṃ sva-bhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate |
bhūta-bhāva-udbhava-karo visargaḥ karma-saṃjñitaḥ ||

body.text:
tadbrahmeti nirdiṣṭaṃ paramam akṣaraṃ na kṣaratīty akṣaram, kṣetrajñasamaṣṭirūpam / tathā ca śrutiḥ, "avyaktam akṣare līyate akṣaraṃ tamasi līyate" ityādikā / paramam akṣaraṃ prakṛtivinirmuktam ātmasvarūpam / svabhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate / svabhāvaḥ prakṛtiḥ / anātmabhūtam, ātmani saṃbadhyamānaṃ bhūtasūkṣmatadvāsanādikaṃ pañcāgnividyāyāṃ jñātavyatayoditam / tadubhayaṃ prāpyatayā tyājyatayā ca mumukṣubhir jñātavyam / bhūtabhāvodbhavakaro visargaḥ karmasaṃjñitaḥ / bhūtabhāvaḥ manuṣyādibhāvaḥ; tadudbhavakaro yo visargaḥ, "pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavanti" iti śrutisiddho yoṣitsaṃbandhajaḥ, sa karmasaṃjñitaḥ / tac cākhilaṃ sānubandham udvejanīyatayā, pariharaṇīyatayā ca mumukṣubhir jñātavyam
/ pariharaṇīyatayā cānantaram eva vakṣyate, "yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti" iti //
body.translated_text: That which was designated as 'that <s>Brahman</s>' — is the supreme imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>). '<s>Akṣara</s>' means that which does not perish — it is the collective form of the individual selves (<s>kṣetrajña</s>). Thus also the <s>śruti</s>: 'The unmanifest dissolves into the imperishable, the imperishable dissolves into darkness' — and so on. The supreme imperishable is the essential nature of the self, freed from <s>Prakṛti</s>. 'One's own nature is called <s>adhyātma</s>' — one's own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is <s>Prakṛti</s>. That which is non-self, yet associated with the self — the subtle elements, their impressions, and the like — is stated as to be known in the <s>Pañcāgnividyā</s> (doctrine of the five fires). Both of these are to be known by the seekers of liberation — as what is to be attained and as what is to be abandoned. 'The creative act that brings about the origination of the states of beings is designated as <s>karma</s>' — 'the state of beings' is the state of being human and the like; the creative act (<s>visarga</s>) that brings about their origination, established through the <s>śruti</s> 'at the fifth oblation, the waters become endowed with human speech,' born of the union with a woman — that is designated as <s>karma</s>. And all of that, together with its consequences, is to be known by seekers of liberation as something to be dreaded and to be avoided. That it is to be avoided will be stated immediately after: 'desiring which, they practice celibacy.' ||

children.text:
tad-brahma iti nirdiṣṭaṃ paramam akṣaraṃ na kṣarati ity akṣaram, kṣetra-jña-samaṣṭi-rūpam / tathā ca śrutiḥ, "avyaktam akṣare līyate akṣaraṃ tamasi līyate" ity-ādikā / paramam akṣaraṃ prakṛti-vinirmuktam ātma-sva-rūpam / sva-bhāvo 'dhyātmam ucyate / sva-bhāvaḥ prakṛtiḥ / anātma-bhūtam, ātmani saṃbadhyamānaṃ bhūta-sūkṣma-tad-vāsanā-ādikaṃ pañca-agni-vidyāyāṃ jñātavyataya ūditam / tad-ubhayaṃ prāpyatayā tyājyatayā ca mumukṣubhir jñātavyam / bhūta-bhāva-udbhava-karo visargaḥ karma-saṃjñitaḥ / bhūta-bhāvaḥ manuṣya-ādi-bhāvaḥ; tad-udbhava-karo yo visargaḥ, "pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣa-vacaso bhavanti" iti śruti-siddho yoṣit-saṃbandha-jaḥ, sa karma-saṃjñitaḥ / tac ca akhilaṃ sa-anubandham udvejanīyatayā, pariharaṇīyatayā ca mumukṣubhir jñātavyam
/ pariharaṇīyatayā ca anantaram eva vakṣyate, "yad icchanto brahma-caryaṃ caranti" iti //
adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaś cādhidaivatam |
children.translated_text: 'The perishable state is <s>adhibhūta</s>, and the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) is <s>adhidaiva</s>.' |

children.text: adhiyajño 'ham evātra dehe dehabhṛtāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: 'I alone am <s>adhiyajña</s> here in this body, O best of embodied beings.' ||

children.text: adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ puruṣaś ca adhidaivatam |
adhiyajño 'ham eva atra dehe deha-bhṛtāṃ vara ||

body.text:
aiśvaryārthināṃ jñātavyatayā nirdiṣṭam adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ viyadādibhūteṣu vartamānaḥ tatpariṇāmaviśeṣaḥ kṣaraṇasvabhāvo vilakṣaṇaḥ śabdasparśādis sāsrayaḥ / vilakṣaṇāḥ sāśrayāś śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ aiśvaryārthibhiḥ prāpyās tair anusandheyāḥ / puruṣaś cādhidaivatam adhidaivataśabdanirdiṣṭaḥ puruṣaḥ adhidaivatam devatopari vartamānaḥ, indraprajāpatiprabhṛtikṛtsnadaivatopari vartamānaḥ, indraprajāpatiprabhṛtīnāṃ bhogyajātad vilakṣaṇaśabdāder bhoktā puruṣaḥ / sā ca bhoktṛtvāvasthā aiśvaryārthibhiḥ prāpyatayānusandheyā / adhiyajño 'ham eva / adhiyajñaḥ yajñair ārādhyatayā vartamānaḥ / atra indrādau mama dehabhūte ātmatayāvasthito 'ham eva yajñair ārādhya iti
mahāyajñādinityanaimittikānuṣṭhānavelāyāṃ trayāṇām adhikāriṇām anusandheyam etat //
body.translated_text: That which was designated as <s>adhibhūta</s>, to be known by those desiring sovereignty — is the perishable state: the distinctive transformations of the elements beginning with ether, whose nature is to perish — the distinctive [objects] such as sound, touch, and the like, together with their substrata. The distinctive [sense-objects] — sound, touch, form, taste, and smell — together with their substrata, are to be attained by those desiring sovereignty and thus to be contemplated by them. 'And the person is <s>adhidaiva</s>' — the <s>puruṣa</s> designated by the word <s>adhidaiva</s> is the one who presides over the deities — one who exists above <s>Indra</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and all other deities; the <s>puruṣa</s> who is the enjoyer of the category of objects of enjoyment — sound and the like — that is different from [those enjoyed by] <s>Indra</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the like. And that state of being an enjoyer is to be contemplated by those desiring sovereignty as something to be attained. 'I alone am <s>adhiyajña</s>' — <s>adhiyajña</s> is the one who exists as the object of propitiation through sacrifices. Here, in <s>Indra</s> and the like who are My bodies, I alone, established as their inner self, am the one to be propitiated through sacrifices — this is to be contemplated by all three classes of qualified aspirants at the time of performing the regular and occasional acts beginning with the great sacrifices. ||

children.text:
aiśvarya-arthināṃ jñātavyatayā nirdiṣṭam adhibhūtaṃ kṣaro bhāvaḥ viyad-ādi-bhūteṣu vartamānaḥ tat-pariṇāma-viśeṣaḥ kṣaraṇa-sva-bhāvo vilakṣaṇaḥ śabda-sparśa-ādis sa-āsrayaḥ / vilakṣaṇāḥ sa-āśrayāś śabda-sparśa-rūpa-rasa-gandhāḥ aiśvarya-arthibhiḥ prāpyās tair anusandheyāḥ / puruṣaś ca adhidaivatam adhidaivata-śabda-nirdiṣṭaḥ puruṣaḥ adhidaivatam devata ūpari vartamānaḥ, indra-prajā-pati-prabhṛti-kṛtsna-daivata ūpari vartamānaḥ, indra-prajā-pati-prabhṛtīnāṃ bhogya-jātad vilakṣaṇa-śabda-āder bhoktā puruṣaḥ / sā ca bhoktṛtva-avasthā aiśvarya-arthibhiḥ prāpyataya ānusandheyā / adhiyajño 'ham eva / adhiyajñaḥ yajñair ārādhyatayā vartamānaḥ / atra indra-ādau mama deha-bhūte ātmataya āvasthito 'ham eva yajñair ārādhya iti
mahā-yajña-ādi-nitya-naimittika-anuṣṭhāna-velāyāṃ trayāṇām adhikāriṇām anusandheyam etat //
antakāle ca mām eva smaran muktvā kalebaram |
children.translated_text: 'And at the end of life, remembering Me alone, leaving the body,' |

children.text: yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'he who departs attains My state — there is no doubt about this.' ||

children.text: anta-kāle ca mām eva smaran muktvā kalebaram |
yaḥ prayāti sa mad-bhāvaṃ yāti na asty atra saṃśayaḥ ||

body.text: idam api trayāṇāṃ sādhāraṇam / antakāle ca mām eva smaran kalevaraṃ tyaktvā yaḥ prayāti, sa madbhāvaṃ yāti mama yo bhāvaḥ svabhāvaḥ taṃ yāti; tadānīṃ yathā mām anusandhatte, tathāvidhākāro bhavatītyarthaḥ; yathā ādibharatādayas tadānīṃ smaryamāṇamṛgasajātīyākārāt saṃbhūtāḥ //
body.translated_text: This too is common to all three [types of aspirants]. At the end of life, remembering Me alone, having left the body, he who departs — he attains My state: he attains My nature (<s>bhāva</s>), My essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). Whatever form he contemplates Me in at that time, he becomes of that very form — this is the meaning. Just as <s>Ādibharata</s> and others were born in the form similar to the deer they were remembering at that time. ||

children.text: idam api trayāṇāṃ sādhāraṇam / anta-kāle ca mām eva smaran kalevaraṃ tyaktvā yaḥ prayāti, sa mad-bhāvaṃ yāti mama yo bhāvaḥ sva-bhāvaḥ taṃ yāti; tadānīṃ yathā mām anusandhatte, tathā-vidha-ākāro bhavati ity-arthaḥ; yathā ādi-bharata-ādayas tadānīṃ smaryamāṇa-mṛga-sajātīya-ākārāt saṃbhūtāḥ //

body.text: smartus svaviṣayasajātīyākāratāpādanam antyapratyayasya svabhāva iti suspaṣṭam āha --
body.translated_text: That the last cognition naturally brings about a form similar to its own object in the one who remembers — this he states very clearly:

children.text: smartus sva-viṣaya-sajātīya-ākāratā-āpādanam antya-pratyayasya sva-bhāva iti suspaṣṭam āha ---
yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaran bhāvaṃ tyajaty ante kalebaram |
children.translated_text: 'Whatever state one remembers when leaving the body at the end,' |

children.text: taṃ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'that very state one attains, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, being always absorbed in that state.' ||

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ va āpi smaran bhāvaṃ tyajaty ante kalebaram |
taṃ tam eva eti kaunteya sadā tad-bhāva-bhāvitaḥ ||

body.text: ante antakāle yaṃ yaṃ vāpi bhāvaṃ smaran kalebaraṃ tyajati, taṃ taṃ bhāvam eva maraṇānantaram eti / antimapratyayaś ca pūrvabhāvitaviṣaya eva jāyate //
body.translated_text: At the end — at the time of death — whatever state one remembers while leaving the body, that very state one attains after death. And the last cognition arises only regarding an object that was previously cultivated. ||

children.text: ante anta-kāle yaṃ yaṃ va āpi bhāvaṃ smaran kalebaraṃ tyajati, taṃ taṃ bhāvam eva maraṇa-anantaram eti / antima-pratyayaś ca pūrva-bhāvita-viṣaya eva jāyate //
tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu mām anusmara yudhya ca |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight.' |

children.text: mayy arpitamanobuddhiḥ mām evaiṣyasy asaṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'With mind and intellect offered to Me, you shall come to Me alone, without doubt.' ||

children.text: tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu mām anusmara yudhya ca |
mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ mām eva eṣyasy asaṃśayaḥ ||

body.text: yasmāt pūrvakālābhyastaviṣaya evāntyapratyayo jāyate, tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣv āprayāṇād ahar ahar mām anusmara / aharahar anusmṛtikaraṃ yuddhādikaṃ varṇāśramānubandhi śrutismṛticoditaṃ nityanaimittikaṃ ca karma kuru / evam upāyena mayy arpitamanobuddhiḥ antakale ca mām eva smaran yathābhilaṣitaprakāraṃ māṃ prāpsyasi; nātra saṃśayaḥ //
body.translated_text: Since the last cognition arises only regarding an object practiced during the previous period, therefore at all times — every day until the time of departure — remember Me. Perform battle and the like — the regular and occasional actions enjoined by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, associated with one's <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s> — which are conducive to daily remembrance. By this method, with mind and intellect offered to Me, and remembering Me alone at the end of life, you shall attain Me in the form you desire — there is no doubt about this. ||

children.text: yasmāt pūrva-kāla-abhyasta-viṣaya eva antya-pratyayo jāyate, tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣv āprayāṇād ahar ahar mām anusmara / ahar-ahar anusmṛti-karaṃ yuddha-ādikaṃ varṇa-āśrama-anubandhi śruti-smṛti-coditaṃ nitya-naimittikaṃ ca karma kuru / evam upāyena mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ anta-kale ca mām eva smaran yathā-abhilaṣita-prakāraṃ māṃ prāpsyasi; na atra saṃśayaḥ //

body.text: evaṃ sāmānyena svaprāpyāvāptir antyapratyayādhīnety uktvā tadarthaṃ trayāṇām upāsanaprakārabhedaṃ vaktum upakramate; tatrāiśvaryārthinām upāsanaprakāraṃ yathopāsanam antyapratyayaprakāraṃ cāha --
body.translated_text: Having thus stated in general that the attainment of one's desired goal depends on the last cognition, He begins to state the specific modes of contemplation for the three [types of aspirants]. Here He states the mode of contemplation and the mode of the last cognition for those desiring sovereignty:

children.text: evaṃ sāmānyena sva-prāpya-avāptir antya-pratyaya-adhīna īty uktvā tad-arthaṃ trayāṇām upāsana-prakāra-bhedaṃ vaktum upakramate; tatra aiśvarya-arthinām upāsana-prakāraṃ yathā-upāsanam antya-pratyaya-prakāraṃ cā aha ---
abhyāsayogayuktena cetasā nānyagāminā |
children.translated_text: 'With mind made steadfast by the practice of <s>yoga</s>, not wandering elsewhere,' |

children.text: paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ yāti pārthānucintayan ||
children.translated_text: 'one goes to the supreme divine Person, O <s>Pārtha</s>, by meditating [on Him].' ||

children.text: abhyāsa-yoga-yuktena cetasā na anya-gāminā |
paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ yāti pārtha anucintayan ||

body.text: aharahar abhyāsayogābhyāṃ yuktatayā nānyagāminā cetasā antakāle paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ māṃ vakṣyamāṇaprakāraṃ cintayan mām eva yāti -- ādibharatamṛgatvaprāptivad aiśvaryaviśiṣṭatayā matsamānākāro bhavati / abhyāsaḥ nityanaimittikāviruddheṣu sarveṣu kāleṣu manasopāsyasaṃśīlanam / yogas tu aharahar yogakāle 'nuṣṭhīyamānaṃ yathoktalakṣaṇam upāsanam //
body.translated_text: With a mind that does not wander elsewhere, made steadfast through daily practice and <s>yoga</s>, at the time of death, meditating on the supreme divine Person — Me — in the manner to be described, one goes to Me alone — just as <s>Ādibharata</s> attained the state of a deer, so [one attains] a form similar to Mine, endowed with sovereignty. Practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) is the habitual cultivation through the mind of the object of contemplation at all times not conflicting with the regular and occasional rites. <s>Yoga</s>, however, is the contemplation of the described characteristics, performed during the daily time of <s>yoga</s> practice. ||

children.text: ahar-ahar abhyāsa-yogābhyāṃ yuktatayā na anya-gāminā cetasā anta-kāle paramaṃ puruṣaṃ divyaṃ māṃ vakṣyamāṇa-prakāraṃ cintayan mām eva yāti --- ādi-bharata-mṛgatva-prāptivad aiśvarya-viśiṣṭatayā mat-samāna-ākāro bhavati / abhyāsaḥ nitya-naimittika-aviruddheṣu sarveṣu kāleṣu manasa ūpāsya-saṃśīlanam / yogas tu ahar-ahar yoga-kāle 'nuṣṭhīyamānaṃ yathā-ukta-lakṣaṇam upāsanam //
kaviṃ purāṇam anuśāsitāram aṇor aṇīyāṃsam anusmared yaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The omniscient, the ancient, the ruler, subtler than the subtle — he who meditates [on Him],' |

children.text: sarvasya dhātāram acintyarūpam ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt ||
children.translated_text: 'the sustainer of all, of inconceivable form, sun-colored, beyond darkness,' ||

children.text: kaviṃ purāṇam anuśāsitāram aṇor aṇīyāṃsam anusmared yaḥ |
sarvasya dhātāram acintya-rūpam āditya-varṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt ||
prayāṇakāle manasācalena bhaktyā yukto yogabalena caiva |
children.translated_text: 'at the time of departure, with an unmoving mind, endowed with devotion and the power of <s>yoga</s>,' |

children.text: bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya samyak sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣam upaiti divyam ||
children.translated_text: 'having properly placed the vital breath between the eyebrows — he attains that supreme divine Person.' ||

children.text: prayāṇa-kāle manasa ācalena bhaktyā yukto yoga-balena ca eva |
bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya samyak sa taṃ paraṃ puruṣam upaiti divyam ||

body.text: kaviṃ sarvajñan purāṇam purātanam anuśāsitāram viśvasya praśāsitāram aṇor aṇīyāṃsam jīvād api sūkṣmataram, sarvasya dhātāram sarvasya sraṣṭāram, acintyarūpam sakaletaravisajātīyasvarūpam, ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastād aprākṛtasvāsādhāraṇadivyarūpam, tam evaṃbhūtam aharahar abhyasyamānabhaktiyuktayogabalena ārūḍhasaṃskāratayā acalena manasā prayāṇakāle bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya saṃsthāpya tatra bhūmadhye divyaṃ puruṣaṃ yo 'nusmaret; sa tam evopaiti -- tadbhāvaṃ yāti, tatsamānāiśvaryo bhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The omniscient (<s>kavi</s>); the ancient (<s>purāṇa</s>) — existing from the beginning; the ruler (<s>anuśāsitṛ</s>) — the governor of the universe; subtler than the subtle — more subtle even than the individual self (<s>jīva</s>); the sustainer (<s>dhātṛ</s>) of all — the creator of all; of inconceivable form — whose essential nature is entirely different from everything else; sun-colored, beyond darkness — of a divine form that is non-material, uniquely His own. He who, through the power of <s>yoga</s> endowed with devotion cultivated day after day — having attained an established disposition by that means — with an unmoving mind at the time of departure, having placed and established the vital breath between the eyebrows, meditates there, between the brows, on the divine Person of such a nature — he attains Him alone, he attains His state: he becomes endowed with sovereignty equal to His — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: kaviṃ sarva-jñan purāṇam purātanam anuśāsitāram viśvasya praśāsitāram aṇor aṇīyāṃsam jīvād api sūkṣmataram, sarvasya dhātāram sarvasya sraṣṭāram, acintya-rūpam sakala-itara-visajātīya-sva-rūpam, āditya-varṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastād aprākṛta-sva-asādhāraṇa-divya-rūpam, tam evaṃ-bhūtam ahar-ahar abhyasyamāna-bhakti-yukta-yoga-balena ārūḍha-saṃskāratayā acalena manasā prayāṇa-kāle bhruvor madhye prāṇam āveśya saṃsthāpya tatra bhū-madhye divyaṃ puruṣaṃ yo 'nusmaret; sa tam eva upaiti --- tad-bhāvaṃ yāti, tat-samāna-aiśvaryo bhavati ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: atha kaivalyārthināṃ smaraṇ aprakāram āha --
body.translated_text: Now He states the mode of contemplation for those desiring <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation as the isolated self):

children.text: atha kaivalya-arthināṃ smaraṇ a-prakāram āha ---
yad akṣaraṃ vedavido vadanti viśanti yad yatayo vītarāgāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'That which the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s> call the imperishable, which the ascetics free from passion enter,' |

children.text: yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa pravakṣye ||
children.translated_text: 'desiring which they practice celibacy — that goal I shall declare to you in brief.' ||

children.text: yad akṣaraṃ veda-vido vadanti viśanti yad yatayo vīta-rāgāḥ |
yad icchanto brahma-caryaṃ caranti tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa pravakṣye ||

body.text: yad akṣaram asthūlatvādiguṇakaṃ vedavido vadanti, vītarāgāś ca yatayo yad akṣaraṃ viśanti, yad akṣaraṃ prāptum icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti, tat padaṃ saṃgraheṇa te pravakṣye / padyate gamyate cetaseti padam; tan nikhilavedāntavedyaṃ matsvarūpam akṣaraṃ yathā upāsyam, tathā saṃkṣepeṇa pravakṣyāmītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: That imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) which the knowers of the <s>Vedas</s> speak of as having the qualities of being non-gross and the like; which the ascetics free from passion enter; desiring which imperishable [state] they practice celibacy — that goal I shall declare to you in brief. Goal (<s>pada</s>) means that which is reached or known by the mind. That [goal], which is My own essential nature — the imperishable knowable through all <s>Vedānta</s> — I shall briefly state in what manner it is to be contemplated — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: yad akṣaram asthūlatva-ādi-guṇakaṃ veda-vido vadanti, vīta-rāgāś ca yatayo yad akṣaraṃ viśanti, yad akṣaraṃ prāptum icchanto brahma-caryaṃ caranti, tat padaṃ saṃgraheṇa te pravakṣye / padyate gamyate cetasa īti padam; tan nikhila-veda-anta-vedyaṃ mat-sva-rūpam akṣaraṃ yathā upāsyam, tathā saṃkṣepeṇa pravakṣyāmi ity-arthaḥ //
sarvadvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca |
children.translated_text: 'Having restrained all the gates [of the senses], confining the mind in the heart,' |

children.text: mūrdhny ādhāyātmanaḥ prāṇam āsthito yogadhāraṇām ||
children.translated_text: 'having placed one's own vital breath in the head, established in <s>yoga</s>-concentration,' ||

children.text: sarva-dvārāṇi saṃyamya mano hṛdi nirudhya ca |
mūrdhny ādhāyā atmanaḥ prāṇam āsthito yoga-dhāraṇām ||
om ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran |
children.translated_text: 'uttering the single syllable <s>Om</s> that is <s>Brahman</s>, remembering Me,' |

children.text: yaḥ prayāti tyajan dehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: 'he who departs, leaving the body — he goes to the supreme goal.' ||

children.text: om ity eka-akṣaraṃ brahma vyāharan mām anusmaran |
yaḥ prayāti tyajan dehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||

body.text: sarvāṇi śrotrādīnīndriyāṇi jñānadvārabhūtāni saṃyamya svavyāpārebhyo vinivartya, hṛdayakamalaniviṣṭe mayy akṣare mano nirudhya, yogākhyāṃ dhāraṇām āsthitaḥ mayy eva niścalāṃ sthitim āsthitaḥ, om ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma madvācakaṃ vyāharan, vācyaṃ mām anusmaran, ātmanaḥ prāṇaṃ mūrdhny ādhāya dehaṃ tyajan yaḥ prayāti -- sa yāti paramāṃ gatiṃ prakṛtiviyuktaṃ matsamānākāram apunarāvṛttim ātmānaṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ / "yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati // avyakto 'kṣara ity uktas tam āhuḥ paramāṃ gatim // ity anantaram eva vakṣyate //
body.translated_text: Having restrained all the sense-organs such as hearing and the like, which are the gates of knowledge, from their respective activities; having confined the mind upon Me, the imperishable, who is seated in the lotus of the heart; having been established in the concentration called <s>yoga</s> — an unwavering abiding in Me alone; uttering the single syllable <s>Om</s> that is <s>Brahman</s>, which designates Me; remembering Me who am designated [by it]; having placed the vital breath in the head — he who departs leaving the body — he goes to the supreme goal: he attains the self that is freed from <s>Prakṛti</s>, of a form similar to Mine, from which there is no return — this is the meaning. 'He who is that [self] in all beings, who does not perish when they perish — the unmanifest, called the imperishable — Him they call the supreme goal' — this will be stated immediately after. ||

children.text: sarvāṇi śrotra-ādīni indriyāṇi jñāna-dvāra-bhūtāni saṃyamya sva-vyāpārebhyo vinivartya, hṛdaya-kamala-niviṣṭe mayy akṣare mano nirudhya, yoga-ākhyāṃ dhāraṇām āsthitaḥ mayy eva niścalāṃ sthitim āsthitaḥ, om ity eka-akṣaraṃ brahma mad-vācakaṃ vyāharan, vācyaṃ mām anusmaran, ātmanaḥ prāṇaṃ mūrdhny ādhāya dehaṃ tyajan yaḥ prayāti --- sa yāti paramāṃ gatiṃ prakṛti-viyuktaṃ mat-samāna-ākāram apunar-āvṛttim ātmānaṃ prāpnoti ity-arthaḥ / "yaḥ sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati // avyakto 'kṣara ity uktas tam āhuḥ paramāṃ gatim // ity anantaram eva vakṣyate //

body.text: evam aiśvaryārthinaḥ kaivalyārthinaś ca svaprāpyānuguṇaṃ bhagavadupāsanaprakāra uktaḥ; atha jñānino bhagavadupāsanaprakāraṃ prāptiprakāraṃ cāha --
body.translated_text: Thus the mode of contemplation for those desiring sovereignty and those desiring <s>kaivalya</s>, corresponding to what they seek to attain, has been stated. Now He states the mode of contemplation and the mode of attainment for the <s>jñānin</s> (the knower):

children.text: evam aiśvarya-arthinaḥ kaivalya-arthinaś ca sva-prāpya-anuguṇaṃ bhagavad-upāsana-prakāra uktaḥ; atha jñānino bhagavad-upāsana-prakāraṃ prāpti-prakāraṃ cā aha ---
ananyacetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He who, with mind on nothing else, constantly remembers Me at all times,' |

children.text: tasyāhaṃ sulabhaḥ pārtha nityayuktasya yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'for that ever-devoted <s>yogin</s>, I am easy to attain, O <s>Pārtha</s>.' ||

children.text: ananya-cetāḥ satataṃ yo māṃ smarati nityaśaḥ |
tasya ahaṃ sulabhaḥ pārtha nitya-yuktasya yoginaḥ ||

body.text: nityaśaḥ mām udyogaprabhṛti satataṃ sarvakālam ananyacetāḥ yaḥ smarati atyarthamatpriyatvena matsmṛtyā vinā ātmadhāraṇam alabhamāno niratiśayapriyāṃ smṛtiṃ yaḥ karoti; tasya nityayuktasya nityayogaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇasya yoginaḥ ahaṃ sulabhaḥ aham eva prāpyaḥ; na madbhāva aiśvaryādikaḥ suprāpaś ca / tadviyogam asahamāno 'ham eva taṃ vṛṇe / "yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ" iti hi śrūyate / matprāptyanuguṇopāsanavipākaṃ tadvirodhinirasanam atyarthamatpriyatvādikaṃ cāham eva dadāmītyarthaḥ / vakṣyate ca "teṣāṃ satatayuktānāṃ bhajatāṃ prītipūrvakam / dadāmi buddhiyogaṃ taṃ yena mām upāyānti te // teṣām evānukampārtham aham ajñānajaṃ tamaḥ / nāśayāmy ātmabhāvastho jñānadīpena bhāsvatā // iti //
body.translated_text: He who constantly — at all times from the commencement of his effort onward — with mind on nothing else, remembers Me — who, because of his extreme love for Me, being unable to sustain himself without remembrance of Me, engages in remembrance that is supremely dear; for that ever-devoted [<s>yogin</s>] — who yearns for perpetual union — I am easy to attain: I alone am what is to be attained, not My state of sovereignty and the like. And I am easy to attain. Unable to bear separation from him, I Myself choose him. 'Whomever He chooses, by him He is attained' — thus it is heard in <s>śruti</s>. The contemplation conducive to attaining Me, the removal of obstacles to it, and the extreme love for Me and the like — all this I Myself grant — this is the meaning. And it will be stated: 'To those who are constantly devoted, who worship with love — I give that <s>buddhiyoga</s> (yoga of understanding) by which they come to Me. Out of compassion for them alone, I, abiding in their hearts, destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.' ||

children.text: nityaśaḥ mām udyoga-prabhṛti satataṃ sarva-kālam ananya-cetāḥ yaḥ smarati atyartha-mat-priyatvena mat-smṛtyā vinā ātma-dhāraṇam alabhamāno niratiśaya-priyāṃ smṛtiṃ yaḥ karoti; tasya nitya-yuktasya nitya-yogaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇasya yoginaḥ ahaṃ sulabhaḥ aham eva prāpyaḥ; na mad-bhāva aiśvarya-ādikaḥ suprāpaś ca / tad-viyogam asahamāno 'ham eva taṃ vṛṇe / "yam eva eṣa vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ" iti hi śrūyate / mat-prāpty-anuguṇa-upāsana-vipākaṃ tad-virodhi-nirasanam atyartha-mat-priyatva-ādikaṃ ca aham eva dadāmi ity-arthaḥ / vakṣyate ca "teṣāṃ satata-yuktānāṃ bhajatāṃ prīti-pūrvakam / dadāmi buddhi-yogaṃ taṃ yena mām upāyānti te // teṣām eva anukampā-artham aham ajñāna-jaṃ tamaḥ / nā aśayāmy ātma-bhāva-stho jñāna-dīpena bhāsvatā // iti //

body.text: ataḥ param adhyāyaśeṣeṇa jñāninaḥ kaivalyārthinaś cāpunarāvṛttim aiśvaryārthinaḥ punarāvṛttiṃ cāha --
body.translated_text: After this, in the remainder of the chapter, He states the non-return of the <s>jñānin</s> and of the one desiring <s>kaivalya</s>, and the return of the one desiring sovereignty:

children.text: ataḥ param adhyāya-śeṣeṇa jñāninaḥ kaivalya-arthinaś ca apunar-āvṛttim aiśvarya-arthinaḥ punar-āvṛttiṃ cā aha ---
mām upetya punarjanma duḥkhālayam aśāśvatam |
children.translated_text: 'Having attained Me, the great souls who have reached the supreme perfection' |

children.text: nāpnuvanti mahātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'do not obtain rebirth, which is the abode of suffering and is impermanent.' ||

children.text: mām upetya punar-janma duḥkha-ālayam aśāśvatam |
nā apnuvanti mahā-ātmānaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ gatāḥ ||

body.text:
ye manuṣyādicaturmukhāntānāṃ matsaṅkalpakṛtāhorātravyavasthāvido janāḥ, te brahmaṇaś caturmukhasya yad ahaḥ tac caturyugasahasrāvasānaṃ viduḥ, rātriṃ ca tathārūpām / tatra brahmaṇo 'harāgamasamaye trailokyāntarvartinyo dehendriyabhogyabhogasthānarūpā vyaktaś caturmukhadehāvasthād avyaktāt prabhavanti / tatraiva avyaktāvasthāviśeṣe caturmukhadehe rātryāgamasamaye pralīyante / sa evāyaṃ karmavaśyo bhūtagrāmo 'harāgame bhūtvā bhutvā rātryāgame pralīyate / punar apy aharāgame prabhavati / tathā varṣatāvasānarūpayugasahasrānte brahmalokaparyantā lokāḥ brahmā ca, "pṛthivyapsu pralīyate āpastejasi līyante" ityādikrameṇa avyaktākṣaratamaḥparyantaṃ mayy eva pralīyante / evaṃ madvyatiriktasya kṛtsnasya kālavyavasthayā matta utpatteḥ mayi
pralayāc cotpattivināśayogitvam avarjanīyam ity aiśvaryagatiṃ prāptānāṃ punarāvṛttir aparihāryā / mām upetānāṃ tu na punarāvṛttiprasaṅgaḥ //

body.text:
tasmād avyaktād acetanaprakṛtirūpāt puruṣārthatayā paraḥ utkṛṣṭo bhāvo 'nyo jñānaikākāratayā tasmād visajātīyaḥ, avyaktaḥ kenacit pramāṇena na vyajyata ity avyaktaḥ, svasaṃvedyasvāsādhāraṇākāra ityarthaḥ; sanātanaḥ utpattivināśānarhatayā nityaḥ yaḥ sarveṣu viyadādibhūteṣu sakāraṇeṣu sakāryeṣu vinaśyatsu tatra tatra sthito 'pi na vinaśyati; saḥ avyakto 'kṣara ityuktaḥ, "ye tv akṣaram anirdeśyam avyaktaṃ paryupāsate", "kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate" ityādiṣu -- taṃ vedavidaḥ paramāṃ gatim āhuḥ / ayam eva, "yaḥ prayāti tyajan dehaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim" ity atra paramagatiśabdanirdiṣṭo 'kṣaraḥ prakṛtisaṃsargaviyuktasvasvarūpeṇāvasthita ātmetyarthaḥ / yam evaṃbhūtaṃ svarūpeṇāvasthitaṃ prāpya na nivartante; tan mama paramaṃ
dhāma paraṃ niyamanasthānam / acetanaprakṛtir ekaṃ niyamanasthānam; tatsaṃsṛṣṭarūpā jīvaprakṛtir dvitīyaṃ niyamanasthānam / acitsaṃsargaviyuktaṃ svarūeṇāvathitaṃ muktasvarūpaṃ paramaṃ niyamanasthānam ityarthaḥ / tac cāpunarāvṛttirūpam / atha vā prakāśavācī dhāmaśabdaḥ; prakāśaḥ ceha jñānam abhipretam; prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭāt parichinnajñānarūpād ātmano 'paricchinnajñānarūpatayā muktasvarūpaṃ paraṃ dhāma //

dhāma paraṃ niyamana-sthānam / acetana-prakṛtir ekaṃ niyamana-sthānam; tat-saṃsṛṣṭa-rūpā jīva-prakṛtir dvitīyaṃ niyamana-sthānam / acit-saṃsarga-viyuktaṃ sva-rūeṇa avathitaṃ mukta-sva-rūpaṃ paramaṃ niyamana-sthānam ity-arthaḥ / tac ca apunar-āvṛtti-rūpam / atha vā prakāśa-vācī dhāma-śabdaḥ; prakāśaḥ ca iha jñānam abhipretam; prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭāt parichinna-jñāna-rūpād ātmano 'paricchinna-jñāna-rūpatayā mukta-sva-rūpaṃ paraṃ dhāma //

athātmayāthātmyaviduḥ paramapuruṣaniṣṭasya ca sādharaṇīm arcirādikāṃ gatim āha -- dvayor apy arcirādikā gatiḥ śrutau śrutā / sā cāpunarāvṛttilakṣaṇā / yathā pañcāgnividyāyām, "tad ya itthaṃ vidur ye ceme 'raṇye śraddhā tapa ity upāsate, te 'rciṣam abhisaṃbhavanty arciṣo 'haḥ" ityādau / arcirādikayā gatasya parabrahmaprāptir apunarāvṛttiś cāmnātā, "sa enān brahma gamayati etena pratipadyamānā imaṃ mānavam āvartaṃ nāvartante" iti / na ca prajāpativākyādau śrutaparavidyāṅgabhūtātmaprāptiviṣayeyam, "tad ya itthaṃ viduḥ" iti gatiśrtuiḥ, "ye ceme 'raṇye śraddhā tapa ity upāsate" iti paravidyāyāḥ pṛthakchrutivaiyārthyāt / pañcāgnividyāyāṃ ca, "iti tu pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣavacaso bhavanti" iti, "ramaṇīyacaraṇāḥ ... kapūyacaraṇāḥ"
iti puṇyapāpahetuko manuṣyādibhāvo 'pām eva bhūtāntarasaṃsṛṣṭānām, ātmanas tu tatpariṣvaṅgamātram iti cidacitor vivekam abhidhāya, "tad ya itthaṃ viduḥ ,,, te 'rciṣam asaṃbhavanti ... imaṃ mānavam āvartaṃ nāvartante" iti vivikte cidacidvastunī tyājyatayā prāpyatayā ca ya itthaṃ viduḥ te 'rcirādinā gacchanti, na ca punar āvartanta ity uktam iti gamyate / ātmayāthātmyavidaḥ paramapuruṣaniṣṭhasya ca "sa enān brahma gamayati" iti brahmaprāptivacanād acidviyuktam ātmavastu brahmātmakatayā brahmaśeṣataikarasam ity anusandheyam; tatkratunyāyāc ca / paraśeṣataikarasatvaṃ ca "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ... yasyātmā śarīram" ityādiśrutisiddham /

athā atma-yāthātmya-viduḥ parama-puruṣa-niṣṭasya ca sādharaṇīm arcira-ādikāṃ gatim āha --- dvayor apy arcira-ādikā gatiḥ śrutau śrutā / sā ca apunar-āvṛtti-lakṣaṇā / yathā pañca-agni-vidyāyām, "tad ya itthaṃ vidur ye ca ime 'raṇye śraddhā tapa ity upāsate, te 'rciṣam abhisaṃbhavanty arciṣo 'haḥ" ity-ādau / arcira-adikayā gatasya para-brahma-prāptir apunar-āvṛttiś cā amnātā, "sa enān brahma gamayati etena pratipadyamānā imaṃ mānavam āvartaṃ nā avartante" iti / na ca prajāpati-vākya-ādau śruta-para-vidyā-aṅga-bhūta-ātma-prāpti-viṣaya īyam, "tad ya itthaṃ viduḥ" iti gati-śrtuiḥ, "ye ca ime 'raṇye śraddhā tapa ity upāsate" iti para-vidyāyāḥ pṛthak-chruti-vaiyārthyāt / pañca-agni-vidyāyāṃ ca, "iti tu pañcamyām āhutāv āpaḥ puruṣa-vacaso bhavanti" iti, "ramaṇīya-caraṇāḥ ... kapūya-caraṇāḥ"

body.text:
rājavidyā vidyānāṃ rājā, rājaguhyaṃ guhyānāṃ rājā / rājñāṃ vidyeti vā rājavidyā / rājāno hi vistīrṇāgādhyamanasaḥ / mahāmanasām iyaṃ vidyetyarthaḥ / mahāmanasa eva hi gopanīyagopanakuśalā iti teṣām eva guhyam / idam uttamaṃ pavitraṃ matprāptivirodhyaśeṣakalmaṣāpaham / pratyakṣāvagamam / avagamyata ity avagamaḥ -- viṣayaḥ; pratyakṣabhūto 'vagamaḥ viṣayo yasya jñānasya tat pratyakṣāvagamam / bhaktirūpeṇopāsanenopāsyamāno 'haṃ tādānīm evopāsituḥ pratyakṣatām upagato bhavāmītyarthaḥ / athāpi dharmyaṃ dharmād anapetam / dharmatvaṃ hi niśśreyasasādhanatvam / svarūpeṇaivātyarthapriyatvena tadānīm eva maddarśanāpādanatayā ca svayaṃ niśśreyasarūpam api niratiśayaniśśreyasarūpātyantikamatprāptisādhanam ityarthaḥ
/ ata eva susukhaṃ kartuṃ susukhopādānam / atyarthapriyatvenopādeyam / avyayam akṣayam; matprāptiṃ sādhayitvā+api svayaṃ na kṣīyate / evaṃrūpam upāsanaṃ kurvato matpradāne kṛte 'pi kiṃcit kṛtaṃ mayā+asyeti me pratibhātītyarthaḥ //

na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni paśya me yogam aiśvaram |
bhūta-bhṛn na ca bhūta-stho mamā atmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ ||

body.text: idaṃ cetanācetanātmakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagad avyaktamūrtinā aprakāśitasvarūpeṇa mayā antaryāmiṇā, tatam asya jagato dhāraṇārthaṃ niyamanārthaṃ ca śeṣitvena vyāptam ityarthaḥ / yathāntaryāmibrāhmaṇe, "yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan ... yaṃ pṛthivī na veda", "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ... yam ātmā na veda" iti cetanācetanavastujātair adṛṣṭeṇāntaryāmiṇā tatra tatra vyāptir uktā / tato matsthāni sarvabhūtāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni mayy antaryāmiṇi sthitāni / tatraiva brāhmaṇe, "yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ ... yaḥ pṛthivīm antaro yamayati, yasyātmā śarīraṃ ... ya ātmānam antaro yamayati" iti śarīratvena niyāmyatvapratipādanāt tadāyatte sthitiniyamane pratipādite; śeṣitvaṃ ca / na cāhaṃ teṣv avasthitaḥ -- ahaṃ tu na tadāyattasthitiḥ; matsthitau tair na kaścid upakāra ityathaḥ / na ca matsthāni bhūtāni -- na ghaṭādīnāṃ jalāder iva mama dhārakatvam / katham? matsaṅkalpena / paśya mamāiśvaraṃ yogam anyatra kutracid asaṃbhāvanīyaṃ madasādhāraṇam āścaryaṃ yogaṃ paśya / ko 'sau yoga? bhūtabhṛn na ca bhūtastho mamātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ / sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhartāham; na ca taiḥ kaścid api mamopakāraḥ / mamātmaiva bhūtabhāvanaḥ -- mama manomayas saṅkalpa eva bhūtānāṃ bhāvayitā dhārayitā niyantā ca //

children.text: idaṃ cetana-acetana-ātmakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā aprakāśita-sva-rūpeṇa mayā antaryāmiṇā, tatam asya jagato dhāraṇa-arthaṃ niyamana-arthaṃ ca śeṣitvena vyāptam ity-arthaḥ / yatha āntaryāmi-brāhmaṇe, "yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan ... yaṃ pṛthivī na veda", "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ... yam ātmā na veda" iti cetana-acetana-vastu-jātair adṛṣṭeṇa antaryāmiṇā tatra tatra vyāptir uktā / tato mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni mayy antaryāmiṇi sthitāni / tatra eva brāhmaṇe, "yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ ... yaḥ pṛthivīm antaro yamayati, yasyā atmā śarīraṃ ... ya ātmānam antaro yamayati" iti śarīratvena niyāmyatva-pratipādanāt tad-āyatte sthiti-niyamane pratipādite; śeṣitvaṃ ca / na ca ahaṃ teṣv avasthitaḥ --- ahaṃ tu na tad-āyatta-sthitiḥ; mat-sthitau tair na kaścid upakāra ity-athaḥ / na ca mat-sthāni bhūtāni --- na ghaṭa-ādīnāṃ jala-āder iva mama dhārakatvam / katham? mat-saṅkalpena / paśya mama aiśvaraṃ yogam anyatra kutracid asaṃbhāvanīyaṃ mad-asādhāraṇam āścaryaṃ yogaṃ paśya / ko 'sau yoga? bhūta-bhṛn na ca bhūta-stho mamā atmā bhūta-bhāvanaḥ / sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ bharta āham; na ca taiḥ kaścid api mama upakāraḥ / mama-ātma aiva bhūta-bhāvanaḥ --- mama mano-mayas saṅkalpa eva bhūtānāṃ bhāvayitā dhārayitā niyantā ca //

body.text: sarvasyāsya svasaṅkalpāyattasthitipravṛttitve nidarśanam āha --

children.text: sarvasya asya sva-saṅkalpa-āyatta-sthiti-pravṛttitve nidarśanam āha ---
yathā+ākāśasthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatrago mahān |
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni matsthānīty upadhāraya ||
yathā+ākāśa-sthito nityaṃ vāyuḥ sarvatra-go mahān |
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni mat-sthāni ity upadhāraya ||

body.text: yathā ākaśe anālambane mahān vayuḥ sthitaḥ sarvatra gacchati; sa tu vāyur nirālambano madāyattasthitir ity avaśyābhyupagamanīyaḥ -- evam eva sarvāṇi bhūtāni tair adṛṣṭe mayi sthitāni mayaiva dhṛtānīty upadhāraya / yathā+āhur vedavidaḥ, "meghodayaḥ sāgarasannivṛttir indor vibhāgaḥ sphuritāni vāyoḥ / vidyudvibhaṅgo gatir uṣṇaraśmer viṣṇor vicitrāḥ prabhavanti māyāḥ" iti viṣṇor ananyasādhāraṇāni mahāścaryāṇītyarthaḥ / śrutir api, "etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryācandramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ", "bhīṣā+asmād vātaḥ pavate,bhīṣodeti sūryaḥ, bhīṣā+asmād agniś cendraś ca" ityādikā //

children.text: yathā ākaśe anālambane mahān vayuḥ sthitaḥ sarvatra gacchati; sa tu vāyur nirālambano mad-āyatta-sthitir ity avaśya-abhyupagamanīyaḥ --- evam eva sarvāṇi bhūtāni tair adṛṣṭe mayi sthitāni maya aiva dhṛtāni ity upadhāraya / yathā+āhur veda-vidaḥ, "megha-udayaḥ sāgara-sannivṛttir indor vibhāgaḥ sphuritāni vāyoḥ / vidyud-vibhaṅgo gatir uṣṇa-raśmer viṣṇor vicitrāḥ prabhavanti māyāḥ" iti viṣṇor ananya-sādhāraṇāni mahā-āścaryāṇi ity-arthaḥ / śrutir api, "etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryā-candra-masau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhataḥ", "bhīṣā+asmād vātaḥ pavate,bhīṣa ūdeti sūryaḥ, bhīṣā+asmād agniś ca indraś ca" ity-ādikā //

hetunā+anena kaunteya jagad dhi parivartate ||

hetunā+anena kaunteya jagad dhi parivartate ||

body.text: tasmāt kṣetrajñakarmānuguṇaṃ madīyā prakṛtiḥ satyasaṅkalpena mayā+adhyakṣeṇekṣitā sacarācaraṃ jagat sūyate / anena kṣetrajñakarmānuguṇamadīkṣaṇena hetunā jagat parivartata iti matsvāmyaṃ satyasaṅkalpatvaṃ nairghṛṇyādidoṣarahitatvam ity evam ādikaṃ mama vasudevasūnor aiśvaraṃ yogaṃ paśya / yathā+āha śrutiḥ, "asmān māyī sṛjate viśvam etat tasmiṃś cānyo māyayā sanniruddhaḥ / māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyān māyinaṃ tu mheśvaram // iti //

children.text: tasmāt kṣetra-jña-karma-anuguṇaṃ madīyā prakṛtiḥ satya-saṅkalpena mayā+adhyakṣeṇā ikṣitā sacara-acaraṃ jagat sūyate / anena kṣetra-jña-karma-anuguṇa-mad-īkṣaṇena hetunā jagat parivartata iti mat-svāmyaṃ satya-saṅkalpatvaṃ nairghṛṇya-ādi-doṣa-rahitatvam ity evam ādikaṃ mama vasu-deva-sūnor aiśvaraṃ yogaṃ paśya / yathā+āha śrutiḥ, "asmān māyī sṛjate viśvam etat tasmiṃś ca anyo māyayā sanniruddhaḥ / māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyān māyinaṃ tu mhā-īśvaram // iti //

body.text: evaṃ māṃ bhūtamaheśvaraṃ sarvajñaṃ satyasaṅkalpaṃ nikhilajagadekakāraṇaṃ paramakāruṇikatayā sarvasamāśrayaṇīyatvāya mānuṣīṃ tanum āśritaṃ svakṛtaiḥ pāpakarmabhir mūḍhā avajānanti prākṛtamanuṣyasamaṃ manyante / bhūtamaheśvarasya mamāpārakāruṇyodāryasauśīlyavātsalyanibandhanaṃ manuṣyatvasamāśrayaṇalakṣaṇam imaṃ paraṃ bhāvam ajānanto manuṣyatvasamāśrayaṇamātreṇa mām itarasajātīyaṃ matvā tiraskurvantītyarthaḥ //

body.text: mama manuṣyatve paramakāruṇyādiparatvatirodhānakarīṃ rākṣasīm āsurīṃ ca mohinīṃ prakṛtim āśritāḥ, moghāśāḥ moghvāñ chitāḥ niṣphalavāñ chitāḥ, moghkarmāṇaḥ moghārambhāḥ, moghajñānāḥ sarveṣu madīyeṣu carācareṣv artheṣu viparītajñānatayā niṣphalajñānāḥ, vicetasaḥ tathā sarvatra vigatayāthātmyajñānāḥ māṃ sarveśvaram itarasamaṃ matvā mayi ca yat kartum icchanti, yad uddiśyārambhān kurvate, tat sarvaṃ moghaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ //

children.text: mama manuṣyatve parama-kāruṇya-ādi-paratva-tirodhāna-karīṃ rākṣasīm āsurīṃ ca mohinīṃ prakṛtim āśritāḥ, mogha-āśāḥ moghvāñ chitāḥ niṣphalavāñ chitāḥ, mogh-karmāṇaḥ mogha-ārambhāḥ, mogha-jñānāḥ sarveṣu madīyeṣu cara-acareṣv artheṣu viparīta-jñānatayā niṣphala-jñānāḥ, vicetasaḥ tathā sarvatra vigata-yāthātmya-jñānāḥ māṃ sarva-īśvaram itara-samaṃ matvā mayi ca yat kartum icchanti, yad uddiśyā arambhān kurvate, tat sarvaṃ moghaṃ bhavati ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: ye tu svakṛtaiḥ puṇyasañcayaiḥ māṃ śaraṇam upagamya vidhvastasamastapāpabandhā daivīṃ prakṛtim āśritā mahātmānaḥ, te, bhūtādim avyayam vāṅmanasāgocaranāmakarmasvarūpaṃ paramakāruṇikatayā sādhuparitrāṇāya manuṣyatvenāvatīrṇaṃ māṃ jñātvā+ananyamanaso māṃ bhajante; matpriyatvātirekeṇa madbhajanena vinā manasaś cātmanaś ca bāhyakaraṇānāṃ ca dhāraṇam alabhamānā madbhajanaikaprayojanā bhajante //
