body.text: atyarthamatpriyatvena matkīrtanayatananamaskārair vinā kṣaṇāṇumātre 'py ātmadhāraṇam alabhamānāḥ, madguṇaviśeṣavācīni mannāmāni smṛtvā pulakāñcitasarvāṅgāḥ harṣagadgadakaṇṭhāḥ, nārāyaṇakṛṣṇavāsedevety evam ādīni satataṃ kīrtayantaḥ, tathaiva yatantaḥ matkarmasv arcanādikeṣu, tadupakāreṣu bhavananandanavanakaraṇādikeṣu ca dṛḍhasaṅkalpā yatamānāḥ, bhaktibhārāvanamitamanobuddhyabhimānapadadvayakaradvayaśirobhir aṣṭāṅgair acintitapāṃsukardamaśarkarādike dharātale daṇḍavat praṇipatantaḥ, satataṃ māṃ nityayuktāḥ nityayogaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇā ātmāntaṃ maddāsyavyavasāyinaḥ upāsate //

children.text: atyartha-mat-priyatvena mat-kīrtana-yatana-namaskārair vinā kṣaṇa-aṇu-mātre 'py ātma-dhāraṇam alabhamānāḥ, mad-guṇa-viśeṣa-vācīni man-nāmāni smṛtvā pulaka-añcita-sarva-aṅgāḥ harṣa-gadgada-kaṇṭhāḥ, nārāyaṇa-kṛṣṇa-vāsedeva ity evam ādīni satataṃ kīrtayantaḥ, tatha aiva yatantaḥ mat-karmasv arcana-ādikeṣu, tad-upakāreṣu bhavana-nandana-vana-karaṇa-ādikeṣu ca dṛḍha-saṅkalpā yatamānāḥ, bhakti-bhāra-avanamita-mano-buddhy-abhimāna-pada-dvaya-kara-dvaya-śirobhir aṣṭa-aṅgair acintita-pāṃsu-kardama-śarkarā-ādike dharā-tale daṇḍavat praṇipatantaḥ, satataṃ māṃ nitya-yuktāḥ nitya-yogaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇā ātma-antaṃ mad-dāsya-vyavasāyinaḥ upāsate //
jñānayajñena cāpy anye yajanto mām upāsate |
ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvatomukham ||
jñāna-yajñena ca apy anye yajanto mām upāsate |
ekatvena pṛthaktvena bahudhā viśvato-mukham ||

body.text: anye 'pi mahātmanaḥ pūrvoktaiḥ kīrtanādibhir jñānākhyena yajñena ca yajanto mām upāsate / katham? bahudhā pṛthaktvena jagadākāreṇa, viśvatomukham viśvaprakāram avasthitaṃ mām ekatvenopāsate / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- bhagavān vāsudeva eva nāmarūpavibhāgānarhātisūkṣmacidacidvastuśarīras san satyasaṅkalpo vividhavibhaktanāmarūpasthūlacidacidvastuśarīraḥ syām iti saṃkalpya sa eka eva devatiryaṅmanuṣyasthāvarākhyavicitrajagaccharīro 'vatiṣṭhata ity anusaṃdadhānāś ca mām upāsate iti //
body.translated_text: Other great souls (<s>mahātmanas</s>) also, worshiping Me through <s>kīrtana</s> (glorification) and other [devotional acts] mentioned earlier, and through the sacrifice called knowledge (<s>jñānayajña</s>), meditate upon Me. How? As manifold (<s>bahudhā</s>), i.e., in differentiated form, as having the form of the universe (<s>jagadākāra</s>), facing everywhere (<s>viśvatomukha</s>), present in every mode — they worship Me as One. What is stated is this: the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vāsudeva</s> alone, having as His body the subtle conscious and non-conscious entities that are too subtle to admit of the differentiation of name and form, being of true will (<s>satyasaṅkalpa</s>), willed 'Let Me become [one] having as My body the gross conscious and non-conscious entities differentiated by manifold distinct names and forms'; and He alone, the One, abides having as His body the variegated universe known as gods, animals, humans, and stationary beings — those who meditate thus also worship Me. //

children.text: anye 'pi mahā-ātmanaḥ pūrva-uktaiḥ kīrtana-ādibhir jñāna-ākhyena yajñena ca yajanto mām upāsate / katham? bahudhā pṛthaktvena jagad-ākāreṇa, viśvato-mukham viśva-prakāram avasthitaṃ mām ekatvena upāsate / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- bhagavān vāsu-deva eva nāma-rūpa-vibhāga-anarha-atisūkṣma-cid-acid-vastu-śarīras san satya-saṅkalpo vividha-vibhakta-nāma-rūpa-sthūla-cid-acid-vastu-śarīraḥ syām iti saṃkalpya sa eka eva deva-tiryaṅ-manuṣya-sthāvara-ākhya-vicitra-jagac-charīro 'vatiṣṭhata ity anusaṃdadhānāś ca mām upāsate iti //

body.text: tathā hi viśvaśarīro 'ham evāvasthita ity āha --
body.translated_text: Accordingly, [the Lord] says that He alone abides as having the universe as His body —

children.text: tathā hi viśva-śarīro 'ham eva avasthita ity āha ---
ahaṃ kratur ahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhā+aham aham auṣadham |
children.translated_text: I am the ritual (<s>kratu</s>); I am the sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>); I am the offering to the ancestors (<s>svadhā</s>); I am the herb (<s>auṣadha</s>);

children.text: mantro 'ham aham evājyam aham agnir ahaṃ hutam ||
children.translated_text: I am the mantra; I Myself am the clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>); I am the fire; I am the oblation (<s>huta</s>). ||

children.text: ahaṃ kratur ahaṃ yajñaḥ svadhā+aham aham auṣadham |
mantro 'ham aham evā ajyam aham agnir ahaṃ hutam ||

body.text: ahaṃ kratuḥ ahaṃ jyotiṣṭomādikaḥ kratuḥ; aham eva mahāyajñaḥ; aham eva pitṛgaṇapuṣṭidā svadhā; auṣadhaṃ haviś cāham eva; aham eva ca mantraḥ; aham eva ca ājyam / pradarśanārtham idam somādikaṃ ca havir aham evetyarthaḥ; aham āhavanīyādiko 'gniḥ; homaś cāham eva //
body.translated_text: I am the <s>kratu</s> — I am the sacrificial ritual such as the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like; I alone am the great sacrifice (<s>mahāyajña</s>); I alone am <s>svadhā</s>, which nourishes the host of ancestors; and the herb, i.e., the oblation material (<s>havis</s>), is also Me alone; the mantra too is Me alone; the clarified butter (<s>ājya</s>) too is Me alone. This is illustrative — the meaning is that the oblation material such as <s>Soma</s> and the like is also Me alone; I am the <s>Āhavanīya</s> and other sacred fires; and the act of oblation (<s>homa</s>) too is Me alone. //

children.text: ahaṃ kratuḥ ahaṃ jyotiṣṭoma-ādikaḥ kratuḥ; aham eva mahā-yajñaḥ; aham eva pitṛ-gaṇa-puṣṭi-dā svadhā; auṣadhaṃ haviś ca aham eva; aham eva ca mantraḥ; aham eva ca ājyam / pradarśana-artham idam soma-ādikaṃ ca havir aham eva ity-arthaḥ; aham āhavanīya-ādiko 'gniḥ; homaś ca aham eva //
pitā+aham asya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ |
children.translated_text: I am the father of this universe, the mother, the sustainer, and the grandfather;

children.text: vedyaṃ pavitram oṅkāra ṛk sāma yajur eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the object of knowledge, the purifier, the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>, and the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Yajur</s> [<s>Vedas</s>]. ||

children.text: pitā+aham asya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ |
vedyaṃ pavitram oṅ-kāra ṛk sāma yajur eva ca ||

body.text: asya sthāvarajaṅgamātmakasya jagataḥ, tatra tatra pitṛtvena, mātṛtvena, dhātṛtvena, pitāmahatvena ca vartamāno 'ham eva / atra dhātṛśabdo mātāpitṛvyatirikte utpattiprayojake cetanaviśeṣe vartate / yat kiñcid vedavedyaṃ pavitram pāvanam,tad aham eva / vedakaś ca vedabījabhūtaḥ praṇavo 'ham eva / ṛksāmayajurātmako vedaś cāham eva //
body.translated_text: Of this universe consisting of the stationary and the moving, I alone am present here and there as the father, as the mother, as the sustainer (<s>dhātṛ</s>), and as the grandfather. Here the word <s>dhātṛ</s> refers to a particular conscious agent who brings about birth, other than the mother and father. Whatever is to be known through the <s>Vedas</s>, and whatever is purifying (<s>pāvana</s>) — that is Me alone. The <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>), which is the seed of the <s>Vedas</s> and their indicator, is also Me alone. And the <s>Vedas</s> in the form of <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Yajur</s> are also Me alone. //

children.text: asya sthāvara-jaṅgama-ātmakasya jagataḥ, tatra tatra pitṛtvena, mātṛtvena, dhātṛtvena, pitā-mahatvena ca vartamāno 'ham eva / atra dhātṛ-śabdo mātā-pitṛ-vyatirikte utpatti-prayojake cetana-viśeṣe vartate / yat kiñcid veda-vedyaṃ pavitram pāvanam,tad aham eva / vedakaś ca veda-bīja-bhūtaḥ praṇavo 'ham eva / ṛk-sāma-yajur-ātmako vedaś ca aham eva //
gatir bhartā prabhus sākṣī nivāsaś śaraṇaṃ suhṛt |
children.translated_text: The goal, the sustainer, the Lord, the witness, the abode, the refuge, the friend;

children.text: prabhavapralayasthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījam avyayam ||
children.translated_text: the origin, dissolution, and resting-place; the treasure-house and the imperishable seed. ||

children.text: gatir bhartā prabhus sākṣī nivāsaś śaraṇaṃ suhṛt |
prabhava-pralaya-sthānaṃ nidhānaṃ bījam avyayam ||

body.text: gamyata iti gatiḥ; tatra tatra prāpyasthānam ityarthaḥ; bhartā dhārayitā, prabhuḥ śāsitā, sākṣī sākṣāddṛṣṭā, nivāsaḥ vāsasthānaṃ veśmādi / śaraṇam / iṣṭasya prāpakatayā+aniṣṭasya nivāraṇatayā ca samāśrayaṇīyaś cetanaḥ śaraṇam / sa cāham eva; sukṛd dhitaiṣī, prabhavapralayasthānam yasya kasyacid yatra kutracid utpattipralayayor yat sthānam, tad aham eva / nidhānaṃ nidhīyata iti nidhānam, utpādyam upasaṃhāryaṃ cāham evetyarthaḥ; avyayaṃ bījam tatra tatra vyayarahitaṃ yat kāraṇam, tad aham eva //
body.translated_text: That which is reached is <s>gati</s> (goal) — the meaning is: the destination to be attained here and there. The sustainer (<s>bhartā</s>) is the upholder; the Lord (<s>prabhu</s>) is the ruler; the witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) is the one who sees directly; the abode (<s>nivāsa</s>) is the dwelling-place, such as a house and the like. Refuge (<s>śaraṇa</s>) — the conscious being who is to be resorted to as the one who procures what is desired and wards off what is undesired — that is refuge; and that too is Me alone. The friend (<s>suhṛd</s>) is the well-wisher. The origin-and-dissolution-place (<s>prabhavapralayasthāna</s>) — whatever is the locus of origination and dissolution for anything anywhere, that is Me alone. The treasure-house (<s>nidhāna</s>) — that which is stored up, i.e., that which is to be produced and that which is to be withdrawn — that too is Me alone, is the meaning. The imperishable seed (<s>avyayaṃ bījam</s>) — whatever cause is free from decay here and there, that is Me alone. //

children.text: gamyata iti gatiḥ; tatra tatra prāpya-sthānam ity-arthaḥ; bhartā dhārayitā, prabhuḥ śāsitā, sākṣī sākṣād-dṛṣṭā, nivāsaḥ vāsa-sthānaṃ veśma-ādi / śaraṇam / iṣṭasya prāpakatayā+aniṣṭasya nivāraṇatayā ca samāśrayaṇīyaś cetanaḥ śaraṇam / sa ca aham eva; sukṛd dhita eṣī, prabhava-pralaya-sthānam yasya kasyacid yatra kutracid utpatti-pralayayor yat sthānam, tad aham eva / nidhānaṃ nidhīyata iti nidhānam, utpādyam upasaṃhāryaṃ ca aham eva ity-arthaḥ; avyayaṃ bījam tatra tatra vyaya-rahitaṃ yat kāraṇam, tad aham eva //
tapāmy aham ahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmy ity utsṛjyāmi ca |
children.translated_text: I give heat; I withhold and release the rain;

children.text: amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuś ca sad asac cāham arjuna ||
children.translated_text: I am immortality and also death; I am being and non-being, O <s>Arjuna</s>. ||

children.text: tapāmy aham ahaṃ varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmy ity utsṛjyāmi ca |
amṛtaṃ ca eva mṛtyuś ca sad asac ca aham arjuna ||

body.text: agnyādityādirūpeṇāham eva tapāmi; grīṣmādāv aham eva varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmi / tathā varṣāsu cāham evotsṛjāmi / amṛtaṃ caiva mṛtyuś ca / yena jīvati loko yena ca mriyate, tadubhayam aham eva / kim atra bahunoktena; sadasac cāham eva / sad yad vartate, asad yad atītam anāgataṃ ca sarvāvasthāvasthitacidacidvastuśarīratayā tat tat prakāro 'ham evāvasthita ityarthaḥ / evaṃ bahudhā pṛthaktvena vibhaktanāmarūpāvasthitakṛtsnajagaccharīratayā tatprakāro 'ham evāvasthita ity ekatvajñānenānanusaṃdadhānāś ca mām upāsate //
body.translated_text: In the form of fire, the sun, and the like, I alone give heat. In summer and the like, I alone withhold the rain. And in the rainy season, I alone release it. I am immortality and also death — that by which the world lives and that by which it dies, both are Me alone. Why say more? Being and non-being too are Me alone. 'Being' (<s>sat</s>) is that which exists [in the present]; 'non-being' (<s>asat</s>) is that which is past and that which is yet to come — the meaning is that I alone abide as having all those modes, by having as My body all conscious and non-conscious entities established in all states. Thus, by having as My body the entire universe established in manifold differentiated names and forms, I alone abide as having those modes — and those who meditate with the knowledge of [this] oneness also worship Me. //

children.text: agny-āditya-ādi-rūpeṇa aham eva tapāmi; grīṣma-ādāv aham eva varṣaṃ nigṛhṇāmi / tathā varṣāsu ca aham eva utsṛjāmi / amṛtaṃ ca eva mṛtyuś ca / yena jīvati loko yena ca mriyate, tad-ubhayam aham eva / kim atra bahuna ūktena; sad-asac ca aham eva / sad yad vartate, asad yad atītam anāgataṃ ca sarva-avasthā-avasthita-cid-acid-vastu-śarīratayā tat tat prakāro 'ham eva avasthita ity-arthaḥ / evaṃ bahudhā pṛthaktvena vibhakta-nāma-rūpa-avasthita-kṛtsna-jagac-charīratayā tat-prakāro 'ham eva avasthita ity ekatva-jñānena ananusaṃdadhānāś ca mām upāsate //

body.text: evaṃ mahātmanāṃ jñānināṃ bhagavadanubhavaikabhogānāṃ vṛttam uktvā teṣām eva viśeṣaṃ darśayitum ajñānāṃ kāmakāmānāṃ vṛttam āha --
body.translated_text: Having described the conduct of the great-souled knowers (<s>jñānins</s>), whose sole enjoyment is the experience of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, [the Lord] now sets forth the conduct of the ignorant, who are driven by desires for [worldly] objects, in order to show the distinction [between them] —

children.text: evaṃ mahā-ātmanāṃ jñānināṃ bhagavad-anubhava-eka-bhogānāṃ vṛttam uktvā teṣām eva viśeṣaṃ darśayitum ajñānāṃ kāma-kāmānāṃ vṛttam āha ---
traividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpāḥ yajñair iṣṭvā svargatiṃ prārthayante |
children.translated_text: The followers of the three <s>Vedas</s>, drinkers of <s>Soma</s>, purified of sins, worshiping through sacrifices, pray for passage to heaven;

children.text: te puṇyam āsādya surendralokam aśnanti divyān divi devabhogān ||
children.translated_text: they, attaining the meritorious world of <s>Indra</s>, enjoy in heaven the divine pleasures of the gods. ||

children.text: traividyā māṃ soma-pāḥ pūta-pāpāḥ yajñair iṣṭvā svar-gatiṃ prārthayante |
te puṇyam āsādya sura-indra-lokam aśnanti divyān divi deva-bhogān ||
te taṃ bhuktvā svargalokaṃ viśālaṃ kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṃ viśanti |
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed that vast heavenly world, when their merit is exhausted, they enter the mortal world;

children.text: evaṃ trayīdharmam anuprapannāḥ gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā labhante ||
children.translated_text: thus, those who follow the threefold <s>Vedic</s> law, desiring objects of desire, obtain going and returning. ||

children.text: te taṃ bhuktvā svarga-lokaṃ viśālaṃ kṣīṇe puṇye martya-lokaṃ viśanti |
evaṃ trayī-dharmam anuprapannāḥ gata-agataṃ kāma-kāmā labhante ||

body.text:
ṛgyajussāmarūpās tisro vidyāḥ trividyam; kevalaṃ trividyaniṣṭhās traividyāḥ, na tu trayyantaniṣṭhāḥ / trayyantaniṣṭhā hi mahātmanaḥ pūrvoktaprakāreṇa nikhilavedavedyaṃ mām eva jñātvā+atimātramadbhaktikāritakīrtanādibhir jñānayajñena ca madekaprāpyā mām evopāsate / traividyās tu vedapratipādyakevalendrādiyāgaśiṣṭasomān pibantaḥ, pūtapāpāḥ svargādiprāptivirodhipāpāt pūtāḥ, taiḥ kevalendrādidevatyatayā+anusaṃhitair yajñair vastutas tadrūpaṃ mām iṣṭvā, tathāvasthitaṃ mām ajānantaḥ svargagatiṃ prārthayante / te puṇyam duḥkhāsaṃbhinnaṃ surendralokaṃ prāpya tatra tatra divyān devabhogān aśnanti / te taṃ viśālaṃ svargalokaṃ bhuktvā tadanubhavahetubhūte puṇye kṣīṇe punar api martyalokaṃ viśanti / evaṃ
trayyantasiddhajñānavidhurāḥ kāmyasvargādikāmāḥ kevalaṃ trayīdharmam anuprapannāḥ gatāgataṃ labhante alpāsthirasvargādīn anubhūya punaḥ punar nivartanta ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The three <s>Vidyās</s> (branches of knowledge) have the form of <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāma</s>; <s>Trividya</s> means the three <s>Vidyās</s>; those who are devoted solely to the three <s>Vidyās</s> are <s>traividyas</s> — but not those devoted to the culmination of the three [<s>Vedas</s>] (i.e., <s>Vedānta</s>). For those devoted to the culmination of the three [<s>Vedas</s>] are the great souls (<s>mahātmanas</s>) who, knowing Me alone as the one to be known by all the <s>Vedas</s> in the manner described above, worship Me alone — who alone am to be attained — through <s>kīrtana</s> and other [devotional acts] prompted by their overwhelming devotion to Me, and through the sacrifice of knowledge. But the <s>traividyas</s>, drinking the <s>Soma</s> remaining from sacrifices directed merely to <s>Indra</s> and other deities as prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s>, purified of sins — i.e., purified from sins that obstruct the attainment of heaven and the like — having worshiped Me through those sacrifices directed merely to <s>Indra</s> and other deities, but not knowing Me as thus constituted, pray for passage to heaven. They, attaining the meritorious world of <s>Indra</s>, unmixed with suffering, enjoy there the divine pleasures of the gods. Having enjoyed that vast heavenly world, when the merit that was the cause of that enjoyment is exhausted, they again enter the mortal world. Thus, devoid of the knowledge established at the culmination of the three [<s>Vedas</s>], desiring objects such as heaven and the like, following merely the threefold <s>Vedic</s> law, they obtain going and returning — meaning that having experienced heaven and the like, which are meager and impermanent, they return again and again. //

children.text:
ṛg-yajus-sāma-rūpās tisro vidyāḥ tri-vidyam; kevalaṃ tri-vidya-niṣṭhās traividyāḥ, na tu trayy-anta-niṣṭhāḥ / trayy-anta-niṣṭhā hi mahā-ātmanaḥ pūrva-ukta-prakāreṇa nikhila-veda-vedyaṃ mām eva jñātvā+atimātra-mad-bhakti-kārita-kīrtana-ādibhir jñāna-yajñena ca mad-eka-prāpyā mām eva upāsate / traividyās tu veda-pratipādya-kevala-indra-ādi-yāga-śiṣṭa-somān pibantaḥ, pūta-pāpāḥ svarga-ādi-prāpti-virodhi-pāpāt pūtāḥ, taiḥ kevala-indra-ādi-devatyatayā+anusaṃhitair yajñair vastutas tad-rūpaṃ mām iṣṭvā, tathā-avasthitaṃ mām ajānantaḥ svarga-gatiṃ prārthayante / te puṇyam duḥkha-asaṃbhinnaṃ sura-indra-lokaṃ prāpya tatra tatra divyān deva-bhogān aśnanti / te taṃ viśālaṃ svarga-lokaṃ bhuktvā tad-anubhava-hetu-bhūte puṇye kṣīṇe punar api martya-lokaṃ viśanti / evaṃ
trayy-anta-siddha-jñāna-vidhurāḥ kāmya-svarga-ādi-kāmāḥ kevalaṃ trayī-dharmam anuprapannāḥ gata-agataṃ labhante alpa-asthira-svarga-ādīn anubhūya punaḥ punar nivartanta ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: mahātmanas tu niratiśayapriyarūpamaccintanaṃ kṛtvā mām anavadhikātiśayānandaṃ prāpyana punar āvartanta iti teṣāṃ viśeṣaṃ darśayati --
body.translated_text: But the great souls, having directed their thought to Me — who am of unsurpassably dear form — attain Me, who am of limitless, unsurpassed bliss, and do not return again. [The Lord] shows their distinction —

children.text: mahā-ātmanas tu niratiśaya-priya-rūpa-mac-cintanaṃ kṛtvā mām anavadhika-atiśaya-ānandaṃ prāpyana punar āvartanta iti teṣāṃ viśeṣaṃ darśayati ---
ananyāś cintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: Those who, being non-different [in purpose], worship Me by contemplating [Me] with undivided attention —

children.text: teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: for those who are ever devoted, I Myself carry their <s>yoga</s> (attainment) and <s>kṣema</s> (preservation). ||

children.text: ananyāś cintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate |
teṣāṃ nitya-abhiyuktānāṃ yoga-kṣemaṃ vahāmy aham ||

body.text: ananyāḥ ananyaprayojanāḥ, maccintanena vinā+ātmadhāraṇālābhān maccintanaikaprayojanāḥ māṃ cintayanto ye mahātmāno janāḥ paryupāsate sarvakalyānṇaguṇānvitaṃ sarvavibhūtiyuktaṃ māṃ parita upāsate, anyūnam upāsate, teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānām mayi nityābhiyogaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇānām, aham matprāptilakṣaṇaṃ yogam, apunarāvṛttirūpaṃ kṣemam ca vahāmi //
body.translated_text: <s>Ananya</s> (non-different) means having no other purpose; since without contemplation of Me they cannot sustain their very selves, those whose sole purpose is contemplation of Me — those great-souled persons (<s>mahātmanas</s>) who worship Me thoroughly (<s>pari-upāsate</s>), i.e., worship Me as endowed with all auspicious qualities and all glories, worship Me completely, worship Me without deficiency — for those who are ever devoted (<s>nityābhiyukta</s>), i.e., those who yearn for perpetual union with Me, I carry their <s>yoga</s> — the attainment of Me — and <s>kṣema</s> — the preservation [of that attainment] in the form of non-return. //

children.text: ananyāḥ ananya-prayojanāḥ, mac-cintanena vinā+ātma-dhāraṇa-alābhān mac-cintana-eka-prayojanāḥ māṃ cintayanto ye mahā-ātmāno janāḥ paryupāsate sarva-kalyānṇa-guṇa-anvitaṃ sarva-vibhūti-yuktaṃ māṃ parita upāsate, anyūnam upāsate, teṣāṃ nitya-abhiyuktānām mayi nitya-abhiyogaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇānām, aham mat-prāpti-lakṣaṇaṃ yogam, apunar-āvṛtti-rūpaṃ kṣemam ca vahāmi //
ye tv anyadevatābhaktā yajante śraddhayā+anvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: But even those who are devoted to other deities, worship with faith —

children.text: te 'pi mām eva kaunteya yajanty avidhipūrvakam ||
children.translated_text: they too worship Me alone, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, though not according to proper injunction. ||

children.text: ye tv anya-devatā-bhaktā yajante śraddhayā+anvitāḥ |
te 'pi mām eva kaunteya yajanty avidhi-pūrvakam ||

body.text:
ye tv indrādidevatābhaktāḥ kevalatrayīniṣṭhāḥ śraddhayā+anvitāḥ indrādīn yajante, te 'pi pūrvoktena nyāyena sarvasya maccharīratayā madātmakatvena, indrādiśabdānāṃ ca madvācitvād vastuto mām eva yajante; api tv avidhipūrvakaṃ yajante / indrādīnāṃ devatānāṃ karamsvārādhyatayā anvayaṃ yathā vedāntavākyāni, "caturhotāro yatra saṃpadaṃ gacchanti deaiḥ" ityādīni vidadhati, na tatpūrvakaṃ yajante / vedāntavākyajātaṃ hi paramapuruṣaśarīratayā+avasthitānām indrādīnām ārādhyatvaṃ vidadhad atmabhūtasya paramapuruṣasyaiva sākṣād ārādhyatvaṃ vidadhāti / caturhotāraḥ agnihotradarśapūrṇamāsādīni karmāṇi, yatra paramātmany ātmatayā+avasthite saty eva taccharīrabhūtendrādidevaiḥ; saṃpadaṃ gacchanti indrādidevānām ārādhanāny
etāni karmāṇītīmāṃ saṃpadaṃ gacchantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: But those who are devoted to other deities such as <s>Indra</s> and the like, who are devoted solely to the three [<s>Vedas</s>], endowed with faith, worship <s>Indra</s> and the like — they too, by the principle stated above — since everything, being My body, has Me as its self, and since words such as '<s>Indra</s>' and the like also denote Me — in reality worship Me alone. However, they worship not according to proper injunction (<s>avidhipūrvakam</s>). They do not worship preceded by the manner in which the <s>Vedānta</s> passages — such as 'Where the four priests achieve concordance with the gods' and the like — prescribe the connection of <s>Indra</s> and other deities as those to be propitiated through ritual action. For the body of <s>Vedānta</s> passages, in prescribing the propitiability of <s>Indra</s> and other deities who are established as the body of the Supreme Person, directly prescribes the propitiability of the Supreme Person who is their self. The four priests (<s>caturhotāraḥ</s>) — the rituals such as <s>Agnihotra</s>, <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, and the like — [achieve concordance] where the Supreme Self, being established as the self [of those deities], [acts] through <s>Indra</s> and other deities who are His body; they achieve concordance — meaning these rituals come to be regarded as acts of propitiation of <s>Indra</s> and other deities. //

children.text:
ye tv indra-ādi-devatā-bhaktāḥ kevala-trayī-niṣṭhāḥ śraddhayā+anvitāḥ indra-ādīn yajante, te 'pi pūrva-uktena nyāyena sarvasya mac-charīratayā mad-ātmakatvena, indra-ādi-śabdānāṃ ca mad-vācitvād vastuto mām eva yajante; api tv avidhi-pūrvakaṃ yajante / indra-ādīnāṃ devatānāṃ karam-sva-ārādhyatayā anvayaṃ yathā veda-anta-vākyāni, "catur-hotāro yatra saṃpadaṃ gacchanti deaiḥ" ity-ādīni vidadhati, na tat-pūrvakaṃ yajante / veda-anta-vākya-jātaṃ hi parama-puruṣa-śarīratayā+avasthitānām indra-ādīnām ārādhyatvaṃ vidadhad atma-bhūtasya parama-puruṣasya eva sākṣād ārādhyatvaṃ vidadhāti / catur-hotāraḥ agni-hotra-darśa-pūrṇa-māsa-ādīni karmāṇi, yatra parama-ātmany ātmatayā+avasthite saty eva tac-charīra-bhūta-indra-ādi-devaiḥ; saṃpadaṃ gacchanti indra-ādi-devānām ārādhanāny
etāni karmāṇi iti imāṃ saṃpadaṃ gacchanti ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: atas traividyā indrādiśarīrasya paramapuruṣasyārādhanāny etāni karmāṇi; ārādhyaś ca sa eveti na jānanti, te ca parimitaphalabhāginaś cyavanasvabhāvāś ca bhavanti; tad āha --
body.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>traividyas</s> do not know that these rituals are [in truth] acts of propitiation of the Supreme Person who is the [inner] self of <s>Indra</s> and the like, and that He alone is the one to be propitiated; and they become recipients of limited fruits and are subject to falling. [The Lord] says this —

children.text: atas traividyā indra-ādi-śarīrasya parama-puruṣasyā arādhanāny etāni karmāṇi; ārādhyaś ca sa eva iti na jānanti, te ca parimita-phala-bhāginaś cyavana-sva-bhāvāś ca bhavanti; tad āha ---
ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca |
children.translated_text: For I alone am the enjoyer and the Lord of all sacrifices;

children.text: na tu mām abhijānanti tattvenātaś cyavanti te ||
children.translated_text: but they do not know Me in truth — hence they fall. ||

children.text: ahaṃ hi sarva-yajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca |
na tu mām abhijānanti tattvena ataś cyavanti te ||

body.text: prabhur eva ca -- tatra tatra phalapradātā cāham eva ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'And the Lord indeed' — the meaning is: and I alone am the bestower of fruits in each case. //

children.text: prabhur eva ca --- tatra tatra phala-pradātā ca aham eva ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: aho mahad idaṃ vaicitryam, yad ekasminn eva karmaṇi vartamānāḥ saṅkalpamātrabhedena kecid atyalpaphalabhāginaś cyavanasvabhāvāś ca bhavanti; kecana anavadhikātiśayānandaparamapuruṣaprāptirūpaphalabhāgino 'punarāvartinaś ca bhavantīty āha --
body.translated_text: Oh, how great is this wonder, that among those engaged in one and the same ritual, merely by a difference of intention (<s>saṅkalpa</s>), some become recipients of extremely meager fruits and are subject to falling, while others become recipients of fruits in the form of attaining the Supreme Person of limitless, unsurpassed bliss, and are subject to non-return — [the Lord] says —

children.text: aho mahad idaṃ vaicitryam, yad ekasminn eva karmaṇi vartamānāḥ saṅkalpa-mātra-bhedena kecid atyalpa-phala-bhāginaś cyavana-sva-bhāvāś ca bhavanti; kecana anavadhika-atiśaya-ānanda-parama-puruṣa-prāpti-rūpa-phala-bhāgino 'punar-āvartinaś ca bhavanti ity āha ---
yānti devavratā devān pitQn yānti pitṛvratāḥ |
children.translated_text: The votaries of the gods go to the gods; the votaries of the ancestors go to the ancestors;

children.text: bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyāḥ yānti madyājino 'pi mām ||
children.translated_text: the worshipers of the spirits go to the spirits; and My worshipers come to Me. ||

children.text: yānti deva-vratā devān pitQn yānti pitṛ-vratāḥ |
bhūtāni yānti bhūta-ijyāḥ yānti mad-yājino 'pi mām ||

body.text:
vrataśabdaḥ saṅklpavācī; devavratāḥ darśapūrṇamāsādibhiḥ karmabhiḥ indrādīn yajāmahe iti indrādiyajanasaṅkalpā ye, te indrādīn devān yānti / ye ca pitṛyajñādibhiḥ pitQn yajāmahe iti pitṛyajanasaṅkalpāḥ, te pitQn yānti / ye ca "yakṣarakaṣaḥpiśācādīni bhūtāni yajāmahe" iti bhūtayajanasaṅkalpāḥ, te bhūtāni yānti / ye te tair eva yajñaiḥ "devapitṛbhūtaśarīrakaṃ paramātmānaṃ bhagavantaṃ vāsudevaṃ yajāmahe" iti māṃ yajante, te madyājino mām eva yānti / devādivratāḥ devādīn prāpya tais saha parimitaṃ bhogaṃ bhuktvā teṣāṃ vinaśakāle tais saha vinaṣṭā bhavanti / madyājinas tu mām anādinidhanaṃ sarvajñaṃ satyasaṅkalpam anavadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇamahodadhim anavadhikātiśayānandaṃ prāpya na
punar nivartanta ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The word <s>vrata</s> means intention (<s>saṅkalpa</s>). The votaries of the gods (<s>devavrata</s>) — those whose intention is 'We shall worship <s>Indra</s> and other [gods]' through rituals such as <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like — they go to the gods such as <s>Indra</s> and the like. And those whose intention is 'We shall worship the ancestors' through the ancestral sacrifice (<s>pitṛyajña</s>) and the like — they go to the ancestors. And those whose intention is 'We shall worship the spirits (<s>bhūtas</s>) such as <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Piśācas</s>, and the like' — they go to those spirits. But those who, through those very same sacrifices, with the intention 'We shall worship the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Supreme Self, who has the gods, ancestors, and spirits as His body' worship Me — those who worship Me come to Me alone. The votaries of the gods and the like, having attained the gods and the like, having enjoyed limited pleasures together with them, at the time of [those deities'] destruction, are destroyed along with them. But those who worship Me, having attained Me — who am without beginning or end, omniscient, of true will, an infinite ocean of innumerable, unsurpassed auspicious qualities, and of limitless, unsurpassed bliss — do not return again, is the meaning. //

children.text:
vrata-śabdaḥ saṅklpa-vācī; deva-vratāḥ darśa-pūrṇa-māsa-ādibhiḥ karmabhiḥ indra-ādīn yajāmahe iti indra-ādi-yajana-saṅkalpā ye, te indra-ādīn devān yānti / ye ca pitṛ-yajña-ādibhiḥ pitQn yajāmahe iti pitṛ-yajana-saṅkalpāḥ, te pitQn yānti / ye ca "yakṣa-rakaṣaḥ-piśāca-adīni bhūtāni yajāmahe" iti bhūta-yajana-saṅkalpāḥ, te bhūtāni yānti / ye te tair eva yajñaiḥ "deva-pitṛ-bhūta-śarīrakaṃ parama-ātmānaṃ bhagavantaṃ vāsudevaṃ yajāmahe" iti māṃ yajante, te mad-yājino mām eva yānti / deva-ādi-vratāḥ deva-ādīn prāpya tais saha parimitaṃ bhogaṃ bhuktvā teṣāṃ vinaśa-kāle tais saha vinaṣṭā bhavanti / mad-yājinas tu mām anādi-nidhanaṃ sarva-jñaṃ satya-saṅkalpam anavadhika-atiśaya-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-mahā-udadhim anavadhika-atiśaya-ānandaṃ prāpya na
punar nivartanta ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: madyājinām ayam api viśeṣo 'stīty āha --
body.translated_text: There is yet another distinction for those who worship Me — [the Lord] says —

children.text: mad-yājinām ayam api viśeṣo 'sti ity āha ---
patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati |
children.translated_text: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water — whoever offers to Me with devotion,

children.text: tad ahaṃ bhaktyupahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that offering made with devotion, I accept from one of purified self. ||

children.text: patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati |
tad ahaṃ bhakty-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayata-ātmanaḥ ||

body.text: sarvasulabhaṃ patraṃ vā puṣpaṃ vā phalaṃ vā toyaṃ vā yo bhaktyā me prayacchati -- atyarthamatpriyatvena tatpradānena vinā+ātmadhāraṇam alabhamānatayā tadekaprayojano yo me patrādikaṃ dadāti; tasya prayatātmanaḥ tatpradānaikaprayojanatvarūpaśuddhiyuktamanasaḥ, tat tathāvidhabhaktyupahṛtam, aham sarveśvaro nikhilajagadudayavibhavalayalīlā+avāptasamastakāmaḥ satyasaṅkalpo 'navadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇaḥ svābhāvikānavadhikātiśayānandasvānubhave vartamāno 'pi, manorathapathadūravarti priyaṃ prāpyaivāśnāmi / yathoktaṃ mokṣadharme, "yāḥ kriyāḥ saṃprayuktās syur ekāntagatabuddhibhiḥ / tāḥ sarvāḥ śirasā devaḥ pratigṛhṇāti vai svayam" iti //
body.translated_text: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water — all easily available — whoever offers to Me with devotion: out of being exceedingly dear to Me, being unable to sustain oneself without offering it, and having that [offering] as one's sole purpose, whoever gives Me a leaf and the like — from that person of purified self (<s>prayatātman</s>), i.e., one whose mind possesses the purity consisting of having the offering as one's sole purpose — that [offering] presented with such devotion, I — the Lord of all, whose sport is the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the entire universe, who has attained all desires, whose will is true, who possesses hosts of innumerable, unsurpassed auspicious qualities, and who, though abiding in the experience of My own natural, limitless, unsurpassed bliss — accept it as if having obtained something dear beyond the reach of imagination. As stated in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>: 'Whatever actions are performed by those whose minds have gone to exclusive devotion, the God Himself receives all of them upon His head.' //

children.text: sarva-sulabhaṃ patraṃ vā puṣpaṃ vā phalaṃ vā toyaṃ vā yo bhaktyā me prayacchati --- atyartha-mat-priyatvena tat-pradānena vinā+ātma-dhāraṇam alabhamānatayā tad-eka-prayojano yo me patra-ādikaṃ dadāti; tasya prayata-ātmanaḥ tat-pradāna-eka-prayojanatva-rūpa-śuddhi-yukta-manasaḥ, tat tathā-vidha-bhakty-upahṛtam, aham sarva-īśvaro nikhila-jagad-udaya-vibhava-laya-līlā+avāpta-samasta-kāmaḥ satya-saṅkalpo 'navadhika-atiśaya-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇaḥ svābhāvika-anavadhika-atiśaya-ānanda-sva-anubhave vartamāno 'pi, mano-ratha-patha-dūra-varti priyaṃ prāpya eva aśnāmi / yathā-uktaṃ mokṣa-dharme, "yāḥ kriyāḥ saṃprayuktās syur eka-anta-gata-buddhibhiḥ / tāḥ sarvāḥ śirasā devaḥ pratigṛhṇāti vai svayam" iti //

body.text: yasmāj jñānināṃ mahātmanāṃ vāṅmanasāgocaro 'yaṃ viśeṣaḥ, tasmāt tvaṃ ca jñānī bhūtvā uktalakṣaṇabhaktibhārāvanamitātmā ātmīyaḥ kīrtanayatanārcanapraṇāmādikaṃ satataṃ kurvāṇo laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ ca nityanaimittikaṃ karma cetthaṃ kurv ity āhā --
body.translated_text: Since this distinction of the great-souled knowers (<s>jñānins</s>) is beyond the reach of speech and mind, therefore, you too, becoming a knower, with a self bowed down by the weight of devotion of the kind described, constantly performing <s>kīrtana</s> (glorification), prostration, worship, obeisance, and the like that are natural to oneself, and performing worldly and <s>Vedic</s> obligatory and occasional actions in this very manner — [the Lord] says —

children.text: yasmāj jñānināṃ mahā-ātmanāṃ vāṅ-manasā-gocaro 'yaṃ viśeṣaḥ, tasmāt tvaṃ ca jñānī bhūtvā ukta-lakṣaṇa-bhakti-bhāra-avanamita-ātmā ātmīyaḥ kīrtana-yatana-arcana-praṇāma-ādikaṃ satataṃ kurvāṇo laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ ca nitya-naimittikaṃ karma ca itthaṃ kurv ity āhā ---
yat karoṣi yad aśnāsi yaj jahoṣi dadāsi yat |
children.translated_text: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give,

children.text: yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣva madarpaṇam ||
children.translated_text: whatever austerity you practice, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, do that as an offering to Me. ||

children.text: yat karoṣi yad aśnāsi yaj jahoṣi dadāsi yat |
yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam ||

body.text:
yad dehayātrāśeṣabhūtaṃ laukikaṃ karma karoṣi, yac ca dehadhāraṇāyāśnāsi, yac ca vaidikaṃ homadānatapaḥprabhṛti nityanaimittikaṃ karma karoṣi, tat sarvaṃ madarpaṇaṃ kuruṣva / arpyata ity arpaṇam sarvasya laukikasya vaidikasya ca karmaṇaḥ kartṛtvaṃ bhoktṛtvam ārādhyatvaṃ ca yathā mayi samarpitaṃ bhavati tathā kuru / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- yāgadānādiṣu ārādhyatayā pratīyamānānāṃ devādīnāṃ karmakartur bhoktuḥ tava ca madīyatayā matsaṅkalpāyattasvarūpasthitipravṛttitayā ca mayy eva paramaśeṣiṇi paramakartari tvāṃ ca kartāraṃ bhoktāram ārādhakam, ārādhyaṃ ca devatājātam, ārādhanaṃ ca kriyājātaṃ sarvaṃ samarpaya; tava manniyāmyatāpūrvakamaccheṣataikarasatām ārādhyādes caitatsvabhāvagarbhatām atyarthaprītiyukto 'nusaṃdhatsva
-- iti //

children.text:
yad deha-yātrā-aśeṣa-bhūtaṃ laukikaṃ karma karoṣi, yac ca deha-dhāraṇāya aśnāsi, yac ca vaidikaṃ homa-dāna-tapaḥ-prabhṛti nitya-naimittikaṃ karma karoṣi, tat sarvaṃ mad-arpaṇaṃ kuruṣva / arpyata ity arpaṇam sarvasya laukikasya vaidikasya ca karmaṇaḥ kartṛtvaṃ bhoktṛtvam ārādhyatvaṃ ca yathā mayi samarpitaṃ bhavati tathā kuru / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- yāga-dāna-ādiṣu ārādhyatayā pratīyamānānāṃ deva-ādīnāṃ karma-kartur bhoktuḥ tava ca madīyatayā mat-saṅkalpa-āyatta-sva-rūpa-sthiti-pravṛttitayā ca mayy eva parama-śeṣiṇi parama-kartari tvāṃ ca kartāraṃ bhoktāram ārādhakam, ārādhyaṃ ca devatā-jātam, ārādhanaṃ ca kriyā-jātaṃ sarvaṃ samarpaya; tava man-niyāmyatā-pūrvaka-mac-cheṣatā-eka-rasatām ārādhya-ādes ca etat-sva-bhāva-garbhatām atyartha-prīti-yukto 'nusaṃdhatsva
--- iti //
śubhāśubhaphalair evaṃ mokṣyase karmabandhanaiḥ |
saṃnyāsayogayuktātmā vimukto mām upaiṣyasi ||
śubha-aśubha-phalair evaṃ mokṣyase karma-bandhanaiḥ |

body.text: evaṃ saṃnyāsākhyayogayuktamanāḥ ātmānaṃ maccheṣatāmanniyāmyataikarasaṃ karma ca sarvaṃ madārādhanam anusaṃdadhāno laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ ca karma kurvan śubhāśubhaphalair anantaiḥ prācīnakarmākhyair bandhanair matprāptivirodhibhis sarvair mokṣyase; tair vimukto mām evopaiṣyasi //

children.text: evaṃ saṃnyāsa-ākhya-yoga-yukta-manāḥ ātmānaṃ mac-cheṣatā-man-niyāmyatā-eka-rasaṃ karma ca sarvaṃ mad-ārādhanam anusaṃdadhāno laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ ca karma kurvan śubha-aśubha-phalair anantaiḥ prācīna-karma-ākhyair bandhanair mat-prāpti-virodhibhis sarvair mokṣyase; tair vimukto mām eva upaiṣyasi //

samo 'haṃ sarvabhūteṣu na me dveṣyo 'sti na priyaḥ |
ye bhajanti tu māṃ bhaktyā mayi te teṣu cāpy aham ||

body.text: devatiryaṅmanuṣyasthāvarātmanā+avasthiteṣu jātitaś cākārataḥ svabhāvato jñānataś cātyantotkṛṣṭāpakṛṣṭarūpeṇa vartamāneṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu samāśrayaṇīyatve samo 'ham; ayaṃ jātyākārasvabhāvajñānādibhir nirkṛṣṭa iti samāśrayaṇe na me dveṣyo 'sti -- udvejanīyatayā na tyājyo 'sti / tathā samāśritatvātirekeṇa jātyādibhir atyantotkṛṣṭo 'yam iti tadvyuktatayā samāśrayaṇe na kaścit priyo 'sti na saṃgrāhyo 'sti / api tu atyarthamatpriyatvena madbhajanena vinā+ātmadhāraṇālābhān madbhajanaikaprayojanā ye māṃ bhajante, te jātyādibhir utkṛṣṭā apakṛṣṭā vā matsamānaguṇavad yathāsukhaṃ mayy eva vartante / aham api teṣu madutkṛṣṭeṣv iva varte //

children.text: deva-tiryaṅ-manuṣya-sthāvara-ātmanā+avasthiteṣu jātitaś cā akārataḥ sva-bhāvato jñānataś ca atyanta-utkṛṣṭa-apakṛṣṭa-rūpeṇa vartamāneṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu samāśrayaṇīyatve samo 'ham; ayaṃ jāty-ākāra-sva-bhāva-jñāna-ādibhir nirkṛṣṭa iti samāśrayaṇe na me dveṣyo 'sti --- udvejanīyatayā na tyājyo 'sti / tathā samāśritatva-atirekeṇa jāty-ādibhir atyanta-utkṛṣṭo 'yam iti tad-vyuktatayā samāśrayaṇe na kaścit priyo 'sti na saṃgrāhyo 'sti / api tu atyartha-mat-priyatvena mad-bhajanena vinā+ātma-dhāraṇa-alābhān mad-bhajana-eka-prayojanā ye māṃ bhajante, te jāty-ādibhir utkṛṣṭā apakṛṣṭā vā mat-samāna-guṇavad yathā-sukhaṃ mayy eva vartante / aham api teṣu mad-utkṛṣṭeṣv iva varte //

body.text:
tatra tatra jātiviśeṣe jātānāṃ yaḥ samācāra upādeyaḥ pariharaṇīyaś ca, tasmād ativṛtto 'py uktaprakāreṇa mām ananyabhāk bhajanaikaprayojano bhajate cet, sādhur eva saḥ vaiṣṇavāgresara eva saḥ / mantavyaḥ bahumantavyaḥ pūrvoktais sama ityarthaḥ / kuta etat? samyagvyavasito hi saḥ -- yato 'sya vyavasāyaḥ susamīcīnaḥ -- bhagavān nikhilajagadekakāraṇabhūtaḥ paraṃ brahma nārāyaṇaś carācarapatir asmatsvāmī mama gurur mama suhṛn mama paramaṃ bhogyam iti sarvair duṣprāpo 'yaṃ vyavasāyas tena kṛtaḥ; tatkāryaṃ cānanyaprayojanaṃ nirantaraṃ bhajanaṃ tasyāsti -- ataḥ sādhur eva; bahumantavyaḥ / asmin vyavasāye, tatkārye coktaprakārabhajane saṃpanne sati tasyācāravyatikramaḥ svalpavaikalyam iti na tāvatā+anādaraṇīyaḥ, api tu bahumantavya evetyarthaḥ
//

//

kṣipraṃ bhavati dharmātmā śaśvacchāntiṃ nigacchati |

na jāyata ity ajaḥ, anena vikāridravyād acetanāt tatsaṃsṛṣṭāt saṃsāricetanāc ca visajātīyatvam uktam / saṃsāricetanasya hi karmakṛtācitsaṃsargo janma / anādim ity anena padena ādimato 'jān muktātmano visajātīyatvam uktam / muktātmano hy ajatvam ādimat; tasya heyasaṃbandhasya pūrvavṛttatvāt tadarhatāsti / ato 'nādim ity anena tadanarhatayā tatpratyanīkatocyate; "niravadyam" ityādiśrutyā ca / evaṃ heyasaṃbandhapratyanīkasvarūpatayā tadanarhaṃ māṃ lokamaheśvaram lokeśvarāṇām apīśvaraṃ martyeṣv asaṃmūḍho yo vetti; itarasajātīyatayaikīkṛtya mohaḥ saṃmohaḥ, tadrahito 'saṃmūḍhaḥ sa madbhaktyutpattivirodhibhis sarvaiḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- loke manuṣyāṇāṃ rājā itaramanuṣyasajātīyaḥ kenacit karmaṇā tadādhipatyaṃ prāptaḥ;
tathā devānām adhipatir api; tathāṇḍādhipatir apītarasaṃsārisajātīyaḥ; tasyāpi bhāvanātrayāntargatatvāt / "yo brahmāṇaṃ vidadhāti" iti śruteś ca / tathānye 'pi ye kecanāṇimādyaiśvaryaṃ prāptāḥ / ayaṃ tu lokamaheśvaraḥ kāryakāraṇāvasthād acetanād baddhān muktāc ca cetanād iśitavyāt sarvasmān nikhilaheyapratyanīkānavadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇaikatānatayā niyamanaikasvabhāvatayā ca visajātīya itītrasajātīyatāmoharahito yo māṃ vetti, sa sarvaiḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyate iti //
body.translated_text:
He does not undergo birth, hence He is 'unborn' (<s>aja</s>) — by this, His dissimilarity from non-conscious matter that undergoes transformation, and from the transmigrating conscious beings who are conjoined with it, is stated. For the birth of a transmigrating conscious being is its conjunction with non-conscious matter brought about by <s>karma</s>. By the word 'beginningless' (<s>anādi</s>), His dissimilarity from the liberated selves, who are [also] unborn but have a beginning, is stated. For the unborn-ness of a liberated self has a beginning; since the connection with what is to be abandoned existed previously, there is fitness for it. Therefore, by 'beginningless,' His unfitness for such [connection], being opposed to all contact with what is to be abandoned, is stated — as also by the <s>śruti</s>: 'He who is without blemish,' and the like. Thus, one who knows Me — who am, by My essential nature being opposed to all contact with what is to be abandoned, unfit for it, the great Lord of the world, the Lord even of the lords of the worlds — without confusion among mortals; confusion is the delusion of identifying Me with others of the same kind, and one free from that is 'unconfused' — he is released from all sins that obstruct the arising of devotion to Me. What is stated is this: In the world, a king among men is of the same kind as other men and has attained lordship over them by some <s>karma</s>;
likewise, the lord of the <s>devas</s> too; likewise, the lord of the cosmic egg is also of the same kind as other transmigrating beings, because he too falls within the three dispositions. And by the <s>śruti</s>: 'He who creates <s>Brahmā</s>.' Likewise, any others who have attained lordship such as <s>aṇimā</s> and the like. But this great Lord of the world is dissimilar from all that is to be governed — from non-conscious [matter] in both its causal and effectual states, from the bound and liberated conscious beings — by His being exclusively constituted of innumerable auspicious qualities opposed to all that is to be abandoned, unsurpassed in excellence, and by His essential nature being solely that of governance. Thus, one who knows Me, free from the delusion of identifying Me as being of the same kind as others — he is released from all sins. //

bhavanti bhāvā bhūtānāṃ matta eva pṛthag-vidhāḥ ||

body.text:
buddhiḥ manaso nirūpaṇasāmarthyam, jñānam cidacidvastuviśeṣaviṣayo niścayaḥ, asaṃmohaḥ pūrvagṛhītād rajatāder visajātīye śuktikādivastuni sajātīyatābuddhinivṛttiḥ; kṣamā manovikārahetau saty apy avikṛtamanastvam; satyam yathādṛṣṭaviṣayaṃ bhūtahitarūpaṃ vacanam / tadanuguṇā manovṛttir ihābhipretā, manovṛttiprakaraṇāt / damaḥ bāhyakaraṇānām anarthaviṣayebhyo niyamanam; śamaḥ antaḥkaraṇasya tathā niyamanam; sukham ātmānukūlānubhavaḥ; duḥkham pratikūlānubhavaḥ; bhavaḥ bhavanam; anukūlānubhavahetukaṃ manaso bhavanam; abhāvaḥ pratikūlānubhavahetuko manaso 'vasādaḥ; bhayam āgāmino duḥkhasya hetudarśanajaṃ duḥkham; tannivṛttiḥ abhayam; ahiṃsā paraduḥkhāhetutvam; samatā ātmani sukṛtsu vipakṣeṣu
cārthānarthayos samamatitvam; tuṣṭiḥ sarveṣv ātmasu dṛṣṭeṣu toṣasvabhāvatvam; tapaḥ śāstrīyo bhogasaṅkocarūpaḥ kāyakleśaḥ; dānam svakīyabhogyānaṃ parasmai pratipādanam; yaśaḥ guṇavattāprathā; ayaśaḥ nairguṇyaprathā / etac cobhayaṃ tadanuguṇamanovṛttidvayaṃ mantavyam, tatprakaraṇāt / tapodāne ca tathā / evam ādyāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhāvāḥ pravṛttinivṛttihetavo manovṛttayo matta eva matsaṅkalpāyattā bhavanti //
body.translated_text:
<s>Buddhi</s> is the capacity of the mind for determination. <s>Jñāna</s> is the ascertainment concerning the distinctive objects — conscious and non-conscious. <s>Asaṃmoha</s> is the cessation of the cognition of similarity with respect to a dissimilar object such as mother-of-pearl, when silver and the like had been previously apprehended. <s>Kṣamā</s> is the state of having an undisturbed mind even when a cause of mental disturbance is present. <s>Satya</s> is speech that corresponds to what is perceived and is conducive to the welfare of beings. What is intended here is the mental disposition corresponding to that, since this is a context dealing with mental dispositions. <s>Dama</s> is the restraint of the external sense-organs from objects that are harmful. <s>Śama</s> is the similar restraint of the internal organ. Happiness is the experience of what is favorable to the self. Sorrow is the experience of what is unfavorable. <s>Bhava</s> (coming into being) is arising — the arising of the mind caused by favorable experience. <s>Abhāva</s> (cessation) is the depression of the mind caused by unfavorable experience. Fear is the sorrow born of perceiving the cause of impending suffering. The cessation of that is fearlessness. Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is being a non-cause of suffering to others. Equanimity is equal-mindedness toward oneself, toward the virtuous, and toward adversaries,
and toward good fortune and misfortune. Contentment (<s>tuṣṭi</s>) is the nature of being pleased upon seeing all selves. Austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is bodily mortification in the form of curtailment of enjoyment as prescribed by scripture. Charity (<s>dāna</s>) is giving what is meant for one's own enjoyment to another. Fame (<s>yaśas</s>) is the reputation of possessing virtues. Infamy (<s>ayaśas</s>) is the reputation of lacking virtues. And both of these should be understood as the two mental dispositions corresponding to them, since this is a context dealing with those. Likewise with austerity and charity. Thus, all dispositions — the mental states that are the causes of activity and cessation — of all beings, beginning with these, arise from Me alone, being dependent on My will. //

children.text:
buddhiḥ manaso nirūpaṇa-sāmarthyam, jñānam cid-acid-vastu-viśeṣa-viṣayo niścayaḥ, asaṃmohaḥ pūrva-gṛhītād rajata-āder visajātīye śuktikā-ādi-vastuni sajātīyatā-buddhi-nivṛttiḥ; kṣamā mano-vikāra-hetau saty apy avikṛta-manastvam; satyam yathā-dṛṣṭa-viṣayaṃ bhūta-hita-rūpaṃ vacanam / tad-anuguṇā mano-vṛttir iha abhipretā, mano-vṛtti-prakaraṇāt / damaḥ bāhya-karaṇānām anartha-viṣayebhyo niyamanam; śamaḥ antaḥkaraṇasya tathā niyamanam; sukham ātma-anukūla-anubhavaḥ; duḥkham pratikūla-anubhavaḥ; bhavaḥ bhavanam; anukūla-anubhava-hetukaṃ manaso bhavanam; abhāvaḥ pratikūla-anubhava-hetuko manaso 'vasādaḥ; bhayam āgāmino duḥkhasya hetu-darśana-jaṃ duḥkham; tan-nivṛttiḥ abhayam; ahiṃsā para-duḥkha-ahetutvam; samatā ātmani sukṛtsu vipakṣeṣu
ca artha-anarthayos sama-matitvam; tuṣṭiḥ sarveṣv ātmasu dṛṣṭeṣu toṣa-sva-bhāvatvam; tapaḥ śāstrīyo bhoga-saṅkoca-rūpaḥ kāya-kleśaḥ; dānam svakīya-bhogyānaṃ parasmai pratipādanam; yaśaḥ guṇavattā-prathā; ayaśaḥ nairguṇya-prathā / etac ca ubhayaṃ tad-anuguṇa-mano-vṛtti-dvayaṃ mantavyam, tat-prakaraṇāt / tapo-dāne ca tathā / evam ādyāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhāvāḥ pravṛtti-nivṛtti-hetavo mano-vṛttayo matta eva mat-saṅkalpa-āyattā bhavanti //

body.text: sarvasya bhūtajātasya sṛṣṭisthityoḥ pravartayitāraś ca matsaṃkalpāyattapravṛttaya ity āha --
body.translated_text: He states that those who initiate creation and sustenance of all classes of beings also have their activity dependent on His will:

children.text: sarvasya bhūta-jātasya sṛṣṭi-sthityoḥ pravartayitāraś ca mat-saṃkalpa-āyatta-pravṛttaya ity āha ---
maharṣayas sapta pūrve catvāro manavas tathā |
children.translated_text: The seven great sages of old and the four <s>Manus</s> likewise,

children.text: madbhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣāṃ loka imāḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: born of My mind, partake of My disposition — from whom are these creatures in the world. ||

children.text: maha-rṣayas sapta pūrve catvāro manavas tathā |
mad-bhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣāṃ loka imāḥ prajāḥ ||

body.text: pūrve sapta maharṣayaḥ atītamanvantare ye bhṛgvādayas sapta maharṣayo nityasṛṣṭipravartanāya brahmaṇo manassaṃbhavāḥ, nityasthitipravartanāya ye ca sārvaṇikā nāma catvāro manavaḥ sthitāḥ, yeṣāṃ santānamaye loke jātā imāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ pratikṣaṇam āpralayād apatyānām utpādakāḥ pālakāś ca bhavanti te bhṛgvādayo manavaś ca madbhāvāḥ mama yo bhāvaḥ sa eva yeṣāṃ bhāvaḥ te madbhāvāḥ, manmate sthitāḥ, matsaṅkalpānuvartina ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The seven great sages of old — those seven great sages such as <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others, who were born from the mind of <s>Brahmā</s> for the perpetual initiation of creation in the past <s>manvantara</s>; and the four <s>Manus</s> called <s>Sāvarṇika</s>, who exist for the perpetual initiation of sustenance; from whose lineage these — all these creatures born in the world — become perpetual begetters and protectors of offspring up to the time of dissolution, every moment — those <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others and those <s>Manus</s> are 'of My disposition' (<s>madbhāva</s>): My disposition is their disposition, meaning they abide in My purpose, following My will — this is the meaning. //

children.text: pūrve sapta maha-rṣayaḥ atīta-manv-antare ye bhṛgv-ādayas sapta maha-rṣayo nitya-sṛṣṭi-pravartanāya brahmaṇo manas-saṃbhavāḥ, nitya-sthiti-pravartanāya ye ca sārvaṇikā nāma catvāro manavaḥ sthitāḥ, yeṣāṃ santāna-maye loke jātā imāḥ sarvāḥ prajāḥ pratikṣaṇam ā-pralayād apatyānām utpādakāḥ pālakāś ca bhavanti te bhṛgv-ādayo manavaś ca mad-bhāvāḥ mama yo bhāvaḥ sa eva yeṣāṃ bhāvaḥ te mad-bhāvāḥ, man-mate sthitāḥ, mat-saṅkalpa-anuvartina ity-arthaḥ //
etāṃ vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ |
children.translated_text: One who knows in truth this <s>vibhūti</s> (sovereignty) and <s>yoga</s> (divine power) of Mine —

children.text: so 'vikampena yogena yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is endowed with unwavering <s>yoga</s> — of this there is no doubt. ||

children.text: etāṃ vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ |
so 'vikampena yogena yujyate na atra saṃśayaḥ ||

body.text: vibhūtiḥ aiśvaryam / etāṃ sarvasya madāyattotpattisthitipravṛttitārūpāṃ vibhūtim, mama heyapratyanīkakalyāṇaguṇagaṇarūpaṃ yogaṃ ca yas tattvato vetti, so 'vikampena aprakampyena bhaktiyogena yujyate / nātra saṃśayaḥ / madvibhūtiviṣayaṃ kalyāṇaguṇaviṣayaṃ ca jñānaṃ bhaktiyogavardhanam iti svayam eva drakṣyasītyabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Vibhūti</s> means sovereignty. One who knows in truth this <s>vibhūti</s> in the form of the dependence of the origination, sustenance, and activity of everything upon Me, and My <s>yoga</s> in the form of a host of auspicious qualities opposed to everything to be rejected — he is endowed with unwavering, unshakable <s>bhaktiyoga</s>. Of this there is no doubt. Knowledge concerning My <s>vibhūti</s> and concerning My auspicious qualities fosters <s>bhaktiyoga</s> — you yourself shall see this — such is the intent. //

children.text: vibhūtiḥ aiśvaryam / etāṃ sarvasya mad-āyatta-utpatti-sthiti-pravṛttitā-rūpāṃ vibhūtim, mama heya-pratyanīka-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-rūpaṃ yogaṃ ca yas tattvato vetti, so 'vikampena aprakampyena bhakti-yogena yujyate / na atra saṃśayaḥ / mad-vibhūti-viṣayaṃ kalyāṇa-guṇa-viṣayaṃ ca jñānaṃ bhakti-yoga-vardhanam iti svayam eva drakṣyasi ity-abhiprāyaḥ //

body.text: vibhūtijñānavipākarūpāṃ bhaktivṛddhiṃ darśayati --
body.translated_text: He shows the increase of devotion, which is the matured result of the knowledge of <s>vibhūti</s>:

children.text: vibhūti-jñāna-vipāka-rūpāṃ bhakti-vṛddhiṃ darśayati ---
ahaṃ, sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṃ pravartate |
children.translated_text: I am the origin of all; from Me everything proceeds. |

children.text: iti matvā bhajante māṃ budhā bhāvasamanvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowing thus, the wise worship Me, endowed with loving disposition. ||

children.text: ahaṃ, sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṃ pravartate |
iti matvā bhajante māṃ budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ ||

body.text: ahaṃ, sarvasya vicitracidacitprapañcasya prabhavaḥ utpattikāraṇam, sarvaṃ matta eva pravartate itīdaṃ mama svābhāvikaṃ niraṃkuśāiśvaryaṃ, sauśīlyasaundaryavātsalyādikalyāṇaguṇagaṇayogaṃ ca matvā budhā jñāninaḥ bhāvasamanvitāḥ māṃ sarvakalyāṇaguṇānvitaṃ bhajante / bhāvaḥ manovṛttiviśeṣaḥ / mayi spṛhayālavo māṃ bhajanta ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: I am the origin — the cause of origination — of the entire variegated expanse of conscious and non-conscious beings. Everything proceeds from Me alone — this is My natural, unobstructed sovereignty, and knowing [this] together with My possession of hosts of auspicious qualities such as condescension (<s>sauśīlya</s>), beauty (<s>saundarya</s>), tender affection (<s>vātsalya</s>), and the like — the wise, the knowledgeable ones, endowed with loving disposition, worship Me who am endowed with all auspicious qualities. <s>Bhāva</s> is a special mental disposition. They worship Me with ardent longing — this is the meaning. //

children.text: ahaṃ, sarvasya vicitra-cid-acit-prapañcasya prabhavaḥ utpatti-kāraṇam, sarvaṃ matta eva pravartate iti idaṃ mama svābhāvikaṃ niraṃkuśa-aiśvaryaṃ, sauśīlya-saundarya-vātsalya-ādi-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-yogaṃ ca matvā budhā jñāninaḥ bhāva-samanvitāḥ māṃ sarva-kalyāṇa-guṇa-anvitaṃ bhajante / bhāvaḥ mano-vṛtti-viśeṣaḥ / mayi spṛhayālavo māṃ bhajanta ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: katham?
body.translated_text: How?

children.text: katham?
maccittā madgataprāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam |
children.translated_text: With minds fixed on Me, with their very lives devoted to Me, enlightening one another,

children.text: kathayantaś ca māṃ nityaṃ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca ||
children.translated_text: and always speaking of Me — they are content and they rejoice. ||

children.text: mac-cittā mad-gata-prāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam |
kathayantaś ca māṃ nityaṃ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca ||

body.text: maccittāḥ mayi niviṣṭamanasaḥ, madgataprāṇāḥ madgatajīvitāḥ, mayā vinātmadhāraṇam alabhamānā ityarthaḥ; svaiḥ svair anubhūtān madīyān guṇān parasparaṃ bodhayantaḥ, madīyāni divyāni ramaṇīyāni karmāṇi ca kathayantaḥ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca -- vaktāras tadvacanenānanyaprayojanena tuṣyanti; śrotāraś ca tacchravaṇenānavadhikātiśayapriyeṇa ramante //
body.translated_text: 'With minds fixed on Me' — with minds absorbed in Me. 'With their lives devoted to Me' — with their very lives going to Me, meaning they are unable to sustain themselves without Me. Enlightening one another about My qualities as experienced by each of them individually; and speaking of My divine and delightful deeds — they are content and they rejoice. The speakers are content with that very act of speaking, which has no other purpose [than the joy of it]; and the listeners rejoice with that hearing, which is of unsurpassingly beloved [content]. //

children.text: mac-cittāḥ mayi niviṣṭa-manasaḥ, mad-gata-prāṇāḥ mad-gata-jīvitāḥ, mayā vinā ātma-dhāraṇam alabhamānā ity-arthaḥ; svaiḥ svair anubhūtān madīyān guṇān parasparaṃ bodhayantaḥ, madīyāni divyāni ramaṇīyāni karmāṇi ca kathayantaḥ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca --- vaktāras tad-vacanena ananya-prayojanena tuṣyanti; śrotāraś ca tac-chravaṇena anavadhika-atiśaya-priyeṇa ramante //
teṣāṃ satatayuktānāṃ bhajatāṃ prītipūrvakam |
children.translated_text: To those who are constantly devoted, who worship with love,

children.text: dadāmi buddhiyogaṃ taṃ yena mām upayānti te ||
children.translated_text: I give that <s>buddhiyoga</s> (yoga of understanding) by which they come to Me. ||

children.text: teṣāṃ satata-yuktānāṃ bhajatāṃ prīti-pūrvakam |
dadāmi buddhi-yogaṃ taṃ yena mām upayānti te ||

body.text: teṣāṃ satatayuktānām mayi satatayogam āśaṃsamānānāṃ māṃ bhajamānānām ahaṃ tam eva buddhiyogaṃ vipākadaśāpannaṃ prītipūrvakaṃ dadāmi; yena te mām upayānti //
body.translated_text: To those who are constantly devoted — who yearn for constant union with Me — who worship Me, I give that very <s>buddhiyoga</s>, which has reached the stage of maturation, with love; by which they come to Me. //

children.text: teṣāṃ satata-yuktānām mayi satata-yogam āśaṃsamānānāṃ māṃ bhajamānānām ahaṃ tam eva buddhi-yogaṃ vipāka-daśā-āpannaṃ prīti-pūrvakaṃ dadāmi; yena te mām upayānti //

body.text: kiñ ca,
body.translated_text: Moreover,

children.text: kiñ ca,
teṣām evānukampārtham aham ajñānajaṃ tamaḥ |
children.translated_text: Out of compassion for them alone, I, abiding in their hearts,

children.text: naśyāmy ātmabhāvastho jñānadīpena bhāsvatā ||
children.translated_text: destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge. ||

children.text: teṣām eva anukampā-artham aham ajñāna-jaṃ tamaḥ |
naśyāmy ātma-bhāva-stho jñāna-dīpena bhāsvatā ||

body.text: teṣām evānugrahārtham aham, ātmabhāvasthaḥ teṣāṃ manovṛttau viṣayatayāvasthitaḥ madīyān kalyāṇaguṇagaṇāṃś cāviṣkurvan madviṣayajñānākhyena bhāsvatā dīpena jñānavirodhiprācīnakarmarūpājñānajaṃ madvyatiriktapūrvābhyastaviṣayaprāvaṇyarūpaṃ tamo nāśayāmi //
body.translated_text: Out of grace for them alone, I, abiding in their mental disposition as an object [of contemplation], revealing My own hosts of auspicious qualities, with the shining lamp called knowledge directed toward Me — I destroy the darkness born of ignorance, in the form of inclination toward previously cultivated objects other than Me, which is born of prior <s>karma</s> that is opposed to knowledge. //

children.text: teṣām eva anugraha-artham aham, ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ teṣāṃ mano-vṛttau viṣayataya āvasthitaḥ madīyān kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇāṃś cā aviṣkurvan mad-viṣaya-jñāna-ākhyena bhāsvatā dīpena jñāna-virodhi-prācīna-karma-rūpa-ajñāna-jaṃ mad-vyatirikta-pūrva-abhyasta-viṣaya-prāvaṇya-rūpaṃ tamo nāśayāmi //

attributes.n: evaṃ sakale1tara-visajātīyaṃ bhagavad-asādhāraṇaṃ śṛṇvatāṃ niratiśayā3nanda-janakaṃ kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-yogaṃ tad-aiśvarya-vitatiṃ ca śrutvā tad-vistāraṃ śrotu-kāmo 'rjuna uvāca ---

children.text: paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān |
children.translated_text: You are the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme abode, the supreme purifier. |

children.text: paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān |

body.text:
paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma paramaṃ pavitraṃ iti yaṃ śrutayo vadanti, sa hi bhavān / "yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante, yena jātāni jīvanti, yat prayanty abhisaṃviśanti, tad vijijñāsasva tad brahmeti", "brahmavid āpnoti param", "sa yo ha vai tat paramaṃ brahma veda brahmaiva bhavati" iti / tathā paraṃ dhāma; dhāmaśabdo jyotirvacanaḥ; paraṃ jyotiḥ "atha yad ataḥ paro divo jyotir dīpyate", "paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate", "taṃ devā jyotiṣāṃ jyotiḥ" iti / tathā ca paramaṃ pavitram paramaṃ pāvanam; smartur aśeṣakalmaṣāśleṣakaram, vināśakaraṃ ca / "yathā puṣkarapalāśa āpo na śliṣyante evam evaṃvidi pāpaṃ karma na śliṣyate", "tad yatheṣīkātūlam agnau protaṃ pradūyetaivaṃ hāsya sarve pāpmānaḥ pradūyante", "nārāyaṇa paraṃ brahma tattvaṃ nagarāyaṇaḥ
paraḥ / nārāyaṇa paro jyotir ātmā nārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ" iti hi śrutayo vadanti ||
body.translated_text:
That which the <s>śrutis</s> declare to be the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme abode, and the supreme purifier — that indeed is You. 'From which these beings are born, by which once born they live, into which they enter upon departing — seek to know that, that is <s>Brahman</s>'; 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s> attains the supreme'; 'He who knows that Supreme <s>Brahman</s> becomes <s>Brahman</s> itself.' Likewise, the supreme abode — the word <s>dhāma</s> means light; the supreme light: 'The light that shines beyond this heaven,' 'Approaching the supreme light, one manifests in one's own form,' 'Him the <s>devas</s> [worship as] the light of lights.' And likewise, the supreme purifier — the supreme means of purification; causing the non-adhesion of all impurities to one who remembers, and causing their destruction. 'As water does not cling to a lotus leaf, so upon one who knows thus, sinful <s>karma</s> does not cling'; 'Just as a tuft of <s>iṣīkā</s> grass cast into fire is burnt up, so all his sins are burnt up.' 'The Supreme <s>Brahman</s> is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; the supreme truth is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;
the supreme light is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; the Supreme Self is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' — thus the <s>śrutis</s> declare. ||

children.text:
paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma paramaṃ pavitraṃ iti yaṃ śrutayo vadanti, sa hi bhavān / "yato vā imāni bhūtāni jāyante, yena jātāni jīvanti, yat prayanty abhisaṃviśanti, tad vijijñāsasva tad brahma iti", "brahma-vid āpnoti param", "sa yo ha vai tat paramaṃ brahma veda brahma eva bhavati" iti / tathā paraṃ dhāma; dhāma-śabdo jyotir-vacanaḥ; paraṃ jyotiḥ "atha yad ataḥ paro divo jyotir dīpyate", "paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇa abhiniṣpadyate", "taṃ devā jyotiṣāṃ jyotiḥ" iti / tathā ca paramaṃ pavitram paramaṃ pāvanam; smartur aśeṣa-kalmaṣa-āśleṣa-karam, vināśa-karaṃ ca / "yathā puṣkara-palāśa āpo na śliṣyante evam evaṃ-vidi pāpaṃ karma na śliṣyate", "tad yatha īṣīkā-tūlam agnau protaṃ pradūyeta evaṃ ha asya sarve pāpmānaḥ pradūyante", "nārāyaṇa paraṃ brahma tattvaṃ nagarāyaṇaḥ
paraḥ / nārāyaṇa paro jyotir ātmā nārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ" iti hi śrutayo vadanti ||

body.text: puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyam ādidevam ajaṃ vibhum //
body.translated_text: The eternal, divine Person, the primal God, unborn, all-pervading. ||

children.text: puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyam ādi-devam ajaṃ vibhum //
āhus tvām ṛṣayaḥ sarve devarṣir nāradas tathā |
children.translated_text: All the sages declare You thus, as also the divine sage <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṃ caiva bravīṣi me ||
children.translated_text: <s>Asita</s>, <s>Devala</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s> — and You Yourself tell me. ||

children.text: āhus tvām ṛṣayaḥ sarve deva-rṣir nāradas tathā |
asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṃ ca eva bravīṣi me ||

body.text: ṛṣayaś ca sarve parāvaratattvayāthātmyavidas tvām eva śāśvataṃ divyaṃ puruṣam ādidevam ajaṃ vibhum āhuḥ; tathaiva devarṣir nāradaḥ asitaḥ devalaḥ vyāsaś ca / "ye ca devavido vipro ye cādhyātmavido janāḥ / te vadanti mahātmānaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dharmaṃ sanātanam // pavitāṇāṃ hi govindaḥ pavitraṃ param ucyate / puṇyānām api puṇyo 'sau maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam / trailokyaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣo devadevaḥ sanātanaḥ / āste harir acintyātmā tatraiva madhusūdanaḥ // BhGR_1.", "eṣa nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān kṣīrārṇavaniketanaḥ / nāgaparyaṅkam utsṛjya hy āgato madhurāṃ purīm // BhGR_1.", "puṇyā dvāravatī tatra yatrāste madhusūdahaḥ / sākṣād devaḥ purāṇo 'sau sa hi dharmas sanātanaḥ" / tathā, "yatra nārāyaṇo devaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ / tatra kṛtsnaṃ jagat pārtha tīrthāny āyatanāni ca // tat puṇyaṃ tat paraṃ brahma tat tīrthaṃ tat tapovanam / tatra devarṣayas siddhāḥ sarve caiva tapodhanāḥ // ādidevo mahāyogī yatrāste madhusūdanaḥ / puṇyānām api tat puṇyaṃ mā bhūt te saṃśayo 'tra vai // BhGR_1.", "kṛṣṇa eva hi lokānām utpattir api cāpyayaḥ / kṛṣṇasya hi kṛte bhūtam idaṃ viśvaṃ carācaram // BhGR_1." iti / tathā svayam eva bravīṣi ca, "bhūmir apo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano budhir eva ca / ahaṃkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā // ityādinā, "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" ityantena //
body.translated_text: And all the sages — those who know the truth of the higher and lower realities — declare You alone to be the eternal, divine Person, the primal God, unborn, and all-pervading; likewise the divine sage <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Asita</s>, <s>Devala</s>, and <s>Vyāsa</s>. 'Those brāhmaṇas who know the <s>devas</s>, and those people who know the inner self — they call the great-souled <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the eternal <s>dharma</s>. <s>Govinda</s> is called the supreme purifier among purifiers; He is the most auspicious among the auspicious, the most meritorious among the meritorious. The lord of the three worlds, the lotus-eyed, the eternal God of gods — there abides <s>Hari</s>, of inconceivable self, that very <s>Madhusūdana</s>.' 'This <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the glorious one, whose abode is the ocean of milk — having left His serpent-couch, has come to the city of <s>Mathurā</s>.' 'Blessed is <s>Dvāravatī</s> where abides <s>Madhusūdana</s>; He is directly the ancient God, He is the eternal <s>dharma</s>.' Likewise, 'Where <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the God, the eternal Supreme Self abides — there is the entire world, O <s>Pārtha</s>, with its sacred waters and holy places. That is the most meritorious, that is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, that is the sacred water, that is the grove of penance. There the divine sages, the perfected ones, and all those rich in austerity [abide]. Where abides <s>Madhusūdana</s>, the primal God, the great <s>yogin</s> — that is the most meritorious of the meritorious; let there be no doubt in you about this.' '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone is the origin and also the dissolution of the worlds; for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s sake this entire universe, moving and unmoving, has come into being.' 'For <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s sake' means: this entire universe is subordinate (<s>śeṣa</s>) to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — this is the meaning. And likewise You Yourself tell me: through 'Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, <s>buddhi</s>, and <s>ahaṃkāra</s> — this is My eightfold <s>Prakṛti</s>' and so on, up to 'I am the origin of all; from Me everything proceeds.' //

children.text: ṛṣayaś ca sarve para-avara-tattva-yāthātmya-vidas tvām eva śāśvataṃ divyaṃ puruṣam ādi-devam ajaṃ vibhum āhuḥ; tatha aiva deva-rṣir nāradaḥ asitaḥ devalaḥ vyāsaś ca / "ye ca deva-vido vipro ye ca adhyātma-vido janāḥ / te vadanti mahā-ātmānaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dharmaṃ sanātanam // pavitāṇāṃ hi govindaḥ pavitraṃ param ucyate / puṇyānām api puṇyo 'sau maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam / trailokyaṃ puṇḍarīka-akṣo deva-devaḥ sanātanaḥ / āste harir acintya-ātmā tatra eva madhu-sūdanaḥ // BhGR_1.", "eṣa nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān kṣīra-arṇava-niketanaḥ / nāga-paryaṅkam utsṛjya hy āgato madhurāṃ purīm // BhGR_1.", "puṇyā dvāravatī tatra yatrā aste madhu-sūdahaḥ / sākṣād devaḥ purāṇo 'sau sa hi dharmas sanātanaḥ" / tathā, "yatra nārāyaṇo devaḥ parama-ātmā sanātanaḥ / tatra kṛtsnaṃ jagat pārtha tīrthāny āyatanāni ca // tat puṇyaṃ tat paraṃ brahma tat tīrthaṃ tat tapo-vanam / tatra deva-rṣayas siddhāḥ sarve ca eva tapo-dhanāḥ // ādi-devo mahā-yogī yatrā aste madhusūdanaḥ / puṇyānām api tat puṇyaṃ mā bhūt te saṃśayo 'tra vai // BhGR_1.", "kṛṣṇa eva hi lokānām utpattir api ca apyayaḥ / kṛṣṇasya hi kṛte bhūtam idaṃ viśvaṃ cara-acaram // BhGR_1." iti / tathā svayam eva bravīṣi ca, "bhūmir apo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano budhir eva ca / ahaṃkāra iti iyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā // ity-ādinā, "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" ity-antena //
sarvam etad ṛtaṃ manye yan māṃ vadasi keśava |
children.translated_text: All this I hold to be true, what You tell me, O <s>Keśava</s>. |

children.text: na hi te bhagavan vyaktiṃ vidur devā na dānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For neither the <s>devas</s> nor the <s>dānavas</s>, O Lord, know Your manifestation. ||

children.text: sarvam etad ṛtaṃ manye yan māṃ vadasi keśava |
na hi te bhagavan vyaktiṃ vidur devā na dānavāḥ ||

body.text: ataḥ sarvam etad yathāvasthitavastukathanaṃ manye, na praśaṃsādyabhiprāyam; yan māṃ prati ananyasādhāraṇam anavadhikātiśayaṃ svābhāvikaṃ tavāiśvaryaṃ kalyāṇaguṇānantyaṃ ca vadasi / ato bhagavan niratiśayajñānaśaktibalāiśvaryavīryatejasāṃ nidhe, te vyaktiṃ vyañjanaprakāraṃ na hi parimitajñānā devā dānavāś ca viduḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore I consider all this to be a statement of things as they actually are, not intended as praise or the like — what you say to me about your sovereignty that is unique to you alone, of unsurpassed and unlimited extent, innate, and your infinite host of auspicious qualities. Therefore, O Lord — treasury of unsurpassed knowledge, power, strength, sovereignty, valor, and splendor — neither the gods nor the demons of limited knowledge know the manner of Your manifestation. ||

children.text: ataḥ sarvam etad yathā-avasthita-vastu-kathanaṃ manye, na praśaṃsā-ādy-abhiprāyam; yan māṃ prati ananya-sādhāraṇam anavadhika-atiśayaṃ svābhāvikaṃ tava aiśvaryaṃ kalyāṇa-guṇa-ānantyaṃ ca vadasi / ato bhagavan niratiśaya-jñāna-śakti-bala-aiśvarya-vīrya-tejasāṃ nidhe, te vyaktiṃ vyañjana-prakāraṃ na hi parimita-jñānā devā dānavāś ca viduḥ //
svayam evātmanātmānaṃ vettha tvaṃ puruṣottama |
children.translated_text: 'You Yourself know Yourself by Yourself alone, O Supreme Person,' |

children.text: bhūtabhāvana bhūteśa devadeva jagatpate ||
children.translated_text: 'O creator of beings, O lord of beings, O god of gods, O master of the universe.' ||

children.text: svayam evā atmanā ātmānaṃ vettha tvaṃ puruṣa-uttama |
bhūta-bhāvana bhūta-īśa deva-deva jagat-pate ||

body.text: he puruṣottama, ātmanā, ātmānam tvāṃ svayam eva svena jñānenaiva vettha / bhūtabhāvana; sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām utpādayitaḥ, bhūteśa sarveṣāṃ niyantaḥ, devadeva daivatānām api paramadaivata, yathā manuṣyamṛgapakṣisarīsṛpādīn saundaryasauśīlyādikalyāṇaguṇagaṇair daivatāni atītya vartante, tathā tāni sarvāṇi daivatāny api tais tair guṇais atītya vartamāna, jagatpate jagatsvāmin //
body.translated_text: O Supreme Person, You know Yourself — You — by Yourself alone, by Your own knowledge. O creator of beings (<s>Bhūtabhāvana</s>) — originator of all beings; O lord of beings (<s>Bhūteśa</s>) — controller of all; O god of gods (<s>Devadeva</s>) — the supreme deity even of the deities: just as the deities surpass humans, animals, birds, reptiles, and the like by their host of auspicious qualities such as beauty, graciousness, and the like, so You exist surpassing all those deities too by those very qualities. O master of the universe (<s>Jagatpati</s>) — sovereign of the world. ||

children.text: he puruṣa-uttama, ātmanā, ātmānam tvāṃ svayam eva svena jñānena eva vettha / bhūta-bhāvana; sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām utpādayitaḥ, bhūta-īśa sarveṣāṃ niyantaḥ, deva-deva daivatānām api parama-daivata, yathā manuṣya-mṛga-pakṣi-sarīsṛpa-ādīn saundarya-sauśīlya-ādi-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇair daivatāni atītya vartante, tathā tāni sarvāṇi daivatāny api tais tair guṇais atītya vartamāna, jagat-pate jagat-svāmin //
vaktum arhasy aśeṣeṇa divyā hy ātmavibhūtayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'You should speak in full of Your divine glories,' |

children.text: yābhir vibhūtibhir lokān imāṃs tvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi ||
children.translated_text: 'by which glories You pervade these worlds and abide.' ||

children.text: vaktum arhasy aśeṣeṇa divyā hy ātma-vibhūtayaḥ |
yābhir vibhūtibhir lokān imāṃs tvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi ||

body.text: divyāḥ tvadasādhāraṇyo vibhūtayo yāḥ, tās tvam evāśeṣeṇa vaktum arhasi / tvam eva vyañjayetyarthaḥ / yābhir anantābhir vibhūtibhiḥ -- yair niyamanaviśeṣair yuktaḥ imān lokān tvaṃ niyantṛtvena vyāpya tiṣṭhasi //
body.translated_text: Those divine glories that are uniquely Yours — You alone should speak of them in full. The meaning is: You alone should reveal them. By which infinite glories — by which specific modes of governance — You pervade these worlds as their controller and abide. ||

children.text: divyāḥ tvad-asādhāraṇyo vibhūtayo yāḥ, tās tvam eva aśeṣeṇa vaktum arhasi / tvam eva vyañjaya ity-arthaḥ / yābhir anantābhir vibhūtibhiḥ --- yair niyamana-viśeṣair yuktaḥ imān lokān tvaṃ niyantṛtvena vyāpya tiṣṭhasi //
kathaṃ vidyām ahaṃ yogī tvāṃ sadā paricintayan |
children.translated_text: 'How may I, a <s>yogin</s>, know You, always meditating upon You?' |

children.text: keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu cintyo 'si bhagavan mayā ||
children.translated_text: 'And in which particular beings are You to be contemplated by me, O Lord?' ||

children.text: kathaṃ vidyām ahaṃ yogī tvāṃ sadā paricintayan |
keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu cintyo 'si bhagavan mayā ||

body.text: ahaṃ yogī -- bhaktiyoganiṣṭhas san bhaktyā tvāṃ sadā paricintayan cintayituṃ pravṛttaḥ cintanīyaṃ tvāṃ paripūrṇāiśvaryādikalyāṇaguṇagaṇaṃ kathaṃ vidyām? pūrvoktabuddhijñānādibhāvavyatirikteṣu keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu mayā niyantṛtvena cintyo 'si? //
body.translated_text: I — a <s>yogin</s>, one established in the discipline of devotion (<s>bhaktiyoga</s>) — having undertaken to meditate upon You always with devotion, how may I know You who are to be contemplated, endowed with a host of auspicious qualities such as complete sovereignty and the like? And in which particular beings — other than the previously mentioned states such as intelligence, knowledge, and the like — are You to be contemplated by me as their controller? ||

children.text: ahaṃ yogī --- bhakti-yoga-niṣṭhas san bhaktyā tvāṃ sadā paricintayan cintayituṃ pravṛttaḥ cintanīyaṃ tvāṃ paripūrṇa-aiśvarya-ādi-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇaṃ kathaṃ vidyām? pūrva-ukta-buddhi-jñāna-ādi-bhāva-vyatirikteṣu keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu mayā niyantṛtvena cintyo 'si? //
vistareṇātmano yogaṃ vibhūtiṃ ca janārdana |
children.translated_text: 'Tell me again in detail of Your <s>yoga</s> (power) and Your glory, O <s>Janārdana</s>.' |

children.text: bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptir hi śṛṇvato nāsti me 'mṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'For there is no satiety for me in hearing this nectar.' ||

children.text: vistareṇā atmano yogaṃ vibhūtiṃ ca jana-ardana |
bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptir hi śṛṇvato na asti me 'mṛtam ||

body.text: "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" iti saṃkṣepeṇoktaṃ tava sraṣṭṛtvādiyogaṃ vibhūtiṃ niyamanaṃ ca bhūyo vistareṇa kathaya / tvayocyamānaṃ tvanmāhātmyāmṛtaṃ śṛṇvato me tṛptir nāsti; hi -- mamātṛptis tvayaiva viditetyabhiprāyaḥ // BhGR_10.18 //
body.translated_text: Tell me again in detail Your creative power and the like — Your <s>yoga</s> (power of being creator and the like) and Your glory (governance) — which were stated in brief as 'I am the origin of all; from Me everything proceeds.' For me, hearing the nectar of Your greatness as spoken by You, there is no satiety. The implication is: my insatiability is known to You Yourself. ||

children.text: "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" iti saṃkṣepeṇa uktaṃ tava sraṣṭṛtva-ādi-yogaṃ vibhūtiṃ niyamanaṃ ca bhūyo vistareṇa kathaya / tvaya ūcyamānaṃ tvan-māhātmya-amṛtaṃ śṛṇvato me tṛptir na asti; hi --- mama atṛptis tvaya aiva vidita īty-abhiprāyaḥ // BhGR_10.18 //
hanta te kathayiṣyāmi vibhūtīr ātmanaś śubhāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, I shall tell you of My auspicious glories,' |

children.text: prādhānyataḥ kuruśreṣṭha nāsty anto vistarasya me ||
children.translated_text: 'by way of the principal ones, O best of <s>Kurus</s>, for there is no end to My extent.' ||

children.text: hanta te kathayiṣyāmi vibhūtīr ātmanaś śubhāḥ |
prādhānyataḥ kuru-śreṣṭha na asty anto vistarasya me ||

body.text: he kuruśreṣṭha! madīyāḥ kalyāṇīr vibhūtīḥ prādhānyatas te kathayiṣyāmi / prādhanyaśabdena utkarṣo vivakṣitaḥ; "purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ mām" iti hi vakṣyate / jagaty utkṛṣṭāḥ kāścana vibhūtīr vakṣyāmi, vistareṇa vaktuṃ śrotuṃ ca na śakyate, tāsām ānantyāt / vibhūtitvaṃ nāma niyāmyatvam; sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ buddhyādayaḥ pṛthagvidhā bhāvā matta eva bhavantīty uktvā, "etāṃ vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ" iti pratipādanāt / tathā tatra yogaśabdanirdiṣṭaṃ sraṣṭṛtvādikaṃ vibhutiśabdanirdiṣṭaṃ tatpravartyatvam iti hy uktaṃ punaś ca, "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate / iti matvā bhajante māṃ budhā bhāvasamanvitāḥ" iti //
body.translated_text: O best of <s>Kurus</s>! I shall tell you of My auspicious glories by way of the principal ones. By the word 'principal' (<s>prādhānya</s>), eminence is intended; for it will be said: 'and know Me as the chief among priests.' I shall speak of certain eminent glories in the world; it is not possible to speak or hear of them in their full extent, because of their infinity. Glory (<s>vibhūti</s>) means that which is governed; for having said 'the various states of all beings such as intelligence and the like arise from Me alone,' He will establish this by saying: 'he who knows in truth this glory and <s>yoga</s> of Mine.' And thus what is designated by the word <s>yoga</s> there — the creatorship and the like — and what is designated by the word <s>vibhūti</s> — the being directed by Him — that has been stated. And again: 'I am the origin of all; from Me everything proceeds — knowing thus, the wise worship Me, endowed with devotion.' ||

children.text: he kuru-śreṣṭha! madīyāḥ kalyāṇīr vibhūtīḥ prādhānyatas te kathayiṣyāmi / prādhanya-śabdena utkarṣo vivakṣitaḥ; "purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ mām" iti hi vakṣyate / jagaty utkṛṣṭāḥ kāścana vibhūtīr vakṣyāmi, vistareṇa vaktuṃ śrotuṃ ca na śakyate, tāsām ānantyāt / vibhūtitvaṃ nāma niyāmyatvam; sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ buddhy-ādayaḥ pṛthag-vidhā bhāvā matta eva bhavanti ity uktvā, "etāṃ vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ" iti pratipādanāt / tathā tatra yoga-śabda-nirdiṣṭaṃ sraṣṭṛtva-ādikaṃ vibhuti-śabda-nirdiṣṭaṃ tat-pravartyatvam iti hy uktaṃ punaś ca, "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate / iti matvā bhajante māṃ budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ" iti //

body.text: tatra sarvabhūtānāṃ pravartanarūpaṃ niyamanam ātmatayāvasthāyetīmam artham, yogaśabdanirdiṣṭaṃ sarvasya sraṣṭṛtvaṃ pālayitṛtvaṃ saṃhartṛtvaṃ ceti suspaṣṭam āha --
body.translated_text: Here, to make clear the meaning that the governance in the form of directing all beings consists in His abiding as their inner self — and to clearly state the creatorship, sustainership, and destructorship designated by the word <s>yoga</s> — He says:

children.text: tatra sarva-bhūtānāṃ pravartana-rūpaṃ niyamanam ātmataya āvasthāya iti imam artham, yoga-śabda-nirdiṣṭaṃ sarvasya sraṣṭṛtvaṃ pālayitṛtvaṃ saṃhartṛtvaṃ ca iti suspaṣṭam āha ---
aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I am the self, O <s>Guḍākeśa</s>, abiding in the hearts of all beings.' |

children.text: aham ādiś ca madhyaṃ ca bhūtānām anta eva ca ||
children.translated_text: 'I am the beginning, the middle, and the end of beings.' ||

children.text: aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarva-bhūta-āśaya-sthitaḥ |
aham ādiś ca madhyaṃ ca bhūtānām anta eva ca ||

body.text:
sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ mama śarīrabhūtānām āśaye hṛdaye aham ātmatayāvasthitaḥ / ātmā hi nāma śarīrasya sarvātmanā ādhāraḥ, niyantā, śeṣī ca / tathā vakṣyate, "sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattas smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca", "īśvaras sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati / bhrāmayan sarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā // BhGR_1." iti / śrūyate ca, "yaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhan sarvebhyo bhūtebhyo 'ntaro yaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni na viduḥ, yasya sarvāṇi bhūtāni śarīraṃ yas sarvāṇi bhūtāny antaro yamayati, eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ" iti, "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyātmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati, sa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ" iti ca / evaṃ sarvabhūtānām ātmatayāvasthito 'haṃ teṣām
ādir madhyaṃ cāntaś ca -- teṣām utpattisthitipralayahetur ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the hearts of all beings who are My bodies, I am established as their inner self. For the self (<s>ātman</s>) is the complete support, controller, and principal of the body. Thus it will be stated: 'And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me come memory, knowledge, and their removal'; 'The Lord abides in the heart-region of all beings, O <s>Arjuna</s>, causing all beings to revolve, mounted on the machine, through <s>Māyā</s>.' And it is heard in <s>śruti</s>: 'He who, abiding in all beings, is interior to all beings, whom all beings do not know, whose body all beings are, who controls all beings from within — He is your self, the inner controller, the immortal'; and 'He who, abiding in the self, is interior to the self, whom the self does not know, whose body the self is, who controls the self from within — He is your self, the inner controller, the immortal.' Thus, abiding as the self of all beings, I am their beginning, middle, and end — meaning: I am the cause of their origination, sustenance, and dissolution. ||

children.text:
sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ mama śarīra-bhūtānām āśaye hṛdaye aham ātmataya āvasthitaḥ / ātmā hi nāma śarīrasya sarva-ātmanā ādhāraḥ, niyantā, śeṣī ca / tathā vakṣyate, "sarvasya ca ahaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattas smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca", "īśvaras sarva-bhūtānāṃ hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati / bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantra-ārūḍhāni māyayā // BhGR_1." iti / śrūyate ca, "yaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhan sarvebhyo bhūtebhyo 'ntaro yaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni na viduḥ, yasya sarvāṇi bhūtāni śarīraṃ yas sarvāṇi bhūtāny antaro yamayati, eṣa ta ātma āntaryāmy amṛtaḥ" iti, "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyā atmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati, sa ta ātma āntaryāmy amṛtaḥ" iti ca / evaṃ sarva-bhūtānām ātmataya āvasthito 'haṃ teṣām
ādir madhyaṃ ca antaś ca --- teṣām utpatti-sthiti-pralaya-hetur ity-arthaḥ //
