body.text: evaṃ bhagavataḥ svavibhūtibhūteṣu sarveṣv ātmatayāvasthānaṃ tattacchabdasāmānādhikaraṇyanirdeśahetuṃ pratipādya vibhūtiviśeṣān sāmānādhikaraṇyena vyapadiśati / bhagavaty ātmatayāvasthite hi sarve śabdās tasminn eva paryavasyanti; yathā devo manuṣyaḥ pakṣī vṛkṣaḥ ityādayaḥ śabdāḥ śarīrāṇi pratipādayantas tattadātmani paryavasyanti / bhagavatas tattadātmatayāvasthānam eva tattacchabdasāmānādhikaraṇyanibandhanam iti vibhūtyupasaṃhāre vakṣyati; "na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ carācaram" iti sarveṣāṃ svenāvinābhāvavacanāt / avinābhāvaś ca niyāmyatayeti; "mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" ity upakramoditam /
body.translated_text: Having thus established that the Lord's abiding as the inner self of all His glories is the basis for the co-referential designation by their respective words, He designates the specific glories by co-referential predication. For when the Lord abides as the inner self, all words ultimately denote Him alone — just as the words 'god,' 'human,' 'bird,' 'tree,' and the like, while conveying bodies, ultimately denote the respective self [within]. That the Lord's abiding as the respective inner self is the very basis for the co-referential predication by the respective words — He will state this in the conclusion of the glories: 'There is no being, moving or unmoving, that can exist without Me' — by this statement of the inseparability of all from Him. And inseparability is by virtue of being governed — as stated at the outset: 'from Me everything proceeds.'

children.text: evaṃ bhagavataḥ sva-vibhūti-bhūteṣu sarveṣv ātmataya āvasthānaṃ tat-tac-chabda-sāmānādhikaraṇya-nirdeśa-hetuṃ pratipādya vibhūti-viśeṣān sāmānādhikaraṇyena vyapadiśati / bhagavaty ātmataya āvasthite hi sarve śabdās tasminn eva paryavasyanti; yathā devo manuṣyaḥ pakṣī vṛkṣaḥ ity-ādayaḥ śabdāḥ śarīrāṇi pratipādayantas tat-tad-ātmani paryavasyanti / bhagavatas tat-tad-ātmataya āvasthānam eva tat-tac-chabda-sāmānādhikaraṇya-nibandhanam iti vibhūty-upasaṃhāre vakṣyati; "na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ cara-acaram" iti sarveṣāṃ svena avinābhāva-vacanāt / avinābhāvaś ca niyāmyataya īti; "mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" ity upakrama-uditam /
ādityānām ahaṃ viṣṇur jyotiṣāṃ ravir aṃśumān |
children.translated_text: 'Among the <s>Ādityas</s> I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>; among luminaries I am the radiant sun.' |

children.text: marīcir marutām asmi nakṣatrāṇām ahaṃ śaśī ||
children.translated_text: 'Among the <s>Maruts</s> I am <s>Marīci</s>; among the stars I am the moon.' ||

children.text: ādityānām ahaṃ viṣṇur jyotiṣāṃ ravir aṃśumān |
marīcir marutām asmi nakṣatrāṇām ahaṃ śaśī ||

body.text: dvādaśasaṃkhyāsaṃkhyātānām ādityānāṃ dvādaśo ya utkṛṣṭo viṣṇur nāmādityaḥ, so 'ham / jyotiṣāṃ jagati prakāśakānāṃ yaḥ aṃśumān raviḥ ādityagaṇaḥ, so 'ham / marutām utkṛṣṭo marīcir yaḥ, so 'ham asmi / nakṣatrāṇām ahaṃ śaśī / neyaṃ nirdhāraṇe ṣaṣṭhī, "bhūtānām asmi cetanā" itivat / nakṣatrāṇāṃ patir yaś candraḥ, so 'ham asmi //
body.translated_text: Among the <s>Ādityas</s>, counted as twelve in number, I am the twelfth — the eminent one named <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Among luminaries — those that illuminate the world — I am the radiant sun, belonging to the group of <s>Ādityas</s>. Among the <s>Maruts</s>, I am the eminent one named <s>Marīci</s>. Among the stars I am the moon. This is not a genitive of partition [selecting one from the class], just as in 'among beings I am consciousness.' The moon who is the lord of the stars — that I am. ||

children.text: dvādaśa-saṃkhyā-saṃkhyātānām ādityānāṃ dvādaśo ya utkṛṣṭo viṣṇur nāmā adityaḥ, so 'ham / jyotiṣāṃ jagati prakāśakānāṃ yaḥ aṃśumān raviḥ āditya-gaṇaḥ, so 'ham / marutām utkṛṣṭo marīcir yaḥ, so 'ham asmi / nakṣatrāṇām ahaṃ śaśī / na iyaṃ nirdhāraṇe ṣaṣṭhī, "bhūtānām asmi cetanā" itivat / nakṣatrāṇāṃ patir yaś candraḥ, so 'ham asmi //
vedānāṃ sāmavedo 'smi devānām asmi vāsavaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Among the <s>Vedas</s> I am the <s>Sāmaveda</s>; among the gods I am <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>).' |

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ manaś cāsmi bhūtānām asmi cetanā ||
children.translated_text: 'Among the senses I am the mind; among beings I am consciousness.' ||

children.text: vedānāṃ sāma-vedo 'smi devānām asmi vāsavaḥ |
indriyāṇāṃ manaś ca asmi bhūtānām asmi cetanā ||

body.text: vedānām ṛgyajussāmātharvaṇāṃ ya utkṛṣṭaḥ sāmavedaḥ, so 'ham / devānām indro 'ham asmi / ekādaśānām indriyāṇāṃ yad utkṛṣṭaṃ mana indriyam, tad aham asmi / iyam api na nirdhāraṇe / bhūtānāṃ cetanāvatāṃ yā cetanā, so 'ham asmi //
body.translated_text: Among the <s>Vedas</s> — <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Atharva</s> — I am the eminent one, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>. Among the gods, I am <s>Indra</s>. Among the eleven senses, I am the mind — the eminent one among the senses. This too is not a genitive of partition. Among beings endowed with consciousness, I am the consciousness [itself]. ||

children.text: vedānām ṛg-yajus-sāma-atharvaṇāṃ ya utkṛṣṭaḥ sāma-vedaḥ, so 'ham / devānām indro 'ham asmi / ekādaśānām indriyāṇāṃ yad utkṛṣṭaṃ mana indriyam, tad aham asmi / iyam api na nirdhāraṇe / bhūtānāṃ cetanāvatāṃ yā cetanā, so 'ham asmi //
rudrāṇāṃ śaṅkaraś cāsmi vitteśo yakṣarakṣasām |
children.translated_text: 'Among the <s>Rudras</s> I am <s>Śaṅkara</s>; among the <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s> I am the lord of wealth (<s>Kubera</s>).' |

children.text: vasūnāṃ pāvakaś cāsmi meruḥ śikhariṇām aham ||
children.translated_text: 'Among the <s>Vasus</s> I am fire (<s>Pāvaka</s>); among the peaked mountains I am <s>Meru</s>.' ||

children.text: rudrāṇāṃ śaṅkaraś ca asmi vitta-īśo yakṣa-rakṣasām |
vasūnāṃ pāvakaś ca asmi meruḥ śikhariṇām aham ||

body.text: rudrāṇām ekādaśānāṃ śaṅkaro 'ham asmi / yakṣarakṣasāṃ vaiśravaṇo 'ham / vasūnām aṣṭānāṃ pāvako 'ham / śikhariṇāṃ śikharaśobhināṃ parvatānāṃ madhye merur aham //
body.translated_text: Among the eleven <s>Rudras</s>, I am <s>Śaṅkara</s>. Among the <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, I am <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (<s>Kubera</s>). Among the eight <s>Vasus</s>, I am <s>Pāvaka</s> (fire). Among the peaked mountains — mountains adorned with peaks — I am <s>Meru</s>. ||

children.text: rudrāṇām ekādaśānāṃ śaṅkaro 'ham asmi / yakṣa-rakṣasāṃ vaiśravaṇo 'ham / vasūnām aṣṭānāṃ pāvako 'ham / śikhariṇāṃ śikhara-śobhināṃ parvatānāṃ madhye merur aham //
purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ māṃ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim |
children.translated_text: 'And know Me, O <s>Pārtha</s>, as <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, the chief among priests.' |

children.text: senānīnām ahaṃ skandaḥ sarasām asmi sāgaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Among generals I am <s>Skanda</s>; among bodies of water I am the ocean.' ||

children.text: purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ māṃ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim |
senānīnām ahaṃ skandaḥ sarasām asmi sāgaraḥ ||

body.text: purodhasām utkṛṣṭo bṛhaspatir yaḥ, so 'ham asmi, senānīnāṃ senāpatīnāṃ skando 'ham asmi / sarasāṃ sāgaro 'ham asmi //
body.translated_text: Among priests, I am the eminent one — <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. Among generals — commanders of armies — I am <s>Skanda</s>. Among bodies of water, I am the ocean. ||

children.text: purodhasām utkṛṣṭo bṛhaspatir yaḥ, so 'ham asmi, senānīnāṃ senā-patīnāṃ skando 'ham asmi / sarasāṃ sāgaro 'ham asmi //
maharṣīṇāṃ bhṛgur ahaṃ girām asmy ekam akṣaram |
children.translated_text: 'Among the great sages I am <s>Bhṛgu</s>; among utterances I am the single syllable [<s>Om</s>].' |

children.text: yajñānāṃ japayajño 'smi sthāvarāṇāṃ himālayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent recitation; among immovable things I am the <s>Himālaya</s>.' ||

children.text: maha-rṣīṇāṃ bhṛgur ahaṃ girām asmy ekam akṣaram |
yajñānāṃ japa-yajño 'smi sthāvarāṇāṃ himālayaḥ ||

body.text: maharṣīṇāṃ marīcyādīnāṃ bhṛgur aham / arthābhidhāyinaḥ śabdā giraḥ, tāsām ekam akṣaraṃ praṇavo 'ham asmi / yajñānām utkṛṣṭo japayajño 'smi / pūrvamātrāṇāṃ himavān aham //
body.translated_text: Among the great sages — <s>Marīci</s> and the others — I am <s>Bhṛgu</s>. Utterances (<s>giras</s>) are words that convey meaning; among them I am the single syllable — <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Om</s>). Among sacrifices, I am the eminent one — the sacrifice of silent recitation (<s>japayajña</s>). Among immovable things, I am <s>Himavān</s> (the <s>Himālaya</s>). ||

children.text: maha-rṣīṇāṃ marīcy-ādīnāṃ bhṛgur aham / artha-abhidhāyinaḥ śabdā giraḥ, tāsām ekam akṣaraṃ praṇavo 'ham asmi / yajñānām utkṛṣṭo japa-yajño 'smi / pūrva-mātrāṇāṃ himavān aham //
aśvatthas sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Among all trees I am the <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig tree); among the divine sages, <s>Nārada</s>.' |

children.text: gandharvāṇāṃ citrarathaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Among the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Citraratha</s>; among the perfected beings, the sage <s>Kapila</s>.' ||

children.text: aśvatthas sarva-vṛkṣāṇāṃ deva-rṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ |
gandharvāṇāṃ citra-rathaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo muniḥ ||
uccaiśśravasam aśvānāṃ viddhi mām amṛtodbhavam |
children.translated_text: 'Know Me as <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> among horses, born from the nectar [churning].' |

children.text: airāvataṃ gajendrāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca narādhipam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Airāvata</s> among the lordly elephants, and the king among human beings.' ||

children.text: uccaiśśravasam aśvānāṃ viddhi mām amṛta-udbhavam |
airāvataṃ gaja-indrāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca nara-adhipam ||
āyudhānām ahaṃ vajraṃ dhenūnām asmi kāmadhuk |
children.translated_text: 'Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows I am <s>Kāmadhuk</s> (the wish-fulfilling cow).' |

children.text: prajanaś cāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇām asmi vāsukiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'And I am <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love) as the progenitor; among serpents I am <s>Vāsuki</s>.' ||

children.text: āyudhānām ahaṃ vajraṃ dhenūnām asmi kāma-dhuk |
prajanaś ca asmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇām asmi vāsukiḥ ||
anantaś cāsmi nāgānāṃ varuṇo yādasām aham |
children.translated_text: 'Among the <s>Nāgas</s> I am <s>Ananta</s>; among aquatic beings I am <s>Varuṇa</s>.' |

children.text: pitQṇām aryamā cāsmi yamaḥ saṃyamatām aham ||
children.translated_text: 'Among the ancestors I am <s>Aryaman</s>; among those who restrain I am <s>Yama</s>.' ||

children.text: anantaś ca asmi nāgānāṃ varuṇo yādasām aham |
pitQṇām aryamā ca asmi yamaḥ saṃyamatām aham ||

body.text: vṛkṣāṇāṃ pūjyo 'śvattho 'ham / devarṣīṇaṃ nārado 'ham / kāmadhuk divyā surabhiḥ / jananahetuḥ kandarpaś cāham asmi / sarpāḥ ekāśirasaḥ; nāgāḥ bahuśirasaḥ / yādāṃsi jalavāsinaḥ, teṣāṃ varuṇo 'ham / daṇḍayatāṃ vaivasvato 'ham //
body.translated_text: Among trees, I am the venerable <s>Aśvattha</s>. Among the divine sages, I am <s>Nārada</s>. <s>Kāmadhuk</s> is the divine cow <s>Surabhi</s>. And I am <s>Kandarpa</s> — the cause of procreation. Serpents (<s>sarpa</s>) are single-headed; <s>Nāgas</s> are many-headed. Aquatic creatures (<s>yādas</s>) are those that dwell in water; among them I am <s>Varuṇa</s>. Among those who punish, I am <s>Vaivasvata</s> (<s>Yama</s>). ||

children.text: vṛkṣāṇāṃ pūjyo 'śvattho 'ham / deva-rṣīṇaṃ nārado 'ham / kāma-dhuk divyā surabhiḥ / janana-hetuḥ kandarpaś ca aham asmi / sarpāḥ ekāśirasaḥ; nāgāḥ bahu-śirasaḥ / yādāṃsi jala-vāsinaḥ, teṣāṃ varuṇo 'ham / daṇḍayatāṃ vaivasvato 'ham //
prahlādaś cāsmi daityānāṃ kālaḥ kalayatām aham |
children.translated_text: 'Among the <s>Daityas</s> I am <s>Prahlāda</s>; among reckoners I am time.' |

children.text: mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛgendro 'haṃ vainateyaś ca pakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: 'Among animals I am the lion; among birds I am <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>).' ||

children.text: prahlādaś ca asmi daityānāṃ kālaḥ kalayatām aham |
mṛgāṇāṃ ca mṛga-indro 'haṃ vainateyaś ca pakṣiṇām ||

body.text: anarthaprepsutayā gaṇayatāṃ madhye kālaḥ mṛtyur aham //
body.translated_text: Among those who reckon with the intention of bringing harm, I am time — death. ||

children.text: anartha-prepsutayā gaṇayatāṃ madhye kālaḥ mṛtyur aham //
pavanaḥ pavatām asmi rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtām aham |
children.translated_text: 'Among purifiers I am the wind; among weapon-bearers I am <s>Rāma</s>.' |

children.text: jhaṣāṇāṃ makaraś cāsmi srotasām asmi jāhnavī ||
children.translated_text: 'Among aquatic creatures I am the crocodile; among rivers I am the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>).' ||

children.text: pavanaḥ pavatām asmi rāmaḥ śastra-bhṛtām aham |
jhaṣāṇāṃ makaraś ca asmi srotasām asmi jāhnavī ||

body.text: pavatām gamanasvabhāvānāṃ pavano 'ham / śastrabhṛtāṃ rāmo 'ham / śastrabhṛttvam atra vibhūtiḥ, arthāntarābhāvāt / ādityādayaś ca kṣetrajñā ātmatvenāvasthitasya bhagavataḥ śarīratayā dharmabhūtā iti śastrabhṛttvasthānīyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Among those whose nature is movement — the purifiers — I am the wind. Among weapon-bearers, I am <s>Rāma</s>. The bearing of weapons is the glory here, since there is no other [category intended]. And the <s>Ādityas</s> and others, being individual selves (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), are in the position of the body of the Lord who abides as their inner self; therefore, they are in the position analogous to weapon-bearing [i.e., they are instruments of the Lord]. ||

children.text: pavatām gamana-sva-bhāvānāṃ pavano 'ham / śastra-bhṛtāṃ rāmo 'ham / śastra-bhṛttvam atra vibhūtiḥ, artha-antara-abhāvāt / āditya-ādayaś ca kṣetra-jñā ātmatvena avasthitasya bhagavataḥ śarīratayā dharma-bhūtā iti śastra-bhṛttva-sthānīyāḥ //
sargāṇām ādir antaś ca madhyaṃ caivāham arjuna |
children.translated_text: 'Of creations I am the beginning, the end, and also the middle, O <s>Arjuna</s>.' |

children.text: adhyātmavidyā vidyānāṃ vādaḥ pravadatām aham ||
children.translated_text: 'Among sciences I am the science of the self; among debaters I am reasoned argument (<s>vāda</s>).' ||

children.text: sargāṇām ādir antaś ca madhyaṃ ca eva aham arjuna |
adhyātma-vidyā vidyānāṃ vādaḥ pravadatām aham ||

body.text: sṛjyanta iti sargāḥ, teṣām ādiḥ kāraṇam; sarvadā sṛjyamānānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ tatra tatra sraṣṭāro 'ham evetyarthaḥ / tathā antaḥ sarvadā saṃhriyamāṇānāṃ tatra tatra saṃhartāro 'py aham eva / tathā ca madhyaṃ pālanam; sarvadā pālyamānānāṃ pālayitāraś cāham evetyarthaḥ / jalpavitaṇḍādi kurvatāṃ tattvanirṇayāya pravṛtto vādo yaḥ, so 'ham //
body.translated_text: Those that are created are 'creations' (<s>sarga</s>); their beginning is the cause. Of all beings that are being created at all times, I alone am the respective creator — this is the meaning. Likewise, the end: of all beings that are being dissolved at all times, I alone am the respective destroyer. And likewise the middle is sustenance: of all beings being sustained at all times, I alone am the respective sustainer — this is the meaning. Among those who engage in debate — <s>jalpa</s>, <s>vitaṇḍā</s>, and the like — the reasoned argument (<s>vāda</s>) that is undertaken for the ascertainment of truth: that I am. ||

children.text: sṛjyanta iti sargāḥ, teṣām ādiḥ kāraṇam; sarvadā sṛjyamānānāṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ tatra tatra sraṣṭāro 'ham eva ity-arthaḥ / tathā antaḥ sarvadā saṃhriyamāṇānāṃ tatra tatra saṃhartāro 'py aham eva / tathā ca madhyaṃ pālanam; sarvadā pālyamānānāṃ pālayitāraś ca aham eva ity-arthaḥ / jalpa-vitaṇḍā-ādi kurvatāṃ tattva-nirṇayāya pravṛtto vādo yaḥ, so 'ham //
akṣarāṇām akāro 'smi dvandvas sāmāsikasya ca |
children.translated_text: 'Among letters I am the letter A; among compounds I am the copulative (<s>dvandva</s>).' |

children.text: aham eva akṣayaḥ kālaḥ dhātāhaṃ viśvatomukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'I alone am imperishable time; I am the creator facing everywhere.' ||

children.text: akṣarāṇām akāro 'smi dvandvas sāmāsikasya ca |
aham eva akṣayaḥ kālaḥ dhāta āhaṃ viśvato-mukhaḥ ||

body.text: akṣarāṇāṃ madhye "akāro vai sarvā vāk" iti śrutisiddhiḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ prakṛtir akāro 'ham sāmāsikaḥ samāsasamūhaḥ; tasya madhye dvandvasamāso 'ham / sa hy ubhayapadārthapradhānatvenotkṛṣṭaḥ / kalāmuhūrtādimayo 'kṣayaḥ kālo 'ham eva / sarvasya sraṣṭā hiraṇyagarbhaś caturmukho 'ham //
body.translated_text: Among letters, I am the letter A — established through the <s>śruti</s> 'the letter A indeed is all speech' — the source of all phonemes. Among compound types (<s>sāmāsika</s>): the collection of compounds — among them I am the copulative compound (<s>dvandva</s>). For it is eminent by virtue of giving prominence to the meanings of both constituent words. I alone am imperishable time, consisting of moments, hours, and the like. I am the four-faced creator <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, facing in all directions. ||

children.text: akṣarāṇāṃ madhye "akāro vai sarvā vāk" iti śruti-siddhiḥ sarva-varṇānāṃ prakṛtir akāro 'ham sāmāsikaḥ samāsa-samūhaḥ; tasya madhye dvandva-samāso 'ham / sa hy ubhaya-pada-artha-pradhānatvena utkṛṣṭaḥ / kalā-muhūrta-ādi-mayo 'kṣayaḥ kālo 'ham eva / sarvasya sraṣṭā hiraṇya-garbhaś catur-mukho 'ham //
mṛtyus sarvaharaś cāham udbhavaś ca bhaviṣyatām |
children.translated_text: 'And I am all-seizing death, and the rise of those yet to come.' |

children.text: kīrtiś śrīr vāk ca nārīṇāṃ smṛtir medhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā ||
children.translated_text: 'Among feminine [qualities] I am fame, beauty, speech, memory, intelligence, steadfastness, and patience.' ||

children.text: mṛtyus sarva-haraś ca aham udbhavaś ca bhaviṣyatām |
kīrtiś śrīr vāk ca nārīṇāṃ smṛtir medhā dhṛtiḥ kṣamā ||

body.text: sarvaprāṇaharo mṛtyuś cāham / utpatsyamānānām udbhavākhyaṃ karma cāham / śrīr aham; kīrtiś cāham; vāk cāham; smṛtiś cāham; medhā cāham; dhṛtiś cāham; kṣamā cāham //
body.translated_text: I am death that seizes all living beings. And I am the action called 'arising' (<s>udbhava</s>) of those yet to come into being. I am <s>Śrī</s> (beauty); I am fame; I am speech; I am memory; I am intelligence; I am steadfastness; I am patience. ||

children.text: sarva-prāṇa-haro mṛtyuś ca aham / utpatsyamānānām udbhava-ākhyaṃ karma ca aham / śrīr aham; kīrtiś ca aham; vāk ca aham; smṛtiś ca aham; medhā ca aham; dhṛtiś ca aham; kṣamā ca aham //
bṛhatsāma tathā sāmnāṃ gāyatrī chandasām aham |
children.translated_text: 'Among the <s>Sāman</s> hymns I am the <s>Bṛhatsāma</s>; among metres I am <s>Gāyatrī</s>.' |

children.text: māsānāṃ mārgaśīrṣo 'ham ṛtūnāṃ kusumākaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Among months I am <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>; among seasons I am the flower-bearer (spring).' ||

children.text: bṛhat-sāma tathā sāmnāṃ gāyatrī chandasām aham |
māsānāṃ mārga-śīrṣo 'ham ṛtūnāṃ kusuma-ākaraḥ ||

body.text: sāmnāṃ bṛhatsāma aham / chandasāṃ gāyatry aham / kusumākaraḥ vasantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Among the <s>Sāman</s> hymns I am the <s>Bṛhatsāma</s>. Among metres I am <s>Gāyatrī</s>. The flower-bearer (<s>Kusumākara</s>) is spring (<s>Vasanta</s>). ||

children.text: sāmnāṃ bṛhat-sāma aham / chandasāṃ gāyatry aham / kusuma-ākaraḥ vasantaḥ //
dyūtaṃ chalayatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham |
children.translated_text: 'Among deceivers I am gambling; I am the splendor of the splendid.' |

children.text: jayo 'smi vyavasāyo 'smi sattvaṃ sattvavatām aham ||
children.translated_text: 'I am the victory; I am the resolve; I am the strength of the strong.' ||

children.text: dyūtaṃ chalayatām asmi tejas tejasvinām aham |
jayo 'smi vyavasāyo 'smi sattvaṃ sattvavatām aham ||

body.text: chalaṃ kurvatāṃ chalāspadeṣv akṣādilakṣaṇaṃ dyutam aham / jetQṇāṃ jayo 'smi / vyavasāyināṃ vyavasāyo 'smi / sattvavatāṃ sattvam aham / sattvam mahāmanastvam //
body.translated_text: Among those who play games of chance, I am the gambling (<s>dyūta</s>) — characterized by dice and the like — which is the basis of deceit. Of the victorious, I am victory. Of the resolute, I am resolve. Of the strong, I am strength (<s>sattva</s>). <s>Sattva</s> [here] means greatness of spirit. //

children.text: chalaṃ kurvatāṃ chala-āspadeṣv akṣa-ādi-lakṣaṇaṃ dyutam aham / jetQṇāṃ jayo 'smi / vyavasāyināṃ vyavasāyo 'smi / sattvavatāṃ sattvam aham / sattvam mahā-manastvam //
vṛṣṇīnāṃ vāsudevo 'smi pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanañjayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, I am <s>Vāsudeva</s>; of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, <s>Dhanañjaya</s>.'

children.text: munīnām apy ahaṃ vyāsaḥ kavīnām uśanā kaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Of the sages, I am <s>Vyāsa</s>; of the poets, the poet <s>Uśanas</s>.' ||

children.text: vṛṣṇīnāṃ vāsu-devo 'smi pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanañ-jayaḥ |
munīnām apy ahaṃ vyāsaḥ kavīnām uśanā kaviḥ ||

body.text: vasudevasūnutvam atra vibhūtiḥ, arthāntarābhāvād eva / pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanañjayo 'rjuno 'ham / munayaḥ mananenātmayāthātmyadarśinaḥ; teṣāṃ vyāso 'ham / kavayaḥ vipaścitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Being the son of <s>Vasudeva</s> is itself the divine manifestation here, since there is no other meaning [intended]. Of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, I am <s>Dhanañjaya</s> — <s>Arjuna</s>. The sages (<s>munis</s>) are those who see the true nature of the self through contemplation (<s>manana</s>); among them, I am <s>Vyāsa</s>. The poets (<s>kavis</s>) are the learned. //

children.text: vasu-deva-sūnutvam atra vibhūtiḥ, artha-antara-abhāvād eva / pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanañ-jayo 'rjuno 'ham / munayaḥ mananenā atma-yāthātmya-darśinaḥ; teṣāṃ vyāso 'ham / kavayaḥ vipaścitaḥ //
daṇḍo damayatām asmi nītir asmi jigīṣatām |
children.translated_text: 'I am the rod of those who punish; I am the statecraft of those who seek victory.'

children.text: maunaṃ caivāsmi guhyānāṃ jñānaṃ jñānavatām aham ||
children.translated_text: 'I am also the silence of secrets; I am the knowledge of the knowledgeable.' ||

children.text: daṇḍo damayatām asmi nītir asmi jigīṣatām |
maunaṃ ca eva asmi guhyānāṃ jñānaṃ jñānavatām aham ||

body.text: niyamātikramaṇe daṇḍaṃ kurvatāṃ daṇḍo 'ham / vijigīṣūṇāṃ jayopāyabhūtā nītir asmi / guhyānāṃ saṃbandhiṣu gopāneṣu maunam asmi / jñānavatāṃ jñānaṃ cāham //
body.translated_text: Of those who impose punishment for transgression of rules, I am the rod of punishment. Of the ambitious who seek victory, I am the statecraft (<s>nīti</s>) that is the means to victory. Of secrets — among things to be concealed from related persons — I am silence. And I am the knowledge of the knowledgeable. //

children.text: niyama-atikramaṇe daṇḍaṃ kurvatāṃ daṇḍo 'ham / vijigīṣūṇāṃ jaya-upāya-bhūtā nītir asmi / guhyānāṃ saṃbandhiṣu gopāneṣu maunam asmi / jñānavatāṃ jñānaṃ ca aham //
yac cāpi sarvabhūtānāṃ bījaṃ tad aham arjuna |
children.translated_text: 'And whatever is the seed of all beings, that am I, O <s>Arjuna</s>.'

children.text: na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ carācaram ||
children.translated_text: 'There is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist without Me.' ||

children.text: yac ca api sarva-bhūtānāṃ bījaṃ tad aham arjuna |
na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ cara-acaram ||

body.text: sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvāvasthāvasthitānām tattadavasthābījabhūtaṃ pratīyamānam apratīyamānaṃ ca yat, tad aham eva / bhūtajātaṃ mayā ātmatayāvasthitena vinā yat syāt, na tad asti / "aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ" iti prakramāt, "na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ carācaram" ity atrāpy ātmatayāvasthānam eva vivakṣitam / sarvaṃ vastujātaṃ sarvāvasthaṃ mayā ātmabhūtena yuktaṃ syād ityarthaḥ / anena sarvasyāsya sāmānādhikaraṇyanirdeśasyātmatayāvasthitir eva hetur iti prakaṭitam //
body.translated_text: Whatever is the seed — whether perceived or unperceived — for the various states in which all beings exist in their various conditions, that am I alone. No class of beings could exist without Me as their inner self. From the context of 'I am the Self, O <s>Guḍākeśa</s>, seated in the hearts of all beings,' the statement 'there is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist without Me' also intends [His] existence as the inner self. The meaning is: all entities in all states would exist as endowed with Me as their Self. By this it is made clear that the reason for the co-referential designation (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of all things [with God] is His existence as their inner self. //

children.text: sarva-bhūtānāṃ sarva-avasthā-avasthitānām tat-tad-avasthā-bīja-bhūtaṃ pratīyamānam apratīyamānaṃ ca yat, tad aham eva / bhūta-jātaṃ mayā ātmataya āvasthitena vinā yat syāt, na tad asti / "aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarva-bhūta-āśaya-sthitaḥ" iti prakramāt, "na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ cara-acaram" ity atra apy ātmataya āvasthānam eva vivakṣitam / sarvaṃ vastu-jātaṃ sarva-avasthaṃ mayā ātma-bhūtena yuktaṃ syād ity-arthaḥ / anena sarvasya asya sāmānādhikaraṇya-nirdeśasyā atmataya āvasthitir eva hetur iti prakaṭitam //
nānto 'sti mama divyānāṃ vibhūtīnāṃ parantapa |
children.translated_text: 'There is no end to My divine manifestations, O <s>Parantapa</s>.'

children.text: eṣa tūddeśataḥ prokto vibhūter vistaro mayā ||
children.translated_text: 'This expansion of [My] manifestations has been declared by Me only by way of indication.' ||

children.text: na anto 'sti mama divyānāṃ vibhūtīnāṃ parantapa |
eṣa tu uddeśataḥ prokto vibhūter vistaro mayā ||

body.text: mama divyānāṃ kalyāṇīnāṃ vibhūtīnām anto nāsti; eṣa tu vibhūter vistaro mayā kaiścid upādhibhiḥ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaḥ //
body.translated_text: There is no end to My divine — auspicious — manifestations. But this expansion of manifestations has been stated by Me briefly, by means of a few illustrative examples. //

children.text: mama divyānāṃ kalyāṇīnāṃ vibhūtīnām anto na asti; eṣa tu vibhūter vistaro mayā kaiścid upādhibhiḥ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaḥ //
yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṃ śrīmad urjitam eva vā |
children.translated_text: 'Whatever being is endowed with glory, with splendor, or with vigor —'

children.text: tat tad evāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejo'ṃśasaṃbhavam ||
children.translated_text: 'know that every one of them springs from a fraction of My power.' ||

children.text: yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṃ śrīmad urjitam eva vā |
tat tad eva avagaccha tvaṃ mama tejo-'ṃśa-saṃbhavam ||

body.text: yad yad vibhūtimad iśitavyasaṃpannaṃ bhūtajātaṃ śrīmat kāntimat, dhanadhānyasamṛddhaṃ vā, ūrjitaṃ kalyāṇārambheṣu udyuktam; tat tan mama tejo'ṃśasaṃbhavam ity avagaccha / tejaḥ parābhibhavanasāmarthyam, mamācintyaśakter niyamanaśaktyekadeśasaṃbhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Whatever class of beings is endowed with glory — possessing that which is to be ruled over; splendid — radiant; or endowed with wealth and abundant grain; or vigorous — actively engaged in auspicious undertakings — know that every one of them springs from a fraction of My power. Power (<s>tejas</s>) is the capacity to overpower others; the meaning is that it springs from a fraction of My inconceivable power of governance. //

children.text: yad yad vibhūtimad iśitavya-saṃpannaṃ bhūta-jātaṃ śrīmat kāntimat, dhana-dhānya-samṛddhaṃ vā, ūrjitaṃ kalyāṇa-ārambheṣu udyuktam; tat tan mama tejo-'ṃśa-saṃbhavam ity avagaccha / tejaḥ para-abhibhavana-sāmarthyam, mama acintya-śakter niyamana-śakty-eka-deśa-saṃbhavati ity-arthaḥ //
atha vā bahunaitena kiṃ jñānena tavārjuna |
children.translated_text: 'Or rather, what need is there for all this detailed knowledge for you, O <s>Arjuna</s>?'

children.text: viṣṭabhyāham idaṃ kṛtsnam ekāṃśena sthito jagat ||
children.translated_text: 'I stand sustaining this entire universe with a single fraction [of Myself].' ||

children.text: atha vā bahuna aitena kiṃ jñānena tava arjuna |
viṣṭabhya aham idaṃ kṛtsnam eka-aṃśena sthito jagat ||

body.text: bahunā etena ucyamānena jñānena kiṃ prayojanam /idaṃ cidacidātmakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagat kāryāvasthaṃ kāraṇāvasthaṃ sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ca svarūpasadbhāve, sthitau, pravṛttibhede ca yathā matsaṅkalpaṃ nātivarteta, tathā mama mahimno 'yutāyutāṃśena viṣṭabhyāham avasthitaḥ / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā parāśareṇa, "yasyāyutāyutāṃśāṃśe viśvaśaktir iyaṃ sthitā" iti //
body.translated_text: What is the use of all this detailed knowledge being spoken? This entire universe consisting of the sentient and non-sentient — in its effectual state and causal state, gross and subtle — so that it does not transgress My will in its existence, persistence, and variety of activity: I stand sustaining [it] with a ten-thousandth of a ten-thousandth fraction of My greatness. As stated by the blessed <s>Parāśara</s>: 'In a fraction of a fraction of ten thousand, this universal power is established.' //

children.text: bahunā etena ucyamānena jñānena kiṃ prayojanam /idaṃ cid-acid-ātmakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagat kārya-avasthaṃ kāraṇa-avasthaṃ sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ ca sva-rūpa-sad-bhāve, sthitau, pravṛtti-bhede ca yathā mat-saṅkalpaṃ na ativarteta, tathā mama mahimno 'yuta-ayuta-aṃśena viṣṭabhya aham avasthitaḥ / yathā-uktaṃ bhagavatā parāśareṇa, "yasya ayuta-ayuta-aṃśa-aṃśe viśva-śaktir iyaṃ sthitā" iti //

body.text: evaṃ bhaktiyoganiṣpattaye tadvivṛddhaye ca sakaletaravilakṣaṇena svābhāvikena bhagavadasādhāraṇena kalyāṇaguṇagaṇena saha bhagavataḥ sarvātmatvaṃ tata eva tadvyatiriktasya kṛtsnasya cidacidātmakasya vastujātasya taccharīratayā tadāyattasvarūpasthitipravṛttitvaṃ coktam / tam etaṃ bhagavadasādhāraṇaṃ svabhāvaṃ kṛtsnasya tadāyattasvarūpasthitipravṛttitāṃ ca bhagavatsakāśād upaśrutya evam eveti nityaś ca tathābhūtaṃ bhagavantaṃ sākṣātkartukāmo 'rjuna uvāca / tathaiva bhagavatprasādād anantaraṃ drakṣyati / "sarvāścaryamayaṃ devam anantaṃ viśvatomukham ... tatraikasthaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ pratibhaktam anekadhāḥ" iti hi vakṣyate /
body.translated_text: Thus, for the accomplishment and growth of <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (the discipline of devotion), there has been stated: the universal selfhood of the Lord, together with His host of auspicious qualities that are natural, unique to the Lord, and distinct from everything else; and therefore, the nature of the entire reality of the sentient and non-sentient other than Him as His body, with its existence, persistence, and activity dependent on Him. Having heard from the Lord this unique nature of the Lord and the dependence of everything's existence, persistence, and activity on Him, <s>Arjuna</s>, having determined 'it is indeed so,' and desiring to directly perceive the Lord as being of such a nature, which is eternal, spoke. And indeed by the grace of the Lord he will see [it] immediately after. For it will be stated: 'the God who is full of all wonders, infinite, with faces everywhere ... the entire universe gathered in one place, divided into manifold [parts].'

children.text: evaṃ bhakti-yoga-niṣpattaye tad-vivṛddhaye ca sakala-itara-vilakṣaṇena svābhāvikena bhagavad-asādhāraṇena kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇena saha bhagavataḥ sarva-ātmatvaṃ tata eva tad-vyatiriktasya kṛtsnasya cid-acid-ātmakasya vastu-jātasya tac-charīratayā tad-āyatta-sva-rūpa-sthiti-pravṛttitvaṃ ca uktam / tam etaṃ bhagavad-asādhāraṇaṃ sva-bhāvaṃ kṛtsnasya tad-āyatta-sva-rūpa-sthiti-pravṛttitāṃ ca bhagavat-sakāśād upaśrutya evam eva iti nityaś ca tathā-bhūtaṃ bhagavantaṃ sākṣāt-kartu-kāmo 'rjuna uvāca / tatha aiva bhagavat-prasādād anantaraṃ drakṣyati / "sarva-āścarya-mayaṃ devam anantaṃ viśvato-mukham ... tatra eka-sthaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ pratibhaktam anekadhāḥ" iti hi vakṣyate /
madanugrahāya paramaṃ guhyam adhyātmasaṃjñitam |
children.translated_text: 'For my grace, the supreme secret known as <s>adhyātma</s>,'

children.text: yat tvayoktaṃ vacas tena moho 'yaṃ vigato mama ||
children.translated_text: 'the words spoken by You — by those, this delusion of mine is dispelled.' ||

children.text: mad-anugrahāya paramaṃ guhyam adhyātma-saṃjñitam |
yat tvaya ūktaṃ vacas tena moho 'yaṃ vigato mama ||

body.text: dehātmābhimānarūpamohena mohitasya mamānugrahaikaprayojanāya paramaṃ guhyam paramaṃ rahasyam adhyātmasaṃjñitam ātmani vaktavyaṃ vacaḥ, "na tv evāhaṃ jātu nāsam" ityādi, "tasmād yogī bhavārjuna" ity etadantaṃ yat tvayoktam, tenāyam mamātmaviṣayo mohaḥ sarvo vigataḥ dūrato nirastaḥ //
body.translated_text: For me, who was deluded by the delusion in the form of the false identification of the self with the body — for my grace alone, the supreme secret, the supreme mystery, the words to be spoken concerning the self, designated as <s>adhyātma</s> — beginning with 'Never indeed was I non-existent' and ending with 'therefore be a <s>yogin</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>' — that which was spoken by You: by those [words], this entire delusion of mine concerning the self is gone, removed far away. //

children.text: deha-ātma-abhimāna-rūpa-mohena mohitasya mama anugraha-eka-prayojanāya paramaṃ guhyam paramaṃ rahasyam adhyātma-saṃjñitam ātmani vaktavyaṃ vacaḥ, "na tv eva ahaṃ jātu nā asam" ity-ādi, "tasmād yogī bhava arjuna" ity etad-antaṃ yat tvaya ūktam, tena ayam mamā atma-viṣayo mohaḥ sarvo vigataḥ dūrato nirastaḥ //

body.text: tathā ca --
body.translated_text: And moreover —

children.text: tathā ca ---
bhavāpyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā |
children.translated_text: 'The origin and dissolution of beings have been heard by me in detail,'

children.text: tvattaḥ kamalapatrākṣa māhātmyam api cāvyayam ||
children.translated_text: 'from You, O lotus-eyed one, and [Your] imperishable greatness as well.' ||

children.text: bhava-apyayau hi bhūtānāṃ śrutau vistaraśo mayā |
tvattaḥ kamala-patra-akṣa māhātmyam api ca avyayam ||

body.text: saptamaprabhṛti daśamaparyante tvadvyatiriktānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ tvattaḥ paramātmano bhavāpyayau utpattipralayau vistaraśo mayā śrutau hi / kamalapatrākṣa, tava avyayaṃ nityaṃ sarvacetanācetanavastuśeṣitvaṃ jñānabalādikalyāṇaguṇagaṇais tavaiva parataratvaṃ sarvādhāratvaṃ cintitanimiṣitādisarvapravṛttiṣu tavaiva pravartayitṛtvam ityādi aparimitaṃ māhātmyaṃ ca śrutam / hiśabdo vakṣyamāṇadidṛkṣādyotanārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: From the seventh [chapter] through the end of the tenth, the origin and dissolution of all beings other than You, from You, the Supreme Self — [these] have been heard by me in detail. O lotus-eyed one, Your imperishable — eternal — greatness has also been heard: Your being the master of all sentient and non-sentient entities, Your supreme transcendence through hosts of auspicious qualities such as knowledge, power, and the like, Your being the support of all, Your being the impeller in all activities such as thinking, blinking, and the like — [all] this immeasurable greatness has been heard. The particle 'hi' is for indicating the desire to see that will be stated [next]. //

children.text: saptama-prabhṛti daśama-paryante tvad-vyatiriktānāṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ tvattaḥ parama-ātmano bhava apyayau utpatti-pralayau vistaraśo mayā śrutau hi / kamala-patra-akṣa, tava avyayaṃ nityaṃ sarva-cetana-acetana-vastu-śeṣitvaṃ jñāna-bala-ādi-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇais tava eva parataratvaṃ sarva-ādhāratvaṃ cintita-nimiṣita-ādi-sarva-pravṛttiṣu tava eva pravartayitṛtvam ity-ādi aparimitaṃ māhātmyaṃ ca śrutam / hi-śabdo vakṣyamāṇa-didṛkṣā-dyotana-arthaḥ //
evam etad yathāttha tvam ātmānaṃ parameśvara |
children.translated_text: 'It is indeed so, as You declare Yourself, O Supreme Lord.'

children.text: draṣṭum icchāmi te rūpam aiśvaraṃ puruṣottama ||
children.translated_text: 'I desire to see Your sovereign form, O Supreme Person.' ||

children.text: evam etad yathā āttha tvam ātmānaṃ parama-īśvara |
draṣṭum icchāmi te rūpam aiśvaraṃ puruṣa-uttama ||

body.text: he parameśvara, evam etad ity avadhṛtam, yathātha tvam ātmānaṃ bravīṣi / puruṣottama āśritavātsalyajaladhe tavāiśvaraṃ tvadasādhāraṇaṃ sarvasya praśāsitṛtve, pālayitṛtve, sraṣṭṛtve, saṃhartṛtve bhartṛtve, kalyāṇaguṇākaratve, parataratve, sakaletaravisajātīyatve 'vasthitaṃ rūpaṃ draṣṭuṃ sākṣātkartum icchāmi //
body.translated_text: O Supreme Lord, it is indeed thus determined, as You declare — speak of — Yourself. O Supreme Person, ocean of affection for those who have taken refuge! I desire to see — to directly perceive — Your sovereign form: the form that is uniquely Yours, established in [Your being] the ruler, protector, creator, destroyer, sustainer, treasury of auspicious qualities, supremely transcendent, and entirely different from all else. //

children.text: he parama-īśvara, evam etad ity avadhṛtam, yathā ātha tvam ātmānaṃ bravīṣi / puruṣa-uttama āśrita-vātsalya-jaladhe tava aiśvaraṃ tvad-asādhāraṇaṃ sarvasya praśāsitṛtve, pālayitṛtve, sraṣṭṛtve, saṃhartṛtve bhartṛtve, kalyāṇa-guṇa-ākaratve, parataratve, sakala-itara-visajātīyatve 'vasthitaṃ rūpaṃ draṣṭuṃ sākṣātkartum icchāmi //
manyase yadi tac chakyaṃ mayā draṣṭum iti prabho |
children.translated_text: 'If You think it is possible for me to see that, O Lord,'

children.text: yogeśvara tato me tvaṃ darśayātmānam avyayam ||
children.translated_text: 'then, O Lord of <s>Yoga</s>, show me Your imperishable Self.' ||

children.text: manyase yadi tac chakyaṃ mayā draṣṭum iti prabho |
yoga-īśvara tato me tvaṃ darśayā atmānam avyayam ||

body.text: tat sarvasya sraṣṭṛ, sarvasya praśāsitṛ, sarvasyādhārabhūtaṃ tvadrūpaṃ mayā draṣṭuṃ śakyam iti yadi manyase, tato yogeśvara -- yogo jñānādikalyāṇaguṇayogaḥ, "paśya me yogam aiśvaram" iti hi vakṣyate -- tvadvyatiriktasya kasyāpy asaṃbhāvitānāṃ jñānabalāiśvaryavīryaśaktitejasāṃ nidhe! ātmānaṃ tvām avyayaṃ me darśaya / avyayam iti kriyāviśeṣaṇam / tvāṃ sakalaṃ me darśayetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: If You think that that form of Yours — which is the creator of all, the ruler of all, the support of all — is possible for me to see, then, O Lord of <s>Yoga</s> — <s>yoga</s> meaning the conjunction of auspicious qualities such as knowledge and the like; for it will be stated: 'behold My sovereign <s>yoga</s>' — O treasure-house of knowledge, power, sovereignty, valor, might, and splendor, which are inconceivable for anyone other than You! Show me Your imperishable self. 'Imperishable' is an adverb modifying the action [of showing] — the meaning is: show me Yourself completely. //

children.text: tat sarvasya sraṣṭṛ, sarvasya praśāsitṛ, sarvasyā adhāra-bhūtaṃ tvad-rūpaṃ mayā draṣṭuṃ śakyam iti yadi manyase, tato yoga-īśvara --- yogo jñāna-ādi-kalyāṇa-guṇa-yogaḥ, "paśya me yogam aiśvaram" iti hi vakṣyate --- tvad-vyatiriktasya kasya apy asaṃbhāvitānāṃ jñāna-bala-aiśvarya-vīrya-śakti-tejasāṃ nidhe! ātmānaṃ tvām avyayaṃ me darśaya / avyayam iti kriyā-viśeṣaṇam / tvāṃ sakalaṃ me darśaya ity-arthaḥ //

attributes.n: evaṃ kautūhalā1nvitena harṣa-gadgada-kaṇṭhena pārthena prārthito bhagavān uvāca ---

children.text: paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Behold, O <s>Pārtha</s>, My forms, by the hundreds and thousands,'

children.text: nānāvidhāni divyāni nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca ||
children.translated_text: 'of many kinds, divine, of various colors and shapes.' ||

children.text: paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ |
nānā-vidhāni divyāni nānā-varṇa-ākṛtīni ca ||

body.text: paśya me sarvāśrayāṇi rūpāṇi; atha śataśaḥ sahasraśaś ca nānāvidhāni nānāprakārāṇi, divyāni aprākṛtāni, nānāvarṇākṛtīni śuklakṛṣṇādinānāvarṇāni, nānākārāṇi ca paśya //
body.translated_text: Behold My forms that are the support of all. And [they are] by the hundreds and thousands, of many kinds — of many varieties, divine — non-material, of various colors and shapes — of various colors such as white, dark, and the like, and of various configurations — behold them! //

children.text: paśya me sarva-āśrayāṇi rūpāṇi; atha śataśaḥ sahasraśaś ca nānā-vidhāni nānā-prakārāṇi, divyāni aprākṛtāni, nānā-varṇa-ākṛtīni śukla-kṛṣṇa-ādi-nānā-varṇāni, nānā-ākārāṇi ca paśya //
paśyādityān vasūn rudrān aśvinau marutas tathā |
children.translated_text: 'Behold the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s> as well;'

children.text: bahūny adṛṣṭapūrvāṇi paśyāścaryāṇi bhārata ||
children.translated_text: 'behold many wonders never seen before, O <s>Bhārata</s>.' ||

children.text: paśyā adityān vasūn rudrān aśvinau marutas tathā |
bahūny adṛṣṭa-pūrvāṇi paśyā aścaryāṇi bhārata ||

body.text: mamaikasmin rūpe paśya ādityān dvādaśa, vasūn aṣṭau, rudrān ekādaśa, aśvinau dvau, marutaś caikonapañcāśatam / pradarśanārtham idam, iha jagati pratyakṣadṛṣṭāni śāstradṛṣṭāni ca yāni vastūni, tāni sarvāṇi, anyāny api sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu ca śāstreṣv adṛṣṭapūrvāṇi bahūny āścaryāṇi paśya //
body.translated_text: In My single form, behold the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, the eight <s>Vasus</s>, the eleven <s>Rudras</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, and the forty-nine <s>Maruts</s>. This is by way of illustration: behold all those entities that have been directly seen and known through scripture in this world — all of them, as well as many other wonders never seen before in any world or in any scripture. //

children.text: mama ekasmin rūpe paśya ādityān dvādaśa, vasūn aṣṭau, rudrān ekādaśa, aśvinau dvau, marutaś ca ekona-pañcāśatam / pradarśana-artham idam, iha jagati pratyakṣa-dṛṣṭāni śāstra-dṛṣṭāni ca yāni vastūni, tāni sarvāṇi, anyāny api sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu ca śāstreṣv adṛṣṭa-pūrvāṇi bahūny āścaryāṇi paśya //
ihaikasthaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ paśyādya sacarācaram |
children.translated_text: 'Behold here today the entire universe, moving and unmoving, gathered in one place,'

children.text: mama dehe guḍākeśa yac cānyad draṣṭum icchasi ||
children.translated_text: 'in My body, O <s>Guḍākeśa</s>, and whatever else you wish to see.' ||

children.text: iha eka-sthaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ paśya adya sacara-acaram |
mama dehe guḍākeśa yac ca anyad draṣṭum icchasi ||

body.text: iha mamaikasmin dehe, tatrāpi ekastham ekadeśasthaṃ sacarācaraṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagat paśya; yac cānyad draṣṭum icchasi, tad apy ekadehaikadeśa eva paśya //
body.translated_text: Here, in My single body, and moreover, gathered in one place — in a single location — behold the entire universe, with its moving and unmoving [beings]. And whatever else you wish to see, behold that too in a single location of [My] single body. //

children.text: iha mama ekasmin dehe, tatra api eka-stham eka-deśa-sthaṃ sacara-acaraṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagat paśya; yac ca anyad draṣṭum icchasi, tad apy eka-deha-eka-deśa eva paśya //
na tu māṃ śakṣyase draṣṭum anenaiva svacakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: 'But you cannot see Me with this your ordinary eye;'

children.text: divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogam aiśvaram ||
children.translated_text: 'I give you a divine eye — behold My sovereign <s>yoga</s>.' ||

children.text: na tu māṃ śakṣyase draṣṭum anena eva sva-cakṣuṣā |
divyaṃ dadāmi te cakṣuḥ paśya me yogam aiśvaram ||

body.text: ahaṃ mama dehaikadeśe sarvaṃ jagad darśayiṣyāmi; tvaṃ tv anena niyataparimitavastugrāhiṇā prākṛtena svacakṣuṣā, māṃ tathābhūtaṃ sakaletaravisajātīyam aparimeyaṃ draṣṭuṃ na śakṣyase / tava divyam aprākṛtaṃ maddarśanasādhanaṃ cakṣur dadāmi / paśya me yogam aiśvaram -- madasādhāraṇaṃ yogaṃ paśya; mamānantajñānādiyogam anantavibhūtiyogaṃ ca paśyetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: I shall show the entire universe in a single location of My body. But you, with this ordinary, material eye of yours — which grasps only limited and specific objects — will not be able to see Me, who am of such a nature, entirely different from everything else, and immeasurable. I give you a divine — non-material — eye that is the means of seeing Me. Behold My sovereign <s>yoga</s> — behold the <s>yoga</s> that is uniquely Mine. The meaning is: behold My infinite conjunction of knowledge and the like, and My infinite conjunction of manifestations. //

children.text: ahaṃ mama deha-eka-deśe sarvaṃ jagad darśayiṣyāmi; tvaṃ tv anena niyata-parimita-vastu-grāhiṇā prākṛtena sva-cakṣuṣā, māṃ tathā-bhūtaṃ sakala-itara-visajātīyam aparimeyaṃ draṣṭuṃ na śakṣyase / tava divyam aprākṛtaṃ mad-darśana-sādhanaṃ cakṣur dadāmi / paśya me yogam aiśvaram --- mad-asādhāraṇaṃ yogaṃ paśya; mama ananta-jñāna-ādi-yogam ananta-vibhūti-yogaṃ ca paśya ity-arthaḥ //
evam uktvā tato rājan mahāyogeśvaro hariḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having thus spoken, then, O king, <s>Hari</s>, the great Lord of <s>Yoga</s>,'

children.text: darśayām āsa pārthāya paramaṃ rūpam aiśvaram ||
children.translated_text: 'showed to <s>Pārtha</s> [His] supreme, sovereign form.' ||

children.text: evam uktvā tato rājan mahā-yoga-īśvaro hariḥ |
darśayām āsa pārthāya paramaṃ rūpam aiśvaram ||

body.text: evam uktvā sārathye 'vasthitaḥ pārthamātulajo mahāyogeśvaro hariḥ mahāścaryayogānām īśvaraḥ parabrahmabhūto nārāyaṇaḥ paramam aiśvaraṃ svāsādhāraṇaṃ rūpaṃ pārthāya pitṛṣvasuḥ pṛthāyāḥ putrāya darśayām āsa / tad vividhavicitranikhilajagadāśrayaṃ viśvasya praśāsitṛ ca rūpam; tac cedṛśam --
body.translated_text: Having thus spoken, the one stationed in the role of charioteer — the nephew of <s>Pārtha</s>'s mother — the great Lord of <s>Yoga</s>, the lord of great and wondrous <s>yogas</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who is the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, showed to <s>Pārtha</s> — the son of <s>Pṛthā</s>, his father's sister — His supreme, sovereign, uniquely His own form. That form was the support of the manifold and wondrous entire universe, and the ruler of the universe. And that [form] was of this nature —

children.text: evam uktvā sārathye 'vasthitaḥ pārtha-mātula-jo mahā-yoga-īśvaro hariḥ mahā-āścarya-yogānām īśvaraḥ para-brahma-bhūto nārāyaṇaḥ paramam aiśvaraṃ sva-asādhāraṇaṃ rūpaṃ pārthāya pitṛ-ṣvasuḥ pṛthāyāḥ putrāya darśayām āsa / tad vividha-vicitra-nikhila-jagad-āśrayaṃ viśvasya praśāsitṛ ca rūpam; tac cā idṛśam ---
anekavaktranayanam anekādbhutadarśanam |
children.translated_text: 'With many mouths and eyes, with many wondrous sights,'

children.text: anekadivyābharaṇaṃ divyānekodyatāyudham ||
children.translated_text: 'with many divine ornaments, with many divine weapons upraised,' ||

children.text: aneka-vaktra-nayanam aneka-adbhuta-darśanam |
aneka-divya-ābharaṇaṃ divya-aneka-udyata-āyudham ||
divyamālyāmbaradharaṃ divyagandhānulepanam |
children.translated_text: 'wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrances,'

children.text: sarvāścaryamayaṃ devam anantaṃ viśvatomukham ||
children.translated_text: 'full of all wonders, the God, infinite, with faces everywhere.' ||

children.text: divya-mālya-ambara-dharaṃ divya-gandha-anulepanam |
sarva-āścarya-mayaṃ devam anantaṃ viśvato-mukham ||

body.text: devaṃ dyotamānam, anantam kālatrayavarti; nikhilajagadāśrayatayā deśakālaparicchedānarham, viśvatomukham viśvadigvartimukham, svocitadivyāmbaragandhamālyābharaṇāyudhānvitam //
body.translated_text: The God (<s>deva</s>) — the shining one; infinite — existing across the three times; by virtue of being the support of the entire universe, not limited by space or time; with faces everywhere — with faces in every direction. Adorned with divine garments, fragrances, garlands, ornaments, and weapons befitting Him. //

children.text: devaṃ dyotamānam, anantam kāla-traya-varti; nikhila-jagad-āśrayatayā deśa-kāla-pariccheda-anarham, viśvato-mukham viśva-dig-varti-mukham, sva-ucita-divya-ambara-gandha-mālya-ābharaṇa-āyudha-anvitam //

body.text: tām eva devaśabdanirdiṣṭāṃ dyotamānatāṃ viśinaṣṭi --
body.translated_text: He elaborates on the shining quality indicated by the word <s>deva</s> —

children.text: tām eva deva-śabda-nirdiṣṭāṃ dyotamānatāṃ viśinaṣṭi ---
divi sūryasahasrasya bhaved yugapad utthitā |
children.translated_text: 'If the radiance of a thousand suns were to rise simultaneously in the sky,'

children.text: yadi bhāḥ, sadṛśī sā syād bhāsas tasya mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'that might be the likeness of the splendor of that great-souled one.' ||

children.text: divi sūrya-sahasrasya bhaved yugapad utthitā |
yadi bhāḥ, sadṛśī sā syād bhāsas tasya mahā-ātmanaḥ ||

body.text: tejaso 'parimitatvadarśanārtham idam; akṣayatejassvarūpam ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: This is to show the boundlessness of [His] radiance. The meaning is: His essential nature is of inexhaustible splendor. //

children.text: tejaso 'parimitatva-darśana-artham idam; akṣaya-tejas-sva-rūpam ity-arthaḥ //
tatraikasthaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ pravibhaktam anekadhā |
children.translated_text: 'There, in the body of the God of gods, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> then beheld'

children.text: apaśyad devadevasya śarīre pāṇḍavas tadā ||
children.translated_text: 'the entire universe gathered in one place, divided into many parts.' ||

children.text: tatra eka-sthaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ pravibhaktam anekadhā |
apaśyad deva-devasya śarīre pāṇḍavas tadā ||

body.text:
tatra anantāyām avistāre, anantabāhūdaravaktranetre, aparimitatejaske, aparimitadivyāyudhopete, svocitāparimitadivyabhūṣaṇe, divyamālyāmbaradhare, divyagandhānulepane, anantāścaryamaye, devadevasya divye śarīre anekadhā pravibhaktaṃ brahmādivividhavicitradevatiryaṅmanuṣyasthāvarādibhoktṛvargapṛthivyantarikṣasvargapātālātalavitalasutalādibhogasthānabhogyabhogopakaraṇabhedabhinnaṃ prakṛtipuruṣātmakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagat, "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate", "hanta te kathayiṣyāmi vibhūtīr ātmanaś śubhāḥ", "aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ", ādityānām ahaṃ viṣṇuḥ" ityādinā, "na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ carācaram", "viṣṭabhyāham idaṃ kṛtsnam ekāṃśena sthito jagat" ityantenoditam, ekastham ekadeśastham;
pāṇḍavo bhagavatprasādalabdhataddarśanānuguṇadivyacakṣur apaśyat //
body.translated_text: There — in that infinite expanse; in that form of infinite arms, bellies, faces, and eyes; of boundless splendor; equipped with boundless divine weapons; adorned with befitting boundless divine ornaments; wearing divine garlands and garments; anointed with divine fragrances; full of infinite wonders — in the divine body of the God of gods: the entire universe consisting of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, divided into the manifold and diverse classes of enjoyers — gods, animals, humans, plants, and the like beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> — and the places of enjoyment — earth, atmosphere, heaven, the nether worlds <s>Atala</s>, <s>Vitala</s>, <s>Sutala</s>, and the like — and the objects of enjoyment and the instruments of enjoyment; [all of which had been described] beginning with 'I am the origin of all; from Me everything proceeds,' 'Lo, I shall declare to you My auspicious manifestations,' 'I am the Self, O <s>Guḍākeśa</s>, seated in the hearts of all beings,' 'Of <s>Ādityas</s>, I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>,' and so on through 'there is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist without Me,' 'I stand sustaining this entire universe with a single fraction' — [all this] gathered in one place, in a single location, the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, with the divine eye obtained by the Lord's grace and suitable for seeing that [form], beheld. //

children.text:
tatra anantāyām avistāre, ananta-bāhu-udara-vaktra-netre, aparimita-tejaske, aparimita-divya-āyudha-upete, sva-ucita-aparimita-divya-bhūṣaṇe, divya-mālya-ambara-dhare, divya-gandha-anulepane, ananta-āścarya-maye, deva-devasya divye śarīre anekadhā pravibhaktaṃ brahmā-ādi-vividha-vicitra-deva-tiryaṅ-manuṣya-sthāvara-ādi-bhoktṛ-varga-pṛthivy-antarikṣa-svarga-pātāla-atala-vitala-sutala-ādi-bhoga-sthāna-bhogya-bhoga-upakaraṇa-bheda-bhinnaṃ prakṛti-puruṣa-ātmakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagat, "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate", "hanta te kathayiṣyāmi vibhūtīr ātmanaś śubhāḥ", "aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarva-bhūta-āśaya-sthitaḥ", ādityānām ahaṃ viṣṇuḥ" ity-ādinā, "na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ cara-acaram", "viṣṭabhya aham idaṃ kṛtsnam eka-aṃśena sthito jagat" ity-antena uditam, eka-stham eka-deśa-stham;
pāṇḍavo bhagavat-prasāda-labdha-tad-darśana-anuguṇa-divya-cakṣur apaśyat //
tatas sa vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭaromā dhanañjayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Then he, <s>Dhanañjaya</s>, filled with wonder, his hair standing on end,'

children.text: praṇamya śirasā devaṃ kṛtāñjalir abhāṣata ||
children.translated_text: 'bowing his head before the God, spoke with joined palms.' ||

children.text: tatas sa vismaya-āviṣṭo hṛṣṭa-romā dhanañjayaḥ |
praṇamya śirasā devaṃ kṛta-añjalir abhāṣata ||

body.text: tato dhanañjayo mahāścaryasya kṛtsnasya jagataḥ svadehaikadeśenāśrayabhūtaṃ kṛtsnasya pravartayitāraṃ ca āścaryatamānantajñānādikalyāṇaguṇagaṇaṃ devaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayāviṣṭo hṛṣṭaromā śirasā daṇḍavat praṇamya kṛtāñjalir abhāṣata //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Dhanañjaya</s>, having seen the Lord — who in a single portion of His own body served as the support of the entire wondrous universe and was the impeller of everything, possessing the most wondrous infinite host of auspicious qualities such as knowledge and the like — was filled with amazement, his hair standing on end, and bowing down prostrate with his head, spoke with joined palms. //

children.text: tato dhanañjayo mahā-āścaryasya kṛtsnasya jagataḥ sva-deha-eka-deśenā aśraya-bhūtaṃ kṛtsnasya pravartayitāraṃ ca āścaryatama-ananta-jñāna-ādi-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇaṃ devaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismaya-āviṣṭo hṛṣṭa-romā śirasā daṇḍavat praṇamya kṛta-añjalir abhāṣata //
paśyāmi devāṃs tava deva dehe sarvāṃs tathā bhūtaviśeṣasaṅgān |
children.translated_text: 'I see the gods in Your body, O Lord, and likewise all the hosts of various beings,' |

children.text: brahmāṇam īśaṃ kamalāsanastham ṛṣīṃś ca sarvān uragāṃś ca dīptān ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Brahmā</s> the lord seated on the lotus, and all the sages, and the radiant serpents.' ||

children.text: paśyāmi devāṃs tava deva dehe sarvāṃs tathā bhūta-viśeṣa-saṅgān |
brahmāṇam īśaṃ kamala-āsana-stham ṛṣīṃś ca sarvān uragāṃś ca dīptān ||

body.text: deva; tava dehe sarvān devān paśyāmi; tathā sarvān prāṇiviśeṣāṇāṃ saṃghān, tathā brahmāṇaṃ caturmukham aṇḍādhipatim, tatheśaṃ kamalāsanasthaṃ -- kamalāsane brahmaṇi sthitam īśaṃ tanmate 'vasthitaṃ tathā devarṣipramukhān sarvān ṛṣīn, uragāṃś ca vāsukitakṣakādīn dīptān //
body.translated_text: O Lord, I see all the gods in Your body; likewise all the assemblages of the various living beings; likewise four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>, the overlord of the cosmic egg; likewise the lord seated on the lotus — the lord established in <s>Brahmā</s> who is the lotus-seat, that is, established in his doctrine; likewise all the sages headed by the divine sages; and the serpents — <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, and others — radiant. //

children.text: deva; tava dehe sarvān devān paśyāmi; tathā sarvān prāṇi-viśeṣāṇāṃ saṃghān, tathā brahmāṇaṃ catur-mukham aṇḍa-adhipatim, tathā īśaṃ kamala-āsana-sthaṃ --- kamala-āsane brahmaṇi sthitam īśaṃ tan-mate 'vasthitaṃ tathā deva-rṣi-pramukhān sarvān ṛṣīn, uragāṃś ca vāsuki-takṣaka-ādīn dīptān //
anekabāhūdaravaktranetraṃ paśyāmi tvāṃ sarvato 'nantarūpam |
children.translated_text: 'With many arms, bellies, faces, and eyes, I see You, infinite in form on every side.' |

children.text: nāntaṃ na madhyaṃ na punas tavādiṃ paśyāmi viśveśvara viśvarūpa ||
children.translated_text: 'Neither end nor middle nor again Your beginning do I see, O Lord of the universe, O Universal Form.' ||

children.text: aneka-bāhu-udara-vaktra-netraṃ paśyāmi tvāṃ sarvato 'nanta-rūpam |
na antaṃ na madhyaṃ na punas tavā adiṃ paśyāmi viśva-īśvara viśva-rūpa ||

body.text: anekabāhūdaravaktranetram anantarūpaṃ tvāṃ sarvataḥ paśyāmi; viśveśvara -- viśvasya niyantaḥ, viśvarūpa -- viśvaśarīra! yatas tvam anantaḥ, atas tava nāntaṃ na madhyaṃ na punas tavādiṃ ca paśyāmi //
body.translated_text: I see You on every side, with many arms, bellies, faces, and eyes, of infinite form. O Lord of the universe — O controller of the universe! O Universal Form — O one whose body is the universe! Since You are infinite, therefore I see neither Your end, nor Your middle, nor again Your beginning. //

children.text: aneka-bāhu-udara-vaktra-netram ananta-rūpaṃ tvāṃ sarvataḥ paśyāmi; viśva-īśvara --- viśvasya niyantaḥ, viśva-rūpa --- viśva-śarīra! yatas tvam anantaḥ, atas tava na antaṃ na madhyaṃ na punas tavā adiṃ ca paśyāmi //
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakriṇaṃ ca tejorāśiṃ sarvato dīptim antam |
children.translated_text: 'Wearing a crown, bearing a mace and a discus, a mass of radiance, shining everywhere,' |

children.text: paśyāmi tvā durnirīkṣaṃ samantād dīptānalārkadyutim aprameyam ||
children.translated_text: 'I see You, difficult to behold on all sides, with the brilliance of blazing fire and sun, immeasurable.' ||

children.text: kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakriṇaṃ ca tejo-rāśiṃ sarvato dīptim antam |
paśyāmi tvā durnirīkṣaṃ samantād dīpta-anala-arka-dyutim aprameyam ||

body.text: tejorāśiṃ sarvato dīptimantaṃ samantād durnirīkṣaṃ dīptānalārkadyutim aprameyaṃ tvāṃ kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakriṇaṃ ca paśyāmi //
body.translated_text: I see You — a mass of radiance, shining everywhere, difficult to behold on all sides, with the brilliance of blazing fire and sun, immeasurable — wearing a crown, bearing a mace and a discus. //

children.text: tejo-rāśiṃ sarvato dīptimantaṃ samantād durnirīkṣaṃ dīpta-anala-arka-dyutim aprameyaṃ tvāṃ kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakriṇaṃ ca paśyāmi //
tvam akṣaraṃ paramaṃ veditavyaṃ tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam |
children.translated_text: 'You are the supreme imperishable to be known; You are the ultimate resting place of this universe.' |

children.text: tvam avyayaḥ śāśvatadharmagoptā sanātanas tvaṃ puruṣo mato me ||
children.translated_text: 'You are the inexhaustible one, the guardian of the eternal <s>dharma</s>; You are the eternal Person — such is my conviction.' ||

children.text: tvam akṣaraṃ paramaṃ veditavyaṃ tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam |
tvam avyayaḥ śāśvata-dharma-goptā sanātanas tvaṃ puruṣo mato me ||

body.text: upaniṣatsu, "dve vidye veditavye" ityādiṣu veditavyatayā nirdiṣṭaṃ paramam akṣaraṃ tvam eva; asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam viśvasyāsya paramādhārabhūtas tvam eva; tvam avyayaḥ vyayarahitaḥ; yat svarūpo yadguṇo yadvibhavaś ca tvam, tenaiva rūpeṇa sarvadāvatiṣṭhase / śāśvatadharmagoptā śāśvatasya nityasya vaidikasya dharmasya evam ādibhir avatārais tvam eva goptā / sanātanas tvaṃ puruṣo mato me -- "vedāham etaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntaṃ", "parāt paraṃ puruṣam" ityādiṣūditaḥ sanātanapuruṣas tvam eveti me mataḥ jñātaḥ / yad ukulatilakas tvam evaṃbhūta idānīṃ sākṣātkṛto mayetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, in passages such as 'Two knowledges are to be known' and the like, that which is indicated as the supreme imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) to be known — that is You alone. The ultimate resting place of this universe — the one who is the supreme substratum of this entire universe — that is You alone. You are the inexhaustible one — devoid of decay. Whatever is Your essential nature, whatever are Your qualities, whatever is Your sovereign glory — You abide always in that very form. The guardian of the eternal <s>dharma</s> — of the eternal, perpetual Vedic <s>dharma</s>, You alone are the protector through descents (<s>avatāras</s>) such as these. 'You are the eternal Person — such is my conviction' — the eternal Person spoken of in [<s>śrutis</s> such as] 'I know this great Person,' 'the Person beyond the beyond' — that You are that eternal Person, this is my conviction, my knowledge. The import is: You who are of such nature have now been directly perceived by me. //

children.text: upaniṣatsu, "dve vidye veditavye" ity-ādiṣu veditavyatayā nirdiṣṭaṃ paramam akṣaraṃ tvam eva; asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam viśvasya asya parama-ādhāra-bhūtas tvam eva; tvam avyayaḥ vyaya-rahitaḥ; yat sva-rūpo yad-guṇo yad-vibhavaś ca tvam, tena eva rūpeṇa sarvada āvatiṣṭhase / śāśvata-dharma-goptā śāśvatasya nityasya vaidikasya dharmasya evam ādibhir avatārais tvam eva goptā / sanātanas tvaṃ puruṣo mato me --- "veda aham etaṃ puruṣaṃ mahā-antaṃ", "parāt paraṃ puruṣam" ity-ādiṣu uditaḥ sanātana-puruṣas tvam eva iti me mataḥ jñātaḥ / yad ukula-tilakas tvam evaṃ-bhūta idānīṃ sākṣāt-kṛto maya īty-arthaḥ //
anādimadhyāntam anantavīryam anantabāhuṃ śaśisūryanetram |
children.translated_text: 'Without beginning, middle, or end, of infinite power, with infinite arms, with the moon and sun as eyes,' |

children.text: paśyāmi tvā dīptahutāśavaktraṃ svatejasā viśvam idaṃ tapantam ||
children.translated_text: 'I see You, with blazing fire as Your mouth, heating this universe with Your own radiance.' ||

children.text: an-ādi-madhya-antam ananta-vīryam ananta-bāhuṃ śaśi-sūrya-netram |
paśyāmi tvā dīpta-huta-āśa-vaktraṃ sva-tejasā viśvam idaṃ tapantam ||

body.text:
anādimadhyāntam ādimadhyāntarahitam / anantavīryam anavadhikātiśayavīryam; vīryaśabdaḥ pradarśanārthaḥ; anavadhikātiśayajñānabalāiśvaryavīryaśaktitejasāṃ nidhim ityarthaḥ / anantabāhum asaṃkhyeyabāhum / so 'pi pradarśanārthaḥ; anantabāhūdarapādavaktrādikam / śaśisūryanetram śaśivat sūryavac ca prasādapratāpayuktasarvanetram / devādīn anukūlān namaskārādi kurvāṇān prati prasādaḥ, tadviparītān asurarākṣasādīn prati pratāpaḥ; "rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti sarve namasyanti ca siddhasaṃghāḥ" iti hi vakṣyate / dīptahutāśavaktram pradīptakālānalavat saṃhārānuguṇavaktram / svatejasā viśvam idaṃ tapantam / tejaḥ parābhibhavanasāmarthyam; svakīyena tejasā viśvam idaṃ tapantaṃ tvāṃ paśyāmi -- evambhūtaṃ sarvasya
sraṣṭāraṃ sarvasyādhārabhūtaṃ sarvasya praśāsitāraṃ sarvasya saṃhartāraṃ jñānādyaparimitaguṇasāgaram ādimadhyāntarahitam evaṃbhūtadivyadehaṃ tvāṃ yathopadeśaṃ sākṣātkaromītyarthaḥ / ekasmin divyadehe anekodarādikaṃ katham? / ittham upapadyate / ekasmāt kaṭipradeśād anantaparimāṇād ūrdhvam udgatā yathoditodarādayaḥ, adhaś ca yathoditadivyapādāḥ; tatraikasmin mukhe netradvayam iti ca na virodhaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Without beginning, middle, or end' — devoid of beginning, middle, and end. 'Of infinite power' — of immeasurably surpassing power; the word 'power' (<s>vīrya</s>) is used representatively, meaning: a treasury of immeasurably surpassing knowledge, strength, sovereignty, power, might, and splendor. 'With infinite arms' — with innumerable arms; this too is representative: with infinite arms, bellies, feet, faces, and the like. 'With the moon and sun as eyes' — having all eyes endowed with grace and majesty like the moon and sun. Grace toward the favorable ones — the gods and others who offer salutations and the like; majesty toward those opposed — the <s>asuras</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and the like. For it will be said: 'The <s>rākṣasas</s> flee in terror to all directions, and all the hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> bow in reverence.' 'With blazing fire as mouth' — with mouths suited for universal dissolution, like blazing fire at the end of time. 'Heating this universe with Your own radiance' — radiance (<s>tejas</s>) is the capacity to overpower others; I see You heating this entire universe with Your own radiance — [I see You] who are thus the creator of all, the substratum of all, the ruler of all, the destroyer of all, an ocean of immeasurable qualities such as knowledge and the like, devoid of beginning, middle, and end, possessing such a divine body — I directly perceive You as taught — this is the meaning. How can there be multiple bellies and the like in a single divine body? This is explained thus: from a single waist-region of infinite dimension, the above-described bellies and the like extend upward, and the described divine feet extend downward; and there is no contradiction in having two eyes in each single face. //

children.text:
an-ādi-madhya-antam ādi-madhya-anta-rahitam / ananta-vīryam anavadhika-atiśaya-vīryam; vīrya-śabdaḥ pradarśana-arthaḥ; anavadhika-atiśaya-jñāna-bala-aiśvarya-vīrya-śakti-tejasāṃ nidhim ity-arthaḥ / ananta-bāhum asaṃkhyeya-bāhum / so 'pi pradarśana-arthaḥ; ananta-bāhu-udara-pāda-vaktra-ādikam / śaśi-sūrya-netram śaśivat sūryavac ca prasāda-pratāpa-yukta-sarva-netram / deva-ādīn anukūlān namaskāra-ādi kurvāṇān prati prasādaḥ, tad-viparītān asura-rākṣasa-ādīn prati pratāpaḥ; "rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti sarve namasyanti ca siddha-saṃghāḥ" iti hi vakṣyate / dīpta-huta-āśa-vaktram pradīpta-kāla-analavat saṃhāra-anuguṇa-vaktram / sva-tejasā viśvam idaṃ tapantam / tejaḥ para-abhibhavana-sāmarthyam; svakīyena tejasā viśvam idaṃ tapantaṃ tvāṃ paśyāmi --- evam-bhūtaṃ sarvasya
sraṣṭāraṃ sarvasyā adhāra-bhūtaṃ sarvasya praśāsitāraṃ sarvasya saṃhartāraṃ jñāna-ādy-aparimita-guṇa-sāgaram ādi-madhya-anta-rahitam evaṃ-bhūta-divya-dehaṃ tvāṃ yatha ūpadeśaṃ sākṣātkaromi ity-arthaḥ / ekasmin divya-dehe aneka-udara-ādikaṃ katham? / ittham upapadyate / ekasmāt kaṭi-pradeśād ananta-parimāṇād ūrdhvam udgatā yathā-udita-udara-ādayaḥ, adhaś ca yathā-udita-divya-pādāḥ; tatra ekasmin mukhe netra-dvayam iti ca na virodhaḥ //

body.text: evaṃbhūtaṃ tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā devādayo 'haṃ ca pravyathitā bhavāma ity āha --
body.translated_text: Having seen You who are of such a nature, the gods and I are greatly agitated — thus he says:

children.text: evaṃ-bhūtaṃ tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā deva-ādayo 'haṃ ca pravyathitā bhavāma ity āha ---
dyāvāpṛthivyor idam antaraṃ hi vyāptaṃ tvayaikena diśaś ca sarvāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, this space between heaven and earth is pervaded by You alone, and all the directions.' |

children.text: dṛṣṭvādbhutaṃ rūpam ugraṃ tad evaṃ lokatrayaṃ pravyathitaṃ mahātman ||
children.translated_text: 'Having seen this wondrous and terrible form of Yours, the three worlds tremble, O great-souled one.' ||

children.text: dyāvā-pṛthivyor idam antaraṃ hi vyāptaṃ tvaya aikena diśaś ca sarvāḥ |
dṛṣṭva ādbhutaṃ rūpam ugraṃ tad evaṃ loka-trayaṃ pravyathitaṃ mahā-ātman ||

body.text:
dyuśabdaḥ pṛthivīśabdaś cobhau uparitanānām adhastanānāṃ ca lokānāṃ pradarśanārthau / dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ antaram avakāśaḥ / yasminn avakāse sarve lokās tiṣṭhanti, sarvo 'yam avakāśo diśaś ca sarvās tvayaikena vyāptāḥ / dṛṣṭvādbhutaṃ rūpam ugraṃ tavedam anantāyām avistāram atyadbhutam atyugraṃ ca rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā lokatrayaṃ pravyathitam yuddhadidṛkṣayā āgateṣu brahmādidevāsurapitṛgaṇasiddhagandharvayakṣarākṣaseṣu pratikūlānukūlamadhyastharūpaṃ lokatrayaṃ sarvaṃ pravyathitam atyantabhītam / mahātman aparicchedyamanovṛtte / eteṣām apy arjunasyaiva viśvāśrayarūpasākṣātkārasādhanaṃ divyaṃ cakṣur bhagavatā dattam / kim artham iti cet, arjunāya svāiśvaryaṃ sarvaṃ pradarśayitum / ata idam ucyate, "dṛṣṭvādbhutaṃ
rūpam ugraṃ tavedaṃ lokatrayaṃ pravyarthitaṃ mahātman" iti //
body.translated_text: The words 'heaven' (<s>dyu</s>) and 'earth' (<s>pṛthivī</s>) are both representative of the upper and lower worlds respectively. The space between heaven and earth is the expanse — the expanse in which all worlds subsist. This entire expanse and all directions are pervaded by You alone. 'Having seen this wondrous and terrible form of Yours' — having seen this form of immeasurable extent, supremely wondrous and supremely terrible, the three worlds tremble. Among those who had come with the desire to witness the battle — <s>Brahmā</s>, the gods, <s>asuras</s>, <s>pitṛs</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s> — the three worlds in the threefold form of those opposed, those favorable, and those neutral, all are greatly agitated, exceedingly terrified. 'O great-souled one' — O one whose mental disposition is incomprehensible! Even for these, the divine eye that is the means of directly perceiving the universal-support form was given by the Lord to <s>Arjuna</s> alone. For what purpose? To display to <s>Arjuna</s> all His sovereign glory. Hence it is said: 'Having seen this wondrous and terrible form of Yours, the three worlds tremble, O great-souled one.' //

children.text:
dyu-śabdaḥ pṛthivī-śabdaś ca ubhau uparitanānām adhastanānāṃ ca lokānāṃ pradarśana-arthau / dyāvā-pṛthivyoḥ antaram avakāśaḥ / yasminn avakāse sarve lokās tiṣṭhanti, sarvo 'yam avakāśo diśaś ca sarvās tvaya aikena vyāptāḥ / dṛṣṭva ādbhutaṃ rūpam ugraṃ tava idam anantāyām avistāram atyadbhutam atyugraṃ ca rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā loka-trayaṃ pravyathitam yuddha-didṛkṣayā āgateṣu brahmā-ādi-deva-asura-pitṛ-gaṇa-siddha-gandharva-yakṣa-rākṣaseṣu pratikūla-anukūla-madhya-stha-rūpaṃ loka-trayaṃ sarvaṃ pravyathitam atyanta-bhītam / mahā-ātman aparicchedya-mano-vṛtte / eteṣām apy arjunasya eva viśva-āśraya-rūpa-sākṣātkāra-sādhanaṃ divyaṃ cakṣur bhagavatā dattam / kim artham iti cet, arjunāya sva-aiśvaryaṃ sarvaṃ pradarśayitum / ata idam ucyate, "dṛṣṭva ādbhutaṃ
rūpam ugraṃ tava idaṃ loka-trayaṃ pravyarthitaṃ mahā-ātman" iti //
amī hi tvā surasaṅghā viśanti kecid bhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛṇanti |
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, these hosts of gods enter into You; some, terrified, praise You with joined palms.' |

children.text: svastīty uktvā maharṣisiddhasaṅghāḥ stuvanti tvāṃ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Having said "Hail!" the hosts of great sages and <s>Siddhas</s> praise You with abundant hymns.' ||

children.text: amī hi tvā sura-saṅghā viśanti kecid bhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛṇanti |
svasti ity uktvā maha-rṣi-siddha-saṅghāḥ stuvanti tvāṃ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ ||

body.text: amī surasaṃghāḥ utkṛṣṭās tvāṃ viśvāśrayam avalokya hṛṣṭamanasaḥ tvan samīpaṃ viśanti / teṣv eva kecid atyugram atyadbhutaṃ ca tavākāram ālokya bhītāḥ prāñjalayaḥ svajñānānuguṇaṃ stutirūpāṇi vākyāni gṛṇanti uccārayanti / apare maharṣisaṃghāḥ siddhasaṃghāś ca parāvaratattvayāthātmyavidaḥ svastīty uktvā puṣkalābhir bhavadanurūpābhiḥ stutibhiḥ stuvanti //
body.translated_text: These exalted hosts of gods, beholding You as the support of the universe, enter Your proximity with joyful hearts. Among them, some, seeing Your exceedingly terrible and exceedingly wondrous form, are terrified and with joined palms utter words in the form of praise appropriate to their own knowledge. Others — hosts of great sages and hosts of <s>Siddhas</s>, who know the true nature of both the higher and the lower reality — having said 'Hail!', praise You with abundant hymns befitting Your nature. //

children.text: amī sura-saṃghāḥ utkṛṣṭās tvāṃ viśva-aśrayam avalokya hṛṣṭa-manasaḥ tvan samīpaṃ viśanti / teṣv eva kecid atyugram atyadbhutaṃ ca tavā akāram ālokya bhītāḥ prāñjalayaḥ sva-jñāna-anuguṇaṃ stuti-rūpāṇi vākyāni gṛṇanti uccārayanti / apare maha-rṣi-saṃghāḥ siddha-saṃghāś ca para-avara-tattva-yāthātmya-vidaḥ svasti ity uktvā puṣkalābhir bhavad-anurūpābhiḥ stutibhiḥ stuvanti //
rudrādityā vasavo ye ca sādhyā viśve 'śvinau marutaś coṣmapāś ca |
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, and the <s>Sādhyas</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the <s>Aśvins</s>, the <s>Maruts</s>, and the <s>Ūṣmapās</s>,' |

children.text: gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṅghā vīkṣyante tvāṃ vismitāś caiva sarve ||
children.translated_text: 'the hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Siddhas</s> — all gaze upon You in wonder.' ||

children.text: rudra-ādityā vasavo ye ca sādhyā viśve 'śvinau marutaś cā uṣma-pāś ca |
gandharva-yakṣa-asura-siddha-saṅghā vīkṣyante tvāṃ vismitāś ca eva sarve ||

body.text: ūṣmapāḥ pitaraḥ, "ūṣmabhāgā hi pitaraḥ" iti śruteḥ / ete sarve vismayam āpannās tvāṃ vīkṣante //
body.translated_text: The <s>Ūṣmapās</s> are the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors), as per the <s>śruti</s>: 'For the ancestors are partakers of the steam.' All these, filled with wonder, gaze upon You. //

children.text: ūṣma-pāḥ pitaraḥ, "ūṣma-bhāgā hi pitaraḥ" iti śruteḥ / ete sarve vismayam āpannās tvāṃ vīkṣante //
rūpaṃ mahat te bahuvaktranetraṃ mahābāho bahubāhūrupādam |
children.translated_text: 'Your great form with many faces, eyes, O mighty-armed one, with many arms, thighs, and feet,' |

children.text: bahūdaraṃ bahudaṃṣṭrākarālaṃ dṛṣṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitās tathāham ||
children.translated_text: 'with many bellies, terrible with many tusks — seeing it, the worlds are agitated, and so am I.' ||

children.text: rūpaṃ mahat te bahu-vaktra-netraṃ mahābāho bahu-bāhu-uru-pādam |
bahu-udaraṃ bahu-daṃṣṭrā-karālaṃ dṛṣṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitās tatha āham ||

body.text: bahvībhir daṃṣṭrābhir atibhīṣaṇākāraṃ lokāḥ pūrvoktāḥ pratikūlānukūlamadhyasthās trividhāḥ sarva eva ahaṃ ca tad evam īdṛśaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā atīva vyathitā bhavāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Of exceedingly terrifying appearance due to numerous tusks — the previously mentioned worlds of three kinds — those opposed, those favorable, and those neutral — all of them and I too, having seen such a form as this, are exceedingly agitated. //

children.text: bahvībhir daṃṣṭrābhir atibhīṣaṇa-ākāraṃ lokāḥ pūrva-uktāḥ pratikūla-anukūla-madhya-sthās tri-vidhāḥ sarva eva ahaṃ ca tad evam īdṛśaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā atīva vyathitā bhavāmaḥ //
nabhasspṛśaṃ dīptam anekavarṇaṃ vyāttānanaṃ dīptaviśālanetram |
children.translated_text: 'Touching the sky, blazing, of many colors, with gaping mouths, with blazing, wide eyes,' |

children.text: dṛsṭvā hi tvā pravyathitāntarātmā dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi śamaṃ ca viṣṇo ||
children.translated_text: 'having seen You thus, my inner self is agitated; I find neither courage nor peace, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' ||

children.text: nabhas-spṛśaṃ dīptam aneka-varṇaṃ vyātta-ānanaṃ dīpta-viśāla-netram |
dṛsṭvā hi tvā pravyathita-antar-ātmā dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi śamaṃ ca viṣṇo ||

body.text: namaśśabdaḥ "tad akṣare parame vyoman", "ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt", "kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāke", "yo asyādhyakṣaḥ parame vyoman" ityādiśrutisiddhitriguṇaprakṛtyatītaparamavyomavācī; savikārasya prakṛtitattvasya, puruṣasya ca sarvāvasthasya, kṛtsnasyāśrayatayā nabhas spṛśam iti vacanāt; "dyāvāpṛthivyor idam antaraṃ hi vyāptam" iti pūrvoktatvāc ca / dīptam anekavarṇaṃ vyāttānanaṃ dīptaviśālanetraṃ tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā pravyathitāntarātmā atyantabhītamanāḥ dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi dehasya dhāraṇaṃ na labhe, manasaś cendriyāṇāṃ ca śamaṃ na labhe / viṣṇo vyāpin! / sarvavyāpinam atimātram atyadbhutam atighoraṃ ca tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā praśithikasarvāvayavo vyākulendriyaś ca bhavāmītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The word 'sky' (<s>nabhas</s>) refers to the supreme space (<s>parama-vyoman</s>) beyond the three <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s>, established in <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'In that imperishable, supreme space,' 'Sun-colored, beyond darkness,' 'In the far side of this rajas, as it wanes,' 'He who is its overseer in the supreme space.' It is said 'touching the sky' because [the Lord] serves as the support by being the substratum of the evolved <s>Prakṛti</s> and of the soul in all its states; and because it was previously stated: 'This space between heaven and earth is pervaded [by You].' Blazing, of many colors, with gaping mouths, with blazing, wide eyes — having seen You thus, my inner self is agitated — my mind is exceedingly terrified; I find no courage — I cannot hold my body steady; and I find no peace of mind and senses. O <s>Viṣṇu</s> — O all-pervading one! Having seen You who are all-pervading, exceedingly wondrous, and exceedingly terrible, I become loosened in all my limbs and confused in all my senses — this is the meaning. //

children.text: namaś-śabdaḥ "tad akṣare parame vyoman", "āditya-varṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt", "kṣayantam asya rajasaḥ parāke", "yo asya adhyakṣaḥ parame vyoman" ity-ādi-śruti-siddhi-tri-guṇa-prakṛty-atīta-parama-vyoma-vācī; savikārasya prakṛti-tattvasya, puruṣasya ca sarva-avasthasya, kṛtsnasyā aśrayatayā nabhas spṛśam iti vacanāt; "dyāvā-pṛthivyor idam antaraṃ hi vyāptam" iti pūrva-uktatvāc ca / dīptam aneka-varṇaṃ vyātta-ānanaṃ dīpta-viśāla-netraṃ tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā pravyathita-antara-ātmā atyanta-bhīta-manāḥ dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi dehasya dhāraṇaṃ na labhe, manasaś ca indriyāṇāṃ ca śamaṃ na labhe / viṣṇo vyāpin! / sarva-vyāpinam atimātram atyadbhutam atighoraṃ ca tvāṃ dṛṣṭvā praśithika-sarva-avayavo vyākula-indriyaś ca bhavāmi ity-arthaḥ //
daṃṣṭrākarālāni ca te mukhāni dṛṣṭvaiva kālānalasannibhāni |
children.translated_text: 'And seeing Your mouths terrible with tusks, resembling the fire of universal dissolution,' |

children.text: diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa ||
children.translated_text: 'I know not the directions, nor do I find comfort. Be gracious, O Lord of the gods, O abode of the universe.' ||

children.text: daṃṣṭrā-karālāni ca te mukhāni dṛṣṭva aiva kāla-anala-sannibhāni |
diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma prasīda deva-īśa jagan-nivāsa ||

body.text: yugāntakālānalavat sarvasaṃhāre pravṛttāni atighorāṇi tava mukhāni dṛṣṭvā diśo na jāne; sukhaṃ ca na labhe / jagatāṃ nivāsa deveśa brahmādīnām īśvarāṇām api paramamaheśvara! māṃ prati prasanno bhava / yathāhaṃ prakṛtiṃ gato bhavāmi, tathā kurv ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Having seen Your mouths, exceedingly terrible, engaged in total destruction like the fire at the end of an age, I know not the directions; nor do I find happiness. O abode of the universe, O Lord of the gods — O supreme great Lord even of lords such as <s>Brahmā</s> and others! Be gracious toward me. Make it so that I return to my normal state — this is the meaning. //

children.text: yuga-anta-kāla-analavat sarva-saṃhāre pravṛttāni atighorāṇi tava mukhāni dṛṣṭvā diśo na jāne; sukhaṃ ca na labhe / jagatāṃ nivāsa deva-īśa brahma-ādīnām īśvarāṇām api parama-mahā-īśvara! māṃ prati prasanno bhava / yatha āhaṃ prakṛtiṃ gato bhavāmi, tathā kurv ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: evaṃ sarvasya jagataḥ svāyattasthitipravṛttitvaṃ darśayan pārthasārathī rājaveṣacchadmanāvasthitānāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ yaudhiṣṭhireṣv anupraviṣṭānāṃ ca asurāṃśānāṃ saṃhāreṇa bhūbhārāvataraṇaṃ svamanīṣitaṃ svenaiva kariṣyamāṇaṃ pārthāya darśayām āsa / sa ca pārtho bhagavataḥ sraṣṭrtvādikaṃ sarvāiśvaryaṃ sākṣātkṛtya tasminn eva bhagavati sarvātmani dhārtarāṣṭrādīnām upasaṃhāram anāgatam api tatprasādalabdhena divyena cakṣuṣā paśyann idaṃ covāca --
body.translated_text: Thus, displaying that the existence and activity of the entire universe depend upon Himself, the Charioteer of <s>Pārtha</s> showed to <s>Arjuna</s> that His own intended purpose — the removal of the earth's burden through the destruction of the demonic portions (<s>asurāṃśas</s>) that had entered [the battlefield], the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> who stood concealed in the guise of kings, and those who had infiltrated among the supporters of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> — would be accomplished by Himself alone. And <s>Pārtha</s>, having directly perceived the sovereignty of the Lord as creator and all else, seeing with the divine eye obtained by His grace even the yet-to-come destruction of the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s> and others in that very Lord who is the self of all, also spoke thus:

children.text: evaṃ sarvasya jagataḥ sva-āyatta-sthiti-pravṛttitvaṃ darśayan pārtha-sārathī rāja-veṣa-cchadmana āvasthitānāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ yaudhiṣṭhireṣv anupraviṣṭānāṃ ca asura-aṃśānāṃ saṃhāreṇa bhūbhāra avataraṇaṃ sva-manīṣitaṃ svena eva kariṣyamāṇaṃ pārthāya darśayām āsa / sa ca pārtho bhagavataḥ sraṣṭrtva-ādikaṃ sarva-aiśvaryaṃ sākṣātkṛtya tasminn eva bhagavati sarva-ātmani dhārtarāṣṭra-ādīnām upasaṃhāram anāgatam api tat-prasāda-labdhena divyena cakṣuṣā paśyann idaṃ ca uvāca ---
amī ca tvā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ sarvaiḥ sahaivāvanipālasaṅghaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'And these sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, together with all the hosts of kings,' |

children.text: bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūtaputras tathāsau sahāsmadīyair api yodhamukhyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and that son of the charioteer [<s>Karṇa</s>], along with our own chief warriors too,' ||

children.text: amī ca tvā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ sarvaiḥ saha eva avani-pāla-saṅghaiḥ |
bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūta-putras tatha āsau saha asmadīyair api yodha-mukhyaiḥ ||
vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti daṃṣṭrākarālāni bhayānakāni |
children.translated_text: 'rush into Your mouths, terrible with tusks and frightful.' |

children.text: kecid vilagnā daśanāntareṣu saṃdṛśyante cūrṇitair uttamāṅgaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Some are seen caught between the teeth with their heads crushed.' ||

children.text: vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti daṃṣṭrā-karālāni bhaya-anakāni |
kecid vilagnā daśana-antareṣu saṃdṛśyante cūrṇitair uttama-aṅgaiḥ ||

body.text: amī dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ duryodhanādayas sarve bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūtaputraḥ karṇaś ca tatpakṣīyair avanipālasamūhaiḥ sarvaiḥ, asmadīyair api kaiścid yodhamukhyais saha tvaramāṇā daṃṣṭrākarālāni bhayānakāni tava vaktrāṇi vināśāya viśanti; tatra kecic cūrṇitair uttamāṅgair daśānāntareṣu vilagnās saṃdṛśyante //
body.translated_text: These sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> — <s>Duryodhana</s> and all the rest — together with <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and the charioteer's son <s>Karṇa</s>, along with all the hosts of kings on their side, and also along with some of our own chief warriors, rush into Your mouths that are terrible with tusks and frightful, [heading] toward destruction. Among them, some are seen caught between the teeth with their heads crushed. //

children.text: amī dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ duryodhana-ādayas sarve bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūta-putraḥ karṇaś ca tat-pakṣīyair avanipāla-samūhaiḥ sarvaiḥ, asmadīyair api kaiścid yodha-mukhyais saha tvaramāṇā daṃṣṭrā-karālāni bhaya-anakāni tava vaktrāṇi vināśāya viśanti; tatra kecic cūrṇitair uttama-aṅgair daśāna-antareṣu vilagnās saṃdṛśyante //
