yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo 'mbuvegāḥ samudram evābhimukhā dravanti |
children.translated_text: 'As the many currents of rivers flow toward the ocean alone,' |

children.text: tathā tavāmī naralokavīrā viśanti vaktrāṇy abhivijvalanti ||
children.translated_text: 'so these heroes of the mortal world enter Your blazing mouths.' ||

children.text: yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo 'mbu-vegāḥ samudram eva abhimukhā dravanti |
tathā tava amī nara-loka-vīrā viśanti vaktrāṇy abhivijvalanti ||
yathā pradīptajvalanaṃ pataṅgā viśanti nāśāya samṛddhavegāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'As moths rush into a blazing fire for their destruction with great speed,' |

children.text: tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokās tavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛddhavegāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'so too these worlds rush into Your mouths for their destruction with great speed.' ||

children.text: yathā pradīpta-jvalanaṃ pataṅgā viśanti nāśāya samṛddha-vegāḥ |
tatha aiva nāśāya viśanti lokās tava api vaktrāṇi samṛddha-vegāḥ ||

body.text: ete rājalokāḥ, bahavo nadīnām ambupravāhāḥ samudram iva, pradīptajvalanam iva ca śalabhāḥ, tava vaktrāṇy abhivijvalanti svayam eva tvaramāṇā ātmanāśāya viśanti //
body.translated_text: These royal personages, like the many water-currents of rivers [flowing] toward the ocean, and like moths toward a blazing fire, rush of their own accord into Your blazing mouths, hastening toward their own destruction. //

children.text: ete rāja-lokāḥ, bahavo nadīnām ambu-pravāhāḥ samudram iva, pradīpta-jvalanam iva ca śalabhāḥ, tava vaktrāṇy abhivijvalanti svayam eva tvaramāṇā ātma-nāśāya viśanti //
lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantāl lokān samagrān vadanair jvaladbhiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'You lick up, devouring all the worlds on every side with Your flaming mouths.' |

children.text: tejobhir āpūrya jagat samagraṃ bhāsas tavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo ||
children.translated_text: 'Filling the entire universe with radiance, Your fierce rays scorch, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>.' ||

children.text: lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantāl lokān samagrān vadanair jvaladbhiḥ |
tejobhir āpūrya jagat samagraṃ bhāsas tava ugrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo ||

body.text: rājalokān samagrān jvaladbhir vadanair grasamānaḥ kopavegena tadrudhirāvasiktamoṣṭhapuṭādikaṃ lelihyase punaḥ punar lehanaṃ karoṣi / tavātighorā bhāsaḥ raśmayaḥ tejobhiḥ svakīyaiḥ prakāśaiḥ jagat samagram āpūrya pratapanti //
body.translated_text: Devouring all the kings with blazing mouths, You lick Your lips and the like, smeared with their blood due to the fury of Your wrath — You lick again and again. Your exceedingly terrible rays (<s>bhāsas</s>), with their own radiances, filling the entire universe, scorch it. //

children.text: rāja-lokān samagrān jvaladbhir vadanair grasamānaḥ kopa-vegena tad-rudhira-avasikta-moṣṭha-puṭa-ādikaṃ lelihyase punaḥ punar lehanaṃ karoṣi / tava atighorā bhāsaḥ raśmayaḥ tejobhiḥ svakīyaiḥ prakāśaiḥ jagat samagram āpūrya pratapanti //
ākhyāhi me ko bhavān ugrarūpo namo 'stu te devavara prasīda |
children.translated_text: Tell me, who are You of terrible form? Salutations to You, O best of gods, be gracious!

children.text: vijñātum icchāmi bhavantam ādyaṃ na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim ||
children.translated_text: I wish to know You, the Primal One, for I do not understand Your purpose. ||

children.text: ākhyāhi me ko bhavān ugra-rūpo namo 'stu te deva-vara prasīda |
vijñātum icchāmi bhavantam ādyaṃ na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim ||

body.text: "darśayātmānam avyayam" iti tavāiśvaryaṃ niraṅkuśaṃ sākṣātkartuṃ prārthitena bhavatā niraṅkuśam aiśvaryaṃ darśayatā atighorarūpam idam āviṣkṛtam / atighorarūpaḥ ko bhavān, kiṃ kartuṃ pravṛtta iti bhavantaṃ jñātum icchāmi / tavābhipretāṃ pravṛttiṃ na jānāmi / etad ākhyāhi me / namo 'stu te devavara! prasīda -- namas te 'stu sarveśvara; evaṃ kartum, anenābhiprāyeṇedaṃ saṃhartṛrūpam āviṣkṛtam ity uktvā prasannarūpaś ca bhava // BhGR_11.31 //
body.translated_text: By You, who were entreated [by me] with 'Show me Your imperishable Self,' this exceedingly terrible form has been revealed while displaying unrestricted sovereignty. Who are You of this exceedingly terrible form? For what purpose have You set forth? — I wish to know You. I do not know Your intended purpose. Tell me this. Salutations to You, O best of gods! Be gracious — salutations to You, O Lord of all; having said 'It is for this purpose, and with this intention, that this destructive form has been revealed,' become of gracious form as well. // BhGR_11.31 //

children.text: "darśayā atmānam avyayam" iti tava aiśvaryaṃ niraṅkuśaṃ sākṣātkartuṃ prārthitena bhavatā niraṅkuśam aiśvaryaṃ darśayatā atighora-rūpam idam āviṣkṛtam / atighora-rūpaḥ ko bhavān, kiṃ kartuṃ pravṛtta iti bhavantaṃ jñātum icchāmi / tava abhipretāṃ pravṛttiṃ na jānāmi / etad ākhyāhi me / namo 'stu te deva-vara! prasīda --- namas te 'stu sarva-īśvara; evaṃ kartum, anena abhiprāyeṇa idaṃ saṃhartṛ-rūpam āviṣkṛtam ity uktvā prasanna-rūpaś ca bhava // BhGR_11.31 //

body.text: āśritavātsalyātirekeṇa viśvāiśvaryaṃ darśayato bhavato ghorarūpāviṣkāre ko 'bhiprāya iti pṛṣṭo bhagavān pārthasārathiḥ svābhiprāyam āha, pārthodyogena vināpi dhārtarāṣṭrapramukham aśeṣaṃ rājalokaṃ nihantum aham eva pravṛtta iti jñāpanāya mama ghorarūpāviṣkāraḥ, tajjñāpanaṃ ca pārtham udyojayitum iti /
body.translated_text: When asked 'What is Your intention in revealing the terrible form, while You display universal sovereignty out of Your excessive affection for those who take refuge [in You]?' — the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the charioteer of <s>Pārtha</s>, states His intention: My revelation of the terrible form is to make known that I Myself have set forth to destroy the entire class of kings headed by the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, even without <s>Pārtha</s>'s effort; and the purpose of that disclosure is to urge <s>Pārtha</s> [to fight] —

children.text: āśrita-vātsalya-atirekeṇa viśva-aiśvaryaṃ darśayato bhavato ghora-rūpa-āviṣkāre ko 'bhiprāya iti pṛṣṭo bhagavān pārtha-sārathiḥ sva-abhiprāyam āha, pārtha-udyogena vina āpi dhārtarāṣṭra-pramukham aśeṣaṃ rāja-lokaṃ nihantum aham eva pravṛtta iti jñāpanāya mama ghora-rūpa-āviṣkāraḥ, taj-jñāpanaṃ ca pārtham udyojayitum iti /
kālo 'smi lokakṣayakṛt pravṛddho lokān samāhartum iha pravṛttaḥ |
children.translated_text: I am <s>Kāla</s> (Time), the mighty destroyer of worlds, engaged here in annihilating the worlds.

children.text: ṛte 'pi tvā na bhaviṣyanti sarve ye 'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even without you, all the warriors arrayed in the opposing armies shall cease to exist. ||

children.text: kālo 'smi loka-kṣaya-kṛt pravṛddho lokān samāhartum iha pravṛttaḥ |
ṛte 'pi tvā na bhaviṣyanti sarve ye 'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ ||

body.text: kalayati gaṇayatīti kālaḥ; sarveṣāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrapramukhānāṃ rājalokānām āyuravasānaṃ gaṇayann ahaṃ tatkṣayakṛd ghorarūpeṇa pravṛddho rājalokān samāhartum ābhimukhyena saṃhartum iha pravṛtto 'smi / ato matsaṃkalpād eva tvām ṛte 'pi -- tvadudyogād rte 'pi ete dhārtarāṣṭrapramukhās tava pratyanīkeṣu ye 'vasthitā yodhāḥ, te sarve na bhaviṣyanti -- vinaṅkṣyanti //
body.translated_text: He who reckons (<s>kalayati</s>) is <s>Kāla</s>; reckoning the end of the lifespan of all the kings headed by the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, I — grown mighty in terrible form as the destroyer of them — have set forth here to annihilate the kings, to destroy them face to face. Therefore, by My will alone, even without you — even without your effort — these warriors who are arrayed in your opposing armies, headed by the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, shall all cease to exist — they shall perish. //

children.text: kalayati gaṇayati iti kālaḥ; sarveṣāṃ dhārtarāṣṭra-pramukhānāṃ rāja-lokānām āyur-avasānaṃ gaṇayann ahaṃ tat-kṣaya-kṛd ghora-rūpeṇa pravṛddho rāja-lokān samāhartum ābhimukhyena saṃhartum iha pravṛtto 'smi / ato mat-saṃkalpād eva tvām ṛte 'pi --- tvad-udyogād rte 'pi ete dhārtarāṣṭra-pramukhās tava pratyanīkeṣu ye 'vasthitā yodhāḥ, te sarve na bhaviṣyanti --- vinaṅkṣyanti //
tasmāt tvam uttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ samṛddham |
children.translated_text: Therefore arise and win glory; having conquered your enemies, enjoy prosperous sovereignty.

children.text: mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvam eva nimittamātraṃ bhava savyasācin ||
children.translated_text: By Me alone have these been slain already; be merely the instrument, O <s>Savyasācin</s>. ||

children.text: tasmāt tvam uttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ samṛddham |
maya aiva ete nihatāḥ pūrvam eva nimitta-mātraṃ bhava savya-sācin ||

body.text: tasmāt tvaṃ tān prati yuddhāyottiṣṭha / tān śatrūn jitvā yaśo labhasva; dharmyaṃ rājyaṃ ca samṛddhaṃ bhuṅkṣva / mayaivaite kṛtāparādhāḥ pūrvam eva nihatāḥ hanane viniyuktāḥ / tvaṃ tu teṣāṃ hanane nimittamātraṃ bhava / mayā hanyamānānāṃ śatrādisthānīyo bhava / savyasācin / ṣaca samavāye; savyena śarasacanaśīlaḥ savyasācī; savyenāpi kareṇa śarasamavāyakaraḥ; karadvayena yoddhuṃ samartha ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore, arise for battle against them. Having conquered those enemies, win glory; and enjoy the righteous and prosperous sovereignty. By Me alone have these offenders been slain already — [i.e.,] appointed for slaying. You, however, be merely the instrument in their slaying — be in the position of an arrow and the like for those being slain by Me. <s>Savyasācin</s> — <s>ṣac</s> means 'joining together'; one who habitually shoots arrows with the left hand is <s>Savyasācin</s>; one who joins arrows even with the left hand; meaning: one capable of fighting with both hands. //

children.text: tasmāt tvaṃ tān prati yuddhāya uttiṣṭha / tān śatrūn jitvā yaśo labhasva; dharmyaṃ rājyaṃ ca samṛddhaṃ bhuṅkṣva / maya aiva ete kṛta-aparādhāḥ pūrvam eva nihatāḥ hanane viniyuktāḥ / tvaṃ tu teṣāṃ hanane nimitta-mātraṃ bhava / mayā hanyamānānāṃ śatra-ādi-sthānīyo bhava / savya-sācin / ṣaca samavāye; savyena śara-sacana-śīlaḥ savya-sācī; savyena api kareṇa śara-samavāya-karaḥ; kara-dvayena yoddhuṃ samartha ity-arthaḥ //
droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca jayadrathaṃ ca karṇaṃ tathānyān api yodhamukhyān |
children.translated_text: <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Jayadratha</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, and other chief warriors too —

children.text: mayā hatāṃs tvaṃ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān ||
children.translated_text: slain by Me, strike them; do not be distressed. Fight — you shall conquer the enemies in battle. ||

children.text: droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca jayad-rathaṃ ca karṇaṃ tatha ānyān api yodha-mukhyān |
mayā hatāṃs tvaṃ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān ||

body.text: droṇabhīṣmakarṇādīn kṛtāparādhatayā mayaiva hanane viniyuktān tvaṃ jahi tvaṃ hanyāḥ / etān gurūn bandhūṃś ca anyān api bhogasaktān kathaṃ haniṣyāmīti mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ -- tān uddiśya dharmādharmabhayena bandhusnehena kāruṇyena ca mā vyathāṃ kṛthāḥ / yatas te kṛtāparādhā mayaiva hanane viniyuktāḥ, ato nirviśaṅko yudhyasva / raṇe sapatnān jetāsi jeṣyasi / naiteṣāṃ vadhe nṛśaṃsatāgandhaḥ; api tu jaya eva labhyata ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Karṇa</s>, and the like, who have been appointed for slaying by Me alone on account of their offenses — you strike them, you slay them. 'How shall I slay these elders, kinsmen, and others attached to enjoyments?' — do not be distressed thus; do not grieve concerning them out of fear of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, out of affection for kinsmen, or out of compassion. Since they are offenders appointed for slaying by Me alone, therefore fight without apprehension. You shall conquer the enemies in battle — you shall be victorious. In their slaying there is not even a trace of cruelty; rather, victory alone is obtained — this is the meaning. //

children.text: droṇa-bhīṣma-karṇa-ādīn kṛta-aparādhatayā maya aiva hanane viniyuktān tvaṃ jahi tvaṃ hanyāḥ / etān gurūn bandhūṃś ca anyān api bhoga-saktān kathaṃ haniṣyāmi iti mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ --- tān uddiśya dharma-adharma-bhayena bandhu-snehena kāruṇyena ca mā vyathāṃ kṛthāḥ / yatas te kṛta-aparādhā maya aiva hanane viniyuktāḥ, ato nirviśaṅko yudhyasva / raṇe sapatnān jetāsi jeṣyasi / na eteṣāṃ vadhe nṛ-śaṃsatā-gandhaḥ; api tu jaya eva labhyata ity-arthaḥ //
etac chrutvā vacanaṃ keśavasya kṛtāñjalir vepamānaḥ kirīṭī |
children.translated_text: Having heard this speech of <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Kirīṭin</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), with joined palms, trembling,

children.text: namaskṛtvā bhūya evāha kṛṣṇaṃ sagadgadaṃ bhītabhītaḥ praṇamya ||
children.translated_text: having bowed, spoke again to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, falteringly, frightened, prostrating himself. ||

children.text: etac chrutvā vacanaṃ keśavasya kṛta-añjalir vepamānaḥ kirīṭī |
namaskṛtvā bhūya evā aha kṛṣṇaṃ sa-gadgadaṃ bhīta-bhītaḥ praṇamya ||

body.text: etad aśritavātsalyajaladheḥ keśavasya vacanaṃ śrutvā arjunas tasmai namaskṛtya bhītabhīto bhūyas taṃ praṇamya kṛtāñjalir vepamānaḥ kirīṭī sagadgadam āha //
body.translated_text: Having heard this speech of <s>Keśava</s>, who is an ocean of affection for those who take refuge [in Him], <s>Arjuna</s>, having bowed to Him, frightened, again prostrating himself before Him, with joined palms, trembling, <s>Kirīṭin</s> spoke falteringly. //

children.text: etad aśrita-vātsalya-jala-dheḥ keśavasya vacanaṃ śrutvā arjunas tasmai namaskṛtya bhīta-bhīto bhūyas taṃ praṇamya kṛta-añjalir vepamānaḥ kirīṭī sa-gadgadam āha //
sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā jagat prahṛṣyaty anurajyate ca |
children.translated_text: It is fitting, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, that by Your glory the world rejoices and is filled with love;

children.text: rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti sarve namasyanti ca siddhasaṅghāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, terrified, flee in all directions, and all the hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> bow in reverence. ||

children.text: sthāne hṛṣī-keśa tava prakīrtyā jagat prahṛṣyaty anurajyate ca |
rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti sarve namasyanti ca siddha-saṅghāḥ ||

body.text: sthāne yuktam / yad etad yuddhadidṛkṣayāgatam aśeṣadevagandharvasiddhayakṣavidyādharakinnarakiṃpuruṣādikaṃ jagat, tvatprasādāt tvāṃ sarveśvaram avalokya tava prakīrtyā sarvaṃ prahṛṣyati, anurajyate ca, yac ca tvām avalokya rakṣāṃsi bhītāni sarvā diśaḥ pradravanti, sarve siddhasaṃghāḥ siddhādyanukūlasaṃghāḥ namasyanti ca -- tad etat sarvaṃ yuktam iti pūrveṇa saṃbandhaḥ //
body.translated_text: It is fitting — it is proper. That this entire world — the hosts of gods, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Kiṃpuruṣas</s>, and the like who have come wishing to witness the battle — by Your grace, beholding You as the Lord of all, rejoices by Your glory, and is filled with love; and that the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, terrified upon beholding You, flee in all directions; and that all the hosts of <s>Siddhas</s> — the hosts of those favorably disposed, such as the <s>Siddhas</s> and the like — bow in reverence — all this is fitting. This connects with the preceding [verse]. //

children.text: sthāne yuktam / yad etad yuddha-didṛkṣayā āgatam aśeṣa-deva-gandharva-siddha-yakṣa-vidyā-dhara-kinnara-kiṃpuruṣa-ādikaṃ jagat, tvat-prasādāt tvāṃ sarva-īśvaram avalokya tava prakīrtyā sarvaṃ prahṛṣyati, anurajyate ca, yac ca tvām avalokya rakṣāṃsi bhītāni sarvā diśaḥ pradravanti, sarve siddha-saṃghāḥ siddha-ādy-anukūla-saṃghāḥ namasyanti ca --- tad etat sarvaṃ yuktam iti pūrveṇa saṃbandhaḥ //

body.text: yuktatām evopapādayati --
body.translated_text: [<s>Arjuna</s>] establishes the fittingness —

children.text: yuktatām eva upapādayati ---
kasmāc ca te na nameran mahātman garīyase brahmaṇo 'py ādikartre |
children.translated_text: And why should they not bow to You, O Great Soul, who are greater even than <s>Brahmā</s>, the original creator?

children.text: kasmāc ca te na nameran mahā-ātman garīyase brahmaṇo 'py ādi-kartre |

body.text: mahātman, te tubhyaṃ garīyase brahmaṇaḥ hiraṇyagarbhasyāpi ādibhūtāya kartre hiraṇyagarbhādayaḥ kasmād dhetor na namaskuryuḥ //
body.translated_text: O Great Soul, why should <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> and the others not bow to You, who are greater [than all], who are the primal creator even of <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>)? //

children.text: mahā-ātman, te tubhyaṃ garīyase brahmaṇaḥ hiraṇya-garbhasya api ādi-bhūtāya kartre hiraṇya-garbha-ādayaḥ kasmād dhetor na namaskuryuḥ //
ananta deveśa jagannivāsa tvam akṣaraṃ sad asat tat paraṃ yat ||
children.translated_text: O Infinite One, Lord of gods, Abode of the universe — You are the Imperishable, Being, Non-being, and that which is beyond. ||

children.text: ananta deva-īśa jagan-nivāsa tvam akṣaraṃ sad asat tat paraṃ yat ||

body.text: ananta deveśa jagannivāsa tvam evākṣaram / na kṣaratīty akṣaraṃ jīvātmatattvam / "na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit" ity ādiśrutisiddho jīvātmā hi na kṣarati / sad asac ca tvam eva sadasacchabdanirdiṣṭaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvenāvasthitaṃ prakṛtitattvaṃ, nāmarūpavibhāgavattayā kāryāvasthaṃ sacchabdanirdiṣṭaṃ tadanarhatayā kāraṇāvastham asacchabdanirdiṣṭaṃ ca tvam eva / tat param yat tasmāt prakṛteḥ prakṛtisaṃbandhinaś ca jīvātmanaḥ param anyan muktātmatattvaṃ yat, tad api tvam eva //
body.translated_text: O Infinite One, Lord of gods, Abode of the universe — You alone are the Imperishable. That which does not decay (<s>na kṣarati</s>) is the imperishable — the reality of the individual self (<s>jīvātmatattva</s>). For the individual self, established in <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'The wise one is neither born nor dies' and the like, does not decay. And Being and Non-being are also You alone — the reality of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), which is designated by the words 'being' (<s>sat</s>) and 'non-being' (<s>asat</s>) and is established in the states of effect and cause: the effect-state, possessing the differentiation of name and form, designated by the word <s>sat</s>; and the causal state, not admitting of such [differentiation], designated by the word <s>asat</s> — both are You alone. That which is beyond (<s>tat param yat</s>) — the reality of the liberated self (<s>muktātmatattva</s>), which is other than, i.e., beyond, <s>Prakṛti</s> and the individual self connected with <s>Prakṛti</s> — that too is You alone. //

children.text: ananta deva-īśa jagan-nivāsa tvam eva akṣaram / na kṣarati ity akṣaraṃ jīva-ātma-tattvam / "na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit" ity ādi-śruti-siddho jīva-ātmā hi na kṣarati / sad asac ca tvam eva sad-asac-chabda-nirdiṣṭaṃ kārya-kāraṇa-bhāvena avasthitaṃ prakṛti-tattvaṃ, nāma-rūpa-vibhāgavattayā kārya-avasthaṃ sac-chabda-nirdiṣṭaṃ tad-anarhatayā kāraṇa-avastham asac-chabda-nirdiṣṭaṃ ca tvam eva / tat param yat tasmāt prakṛteḥ prakṛti-saṃbandhinaś ca jīva-ātmanaḥ param anyan mukta-ātma-tattvaṃ yat, tad api tvam eva //
tvam ādidevaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇas tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam |
children.translated_text: You are the primal God, the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>; You are the supreme resting-place of this universe.

children.text: tvam ādi-devaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇas tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam |

body.text: atas tvam ādidevaḥ, puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ, tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam / nidhīyate tvayi viśvam iti tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam; viśvasya śarīrabhūtasyātmatayā paramādhārabhūtas tvam evetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore You are the primal God, the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>; You are the supreme resting-place of this universe. The universe is deposited in You — thus You are the supreme resting-place of this universe; the meaning is that, as the self of the universe which is Your body, You alone are the supreme support. //

children.text: atas tvam ādi-devaḥ, puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ, tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam / nidhīyate tvayi viśvam iti tvam asya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam; viśvasya śarīra-bhūtasyā atmatayā parama-ādhāra-bhūtas tvam eva ity-arthaḥ //
vettāsi vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma tvayā tataṃ viśvam anantarūpa ||
children.translated_text: You are the knower and the knowable, and the supreme abode; by You is the universe pervaded, O One of infinite forms. ||

children.text: vetta āsi vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma tvayā tataṃ viśvam ananta-rūpa ||

body.text: jagati sarvo veditā vedyaṃ ca sarvaṃ tvam eva / evaṃ sarvātmatayāvasthitas tvam eva paraṃ ca dhāma sthānam; prāpyasthānam ityarthaḥ / tvayā tataṃ viśvam anantarūpa / tvayātmatvena viśvaṃ cidacinmiśraṃ jagat tataṃ vyāptam //
body.translated_text: In the world, every knower and everything knowable are You alone. Thus established as the self of all, You alone are also the supreme abode — the supreme destination; meaning: the goal to be attained. By You is the universe pervaded, O One of infinite forms — by You, as their self, the entire universe of conscious and non-conscious beings is pervaded, i.e., permeated. //

children.text: jagati sarvo veditā vedyaṃ ca sarvaṃ tvam eva / evaṃ sarva-ātmataya āvasthitas tvam eva paraṃ ca dhāma sthānam; prāpya-sthānam ity-arthaḥ / tvayā tataṃ viśvam ananta-rūpa / tvayā ātmatvena viśvaṃ cid-acin-miśraṃ jagat tataṃ vyāptam //

body.text: atas tvam eva vāyvādiśabdavācya ity āha --
body.translated_text: Therefore, You alone are denoted by the words <s>Vāyu</s> and the like — [<s>Arjuna</s>] says —

children.text: atas tvam eva vāyv-ādi-śabda-vācya ity āha ---
vāyur yamo 'gnir varuṇaś śaśāṅkaḥ prajāpatis tvaṃ prapitāmahaś ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, the Moon, <s>Prajāpati</s> — You are [all these], and the great-grandfather too.

children.text: vāyur yamo 'gnir varuṇaś śaśa-aṅkaḥ prajāpatis tvaṃ prapitāmahaś ca |

body.text: sarveṣāṃ prapitāmahas tvam eva; pitāmahādayaś ca / sarvasāṃ prajānāṃ pitaraḥ prajāpatayaḥ, prajāpatīnāṃ pitā hiraṇyagarbhaḥ prajānāṃ pitāmahaḥ, hiraṇyagarbhasyāpi pitā tvaṃ prajānāṃ prapitāmahaḥ / pitāmahādīnām ātmatayā tattacchabdavācyas tvam evetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: You alone are the great-grandfather of all; and the grandfather and the rest. The fathers of all creatures are the <s>Prajāpatis</s>; the father of the <s>Prajāpatis</s> is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the grandfather of all creatures; and the father even of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is You, the great-grandfather of all creatures. The meaning is that, as the self of the grandfather and the rest, You alone are denoted by those respective words. //

children.text: sarveṣāṃ prapitāmahas tvam eva; pitāmaha-ādayaś ca / sarvasāṃ prajānāṃ pitaraḥ prajā-patayaḥ, prajāpatīnāṃ pitā hiraṇya-garbhaḥ prajānāṃ pitāmahaḥ, hiraṇya-garbhasya api pitā tvaṃ prajānāṃ prapitāmahaḥ / pitāmaha-ādīnām ātmatayā tat-tac-chabda-vācyas tvam eva ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: atyadbhutākāraṃ bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣotphullanayano 'tyantasādhvasāvanataḥ sarvato namaskaroti //
body.translated_text: Having beheld the <s>Bhagavān</s> of exceedingly wondrous form, with eyes wide open in delight, bowed down in extreme awe, he offers salutations from all sides. //

children.text: atyadbhuta-ākāraṃ bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣa-utphulla-nayano 'tyanta-sādhvasa-avanataḥ sarvato namaskaroti //
namo namas te 'stu sahasrakṛtvaḥ punaś ca bhūyo 'pi namo namas te ||
children.translated_text: Salutations, salutations to You a thousand times, and again and yet again, salutations, salutations to You! ||

children.text: namo namas te 'stu sahasra-kṛtvaḥ punaś ca bhūyo 'pi namo namas te ||
namaḥ purastād atha pṛṣṭhatas te namo 'stu te sarvata eva sarva |
children.translated_text: Salutations to You from the front, and from behind; salutations to You from every side, O All!

children.text: anantavīryāmitavikramas tvaṃ sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato 'si sarvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are of infinite valor and immeasurable prowess; You pervade all — therefore You are All. ||

children.text: namaḥ purastād atha pṛṣṭhatas te namo 'stu te sarvata eva sarva |
ananta-vīrya-amita-vikramas tvaṃ sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato 'si sarvaḥ ||

body.text: amitavīrya, aparimitaparākramas tvaṃ sarvātmatayā samāpnoṣi; tataḥ sarvo 'si / yatas tvaṃ sarvaṃ cidacidvastujātam ātmatayā samāpnoṣi, ataḥ sarvasya cidacidvastujātasya tvaccharīratayā tvatprakāratvāt sarvaprakāras tvam eva sarvaśabdavācyo 'sītyarthaḥ / "tvam akṣaraṃ sad asat", "vāyur yamo 'gniḥ" ityādisarvasāmānādhikaraṇyanirdeśasyātmatayā vyāptir eva hetur iti suvyaktam uktam, "tvayā tataṃ viśvam anantarūpa", "sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato 'si sarvaḥ" iti ca //
body.translated_text: O One of immeasurable valor, of unlimited prowess — You pervade all as the self of all; therefore You are All. Since You pervade the entire aggregate of conscious and non-conscious entities as their self, therefore, since the entire aggregate of conscious and non-conscious entities, being Your body, has You as its mode — You alone, as the possessor of all modes, are denoted by the word 'All.' 'You are the Imperishable, Being, Non-being,' '<s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Agni</s>' — and so on: it is very clearly stated that pervading as the self is the reason for all such co-referential predications (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), as in 'By You is the universe pervaded, O One of infinite forms' and 'You pervade all — therefore You are All.' //

children.text: amita-vīrya, aparimita-parākramas tvaṃ sarva-ātmatayā samāpnoṣi; tataḥ sarvo 'si / yatas tvaṃ sarvaṃ cid-acid-vastu-jātam ātmatayā samāpnoṣi, ataḥ sarvasya cid-acid-vastu-jātasya tvac-charīratayā tvat-prakāratvāt sarva-prakāras tvam eva sarva-śabda-vācyo 'si ity-arthaḥ / "tvam akṣaraṃ sad asat", "vāyur yamo 'gniḥ" ity-ādi-sarva-sāmānādhikaraṇya-nirdeśasyā atmatayā vyāptir eva hetur iti suvyaktam uktam, "tvayā tataṃ viśvam ananta-rūpa", "sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato 'si sarvaḥ" iti ca //
sakheti matvā prasabhaṃ yad uktaṃ he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti |
children.translated_text: Having presumed You to be a friend, I rashly addressed You as 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! O <s>Yādava</s>! O friend!' —

children.text: ajānatā mahimānaṃ tavemaṃ mayā pramādāt praṇayena vāpi ||
children.translated_text: not knowing this greatness of Yours, through negligence or even through affection. ||

children.text: sakha īti matvā prasabhaṃ yad uktaṃ he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakha īti |
ajānatā mahimānaṃ tava imaṃ mayā pramādāt praṇayena va āpi ||
yaś cāpahāsārtham asatkṛto 'si vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu |
children.translated_text: And if I have shown You disrespect in jest, during play, rest, sitting, or dining,

children.text: eko 'tha vāpy acyuta tatsamakṣaṃ tat kṣāmaye tvām aham aprameyam ||
children.translated_text: whether alone or in the presence of others, O <s>Acyuta</s> — I ask forgiveness of You, the immeasurable. ||

children.text: yaś ca apahāsa-artham asat-kṛto 'si vihāra-śayyā-āsana-bhojaneṣu |
eko 'tha va āpy acyuta tat-samakṣaṃ tat kṣāmaye tvām aham aprameyam ||

body.text: tavānantavīryatvāmitavikramatvasarvāntarātmatvasraṣṭṛtvādiko yo mahimā, tam imam ajānatā mayā pramādān mohāt, praṇayena ciraparicayena vā sakheti mama vayasyaḥ iti matvā, he kṛṣṇa, he yādava, he sakhā iti tvayi prasabham vinayāpetaṃ yad uktaṃ, yac ca prihāsārthaṃ sarvadaiva satkārārhas tvam asatkṛto 'si, vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu ca sahakṛteṣu ekānte vaḥ samakṣaṃ vā yad asatkṛto 'si; tat sarvaṃ tvām aprameyam ahaṃ kṣāmaye //
body.translated_text: Your infinite valor, unlimited prowess, being the inner self of all, creatorship, and other [aspects of] greatness — not knowing this greatness of Yours, through negligence, i.e., through delusion, or through affection, i.e., long familiarity — thinking 'He is my friend,' I rashly, i.e., without propriety, addressed You as 'O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! O <s>Yādava</s>! O friend!'; and if in jest You — who are always worthy of honor — have been treated with disrespect; and during play, rest, sitting, dining, and other shared activities, whether alone or in the presence of others, You have been treated with disrespect — for all that, I ask forgiveness of You, the immeasurable. //

children.text: tava ananta-vīryatva-amita-vikramatva-sarva-antara-ātmatva-sraṣṭṛtva-ādiko yo mahimā, tam imam ajānatā mayā pramādān mohāt, praṇayena cira-paricayena vā sakha īti mama vayasyaḥ iti matvā, he kṛṣṇa, he yādava, he sakhā iti tvayi prasabham vinaya-apetaṃ yad uktaṃ, yac ca prihāsa-arthaṃ sarvada aiva sat-kāra-arhas tvam asat-kṛto 'si, vihāra-śayyā-āsana-bhojaneṣu ca saha-kṛteṣu eka-ante vaḥ samakṣaṃ vā yad asat-kṛto 'si; tat sarvaṃ tvām aprameyam ahaṃ kṣāmaye //
pitāsi lokasya carācarasya tvam asya pūjyaś ca guru garīyān |
children.translated_text: You are the father of this world, of the moving and the unmoving; You are its venerable and greatest teacher.

children.text: na tvatsamo 'sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto 'nyo lokatraye 'py apratimaprabhāva ||
children.translated_text: There is none equal to You — how then could there be another greater in all the three worlds, O One of incomparable power? ||

children.text: pita āsi lokasya cara-acarasya tvam asya pūjyaś ca guru garīyān |
na tvat-samo 'sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto 'nyo loka-traye 'py apratima-prabhāva ||

body.text: apratimaprabhāva! tvam asya sarvasya carācarasya lokasya pitāsi / asya lokasya guruś cāsi; atas tvam asya carācarasya lokasya garīyān pūjyatamaḥ / na tvatsamo 'sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto 'nyaḥ -- lokatraye 'pi tvadanyaḥ kāruṇyādinā kenāpi guṇena na tvatsamo 'sti / kuto 'bhyadhikaḥ? //
body.translated_text: O One of incomparable power! You are the father of this entire world of moving and unmoving beings. You are also the teacher of this world; therefore You are the most venerable, the most worthy of honor, of this world of moving and unmoving beings. There is none equal to You, how then could there be another greater? — in all the three worlds, there is none equal to You in any quality such as compassion and the like. How then could there be one greater? //

children.text: apratima-prabhāva! tvam asya sarvasya cara-acarasya lokasya pita āsi / asya lokasya guruś ca asi; atas tvam asya cara-acarasya lokasya garīyān pūjyatamaḥ / na tvat-samo 'sty abhyadhikaḥ kuto 'nyaḥ --- loka-traye 'pi tvad-anyaḥ kāruṇya-ādinā kena api guṇena na tvat-samo 'sti / kuto 'bhyadhikaḥ? //
tasmāt praṇamya praṇidhāya kāryaṃ prasādaye tvām aham īśam īḍyam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, bowing down and prostrating my body, I seek Your grace, O Lord worthy of praise.

children.text: piteva putrasya sakheva sakhyuḥ priyaḥ priyāyārhasi deva soḍhum ||
children.translated_text: As a father to a son, as a friend to a friend, as a beloved to a beloved — please, O God, bear with [me]. ||

children.text: tasmāt praṇamya praṇidhāya kāryaṃ prasādaye tvām aham īśam īḍyam |
pita īva putrasya sakha īva sakhyuḥ priyaḥ priyāya arhasi deva soḍhum ||

body.text: yasmāt tvaṃ sarvasya pitā pūjyatamo guruś ca kāruṇyādiguṇaiś ca sarvādhiko 'si, tasmāt tvām īśam īḍyaṃ praṇamya praṇidhāya ca kāyaṃ, prasādaye; yathā kṛtāparādhasyāpi putrasya, yathā ca sakhyuḥ, praṇāmapūrvaṃ prārthitaḥ pitā vā sakhā vā prasīdati; tathā tvaṃ paramakāruṇikaḥ priyāya me sarvaṃ soḍhum arhasi //
body.translated_text: Since You are the father of all, the most venerable teacher, and surpass all in qualities such as compassion and the like, therefore, bowing down to You, the Lord worthy of praise, and prostrating my body, I seek Your grace. Just as a father, even when an offense has been committed by a son, and just as a friend [forgives a friend] — when entreated with prostration, a father or a friend becomes gracious — so may You, the supremely compassionate, deign to bear with everything toward me, who am dear [to You]. //

children.text: yasmāt tvaṃ sarvasya pitā pūjyatamo guruś ca kāruṇya-ādi-guṇaiś ca sarva-adhiko 'si, tasmāt tvām īśam īḍyaṃ praṇamya praṇidhāya ca kāyaṃ, prasādaye; yathā kṛta-aparādhasya api putrasya, yathā ca sakhyuḥ, praṇāma-pūrvaṃ prārthitaḥ pitā vā sakhā vā prasīdati; tathā tvaṃ parama-kāruṇikaḥ priyāya me sarvaṃ soḍhum arhasi //
adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ hṛṣito 'smi dṛṣṭvā bhayena ca pravyathitaṃ mano me |
children.translated_text: Having seen what was never seen before, I am delighted, yet my mind is troubled with fear.

children.text: tad eva me darśaya deva rūpaṃ prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa ||
children.translated_text: Show me that very [previous] form, O God; be gracious, O Lord of gods, Abode of the universe. ||

children.text: adṛṣṭa-pūrvaṃ hṛṣito 'smi dṛṣṭvā bhayena ca pravyathitaṃ mano me |
tad eva me darśaya deva rūpaṃ prasīda deva-īśa jagan-nivāsa ||

body.text: adṛṣṭapūrvam -- atyadbhutam atyugraṃ ca tava rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣito 'smi prīto 'smi / bhayena pravyathitaṃ ca me manaḥ / atas tad eva tava suprasannaṃ rūpaṃ me darśaya / prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa -- mayi prasādaṃ kuru, devānāṃ brahmādīnām apīśa, nikhilajagadāśrayabhūta //
body.translated_text: Having seen Your exceedingly wondrous and exceedingly terrible form, never seen before, I am delighted — I am pleased. Yet my mind is also troubled with fear. Therefore, show me that very gracious form of Yours. Be gracious, O Lord of gods, Abode of the universe — show grace to me; O Lord even of the gods such as <s>Brahmā</s> and the like; O One who is the refuge of the entire universe. //

children.text: adṛṣṭa-pūrvam --- atyadbhutam atyugraṃ ca tava rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣito 'smi prīto 'smi / bhayena pravyathitaṃ ca me manaḥ / atas tad eva tava suprasannaṃ rūpaṃ me darśaya / prasīda deva-īśa jagan-nivāsa --- mayi prasādaṃ kuru, devānāṃ brahma-ādīnām apī iśa, nikhila-jagad-āśraya-bhūta //
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakrahastam icchāmi tvāṃ draṣṭum ahaṃ tathaiva |
children.translated_text: I wish to see You bearing the crown, the mace, and the discus in hand, just as before.

children.text: tenaiva rūpeṇa caturbhujena sahasrabāho bhava viśvamūrte ||
children.translated_text: Assume that very four-armed form, O thousand-armed One, O Universal Form! ||

children.text: kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakra-hastam icchāmi tvāṃ draṣṭum ahaṃ tatha aiva |
tena eva rūpeṇa catur-bhujena sahasra-bāho bhava viśva-mūrte ||

body.text: tathaiva pūrvavat, kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakrahastaṃ tvāṃ draṣṭum icchāmi / atas tenaiva pūrvasiddhena caturbhujena rūpeṇa yukto bhava / sahasrabāho viśvamūrte idānīṃ sahasrabāhutvena viśvaśarīratvena dṛśyamānarūpas tvaṃ tenaiva rūpeṇa yukto bhavetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the same way as before, I desire to see You wearing a crown, bearing a mace, with discus in hand. Therefore, be endowed with that very previously established four-armed form. O thousand-armed one, O Universal Form — You who are now seen in the form of having a thousand arms and a universal body, be endowed with that very [four-armed] form — this is the meaning. //

children.text: tatha aiva pūrvavat, kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ cakra-hastaṃ tvāṃ draṣṭum icchāmi / atas tena eva pūrva-siddhena catur-bhujena rūpeṇa yukto bhava / sahasra-bāho viśva-mūrte idānīṃ sahasra-bāhutvena viśva-śarīratvena dṛśyamāna-rūpas tvaṃ tena eva rūpeṇa yukto bhava ity-arthaḥ //
mayā prasannena tavārjunedaṃ rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitam ātmayogāt |
children.translated_text: 'By Me, being pleased, this supreme form was shown to you through My own <s>yoga</s>, O <s>Arjuna</s>.'

children.text: tejomayaṃ viśvam anantam ādyaṃ yan me tvadanyena na dṛṣṭapūrvam ||
children.translated_text: 'Full of radiance, universal, infinite, primeval — which none other than you has ever seen before.' ||

children.text: mayā prasannena tava arjuna idaṃ rūpaṃ paraṃ darśitam ātma-yogāt |
tejo-mayaṃ viśvam anantam ādyaṃ yan me tvad-anyena na dṛṣṭa-pūrvam ||

body.text: yan me tejomayaṃ tejasāṃ rāśiḥ; viśvaṃ viśvātmabhūtam, anantam antarahitam; pradarśanārtham idam; ādimadhyāntarahitam; ādyam madvyatiriktasya kṛtsnasyādibhūtam, tvadanyena kenāpi na dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ rūpam -- tad idaṃ prasannena mayā madbhaktāya te darśitam; ātmayogād atmanas satyasaṃkalpatvayogāt //
body.translated_text: This form of Mine which is full of radiance — a mass of splendors; universal — having the entire universe as its self; infinite — without end; this word is illustrative: without beginning, middle, or end; primeval — the origin of the entire [creation] other than Myself — which has not been seen before by anyone other than you — this form was shown by Me, being pleased, to you My devotee, through My own <s>yoga</s> — through the <s>yoga</s> of My own truthfulness of will. //

children.text: yan me tejo-mayaṃ tejasāṃ rāśiḥ; viśvaṃ viśva-ātma-bhūtam, anantam anta-rahitam; pradarśana-artham idam; ādi-madhya-anta-rahitam; ādyam mad-vyatiriktasya kṛtsnasyā adi-bhūtam, tvad-anyena kena api na dṛṣṭa-pūrvaṃ rūpam --- tad idaṃ prasannena mayā mad-bhaktāya te darśitam; ātma-yogād atmanas satya-saṃkalpatva-yogāt //

body.text: ananyabhaktivyatiriktaiḥ sarvair apy upāyair yathāvad avasthito 'haṃ draṣṭuṃ na śakya ity āha --
body.translated_text: He says that by all means other than exclusive devotion, I cannot be seen as I truly am —

children.text: ananya-bhakti-vyatiriktaiḥ sarvair apy upāyair yathāvad avasthito 'haṃ draṣṭuṃ na śakya ity āha ---
na vedayajñādhyayanair na dānair na ca kriyābhir na tapobhir ugraiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Not through the <s>Vedas</s>, nor through sacrifices and study, nor through gifts, nor through rituals, nor through severe austerities,'

children.text: evaṃrūpaś śakya ahaṃ nṛloke draṣṭuṃ tvadanyena kurupravīra ||
children.translated_text: 'can I be seen in such a form in the world of mortals, by anyone other than you, O foremost of the <s>Kurus</s>.' ||

children.text: na veda-yajña-adhyayanair na dānair na ca kriyābhir na tapobhir ugraiḥ |
evaṃ-rūpaś śakya ahaṃ nṛ-loke draṣṭuṃ tvad-anyena kuru-pravīra ||

body.text: evaṃrūpo yathāvad avathito 'haṃ mayi bhaktimatas tvatto 'nyena ekāntabhaktirahitena kenāpi puruṣeṇa vedayajñādibhiḥ kevalair draṣṭuṃ na śakyaḥ //
body.translated_text: In such a form — as I truly am — I cannot be seen by anyone other than you, who has devotion to Me — by anyone devoid of exclusive devotion — through the <s>Vedas</s>, sacrifices, and the like alone, without [devotion]. //

children.text: evaṃ-rūpo yathāvad avathito 'haṃ mayi bhaktimatas tvatto 'nyena eka-anta-bhakti-rahitena kena api puruṣeṇa veda-yajña-ādibhiḥ kevalair draṣṭuṃ na śakyaḥ //
mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍhabhāvo dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ghoram īdṛṅ mamedam |
children.translated_text: 'Let there be no distress and no bewilderment in you, having seen this fearsome form of Mine.'

children.text: vyapetabhīḥ prītamanāḥ punas tvaṃ tad eva me rūpam idaṃ prapaśya ||
children.translated_text: 'Free from fear, with gladdened mind, behold again that very form of Mine.' ||

children.text: mā te vyathā mā ca vimūḍha-bhāvo dṛṣṭvā rūpaṃ ghoram īdṛṅ mama idam |
vyapeta-bhīḥ prīta-manāḥ punas tvaṃ tad eva me rūpam idaṃ prapaśya ||

body.text: īdṛśaghorarūpadarśanena te yā vyathā, yaś ca vimūḍhabhāvo vartate, tadubhayaṃ mā bhūt; tvayā abhyastapūrvam eva saumyaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmi, tad evedaṃ mama rūpaṃ prapaśya //
body.translated_text: Let that distress and that bewilderment which have arisen in you from seeing such a fearsome form — let both of them cease. I shall show [you] the gentle form that was previously familiar to you. Behold that very form of Mine. //

children.text: īdṛśa-ghora-rūpa-darśanena te yā vyathā, yaś ca vimūḍha-bhāvo vartate, tad-ubhayaṃ mā bhūt; tvayā abhyasta-pūrvam eva saumyaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmi, tad eva idaṃ mama rūpaṃ prapaśya //
ity arjunaṃ vāsudevas tathoktvā svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayām āsa bhūyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having thus spoken to <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s> showed His own form again.'

children.text: āśvāsayām āsa ca bhītam enaṃ bhūtvā punas saumyavapur mahātmā ||
children.translated_text: 'And the great-souled one, having again assumed His gentle form, comforted him who was frightened.' ||

children.text: ity arjunaṃ vāsu-devas tatha ūktvā svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayām āsa bhūyaḥ |
āśvāsayām āsa ca bhītam enaṃ bhūtvā punas saumya-vapur mahā-ātmā ||

body.text:
evaṃ pāṇḍutanayaṃ bhagavān vasudevasūnur uktvā bhūyaḥ svakīyam eva caturbhujaṃ rūpaṃ darśayām āsa; aparicitarupadarśanena bhītam enaṃ punar api paricitasaumyavapur bhūtvā āśvāsayām āsa ca, mahātmā satyasaṅkalpaḥ / asya sarveśvarasya paramapuruṣasya parasya brahmaṇo jagadupakṛtimartyasya vasudevasūnoś caturbhujam eva svakīyaṃ rūpam; kaṃsād bhītavasudevaprārthanena ākaṃsavadhād bhujadvayam upasaṃhṛtaṃ paścād āviṣkṛtaṃ ca / "jāto 'si deva deveśa śaṅkhacakragadādhara / divyaṃ rūpam idaṃ deva prasādenopsaṃhara // ..... upasaṃhara viśvātman rūpam etac caturbhujam" iti hi prārthitam / śiśupālasyāpi dviṣato 'navaratabhāvanāviṣayaś caturbhujam eva vasudevasūno rūpam, "udārapīvaracaturbāhuṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam" iti / ataḥ pārthenātra
tenaiva rūpeṇa caturbhujanety ucyate //
body.translated_text: Having thus spoken to the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, the blessed son of <s>Vasudeva</s> again showed His own four-armed form. And having again assumed the familiar gentle form, He comforted him who was frightened by the sight of an unfamiliar form — the great-souled one, the one of true will. The four-armed form alone is the own form of this Lord of all, the Supreme Person, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, who took on a mortal form for the benefit of the world as the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>. [Two of the] arms were withdrawn at the request of <s>Vasudeva</s>, who was afraid of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, [and remained so] until the slaying of <s>Kaṃsa</s>; afterwards they were manifested again. For the prayer was: 'You are born, O God, Lord of the gods, bearing conch, discus, and mace! Withdraw this divine form, O God, by [Your] grace... Withdraw, O universal Self, this four-armed form.' Even for <s>Śiśupāla</s>, an enemy, the form that was the object of his unceasing contemplation was the four-armed form of the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>: 'noble, robust, four-armed, bearing conch, discus, and mace.' Therefore, here <s>Pārtha</s> says 'with that very four-armed form.' //

children.text:
evaṃ pāṇḍu-tanayaṃ bhagavān vasu-deva-sūnur uktvā bhūyaḥ svakīyam eva catur-bhujaṃ rūpaṃ darśayām āsa; aparicita-rupa-darśanena bhītam enaṃ punar api paricita-saumya-vapur bhūtvā āśvāsayām āsa ca, mahā-ātmā satya-saṅkalpaḥ / asya sarva-īśvarasya parama-puruṣasya parasya brahmaṇo jagad-upakṛti-martyasya vasu-deva-sūnoś catur-bhujam eva svakīyaṃ rūpam; kaṃsād bhīta-vasu-deva-prārthanena ākaṃsa-vadhād bhuja-dvayam upasaṃhṛtaṃ paścād āviṣkṛtaṃ ca / "jāto 'si deva deva-īśa śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-dhara / divyaṃ rūpam idaṃ deva prasādena upsaṃhara // ..... upasaṃhara viśva-ātman rūpam etac catur-bhujam" iti hi prārthitam / śiśu-pālasya api dviṣato 'navarata-bhāvanā-viṣayaś catur-bhujam eva vasu-deva-sūno rūpam, "udāra-pīvara-catur-bāhuṃ śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-dharam" iti / ataḥ pārthena atra
tena eva rūpeṇa catur-bhujana ity ucyate //
dṛṣṭvedaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ tava saumyaṃ janārdana |
children.translated_text: 'Having seen this gentle human form of Yours, O <s>Janārdana</s>,'

children.text: idānīm asmi saṃvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'now I have become composed, with collected mind, returned to my nature.' ||

children.text: dṛṣṭva īdaṃ mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ tava saumyaṃ jana-ardana |
idānīm asmi saṃvṛttaḥ sacetāḥ prakṛtiṃ gataḥ ||

body.text: anavadhikātiśayasaundaryasaukumāryalāvaṇyādiyuktaṃ tavaivāsādhāraṇaṃ manuṣyatvasaṃsthānasaṃsthitam atisaumyam idaṃ tava rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā idānīṃ sacetās saṃvṛtto 'smi; prakṛtiṃ gataś ca //
body.translated_text: Having seen this exceedingly gentle form of Yours — endowed with immeasurable, surpassing beauty, delicacy, charm, and the like, uniquely Yours, established in the configuration of a human form — I have now become composed, with collected mind, and have returned to my nature. //

children.text: anavadhika-atiśaya-saundarya-saukumārya-lāvaṇya-ādi-yuktaṃ tava eva asādhāraṇaṃ manuṣyatva-saṃsthāna-saṃsthitam atisaumyam idaṃ tava rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā idānīṃ sa-cetās saṃvṛtto 'smi; prakṛtiṃ gataś ca //
sudurdarśam idaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavān asi yan mama |
children.translated_text: 'This form of Mine that you have seen is very difficult to behold.'

children.text: devā apy asya rūpasya nityaṃ darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Even the gods are ever longing to see this form.' ||

children.text: su-dur-darśam idaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭavān asi yan mama |
devā apy asya rūpasya nityaṃ darśana-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ ||

body.text: mama idaṃ sarvasya praśāsane 'vasthitaṃ sarvāsrayaṃ sarvakāraṇabhūtaṃ rūpaṃ yad dṛṣṭavān asi, tat sudurdarśaṃ na kenāpi draṣṭuṃ śakyam / asya rūpasya devā api nityaṃ darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ, na tu dṛṣṭavantaḥ //
body.translated_text: This form of Mine — established in the governance of all, the support of all, the cause of all — which you have beheld, is very difficult to behold — it cannot be seen by anyone. Even the gods are ever longing to see this form, but they have not seen [it]. //

children.text: mama idaṃ sarvasya praśāsane 'vasthitaṃ sarva-āsrayaṃ sarva-kāraṇa-bhūtaṃ rūpaṃ yad dṛṣṭavān asi, tat sudurdarśaṃ na kena api draṣṭuṃ śakyam / asya rūpasya devā api nityaṃ darśana-kāṅkṣiṇaḥ, na tu dṛṣṭavantaḥ //

body.text: kuta ity atra āha --
body.translated_text: As to why, He says —

children.text: kuta ity atra āha ---
nāhaṃ vedair na tapasā na dānena na cejyayā |
children.translated_text: 'Not through the <s>Vedas</s>, not through austerity, not through gifts, and not through sacrifice,'

children.text: śakya evaṃvidho draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavān asi mām yathā ||
children.translated_text: 'can I be seen in this manner — as you have seen Me.' ||

children.text: na ahaṃ vedair na tapasā na dānena na ca ijyayā |
śakya evaṃ-vidho draṣṭuṃ dṛṣṭavān asi mām yathā ||
bhaktyā tv ananyayā śakya aham evaṃvidho 'rjuna |
children.translated_text: 'But by exclusive devotion alone can I be known, O <s>Arjuna</s>, in this manner,'

children.text: jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca parantapa ||
children.translated_text: 'and be seen and be entered into in truth, O <s>Parantapa</s>.' ||

children.text: bhaktyā tv ananyayā śakya aham evaṃ-vidho 'rjuna |
jñātuṃ draṣṭuṃ ca tattvena praveṣṭuṃ ca paran-tapa ||

body.text: vedair adhyāpanapravacanādhyayanaśravaṇajapaviṣayaiḥ, yāgadānahomatapobhiś ca madbhaktivirahitaiḥ kevalaiḥ yathāvad avasthito 'haṃ draṣṭum aśakyaḥ / ananyayā tu bhaktyā tattvataś śāstrair jñātuṃ tattvatas sākṣātkartuṃ, tattvataḥ praveṣṭuṃ ca śakyaḥ / tathā ca śrutiḥ, "nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena / yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām" iti //
body.translated_text: Through the <s>Vedas</s> — whose subject matter is teaching, discoursing, study, listening, and recitation — through sacrifices, gifts, fire-offerings, and austerities, without devotion to Me, [these] alone cannot see Me as I truly am. But through exclusive devotion, I can be known in truth through the scriptures, directly perceived in truth, and entered into in truth. And so the <s>śruti</s>: 'This Self cannot be obtained through discourse, nor through intelligence, nor through much learning. He whom this [Self] chooses — by him it is obtained; to him this Self reveals its own form.' //

children.text: vedair adhyāpana-pravacana-adhyayana-śravaṇa-japa-viṣayaiḥ, yāga-dāna-homa-tapobhiś ca mad-bhakti-virahitaiḥ kevalaiḥ yathāvad avasthito 'haṃ draṣṭum aśakyaḥ / ananyayā tu bhaktyā tattvataś śāstrair jñātuṃ tattvatas sākṣātkartuṃ, tattvataḥ praveṣṭuṃ ca śakyaḥ / tathā ca śrutiḥ, "na ayam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena / yam eva eṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasya eṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām" iti //
matkarmakṛn matparamo madbhaktas saṅgavarjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He who performs actions for Me, who has Me as the supreme [goal], who is devoted to Me, free from attachment,'

children.text: nirvairas sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ sa mām eti pāṇḍava ||
children.translated_text: 'who is without enmity toward all beings — he comes to Me, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>.' ||

children.text: mat-karma-kṛn mat-paramo mad-bhaktas saṅga-varjitaḥ |
nirvairas sarva-bhūteṣu yaḥ sa mām eti pāṇḍava ||

body.text:
vedādhyayanādīni sarvāṇi karmāṇi madārādhanarūpāṇīti yaḥ karoti, sa matkarmakṛt / matparamaḥ -- sarveṣām ārambhāṇām aham eva paramoddeśyo yasya, sa matparamaḥ / madbhaktaḥ -- atyarthamatpriyatvena matkīrtanastutidhyānārcanapraṇāmādibhir vinā ātmadhāraṇam alabhamāno madekaprayojanatayā yaḥ satataṃ tāni karoti, sa madbhaktaḥ / saṅgavarjitaḥ madekapriyatvenetarasaṅgam asahamānaḥ / nirvairas sarvabhūteṣu -- matsaṃśleṣaviyogaikasukhaduḥkhasvabhāvatvāt svaduḥkhasya svāparādhananimittatvānusaṃdhānāc ca sarvabhūtānāṃ paramapuruṣaparatantratvānusaṃdhānāc ca sarvabhūteṣu vairanimittābhāvāt teṣu nirvairaḥ / ya evaṃ bhūtaḥ, sa mām iti māṃ yathāvad avasthitaṃ prāpnoti; nirastāvidyādyaśeṣadoṣagandho madekānubhavo
bhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: He who performs all actions — study of the <s>Vedas</s> and the like — as being in the form of My worship, he is one who performs actions for Me (<s>matkarmakṛt</s>). He who has Me as the supreme [goal] (<s>matparama</s>) — he for whom I alone am the supreme aim of all undertakings. He who is devoted to Me (<s>madbhakta</s>) — he who, due to his exceedingly great love for Me, being unable to sustain himself without singing, praising, meditating, worshipping, bowing to Me, and the like, with Me as his sole purpose, constantly performs those [acts of devotion]. He who is free from attachment (<s>saṅgavarjita</s>) — who, due to having Me alone as dear, cannot tolerate attachment to anything else. He who is without enmity toward all beings — because his nature is to experience happiness and sorrow solely through union with and separation from Me, because he contemplates that his own suffering is caused by his own offenses, and because he contemplates that all beings are dependent on the Supreme Person — since there is no cause for enmity toward any of them, he is without enmity toward them. He who is of such a nature — he comes to Me, he attains Me as I truly am. The meaning is: with every trace of defects such as <s>avidyā</s> removed, he becomes one whose sole experience is of Me. //

children.text:
veda-adhyayana-ādīni sarvāṇi karmāṇi mad-ārādhana-rūpāṇi iti yaḥ karoti, sa mat-karma-kṛt / mat-paramaḥ --- sarveṣām ārambhāṇām aham eva parama-uddeśyo yasya, sa mat-paramaḥ / mad-bhaktaḥ --- atyartha-mat-priyatvena mat-kīrtana-stuti-dhyāna-arcana-praṇāma-ādibhir vinā ātma-dhāraṇam alabhamāno mad-eka-prayojanatayā yaḥ satataṃ tāni karoti, sa mad-bhaktaḥ / saṅga-varjitaḥ mad-eka-priyatvena itara-saṅgam asahamānaḥ / nirvairas sarva-bhūteṣu --- mat-saṃśleṣa-viyoga-eka-sukha-duḥkha-sva-bhāvatvāt sva-duḥkhasya sva-aparādhana-nimittatva-anusaṃdhānāc ca sarva-bhūtānāṃ parama-puruṣa-para-tantratva-anusaṃdhānāc ca sarva-bhūteṣu vaira-nimitta-abhāvāt teṣu nirvairaḥ / ya evaṃ bhūtaḥ, sa mām iti māṃ yathāvad avasthitaṃ prāpnoti; nirasta-avidyā-ādy-aśeṣa-doṣa-gandho mad-eka-anubhavo
bhavati ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: bhaktiyoganiṣṭhānāṃ prāpyabhūtasya parasya brahmaṇo bhagavato nārāyaṇasya niraṅkuśāiśvaryaṃ sākṣātkartukāmāyārjunāya anavadhikātiśayakāruṇyāudāryasauśīlyādiguṇasāgareṇa satyasaṃkalpena bhagavatā svāiśvaryaṃ yathāvad avasthitaṃ darśitam; uktaṃ ca tattvato bhagavajjñānadarśanaprāptīnām aikāntikātyantikabhagavadbhaktyekalabhyatvam / ananataram ātmaprāptisādhanabhūtād atmopāsanād bhaktirūpasya bhagavadupāsanasya svasādhyaniṣpādane śaighryāt susukhopādānatvāc ca śraiṣṭhyam, bhagavadupāsanopāyaś ca, tadaśaktasyākṣaraniṣṭhatā, tadapekṣitāś cocyante / bhagavadupāsanasya prāpyabhūtopāsyaśraiṣṭhyāc śraiṣṭhyaṃ tu, "yoginām api sarveṣāṃ madgatenāntarātmanā / śraddhāvān bhajate yo mām sa me yuktatamo mataḥ //  ity atroktam
body.translated_text: For <s>Arjuna</s>, who desired to directly perceive the unobstructed sovereignty of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — who is the one to be attained by those established in <s>bhaktiyoga</s> — by the Lord whose will is true, who is an ocean of auspicious qualities such as immeasurable, surpassing compassion, generosity, accessibility, and the like — His sovereignty as it truly is was shown. And it was stated that the true knowledge, direct perception, and attainment of the Lord are obtainable only through exclusive and ultimate devotion to the Lord. Next, the superiority of worship of the Lord — which has the form of devotion — over worship of the self that is the means to self-attainment, by reason of the excellence of the object worshipped which is to be attained, the swiftness in accomplishing its goal, and the ease of its adoption, is stated; and the means for worship of the Lord, and for one incapable of that, fixation on the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), and the prerequisites for that, are stated. The superiority of worship of the Lord, however, was stated earlier: 'Among all <s>yogins</s>, he who with his inner self directed to Me worships Me with faith — he is considered by Me to be the most disciplined.'

children.text: bhakti-yoga-niṣṭhānāṃ prāpya-bhūtasya parasya brahmaṇo bhagavato nārāyaṇasya niraṅkuśa-aiśvaryaṃ sākṣātkartu-kāmāya arjunāya anavadhika-atiśaya-kāruṇya-audārya-sauśīlya-ādi-guṇa-sāgareṇa satya-saṃkalpena bhagavatā sva-aiśvaryaṃ yathāvad avasthitaṃ darśitam; uktaṃ ca tattvato bhagavaj-jñāna-darśana-prāptīnām aikāntika-ātyantika-bhagavad-bhakty-eka-labhyatvam / ananataram ātma-prāpti-sādhana-bhūtād atma-upāsanād bhakti-rūpasya bhagavad-upāsanasya sva-sādhya-niṣpādane śaighryāt su-sukha-upādānatvāc ca śraiṣṭhyam, bhagavad-upāsana-upāyaś ca, tad-aśaktasya akṣara-niṣṭhatā, tad-apekṣitāś ca ucyante / bhagavad-upāsanasya prāpya-bhūta-upāsya-śraiṣṭhyāc śraiṣṭhyaṃ tu, "yoginām api sarveṣāṃ mad-gatena antarātmanā / śraddhāvān bhajate yo mām sa me yuktatamo mataḥ //  ity atra uktam
evaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktās tvāṃ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: 'Those devotees who, being ever-disciplined, worship You in this manner,'

children.text: ye cāpy akṣaram avyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'and those who [worship] the imperishable unmanifest — of these, who are the best knowers of <s>yoga</s>?' ||

children.text: evaṃ satata-yuktā ye bhaktās tvāṃ paryupāsate |
ye ca apy akṣaram avyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yoga-vittamāḥ ||

body.text: evam -- "matkarmakṛt" ityādinoktena prakāreṇa, satatayuktāḥ bhagavantaṃ tvām eva paraṃ prāpyaṃ manvānāḥ ye bhaktāḥ, tvām sakalavibhūtiyuktam anavadhikātiśayasaundaryasauśīlyasārvajñyasatyasaṃkalpatvādyanantaguṇasāgaraṃ paripūrṇam upāsate, ye cāpy akṣaraṃ pratyagātmasvarūpam tad eva ca avyaktaṃ cakṣurādikaraṇānabhivyaktasvarūpam upāsate; teṣām ubhayeṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ -- ke svasādhyaṃ prati śīghragāmina ityarthaḥ, "bhavāmi na cirāt pārtha" iti uttaratra yogavittamatvaṃ śaighryaviṣayam iti hi vyañjayiṣyate //
body.translated_text: In this manner — as described by 'he who performs actions for Me' and so forth — those devotees who are ever-disciplined, regarding You the Lord as the supreme object of attainment, worship You — endowed with all manifestations, an ocean of infinite auspicious qualities such as immeasurable, surpassing beauty, accessibility, omniscience, truthfulness of will, and the like, complete in all respects; and those who worship the imperishable — the essential nature of the individual self (<s>pratyagātman</s>), which is also unmanifest — not manifested to the sense-organs such as the eyes and the like in its essential nature — of these two, who are the best knowers of <s>yoga</s>? The meaning is: who are the swiftest in reaching their own goal? For it will be indicated later, by 'I become [their savior] in no long time, O <s>Pārtha</s>,' that the best-in-<s>yoga</s>-ness is with respect to swiftness. //

children.text: evam --- "mat-karma-kṛt" ity-ādina ūktena prakāreṇa, satata-yuktāḥ bhagavantaṃ tvām eva paraṃ prāpyaṃ manvānāḥ ye bhaktāḥ, tvām sakala-vibhūti-yuktam anavadhika-atiśaya-saundarya-sauśīlya-sārvajñya-satya-saṃkalpatva-ādy-ananta-guṇa-sāgaraṃ paripūrṇam upāsate, ye ca apy akṣaraṃ pratyag-ātma-sva-rūpam tad eva ca avyaktaṃ cakṣur-ādi-karaṇa-anabhivyakta-sva-rūpam upāsate; teṣām ubhayeṣāṃ ke yoga-vittamāḥ --- ke sva-sādhyaṃ prati śīghra-gāmina ity-arthaḥ, "bhavāmi na cirāt pārtha" iti uttaratra yoga-vittamatvaṃ śaighrya-viṣayam iti hi vyañjayiṣyate //
mayy āveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate |
children.translated_text: 'Those who, fixing their mind on Me, worship Me, ever-disciplined,'

children.text: śraddhayā parayopetās te me yuktatamāḥ matāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'endowed with supreme faith — they are considered by Me to be the best in <s>yoga</s>.' ||

children.text: mayy āveśya mano ye māṃ nitya-yuktā upāsate |
śraddhayā paraya ūpetās te me yuktatamāḥ matāḥ ||

body.text: atyarthamatpriyatvena mano mayy āveśya śraddhayā parayopetāḥ nityayuktāḥ nityayogaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇāḥ ye mām upāsate -- prāpyaviṣayaṃ mano mayy āveśya ye mām upāsata ityarthaḥ -- te yuktatamāḥ -- māṃ sukhenācirāt prāpnuvantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Those who, due to their exceedingly great love for Me, fix their mind on Me, endowed with supreme faith, ever-disciplined — yearning for perpetual union — worship Me — fixing their mind on Me as the object to be attained, and worship Me — this is the meaning. They are the best in <s>yoga</s> — the meaning is: they attain Me easily and quickly. //

children.text: atyartha-mat-priyatvena mano mayy āveśya śraddhayā paraya ūpetāḥ nitya-yuktāḥ nitya-yogaṃ kāṅkṣamāṇāḥ ye mām upāsate --- prāpya-viṣayaṃ mano mayy āveśya ye mām upāsata ity-arthaḥ --- te yuktatamāḥ --- māṃ sukhena acirāt prāpnuvanti ity-arthaḥ //
ye tv akṣaram anirdeśyam avyaktaṃ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: 'But those who worship the imperishable, the indefinable, the unmanifest,'

children.text: sarvatragam acintyaṃ ca kūṭastham acalaṃ dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: 'the all-pervading, the inconceivable, the immovable, the unchanging, the firm,' ||

children.text: ye tv akṣaram anirdeśyam avyaktaṃ paryupāsate |
sarvatra-gam acintyaṃ ca kūṭa-stham acalaṃ dhruvam ||
sanniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'having restrained the entire group of senses, even-minded everywhere,'

children.text: te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'they too attain Me, devoted to the welfare of all beings.' ||

children.text: sanniyamya indriya-grāmaṃ sarvatra sama-buddhayaḥ |
te prāpnuvanti mām eva sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ ||
kleśo 'dhikataras teṣām avyaktāsaktacetasām |
children.translated_text: 'The difficulty is greater for those whose minds are set on the unmanifest;'

children.text: avyaktā hi gatir duḥkhaṃ dehavadbhir avāpyate ||
children.translated_text: 'for the unmanifest goal is attained with hardship by the embodied.' ||

children.text: kleśo 'dhikataras teṣām avyakta-asakta-cetasām |
avyaktā hi gatir duḥkhaṃ dehavadbhir avāpyate ||

body.text:
ye tu akṣaram pratyagātmasvarūpam, anirdeśyam dehād anyatayā devādiśabdānirdeśyam tata eva cakṣurādikaraṇānabhivyaktam, sarvatragam acintyaṃ ca -- sarvatra devādideheṣu vartamānam api tadvisajātīyatayā tena tena rūpeṇa cintayitum anarham, tata eva kūṭastham sarvasādhāraṇam -- tat tad devādyasādhāraṇākārāsaṃbaddham ityarthaḥ -- apariṇāmitvena svāsādhāraṇākārān na calati na cyavata ity acalam, tata eva dhruvam, nityam / sanniyāmyendriyagrāmam cakṣurādikam indriyagrāmaṃ sarvaṃ svavyāpārebhyas samyaṅniyamya, sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ sarvatra devādiviṣamākāreṣu deheṣv avasthiteṣv ātmasu jñānaikākāratayā samabuddhayaḥ, tata eva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ sarvabhūtāhitarahitatvān nivṛttāḥ / sarvabhūtāhitarahitatvaṃ hy ātmano devādiviṣamākārābhimānanimittam
/ ya evam akṣaram upāsate, te 'pi māṃ prāpnuvanty eva -- matsamānākāram asaṃsāriṇam ātmānaṃ prāpnuvanty evetyarthaḥ / "mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ" iti hi vakṣyate / śrūyate ca, "nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyam upaiti" iti / tathā akṣaraśabdanirdiṣṭāt kūṭasthād anyatvaṃ parasya brahmaṇo vakṣyate, "kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate / uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ" iti / "atha parā yayā tad akṣaram adhikgamyate" ity akṣaravidyāyāṃ tu akṣaraśabdanirdiṣṭaṃ param eva brahma, bhūtayonitvādeḥ /teṣām avyaktāsaktacetasāṃ kleśas tv adhikataraḥ / avyaktā hi gatiḥ avyaktaviṣayā manovṛttiḥ dehavadbhiḥ dehātmābhimānayuktaiḥ duḥkhenāvāpyate / dehavanto hi deham eva ātmānaṃ manyante //
body.translated_text: But those who [worship] the imperishable — the essential nature of the individual self; indefinable — not describable by words such as 'god' and the like since it is different from the body; for that very reason, unmanifest — not manifested to sense-organs such as the eyes and the like in its essential nature; all-pervading and inconceivable — though present in all bodies of gods and the like, it is of a nature entirely different from them, hence it cannot be conceived as having this or that form; for that very reason, immovable (<s>kūṭastha</s>) — common to all, meaning: not connected with the specific configurations of gods and the like; unchanging (<s>acala</s>) — it does not move away from or deviate from its own unique form due to being free from transformation; for that very reason, firm (<s>dhruva</s>) — permanent, eternal. Having restrained the entire group of senses — having fully restrained all sense-organs such as the eyes and the like from their respective activities. Even-minded everywhere — regarding the selves established in the disparately formed bodies of gods and the like, having an equal understanding due to their having the single form of knowledge. For that very reason, devoted to the welfare of all beings — freed from [causing] harm to any beings, since there is no harm to any being from the self's perspective. For the self's identification with the disparate forms of gods and the like [in terms of causing harm] is caused by the false identification with [those forms]. Those who thus worship the imperishable — they too attain Me alone. The meaning is: they attain the self which is of a form similar to Mine, free from <s>saṃsāra</s>. For it will be stated: 'They have attained equality with Me.' And it is heard in <s>śruti</s>: 'Free from stain, he attains supreme equality.' Also, the otherness of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> from the immovable (<s>kūṭastha</s>) designated by the word <s>akṣara</s> will be stated: 'The immovable is called <s>akṣara</s>; but the Supreme Person is other [than that].' In the <s>akṣaravidyā</s> (knowledge of the imperishable), however — 'Now the higher [knowledge] by which that imperishable is attained' — the word <s>akṣara</s> designates the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> itself, because of [its being described as] the source of beings and the like. But the difficulty for those whose minds are set on the unmanifest is greater. For the unmanifest goal — the mental activity directed toward the unmanifest — is attained with hardship by the embodied — by those who identify the self with the body. For the embodied think the body alone is the self. //

children.text:
ye tu akṣaram pratyag-ātma-sva-rūpam, anirdeśyam dehād anyatayā deva-ādi-śabda-anirdeśyam tata eva cakṣur-ādi-karaṇa-anabhivyaktam, sarvatra-gam acintyaṃ ca --- sarvatra deva-ādi-deheṣu vartamānam api tad-visajātīyatayā tena tena rūpeṇa cintayitum anarham, tata eva kūṭa-stham sarva-sādhāraṇam --- tat tad deva-ādy-asādhāraṇa-ākāra-asaṃbaddham ity-arthaḥ --- apariṇāmitvena sva-asādhāraṇa-ākārān na calati na cyavata ity acalam, tata eva dhruvam, nityam / sanniyāmya-indriya-grāmam cakṣur-ādikam indriya-grāmaṃ sarvaṃ sva-vyāpārebhyas samyaṅ-niyamya, sarvatra sama-buddhayaḥ sarvatra deva-ādi-viṣama-ākāreṣu deheṣv avasthiteṣv ātmasu jñāna-eka-ākāratayā sama-buddhayaḥ, tata eva sarva-bhūta-hite ratāḥ sarva-bhūta-ahita-rahitatvān nivṛttāḥ / sarva-bhūta-ahita-rahitatvaṃ hy ātmano deva-ādi-viṣama-ākāra-abhimāna-nimittam
/ ya evam akṣaram upāsate, te 'pi māṃ prāpnuvanty eva --- mat-samāna-ākāram asaṃsāriṇam ātmānaṃ prāpnuvanty eva ity-arthaḥ / "mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ" iti hi vakṣyate / śrūyate ca, "nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyam upaiti" iti / tathā akṣara-śabda-nirdiṣṭāt kūṭa-sthād anyatvaṃ parasya brahmaṇo vakṣyate, "kūṭa-stho 'kṣara ucyate / uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ" iti / "atha parā yayā tad akṣaram adhikgamyate" ity akṣara-vidyāyāṃ tu akṣara-śabda-nirdiṣṭaṃ param eva brahma, bhūta-yonitva-ādeḥ /teṣām avyakta-asakta-cetasāṃ kleśas tv adhikataraḥ / avyaktā hi gatiḥ avyakta-viṣayā mano-vṛttiḥ dehavadbhiḥ deha-ātma-abhimāna-yuktaiḥ duḥkhena avāpyate / dehavanto hi deham eva ātmānaṃ manyante //

body.text: bhagavantam upāsīnānāṃ yuktatamatvaṃ suvyaktam āha --
body.translated_text: He states clearly the best-in-<s>yoga</s>-ness of those who worship the Lord —

children.text: bhagavantam upāsīnānāṃ yuktatamatvaṃ suvyaktam āha ---
ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'But those who, renouncing all actions in Me, with Me as the supreme [goal],'

children.text: ananyenaiva yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate ||
children.translated_text: 'worship Me, meditating [on Me] through exclusive <s>yoga</s>,' ||

children.text: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya mat-parāḥ |
ananyena eva yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate ||
teṣām ahaṃ samuddhartā mṛtyusaṃsārasāgarāt |
children.translated_text: 'for them, I become the deliverer from the ocean of the cycle of death,'

children.text: bhavāmi na cirāt pārtha mayy āveśitacetasām ||
children.translated_text: 'in no long time, O <s>Pārtha</s> — for those whose minds are fixed on Me.' ||

children.text: teṣām ahaṃ samuddhartā mṛtyu-saṃsāra-sāgarāt |
bhavāmi na cirāt pārtha mayy āveśita-cetasām ||

body.text: ye tu laukikāni dehayātrāśeṣabhūtāni, dehadhāraṇārthāni ca aśanādīni karmāṇi, vaidikāni ca yagadānahomatapaḥprabhṛtīni sarvāṇi sakāraṇāni soddeśyāni adhyātmacetasā mayi saṃnyasya, matparāḥ madekaprāpyāḥ, ananyenaiva yogena ananyaprayojanena yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate dhyānārcanapraṇāmastutikīrtanādīni svayam evātyarthapriyāṇi prāpyasamāni kurvanto mām upāsata ityarthaḥ / teṣāṃ matprāptivirodhitayā mṛtyubhūtāt saṃsārākhyāt sāgarād aham acireṇaiva kālena samuddhartā bhavāmi //
body.translated_text: But those who, with their minds fixed on the inner self, offer unto Me all actions — both the worldly actions such as the acquisition of materials and the like that are subsidiary to bodily maintenance and sustenance, and the scriptural actions such as sacrifice, charity, fire-offerings, austerity, and the like, together with their causes and purposes — who are devoted to Me (<s>matparāḥ</s>), having Me alone as what is to be attained, who meditate upon Me with undivided <s>yoga</s> — with <s>yoga</s> having no other purpose — who worship Me, performing meditation, worship, prostration, praise, chanting of names, circumambulation, and the like, which are themselves supremely dear and equal to the goal to be attained — for them, I become in a very short time the deliverer from the ocean called <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is death itself, being opposed to attaining Me. ||

children.text: ye tu laukikāni deha-yātrā-aśeṣa-bhūtāni, deha-dhāraṇa-arthāni ca aśana-ādīni karmāṇi, vaidikāni ca yaga-dāna-homa-tapaḥ-prabhṛtīni sarvāṇi sakāraṇāni sa-uddeśyāni adhyātma-cetasā mayi saṃnyasya, mat-parāḥ mad-eka-prāpyāḥ, ananyena eva yogena ananya-prayojanena yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate dhyāna-arcana-praṇāma-stuti-kīrtana-ādīni svayam eva atyartha-priyāṇi prāpya-samāni kurvanto mām upāsata ity-arthaḥ / teṣāṃ mat-prāpti-virodhitayā mṛtyu-bhūtāt saṃsāra-ākhyāt sāgarād aham acireṇa eva kālena samuddhartā bhavāmi //
mayy eva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya |
children.translated_text: 'Fix your mind on Me; let your intellect dwell in Me.' |

children.text: nivasiṣyasi mayy eva ata ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'You shall dwell in Me alone hereafter — there is no doubt.' ||

children.text: mayy eva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya |
nivasiṣyasi mayy eva ata ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||

body.text: ato 'tiśayitapuruṣārthatvāt sulabhatvād aciralabhyatvāc ca mayy eva mana ādhatsva mayi manassamādhānaṃ kuru / mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya aham eva paramaprāpya ity adhyavasāyaṃ kuru / ata ūrdhvaṃ mayy eva nivasiṣyasi / aham eva paramaprāpya ity adhyavasāyapūrvakamanoniveśanānantaram eva mayi nivasiṣyasītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Since [this goal] is the supreme human goal, easy to attain, and quickly attainable — fix your mind on Me, establish concentration of mind on Me. Let your intellect dwell in Me — resolve that 'I alone am the supreme goal to be attained.' Hereafter, you shall dwell in Me alone. The meaning is: immediately upon the establishment of the mind preceded by the resolve that 'I alone am the supreme goal,' you shall dwell in Me. ||

children.text: ato 'tiśayita-puruṣa-arthatvāt sulabhatvād acira-labhyatvāc ca mayy eva mana ādhatsva mayi manas-samādhānaṃ kuru / mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya aham eva parama-prāpya ity adhyavasāyaṃ kuru / ata ūrdhvaṃ mayy eva nivasiṣyasi / aham eva parama-prāpya ity adhyavasāya-pūrvaka-mano-niveśana-anantaram eva mayi nivasiṣyasi ity-arthaḥ //
atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram |
children.translated_text: 'But if you are unable to fix your mind steadily on Me,' |

children.text: abhyāsayogena tato mām icchāptuṃ dhanañjaya ||
children.translated_text: 'then seek to attain Me through the <s>yoga</s> of practice, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>.' ||

children.text: atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram |
abhyāsa-yogena tato mām icchā āptuṃ dhanañ-jaya ||

body.text: atha sahasaiva mayi sthiraṃ cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi, tato 'bhyāsayogena mām āptum iccha svābhāvikānavadhikātiśayasaundaryasauśīlyasauhārdavātsalyakāruṇyamādhuryagāmbhīryāudāryaśairyavīryaparākramasārvajñyasatyakāmatvasatyasaṃkalpatvasarveśvaratvasakalakāraṇatvādyasaṃkhyeyaguṇasāgare nikhilaheyapratyanīke mayi niratiśayapremagarbhasmṛtyabhyāsayogena sthiraṃ cittasamādhānaṃ labdhvā māṃ prāptum iccha //
body.translated_text: But if you are unable to fix your mind steadily on Me all at once, then seek to attain Me through the <s>yoga</s> of practice — through the practice of remembrance imbued with the highest love directed toward Me, who am an ocean of innumerable qualities: innate, unsurpassable beauty, graciousness, friendliness, tenderness, compassion, sweetness, depth, generosity, steadfastness, valor, heroism, omniscience, true desire, true resolve, sovereignty over all, being the cause of all, and the like — who am the opposite of all that is undesirable. Having thus gained a steady establishment of mind through the <s>yoga</s> of practice, seek to attain Me. ||

children.text: atha sahasa aiva mayi sthiraṃ cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi, tato 'bhyāsa-yogena mām āptum iccha svābhāvika-anavadhika-atiśaya-saundarya-sauśīlya-sauhārda-vātsalya-kāruṇya-mādhurya-gāmbhīrya-audārya-śairya-vīrya-parākrama-sārvajñya-satya-kāmatva-satya-saṃkalpatva-sarva-īśvaratva-sakala-kāraṇatva-ādy-asaṃkhyeya-guṇa-sāgare nikhila-heya-pratyanīke mayi niratiśaya-prema-garbha-smṛty-abhyāsa-yogena sthiraṃ citta-samādhānaṃ labdhvā māṃ prāptum iccha //
abhyāse 'py asamartho 'si matkarmaparamo bhava |
children.translated_text: 'If you are incapable even of practice, be devoted to action for My sake.' |

children.text: madartham api karmāṇi kurvan siddhim avāpsyasi ||
children.translated_text: 'Even performing actions for My sake, you shall attain perfection.' ||

children.text: abhyāse 'py asamartho 'si mat-karma-paramo bhava |
mad-artham api karmāṇi kurvan siddhim avāpsyasi ||

body.text: athaivaṃvidhasmṛtyabhyāse 'py asamartho 'si, matkarmaparamo bhava / madīyāni karmāṇy ālayanirmāṇodyonakaraṇapradīpāropaṇamārjanābhyukṣaṇopalepanapuṣpāharaṇapūjāpravartananāmasaṃkīrtanapradakṣiṇastutinamaskārādīni; tāni atyarthapriyatvenācara / atyarthapriyatvena madarthaṃ karmāṇi kurvann api acirād abhyāsayogapūrvikāṃ mayi sthirāṃ cittasthitiṃ labdhvā matprāptirūpāṃ siddhim avāpsyasi //
body.translated_text: If you are incapable even of such practice of remembrance, be devoted to actions for My sake. My actions are: building and maintaining temples, arranging lighting, sweeping, sprinkling, applying sandalwood paste, gathering flowers, conducting worship, chanting names, circumambulation, praise, prostration, and the like. Perform these as supremely dear [to you]. Even performing actions for My sake with supreme devotion, in a short time you shall gain a steady mental establishment in Me preceded by the <s>yoga</s> of practice, and you shall attain the perfection in the form of attaining Me. ||

children.text: atha evaṃ-vidha-smṛty-abhyāse 'py asamartho 'si, mat-karma-paramo bhava / madīyāni karmāṇy ālaya-nirmāṇa-udyona-karaṇa-pradīpa-āropaṇa-mārjana-abhyukṣaṇa-upalepana-puṣpa-āharaṇa-pūjā-pravartana-nāma-saṃkīrtana-pradakṣiṇa-stuti-namaskāra-ādīni; tāni atyartha-priyatvenā acara / atyartha-priyatvena mad-arthaṃ karmāṇi kurvann api acirād abhyāsa-yoga-pūrvikāṃ mayi sthirāṃ citta-sthitiṃ labdhvā mat-prāpti-rūpāṃ siddhim avāpsyasi //
athaitad apy aśakto 'si kartuṃ madyogam āśritaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'But if you are incapable even of doing this, having taken refuge in My <s>yoga</s>,' |

children.text: sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān ||
children.translated_text: 'then renounce the fruits of all actions, being self-controlled.' ||

children.text: atha etad apy aśakto 'si kartuṃ mad-yogam āśritaḥ |
sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṃ tataḥ kuru yata-ātmavān ||

body.text:
atha madyogam āśrityaitad api kartuṃ na śaknoṣi -- madguṇānusandhānakṛtamadekapriyatvākāraṃ bhaktiyogam āśritya bhaktiyogāṅkurarūpam etan matkarmāpi kartuṃ na śaknoṣi, tato 'kṣarayogam ātmasvabhāvānusandhānarūpaṃ parabhaktijananaṃ pūrvaṣaṭkoditam āśritya tadupāyatayā sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ kuru / matpriyatvena madekaprāpyatābuddhir hi prakṣīṇāśeṣapāpasyaiva jāyate / yatātmavān yatamanaskaḥ / tato 'nabhisaṃhitaphalena madārādhanarūpeṇānuṣṭhitena karmaṇā siddhenātmadhyānena nivṛttāvidyādisarvatirodhāne maccheṣataikasvarūpe pratyagātmani sākṣātkṛte sati mayi parā bhaktiḥ svayam evotpadyate / tathā ca vakṣyate, "svakarmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ" ity ārabhya, "vimucya nirmamaś śānto brahmabhūyāya
kalapate / brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati / samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām" iti //
body.translated_text: But if, having taken refuge in My <s>yoga</s> — having resorted to <s>bhaktiyoga</s> in the form of exclusive devotion to Me arising from the contemplation of My qualities — you are unable even to do this, even this action for My sake, which is the sprout of <s>bhaktiyoga</s>, then, having resorted to the <s>yoga</s> of the imperishable (<s>akṣarayoga</s>) — the contemplation of the true nature of the self, which generates supreme devotion and which was taught in the first six chapters — renounce the fruits of all actions as a means to that. For the understanding that 'I alone am supremely lovable and the sole goal to be attained' arises only in one whose every sin has been exhausted. Being self-controlled — with controlled mind. Then, through action performed without attachment to its fruits, in the form of worshipping Me, and through the contemplation of the self perfected thereby — when the veiling of all ignorance and the like is removed and the inner self, whose sole essential nature is being a dependent (<s>śeṣa</s>) of Me, is directly realized — supreme devotion to Me arises spontaneously. And thus it will be stated: 'By worshipping Him through one's own actions, a human being attains perfection' — beginning from there up to: 'free from possessiveness, serene, he becomes fit for becoming <s>Brahman</s>. Having become <s>Brahman</s>, serene in self, he neither grieves nor desires; equal toward all beings, he attains supreme devotion to Me.' ||

children.text:
atha mad-yogam āśritya etad api kartuṃ na śaknoṣi --- mad-guṇa-anusandhāna-kṛta-mad-eka-priyatva-ākāraṃ bhakti-yogam āśritya bhakti-yoga-aṅkura-rūpam etan mat-karma api kartuṃ na śaknoṣi, tato 'kṣara-yogam ātma-sva-bhāva-anusandhāna-rūpaṃ para-bhakti-jananaṃ pūrva-ṣaṭka-uditam āśritya tad-upāyatayā sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṃ kuru / mat-priyatvena mad-eka-prāpyatā-buddhir hi prakṣīṇa-aśeṣa-pāpasya eva jāyate / yata-ātmavān yata-manaskaḥ / tato 'nabhisaṃhita-phalena mad-ārādhana-rūpeṇa anuṣṭhitena karmaṇā siddhenā atma-dhyānena nivṛtta-avidyā-ādi-sarva-tirodhāne mac-cheṣatā-eka-sva-rūpe pratyag-ātmani sākṣātkṛte sati mayi parā bhaktiḥ svayam eva utpadyate / tathā ca vakṣyate, "sva-karmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ" ity ārabhya, "vimucya nirmamaś śānto brahma-bhūyāya
kalapate / brahma-bhūtaḥ prasanna-ātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati / samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu mad-bhaktiṃ labhate parām" iti //
śreyo hi jñānam abhyāsāj jñānād dhyānaṃ viśiṣyate |
children.translated_text: 'Knowledge is better than practice; meditation is distinguished from knowledge.' |

children.text: dhyānāt karmaphalatyāgaḥ tyāgāc chāntir anantaram ||
children.translated_text: 'From meditation, the renunciation of the fruits of action; from renunciation, peace follows immediately.' ||

children.text: śreyo hi jñānam abhyāsāj jñānād dhyānaṃ viśiṣyate |
dhyānāt karma-phala-tyāgaḥ tyāgāc chāntir anantaram ||

body.text: atyarthaprītivirahitāt karkaśarūpāt smṛtyabhyāsād akṣarayāthātmyānusandhānapūrvakaṃ tadāparokṣyajñānam eva ātmahitatvena viśiṣyate / ātmāparokṣyajñānād apy aniṣpannarūpāt tadupāyabhūtātmadhyānam evātmahitatve viśiṣyate / taddhyānād apy aniṣpannarūpāt tadupāyabhūtaṃ phalatyāgenānuṣṭhitaṃ karmaiva viśiṣyate / anabhisaṃhitaphalād anuṣṭhitāt karmaṇo 'nantaram eva nirastapāpatayā manasaś śāntir bhaviṣyati; śānte manasi ātmadhyānaṃ saṃpatsyate; dhyānāc ca tadāparokṣyam; tadāparokṣyāt parā bhaktiḥ -- iti bhaktiyogābhyāsāśaktasyātmaniṣṭhaiva śreyasī / ātmaniṣṭhasyāpi aśāntamanaso niṣṭhāprāptaye antargatātmajñānānabhisaṃhitaphalakarmaniṣṭhaiva śreyasītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Better than the practice of remembrance that is harsh in nature and devoid of the highest love — is knowledge in the form of direct realization, preceded by the contemplation of the true nature of the imperishable self; it is distinguished in terms of being beneficial to the self. Better even than knowledge of the self that has not yet ripened into direct realization — is meditation upon the self, which is the means to that realization, in terms of being beneficial to the self. Better even than meditation that has not yet ripened — is action itself, performed with the renunciation of its fruits, which is the means to that meditation. From action performed without regard for its fruits, immediately afterward, peace of mind will arise through the elimination of sin; when the mind is pacified, contemplation of the self will succeed; from contemplation, direct realization thereof; and from direct realization, supreme devotion — thus, for one incapable of the practice of <s>bhaktiyoga</s>, establishment in the knowledge of the self is better. And for one established in the knowledge of the self, if his mind is not yet pacified, establishment in action performed without attachment to results, which contains within it the knowledge of the self — that alone is better. This is the meaning. ||

children.text: atyartha-prīti-virahitāt karkaśa-rūpāt smṛty-abhyāsād akṣara-yāthātmya-anusandhāna-pūrvakaṃ tad-āparokṣya-jñānam eva ātma-hitatvena viśiṣyate / ātma-āparokṣya-jñānād apy aniṣpanna-rūpāt tad-upāya-bhūta-ātma-dhyānam evā atma-hitatve viśiṣyate / tad-dhyānād apy aniṣpanna-rūpāt tad-upāya-bhūtaṃ phala-tyāgena anuṣṭhitaṃ karma eva viśiṣyate / anabhisaṃhita-phalād anuṣṭhitāt karmaṇo 'nantaram eva nirasta-pāpatayā manasaś śāntir bhaviṣyati; śānte manasi ātma-dhyānaṃ saṃpatsyate; dhyānāc ca tad-āparokṣyam; tad-āparokṣyāt parā bhaktiḥ --- iti bhakti-yoga-abhyāsa-aśaktasyā atma-niṣṭha aiva śreyasī / ātma-niṣṭhasya api aśānta-manaso niṣṭhā-prāptaye antargata-ātma-jñāna-anabhisaṃhita-phala-karma-niṣṭha aiva śreyasi īty-arthaḥ //

body.text: anabhisaṃhitaphalakarmaniṣṭhasyopādeyān guṇān āha --
body.translated_text: He states the qualities to be adopted by one established in the discipline of action performed without attachment to its results:

children.text: anabhisaṃhita-phala-karma-niṣṭhasya upādeyān guṇān āha ---
adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca |
children.translated_text: 'One who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate,' |

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī ||
children.translated_text: 'free from possessiveness, free from ego, equanimous in pain and pleasure, patient,' ||

children.text: adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca |
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ kṣamī ||
santuṣṭas satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ |
