children.translated_text: 'always content, self-controlled, of firm resolve, a <s>yogin</s>,' |

children.text: mayy arpitamanobuddhir yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'with mind and intellect offered to Me — such a devotee of Mine is dear to Me.' ||

children.text: santuṣṭas satataṃ yogī yata-ātmā dṛḍha-niścayaḥ |
mayy arpita-mano-buddhir yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||

body.text:
adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānām -- vidviṣatām apakurvatām api sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām adveṣṭā -- madaparādhānuguṇam īśvarapreritāny etāni bhūtāni dviṣanty apakurvanti cety anusandadhānaḥ; teṣu dviṣatsu apkurvatsu ca sarvabhūteṣu maitrīṃ matiṃ kurvan maitraḥ, teṣv eva duḥkhiteṣu karuṇāṃ kurvan karuṇaḥ, nirmamaḥ dehendriyeṣu tatsaṃbandhiṣu ca nirmamaḥ, nirahaṅkāraḥ dehātmābhimānarahitaḥ, tata eva samaduḥkhasukhaḥ sukhaduḥkhāgamayoḥ sāṅkalpikayoḥ harṣodvegarahitaḥ, kṣamī sparśaprabhavayor avarjanīyayor api tayor vikārarahitaḥ, saṃtuṣṭaḥ yadṛcchopanatena yena kenāpi dehadhāraṇadravyeṇa saṃtuṣṭaḥ, satataṃ yogī satataṃ prakṛtiviyuktātmānusandhānaparaḥ, yatātmā niyamitamanovṛttiḥ, dṛḍhaniścayaḥ
adhyātmaśāstroditeṣv artheṣu dṛḍhaniścayaḥ, mayy arpitamanobuddhiḥ bhagavān vāsedeva evānabhisaṃhitaphalenānuṣṭhitena karmaṇā ārādhyate, ārādhitaś ca mama ātmāparokṣyaṃ sādhayiṣyatīti mayy arpitamanobuddhiḥ, ya evaṃbhūto madbhaktaḥ -- evaṃ karmayogena māṃ bhajamāno yaḥ, sa me priyaḥ //
body.translated_text: One who hates no being — even toward all beings who hate him and do harm to him, he bears no hatred, contemplating that these beings hate and harm [him] as impelled by the Lord in accordance with his own offenses against the Lord. Toward those beings who hate and harm [him] — being friendly, maintaining a disposition of friendship; toward those very same beings when afflicted — being compassionate; free from possessiveness — devoid of the sense of 'mine' regarding the body, senses, and things connected with them; free from ego — devoid of the false identification of the self with the body; and for that very reason, equanimous in pain and pleasure — free from elation and agitation at the occurrence of pleasure and pain that are products of mental imagination; patient — free from agitation even with respect to unavoidable [experiences of] cold, heat, contact with persons, and the like that are produced by sensory contact; always content — content with whatever substance for bodily maintenance that comes of its own accord, however meager; always a <s>yogin</s> — always devoted to the contemplation of the self as separated from <s>Prakṛti</s>; self-controlled — with disciplined mental activity; of firm resolve — of firm conviction regarding the matters taught in the scriptures of the self; with mind and intellect offered to Me — [thinking] 'The Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s> is to be propitiated through action performed without attachment to results, and once propitiated, He will bring about the direct realization of my self' — thus having mind and intellect offered to Me. He who is of such nature, My devotee — who worships Me through <s>karmayoga</s> in this manner — he is dear to Me. ||

children.text:
adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānām --- vidviṣatām apakurvatām api sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām adveṣṭā --- mad-aparādha-anuguṇam īśvara-preritāny etāni bhūtāni dviṣanty apakurvanti ca ity anusandadhānaḥ; teṣu dviṣatsu apkurvatsu ca sarva-bhūteṣu maitrīṃ matiṃ kurvan maitraḥ, teṣv eva duḥkhiteṣu karuṇāṃ kurvan karuṇaḥ, nirmamaḥ deha-indriyeṣu tat-saṃbandhiṣu ca nirmamaḥ, nirahaṅkāraḥ deha-ātma-abhimāna-rahitaḥ, tata eva sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ sukha-duḥkha-āgamayoḥ sāṅkalpikayoḥ harṣa-udvega-rahitaḥ, kṣamī sparśa-prabhavayor avarjanīyayor api tayor vikāra-rahitaḥ, saṃtuṣṭaḥ yadṛcchā-upanatena yena kena api deha-dhāraṇa-dravyeṇa saṃtuṣṭaḥ, satataṃ yogī satataṃ prakṛti-viyukta-ātma-anusandhāna-paraḥ, yata-ātmā niyamita-mano-vṛttiḥ, dṛḍha-niścayaḥ
adhyātma-śāstra-uditeṣv artheṣu dṛḍha-niścayaḥ, mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ bhagavān vāse-deva eva anabhisaṃhita-phalena anuṣṭhitena karmaṇā ārādhyate, ārādhitaś ca mama ātma-āparokṣyaṃ sādhayiṣyati iti mayy arpita-mano-buddhiḥ, ya evaṃ-bhūto mad-bhaktaḥ --- evaṃ karma-yogena māṃ bhajamāno yaḥ, sa me priyaḥ //
yasmān nodvijate loko lokān nodvijate ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He from whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world,' |

children.text: harṣāmarṣabhayodvegair mukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'freed from elation, resentment, fear, and anxiety — he too is dear to Me.' ||

children.text: yasmān na udvijate loko lokān na udvijate ca yaḥ |
harṣa-amarṣa-bhaya-udvegair mukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ ||

body.text: yasmāt karmaniṣṭhāt puruṣān nimittabhūtāl loko nodvijate -- yo lokodvegakaraṃ karma kiñcid api na karotītyarthaḥ / lokāc ca nimittabhūtād yo nodvijate -- yam uddiśya sarvaloko nodvegakaraṃ karma karoti; sarvāvirodhitvaniścayāt / ata eva kañcana prati harṣeṇa, kañcana prati amarṣeṇa, kañcana prati bhayena, kañcana prati udvegena muktah; evaṃbhūto yaḥ, so 'pi mama priyaḥ //
body.translated_text: The world is not agitated by that person established in the discipline of action — meaning: he does not perform any action that would cause agitation in the world. And he who is not agitated by the world as its cause — he toward whom the entire world does not perform any action that would cause agitation, because of his firm conviction that he is inimical to none. For this very reason, he is freed from elation toward some, resentment toward some, fear of some, and anxiety regarding some. One who is of such a nature — he too is dear to Me. ||

children.text: yasmāt karma-niṣṭhāt puruṣān nimitta-bhūtāl loko na udvijate --- yo loka-udvega-karaṃ karma kiñcid api na karoti ity-arthaḥ / lokāc ca nimitta-bhūtād yo na udvijate --- yam uddiśya sarva-loko na udvega-karaṃ karma karoti; sarva-avirodhitva-niścayāt / ata eva kañcana prati harṣeṇa, kañcana prati amarṣeṇa, kañcana prati bhayena, kañcana prati udvegena muktah; evaṃ-bhūto yaḥ, so 'pi mama priyaḥ //
anapekṣaḥ śucir dakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Without expectations, pure, capable, impartial, free from distress,' |

children.text: sarvārambhaparityāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'renouncing all [selfish] undertakings — such a devotee of Mine is dear to Me.' ||

children.text: anapekṣaḥ śucir dakṣa udāsīno gata-vyathaḥ |
sarva-ārambha-parityāgī yo mad-bhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||

body.text: anapekṣaḥ ātmavyatirikte kṛtsne vastuny anapekṣaḥ, śuciḥ śāstravihitadravyavardhitakāyaḥ, dakṣaḥ -- śāstrīyakriyopādānasamarthaḥ, anyatrodāsīnaḥ, ganavyathaḥ śāstrīyakriyānirvṛttau avarjanīyaśītoṣṇapuruṣasparśādiduḥkheṣu vyathārahitaḥ, sarvārambhaparityāgī śāstrīyavyatiriktasarvakarmārambhaparityāgī, ya evaṃbhūto madbhaktaḥ, sa me priyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Without expectations — without expectations regarding anything other than the self; pure — whose body is nurtured by substances prescribed by scripture; capable — competent for the undertaking of scriptural activities; impartial toward other things; free from distress — free from distress regarding the unavoidable sufferings of cold, heat, human contact, and the like that arise in the course of performing scriptural activities; renouncing all [selfish] undertakings — renouncing all undertakings of actions other than those prescribed by scripture. He who is of such a nature, My devotee — he is dear to Me. ||

children.text: anapekṣaḥ ātma-vyatirikte kṛtsne vastuny anapekṣaḥ, śuciḥ śāstra-vihita-dravya-vardhita-kāyaḥ, dakṣaḥ --- śāstrīya-kriyā-upādāna-samarthaḥ, anyatra udāsīnaḥ, gana-vyathaḥ śāstrīya-kriyā-nirvṛttau avarjanīya-śīta-uṣṇa-puruṣa-sparśa-ādi-duḥkheṣu vyathā-rahitaḥ, sarva-ārambha-parityāgī śāstrīya-vyatirikta-sarva-karma-ārambha-parityāgī, ya evaṃ-bhūto mad-bhaktaḥ, sa me priyaḥ //
yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
children.translated_text: 'He who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor desires,' |

children.text: śubhāśubhaparityāgī bhaktimān yaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'who renounces both the auspicious and the inauspicious — such a devoted one is dear to Me.' ||

children.text: yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
śubha-aśubha-parityāgī bhaktimān yaḥ sa me priyaḥ ||

body.text: yo na hṛṣyati -- yan manuṣyāṇāṃ harṣanimittaṃ priyajātam, tat prāpya yaḥ karmayogī na hṛṣyati; yac cāpriyam, tat prāpya na dveṣṭi; yac ca manuṣyāṇāṃ śokanimittaṃ bhāryāputravittakṣayādikam, tat prāpya na śocati; tathāvidham aprāptaṃ ca na kāṅkṣati; śubhāśubhaparityāgī pāpavat puṇyasyāpi bandhahetutvāviśeṣād ubhayaparityāgī / ya evaṃbhūto bhaktimān, sa me priyaḥ //
body.translated_text: He who does not rejoice — that which is the cause of joy for human beings, the occurrence of what is pleasant: upon obtaining it, the <s>karmayogin</s> does not rejoice. And that which is unpleasant — upon obtaining it, he does not hate. And that which is the cause of grief for humans — the loss of wife, son, wealth, and the like — upon [experiencing] that, he does not grieve. And such things not yet obtained, he does not desire. One who renounces both the auspicious and the inauspicious — since merit, like sin, is a cause of bondage without distinction, he renounces both. He who is of such a nature, who has devotion — he is dear to Me. ||

children.text: yo na hṛṣyati --- yan manuṣyāṇāṃ harṣa-nimittaṃ priya-jātam, tat prāpya yaḥ karma-yogī na hṛṣyati; yac ca apriyam, tat prāpya na dveṣṭi; yac ca manuṣyāṇāṃ śoka-nimittaṃ bhāryā-putra-vitta-kṣaya-ādikam, tat prāpya na śocati; tathā-vidham aprāptaṃ ca na kāṅkṣati; śubha-aśubha-parityāgī pāpavat puṇyasya api bandha-hetutva-aviśeṣād ubhaya-parityāgī / ya evaṃ-bhūto bhaktimān, sa me priyaḥ //
samaś śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāvamānayoḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Equal toward foe and friend, and likewise in honor and dishonor,' |

children.text: śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'in cold and heat, pleasure and pain — equal, free from attachment,' ||

children.text: samaś śatrau ca mitre ca tathā māna-avamānayoḥ |
śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅga-vivarjitaḥ ||
tulyanindāstutir maunī saṃtuṣṭo yena kenacit |
children.translated_text: 'the same in blame and praise, silent, content with whatever,' |

children.text: aniketaḥ sthiramatir bhaktimān me priyo naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'homeless, of steady mind, devoted — such a person is dear to Me.' ||

children.text: tulya-nindā-stutir maunī saṃtuṣṭo yena kenacit |
aniketaḥ sthira-matir bhaktimān me priyo naraḥ ||

body.text: "adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānām" ityādinā śatrumitrādiṣu dveṣādirahitatvam uktam; atra teṣu sannihiteṣv api samacittatvaṃ tato 'py atirikto viśeṣa ucyate / ātmani sthiramatitvena niketanādiṣv asakta ity aniketaḥ; tata eva mānāvamānādiṣv api samaḥ; ya evaṃbhūto bhaktimān, sa me priyaḥ // BhGR_12.18 //19//
body.translated_text: By 'one who hates no being' and so on, freedom from hatred and the like toward enemies, friends, and others was stated. Here, equanimity of mind even when they are present is stated — a further distinction beyond that. Being of steady mind regarding the self, he is unattached to dwelling-places and the like — hence 'homeless' (<s>aniketa</s>). For that very reason, he is equal even in honor and dishonor and the like. He who is of such a nature, who has devotion — he is dear to Me. ||

children.text: "adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānām" ity-ādinā śatru-mitra-ādiṣu dveṣa-ādi-rahitatvam uktam; atra teṣu sannihiteṣv api sama-cittatvaṃ tato 'py atirikto viśeṣa ucyate / ātmani sthira-matitvena niketana-ādiṣv asakta ity aniketaḥ; tata eva māna-avamāna-ādiṣv api samaḥ; ya evaṃ-bhūto bhaktimān, sa me priyaḥ // BhGR_12.18 //19//

body.text: asmād ātmaniṣṭhād bhaktiyoganiṣṭhasya śraiṣṭhyaṃ pratipādayan yathopakramam upasaṃharati --
body.translated_text: Establishing the superiority of one established in <s>bhaktiyoga</s> over one established in the knowledge of the self, He concludes as He began:

children.text: asmād ātma-niṣṭhād bhakti-yoga-niṣṭhasya śraiṣṭhyaṃ pratipādayan yathā-upakramam upasaṃharati ---
ye tu dharmyāmṛtam idaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: 'But those who worship this immortal <s>dharma</s> as declared,' |

children.text: śraddadhānā matparamā bhaktās te 'tīva me priyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'full of faith, devoted to Me as the supreme goal — those devotees are exceedingly dear to Me.' ||

children.text: ye tu dharmya-amṛtam idaṃ yathā-uktaṃ paryupāsate |
śraddadhānā mat-paramā bhaktās te 'tīva me priyāḥ ||

body.text: dharmyaṃ cāmṛtaṃ ceti dharmyāmṛtam, ye tu prāpyasamaṃ prāpakaṃ bhaktiyogam, yathoktam -- "mayy āveśya mano ye mām"ityādinoktena prakāreṇa upāsate; te bhaktāḥ atitarāṃ mama priyāḥ //
body.translated_text: '<s>Dharmya</s>' (righteous) and '<s>amṛta</s>' (immortal) — hence '<s>dharmyāmṛta</s>' (the immortal righteousness). Those who worship <s>bhaktiyoga</s>, which is both the means and equal to the goal to be attained, in the manner declared — as stated beginning with 'those who fix their minds on Me' — those devotees are exceedingly dear to Me. ||

children.text: dharmyaṃ ca amṛtaṃ ca iti dharmya-amṛtam, ye tu prāpya-samaṃ prāpakaṃ bhakti-yogam, yathā-uktam --- "mayy āveśya mano ye mām"ity-ādina ūktena prakāreṇa upāsate; te bhaktāḥ atitarāṃ mama priyāḥ //

body.text:
pūrvasmin ṣaṭke paramaprāpyasya parasya brahmaṇo bhagavato vāsudevasya prāptyupāyabhūtabhaktirūpabhagavadupāsanāṅgabhūtaṃ prāptuḥ pratyagātmano yāthātmyadarśanaṃ jñānayogakarmayogalakṣaṇaniṣṭhādvayasādhyam uktam / madhyame ca paramaprāpyabhūtabhagavadtattvayāthātmyatanmāhātmyajñānapūrvakāikāntikātyantikabhaktiyoganiṣṭhā pratipāditā / atiśayitāiśvaryāpekṣāṇām ātmakaivalyamātrāpekṣāṇāṃ ca bhaktiyogas tattadapekṣitasādhanam iti coktam / idānīm uparitane ṣaṭke prakṛtipuruṣatatsaṃsargarūpaprapañceśvaratadyāthātmyakarmajñānabhaktisvarūpatadupādānaprakārāś ca ṣaṭkadvayoditā viśodhyante / tatra tāvat trayodaśe dehātmanoḥ svarūpam, dehayāthātmyaśodhanam, dehaviyuktātmaprāptyupāyaḥ,
viviktātmasvarūpasaṃśodhanam, tathāvidhasyātmanaś cācitsaṃbandhahetuḥ, tato vivekānusandhānaprakāraś cocyate/
body.translated_text: In the first group of six [chapters]: the direct realization of the true nature of the inner self — who is the one seeking to attain — which is an auxiliary to the worship of the Lord in the form of devotion that is the means for attaining the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, who is the supreme goal — was stated as accomplishable through the twofold discipline characterized as <s>jñānayoga</s> and <s>karmayoga</s>. In the middle [group of six]: the establishment in <s>bhaktiyoga</s> that is exclusive and ultimate, preceded by the knowledge of the true nature and greatness of the Lord who is the supreme goal, was set forth. And it was stated that <s>bhaktiyoga</s> is the means for those who desire even the surpassing sovereignty and for those who desire mere isolation of the self (<s>kaivalya</s>), for attaining their respective [goals]. Now, in the upper [final] group of six chapters: the matters taught in both [previous] groups of six are purified [and refined] — the nature of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, the manifest world that is the conjunction of these two, the Lord, the true nature of each, <s>karma</s>, <s>jñāna</s>, <s>bhakti</s> — their essential natures and the modes of their adoption. In this [thirteenth chapter], first: the essential nature of the body and the self, the purification of the true nature of the body, the means for attaining the self separated from the body, the purification of the essential nature of the distinct self, the cause of the connection of such a self with non-conscious [matter], and the mode of contemplation for discrimination from it — are stated.

children.text:
pūrvasmin ṣaṭke parama-prāpyasya parasya brahmaṇo bhagavato vāsu-devasya prāpty-upāya-bhūta-bhakti-rūpa-bhagavad-upāsana-aṅga-bhūtaṃ prāptuḥ pratyag-ātmano yāthātmya-darśanaṃ jñāna-yoga-karma-yoga-lakṣaṇa-niṣṭhā-dvaya-sādhyam uktam / madhyame ca parama-prāpya-bhūta-bhagavad-tattva-yāthātmya-tan-māhātmya-jñāna-pūrvaka-aikāntika-ātyantika-bhakti-yoga-niṣṭhā pratipāditā / atiśayita-aiśvarya-apekṣāṇām ātma-kaivalya-mātra-apekṣāṇāṃ ca bhakti-yogas tat-tad-apekṣita-sādhanam iti ca uktam / idānīm uparitane ṣaṭke prakṛti-puruṣa-tat-saṃsarga-rūpa-prapañca-īśvara-tad-yāthātmya-karma-jñāna-bhakti-sva-rūpa-tad-upādāna-prakārāś ca ṣaṭka-dvaya-uditā viśodhyante / tatra tāvat trayo-daśe deha-ātmanoḥ sva-rūpam, deha-yāthātmya-śodhanam, deha-viyukta-ātma-prāpty-upāyaḥ,
vivikta-ātma-sva-rūpa-saṃśodhanam, tathā-vidhasyā atmanaś ca acit-saṃbandha-hetuḥ, tato viveka-anusandhāna-prakāraś ca ucyate/
idaṃ śarīraṃ kaunteya kṣetram ity abhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: 'This body, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, is called the field (<s>kṣetra</s>).' |

children.text: etad yo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'He who knows this — him the knowers call the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>).' ||

children.text: idaṃ śarīraṃ kaunteya kṣetram ity abhidhīyate |
etad yo vetti taṃ prāhuḥ kṣetra-jña iti tad-vidaḥ ||

body.text:
idaṃ śarīram devo 'ham, manuṣyo 'ham, sthūlo 'ham, kṛśo 'ham iti ātmano bhoktrā saha sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratīyamānaṃ bhoktur ātmano 'rthāntarabhūtasya bhogakṣetram iti śarīrayāthātmyavidbhir abhidhīyate / etad avayavaśaḥ saṃghātarūpeṇa ca, idam ahaṃ vedmīti yo vetti, taṃ vedyabhūtād asmād veditṛtvenārthāntarabhūtam, kṣetrajña iti tadvidaḥ ātmayāthātmyavidaḥ prāhuḥ / yady api dehavyatiriktaghaṭādyarthānusandhānavelāyāṃ "devo 'ham, manuṣyo 'haṃ ghaṭādikaṃ jānāmi" iti dehasāmānādhikaraṇyena jñātāram ātmānam anusandhatte, tathāpi dehānubhavavelāyāṃ deham api ghaṭādikam iva "idam ahaṃ vedmi" iti vedyatayā veditānubhavatīti veditur ātmano vedyatayā śarīram api ghaṭādivad arthāntarabhūtam / tathā ghaṭāder iva vedyabhūtāc
charīrād api veditā kṣetrajño 'rthāntarabhūtaḥ / sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratītis tu vastutaś śarīrasya gotvādivad atmaviśeṣaṇataikasvabhāvatayā tadapṛthaksiddher upapannā / tatra veditur asādhāraṇākārasya cakṣurādikaraṇāviṣayatvād yogasaṃskṛtamanoviṣayatvāc ca prakṛtisannidhānād eva mūḍhāḥ prakṛtyākāram eva veditāraṃ paśyanti, tathā ca vakṣyati, "utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ vāpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇānvitam / vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ" iti //
body.translated_text:
This body — cognized in co-ordinate predication with the experiencer as 'I am a god,' 'I am a human,' 'I am stout,' 'I am thin' — is designated by those who know the true nature of the body as the field of experience (<s>kṣetra</s>), being a distinct entity from the experiencer self. He who knows this [body] — in its parts and in its aggregate form — as 'I know this,' is spoken of as the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) by those who know the truth, the knowers of the true nature of the self, [for he is] a distinct entity from this object of knowledge, being the knower. Although, at the time of cognizing objects other than the body such as a pot and the like, one cognizes the self as the knower in co-ordinate predication with the body — 'I, a god, I, a human, know the pot and the like' — nevertheless, at the time of experiencing the body itself, one experiences the body too, like a pot and the like, as an object of knowledge: 'I know this.' Therefore, the body too, like a pot and the like, is a distinct entity from the knower self, being an object of knowledge. Likewise, the knower — the <s>kṣetrajña</s> — is a distinct entity from the body,
which is an object of knowledge, just as [he is distinct] from a pot and the like. The cognition in co-ordinate predication [of self and body] is, in reality, justified because the body, like cow-hood [qualifying a cow], is by nature solely a qualifying attribute of the self, and is therefore non-separate in its existence from it. Therein, since the unique form of the knower is not an object of the sense-organs such as the eye and the like, and is an object only of the mind refined by <s>yoga</s>, the deluded — due to the proximity of <s>Prakṛti</s> alone — see the knower as having only the form of <s>Prakṛti</s>. And thus it will be said: 'The deluded do not see him departing, remaining, or experiencing, endowed with the <s>guṇas</s>; those with the eye of knowledge see.' //

children.text:
idaṃ śarīram devo 'ham, manuṣyo 'ham, sthūlo 'ham, kṛśo 'ham iti ātmano bhoktrā saha sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratīyamānaṃ bhoktur ātmano 'rtha-antara-bhūtasya bhoga-kṣetram iti śarīra-yāthātmya-vidbhir abhidhīyate / etad avayavaśaḥ saṃghāta-rūpeṇa ca, idam ahaṃ vedmi iti yo vetti, taṃ vedya-bhūtād asmād veditṛtvena artha-antara-bhūtam, kṣetra-jña iti tad-vidaḥ ātma-yāthātmya-vidaḥ prāhuḥ / yady api deha-vyatirikta-ghaṭa-ādy-artha-anusandhāna-velāyāṃ "devo 'ham, manuṣyo 'haṃ ghaṭa-ādikaṃ jānāmi" iti deha-sāmānādhikaraṇyena jñātāram ātmānam anusandhatte, tatha āpi deha-anubhava-velāyāṃ deham api ghaṭa-ādikam iva "idam ahaṃ vedmi" iti vedyatayā vedita ānubhavati iti veditur ātmano vedyatayā śarīram api ghaṭa-ādivad artha-antara-bhūtam / tathā ghaṭa-āder iva vedya-bhūtāc
charīrād api veditā kṣetra-jño 'rtha-antara-bhūtaḥ / sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratītis tu vastutaś śarīrasya gotva-ādivad atma-viśeṣaṇata aika-sva-bhāvatayā tad-apṛthak-siddher upapannā / tatra veditur asādhāraṇa-ākārasya cakṣur-ādi-karaṇa-aviṣayatvād yoga-saṃskṛta-mano-viṣayatvāc ca prakṛti-sannidhānād eva mūḍhāḥ prakṛty-ākāram eva veditāraṃ paśyanti, tathā ca vakṣyati, "utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ va āpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇa-anvitam / vimūḍhā na anupaśyanti paśyanti jñāna-cakṣuṣaḥ" iti //
kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi sarvakṣetreṣu bhārata |
children.translated_text: And know Me also as the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) in all <s>kṣetras</s> (fields), O <s>Bhārata</s>. |

children.text: kṣetrakṣetrajñayor jñānaṃ yat taj jñānaṃ mataṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: The knowledge of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s> — that is [true] knowledge in My view. ||

children.text: kṣetra-jñaṃ ca api māṃ viddhi sarva-kṣetreṣu bhārata |
kṣetra-kṣetra-jñayor jñānaṃ yat taj jñānaṃ mataṃ mama ||

body.text:
devamanuṣyādisarvakṣetreṣu veditṛtvākāraṃ kṣetrajñaṃ ca māṃ viddhi -- madātmakaṃ viddhi; kṣetrajñaṃ cāpīti apiśabdāt kṣetram api māṃ viddhīty uktam iti gamyate / yathā kṣetraṃ kṣetrajñaviśeṣaṇataikasvabhāvatayā tadapṛthaksiddheḥ tatsāmānādhikaraṇyenaiva nirdeśyam, tathā kṣetraṃ kṣetrajñaṃ ca madviśeṣaṇataikasvabhāvatayā madapṛthaksiddheḥ matsāmānādhikaraṇyenaiva nirdeśyau viddhi / pṛthivyādisaṃghātarūpasya kṣetrasya kṣetrajñasya ca bhagavaccharīrataikasvarūpatayā bhagavadātmakatvaṃ śrutayo vadanti, "yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā antaro yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīm antaro yamayati sa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ" ity ārabhya, "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyātmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati sa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ" ity ādyāḥ / idam evāntaryāmitayā sarvakṣetrajñānām ātmatvenāvasthānaṃ bhagavataḥ tatsāmānādhikaraṇyena vyapadeśahetuḥ / "aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ", "na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ carācaram" ,"viṣṭabhyāham idaṃ kṛtsnam ekāṃśena sthito jagat" iti purastād upariṣṭāc cābhidhāya, madhye sāmānādhikaraṇyena vyapadiśati, "ādityānām ahaṃ viṣṇuḥ" ityādinā / yad idaṃ kṣetrakṣetrajñayoḥ vivekaviṣayaṃ tayor madātmakatvaviṣayaṃ ca jñānam uktam, tad evopādeyaṃ jñānam iti mama matam / kecid āhuḥ -- "kṣetrajñaṃ cāpi māṃ viddhi" iti sāmānādhikaraṇyenaikatvam avagamyate / tataś ceśvarasyaiva sato 'jñānāt kṣetrajñatvam
iva bhavatīty abhyupagantavyam / tannivṛttyarthaś cāyam ekatvopadeśaḥ / anena ca āptatamabhagavadupadeśena, "rajjur eṣā na sarpaḥ" ity āptopadeśena sarpatvabhramanivṛttivat kṣetrajñatvabhramo nivartate -- iti /
te praṣṭavyāḥ -- ayam upadeṣṭā bhagavān vāsudevaḥ parameśvaraḥ kim ātmayāthātmyasākṣātkāreṇa nivṛttājñānaḥ uta neti / nivṛttājñānaś cet, nirviśeṣacinmātraikasvarūpe ātmani anyatadrūpādhyāsāsaṃbhāvanayā kaunteyādibhedadarśanaṃ, tān praty upadeśādivyāpārāś ca na saṃbhavanti / athātmasākṣātkārābhāvād anivṛttājñānaḥ, na tarhy ajñatvād evātmajñānopadeśasaṃbhavaḥ; "upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninas tattvadarśinaḥ" iti hy uktam / ata evam ādivādā anākalitaśrutismṛtītihāsapurāṇanyāyasvavāgvirodhair ajñānibhir jaganmohanāya pravartitā ity anādaraṇīyāḥ / atredaṃ tattvam --
acidvastunaś cidvastunaḥ parasya ca brahmaṇo bhogyatvena bhoktṛtvena ceśitṛtvena ca svarūpavivekam āhuḥ kāścana śrutayaḥ, "asmān māyī sṛjate viśvam etat tasmiṃś cānyo māyayā sanniruddhaḥ", "māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyān māyinaṃ tu maheśvaraṃ", "kṣaraṃ pradhānam amṛtākṣaraṃ haraḥ kṣarātmānāv īśate deva ekaḥ" -- amṛtākṣaraṃ haraḥ iti bhoktā nirdiśyate; pradhānam ātmano bhogyatvena haratīti haraḥ -- "sa kāraṇaṃ karaṇādhipādhipo na cāsya kaściñ janitā na cādhipaḥ", "pradhānakṣetrajñapatir guṇeśaḥ", "patiṃ viśvasyātmeśvaraṃ śāśvataṃ śivam acyutam", "jñājñau dvāv ajāv īśanīśau", "nityo nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān", "bhoktā bhogyaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā", "pṛthagātmānaṃ
preritāraṃ ca matvā juṣṭas tatas tenāmṛtatvam eti", "tayor anyaḥ pippalaṃ svādv atty anaśnann anyo 'bhicākaśīti", "ajām ekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇāṃ bahvīṃ prajāṃ janayantīṃ sarūpām / ajo hy eko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahāty enāṃ bhuktabhogām ajo 'nyaḥ" ityādyāḥ / atrāpi, "ahaṅkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā / apareyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām / jīvabhūtāṃ", "sarvabhūtāni kauntteya prakṛtiṃ yānti māmikām / kalpakṣaye punas tāni kalpādau visṛjāmy aham // prakṛtiṃ svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ / bhūtagrāmam imaṃ kṛtsnam avaśaṃ prakṛter vaśāt // ..... mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtis sūyate sacarācaram / hetunānena kaunteya jagad dhi parivartate //prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhy anādī ubhāv api "mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmy aham / saṃbhavas sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata" iti / jagadyonibhūtaṃ mahad brahma madīyaṃ prakṛtyākhyaṃ bhūtasūkṣmam acidvastu yat, tasmin cetanākhyaṃ garbhaṃ saṃyojayāmi; tato matsaṅkalpakṛtāc cidacitsaṃsargād eva devādisthāvarāntānām acinmiśrāṇāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃbhavo bhavatītyarthaḥ /
evaṃ bhoktṛbhogyarūpeṇāvasthitayoḥ sarvāvasthāvasthitayoś cidacitoḥ paramapuruṣaśarīratayā tanniyāmyatvena tadapṛthaksthitiṃ paramapuruṣasya cātmatvam āhuḥ kāścana śrutayaḥ, "yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā antaro yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīm antaro yamayati" ity ārabhya, "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyātmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati sa ta ātmāntaryāmyamṛtāḥ" iti; tathā, "yaḥ pṛthivīm antare sañcaran yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaṃ pṛthivī na veda" ity ārabhya, yo 'kṣaram antare sañcaran yasyākṣaraṃ śarīraṃ yam akṣaraṃ na veda", "yo mṛtyum antare sañcaran yasya mṛtyuś śarīraṃ yaṃ mṛtyur na veda eṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmāpahatapāpmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇa",
-- atra mṛtyuśabdena tamaśśabdavācyaṃ sūkṣmāvastham acidvastv abhidhīyate, asyām evopaniṣadi, "avyaktam akṣare līyate akṣaraṃ tamasi līyate" iti vacanāt -- "antaḥpraviṣṭaś śāstā janānāṃ sarvātmā" iti ca / evaṃ sarvāvasthāvasthitacidacidvastuśarīratayā tatprakāraḥ paramapuruṣa eva kāryāvasthakāraṇāvasthajagadrūpeṇāvasthita itīmam arthaṃ jñāpayituṃ kāścana śrutayaḥ kāryāvathaṃ kāraṇāvathaṃ ca jagat sa evety āhuḥ, "sad eva somyedam agra āsīd ekam evādvitīyam", "tad aikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti / tat tejo 'sṛjata" ity ārabhya, "sanmūlās somyemās sarvāḥ prajās sadāyatanās satpratiṣṭhā", "aitadātmyam idaṃ sarvaṃ tat satyaṃ sa ātmā tat tvam asi śvetaketo" iti / tathā, "so 'kāmayata, bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti / sa tapo 'tapyata, sa tapas taptvā, idaṃ
sarvam asṛjata" ity ārabhya, "satyaṃ cāmṛtaṃ ca satyam abhavat" iti / atrāpi śrutyantarasiddhiś cidacitoḥ paramapuruṣasya ca svarūpavivekaḥ smāritaḥ, "hantāham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇi", "tat sṛṣṭvā, tad evānupraviśat, tadanupraviśya, sac ca tyac cābhavat ..... vijñānaṃ cāvijñānaṃ ca satyaṃ cānṛtaṃ ca satyam abhavat" iti ca / evaṃbhūtam eva nāmarūpavyākaraṇam, "tad dhedaṃ tarhy avyākṛtam āsīt, tannāmarūpābhyāṃ vyākriyata" ity atrāpy uktam /
ataḥ kāryāvasthaḥ kāraṇāvasthaś ca sthūlasūkṣmacidacidvastuśarīraḥ paramapuruṣa eveti, kāraṇāt kāryasyānanyatvena kāraṇavijñānena kāryasya jñātatayaikavijñānena sarvavijñānaṃ ca samīhitam upapannataram / "hantāham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenātmanānupraviśya nāmarūpe vyākaravāṇi" iti, "tisro devatāḥ" iti sarvam acidvastu nirdiśya tatra svātmakajīvānupraveśena nāmarūpavyākaraṇavacanāt sarve vācakāḥ śabdāḥ acijjīvaviśiṣṭaparamātmana eva vācakā iti kāraṇāvasthaparamātmavācinā śabdena kāryavācinaḥ śabdasya sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ mukhyavṛttam / ataḥ sthūlasūkṣmacidacitprakāraṃ brahmaiva kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ ceti brahmopādānaṃ jagat / sūkṣmacidacidvastuśarīraṃ brahmaiva kāraṇam iti jagato brahmopādānatve
'pi saṃghātasyopādānatvena cidacitor brahmaṇaś ca svabhāvāsaṅkaro 'py upapannataraḥ / yathā śuklakṛṣṇaraktatantusaṃghātopādānatve 'pi citrapaṭasya tattattantupradeśa eva śauklyādisaṃbandha iti kāryāvasthāyām api na sarvatra varṇasaṅkaraḥ -- tathā cidacidīśvarasaṃghātopādānatve 'pi jagataḥ kāryāvasthāyām api bhoktṛtvabhogyatvaniyantṛtvādyasaṅkaraḥ / tantūnāṃ pṛthaksthitiyogyānām eva puruṣecchayā kadācit saṃhatānāṃ kāraṇatvaṃ kāryatvaṃ ca; iha tu cidacitos sarvāvasthayoḥ paramapuruṣaśarīratvena tatprakāratayaiva padārthatvāt tatprakāraḥ paramapuruṣa eva karāṇa kāryaṃ ca; sa eva sarvadā sarvaśabdavācya iti viśeṣaḥ / svabhāvabhedas tadasaṅkaraś ca tatra cātra ca tulyaḥ / evaṃ ca sati parasya brahmaṇaḥ kāryānupraveśe 'pi
svarūpānyathābhāvābhāvād avikṛtatvam upapannataram / sthūlāvasthasya nāmarūpavibhāgavibhaktasya cidacidvastunaḥ ātmatayāvasthānāt kāryatvam apy upapannam / avasthāntarāpattir eva hi kāryatā / nirguṇavādāś ca parasya brahmaṇo heyaguṇasaṃbandhābhāvād upapadyante / "apahatapāpmā vijaro vimṛtyur viśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ" iti heyaguṇān pratiṣidhya, "satyakāmas satyasaṅkalpaḥ" iti kalyāṇaguṇagaṇān vidadhatīyaṃ śrutir eva anyatra sāmānyenāvagataṃ guṇaniṣedhaṃ heyaguṇaviṣayaṃ vyavasthāpayati / jñānasvarūpa brahma iti vādaś ca sarvajñasya sarvaśakter nikhilaheyapratyanīkakaylāṇaguṇākarasya brahmaṇaḥ svarūpaṃ jñānaikanirūpaṇīyaṃ svaprakāśatayā jñānasvarūpaṃ cety abhyupagamād upapannataraḥ / "yas sarvajñaḥ sarvavit", "parāsya
śaktir vividhaiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñānabalakriyā ca, "vijñātāram are kena vijānīyāt" ityādikāḥ jñātṛtvam āvedayanti / "satyaṃ jñānam" ityādikāś ca jñānaikanirūpaṇīyatayā svaprakāśatayā ca jñānasvarūpatām / "so 'kāmayata bahu syām", "tad aikṣata bahu syām", "tan nāmarūpābhyām eva vyākriyata" iti brahmaiva svasaṅkalpād vicitrasthiratrasarūpatayā nānāprakāram avasthitam iti tatpratyanīkābrahmātmakavastunānātvam atattvam iti pratiṣidhyate, "mṛtyuḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati ..... neha nānāsti kiñcana", "yatra hi dvaitam iva bhavati tad itara itaraṃ paśyati / yatra tv asya sarvam ātmaivābhūt tat kena kaṃ paśyet" ityādinā / na punaḥ, "bahu syāṃ prajāyeya" ityādiśrutisiddhaṃ svasaṅkalpakṛtaṃ brahmaṇo nānānāmarūpabhāktvena nānāprakāratvam
api niṣidhyate / "yatra tv asya sarvam ātmaivābhūt" iti niṣedhavākyārambhe ca tat sthāpitam, "sarvaṃ taṃ parādād yo 'nyatarātmanas sarvaṃ veda", "tasya etasya mahato bhūtasya niśśvasitam etad yad ṛgvedaḥ" ityādinā /
evaṃ cidacidīśvarāṇāṃ svarūpabhedaṃ svabhāvabhedaṃ ca vadantīnāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaṃ kāryakāraṇayor ananyatvaṃ vadantīnāṃ ca sarvāsāṃ śrutīnām avirodhaḥ, cidacitoḥ paramātmanaś ca sarvadā śarīrātmabhāvaṃ śarīrabhūtayoḥ kāraṇadaśāyāṃ nāmarūpavibhāgānarhasūkṣmadaśāpattiṃ kāryadaśāyāṃ ca tadarhasthūladaśāpattiṃ vadantībhiḥ śrutibhir eva jñāyata iti brahmājñānavādasyāupādhikabrahmabhedavādasya anyasyāpi apanyāyamūlasya sakalaśrutiviruddhasya na kathaṃcid apy avakāśo dṛśyata ity alam ativistareṇa //
body.translated_text:
'Know the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) in the form of the knower in all fields — those of gods, humans, and the like — as having Me as its self' — that is, know it as having Me as its essence. From the word 'also' in 'and the <s>kṣetrajña</s> also,' it is understood that the field (<s>kṣetra</s>) too should be known as having Me [as its essence]. Just as the field, being of a nature inseparable from the <s>kṣetrajña</s> by virtue of being its attribute, is to be designated only through co-referential predication (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) with it, so too know that the field and the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, being of a nature inseparable from Me by virtue of being My attributes, are to be designated only through co-referential predication with Me. The <s>śrutis</s> declare that the field — in the form of the aggregate of earth and the like — and the <s>kṣetrajña</s> have the Lord as their essence by virtue of having the Lord's body as their sole essential nature: 'He who, standing in the earth, is interior to the earth, whom the earth does not know, whose body the earth is, who controls the earth from within — He is your self, the inner controller, the immortal' — beginning thus, [and continuing] up to: 'He who, standing in the self, is interior to the self, whom the self does not know, whose body the self is, who controls the self from within — He is your self, the inner controller, the immortal' — and so on. This very presence of the Lord as the self of all <s>kṣetrajñas</s> through being their inner controller is the ground for designating Him through co-referential predication with them. 'I am the self, O <s>Guḍākeśa</s>, seated in the heart of all beings,' 'There is nothing existent, moving or unmoving, that could be without Me,' 'I pervade this entire universe, standing in a single portion' — having stated [these] before and after, He designates [Himself] in between through co-referential predication, by [statements such as] 'Among the <s>Ādityas</s> I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>' and so on. This knowledge concerning the distinction between the field and the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, and concerning their having Me as their essence — this alone is the knowledge to be adopted: such is My view.

Some say: 'Know the <s>kṣetrajña</s> also as Me' — by this, through co-referential predication, oneness is understood. And therefore it must be accepted that the Lord alone, being [in reality one], appears as if a <s>kṣetrajña</s> due to ignorance. And this teaching of oneness is for the purpose of removing that [ignorance]. And by this most authoritative teaching of the Lord, just as the delusion of [seeing] a snake is removed by the trustworthy instruction 'This is a rope, not a snake,' so the delusion of being a <s>kṣetrajña</s> is removed — thus [they say].

They are to be asked: Is this teacher, the Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Supreme Lord, one whose ignorance has been removed by the direct realization of the true nature of the self, or not? If His ignorance has been removed, then in a self whose sole essential nature is undifferentiated pure consciousness, since the superimposition of any other form upon it is inconceivable, the perception of distinctions such as <s>Kaunteya</s> (son of <s>Kuntī</s>) and the like, and activities such as teaching toward them, are impossible. If, on the other hand, His ignorance has not been removed due to the absence of direct self-realization, then, being ignorant Himself, the possibility of teaching knowledge of the self does not exist; for it has been said: 'The knowers who have seen the truth will teach you knowledge.' Therefore, such doctrines and the like, propounded by ignorant persons who fail to comprehend the contradictions with <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>itihāsa</s>, <s>purāṇa</s>, logic, and their own statements, for the purpose of deluding the world, are not to be regarded. Here, the truth is as follows:

Certain <s>śrutis</s> declare the distinction of essential nature among the non-conscious substance, the conscious substance, and the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — as what is to be enjoyed, as the enjoyer, and as the controller respectively: 'From this the magician (<s>māyin</s>) projects this entire [universe]; and in it the other is confined by <s>māyā</s>,' 'Know <s>māyā</s> to be <s>Prakṛti</s>, and the possessor of <s>māyā</s> to be the great Lord,' 'The perishable is the <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter); the immortal imperishable is <s>Hara</s> — the one God rules over the perishable and the soul' — 'the immortal imperishable is <s>Hara</s>' designates the enjoyer; <s>Hara</s> means the one who takes away (<s>harati</s>) the <s>pradhāna</s> as something to be enjoyed by the self — 'He is the cause, the lord of the lords of the organs; He has no progenitor and no overlord,' 'the lord of <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>, the master of the <s>guṇas</s>,' 'the lord of the universe, the ruler of selves, the eternal, the auspicious, the imperishable,' 'the two unborn, the knowing and the unknowing, the ruling and the non-ruling,' 'the eternal among eternals, the conscious among the conscious, the one among the many who fulfills desires,' 'having known the enjoyer, the enjoyable, and the impeller,' 'having known the self as distinct, and the impeller, and being favored by Him, one attains immortality,' 'of these two, the other eats the sweet fruit; the other looks on without eating,' 'One unborn female, red, white, and black, producing many offspring of similar form — one unborn male lies with her enjoying; another unborn male leaves her after her pleasures are exhausted' — and so on.

Here too [in the <s>Gītā</s>]: 'Egoism and the rest — this is My <s>Prakṛti</s> divided eightfold. This is the lower; know My other, higher <s>Prakṛti</s>, which has become the living souls,' 'All beings, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, go to My <s>Prakṛti</s> at the end of the age; at the beginning of the age I send them forth again. Resorting to My own <s>Prakṛti</s>, I send forth again and again this entire multitude of beings, helpless under the sway of <s>Prakṛti</s>... Under My supervision, <s>Prakṛti</s> gives birth to the moving and the unmoving; by this cause, O <s>Kaunteya</s>, the world revolves,' 'Know both <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> to be beginningless,' 'My womb is the great <s>Brahman</s>; in that I place the seed. The origination of all beings then comes about, O <s>Bhārata</s>' — the great <s>Brahman</s> that is the womb of the universe, My own, called <s>Prakṛti</s>, the subtle element, the non-conscious substance — in that I conjoin the seed called the conscious [soul]; from that — from the conjunction of the conscious and the non-conscious brought about by My will — the origination of all beings, from gods down to immovable things, mixed with the non-conscious, comes about — this is the meaning.

Thus, certain <s>śrutis</s> declare that the conscious and non-conscious entities, which subsist in the form of enjoyer and enjoyed in all states, have their inseparable existence in the Supreme Person by virtue of being His body and being governed by Him, and declare the Supreme Person's being their self: 'He who, standing in the earth, is interior to the earth, whom the earth does not know, whose body the earth is, who controls the earth from within' — beginning thus, [and continuing up to]: 'He who, standing in the self, is interior to the self, whom the self does not know, whose body the self is, who controls the self from within — He is your self, the inner controller, the immortal.' Likewise: 'He who moves within the earth, whose body the earth is, whom the earth does not know' — beginning thus, [up to]: 'He who moves within the imperishable, whose body the imperishable is, whom the imperishable does not know,' 'He who moves within death, whose body death is, whom death does not know — He is the inner self of all beings, free from evil, divine, the one God, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' — here, by the word 'death,' the non-conscious substance in its subtle state, denoted by the word 'darkness,' is referred to, since in this very <s>Upaniṣad</s> it is stated: 'The unmanifest dissolves into the imperishable, the imperishable dissolves into darkness.' Also: 'Having entered within, He is the ruler of all people, the self of all.'

Thus, certain <s>śrutis</s>, in order to make known this truth — that the Supreme Person alone, having the conscious and non-conscious substances in all their states as His body and thus as His modes (<s>prakāra</s>), subsists in the form of the universe in both its causal and effectual states — declare that the universe in its effectual state and in its causal state is He alone: 'Being (<s>sat</s>) alone, dear one, was this in the beginning, one only, without a second,' 'It willed: "May I become many, may I be born." It created fire' — beginning thus, [up to]: 'All these creatures have Being as their root, Being as their abode, Being as their support,' 'All this has that as its self; that is the truth; He is the self; that you are, O <s>Śvetaketu</s>.' Likewise: 'He desired: "May I become many, may I be born." He performed austerity. Having performed austerity, He created all this' — beginning thus, [up to]: 'He became truth and immortality; He became truth.'

Here too, the distinction of essential nature among the conscious, the non-conscious, and the Supreme Person, established in other <s>śrutis</s>, is recalled: 'Let Me enter these three divinities with this living self and differentiate names and forms,' 'Having created that, He entered into that very [creation]. Having entered, He became both the existent and the beyond... both the conscious and the non-conscious, both truth and non-truth — He became truth.' The differentiation of names and forms is precisely of this nature, as stated also in: 'That was then undifferentiated; it was differentiated by name and form.'

Therefore, since the Supreme Person alone, having the gross and subtle conscious and non-conscious substances as His body, [is both cause and effect], and since the effect is non-different from the cause, the assertion that by knowing the cause, the effect is known — that by one act of knowing, all is known — is most well-established. Since [the <s>śruti</s>] says 'Let Me enter these three divinities with this living self and differentiate names and forms,' designating all non-conscious substance as 'three divinities' and stating that the differentiation of names and forms occurs through the entry of the living souls that have Him as their self, all designating words are designators of the Supreme Self alone as qualified by the non-conscious and the conscious. Therefore, the co-referential predication of the word denoting the effect with the word denoting the cause-state Supreme Self is in its primary sense. Hence, <s>Brahman</s> alone, having the gross and subtle conscious and non-conscious as Its modes, is both the effect and the cause — thus the universe has <s>Brahman</s> as its material cause. Since <s>Brahman</s> having the subtle conscious and non-conscious substances as Its body is itself the cause, even though <s>Brahman</s> is the material cause of the universe, since the aggregate is the material cause, there is no confusion of the essential natures of the conscious, the non-conscious, and <s>Brahman</s> — this too is most well-established. Just as when a multi-colored fabric has an aggregate of white, black, and red threads as its material cause, whiteness and the like pertain only to the respective thread-portions, so that even in the effectual state there is no confusion of colors everywhere — similarly, even though the universe has the aggregate of the conscious, the non-conscious, and the Lord as its material cause, even in the effectual state there is no confusion of the [properties of] being the enjoyer, being the enjoyed, and being the controller. In the case of threads, which are capable of existing separately, their being cause and effect arises from their being sometimes aggregated by human will. But here, since the conscious and the non-conscious in all states are entities only as modes of the Supreme Person by virtue of being His body, the Supreme Person who has them as His modes is alone both the cause and the effect; He alone is at all times expressible by all words — this is the distinction. The difference of essential natures and their non-confusion is the same in both cases.

And this being so, even though the supreme <s>Brahman</s> enters into the effect, since there is no alteration of His essential nature, His being unmodified (<s>avikṛta</s>) is most well-established. And since He abides as the self of the conscious and non-conscious substance in the gross state, differentiated by the distinctions of name and form, His being the effect is also established — for being an effect is nothing but the attainment of a different state. And the statements of <s>Brahman</s> being without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>) are established as referring to the absence of any connection with defective qualities in the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. The <s>śruti</s> itself, having negated defective qualities — 'free from evil, free from old age, free from death, free from sorrow, free from hunger, free from thirst' — and then setting forth a host of auspicious qualities — 'of true will, of true resolve' — thereby determines that the negation of qualities understood generally elsewhere pertains [only] to defective qualities. And the doctrine that <s>Brahman</s> is of the nature of consciousness is most well-established, since it is accepted that the essential nature of <s>Brahman</s> — who is omniscient, omnipotent, a treasure-house of auspicious qualities opposed to all that is defective — is definable solely by consciousness, and is of the nature of consciousness by virtue of being self-luminous. 'He who is all-knowing, all-perceiving,' 'His supreme power is heard to be of various kinds — natural knowledge, strength, and action,' 'How would you know the knower?' — and such [passages] reveal His nature as knower. 'Truth, knowledge' and such [passages reveal] His being of the nature of consciousness by virtue of being definable solely by consciousness and being self-luminous. 'He desired: "May I become many,"' 'It willed: "May I become many,"' 'It was differentiated by name and form' — since <s>Brahman</s> alone, by Its own will, subsists in manifold modes in the form of the diverse moving and unmoving [entities], what is negated is the multiplicity of non-<s>Brahman</s> substances that would be opposed to this: 'Death after death does he obtain who sees as if there is multiplicity here... There is no multiplicity here whatsoever,' 'Where there is, as it were, duality, there one sees the other... But where all this has become the self alone, then by what and whom would one see?' — and so on. But the manifold modal existence of <s>Brahman</s> through possessing diverse names and forms, brought about by Its own will, which is established in <s>śrutis</s> like 'May I become many, may I be born' — that is not negated. And in the introductory passage of the negation: 'Where all this has become the self alone' — that [multiplicity as modes of the self] is established: 'Everything abandons him who knows all as other than the self,' 'The exhalations of this great being are the <s>Ṛgveda</s>' — and so on.

Thus, there is no contradiction among all the <s>śrutis</s> — those that declare the distinction of essential nature and the difference of characteristics among the conscious, the non-conscious, and the Lord, and those that declare the cause-effect relationship and the non-difference of cause and effect — since it is known from the <s>śrutis</s> themselves that the conscious and the non-conscious always stand in the relation of body to the Supreme Self, and that in the causal state [the body] attains a subtle condition not susceptible to the differentiation of name and form, while in the effectual state it attains a gross condition susceptible to that [differentiation]. Therefore, no room whatsoever is found for the doctrine of <s>Brahman</s>'s ignorance, for the doctrine of <s>Brahman</s>'s difference being due to limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), or for any other [doctrine] that is rooted in fallacious reasoning and contradicts all <s>śrutis</s>. Enough of excessive elaboration. //

deva-manuṣya-ādi-sarva-kṣetreṣu veditṛtva-ākāraṃ kṣetra-jñaṃ ca māṃ viddhi --- mad-ātmakaṃ viddhi; kṣetra-jñaṃ ca api iti api-śabdāt kṣetram api māṃ viddhi ity uktam iti gamyate / yathā kṣetraṃ kṣetra-jña-viśeṣaṇatā-eka-sva-bhāvatayā tad-apṛthak-siddheḥ tat-sāmānādhikaraṇyena eva nirdeśyam, tathā kṣetraṃ kṣetra-jñaṃ ca mad-viśeṣaṇatā-eka-sva-bhāvatayā mad-apṛthak-siddheḥ mat-sāmānādhikaraṇyena eva nirdeśyau viddhi / pṛthivy-ādi-saṃghāta-rūpasya kṣetrasya kṣetra-jñasya ca bhagavac-charīratā-eka-sva-rūpatayā bhagavad-ātmakatvaṃ śrutayo vadanti, "yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā antaro yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīm antaro yamayati sa ta ātma āntaryāmy amṛtaḥ" ity ārabhya, "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyā atmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati sa ta ātma āntaryāmy amṛtaḥ" ity ādyāḥ / idam eva antaryāmitayā sarva-kṣetra-jñānām ātmatvena avasthānaṃ bhagavataḥ tat-sāmānādhikaraṇyena vyapadeśa-hetuḥ / "aham ātmā guḍākeśa sarva-bhūta-āśaya-sthitaḥ", "na tad asti vinā yat syān mayā bhūtaṃ cara-acaram" ,"viṣṭabhya aham idaṃ kṛtsnam eka-aṃśena sthito jagat" iti purastād upariṣṭāc ca abhidhāya, madhye sāmānādhikaraṇyena vyapadiśati, "ādityānām ahaṃ viṣṇuḥ" ity-ādinā / yad idaṃ kṣetra-kṣetra-jñayoḥ viveka-viṣayaṃ tayor mad-ātmakatva-viṣayaṃ ca jñānam uktam, tad eva upādeyaṃ jñānam iti mama matam / kecid āhuḥ --- "kṣetra-jñaṃ ca api māṃ viddhi" iti sāmānādhikaraṇyena ekatvam avagamyate / tataś ca iśvarasya eva sato 'jñānāt kṣetra-jñatvam
iva bhavati ity abhyupagantavyam / tan-nivṛtty-arthaś ca ayam ekatva-upadeśaḥ / anena ca āptatama-bhagavad-upadeśena, "rajjur eṣā na sarpaḥ" ity āpta-upadeśena sarpatva-bhrama-nivṛttivat kṣetra-jñatva-bhramo nivartate --- iti /
te praṣṭavyāḥ --- ayam upadeṣṭā bhagavān vāsu-devaḥ parama-īśvaraḥ kim ātma-yāthātmya-sākṣātkāreṇa nivṛtta-ajñānaḥ uta na iti / nivṛtta-ajñānaś cet, nirviśeṣa-cin-mātra-eka-sva-rūpe ātmani anya-tad-rūpa-adhyāsa-asaṃbhāvanayā kaunteya-ādi-bheda-darśanaṃ, tān praty upadeśa-ādi-vyāpārāś ca na saṃbhavanti / athā atma-sākṣātkāra-abhāvād anivṛtta-ajñānaḥ, na tarhy ajñatvād evā atma-jñāna-upadeśa-saṃbhavaḥ; "upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninas tattva-darśinaḥ" iti hy uktam / ata evam ādi-vādā anākalita-śruti-smṛti-itihāsa-purāṇa-nyāya-sva-vāg-virodhair ajñānibhir jagan-mohanāya pravartitā ity anādaraṇīyāḥ / atra idaṃ tattvam ---
acid-vastunaś cid-vastunaḥ parasya ca brahmaṇo bhogyatvena bhoktṛtvena cā iśitṛtvena ca sva-rūpa-vivekam āhuḥ kāścana śrutayaḥ, "asmān māyī sṛjate viśvam etat tasmiṃś ca anyo māyayā sanniruddhaḥ", "māyāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ vidyān māyinaṃ tu mahā-īśvaraṃ", "kṣaraṃ pradhānam amṛta-akṣaraṃ haraḥ kṣara-ātmānāv īśate deva ekaḥ" --- amṛta-akṣaraṃ haraḥ iti bhoktā nirdiśyate; pradhānam ātmano bhogyatvena harati iti haraḥ --- "sa kāraṇaṃ karaṇa-adhipa-adhipo na ca asya kaściñ janitā na ca adhipaḥ", "pradhāna-kṣetra-jña-patir guṇa-īśaḥ", "patiṃ viśvasyā atma-īśvaraṃ śāśvataṃ śivam acyutam", "jña-ajñau dvāv ajāv īś-anīśau", "nityo nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān", "bhoktā bhogyaṃ preritāraṃ ca matvā", "pṛthag-ātmānaṃ
preritāraṃ ca matvā juṣṭas tatas tena amṛtatvam eti", "tayor anyaḥ pippalaṃ svādv atty anaśnann anyo 'bhicākaśīti", "ajām ekāṃ lohita-śukla-kṛṣṇāṃ bahvīṃ prajāṃ janayantīṃ sarūpām / ajo hy eko juṣamāṇo 'nuśete jahāty enāṃ bhukta-bhogām ajo 'nyaḥ" ity-ādyāḥ / atra api, "ahaṅkāra iti iyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā / apara īyam itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām / jīva-bhūtāṃ", "sarva-bhūtāni kauntteya prakṛtiṃ yānti māmikām / kalpa-kṣaye punas tāni kalpa-ādau visṛjāmy aham // prakṛtiṃ svām avaṣṭabhya visṛjāmi punaḥ punaḥ / bhūta-grāmam imaṃ kṛtsnam avaśaṃ prakṛter vaśāt // ..... maya ādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtis sūyate sacara-acaram / hetuna ānena kaunteya jagad dhi parivartate //prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ ca eva viddhy anādī ubhāv api "mama yonir mahad brahma tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmy aham / saṃbhavas sarva-bhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata" iti / jagad-yoni-bhūtaṃ mahad brahma madīyaṃ prakṛty-ākhyaṃ bhūta-sūkṣmam acid-vastu yat, tasmin cetana-ākhyaṃ garbhaṃ saṃyojayāmi; tato mat-saṅkalpa-kṛtāc cid-acit-saṃsargād eva deva-ādi-sthāvara-antānām acin-miśrāṇāṃ sarva-bhūtānāṃ saṃbhavo bhavati ity-arthaḥ /
evaṃ bhoktṛ-bhogya-rūpeṇa avasthitayoḥ sarva-avastha-avasthitayoś cid-acitoḥ parama-puruṣa-śarīratayā tan-niyāmyatvena tad-apṛthak-sthitiṃ parama-puruṣasya cā atmatvam āhuḥ kāścana śrutayaḥ, "yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā antaro yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīm antaro yamayati" ity ārabhya, "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyā atmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati sa ta ātma āntaryāmy-amṛtāḥ" iti; tathā, "yaḥ pṛthivīm antare sañcaran yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaṃ pṛthivī na veda" ity ārabhya, yo 'kṣaram antare sañcaran yasya akṣaraṃ śarīraṃ yam akṣaraṃ na veda", "yo mṛtyum antare sañcaran yasya mṛtyuś śarīraṃ yaṃ mṛtyur na veda eṣa sarva-bhūta-antara-ātma āpahata-pāpmā divyo deva eko nārāyaṇa",
--- atra mṛtyu-śabdena tamaś-śabda-vācyaṃ sūkṣma-avastham acid-vastv abhidhīyate, asyām eva upaniṣadi, "avyaktam akṣare līyate akṣaraṃ tamasi līyate" iti vacanāt --- "antaḥ-praviṣṭaś śāstā janānāṃ sarva-ātmā" iti ca / evaṃ sarva-avasthā-avasthita-cid-acid-vastu-śarīratayā tat-prakāraḥ parama-puruṣa eva kārya-avastha-kāraṇa-avastha-jagad-rūpeṇa avasthita iti imam arthaṃ jñāpayituṃ kāścana śrutayaḥ kārya-avathaṃ kāraṇa-avathaṃ ca jagat sa eva ity āhuḥ, "sad eva somya idam agra āsīd ekam eva advitīyam", "tad aikṣata bahu syāṃ prajāyeya iti / tat tejo 'sṛjata" ity ārabhya, "san-mūlās somya imās sarvāḥ prajās sad-āyatanās sat-pratiṣṭhā", "aitad-ātmyam idaṃ sarvaṃ tat satyaṃ sa ātmā tat tvam asi śveta-keto" iti / tathā, "so 'kāmayata, bahu syāṃ prajāyeya iti / sa tapo 'tapyata, sa tapas taptvā, idaṃ
sarvam asṛjata" ity ārabhya, "satyaṃ ca amṛtaṃ ca satyam abhavat" iti / atra api śruty-antara-siddhiś cid-acitoḥ parama-puruṣasya ca sva-rūpa-vivekaḥ smāritaḥ, "hanta aham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenā atmana ānupraviśya nāma-rūpe vyākaravāṇi", "tat sṛṣṭvā, tad eva anupraviśat, tad-anupraviśya, sac ca tyac ca abhavat ..... vijñānaṃ ca avijñānaṃ ca satyaṃ ca anṛtaṃ ca satyam abhavat" iti ca / evaṃ-bhūtam eva nāma-rūpa-vyākaraṇam, "tad dha idaṃ tarhy avyākṛtam āsīt, tan-nāma-rūpābhyāṃ vyākriyata" ity atra apy uktam /
ataḥ kārya-avasthaḥ kāraṇa-avasthaś ca sthūla-sūkṣma-cid-acid-vastu-śarīraḥ parama-puruṣa eva iti, kāraṇāt kāryasya ananyatvena kāraṇa-vijñānena kāryasya jñātataya aika-vijñānena sarva-vijñānaṃ ca samīhitam upapannataram / "hanta aham imās tisro devatā anena jīvenā atmana ānupraviśya nāma-rūpe vyākaravāṇi" iti, "tisro devatāḥ" iti sarvam acid-vastu nirdiśya tatra sva-ātmaka-jīva-anupraveśena nāma-rūpa-vyākaraṇa-vacanāt sarve vācakāḥ śabdāḥ acij-jīva-viśiṣṭa-parama-ātmana eva vācakā iti kāraṇa-avastha-parama-ātma-vācinā śabdena kārya-vācinaḥ śabdasya sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ mukhya-vṛttam / ataḥ sthūla-sūkṣma-cid-acit-prakāraṃ brahma eva kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ ca iti brahma-upādānaṃ jagat / sūkṣma-cid-acid-vastu-śarīraṃ brahma eva kāraṇam iti jagato brahma-upādānatve
'pi saṃghātasya upādānatvena cid-acitor brahmaṇaś ca sva-bhāva-asaṅkaro 'py upapannataraḥ / yathā śukla-kṛṣṇa-rakta-tantu-saṃghāta-upādānatve 'pi citra-paṭasya tat-tat-tantu-pradeśa eva śauklya-ādi-saṃbandha iti kārya-avasthāyām api na sarvatra varṇa-saṅkaraḥ --- tathā cid-acid-īśvara-saṃghāta-upādānatve 'pi jagataḥ kārya-avasthāyām api bhoktṛtva-bhogyatva-niyantṛtva-ādy-asaṅkaraḥ / tantūnāṃ pṛthak-sthiti-yogyānām eva puruṣa-icchayā kadācit saṃhatānāṃ kāraṇatvaṃ kāryatvaṃ ca; iha tu cid-acitos sarva-avasthayoḥ parama-puruṣa-śarīratvena tat-prakārataya aiva pada-arthatvāt tat-prakāraḥ parama-puruṣa eva karāṇa kāryaṃ ca; sa eva sarvadā sarva-śabda-vācya iti viśeṣaḥ / sva-bhāva-bhedas tad-asaṅkaraś ca tatra ca atra ca tulyaḥ / evaṃ ca sati parasya brahmaṇaḥ kārya-anupraveśe 'pi
sva-rūpa-anyathā-bhāva-abhāvād avikṛtatvam upapannataram / sthūla-avasthasya nāma-rūpa-vibhāga-vibhaktasya cid-acid-vastunaḥ ātmataya āvasthānāt kāryatvam apy upapannam / avasthā-antara-āpattir eva hi kāryatā / nirguṇa-vādāś ca parasya brahmaṇo heya-guṇa-saṃbandha-abhāvād upapadyante / "apahata-pāpmā vijaro vimṛtyur viśoko vijighatso 'pipāsaḥ" iti heya-guṇān pratiṣidhya, "satya-kāmas satya-saṅkalpaḥ" iti kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇān vidadhati īyaṃ śrutir eva anyatra sāmānyena avagataṃ guṇa-niṣedhaṃ heya-guṇa-viṣayaṃ vyavasthāpayati / jñāna-sva-rūpa brahma iti vādaś ca sarva-jñasya sarva-śakter nikhila-heya-pratyanīka-kaylāṇa-guṇa-ākarasya brahmaṇaḥ sva-rūpaṃ jñāna-eka-nirūpaṇīyaṃ sva-prakāśatayā jñāna-sva-rūpaṃ ca ity abhyupagamād upapannataraḥ / "yas sarva-jñaḥ sarva-vit", "para āsya
śaktir vividha aiva śrūyate svābhāvikī jñāna-bala-kriyā ca, "vijñātāram are kena vijānīyāt" ity-ādikāḥ jñātṛtvam āvedayanti / "satyaṃ jñānam" ity-ādikāś ca jñāna-eka-nirūpaṇīyatayā sva-prakāśatayā ca jñāna-sva-rūpatām / "so 'kāmayata bahu syām", "tad aikṣata bahu syām", "tan nāma-rūpābhyām eva vyākriyata" iti brahma eva sva-saṅkalpād vicitra-sthira-trasa-rūpatayā nānā-prakāram avasthitam iti tat-pratyanīka-abrahma-ātmaka-vastu-nānātvam atattvam iti pratiṣidhyate, "mṛtyuḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāna īva paśyati ..... na iha nāna āsti kiñcana", "yatra hi dvaitam iva bhavati tad itara itaraṃ paśyati / yatra tv asya sarvam ātma aiva abhūt tat kena kaṃ paśyet" ity-ādinā / na punaḥ, "bahu syāṃ prajāyeya" ity-ādi-śruti-siddhaṃ sva-saṅkalpa-kṛtaṃ brahmaṇo nānā-nāma-rūpa-bhāktvena nānā-prakāratvam
api niṣidhyate / "yatra tv asya sarvam ātma aiva abhūt" iti niṣedha-vākya-ārambhe ca tat sthāpitam, "sarvaṃ taṃ parā-dād yo 'nyatarā atmanas sarvaṃ veda", "tasya etasya mahato bhūtasya niśśvasitam etad yad ṛg-vedaḥ" ity-ādinā /
evaṃ cid-acid-īśvarāṇāṃ sva-rūpa-bhedaṃ sva-bhāva-bhedaṃ ca vadantīnāṃ kārya-kāraṇa-bhāvaṃ kārya-kāraṇayor ananyatvaṃ vadantīnāṃ ca sarvāsāṃ śrutīnām avirodhaḥ, cid-acitoḥ parama-ātmanaś ca sarvadā śarīra-ātma-bhāvaṃ śarīra-bhūtayoḥ kāraṇa-daśāyāṃ nāma-rūpa-vibhāga-anarha-sūkṣma-daśā-āpattiṃ kārya-daśāyāṃ ca tad-arha-sthūla-daśa-āpattiṃ vadantībhiḥ śrutibhir eva jñāyata iti brahma-ajñāna-vādasya aupādhika-brahma-bheda-vādasya anyasya api apanyāya-mūlasya sakala-śruti-viruddhasya na kathaṃcid apy avakāśo dṛśyata ity alam ativistareṇa //
tat kṣetraṃ yac ca yādṛk ca yadvikāri yataś ca yat |
children.translated_text: That <s>kṣetra</s> — what it is, of what kind, what its modifications are, from what [cause] and what [it is] —

children.text: sa ca yo yatprabhāvaś ca tat samāsena me śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: and who he [the <s>kṣetrajña</s>] is and what his powers are — hear that from Me in brief. ||

children.text: tat kṣetraṃ yac ca yādṛk ca yad-vikāri yataś ca yat |
sa ca yo yat-prabhāvaś ca tat samāsena me śṛṇu ||

body.text: tat kṣetraṃ yac ca -- yad dravyam, yādṛk ca yeṣām āśrayabhūtam, yadvikāri ye cāsya vikārāḥ, yataś ca -- yato hetor idam utpannam; yasmai prayojanāyotpannam ityarthaḥ, yat -- yatsvarūpaṃ cedam, sa ca yaḥ -- sa ca kṣetrajño yaḥ yatsvarūpaḥ, yatprabhāvaś ca ye cāsya prabhāvāḥ, tat sarvam, samāsena saṃkṣepeṇa mattaḥ śṛṇu //
body.translated_text: 'That <s>kṣetra</s> — what it is' — what substance it is; 'of what kind' — of what entities it is the substratum; 'what its modifications are' — what its transformations are; 'from what' — from what cause it has arisen; meaning: for what purpose it has arisen; 'what' — what its essential nature is; 'and who he is' — and who the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is, what his essential nature is; 'and what his powers are' — and what his powers are — hear all that from Me in brief, in summary. //

children.text: tat kṣetraṃ yac ca --- yad dravyam, yādṛk ca yeṣām āśraya-bhūtam, yad-vikāri ye ca asya vikārāḥ, yataś ca --- yato hetor idam utpannam; yasmai prayojanāya utpannam ity-arthaḥ, yat --- yat-sva-rūpaṃ ca idam, sa ca yaḥ --- sa ca kṣetra-jño yaḥ yat-sva-rūpaḥ, yat-prabhāvaś ca ye ca asya prabhāvāḥ, tat sarvam, samāsena saṃkṣepeṇa mattaḥ śṛṇu //
ṛṣibhir bahudhā gītaṃ chandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛthak |
children.translated_text: It has been sung in many ways by the sages, separately in various <s>Vedic</s> metres,

children.text: brahmasūtrapadaiś caiva hetumadbhir viniścitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also by the well-reasoned and conclusive words of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>. ||

children.text: ṛṣibhir bahudhā gītaṃ chandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛthak |
brahma-sūtra-padaiś ca eva hetumadbhir viniścitaiḥ ||

body.text:
tad idaṃ kṣetrakṣetrajñayāthātmyam ṛṣibhiḥ parāśarādibhiḥ bahudhā bahuprakāraṃ gītam -- "ahaṃ tvam ca tathānye ca bhūtair uhyāma pārthiva / guṇapravāhapatito bhūtavargo 'pi yātyayam // karmavaśyā guṇā hy ete sattvādyāḥ pṛthivīpate / avidyāsañcitaṃ karma tac cāśeṣeṣu jantuṣu // ātmā śuddho 'kṣaraś śānto nirguṇaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ // BhGR_13."; tathā, "piṇḍaḥ pṛthak yataḥ puṃsaḥ śiraḥpāṇyādilakṣaṇaḥ / tato 'ham iti kutraitāṃ saṃjñāṃ rājan karomy aham"; tathā ca, "kiṃ tvam etacchiraḥ kiṃ nu urastava tathodaram / kim u pādādikaṃ tvaṃ vai tavaitat kiṃ mahīpate // samastāvayavebhyas tvaṃ pṛthak bhūya vyavasthitaḥ / ko 'ham ity eva nipuṇo bhūtvā cintaya pārthiva // BhGR_13." iti / evaṃ viviktayor dvayoḥ vāsudevātmakatvaṃ
cāhuḥ, "indriyāṇi mano buddhis sattvaṃ tejo balaṃ dhṛtiḥ / vāsudevātmakāny āhuḥ kṣetraṃ kṣetrajñam eva ca // BhGR_13." iti / chandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛthak -- pṛthagvidhaiś chandobhiś ca ṛgyajussāmātharvabhiḥ dehātmanoḥ svarūpaṃ pṛthag gītam -- "tasmād vā etasmād ātmana ākāśas saṃbhūtaḥ / ākāśād vāyuḥ / vāyor agniḥ / agner āpaḥ / adbhyaḥ pṛthivī / pṛthivyā oṣadhayaḥ / oṣadhībhyo 'nnam / annāt puruṣaḥ / sa vā eṣa puruṣo 'nnarasamayaḥ" iti śarīrasvarūpam abhidhāya tasmād antaraṃ prāṇamayaṃ tasmāc cāntaraṃ manomayam abhidhāya, "tasmād vā etasmād manomayād anyo 'ntara ātmā vijñānamayaḥ" iti kṣetrajñasvarūpam abhidhāya, "tasmād vā etasmād vijñānamayād anyo 'ntara ātmānandamayaḥ" iti kṣetrajñasyāpy
antarātmatayā ānanndamayaḥ paramātmābhihitaḥ / evam ṛksāmātharvasu ca tatra tatra kṣetrakṣetrajñayoḥ pṛthagbhāvas tayor brahmātmakatvaṃ ca suspaṣṭaṃ gītam / brahmasūtrapadaiś caiva -- brahmapratipādanasūtrākhyaiḥ padaiḥ śārīrakasūtraiḥ, hetumadbhiḥ heyayuktaiḥ, viniścitaiḥ nirṇayāntaiḥ; "na viyad aśruteḥ" ityārabhya kṣetraprakāranirṇaya uktaḥ / "nātmā śruter nityatvāc ca tābhyaḥ" ityārabhya kṣetrajñayāthātmyanirṇaya uktaḥ / "parāt tu tacchruteḥ" iti bhagavatpravartyatvena bhagavadātmakatvam uktam / evaṃ bahudhā gītaṃ kṣetrakṣetrajñayāthātmyaṃ mayā saṃkṣepeṇa suspaṣṭam ucyamānaṃ śṛṇv ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text:
This truth about the nature of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s> has been sung by sages such as <s>Parāśara</s> and others in many ways, in many modes — 'I and you and likewise others are carried along by the elements, O king; this stream of <s>guṇas</s> [sweeps along] the aggregation of beings too. These <s>guṇas</s> beginning with <s>sattva</s> are subject to <s>karma</s>, O lord of the earth; and <s>karma</s> accumulated through ignorance [operates] in all beings. The self is pure, imperishable, tranquil, devoid of <s>guṇas</s>, beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>.' Likewise, 'Since a person's body, characterized by head, hands, and the like, is separate [from the self], where then do I apply this designation "I," O king?' And likewise, 'Are you this head? Or is this your chest, or your belly? Are you these feet and the like? Or are these yours, O king? You are established as something distinct from all the limbs. Having become discerning, reflect thus: "Who am I?" O king.' Thus, having distinguished the two, they also declare their having <s>Vāsudeva</s> as their self: 'The senses, the mind, <s>buddhi</s>, <s>sattva</s>, radiance, strength, and firmness —
they declare as having <s>Vāsudeva</s> as their self — both the <s>kṣetra</s> and the <s>kṣetrajña</s>.' 'Separately in various <s>Vedic</s> metres' — by the different <s>Vedas</s> — <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Atharva</s> — the essential nature of body and self has been separately stated. Having stated the essential nature of the body as 'From that very self, space was born; from space, air; from air, fire; from fire, water; from water, earth; from earth, herbs; from herbs, food; from food, the person. That person indeed is made of the essence of food,' and having stated the sheath of <s>prāṇa</s> within that, and the sheath of mind within that, [the <s>śruti</s> then states]: 'Within that sheath of mind is another inner self, the sheath of knowledge (<s>vijñānamaya</s>)' — thus stating the essential nature of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>; [and then]: 'Within that sheath of knowledge is another inner self, the sheath of bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>)' — thus the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātmā</s>) as the blissful one is declared as the inner self even of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>.
Likewise, in the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Atharva Vedas</s> too, in various places, the separateness of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>, and their having <s>Brahman</s> as their self, have been very clearly stated. 'And also by the words of the <s>Brahmasūtras</s>' — by the aphorisms called <s>Brahma</s>-establishing <s>sūtras</s>, i.e., the <s>Śārīrakasūtras</s>; 'well-reasoned' — endowed with reasoning; 'conclusive' — ending in determinations. Beginning with 'Not space, because it is not taught [as created],' the determination of the nature of the <s>kṣetra</s> has been stated. Beginning with 'Not the self, because of <s>śruti</s>, and because of eternality, from those [sources],' the determination of the true nature of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> has been stated. By 'But from the Supreme, because of the teaching about that,' it is stated that [the <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>] have the Lord as their self, being directed by the Lord. Thus, the truth about the nature of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s>, sung in many ways, is now being stated by Me concisely and very clearly — listen — this is the meaning. //

children.text:
tad idaṃ kṣetra-kṣetra-jña-yāthātmyam ṛṣibhiḥ parāśara-ādibhiḥ bahudhā bahu-prakāraṃ gītam --- "ahaṃ tvam ca tatha ānye ca bhūtair uhyāma pārthiva / guṇa-pravāha-patito bhūta-vargo 'pi ya ātyayam // karma-vaśyā guṇā hy ete sattva-ādyāḥ pṛthivī-pate / avidyā-sañcitaṃ karma tac ca aśeṣeṣu jantuṣu // ātmā śuddho 'kṣaraś śānto nirguṇaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ // BhGR_13."; tathā, "piṇḍaḥ pṛthak yataḥ puṃsaḥ śiraḥ-pāṇy-ādi-lakṣaṇaḥ / tato 'ham iti kutra etāṃ saṃjñāṃ rājan karomy aham"; tathā ca, "kiṃ tvam etac-chiraḥ kiṃ nu urastava tatha ūdaram / kim u pāda-ādikaṃ tvaṃ vai tava etat kiṃ mahī-pate // samasta-avayavebhyas tvaṃ pṛthak bhūya vyavasthitaḥ / ko 'ham ity eva nipuṇo bhūtvā cintaya pārthiva // BhGR_13." iti / evaṃ viviktayor dvayoḥ vāsu-deva-ātmakatvaṃ
cā ahuḥ, "indriyāṇi mano buddhis sattvaṃ tejo balaṃ dhṛtiḥ / vāsudeva-ātmakāny āhuḥ kṣetraṃ kṣetra-jñam eva ca // BhGR_13." iti / chandobhir vividhaiḥ pṛthak --- pṛthag-vidhaiś chandobhiś ca ṛg-yajus-sāma-atharvabhiḥ deha-ātmanoḥ sva-rūpaṃ pṛthag gītam --- "tasmād vā etasmād ātmana ākāśas saṃbhūtaḥ / ākāśād vāyuḥ / vāyor agniḥ / agner āpaḥ / adbhyaḥ pṛthivī / pṛthivyā oṣadhayaḥ / oṣadhībhyo 'nnam / annāt puruṣaḥ / sa vā eṣa puruṣo 'nna-rasa-mayaḥ" iti śarīra-sva-rūpam abhidhāya tasmād antaraṃ prāṇa-mayaṃ tasmāc ca antaraṃ mano-mayam abhidhāya, "tasmād vā etasmād mano-mayād anyo 'ntara ātmā vijñāna-mayaḥ" iti kṣetra-jña-sva-rūpam abhidhāya, "tasmād vā etasmād vijñāna-mayād anyo 'ntara ātmā ānanda-mayaḥ" iti kṣetra-jñasya apy
antara-ātmatayā ānannda-mayaḥ parama-ātma ābhihitaḥ / evam ṛk-sāma-atharvasu ca tatra tatra kṣetra-kṣetra-jñayoḥ pṛthag-bhāvas tayor brahma-ātmakatvaṃ ca suspaṣṭaṃ gītam / brahma-sūtra-padaiś ca eva --- brahma-pratipādana-sūtra-ākhyaiḥ padaiḥ śārīraka-sūtraiḥ, hetumadbhiḥ heya-yuktaiḥ, viniścitaiḥ nirṇaya-antaiḥ; "na viyad aśruteḥ" ity-ārabhya kṣetra-prakāra-nirṇaya uktaḥ / "nā atmā śruter nityatvāc ca tābhyaḥ" ity-ārabhya kṣetra-jña-yāthātmya-nirṇaya uktaḥ / "parāt tu tac-chruteḥ" iti bhagavat-pravartyatvena bhagavad-ātmakatvam uktam / evaṃ bahudhā gītaṃ kṣetra-kṣetra-jña-yāthātmyaṃ mayā saṃkṣepeṇa suspaṣṭam ucyamānaṃ śṛṇv ity-arthaḥ //
mahābhūtāny ahaṅkāro buddhir avyaktam eva ca |
children.translated_text: The great elements, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), and the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) too,

children.text: indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca pañca cendriyagocarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ten senses and the one [mind], and the five objects of the senses —

children.text: mahā-bhūtāny ahaṅkāro buddhir avyaktam eva ca |
indriyāṇi daśa ekaṃ ca pañca ca indriya-gocarāḥ ||
icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃghātaś cetanādhṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: desire, aversion, happiness, sorrow, the bodily aggregate, consciousness, and steadfastness —

children.text: etat kṣetraṃ samāsena savikāram udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: this is the <s>kṣetra</s>, briefly described with its modifications. ||

children.text: icchā dveṣaḥ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃghātaś cetana-ādhṛtiḥ |
etat kṣetraṃ samāsena savikāram udāhṛtam ||

body.text:
mahābhūtāny ahaṃkāro buddhir avyaktam eva ceti kṣetrārambhakadravyāṇi; pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśāḥ mahābhūtāni, ahaṃkāro bhūtādiḥ, buddhiḥ mahān, avyaktaṃ prakṛtiḥ; indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca pañca cendriyagocarā iti kṣetrāśritāni tattvāni; śrotratvakcakṣurjihvāghrāṇāni pañca jñānendriyāṇi, vākpāṇipādapāyūpasthāni pañca karmendriyāṇīti tāni daśa, ekam iti manaḥ; indriyagocarāś ca pañca śabdasparśarūparasagandhāḥ; icchā dveṣas sukhaṃ duḥkham iti kṣetrakāryāṇi kṣetravikārā ucyante; yady apīcchādveṣasukhaduḥkhāny ātmadharmabhūtāni, tathāpy ātmanaḥ kṣetrasaṃbandhaprayuktānīti kṣetrakāryatayā kṣetravikārā ucyante / teṣāṃ puruṣadharmatvam, "puruṣas sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve hetur ucyate"
iti vakṣyate; saṃghātaś cetanādhṛtiḥ / ādhṛtiḥ ādhāraḥ sukhaduḥkhe bhuñjānasya bhogāpavargau sādhayataś ca cetanasyādhāratayotpanno bhūtasaṃghātaḥ / prakṛtyādipṛthivyantadravyārabdham indriyāśrayabhūtam icchādveṣasukhaduḥkhavikāri bhūtasaṃghātarūpaṃ cetanasukhaduḥkhopabhogādhāratvaprayojanaṃ kṣetram ity uktaṃ bhavati; etat kṣetraṃ samāsena saṃkṣepeṇa sakivāraṃ sakāryam udāhṛtam //
body.translated_text:
'The great elements, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, <s>buddhi</s>, and the unmanifest too' — these are the substances that constitute the <s>kṣetra</s>: earth, water, fire, air, and space are the great elements; <s>ahaṅkāra</s> is <s>bhūtādi</s> (the origin of elements); <s>buddhi</s> is <s>mahat</s> (the great principle); the unmanifest is <s>Prakṛti</s>. 'The ten senses and the one, and the five objects of the senses' — these are the principles residing in the <s>kṣetra</s>: hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell — the five organs of knowledge; speech, hands, feet, the organ of excretion, and the organ of generation — the five organs of action — these are the ten. 'The one' is the mind. The five objects of the senses are sound, touch, form, taste, and smell. 'Desire, aversion, happiness, sorrow' — these are called the effects of the <s>kṣetra</s>, the modifications of the <s>kṣetra</s>. Although desire, aversion, happiness, and sorrow are properties of the self, nevertheless, since they arise from the self's connection with the <s>kṣetra</s>, they are called modifications of the <s>kṣetra</s> as its effects. That they are properties of the <s>puruṣa</s> will be stated:
'The <s>puruṣa</s> is said to be the cause of the experience of happiness and sorrow.' 'The aggregate, consciousness, and steadfastness' — steadfastness (<s>ādhṛti</s>) means support; the aggregate of elements produced as the support of the conscious being who experiences happiness and sorrow and strives for enjoyment and liberation. Thus it is stated that the <s>kṣetra</s> is the aggregate of elements — constituted of substances from <s>Prakṛti</s> down to earth, serving as the substratum of the senses, undergoing modifications such as desire, aversion, happiness, and sorrow — whose purpose is to serve as the support for the conscious being's experience of happiness and sorrow. 'This is the <s>kṣetra</s>, briefly described' — in summary, with its modifications, with its effects, it has been described. //

children.text:
mahā-bhūtāny ahaṃkāro buddhir avyaktam eva ca iti kṣetra-ārambhaka-dravyāṇi; pṛthivy-ap-tejo-vāyv-ākāśāḥ mahā-bhūtāni, ahaṃkāro bhūta-ādiḥ, buddhiḥ mahān, avyaktaṃ prakṛtiḥ; indriyāṇi daśa ekaṃ ca pañca ca indriya-gocarā iti kṣetra-āśritāni tattvāni; śrotra-tvak-cakṣur-jihvā-ghrāṇāni pañca jñāna-indriyāṇi, vāk-pāṇi-pāda-pāyu-upasthāni pañca karma-indriyāṇi iti tāni daśa, ekam iti manaḥ; indriya-gocarāś ca pañca śabda-sparśa-rūpa-rasa-gandhāḥ; icchā dveṣas sukhaṃ duḥkham iti kṣetra-kāryāṇi kṣetra-vikārā ucyante; yady api icchā-dveṣa-sukha-duḥkhāny ātma-dharma-bhūtāni, tatha āpy ātmanaḥ kṣetra-saṃbandha-prayuktāni iti kṣetra-kāryatayā kṣetra-vikārā ucyante / teṣāṃ puruṣa-dharmatvam, "puruṣas sukha-duḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve hetur ucyate"
iti vakṣyate; saṃghātaś cetana-ādhṛtiḥ / ādhṛtiḥ ādhāraḥ sukha-duḥkhe bhuñjānasya bhoga-apavargau sādhayataś ca cetanasyā adhārataya ūtpanno bhūta-saṃghātaḥ / prakṛty-ādi-pṛthivy-anta-dravya-ārabdham indriya-āśraya-bhūtam icchā-dveṣa-sukha-duḥkha-vikāri bhūta-saṃghāta-rūpaṃ cetana-sukha-duḥkha-upabhoga-ādhāratva-prayojanaṃ kṣetram ity uktaṃ bhavati; etat kṣetraṃ samāsena saṃkṣepeṇa sakivāraṃ sakāryam udāhṛtam //

body.text: atha kṣetrakāryeṣv ātmajñānasādhanatayopādeyā guṇāḥ procyante --
body.translated_text: Now the qualities that are to be adopted as means to self-knowledge, among the effects of the <s>kṣetra</s>, are stated:

children.text: atha kṣetra-kāryeṣv ātma-jñāna-sādhanataya ūpādeyā guṇāḥ procyante ---
amānitvam adambhitvam ahiṃsā kṣāntir ārjavam |
children.translated_text: Absence of pride, absence of ostentation, non-violence, forbearance, uprightness,

children.text: ācāryopāsanaṃ śaucaṃ sthairyam ātmavinigrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: service to the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-restraint, ||

children.text: amānitvam adambhitvam ahiṃsā kṣāntir ārjavam |
ācārya-upāsanaṃ śaucaṃ sthairyam ātma-vinigrahaḥ ||

body.text: amānitvam utkṛṣṭajaneṣv avadhīraṇārahitatvam; adambhitvam -- dhārmikatvayaśaḥprayojanatayā dharmānuṣṭhānaṃ dambhaḥ, tadrahitatvam; ahiṃsā vāṅmanaḥkāyaiḥ parapīḍārahitatvam; kṣāntiḥ paraiḥ pīḍyamānasyāpi tān prati avikṛtacittatvam / ārjavam parān prati vāṅmanaḥkāyaprabhṛtīnām ekarūpatā; ācāryopāsanam ātmajñānapradāyini ācārye praṇipātaparipraśnasevādiniratatvam; śaucaṃ ātmajñānatatsādhanayogyatā manovākkāyagatā śāstrasiddhā; stairyam adhyātmaśāstrodite 'rthe niścalatvam; ātmavinigrahaḥ ātmasvarūpavyatiriktaviṣayebhyo manaso nivartanam //
body.translated_text: Absence of pride (<s>amānitva</s>) is being free from contempt toward distinguished persons. Absence of ostentation (<s>adambhitva</s>) — ostentation (<s>dambha</s>) is the performance of <s>dharma</s> for the purpose of gaining a reputation for being righteous; freedom from that. Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is being free from causing suffering to others through speech, mind, and body. Forbearance (<s>kṣānti</s>) is having an undisturbed mind even toward those who cause suffering. Uprightness (<s>ārjava</s>) is the uniformity of speech, mind, body, and the like toward others. Service to the teacher (<s>ācāryopāsana</s>) is being devoted to prostration, questioning, and attendance upon the teacher who imparts self-knowledge. Purity (<s>śauca</s>) is the fitness of mind, speech, and body for self-knowledge and its means, as established by scripture. Steadfastness (<s>sthairya</s>) is being unwavering in the truths taught in the scripture on the self. Self-restraint (<s>ātmavinigraha</s>) is the withdrawal of the mind from objects other than the essential nature of the self. //

children.text: amānitvam utkṛṣṭa-janeṣv avadhīraṇa-arahitatvam; adambhitvam --- dhārmikatva-yaśaḥ-prayojanatayā dharma-anuṣṭhānaṃ dambhaḥ, tad-rahitatvam; ahiṃsā vāṅ-manaḥ-kāyaiḥ para-pīḍa-arahitatvam; kṣāntiḥ paraiḥ pīḍyamānasya api tān prati avikṛta-cittatvam / ārjavam parān prati vāṅ-manaḥ-kāya-prabhṛtīnām eka-rūpatā; ācārya-upāsanam ātma-jñāna-pradāyini ācārye praṇipāta-paripraśna-sevā-ādi-niratatvam; śaucaṃ ātma-jñāna-tat-sādhana-yogyatā mano-vāk-kāya-gatā śāstra-siddhā; stairyam adhyātma-śāstra-udite 'rthe niścalatvam; ātma-vinigrahaḥ ātma-sva-rūpa-vyatirikta-viṣayebhyo manaso nivartanam //
indriyārtheṣu vairāgyam anahaṅkāra eva ca |
children.translated_text: Dispassion toward sense-objects, and freedom from egoism,

children.text: janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanam ||
children.translated_text: perception of the defect of suffering in birth, death, old age, and disease. ||

children.text: indriya-artheṣu vairāgyam anahaṅkāra eva ca |
janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣa-anudarśanam ||

body.text: indriyārtheṣu vairāgyam ātmavyatirikteṣu viṣayeṣu sadoṣatānusaṃdhānenodvejanam; anahaṃkāraḥ anātmani dehe ātmābhimānarahitatvam; pradarśanārtham idam; anātmīyeṣv ātmīyābhimānarahitatvaṃ ca vivakṣitam / janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhadoṣānudarśanam saśarīratve janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkharūpasya doṣasyāvarjanīyatvānusaṃdhānam //
body.translated_text: Dispassion toward sense-objects (<s>vairāgya</s>) is the aversion arising from contemplation of the defectiveness of objects other than the self. Freedom from egoism (<s>anahaṅkāra</s>) is being free from the false identification of the self with the non-self body. This is stated as an example; freedom from the false sense of 'mine' regarding what does not belong to the self is also intended. Perception of the defect of suffering in birth, death, old age, and disease is the contemplation of the unavoidable nature of the defect consisting of the suffering of birth, death, old age, and disease when embodied. //

children.text: indriya-artheṣu vairāgyam ātma-vyatirikteṣu viṣayeṣu sadoṣatā-anusaṃdhānena udvejanam; anahaṃkāraḥ anātmani dehe ātma-abhimāna-rahitatvam; pradarśana-artham idam; anātmīyeṣv ātmīya-abhimāna-rahitatvaṃ ca vivakṣitam / janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-doṣa-anudarśanam saśarīratve janma-mṛtyu-jarā-vyādhi-duḥkha-rūpasya doṣasya avarjanīyatva-anusaṃdhānam //
asaktir anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu |
children.translated_text: Non-attachment, absence of excessive affection for son, wife, home, and the like,

children.text: nityaṃ ca samacittatvam iṣṭāniṣṭopapattiṣu ||
children.translated_text: and constant equanimity of mind in the occurrence of the desirable and the undesirable. ||

children.text: asaktir anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putra-dāra-gṛha-ādiṣu |
nityaṃ ca sama-cittatvam iṣṭa-aniṣṭa-upapattiṣu ||

body.text: asaktiḥ ātmavyatiriktaparigraheṣu saṅgarahitatvam; anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putradāragṛhādiṣu teṣu śāstrīyakarmopakaraṇatvātirekeṇa śleṣarahitatvam; saṃkalpaprabhaveṣv iṣṭāniṣṭopanipāteṣu harṣodvegarahitatvam //
body.translated_text: Non-attachment (<s>asakti</s>) is being free from clinging to possessions other than the self. Absence of excessive affection (<s>anabhiṣvaṅga</s>) toward son, wife, home, and the like is being free from attachment to them beyond their utility as instruments for scripturally enjoined duties. Equanimity is freedom from elation and distress in the occurrences of the desirable and undesirable that arise from <s>saṅkalpa</s> (volition). //

children.text: asaktiḥ ātma-vyatirikta-parigraheṣu saṅga-rahitatvam; anabhiṣvaṅgaḥ putra-dāra-gṛha-ādiṣu teṣu śāstrīya-karma-upakaraṇatva-atirekeṇa śleṣa-rahitatvam; saṃkalpa-prabhaveṣv iṣṭa-aniṣṭa-upanipāteṣu harṣa-udvega-rahitatvam //
mayi cānanyayogena bhaktir avyabhicāriṇī |
children.translated_text: And unswerving devotion to Me through exclusive <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: viviktadeśasevitvam aratir janasaṃsadi ||
children.translated_text: resorting to secluded places, and finding no delight in the company of people. ||

children.text: mayi ca ananya-yogena bhaktir avyabhicāriṇī |
vivikta-deśa-sevitvam aratir jana-saṃsadi ||

body.text: mayi sarveśvare ca aikāntyayogena sthirā bhaktiḥ, janavarjitadeśavāsitvam, janasaṃsadi cāprītiḥ //
body.translated_text: And toward Me, the Lord of all, steadfast devotion through exclusive <s>yoga</s>; dwelling in places free from people; and finding no pleasure in the company of people. //
