children.text: mayi sarva-īśvare ca aikāntya-yogena sthirā bhaktiḥ, jana-varjita-deśa-vāsitvam, jana-saṃsadi ca aprītiḥ //
adhyātmajñānanityatvaṃ tattvajñānārthacintanam |
children.translated_text: Constant devotion to knowledge of the self, and contemplation of the purpose of knowledge of the truth —

children.text: etaj jñānam iti proktam ajñānaṃ yad ato 'nyathā ||
children.translated_text: this is declared to be knowledge; what is contrary to this is ignorance. ||

children.text: adhyātma-jñāna-nityatvaṃ tattva-jñāna-artha-cintanam |
etaj jñānam iti proktam ajñānaṃ yad ato 'nyathā ||

body.text: ātmani jñānam adhyātmajñānam tanniṣṭhatvam, tattvajñānārthacintanam tattvajñānaprayojanaṃ yac cintanaṃ tan niratatvam ityarthaḥ / jñāyate 'nenātmeti jñānam, ātmajñānasādhanam ityarthaḥ; kṣetrasaṃbandhinaḥ puruṣasyāmānitvādikam uktaṃ guṇabṛnham evātmajñānopayogi, etadvyatiriktaṃ sarvaṃ kṣetrakāryam ātmajñānavirodhīti ajñānam //
body.translated_text: Knowledge of the self is <s>adhyātmajñāna</s>; constant devotion to that is being established in it. Contemplation of the purpose of knowledge of the truth — being devoted to that contemplation whose purpose is the knowledge of the truth — this is the meaning. 'Knowledge' (<s>jñāna</s>) means 'that by which the self is known' — i.e., the means to self-knowledge. The qualities beginning with absence of pride, stated in connection with the person associated with the <s>kṣetra</s>, are a development of [these] qualities that are conducive to self-knowledge alone. Everything other than this, all effects of the <s>kṣetra</s>, is opposed to self-knowledge and is therefore ignorance. //

children.text: ātmani jñānam adhyātma-jñānam tan-niṣṭhatvam, tattva-jñāna-artha-cintanam tattva-jñāna-prayojanaṃ yac cintanaṃ tan niratatvam ity-arthaḥ / jñāyate 'nenā atma īti jñānam, ātma-jñāna-sādhanam ity-arthaḥ; kṣetra-saṃbandhinaḥ puruṣasya amānitva-ādikam uktaṃ guṇa-bṛnham evā atma-jñāna-upayogi, etad-vyatiriktaṃ sarvaṃ kṣetra-kāryam ātma-jñāna-virodhi iti ajñānam //

body.text: atha etad yo vettīti veditṛtvalakṣaṇenoktasya kṣetrajñasya svarūpaṃ viśodhyate --
body.translated_text: Now the essential nature of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, who was described by the characteristic of being a knower — 'he who knows this' — is purified [i.e., elucidated]:

children.text: atha etad yo vetti iti veditṛtva-lakṣaṇena uktasya kṣetra-jñasya sva-rūpaṃ viśodhyate ---
jñeyaṃ yat tat pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātvāmṛtam aśnute |
children.translated_text: I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality —

children.text: anādi matparaṃ brahma na sat tan nāsad ucyate ||
children.translated_text: beginningless, having Me as the supreme, it is <s>Brahman</s>; it is called neither being nor non-being. ||

children.text: jñeyaṃ yat tat pravakṣyāmi yaj jñātva āmṛtam aśnute |
anādi mat-paraṃ brahma na sat tan na asad ucyate ||

body.text:
amānitvādibhiḥ sādhanaiḥ jñeyaṃ prāpyaṃ yat pratyagātmasvarūpaṃ tat pravakṣyāmi, yaj jñātvā janmajarāmaraṇādiprākṛtadharmarahitam amṛtam ātmānaṃ prāpnoti; ādir yasya na vidyate, tad anādi; asya hi pratyagātmana utpattir na vidyate; tata evānto na vidyate / śrutiś ca, "na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit" iti, matparam ahaṃ paro yasya tan matparam / "itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām, jīvabhūtām" iti hy uktam / bhagavaccharīratayā bhagavaccheṣataikarasaṃ hy ātmasvarūpam; tathā ca śrutiḥ, "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam atmā na veda yasyātmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati" iti, tathā, "sa kāraṇaṃ karaṇādhipādhipo na cāsya kaściñ janitā na cādhipaḥ", "pradhānakṣetrajñapatir guṇeśaḥ" ityādikā / brahma bṛhattvaguṇayogi, śarīrāder arthāntarabhūtam,
svataḥ śarīrādibhiḥ paricchedarahitaṃ kṣetrajñatattvam ityarthaḥ; "sa cānantyāya kalpate" iti hi śrūyate; śarīraparicchinnatvam aṇutvaṃ cāsya karmakṛtam / karmabandhān muktasyānantyam / ātmany api brahmaśabdaḥ prayujyate, "sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate / brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham amṛtasyāvyayasya ca", "brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati / samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām // BhGR_13." iti / na sat tan nāsad ucyate kāryakāraṇarūpāvasthādvayarahitatayā sadasacchabdābhyām ātmasavarūpaṃ nocyate / kāryāvasthāyāṃ hi devādināmarūpabhāktvena sad ity ucyate, tadanarhatā kāraṇāvasthāyām asad ity ucyate / tathā ca śrutiḥ, "asad vā idam agra āsīt / tato vai sad ajāyata","tad dhedaṃ tarhy avyākṛtam āsīt tannāmarūpābhyāṃ
vyākriyata" ityādikā / kāryakāraṇāvasthādvayānvayas tv ātmanaḥ karmarūpāvidyāveṣṭanakṛtaḥ, na svarūpakṛta iti sadasacchabdābhyām ātmasvarūpaṃ nocyate / yady api "asad vā idam agra āsīt" iti kāraṇāvasthaṃ paraṃ brahmocyate, tathāpi nāmarūpavibhāgānarhasūkṣmacidacidvastuśarīraṃ paraṃ brahma kāraṇāvastham iti kāraṇāvasthāyāṃ kṣetrakṣetrajñasvarūpam api asacchabdavācyam, kṣetrajñasya sāvasthā karmakṛteti pariśuddhasvarūpaṃ na sadasacchabdanirdeśyam //
body.translated_text:
That which is to be known — to be attained — through the means beginning with absence of pride, the essential nature of the inner self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) — I shall declare that, knowing which one attains the self as immortal — free from the material properties of birth, old age, death, and the like. That whose beginning is not known is 'beginningless'; for this inner self has no origination; and therefore no end either. And the <s>śruti</s> states: 'The wise one is neither born nor dies.' 'Having Me as the supreme' — I am the supreme of whom, that is 'having Me as the supreme.' For it has been stated: 'Know My other, higher <s>Prakṛti</s>, which has become the living beings.' For the essential nature of the self is constituted solely of being the subordinate (<s>śeṣa</s>) of the Lord, having the Lord as its body. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'He who dwells in the self, who is interior to the self, whom the self does not know, whose body the self is, who controls the self from within.' Likewise, 'He is the cause, the lord of the lords of the senses, and He has no progenitor and no lord'; 'The lord of <s>Prakṛti</s> and the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, the ruler of the <s>guṇas</s>' — and such [texts]. '<s>Brahman</s>' — possessing the quality of greatness (<s>bṛhattva</s>), being a distinct entity from the body and the like,
by its own nature devoid of the limitation imposed by the body and the like — [this is] the reality of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, this is the meaning. For it is heard: 'He is fit for infinitude.' The limitation to atomic size and its embodied state are brought about by <s>karma</s>. When freed from the bondage of <s>karma</s>, [the self attains] infinitude. The word <s>Brahman</s> is used with reference to the self too: 'Having transcended these <s>guṇas</s>, he is fit for becoming <s>Brahman</s>. For I am the foundation of <s>Brahman</s>, of the immortal and the imperishable'; 'Having become <s>Brahman</s>, with a serene self, he neither grieves nor desires; being equal toward all beings, he attains supreme devotion to Me.' 'It is called neither being nor non-being' — the essential nature of the self is not denoted by the words 'being' (<s>sat</s>) or 'non-being' (<s>asat</s>), because it is devoid of both states — the effect-state and the cause-state. For in the effect-state, it is called 'being' (<s>sat</s>) because of partaking of names and forms such as gods and the like; in the cause-state, it is called 'non-being' (<s>asat</s>) because it is not fit for that. And thus the <s>śruti</s>: 'This was indeed non-being (<s>asat</s>) in the beginning; from that, being (<s>sat</s>) was born'; 'That was then undifferentiated; it became differentiated by name and form' — and such [texts]. But the self's connection with both the effect-state and the cause-state is brought about by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) in the form of <s>karma</s>, and is not due to its own essential nature — therefore the essential nature of the self is not denoted by the words 'being' and 'non-being.' Although in 'This was indeed non-being in the beginning,' the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> in the cause-state is spoken of, nevertheless, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> in the cause-state has as its body the subtle conscious and non-conscious entities that are not fit for differentiation of name and form — and thus in the cause-state, the essential nature of the <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>kṣetrajña</s> too is denoted by the word 'non-being.' But that state of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is brought about by <s>karma</s>, and therefore the purified essential nature [of the self] is not to be denoted by the words 'being' and 'non-being.' //

children.text:
amānitva-ādibhiḥ sādhanaiḥ jñeyaṃ prāpyaṃ yat pratyag-ātma-sva-rūpaṃ tat pravakṣyāmi, yaj jñātvā janma-jarā-maraṇa-ādi-prākṛta-dharma-rahitam amṛtam ātmānaṃ prāpnoti; ādir yasya na vidyate, tad anādi; asya hi pratyag-ātmana utpattir na vidyate; tata eva anto na vidyate / śrutiś ca, "na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścit" iti, mat-param ahaṃ paro yasya tan mat-param / "itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām, jīva-bhūtām" iti hy uktam / bhagavac-charīratayā bhagavac-cheṣatā-eka-rasaṃ hy ātma-sva-rūpam; tathā ca śrutiḥ, "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam atmā na veda yasyā atmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati" iti, tathā, "sa kāraṇaṃ karaṇa-adhipa-adhipo na ca asya kaściñ janitā na ca adhipaḥ", "pradhāna-kṣetra-jña-patir guṇa-īśaḥ" ity-ādikā / brahma bṛhattva-guṇa-yogi, śarīra-āder artha-antara-bhūtam,
svataḥ śarīra-ādibhiḥ pariccheda-rahitaṃ kṣetra-jña-tattvam ity-arthaḥ; "sa ca anantyāya kalpate" iti hi śrūyate; śarīra-paricchinnatvam aṇutvaṃ ca asya karma-kṛtam / karma-bandhān muktasya anantyam / ātmany api brahma-śabdaḥ prayujyate, "sa guṇān samatītya etān brahma-bhūyāya kalpate / brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭha āham amṛtasya avyayasya ca", "brahma-bhūtaḥ prasanna-ātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati / samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu mad-bhaktiṃ labhate parām // BhGR_13." iti / na sat tan na asad ucyate kārya-kāraṇa-rūpa-avasthā-dvaya-rahitatayā sad-asac-chabdābhyām ātma-sava-rūpaṃ na ucyate / kārya-avasthāyāṃ hi deva-ādi-nāma-rūpa-bhāktvena sad ity ucyate, tad-anarhatā kāraṇa-avasthāyām asad ity ucyate / tathā ca śrutiḥ, "asad vā idam agra āsīt / tato vai sad ajāyata","tad dha idaṃ tarhy avyākṛtam āsīt tan-nāma-rūpābhyāṃ
vyākriyata" ity-ādikā / kārya-kāraṇa-avasthā-dvaya-anvayas tv ātmanaḥ karma-rūpa-avidyā-veṣṭana-kṛtaḥ, na sva-rūpa-kṛta iti sad-asac-chabdābhyām ātma-sva-rūpaṃ na ucyate / yady api "asad vā idam agra āsīt" iti kāraṇa-avasthaṃ paraṃ brahma ucyate, tatha āpi nāma-rūpa-vibhāga-anarha-sūkṣma-cid-acid-vastu-śarīraṃ paraṃ brahma kāraṇa-avastham iti kāraṇa-avasthāyāṃ kṣetra-kṣetra-jña-sva-rūpam api asac-chabda-vācyam, kṣetra-jñasya sa āvasthā karma-kṛta īti pariśuddha-sva-rūpaṃ na sad-asac-chabda-nirdeśyam //
sarvataḥpāṇipādaṃ tat sarvato'kṣiśiromukham |
children.translated_text: With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, |

children.text: sarvataśśrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: having ears everywhere, it abides in the world, enveloping all. ||

children.text: sarvataḥ-pāṇi-pādaṃ tat sarvato-'kṣi-śiro-mukham |
sarvataś-śrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati ||

body.text: sarvataḥ pāṇipādaṃ tat pariśuddhātmasvarūpaṃ sarvataḥ pāṇipādakāryaśaktam, tathā sarvato 'kṣiśiromukhaṃ sarvataś śrutimat sarvataś cakṣurādikāryakṛt, "apāṇipādo javano grahītā paśyaty acakṣuḥ sa śṛṇoty akarṇaḥ" iti parasya brahmaṇo 'pāṇipādasyāpi sarvataḥ pāṇipādādikāryakṛttvaṃ śrūyate / pratyagātmano 'pi pariśuddhasya tatsāmyāpattyā sarvataḥ pāṇipādādikāryakṛttvaṃ śrutisiddham eva / "tadā vidvān puṇyapāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyam upaiti" iti hi śrūyate / "idaṃ jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ" iti ca vakṣyate / loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati loke yad vastujātaṃ tat sarvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhati, pariśuddhasvarūpaṃ deśādiparicchedarahitatayā sarvagatam ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: That which has hands and feet everywhere — that purified self-nature (<s>pariśuddhātmasvarūpa</s>) has the capacity to perform the functions of hands and feet everywhere; likewise, having eyes, heads, and faces everywhere, having ears everywhere — it performs the functions of eyes and the like everywhere. [As the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'Without hands and feet, He is swift and a grasper; He sees without eyes, He hears without ears' — thus it is heard that the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, even without hands and feet, performs the functions of hands, feet, and the like everywhere. For the individual self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) too, in its purified state, the capacity to perform the functions of hands, feet, and the like everywhere is established in <s>śruti</s> itself, through [its] attaining equality with That. For it is heard: 'Then the wise one, having shaken off merit and demerit, free from stain, attains supreme equality.' And it will be stated [later]: 'Having resorted to this knowledge, they have attained to My nature (<s>sādharmya</s>).' It abides in the world enveloping all — whatever class of entities exists in the world, it abides pervading all of them; the meaning is that the purified self-nature, being free from limitation by place and the like, is all-pervading. //

children.text: sarvataḥ pāṇi-pādaṃ tat pariśuddha-ātma-sva-rūpaṃ sarvataḥ pāṇi-pāda-kārya-śaktam, tathā sarvato 'kṣi-śiro-mukhaṃ sarvataś śrutimat sarvataś cakṣur-ādi-kārya-kṛt, "apāṇi-pādo javano grahītā paśyaty acakṣuḥ sa śṛṇoty akarṇaḥ" iti parasya brahmaṇo 'pāṇi-pādasya api sarvataḥ pāṇi-pāda-ādi-kārya-kṛttvaṃ śrūyate / pratyag-ātmano 'pi pariśuddhasya tat-sāmya-āpattyā sarvataḥ pāṇi-pāda-ādi-kārya-kṛttvaṃ śruti-siddham eva / "tadā vidvān puṇya-pāpe vidhūya nirañjanaḥ paramaṃ sāmyam upaiti" iti hi śrūyate / "idaṃ jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ" iti ca vakṣyate / loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati loke yad vastu-jātaṃ tat sarvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhati, pariśuddha-sva-rūpaṃ deśa-ādi-pariccheda-rahitatayā sarva-gatam ity-arthaḥ //
sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitam |
children.translated_text: Appearing to have the qualities of all the senses, yet devoid of all the senses;

children.text: asaktaṃ sarvabhṛc caiva nirguṇaṃ guṇabhoktṛ ca ||
children.translated_text: unattached, yet sustaining all; free from the <s>guṇas</s>, yet the experiencer of the <s>guṇas</s>. ||

children.text: sarva-indriya-guṇa-ābhāsaṃ sarva-indriya-vivarjitam |
asaktaṃ sarva-bhṛc ca eva nirguṇaṃ guṇa-bhoktṛ ca ||

body.text: sarvendriyaguṇābhāsam sarvendriyaguṇair ābhāso yasya tat sarvendriyābhāsam / indriyaguṇā indriyavṛttayaḥ / indriyavṛttibhir api viṣayān jñatuṃ samartham ityarthaḥ / svabhāvatas sarvendriyavivarjitam vinaivendriyavṛttibhiḥ svata eva sarvaṃ jānātītyarthaḥ / asaktam svabhāvato devādidehasaṅgarahitam, sarvabhṛc caiva devādisarvadehabharaṇasamarthaṃ ca; "sa ekadhā bhavati tridhā bhavati" ityādiśruteḥ / nirguṇam tathā svabhāvatas sattvādiguṇarahitam / guṇabhoktṛ ca sattvādīnāṃ guṇānāṃ bhogasamarthaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: Appearing to have the qualities of all the senses (<s>sarvendriyaguṇābhāsam</s>) — that which has the appearance (<s>ābhāsa</s>) of the qualities of all the senses, i.e., the activities of the senses. By means of the activities of the senses too, it is capable of knowing objects — this is the meaning. By nature devoid of all the senses (<s>sarvendriyavivarjitam</s>) — even without the activities of the senses, it knows everything by itself — this is the meaning. Unattached (<s>asakta</s>) — by nature free from connection with bodies such as those of gods and the like; yet sustaining all (<s>sarvabhṛt</s>) — yet capable of sustaining all bodies such as those of gods and the like; [as the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'He becomes one, He becomes three' and so on. Free from the <s>guṇas</s> (<s>nirguṇa</s>) — likewise, by nature free from the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like; yet the experiencer of the <s>guṇas</s> (<s>guṇabhoktṛ</s>) — yet capable of experiencing the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like. //

children.text: sarva-indriya-guṇa-ābhāsam sarva-indriya-guṇair ābhāso yasya tat sarva-indriya-ābhāsam / indriya-guṇā indriya-vṛttayaḥ / indriya-vṛttibhir api viṣayān jñatuṃ samartham ity-arthaḥ / sva-bhāvatas sarva-indriya-vivarjitam vina aiva indriya-vṛttibhiḥ svata eva sarvaṃ jānāti ity-arthaḥ / asaktam sva-bhāvato deva-ādi-deha-saṅga-rahitam, sarva-bhṛc ca eva deva-ādi-sarva-deha-bharaṇa-samarthaṃ ca; "sa ekadhā bhavati tridhā bhavati" ity-ādi-śruteḥ / nirguṇam tathā sva-bhāvatas sattva-ādi-guṇa-rahitam / guṇa-bhoktṛ ca sattva-ādīnāṃ guṇānāṃ bhoga-samarthaṃ ca //
bahir antaś ca bhūtānām acaraṃ caram eva ca |
children.translated_text: Outside and inside beings; unmoving yet moving;

children.text: sūkṣmatvāt tad avijñeyaṃ dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tat ||
children.translated_text: because of its subtlety, it is unknowable; it is far away and yet near. ||

children.text: bahir antaś ca bhūtānām acaraṃ caram eva ca |
sūkṣmatvāt tad avijñeyaṃ dūra-sthaṃ ca antike ca tat ||

body.text: pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni parityajyāśarīro bahir vartate; teṣām antaś ca vartate, "jakṣat krīḍan ramamāṇaḥ strībhir vā yānair vā" ityādiśrutisiddhasvacchandavṛttiṣu / acaraṃ caram eva ca -- svabhāvato 'caram; caram ca dehitve / sūkṣmatvāt tadavijñeyam evaṃ sarvaśaktiyuktaṃ sarvajñāṃ tad atmatattvam asmin kṣetre vartamānam apy atisūkṣmatvād dehāt pṛthaktvena saṃsāribhir avijñeyam, dūrasthaṃ cāntike ca tad amānitvādyuktaguṇarahitānāṃ viparītaguṇāṇāṃ puṃsāṃ svadehe vartamānam apy atidūrastham, tathā amānitvādiguṇopetānāṃ tad evāntike vartate //
body.translated_text: Having abandoned the elements such as earth and the like [that form the body], it exists outside, as a disembodied being; and it also exists inside them — in the states of spontaneous activity established in <s>śruti</s> [such as:] 'eating, playing, enjoying, with women or with vehicles,' and the like. Unmoving yet moving — by nature it is unmoving; yet it moves when embodied. Because of its subtlety, it is unknowable — though endowed with all powers and omniscient, this self-reality (<s>ātmatattva</s>), even while present in this body (<s>kṣetra</s>), is unknowable by those in <s>saṃsāra</s> as something distinct from the body, due to its extreme subtlety. It is far away and yet near — for persons who lack the qualities such as humility (<s>amānitva</s>) and the like, and possess contrary qualities, it is exceedingly far away even though present in their own body; likewise, for those endowed with qualities such as humility and the like, that very [self] is near. //

children.text: pṛthivy-ādīni bhūtāni parityajya aśarīro bahir vartate; teṣām antaś ca vartate, "jakṣat krīḍan ramamāṇaḥ strībhir vā yānair vā" ity-ādi-śruti-siddha-svacchanda-vṛttiṣu / acaraṃ caram eva ca --- sva-bhāvato 'caram; caram ca dehitve / sūkṣmatvāt tad-avijñeyam evaṃ sarva-śakti-yuktaṃ sarva-jñāṃ tad atma-tattvam asmin kṣetre vartamānam apy atisūkṣmatvād dehāt pṛthaktvena saṃsāribhir avijñeyam, dūra-sthaṃ ca antike ca tad amānitva-ādy-ukta-guṇa-rahitānāṃ viparīta-guṇāṇāṃ puṃsāṃ sva-dehe vartamānam apy atidūra-stham, tathā amānitva-ādi-guṇa-upetānāṃ tad eva antike vartate //
avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktam iva ca sthitam |
children.translated_text: Undivided among beings, yet appearing as if divided;

children.text: bhūtabhartṛ ca taj jñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca ||
children.translated_text: it is to be known as the sustainer of beings, and as that which absorbs and generates [them]. ||

children.text: avibhaktaṃ ca bhūteṣu vibhaktam iva ca sthitam |
bhūta-bhartṛ ca taj jñeyaṃ grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca ||

body.text:
devamanuṣyādibhūteṣu sarvatra sthitam ātmavastu veditṛtvaikākāratayā avibhaktam / aviduṣāṃ devādyākāreṇa "ayaṃ devo manuṣyaḥ" iti vibhaktam iva ca sthitam / devo 'ham, manuṣyo 'ham iti dehasāmānādhikaraṇyenānusandhīyamānam api veditṛtvena dehād arthāntarabhūtaṃ jñātuṃ śakyam iti ādāv uktam eva, "etad yo vetti" iti, idānīṃ prakārāntaraiś ca jñātuṃ śakyam ity āja bhūtabhartṛ ceti / bhūtānāṃ pṛthivyādīnāṃ deharūpeṇa saṃhatānāṃ yad bhartṛ, tad bhartavyebhyo bhūtebhyo 'rthāntaraṃ jñeyam; arthāntaram iti jñātuṃ śakyam ityarthaḥ / tathā grasiṣṇu annādīnāṃ bhautikānāṃ grasiṣṇu, grasyamānebhyo bhūtebhyo grasitṛtvenārthāntrabhūtam iti jñātuṃ śakyam / prabhaviṣṇu ca prabhavahetuś ca, grastānām annādīnām ākārāntareṇa
pariṇatānāṃ prabhahetuḥ, tebhyo 'rthāntaram iti jñātuṃ śakyam ityarthaḥ; mṛtaśarīre grasanaprabhavādīnām adarśanān na bhūtasaṃghātarūpaṃ kṣetraṃ grasanaprabhavabharaṇahetur iti niścīyate //
body.translated_text: The self-reality, present everywhere among beings such as gods, humans, and the like, is undivided — being of one form as a knower. To the ignorant, it appears as if divided in the forms of gods and the like — 'This is a god, this is a human.' Although cognized in co-ordinate predication with the body as 'I am a god, I am a human,' it can be known as something distinct from the body by [its nature as] a knower — this was stated at the outset: 'He who knows this.' Now [the Lord] says it can also be known by other means — 'the sustainer of beings': that which sustains beings — the elements such as earth and the like conjoined in the form of a body — is to be known as something distinct from the beings [it] sustains; 'distinct' means 'can be known [as such]' — this is the meaning. Likewise, that which absorbs (<s>grasiṣṇu</s>) — that which absorbs material things such as food and the like — can be known as something distinct from the material beings [it] absorbs, by [its nature as] the absorber. And that which generates (<s>prabhaviṣṇu</s>) — that which is the cause of generation, the cause of the re-emergence in another form of the food and the like that has been absorbed — can be known as something distinct from them, is the meaning. Since in a dead body the absorption, generation, and the like are not seen, it is ascertained that the field (<s>kṣetra</s>) in the form of the material aggregate is not the cause of absorption, generation, and sustenance. //

children.text:
deva-manuṣya-ādi-bhūteṣu sarvatra sthitam ātma-vastu veditṛtva-eka-ākāratayā avibhaktam / aviduṣāṃ deva-ādy-ākāreṇa "ayaṃ devo manuṣyaḥ" iti vibhaktam iva ca sthitam / devo 'ham, manuṣyo 'ham iti deha-sāmānādhikaraṇyena anusandhīyamānam api veditṛtvena dehād artha-antara-bhūtaṃ jñātuṃ śakyam iti ādāv uktam eva, "etad yo vetti" iti, idānīṃ prakāra-antaraiś ca jñātuṃ śakyam ity āja bhūta-bhartṛ ca iti / bhūtānāṃ pṛthivy-ādīnāṃ deha-rūpeṇa saṃhatānāṃ yad bhartṛ, tad bhartavyebhyo bhūtebhyo 'rtha-antaraṃ jñeyam; artha-antaram iti jñātuṃ śakyam ity-arthaḥ / tathā grasiṣṇu anna-ādīnāṃ bhautikānāṃ grasiṣṇu, grasyamānebhyo bhūtebhyo grasitṛtvena artha-antra-bhūtam iti jñātuṃ śakyam / prabhaviṣṇu ca prabhava-hetuś ca, grastānām anna-ādīnām ākāra-antareṇa
pariṇatānāṃ prabha-hetuḥ, tebhyo 'rtha-antaram iti jñātuṃ śakyam ity-arthaḥ; mṛta-śarīre grasana-prabhava-ādīnām adarśanān na bhūta-saṃghāta-rūpaṃ kṣetraṃ grasana-prabhava-bharaṇa-hetur iti niścīyate //
jyotiṣām api taj jyotis tamasaḥ param ucyate |
children.translated_text: It is the light even of lights; it is said to be beyond darkness.

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānagamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: It is knowledge, the knowable, and that which is to be reached by knowledge; it is seated in the heart of all. ||

children.text: jyotiṣām api taj jyotis tamasaḥ param ucyate |
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñāna-gamyaṃ hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam ||

body.text: jyotiśām dīpādityamaṇiprabhṛtīnām api tad eva jyotiḥ prakāśakam, dīpādityādīnām apy ātmaprabhārūpaṃ / jñānam eva prakāśakam / dīpādayas tu viṣayendriyasannikarṣavirodhisaṃtamasanirasanamātraṃ kurvate / tāvan mātreṇa teṣāṃ prakāśakatvam / tamasaḥ param ucyate / tamaśśabdaḥ sūkṣmāvasthaprakṛtivacanaḥ / prakṛteḥ param ucyata ityarthaḥ / ato jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānaikākāram iti jñeyam / tac ca jñānagamyam amānitvādibhir jñānasādhanair uktaiḥ prāpyam ityarthaḥ / hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam sarvasya manuṣyādeḥ hṛdi viśeṣaṇāvasthitam -- sannihitam //
body.translated_text: It is the light even of lights such as lamps, the sun, gems, and the like — their illuminator; even the light of lamps, the sun, and the like is of the nature of the self's own radiance. Knowledge alone is the illuminator. Lamps and the like merely remove the darkness that obstructs the contact between the sense-organs and their objects; only to that extent are they illuminators. It is said to be beyond darkness (<s>tamasaḥ param</s>) — the word <s>tamas</s> (darkness) here refers to <s>Prakṛti</s> in its subtle state; the meaning is: it is said to be beyond <s>Prakṛti</s>. Therefore it is knowledge, the knowable — it is to be known as having the sole form of knowledge; and it is to be reached by knowledge (<s>jñānagamya</s>) — it is to be attained by the means of knowledge stated [above], such as humility (<s>amānitva</s>) and the like — this is the meaning. It is seated in the heart of all — it is specially established, i.e., present, in the heart of every human being and the like. //

children.text: jyotiśām dīpa-āditya-maṇi-prabhṛtīnām api tad eva jyotiḥ prakāśakam, dīpa-āditya-ādīnām apy ātma-prabhā-rūpaṃ / jñānam eva prakāśakam / dīpa-ādayas tu viṣaya-indriya-sannikarṣa-virodhi-saṃtamasa-nirasana-mātraṃ kurvate / tāvan mātreṇa teṣāṃ prakāśakatvam / tamasaḥ param ucyate / tamaś-śabdaḥ sūkṣma-avastha-prakṛti-vacanaḥ / prakṛteḥ param ucyata ity-arthaḥ / ato jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ jñāna-eka-ākāram iti jñeyam / tac ca jñāna-gamyam amānitva-ādibhir jñāna-sādhanair uktaiḥ prāpyam ity-arthaḥ / hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam sarvasya manuṣya-ādeḥ hṛdi viśeṣaṇa-avasthitam --- sannihitam //
iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ coktaṃ samāsataḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus the field (<s>kṣetra</s>), knowledge, and the knowable have been briefly stated.

children.text: madbhakta etad vijñāya madbhāvāyopapadyate ||
children.translated_text: My devotee, understanding this, becomes fit for My state. ||

children.text: iti kṣetraṃ tathā jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca uktaṃ samāsataḥ |
mad-bhakta etad vijñāya mad-bhāvāya upapadyate ||

body.text: evaṃ "mahābhūtāny ahaṅkāraḥ" ityādinā "saṃghātaś cetanādhṛtir" ityantena kṣetratattvaṃ samāsenoktam / "amānitvam" ityādinā "tattvajñānārthacintanam" ityantena jñātavyasyātmatattvasya jñānasādhanam uktam / "anādi matparam" ityādinā "hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam" ityantena jñeyasya kṣetrajñasya yāthātmyaṃ ca saṃkṣepeṇoktam / madbhaktaḥ etat kṣetrayāthātmyaṃ, kṣetrād viviktātmasvarūpaprāptyupāyayāthātmyaṃ kṣetrajñayāthātmyaṃ ca vijñāya, madbhāvāyopapadyate / mama yo bhāvaḥ svabhāvaḥ, asaṃsāritvam asaṃsāritvaprāptaye upapanno bhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, by [the passage beginning] 'the great elements, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego)' and ending with 'the aggregate sustained by consciousness,' the reality of the field (<s>kṣetra</s>) has been briefly stated. By [the passage beginning] 'humility (<s>amānitva</s>)' and ending with 'contemplation directed toward the purpose of knowledge of the truth (<s>tattvajñānārthacintana</s>),' the means of knowledge of the self-reality that is to be known has been stated. And by [the passage beginning] 'beginningless, having Me as the supreme' and ending with 'seated in the heart of all,' the true nature of the knowable — the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (field-knower) — has been briefly stated. My devotee, understanding this — the true nature of the field, the true nature of the means of attaining the self that is distinct from the field, and the true nature of the field-knower — becomes fit for My state (<s>madbhāva</s>). My state (<s>bhāva</s>) means My nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), which is freedom from <s>saṃsāra</s>; the meaning is: he becomes fit for attaining freedom from <s>saṃsāra</s>. //

children.text: evaṃ "mahā-bhūtāny ahaṅkāraḥ" ity-ādinā "saṃghātaś cetana-ādhṛtir" ity-antena kṣetra-tattvaṃ samāsena uktam / "amānitvam" ity-ādinā "tattva-jñāna-artha-cintanam" ity-antena jñātavyasyā atma-tattvasya jñāna-sādhanam uktam / "anādi mat-param" ity-ādinā "hṛdi sarvasya viṣṭhitam" ity-antena jñeyasya kṣetra-jñasya yāthātmyaṃ ca saṃkṣepeṇa uktam / mad-bhaktaḥ etat kṣetra-yāthātmyaṃ, kṣetrād vivikta-ātma-sva-rūpa-prāpty-upāya-yāthātmyaṃ kṣetra-jña-yāthātmyaṃ ca vijñāya, mad-bhāvāya upapadyate / mama yo bhāvaḥ sva-bhāvaḥ, asaṃsāritvam asaṃsāritva-prāptaye upapanno bhavati ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: athātyantaviviktasvabhāvayoḥ prakṛtyātmanoḥ saṃsargasyānāditvaṃ saṃsṛṣṭayor dvayoḥ kāryabhedaḥ saṃsargahetuś cocyate --
body.translated_text: Now the beginninglessness of the conjunction of <s>Prakṛti</s> and the self — which are of utterly distinct natures — the different effects of the two when conjoined, and the cause of their conjunction, are stated —

children.text: atha atyanta-vivikta-sva-bhāvayoḥ prakṛty-ātmanoḥ saṃsargasya anāditvaṃ saṃsṛṣṭayor dvayoḥ kārya-bhedaḥ saṃsarga-hetuś ca ucyate ---
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhy anādī ubhāv api |
children.translated_text: Know that both <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> are beginningless;

children.text: vikārāṃś ca guṇāṃś caiva viddhi prakṛtisaṃbhavān ||
children.translated_text: and know that the modifications and the <s>guṇas</s> are born of <s>Prakṛti</s>. ||

children.text: prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ ca eva viddhy anādī ubhāv api |
vikārāṃś ca guṇāṃś ca eva viddhi prakṛti-saṃbhavān ||

body.text: prakṛtipuruṣau ubhau anyonyasaṃsṛṣṭau anādī iti viddhi; bandhahetubhūtān vikārān icchādveṣādīn, amānitvādikāṃś ca guṇām mokṣahetubhūtān prakṛtisaṃbhavān viddhi / puruṣeṇa saṃsṛṣṭeyam anādikālapravṛttā kṣetrākārapariṇātā prakṛtiḥ svavikārair icchādveṣādibhiḥ puruṣasya bandhuhetur bhavati; saivāmānitvādibhiḥ svavikāraiḥ puruṣasyāpavargahetur bhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Know that both <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>, mutually conjoined, are beginningless. Know that the modifications — desire, aversion, and the like — which are the causes of bondage, and the qualities such as humility (<s>amānitva</s>) and the like — which are the causes of liberation — are born of <s>Prakṛti</s>. This <s>Prakṛti</s>, conjoined with the <s>Puruṣa</s> from beginningless time, having transformed into the form of the field (<s>kṣetra</s>), through its own modifications such as desire, aversion, and the like, becomes the cause of bondage for the <s>Puruṣa</s>; that very same [<s>Prakṛti</s>], through its own modifications such as humility and the like, becomes the cause of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) for the <s>Puruṣa</s> — this is the meaning. //

children.text: prakṛti-puruṣau ubhau anyonya-saṃsṛṣṭau anādī iti viddhi; bandha-hetu-bhūtān vikārān icchā-dveṣa-ādīn, amānitva-ādikāṃś ca guṇām mokṣa-hetu-bhūtān prakṛti-saṃbhavān viddhi / puruṣeṇa saṃsṛṣṭa īyam anādi-kāla-pravṛttā kṣetra-ākāra-pariṇātā prakṛtiḥ sva-vikārair icchā-dveṣa-ādibhiḥ puruṣasya bandhu-hetur bhavati; sa eva amānitva-ādibhiḥ sva-vikāraiḥ puruṣasya apavarga-hetur bhavati ity-arthaḥ //
kāryakāraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtir ucyate |
children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s> is said to be the cause in the production of the body and the sense-organs;

children.text: puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve hetur ucyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s> is said to be the cause in the experience of pleasure and pain. ||

children.text: kārya-kāraṇa-kartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtir ucyate |
puruṣaḥ sukha-duḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve hetur ucyate ||

body.text: kāryaṃ śarīram; kāraṇāni jñānakarmātmakāni samanaskānīndriyāṇi / teṣāṃ kriyākāritve puruṣādhiṣṭhitā prakṛtir eva hetuḥ; puruṣādhiṣṭhitakṣetrākārapariṇataprakṛtyāśrayāḥ bhogasādhanabhūtāḥ kriyā ityarthaḥ / puruṣasyādhiṣṭhātṛtvam eva; tadapekṣayā, "kartā śāstrārthavattvāt" ityādikam uktam; śarīrādhiṣṭhānaprayatnahetutvam eva hi puruṣasya kartṛtvam / prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭaḥ puruṣaḥ sukhaduḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve hetuḥ, sukhaduḥkhānubhavāśraya ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The body is the effect (<s>kārya</s>); the causes (<s>kāraṇa</s>) are the sense-organs, which are of the nature of knowledge and action, together with the mind. In the activity of producing these, <s>Prakṛti</s> — presided over by the <s>Puruṣa</s> — alone is the cause; the meaning is: the activities that serve as the means of experience are dependent on <s>Prakṛti</s> that has transformed into the form of the field, presided over by the <s>Puruṣa</s>. The <s>Puruṣa</s>'s role is only that of the presider; in relation to that, [statements such as] 'The agent [is the self], because of the purposefulness of scripture' and the like have been said. For the agency of the <s>Puruṣa</s> consists only in being the cause of effort through presiding over the body. The <s>Puruṣa</s> conjoined with <s>Prakṛti</s> is said to be the cause in the experience of pleasure and pain — meaning: [the <s>Puruṣa</s>] is the locus of the experience of pleasure and pain. //

children.text: kāryaṃ śarīram; kāraṇāni jñāna-karma-ātmakāni sa-manaskāni indriyāṇi / teṣāṃ kriyā-kāritve puruṣa-adhiṣṭhitā prakṛtir eva hetuḥ; puruṣa-adhiṣṭhita-kṣetra-ākāra-pariṇata-prakṛty-āśrayāḥ bhoga-sādhana-bhūtāḥ kriyā ity-arthaḥ / puruṣasya adhiṣṭhātṛtvam eva; tad-apekṣayā, "kartā śāstra-arthavattvāt" ity-ādikam uktam; śarīra-adhiṣṭhāna-prayatna-hetutvam eva hi puruṣasya kartṛtvam / prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭaḥ puruṣaḥ sukha-duḥkhānāṃ bhoktṛtve hetuḥ, sukha-duḥkha-anubhava-āśraya ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: evam anyonyasaṃsṛṣṭayoḥ prakṛtipuruṣayoḥ kāryabheda uktaḥ; puruṣasya svatas svānubhavaikasukhasyāpi vaiṣayikasukhaduḥkhopabhogahetum āha --
body.translated_text: Thus the different effects of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> when mutually conjoined have been stated. [The Lord] now states the cause of the experience of worldly pleasure and pain for the <s>Puruṣa</s>, who by its own nature has only the bliss of self-experience —

children.text: evam anyonya-saṃsṛṣṭayoḥ prakṛti-puruṣayoḥ kārya-bheda uktaḥ; puruṣasya svatas sva-anubhava-eka-sukhasya api vaiṣayika-sukha-duḥkha-upabhoga-hetum āha ---
puruṣaḥ prakṛtistho hi bhuṅkte prakṛtijān guṇān |
children.translated_text: For the <s>Puruṣa</s>, established in <s>Prakṛti</s>, experiences the <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s>. |

children.text: puruṣaḥ prakṛti-stho hi bhuṅkte prakṛti-jān guṇān |

body.text: guṇaśabdaḥ svakāryeṣv aupacārikaḥ / svatas svānubhavaikasukhaḥ puruṣaḥ prakṛtisthaḥ prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭaḥ, prakṛtijān guṇān prakṛtisaṃsargopādhikān sattvādiguṇakāryabhūtān sukhaduḥkhādīn, bhuṅkte anubhavati / prakṛtisaṃsargahetum āha --
body.translated_text: The word <s>guṇa</s> is used figuratively for their effects. The <s>Puruṣa</s>, whose bliss by its own nature is solely self-experience, being established in <s>Prakṛti</s>, i.e., conjoined with <s>Prakṛti</s>, experiences the <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s> — the pleasure, pain, and the like that are effects of the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like, conditioned by conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s>. [The Lord] states the cause of the conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s> —

children.text: guṇa-śabdaḥ sva-kāryeṣv aupacārikaḥ / svatas sva-anubhava-eka-sukhaḥ puruṣaḥ prakṛti-sthaḥ prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭaḥ, prakṛti-jān guṇān prakṛti-saṃsarga-upādhikān sattva-ādi-guṇa-kārya-bhūtān sukha-duḥkha-ādīn, bhuṅkte anubhavati / prakṛti-saṃsarga-hetum āha ---
kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo 'sya sadasadyonijanmasu ||
children.translated_text: Attachment to the <s>guṇas</s> is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs. ||

children.text: kāraṇaṃ guṇa-saṅgo 'sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu ||

body.text: pūrvapūrvaprakṛtipariṇāmarūpadevamanuṣyādiyoniviśeṣeṣu sthito 'yaṃ puruṣas tattadyoniprayuktasattvādiguṇamayeṣu sukhaduḥkhādiṣu saktaḥ tatsādhanabhūteṣu puṇyapāpakarmasu pravartate; tatas tatpuṇyapāpaphalānubhavāya sadasadyoniṣu sādhvasādhuṣu yoniṣu jāyate; tataś ca karmārabhate; tato jāyate; yāvad amānitvādikān ātmaprāptisādhanabhūtān guṇān sevate, tāvad eva saṃsarati / tad idam uktaṃ kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo 'sya sadasadyonijanmasu iti //
body.translated_text: This <s>Puruṣa</s>, established in the particular wombs of gods, humans, and the like — which are the transformations of <s>Prakṛti</s> from prior [lives] — being attached to pleasure, pain, and the like constituted by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like pertaining to those respective wombs, engages in meritorious and sinful actions that are the means [of obtaining them]; then, for the experience of the fruits of those merits and sins, it is born in good and evil wombs — good and bad births; and then again it undertakes actions; then again it is born. As long as it cultivates the qualities such as humility and the like, which are the means of attaining the self, so long does it continue in <s>saṃsāra</s>. This is what is stated: attachment to the <s>guṇas</s> is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs. //

children.text: pūrva-pūrva-prakṛti-pariṇāma-rūpa-deva-manuṣya-ādi-yoni-viśeṣeṣu sthito 'yaṃ puruṣas tat-tad-yoni-prayukta-sattva-ādi-guṇa-mayeṣu sukha-duḥkha-ādiṣu saktaḥ tat-sādhana-bhūteṣu puṇya-pāpa-karmasu pravartate; tatas tat-puṇya-pāpa-phala-anubhavāya sad-asad-yoniṣu sādhv-asādhuṣu yoniṣu jāyate; tataś ca karmā arabhate; tato jāyate; yāvad amānitva-ādikān ātma-prāpti-sādhana-bhūtān guṇān sevate, tāvad eva saṃsarati / tad idam uktaṃ kāraṇaṃ guṇa-saṅgo 'sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu iti //
upadraṣṭānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā maheśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: The witness, the permitter, the sustainer, the experiencer, the great Lord,

children.text: paramātmeti cāpy ukto dehe 'smin puruṣaḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also called the Supreme Self — [such is] the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> in this body. ||

children.text: upadraṣṭa ānumantā ca bhartā bhoktā mahā-īśvaraḥ |
parama-ātma īti ca apy ukto dehe 'smin puruṣaḥ paraḥ ||

body.text:
asmin dehe 'vasthito 'yaṃ puruṣo dehapravṛttyanuguṇasaṅkalpādirūpeṇa dehasyopadraṣṭā anumantā ca bhavati / tathā dehasya bhartā ca bhavati; tathā dehapravṛttijanitasukhaduḥkhayor bhoktā ca bhavati / evaṃ dehaniyamanena, dehabharaṇena, dehaśeṣitvena ca dehendriyamanāṃsi prati maheśvaro bhavati / tathā ca vakṣyate, "śarīraṃ yad avāpnoti yac cāpy utkrāmatīśvaraḥ / gṛhītvaitāni saṃyāti vāyur gandhān ivāśayāt // BhGR_13." iti / asmin dehe dehendriyamanāṃsi prati paramātmeti cāpy uktaḥ / dehe manasi ca ātmaśabdo 'nantaram eva prayujyate, "dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecid ātmānam ātmanā" iti; apiśabdān maheśvara ity apy ukta iti gamyate; puruṣaḥ paraḥ "anādi matparam" ityādinokto 'paricchinnajñānaśaktir ayaṃ puruṣo 'nādiprakṛtisaṃbandhakṛtaguṇasaṅgād etad
dehamātramaheśvaro dehamātraparamātmā ca bhavati //
body.translated_text: This <s>Puruṣa</s>, established in this body, becomes the witness (<s>upadraṣṭṛ</s>) and the permitter (<s>anumantṛ</s>) of the body — in the form of willing and the like that conform to the activities of the body. Likewise, it becomes the sustainer (<s>bhartṛ</s>) of the body; likewise, the experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>) of the pleasure and pain generated by the activities of the body. Thus, by governing the body, sustaining the body, and being the master (<s>śeṣin</s>) for whose sake the body exists, it becomes the great Lord (<s>maheśvara</s>) with respect to the body, sense-organs, and mind. And thus it will be stated: 'The lord (<s>īśvara</s>), when he obtains a body and when he departs from it, takes these [senses] and goes, as the wind carries fragrances from their source.' Also called the Supreme Self (<s>paramātmā</s>) in this body — with respect to the body, sense-organs, and mind. Since the word <s>ātman</s> (self) is used immediately after with respect to the body and the mind — as in 'Through meditation, some see the self by the self in the self' — from the word 'also' (<s>api</s>), it is understood that [the <s>Puruṣa</s>] is also called <s>maheśvara</s>. The supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>puruṣaḥ paraḥ</s>) — this <s>Puruṣa</s> described [beginning with] 'beginningless, having Me as the supreme,' possessing unlimited power of knowledge, becomes — due to attachment to the <s>guṇas</s> caused by beginningless connection with <s>Prakṛti</s> — merely the great Lord of this body alone, and merely the Supreme Self of this body alone. //

children.text:
asmin dehe 'vasthito 'yaṃ puruṣo deha-pravṛtty-anuguṇa-saṅkalpa-ādi-rūpeṇa dehasya upadraṣṭā anumantā ca bhavati / tathā dehasya bhartā ca bhavati; tathā deha-pravṛtti-janita-sukha-duḥkhayor bhoktā ca bhavati / evaṃ deha-niyamanena, deha-bharaṇena, deha-śeṣitvena ca deha-indriya-manāṃsi prati mahā-īśvaro bhavati / tathā ca vakṣyate, "śarīraṃ yad avāpnoti yac ca apy utkrāmatī iśvaraḥ / gṛhītva aitāni saṃyāti vāyur gandhān ivā āśayāt // BhGR_13." iti / asmin dehe deha-indriya-manāṃsi prati parama-ātma īti ca apy uktaḥ / dehe manasi ca ātma-śabdo 'nantaram eva prayujyate, "dhyānenā atmani paśyanti kecid ātmānam ātmanā" iti; api-śabdān mahā-īśvara ity apy ukta iti gamyate; puruṣaḥ paraḥ "anādi mat-param" ity-ādina ūkto 'paricchinna-jñāna-śaktir ayaṃ puruṣo 'nādi-prakṛti-saṃbandha-kṛta-guṇa-saṅgād etad
deha-mātra-mahā-īśvaro deha-mātra-parama-ātmā ca bhavati //
ya enaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇais saha |
children.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s> together with the <s>guṇas</s> —

children.text: sarvathā vartamāno 'pi na sa bhūyo 'bhijāyate ||
children.translated_text: though existing in any condition whatsoever, he is not born again. ||

children.text: ya enaṃ vetti puruṣaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca guṇais saha |
sarvathā vartamāno 'pi na sa bhūyo 'bhijāyate ||

body.text: enam uktasvabhāvaṃ puruṣam, uktasvabhāvāṃ ca prakṛtiṃ vakṣyamāṇasvabhāvayuktaiḥ sattvādibhir guṇaiḥ saha, yo vetti yathāvad vivekena jānāti, sa sarvathā devamanuṣyādideheṣv atimātrakliṣṭaprakāreṇa vartamāno 'pi, na bhūyo 'bhijāyate na bhūyaḥ prakṛtyā saṃsargam arhati, aparicchinnajñānalakaṣaṇam apahatapāpmānam ātmānaṃ taddehāvasānasamaye prāpnotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: He who knows this <s>Puruṣa</s> of the nature described, and <s>Prakṛti</s> of the nature described, together with the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like whose nature will be described — whoever knows [them] properly, with discrimination — he, though existing in any condition whatsoever, even in exceedingly afflicted states among bodies of gods, humans, and the like, is not born again — he no longer deserves conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s>; the meaning is that at the end of that embodiment, he attains the self characterized by unlimited knowledge and free from all evil. //

children.text: enam ukta-sva-bhāvaṃ puruṣam, ukta-sva-bhāvāṃ ca prakṛtiṃ vakṣyamāṇa-sva-bhāva-yuktaiḥ sattva-ādibhir guṇaiḥ saha, yo vetti yathāvad vivekena jānāti, sa sarvathā deva-manuṣya-ādi-deheṣv atimātra-kliṣṭa-prakāreṇa vartamāno 'pi, na bhūyo 'bhijāyate na bhūyaḥ prakṛtyā saṃsargam arhati, aparicchinna-jñāna-lakaṣaṇam apahata-pāpmānam ātmānaṃ tad-deha-avasāna-samaye prāpnoti ity-arthaḥ //
dhyānenātmani paśyanti kecid ātmānam ātmanā |
children.translated_text: Through meditation, some see the self by the self in the self;

children.text: anye sāṅkhyena yogena karmayogena cāpare ||
children.translated_text: others through <s>Sāṅkhya</s> <s>yoga</s>, and yet others through <s>Karmayoga</s>. ||

children.text: dhyānenā atmani paśyanti kecid ātmānam ātmanā |
anye sāṅkhyena yogena karma-yogena ca apare ||

body.text: kecin niṣpannayogāḥ ātmani śarīre 'vasthitam ātmānam ātmanā manasā dhyānena yogena paśyanti / anye ca aniṣpannayogāḥ, sāṃkhyena yogena jñānayogena yogayogyaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā ātmānaṃ paśyanti / apare jñānayogānadhikāriṇaḥ, tadadhikāriṇaś ca sukaropāyasaktāḥ, vyapadeśyāś ca karmayogenāntargatajñānena manaso yogayogyatām āpādya ātmānaṃ paśyanti //
body.translated_text: Some who have perfected their <s>yoga</s> see the self — abiding in the body — by the self, i.e., by the mind, through meditation, through <s>yoga</s>. Others who have not yet perfected their <s>yoga</s> make the mind fit for <s>yoga</s> through <s>sāṃkhyayoga</s> — the <s>yoga</s> of knowledge (<s>jñānayoga</s>) — and [thereby] see the self. Still others who are not qualified for <s>jñānayoga</s>, and even those who are qualified but are devoted to the easier means, and those who are to be designated [as following <s>karmayoga</s>] — make the mind fit for <s>yoga</s> through <s>karmayoga</s> that contains knowledge within it, and [thereby] see the self. ||

children.text: kecin niṣpanna-yogāḥ ātmani śarīre 'vasthitam ātmānam ātmanā manasā dhyānena yogena paśyanti / anye ca aniṣpanna-yogāḥ, sāṃkhyena yogena jñāna-yogena yoga-yogyaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā ātmānaṃ paśyanti / apare jñāna-yoga-anadhikāriṇaḥ, tad-adhikāriṇaś ca sukara-upāya-saktāḥ, vyapadeśyāś ca karma-yogena antar-gata-jñānena manaso yoga-yogyatām āpādya ātmānaṃ paśyanti //
anye tv evam ajānantaḥ śrutvānyebhyaś ca upāsate |
children.translated_text: 'But others, not knowing thus, worship having heard from others.' |

children.text: te 'pi cātitaranty eva mṛtyuṃ śrutiparāyaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'And they too cross beyond death, being devoted to what they have heard.' ||

children.text: anye tv evam ajānantaḥ śrutva ānyebhyaś ca upāsate |
te 'pi ca atitaranty eva mṛtyuṃ śruti-parāyaṇāḥ ||

body.text: anye tu karmayogādiṣu ātmāvalokanasādhaneṣv anadhikṛtāḥ anyebhyaḥ tattvadarśibhyo jñānibhyaḥ śrutvā karmayogādibhir ātmānam upāsate; te 'py ātmadarśanena mṛtyum atitaranti / ye śrutiparāyaṇāḥ śravaṇamātraniṣṭhāḥ, ete ca śravaṇaniṣṭhāḥ pūtapāpāḥ krameṇa karmayogādikam ārabhyātitaranty eva mṛtyum / apiśabdāc ca pūrvabhedo 'vagamyate //
body.translated_text: But others who are not qualified for the means of seeing the self such as <s>karmayoga</s> and the like — having heard from others, from knowers who have seen the truth — worship the self through <s>karmayoga</s> and the like. They too cross beyond death through the vision of the self. Those who are devoted solely to hearing — they too, having purified their sins, gradually undertaking <s>karmayoga</s> and the like, do indeed cross beyond death. And from the word 'too' (<s>api</s>), their difference from those previously mentioned is understood. ||

children.text: anye tu karma-yoga-ādiṣu ātma-avalokana-sādhaneṣv anadhikṛtāḥ anyebhyaḥ tattva-darśibhyo jñānibhyaḥ śrutvā karma-yoga-ādibhir ātmānam upāsate; te 'py ātma-darśanena mṛtyum atitaranti / ye śruti-parāyaṇāḥ śravaṇa-mātra-niṣṭhāḥ, ete ca śravaṇa-niṣṭhāḥ pūta-pāpāḥ krameṇa karma-yoga-ādikam ārabhya atitaranty eva mṛtyum / api-śabdāc ca pūrva-bhedo 'vagamyate //

body.text: atha prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭasyātmano vivekānusandhānaprakāraṃ vaktuṃ sarvaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca sattvaṃ cidacitsaṃsargajam ity āha --
body.translated_text: Now, to state the mode of contemplation for discrimination of the self that is conjoined with <s>Prakṛti</s>, He says that every being — stationary and moving — is born from the conjunction of the conscious and the non-conscious:

children.text: atha prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭasyā atmano viveka-anusandhāna-prakāraṃ vaktuṃ sarvaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca sattvaṃ cid-acit-saṃsarga-jam ity āha ---
yāvat saṃjāyate kiñcit sattvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam |
children.translated_text: 'Whatever being is born, whether stationary or moving,' |

children.text: kṣetrakṣetrajñasaṃyogāt tad viddhi bharatarṣabha ||
children.translated_text: 'know that to be from the conjunction of the field and the knower of the field, O best of <s>Bhāratas</s>.' ||

children.text: yāvat saṃjāyate kiñcit sattvaṃ sthāvara-jaṅgamam |
kṣetra-kṣetra-jña-saṃyogāt tad viddhi bharata-rṣabha ||

body.text: yāvat sthāvarajaṅgamātmanā sattvaṃ jāyate, tāvat kṣetrakṣetrajñayor itaretarasaṃyogād eva jāyate saṃyuktam eva jāyate, na tv itaretaraviyuktam ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Whatever being is born in the form of stationary or moving [entities] — all that is born from the mutual conjunction of the field (<s>kṣetra</s>) and the knower of the field (<s>kṣetrajña</s>) alone; it is born as conjoined — meaning: it is not born as separated from either of them. ||

children.text: yāvat sthāvara-jaṅgama-ātmanā sattvaṃ jāyate, tāvat kṣetra-kṣetra-jñayor itara-itara-saṃyogād eva jāyate saṃyuktam eva jāyate, na tv itara-itara-viyuktam ity-arthaḥ //
samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram |
children.translated_text: 'He who sees the supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings,' |

children.text: vinaśyatsv avinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||
children.translated_text: 'not perishing when they perish — he [truly] sees.' ||

children.text: samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parama-īśvaram |
vinaśyatsv a-vinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa paśyati ||

body.text: evam itaretarayukteṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu devādiviṣamākārād viyuktaṃ tatra tatra tattaddehendriyamanāṃsi prati parameśvaratvena sthitam ātmānaṃ jñātṛtvena samānākāraṃ teṣu dehādiṣu vinaśyatsu vināśānarhasvabhāvenāvinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati, sa -- paśyati sa ātmānaṃ yathāvad avasthitaṃ paśyati / yas tu devādiviṣamākāreṇātmānam api viṣamākāraṃ janmavināśādiyuktaṃ ca paśyati, sa nityam eva saṃsaratītyabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in all beings that are mutually conjoined [as field and knower] — he who sees the self as separated from the unequal forms of gods and the like, as abiding therein as the supreme lord (<s>parameśvara</s>) over the respective bodies, senses, and minds, as of uniform form by virtue of being the knower, and as not perishing — being of a nature unfit for destruction — when those bodies and the like perish: he sees — he sees the self as it truly is. But he who sees the self as having an unequal form corresponding to the unequal forms of gods and the like, and as subject to birth, destruction, and so on — he transmigrates eternally. This is the import. ||

children.text: evam itara-itara-yukteṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu deva-ādi-viṣama-ākārād viyuktaṃ tatra tatra tat-tad-deha-indriya-manāṃsi prati parama-īśvaratvena sthitam ātmānaṃ jñātṛtvena samāna-akāraṃ teṣu deha-ādiṣu vinaśyatsu vināśa-anarha-sva-bhāvena avinaśyantaṃ yaḥ paśyati, sa --- paśyati sa ātmānaṃ yathāvad avasthitaṃ paśyati / yas tu deva-ādi-viṣama-ākāreṇā atmānam api viṣama-ākāraṃ janma-vināśa-ādi-yuktaṃ ca paśyati, sa nityam eva saṃsarati ity-abhiprāyaḥ //
samaṃ paśyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśvaram |
children.translated_text: 'For seeing the Lord equally present everywhere,' |

children.text: na hinasty ātmanātmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: 'he does not injure the self by the self; thence he goes to the supreme goal.' ||

children.text: samaṃ paśyan hi sarvatra samavasthitam īśvaram |
na hinasty ātmanā ātmānaṃ tato yāti parāṃ gatim ||

body.text: sarvatra devādiśarīreṣu tattaccheṣitvenādhāratayā viyantṛtayā ca sthitam īśvaram ātmānaṃ devādiviṣamākāraviyuktaṃ jñānaikākāratayā samaṃ paśyan ātmanā manasā, svam ātmānaṃ na hinasti rakṣati, saṃsārān mocayati / tataḥ tasmāj jñātṛtayā sarvatra samānākāradarśanāt parāṃ gatiṃ yāti; gamyata iti gatiḥ; paraṃ gantavyaṃ yathāvad avasthitam ātmānaṃ prāpnoti; devādyākārayuktatayā sarvatra viṣamam ātmānaṃ paśyan ātmānaṃ hinasti -- bhavajaladhimadhye prakṣipati //
body.translated_text: Seeing the self — the lord (<s>īśvara</s>) — as present everywhere in the bodies of gods and the like, as their dependent (<s>śeṣin</s>), support, and controller, as equal by virtue of the single form of knowledge, separated from the unequal forms of gods and the like — seeing thus with the mind, he does not injure his own self: he protects it, he liberates it from <s>saṃsāra</s>. From that — from seeing it as of uniform form everywhere by virtue of being the knower — he goes to the supreme goal. 'Goal' (<s>gati</s>) means that which is reached; he attains the supreme destination — the self as it truly is. But he who sees the self as unequal everywhere due to its association with the forms of gods and the like — he injures the self: he casts it into the ocean of mundane existence. ||

children.text: sarvatra deva-ādi-śarīreṣu tat-tac-cheṣitvenā adhāratayā viyantṛtayā ca sthitam īśvaram ātmānaṃ deva-ādi-viṣama-ākāra-viyuktaṃ jñāna-eka-ākāratayā samaṃ paśyan ātmanā manasā, svam ātmānaṃ na hinasti rakṣati, saṃsārān mocayati / tataḥ tasmāj jñātṛtayā sarvatra samāna-ākāra-darśanāt parāṃ gatiṃ yāti; gamyata iti gatiḥ; paraṃ gantavyaṃ yathāvad avasthitam ātmānaṃ prāpnoti; deva-ādy-ākāra-yuktatayā sarvatra viṣamam ātmānaṃ paśyan ātmānaṃ hinasti --- bhava-jaladhi-madhye prakṣipati //
prakṛtyaiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He who sees that all actions are performed by <s>Prakṛti</s> alone,' |

children.text: yaḥ paśyati tathātmānam akartāraṃ sa paśyati ||
children.translated_text: 'and likewise that the self is a non-doer — he [truly] sees.' ||

children.text: prakṛtya aiva ca karmāṇi kriyamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ |
yaḥ paśyati tathā ātmānam akartāraṃ sa paśyati ||

body.text: sarvāṇi karmāṇi, "kāryakāraṇakartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtir ucyate" iti pūrvoktarītyā prakṛtyā kriyamāṇānīti yaḥ paśyati, tathā ātmānaṃ jñānākāraṃ akartāraṃ ca yaḥ paśyati, tasya prakṛtisaṃyogas tadadhiṣṭhānaṃ tajjanyasukhaduḥkhānubhavaś ca karmarūpājñānakṛtānīti ca yaḥ paśyati, sa ātmānaṃ yathāvad avasthitaṃ paśyati //
body.translated_text: He who sees that all actions are performed by <s>Prakṛti</s>, in the manner previously stated — 'the cause of the effect, the instrument, and the agency is said to be <s>Prakṛti</s>' — and who likewise sees the self as having the form of knowledge and as a non-doer; and who sees that its conjunction with <s>Prakṛti</s>, its presiding over it, and its experience of the pleasure and pain produced by it are all caused by ignorance in the form of <s>karma</s> — he sees the self as it truly is. ||

children.text: sarvāṇi karmāṇi, "kārya-kāraṇa-kartṛtve hetuḥ prakṛtir ucyate" iti pūrva-ukta-rītyā prakṛtyā kriyamāṇāni iti yaḥ paśyati, tathā ātmānaṃ jñāna-ākāraṃ akartāraṃ ca yaḥ paśyati, tasya prakṛti-saṃyogas tad-adhiṣṭhānaṃ taj-janya-sukha-duḥkha-anubhavaś ca karma-rūpa-ajñāna-kṛtāni iti ca yaḥ paśyati, sa ātmānaṃ yathāvad avasthitaṃ paśyati //
yadā bhūtapṛthagbhāvam ekastham anupaśyati |
children.translated_text: 'When one perceives the diverse states of beings as resting in the One,' |

children.text: tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma saṃpadyate tadā ||
children.translated_text: 'and their expansion from that alone — then one attains <s>Brahman</s>.' ||

children.text: yadā bhūta-pṛthag-bhāvam eka-stham anupaśyati |
tata eva ca vistāraṃ brahma saṃpadyate tadā ||

body.text: prakṛtipuruṣatattvadvayātmakeṣu devādiṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu satsu teṣāṃ devatvamanuṣyatvahrasvatvadīrghatvādipṛthagbhāvam ekastham ekatattvastham -- prakṛtisthaṃ yadā paśyati, nātmastham, tata eva prakṛtita evottarottaraputrapautrādibhedavistāraṃ ca yadā paśyati, tadaiva brahmasaṃpadyate anavacchinnaṃ jñānaikākāram ātmānaṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Among all beings — gods and the like — which consist of the twofold reality of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>: when one perceives that their diverse states — their differentiation as godhood, humanhood, shortness, tallness, and the like — rest in the One, i.e., rest in a single reality — rest in <s>Prakṛti</s> — and are not in the self; and when one perceives the ever-further expansion into sons, grandsons, and the like as being from that [<s>Prakṛti</s>] alone — then indeed one attains <s>Brahman</s>: one attains the self, which is unlimited and has the single form of knowledge. This is the meaning. ||

children.text: prakṛti-puruṣa-tattva-dvaya-ātmakeṣu deva-ādiṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu satsu teṣāṃ devatva-manuṣyatva-hrasvatva-dīrghatva-ādi-pṛthag-bhāvam eka-stham eka-tattva-stham --- prakṛti-sthaṃ yadā paśyati, nā atma-stham, tata eva prakṛtita eva uttara-uttara-putra-pautra-ādi-bheda-vistāraṃ ca yadā paśyati, tada aiva brahma-saṃpadyate anavacchinnaṃ jñāna-eka-ākāram ātmānaṃ prāpnoti ity-arthaḥ //
anāditvān nirguṇatvāt paramātmāyam avyayaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Being beginningless and without <s>guṇas</s>, this supreme self is imperishable.' |

children.text: śarīrastho 'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate ||
children.translated_text: 'Though dwelling in the body, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, it neither acts nor is tainted.' ||

children.text: anāditvān nirguṇatvāt parama-ātma āyam avyayaḥ |
śarīra-stho 'pi kaunteya na karoti na lipyate ||

body.text: ayaṃ paramātmā dehān niṣkṛṣya svasvabhāvena nirūpitaḥ, śarīrastho 'pi anāditvād anārabhyatvād avyayaḥ vyayarahitaḥ, nirguṇatvāt sattvādiguṇarahitatvān na karoti, na lipyate dehasvabhāvair na lipyate //
body.translated_text: This supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>), when defined by its own essential nature extracted from the bodies, though dwelling in the body, is imperishable — free from decay — because of being beginningless, i.e., not produced; and because of being without <s>guṇas</s> — devoid of the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like — it neither acts nor is tainted by the characteristics of the body. ||

children.text: ayaṃ parama-ātmā dehān niṣkṛṣya sva-sva-bhāvena nirūpitaḥ, śarīra-stho 'pi anāditvād anārabhyatvād avyayaḥ vyaya-rahitaḥ, nirguṇatvāt sattva-ādi-guṇa-rahitatvān na karoti, na lipyate deha-sva-bhāvair na lipyate //

body.text: yady api nirguṇatvān na karoti, nityasaṃyukto dehasvabhāvaiḥ kathaṃ na lipyata ity atrāha --
body.translated_text: Even though it does not act because of being without <s>guṇas</s>, how is it not tainted when it is eternally conjoined with the characteristics of the body? To this he says:

children.text: yady api nirguṇatvān na karoti, nitya-saṃyukto deha-sva-bhāvaiḥ kathaṃ na lipyata ity atrā aha ---
yathā sarvagataṃ saukṣmyād ākāśaṃ nopalipyate |
children.translated_text: 'Just as the all-pervading space, because of its subtlety, is not tainted,' |

children.text: sarvatrāvasthito dehe tathātmā nopalipyate ||
children.translated_text: 'so the self, though present everywhere in the body, is not tainted.' ||

children.text: yathā sarva-gataṃ saukṣmyād ākāśaṃ na upalipyate |
sarvatra avasthito dehe tathā ātmā na upalipyate ||

body.text: yathā ākāśaṃ sarvagatam api sarvair vastubhis saṃyuktam api saukṣmyāt sarvavastusvabhāvair na lipyate, tathā ātmā atisaukṣmyāt sarvatra devamanuṣyādau dehe 'vasthito 'pi tattaddehasvabhāvair na lipyate //
body.translated_text: Just as space, though all-pervading, though conjoined with all objects, is not tainted by the characteristics of any objects because of its subtlety — so the self, because of its extreme subtlety, though present everywhere in the bodies of gods, humans, and the like, is not tainted by the characteristics of those respective bodies. ||

children.text: yathā ākāśaṃ sarva-gatam api sarvair vastubhis saṃyuktam api saukṣmyāt sarva-vastu-sva-bhāvair na lipyate, tathā ātmā atisaukṣmyāt sarvatra deva-manuṣya-ādau dehe 'vasthito 'pi tat-tad-deha-sva-bhāvair na lipyate //
yathā prakāśayaty ekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokam imaṃ raviḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Just as the single sun illuminates this entire world,' |

children.text: kṣetraṃ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata ||
children.translated_text: 'so the owner of the field illuminates the entire field, O <s>Bhārata</s>.' ||

children.text: yathā prakāśayaty ekaḥ kṛtsnaṃ lokam imaṃ raviḥ |
kṣetraṃ kṣetrī tathā kṛtsnaṃ prakāśayati bhārata ||

body.text: yathaika ādityaḥ svayā prabhayā kṛtsnam imaṃ lokaṃ prakāśayati, tathā kṣetram api kṣetrī, "mamedaṃ kṣetram īdṛśam" iti kṛtsnam bahirantaś cā-pādatalamastakaṃ svakīyena jñānena prakāśayati / ataḥ prakāśyāl lokāt prakāśakādityavad veditṛtvena vedyabhūtād asmāt kṣetrād atyantavilakṣaṇo 'yam uktalakṣaṇa ātmetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Just as the single sun illuminates this entire world by its own radiance, so the owner of the field (<s>kṣetrin</s>) illuminates the entire field — [knowing it as] 'this field of such a kind is mine' — from the sole of the foot to the crown of the head, both externally and internally, by his own knowledge. Therefore, just as the sun, the illuminator, is utterly different from the world that is illuminated, so is this self of the described characteristics utterly different from this field that is the object of knowledge, being the knower — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: yatha aika ādityaḥ svayā prabhayā kṛtsnam imaṃ lokaṃ prakāśayati, tathā kṣetram api kṣetrī, "mama idaṃ kṣetram īdṛśam" iti kṛtsnam bahir-antaś cā a-pāda-tala-mastakaṃ svakīyena jñānena prakāśayati / ataḥ prakāśyāl lokāt prakāśaka-ādityavad veditṛtvena vedya-bhūtād asmāt kṣetrād atyanta-vilakṣaṇo 'yam ukta-lakṣaṇa ātma īty-arthaḥ //
kṣetrakṣetrajñayor evam antaraṃ jñānacakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: 'Those who, with the eye of knowledge, thus know the difference between the field and the knower of the field,' |

children.text: bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca ye vidur yānti te param ||
children.translated_text: 'and the liberation of beings from <s>Prakṛti</s> — they go to the Supreme.' ||

children.text: kṣetra-kṣetra-jñayor evam antaraṃ jñāna-cakṣuṣā |
bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣaṃ ca ye vidur yānti te param ||

body.text: evam uktena prakāreṇa kṣetrakṣetrajñayor antaraṃ viśeṣaṃ vivekaviṣayajñānākhyena cakṣuṣā ye viduḥ, bhūtaprakṛtimokṣaṃ ca, te paraṃ yānti nirmuktabandham ātmānaṃ prāpnuvanti / mokṣyate 'neneti mokṣaḥ, amānitvādikaṃ mokṣasādhanam ityarthaḥ; kṣetrakṣetrajñayor vivekaviṣayeṇoktena jñānena tayor vivekaṃ viditvā bhūtākārapariṇataprakṛtimokṣopāyam amānitvādikaṃ cāgamya ya ācaranti, te nirmuktabandhāḥ svena rūpeṇāvasthitam anavacchinnajñānalakṣaṇam ātmānaṃ prāpnuvantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Those who, through the eye in the form of knowledge concerning discrimination — in the manner described — know the difference, the distinction, between the field and the knower of the field; and [who know] the liberation of beings from <s>Prakṛti</s> — they go to the Supreme, they attain the self freed from bondage. That by which one is liberated is <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation); <s>mokṣa</s> means the means of liberation, i.e., the qualities beginning with humility and the like. Those who, through the knowledge described that pertains to the discrimination of the field and the knower of the field, know their distinction, and who also adopt the means of liberation from <s>Prakṛti</s> — beginning with humility and the like — that has taken the form of beings, and who practice accordingly: they attain the self as it truly is, freed from bondage, characterized by unlimited knowledge. This is the meaning. ||

children.text: evam uktena prakāreṇa kṣetra-kṣetra-jñayor antaraṃ viśeṣaṃ viveka-viṣaya-jñāna-ākhyena cakṣuṣā ye viduḥ, bhūta-prakṛti-mokṣaṃ ca, te paraṃ yānti nirmukta-bandham ātmānaṃ prāpnuvanti / mokṣyate 'nena iti mokṣaḥ, amānitva-ādikaṃ mokṣa-sādhanam ity-arthaḥ; kṣetra-kṣetra-jñayor viveka-viṣayeṇa uktena jñānena tayor vivekaṃ viditvā bhūta-ākāra-pariṇata-prakṛti-mokṣa-upāyam amānitva-ādikaṃ cā agamya ya ācaranti, te nirmukta-bandhāḥ svena rūpeṇa avasthitam anavacchinna-jñāna-lakṣaṇam ātmānaṃ prāpnuvanti ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: trayodaśe prakṛtipuruṣayor anyānyasaṃsṛṣṭayoḥ svarūpayāthātmayaṃ vijñāya amānitvādibhiḥ bhagavadbhaktyanugṛhītair bandhān mucyata ity uktam / tatra bandhahetuḥ pūrvapūrvasattvādiguṇamayasukhādisaṅga iti cābhihitam, "kāraṇaṃ guṇasaṅgo 'sya sadasadyonijanmasu" iti / athedānīṃ guṇānāṃ bandhahetutāprakāraḥ, guṇanivartanaprakāraś cocyate /
body.translated_text: In the thirteenth [chapter], having understood the true nature of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> that are mutually conjoined, one is freed from bondage through the qualities beginning with humility and the like, graced by devotion to the Lord — this was stated. Therein, it was also stated that the cause of bondage is the attachment to pleasure and the like that consist of the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the rest from previous [births]: 'the cause of his births in good and evil wombs is the attachment to the <s>guṇas</s>.' Now, the manner in which the <s>guṇas</s> cause bondage, and the manner of transcending the <s>guṇas</s>, are stated.

children.text: trayo-daśe prakṛti-puruṣayor anya-anya-saṃsṛṣṭayoḥ sva-rūpa-yāthātmayaṃ vijñāya amānitva-ādibhiḥ bhagavad-bhakty-anugṛhītair bandhān mucyata ity uktam / tatra bandha-hetuḥ pūrva-pūrva-sattva-ādi-guṇa-maya-sukha-ādi-saṅga iti ca abhihitam, "kāraṇaṃ guṇa-saṅgo 'sya sad-asad-yoni-janmasu" iti / atha idānīṃ guṇānāṃ bandha-hetutā-prakāraḥ, guṇa-nivartana-prakāraś ca ucyate /
paraṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṃ jñānam uttamam |
children.translated_text: 'I shall declare again the supreme knowledge, the best of all knowledges,' |

children.text: yaj jñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṃ siddhim ito gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'knowing which, all the sages have gone from here to the highest perfection.' ||

children.text: paraṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi jñānānāṃ jñānam uttamam |
yaj jñātvā munayaḥ sarve parāṃ siddhim ito gatāḥ ||

body.text: param pūrvoktād anyat prakṛtipuruṣāntargatam eva sattvādiguṇaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi / tac ca jñānaṃ sarveṣāṃ prakṛtipuruṣaviṣayajñānānām uttamam / yaj jñānaṃ jñātvā sarve munayas tan mananaśīlāḥ itaḥ saṃsārabandhāt parāṃ siddhiṃ gatāḥ parāṃ pariśuddhātmasvarūpaprāptirūpāṃ siddhim avāptāḥ //
body.translated_text: I shall declare again another knowledge — pertaining to <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> but concerning the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the rest — that is supreme, i.e., different from what was previously stated. And that knowledge is the best of all knowledges pertaining to <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>. Knowing which knowledge, all the sages — those given to contemplation — have gone from here, from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>, to the highest perfection — have attained the highest perfection in the form of the realization of the supremely pure essential nature of the self. ||

children.text: param pūrva-uktād anyat prakṛti-puruṣa-antargatam eva sattva-ādi-guṇa-viṣayaṃ jñānaṃ bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi / tac ca jñānaṃ sarveṣāṃ prakṛti-puruṣa-viṣaya-jñānānām uttamam / yaj jñānaṃ jñātvā sarve munayas tan manana-śīlāḥ itaḥ saṃsāra-bandhāt parāṃ siddhiṃ gatāḥ parāṃ pariśuddha-ātma-sva-rūpa-prāpti-rūpāṃ siddhim avāptāḥ //

body.text: punar api taj jñānaṃ phalena viśinaṣṭi --
body.translated_text: He further distinguishes that knowledge by its fruit:

children.text: punar api taj jñānaṃ phalena viśinaṣṭi ---
idaṃ jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having resorted to this knowledge, having attained a state similar to Mine,' |

children.text: sarge 'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca ||
children.translated_text: 'they are not born even at creation, nor do they suffer at dissolution.' ||

children.text: idaṃ jñānam upāśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ |
sarge 'pi na upajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca ||

body.text: idam vakṣyamāṇaṃ jñānam upaśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ matsāmyaṃ prāptāḥ, sarge 'pi nopajāyante -- na sṛjikarmatāṃ bhajante; pralaye na vyathanti ca -- na ca saṃhṛtikarmatām //
body.translated_text: Having resorted to this knowledge that will be stated, having attained a state similar to Mine — having reached equality with Me — they are not born even at creation: they do not become the objects of the act of creation. Nor do they suffer at dissolution: they do not become the objects of the act of dissolution either. ||

children.text: idam vakṣyamāṇaṃ jñānam upaśritya mama sādharmyam āgatāḥ mat-sāmyaṃ prāptāḥ, sarge 'pi na upajāyante --- na sṛji-karmatāṃ bhajante; pralaye na vyathanti ca --- na ca saṃhṛti-karmatām //

body.text: atha prākṛtānāṃ guṇānāṃ bandhahetutāprakāraṃ vaktuṃ sarvasya bhūtajātasya prakṛtipuruṣasaṃsargajatvaṃ "yāvat saṃjāyate kiñcit" ity anenoktaṃ bhagavatā svenaiva kṛtam ity āha --
body.translated_text: Now, to state the manner in which the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>Prakṛti</s> cause bondage, He says that the fact that every class of beings is born from the conjunction of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — as stated in 'whatever being is born' — was brought about by the Lord Himself:

children.text: atha prākṛtānāṃ guṇānāṃ bandha-hetutā-prakāraṃ vaktuṃ sarvasya bhūta-jātasya prakṛti-puruṣa-saṃsarga-jatvaṃ "yāvat saṃjāyate kiñcit" ity anena uktaṃ bhagavatā svena eva kṛtam ity āha ---
mama yonir mahadbrahma tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmy aham |
children.translated_text: 'My womb is the great <s>Brahman</s>; in that I place the seed.' |

children.text: saṃbhavas sarvabhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata ||
children.translated_text: 'The birth of all beings comes from that, O <s>Bhārata</s>.' ||

children.text: mama yonir mahad-brahma tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmy aham |
saṃbhavas sarva-bhūtānāṃ tato bhavati bhārata ||

body.text:
kṛtsnasya jagato yonibhūtaṃ mama mahadbrahma yat, tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmy aham; "bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhir eva ca / ahaṅkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā // apareyam" iti nirdiṣṭā acetanaprakṛtiḥ mahadahaṅkārādivikārāṇāṃ kāraṇatayā mahadbrahmety ucyate / śrutāv api kvacit prakṛtir api brahmeti nirdiśyate, "yas sarvajñas sarvavid yasya jñānamayaṃ tapaḥ / tasmād etad brahma nāma rūpam annaṃ ca jāyate" iti; "itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām / jīvabhūtām" iti cetanapuñjarūpā yā parā prakṛtir nirdiṣṭā, seha sakalaprāṇibījatayā garbhaśabdenocyate / tasmin acetane yonibhūte mahati brahmaṇi cetanapuñjarūpaṃ garbhaṃ dadhāmi; acetanaprakṛtyā bhogakṣetrabhūtayā bhoktṛvargapuñjabhūtāṃ cetanaprakṛtiṃ saṃyojayāmītyarthaḥ
/ tataḥ tasmāt prakṛtidvayasaṃyogān matsaṃkalpakṛtāt sarvabhūtānāṃ brahmādistambaparyantānāṃ saṃbhavo bhavati //
body.translated_text: My great <s>Brahman</s>, which is the womb of the entire universe — in that I place the seed. The non-conscious <s>Prakṛti</s>, designated as 'earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and ego — this is My eightfold <s>Prakṛti</s>, the lower one' — is called the 'great <s>Brahman</s>' because it is the cause of the modifications such as <s>mahat</s>, <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, and the like. In <s>śruti</s> also, <s>Prakṛti</s> is sometimes designated as <s>Brahman</s>: 'From Him — who is omniscient, whose austerity consists of knowledge — this <s>Brahman</s>, name, form, and food are born.' The higher <s>Prakṛti</s>, designated as 'But know My other <s>Prakṛti</s>, the higher one, which has become the living beings' — that aggregate of conscious beings — is here called the 'seed' (<s>garbha</s>) because it is the seed of all living beings. In that non-conscious [<s>Prakṛti</s>] which is the womb, the great <s>Brahman</s>, I place the seed in the form of the aggregate of conscious beings — meaning: I conjoin the conscious <s>Prakṛti</s>, which is the aggregate of experiencers, with the non-conscious <s>Prakṛti</s>, which is the field of experience. From that — from the conjunction of the two <s>Prakṛtis</s> brought about by My will — comes the birth of all beings, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass. ||

children.text:
kṛtsnasya jagato yoni-bhūtaṃ mama mahad-brahma yat, tasmin garbhaṃ dadhāmy aham; "bhūmir āpo 'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhir eva ca / ahaṅkāra iti iyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtir aṣṭadhā // apara īyam" iti nirdiṣṭā acetana-prakṛtiḥ mahad-ahaṅkāra-ādi-vikārāṇāṃ kāraṇatayā mahad-brahma ity ucyate / śrutāv api kvacit prakṛtir api brahma iti nirdiśyate, "yas sarva-jñas sarva-vid yasya jñāna-mayaṃ tapaḥ / tasmād etad brahma nāma rūpam annaṃ ca jāyate" iti; "itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām / jīva-bhūtām" iti cetana-puñja-rūpā yā parā prakṛtir nirdiṣṭā, sa īha sakala-prāṇi-bījatayā garbha-śabdena ucyate / tasmin acetane yoni-bhūte mahati brahmaṇi cetana-puñja-rūpaṃ garbhaṃ dadhāmi; acetana-prakṛtyā bhoga-kṣetra-bhūtayā bhoktṛ-varga-puñja-bhūtāṃ cetana-prakṛtiṃ saṃyojayāmi ity-arthaḥ
/ tataḥ tasmāt prakṛti-dvaya-saṃyogān mat-saṃkalpa-kṛtāt sarva-bhūtānāṃ brahmā-ādi-stamba-paryantānāṃ saṃbhavo bhavati //

body.text: kāryāvastho 'pi cidacitprakṛtisaṃsargo mayaiva kṛta ity āha --
body.translated_text: He says that even in the state of effects, the conjunction of the conscious and non-conscious <s>Prakṛtis</s> is brought about by Himself:

children.text: kārya-avastho 'pi cid-acit-prakṛti-saṃsargo maya aiva kṛta ity āha ---
sarvayoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ saṃbhavanti yāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'In all wombs, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, whatever forms come into being,' |

children.text: tāsāṃ brahma mahad yonir ahaṃ bījapradaḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: 'for all of them the great <s>Brahman</s> is the womb, and I am the seed-giving father.' ||

children.text: sarva-yoniṣu kaunteya mūrtayaḥ saṃbhavanti yāḥ |
tāsāṃ brahma mahad yonir ahaṃ bīja-pradaḥ pitā ||

body.text: sarvāsu devagandharvayakṣarākṣasamanuṣyapaśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpādiṣu yoniṣu tattanmūrtayo yāḥ saṃbhavanti jāyante, tāsāṃ brahma mahad yoniḥ kāraṇam; mayā saṃyojitacetanavargā mahadādiviśeṣāntāvasthā prakṛtiḥ kāraṇam ityarthaḥ / ahaṃ bījapradaḥ pitā -- tatra tatra ca tattatkarmānuguṇyena cetanavargasya saṃyojakaś cāham ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: In all wombs — gods, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, humans, animals, beasts, birds, reptiles, and the like — whatever respective forms come into being, for all of them the great <s>Brahman</s> is the womb, the cause — meaning: <s>Prakṛti</s>, in the state from <s>mahat</s> to the specific elements, with the conscious beings conjoined by Me, is the cause. I am the seed-giving father — meaning: and I am the one who conjoins the conscious beings with their respective [bodies] in accordance with their respective <s>karma</s> in each case. ||

children.text: sarvāsu deva-gandharva-yakṣa-rākṣasa-manuṣya-paśu-mṛga-pakṣi-sarīsṛpa-ādiṣu yoniṣu tat-tan-mūrtayo yāḥ saṃbhavanti jāyante, tāsāṃ brahma mahad yoniḥ kāraṇam; mayā saṃyojita-cetana-vargā mahad-ādi-viśeṣa-anta-avasthā prakṛtiḥ kāraṇam ity-arthaḥ / ahaṃ bīja-pradaḥ pitā --- tatra tatra ca tat-tat-karma-anuguṇyena cetana-vargasya saṃyojakaś ca aham ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: evaṃ sargādau prācīnakarmavaśād acitsaṃsargeṇa devādiyoniṣu jātānāṃ punaḥ punar devādibhāvena janmahetum āha --
body.translated_text: Thus, He states the cause of the repeated birth in the forms of gods and the like, for those who, at the beginning of creation, are born in the wombs of gods and the like due to the force of prior <s>karma</s> conjoined with non-conscious [matter]:

children.text: evaṃ sarga-ādau prācīna-karma-vaśād acit-saṃsargeṇa deva-ādi-yoniṣu jātānāṃ punaḥ punar deva-ādi-bhāvena janma-hetum āha ---
sattvaṃ rajas tama iti guṇāḥ prakṛtisaṃbhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s>' |

children.text: nibadhnanti mahābāho dehe dehinam avyayam ||
children.translated_text: 'bind the imperishable embodied one in the body, O mighty-armed.' ||

children.text: sattvaṃ rajas tama iti guṇāḥ prakṛti-saṃbhavāḥ |
nibadhnanti mahā-bāho dehe dehinam avyayam ||

body.text: sattvarajastamāṃsi trayo guṇāḥ prakṛteḥ svarūpānubandhinaḥ svabhāvaviśeṣāḥ prakāśādikāryaikanirūpaṇīyāḥ prakṛtyavasthāyām anudbhūtāḥ tadvikāreṣu mahadādiṣu udbhūtāḥ mahadādiviśeṣāntair ārabdhadevamanuṣyādidehasaṃbandhinam enaṃ dehinam, avyayam svato guṇasaṃbandhānarhaṃ dehe vartamānaṃ nibadhnanti, dehe vartamānatvopādhinā nibadhnantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — these three <s>guṇas</s> are specific modes that are inseparable from the essential nature of <s>Prakṛti</s>, definable solely through their respective effects such as illumination and the like; in the state of <s>Prakṛti</s> [before creation] they are unmanifest, and in its modifications — <s>mahat</s> and the like — they become manifest. They bind this embodied one (<s>dehin</s>), who is connected with the body constituted from <s>mahat</s> through to the specific elements, who is imperishable — by his own nature unfit for conjunction with the <s>guṇas</s> — in the body. The meaning is: they bind him through the condition of being in the body. ||

children.text: sattva-rajas-tamāṃsi trayo guṇāḥ prakṛteḥ sva-rūpa-anubandhinaḥ sva-bhāva-viśeṣāḥ prakāśa-ādi-kārya-eka-nirūpaṇīyāḥ prakṛty-avasthāyām anudbhūtāḥ tad-vikāreṣu mahad-ādiṣu udbhūtāḥ mahad-ādi-viśeṣa-antair ārabdha-deva-manuṣya-ādi-deha-saṃbandhinam enaṃ dehinam, avyayam svato guṇa-saṃbandha-anarhaṃ dehe vartamānaṃ nibadhnanti, dehe vartamānatva-upādhinā nibadhnanti ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: sattvarajastamasām ākāraṃ bandhanaprakāraṃ cāha --
body.translated_text: He states the form of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, and the manner in which they cause bondage:

children.text: sattva-rajas-tamasām ākāraṃ bandhana-prakāraṃ cā aha ---
tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvāt prakāśakam anāmayam |
children.translated_text: 'Of these, <s>sattva</s>, being pure, is illuminating and free from affliction.'

children.text: sukhasaṅgena badhnāti jñānasaṅgena cānagha ||
children.translated_text: 'It binds through attachment to happiness and attachment to knowledge, O sinless one.' ||

children.text: tatra sattvaṃ nirmalatvāt prakāśakam anāmayam |
sukha-saṅgena badhnāti jñāna-saṅgena ca anagha ||

body.text: tatra sattvarajastamas tu sattvasya svarūpam īdṛśam nirmalatvāt prakāśakam; prakāśasukhāvaraṇasvabhāvarahitatā nirmalatvam; prakāśasukhajananaikāntasvabhāvatayā prakāśasukhahetubhūtam ityarthaḥ / prakāśaḥ vastuyāthātmyāvabodhaḥ / anāmayam āmayākhyaṃ kāryaṃ na vidyata ity anāmayam; arogatāhetur ityarthaḥ / eṣa sattvākhyo guṇo dehinam enaṃ sukhasaṅgena jñānasaṅgena ca badhnāti puruṣasya sukhasaṅgaṃ jñānasaṅgaṃ ca janayatītyarthaḥ/ jñānasukhayos saṅge hi jāte tatsādhaneṣu laukikavaidikeṣu pravartate; tataś ca tatphalānubhavasādhanabhūtāsu yoniṣu jāyata iti sattvaṃ sukhajñānasaṅgadvāreṇa puruṣaṃ badhnāti / jñānasukhajananaṃ punar api tayos saṅgajananaṃ ca sattvam ity uktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: Among these — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — the nature of <s>sattva</s> is thus: due to its purity, it is illuminating. Purity means the absence of the nature that obscures illumination and happiness. Being exclusively of the nature that produces illumination and happiness, it is the cause of illumination and happiness — this is the meaning. Illumination (<s>prakāśa</s>) is the comprehension of the true nature of things. Free from affliction (<s>anāmaya</s>) — there is no effect called affliction — meaning: it is the cause of freedom from disease. This <s>guṇa</s> called <s>sattva</s> binds the embodied self through attachment to happiness and attachment to knowledge — meaning: it produces in the person attachment to happiness and attachment to knowledge. For when attachment to knowledge and happiness arises, one engages in the worldly and Vedic means for them; and from that, one is born in wombs that serve as means for experiencing the fruits thereof. Thus <s>sattva</s> binds the person through the door of attachment to happiness and knowledge. That <s>sattva</s> produces knowledge and happiness, and again produces attachment to them — this is what is being stated. //

children.text: tatra sattva-rajas-tamas tu sattvasya sva-rūpam īdṛśam nirmalatvāt prakāśakam; prakāśa-sukha-āvaraṇa-sva-bhāva-rahitatā nirmalatvam; prakāśa-sukha-janana-eka-anta-sva-bhāvatayā prakāśa-sukha-hetu-bhūtam ity-arthaḥ / prakāśaḥ vastu-yāthātmya-avabodhaḥ / anāmayam āmaya-ākhyaṃ kāryaṃ na vidyata ity anāmayam; arogatā-hetur ity-arthaḥ / eṣa sattva-ākhyo guṇo dehinam enaṃ sukha-saṅgena jñāna-saṅgena ca badhnāti puruṣasya sukha-saṅgaṃ jñāna-saṅgaṃ ca janayati ity-arthaḥ/ jñāna-sukhayos saṅge hi jāte tat-sādhaneṣu laukika-vaidikeṣu pravartate; tataś ca tat-phala-anubhava-sādhana-bhūtāsu yoniṣu jāyata iti sattvaṃ sukha-jñāna-saṅga-dvāreṇa puruṣaṃ badhnāti / jñāna-sukha-jananaṃ punar api tayos saṅga-jananaṃ ca sattvam ity uktaṃ bhavati //
rajo rāgātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam |
children.translated_text: 'Know <s>rajas</s> to be of the nature of passion, the source of craving and attachment.'

children.text: tan nibadhnāti kaunteya karmasaṅgena dehinam ||
children.translated_text: 'It binds the embodied one through attachment to action, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>.' ||

children.text: rajo rāga-ātmakaṃ viddhi tṛṣṇā-saṅga-samudbhavam |
tan nibadhnāti kaunteya karma-saṅgena dehinam ||
