body.text: rajo rāgātmakam rāgahetubhūtam / rāgaḥ yoṣitpuruṣayor anyānyaspṛhā / tṛṇāsaṅgasamudbhavam tṛṣṇāsaṅgayor udbhavasthānam -- tṛṣṇāsaṅgahetubhūtam ityarthaḥ / tṛṣṇā śabdādisarvaviṣayaspṛhā; saṅgaḥ putramitrādiṣu saṃbandhiṣu saṃśleṣaspṛhā / tad rajaḥ dehinaṃ karmasu kriyāsu spṛhājananadvāreṇa nibadhnāti; kriyāsu hi spṛhayā yāḥ kriyā ārabhate dehī, tāś ca puṇyapāparūpā iti tatphalānubhavasādhanabhūtāsu yoniṣu janmahetavo bhavanti / ataḥ karmasaṅgadvāreṇa rajo dehinaṃ nibadhnāti / tad evaṃ rajo rāgatṛṣṇāsaṅgahetuḥ karmasaṅgahetuś cety uktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: <s>Rajas</s> is of the nature of passion (<s>rāga</s>) — it is the cause of passion. Passion is the mutual desire between woman and man. It is the source of craving and attachment — the place of origin of craving and attachment, meaning: it is the cause of craving and attachment. Craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is the desire for all objects such as sound and the like. Attachment (<s>saṅga</s>) is the desire for intimate connection with relatives such as sons, friends, and the like. That <s>rajas</s> binds the embodied one through the door of attachment to actions — activities: it binds through generating desire for activities. For when the embodied one undertakes activities through desire for them, those activities, being of the nature of merit and demerit, become the causes of birth in wombs that serve as means for experiencing their fruits. Therefore, <s>rajas</s> binds the embodied one through the door of attachment to action. Thus it is stated that <s>rajas</s> is the cause of passion, craving, and attachment, and is also the cause of attachment to action. //

children.text: rajo rāga-ātmakam rāga-hetu-bhūtam / rāgaḥ yoṣit-puruṣayor anya-anya-spṛhā / tṛṇā-saṅga-samudbhavam tṛṣṇā-saṅgayor udbhava-sthānam --- tṛṣṇā-saṅga-hetu-bhūtam ity-arthaḥ / tṛṣṇā śabda-ādi-sarva-viṣaya-spṛhā; saṅgaḥ putra-mitra-ādiṣu saṃbandhiṣu saṃśleṣa-spṛhā / tad rajaḥ dehinaṃ karmasu kriyāsu spṛhā-janana-dvāreṇa nibadhnāti; kriyāsu hi spṛhayā yāḥ kriyā ārabhate dehī, tāś ca puṇya-pāpa-rūpā iti tat-phala-anubhava-sādhana-bhūtāsu yoniṣu janma-hetavo bhavanti / ataḥ karma-saṅga-dvāreṇa rajo dehinaṃ nibadhnāti / tad evaṃ rajo rāga-tṛṣṇā-saṅga-hetuḥ karma-saṅga-hetuś ca ity uktaṃ bhavati //
tamas tv ajñānajaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarvadehinām |
children.translated_text: 'But know <s>tamas</s> to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings.'

children.text: pramādālasyanidrābhis tan nibadhnāti bhārata ||
children.translated_text: 'It binds through heedlessness, indolence, and sleep, O <s>Bhārata</s>.' ||

children.text: tamas tv ajñāna-jaṃ viddhi mohanaṃ sarva-dehinām |
pramāda-ālasya-nidrābhis tan nibadhnāti bhārata ||

body.text: jñānād anyad iha ajñānam abhipretam / jñānaṃ vastuyathātmyāvabodhaḥ; tasmād anyat tadviparyayajñānam / tamas tu vastuyāthātmyaviaparītaviṣayajñānajam / mohanaṃ sarvadehinām / moho viparyayajñānam; viparyayajñānahetur ityarthaḥ / tat tamaḥ pramādālasyanidrāhetutayā taddvāreṇa dehinaṃ nibadhnāti / pramādaḥ kartavyāt karmaṇo 'nyatra pravṛttihetubhūtam anavadhānam / ālasyam karmasv anārambhasvabhāvaḥ; stabdhateti yāvat / puruṣasyendriyapravartanaśrāntyā sarvendriyapravartanoparatir nidrā; tatra bāhyendriyapravartanoparamaḥ svapnaḥ; manaso 'py uparatiḥ suṣuptiḥ //
body.translated_text: What is intended here by 'ignorance' is something other than knowledge. Knowledge is the comprehension of things as they truly are; what is other than that is erroneous knowledge — the opposite of that. <s>Tamas</s> is born of knowledge whose object is the opposite of the true nature of things. It deludes all embodied beings. Delusion (<s>moha</s>) is erroneous knowledge; the meaning is: it is the cause of erroneous knowledge. That <s>tamas</s> binds the embodied one through being the cause of heedlessness, indolence, and sleep — through their door. Heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>) is inattentiveness that causes engagement in things other than what ought to be done. Indolence (<s>ālasya</s>) is the nature of not undertaking actions — torpor, in other words. Sleep (<s>nidrā</s>) is the cessation of all sense activity due to the fatigue of the person's impelling of the senses. Therein, the cessation of external sense activity is dreaming; the cessation of the mind too is deep sleep. //

children.text: jñānād anyad iha ajñānam abhipretam / jñānaṃ vastu-yathātmya-avabodhaḥ; tasmād anyat tad-viparyaya-jñānam / tamas tu vastu-yāthātmya-viaparīta-viṣaya-jñāna-jam / mohanaṃ sarva-dehinām / moho viparyaya-jñānam; viparyaya-jñāna-hetur ity-arthaḥ / tat tamaḥ pramāda-ālasya-nidrā-hetutayā tad-dvāreṇa dehinaṃ nibadhnāti / pramādaḥ kartavyāt karmaṇo 'nyatra pravṛtti-hetu-bhūtam anavadhānam / ālasyam karmasv anārambha-sva-bhāvaḥ; stabdhata īti yāvat / puruṣasya indriya-pravartana-śrāntyā sarva-indriya-pravartana-uparatir nidrā; tatra bāhya-indriya-pravartana-uparamaḥ svapnaḥ; manaso 'py uparatiḥ suṣuptiḥ //

body.text: sattvādīnāṃ bandhadvārabhūteṣu pradhānāny āha --
body.translated_text: He states the predominant doors of bondage for <s>sattva</s> and the others —

children.text: sattva-ādīnāṃ bandha-dvāra-bhūteṣu pradhānāny āha ---
sattvaṃ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata |
children.translated_text: '<s>Sattva</s> causes attachment to happiness; <s>rajas</s> to action, O <s>Bhārata</s>.'

children.text: jñānam āvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayaty uta ||
children.translated_text: 'But <s>tamas</s>, having veiled knowledge, causes attachment to heedlessness.' ||

children.text: sattvaṃ sukhe sañjayati rajaḥ karmaṇi bhārata |
jñānam āvṛtya tu tamaḥ pramāde sañjayaty uta ||

body.text: sattvaṃ sukhasaṅgapradhānam; rajaḥ karmasaṅgapradhānam; tamas tu vastuyāthātmyajñānam āvṛtya viparītajñānahetutayā kartavyaviparītapravṛttisaṅgapradhānam //
body.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> has attachment to happiness as its predominant [effect]. <s>Rajas</s> has attachment to action as its predominant [effect]. But <s>tamas</s>, having veiled the knowledge of things as they truly are, has attachment to activity that is the opposite of what ought to be done as its predominant [effect], by being the cause of erroneous knowledge. //

children.text: sattvaṃ sukha-saṅga-pradhānam; rajaḥ karma-saṅga-pradhānam; tamas tu vastu-yāthātmya-jñānam āvṛtya viparīta-jñāna-hetutayā kartavya-viparīta-pravṛtti-saṅga-pradhānam //

body.text: dehākārapariṇatāyāḥ prakṛteḥ svarūpānubandhinaḥ sattvādayo guṇāḥ; te ca svarūpānubandhitvena sarvadā sarve vartante iti parasparaviruddhaṃ kāryaṃ kathaṃ janayantīty atra āha --
body.translated_text: The <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the others — are inherent in <s>Prakṛti</s> which has transformed into the form of the body, and by virtue of their being inherent, they are always present in all [bodies]. Then how do they produce mutually contradictory effects? To this he says —

children.text: deha-ākāra-pariṇatāyāḥ prakṛteḥ sva-rūpa-anubandhinaḥ sattva-ādayo guṇāḥ; te ca sva-rūpa-anubandhitvena sarvadā sarve vartante iti paras-para-viruddhaṃ kāryaṃ kathaṃ janayanti ity atra āha ---
rajas tamaś cābhibhūya sattvaṃ bhavati bhārata |
children.translated_text: '<s>Sattva</s> prevails, having overpowered <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>, O <s>Bhārata</s>;'

children.text: rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaś caiva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajas tathā ||
children.translated_text: '<s>rajas</s> [prevails, having overpowered] <s>sattva</s> and <s>tamas</s>; and <s>tamas</s> [prevails, having overpowered] <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>, likewise.' ||

children.text: rajas tamaś ca abhibhūya sattvaṃ bhavati bhārata |
rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaś ca eva tamaḥ sattvaṃ rajas tathā ||

body.text: yady api sattvādyas trayaḥ prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭātmasvarūpānubandhinaḥ, tathāpi prācīnakarmavaśād dehāpy āyanabhūtāhāravaiṣamyāc ca sattvādayaḥ parasparasamudbhavābhibhavarūpeṇa vartante / rajastamasī kadācid abhibhūya sattvam udriktaṃ vartate; tathā tamassattve abhibhūya rajaḥ kadācit; kadācic ca rajassattve abhibhūya tamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Although the three — <s>sattva</s> and the others — are inherent in the essential nature of the self conjoined with <s>Prakṛti</s>, nevertheless, due to the force of prior <s>karmas</s> and due to the inequality of food and the like that serve as means of bodily sustenance, <s>sattva</s> and the others function in the manner of mutual arising and mutual overpowering. Sometimes <s>sattva</s> prevails, having overpowered <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>. Likewise, sometimes <s>rajas</s>, having overpowered <s>tamas</s> and <s>sattva</s>. And sometimes <s>tamas</s>, having overpowered <s>rajas</s> and <s>sattva</s>. //

children.text: yady api sattva-ādyas trayaḥ prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭa-ātma-sva-rūpa-anubandhinaḥ, tatha āpi prācīna-karma-vaśād deha apy āyana-bhūta-āhāra-vaiṣamyāc ca sattva-ādayaḥ paras-para-samudbhava-abhibhava-rūpeṇa vartante / rajas-tamasī kadācid abhibhūya sattvam udriktaṃ vartate; tathā tamas-sattve abhibhūya rajaḥ kadācit; kadācic ca rajas-sattve abhibhūya tamaḥ //

body.text: tac ca kāryopalabhyaivāvagacched ity āha --
body.translated_text: And one should recognize that through the apprehension of its effects — he says —

children.text: tac ca kārya-upalabhya eva avagacched ity āha ---
sarvadvāreṣu dehe 'smin prakāśa upajāyate /
children.translated_text: 'When in all the gates of this body, illumination arises —'

children.text: jñānaṃ yadā tadā vidyād vivṛddhaṃ sattvam ity uta ||
children.translated_text: 'knowledge — then one should know that <s>sattva</s> has increased.' ||

children.text: sarva-dvāreṣu dehe 'smin prakāśa upajāyate /
jñānaṃ yadā tadā vidyād vivṛddhaṃ sattvam ity uta ||

body.text: sarveṣu cakṣurādiṣu jñānadvāreṣu yadā vastuyāthātmyaprakāśe jñānam upajāyate, tadā tasmin dehe sattvaṃ pravṛddham iti vidyāt //
body.translated_text: When in all the gates of knowledge — the eyes and the other [senses] — knowledge in the form of the illumination of things as they truly are arises, then one should know that <s>sattva</s> has increased in that body. //

children.text: sarveṣu cakṣur-ādiṣu jñāna-dvāreṣu yadā vastu-yāthātmya-prakāśe jñānam upajāyate, tadā tasmin dehe sattvaṃ pravṛddham iti vidyāt //
lobhaḥ pravṛttir ārambhaḥ karmaṇām aśamaḥ spṛhā /
children.translated_text: 'Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness, desire —'

children.text: rajasy etāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharatarṣabha //
children.translated_text: 'these arise when <s>rajas</s> has increased, O bull of the <s>Bhāratas</s>.' ||

children.text: lobhaḥ pravṛttir ārambhaḥ karmaṇām aśamaḥ spṛhā /
rajasy etāni jāyante vivṛddhe bharata-rṣabha //

body.text: lobhaḥ svakīyadravyasyātyāgaśīlatā; pravṛttiḥ prayojanam anuddiśyāpi calanasvabhāvātā; ārambhaḥ karmaṇām -- phalasādhanabhūtānāṃ karmaṇām ārambhaḥ; aśamaḥ indriyānuratiḥ; spṛhā -- viṣayecchā / etāni rajasi pravṛddhe jāyante / yadā lobhādayo vartante, tadā rajaḥ pravṛddham iti vidyād ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Greed (<s>lobha</s>) is the disposition of not giving away one's own possessions. Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is the nature of being restless even without any purpose in view. Undertaking of actions — the initiation of actions that are the means of obtaining results. Restlessness (<s>aśama</s>) — attachment to the senses. Desire (<s>spṛhā</s>) — longing for sense-objects. These arise when <s>rajas</s> has increased. The meaning is: when greed and the like are present, one should know that <s>rajas</s> has increased. //

children.text: lobhaḥ svakīya-dravyasya atyāga-śīlatā; pravṛttiḥ prayojanam anuddiśya api calana-sva-bhāvātā; ārambhaḥ karmaṇām --- phala-sādhana-bhūtānāṃ karmaṇām ārambhaḥ; aśamaḥ indriya-anuratiḥ; spṛhā --- viṣaya-icchā / etāni rajasi pravṛddhe jāyante / yadā lobha-ādayo vartante, tadā rajaḥ pravṛddham iti vidyād ity-arthaḥ //
aprakāśo 'pravṛttiś ca pramādo moha eva ca /
children.translated_text: 'Darkness, non-activity, heedlessness, and delusion itself —'

children.text: tamasy etāni jāyante vivṛddhe kurunandana //
children.translated_text: 'these arise when <s>tamas</s> has increased, O scion of the <s>Kurus</s>.' ||

children.text: aprakāśo 'pravṛttiś ca pramādo moha eva ca /
tamasy etāni jāyante vivṛddhe kuru-nandana //

body.text: aprakāśaḥ jñānānudayaḥ; apravṛttiś ca stabdhatā; pramādaḥ akāryapravṛttiphalam anavadhānam; mohaḥ viparītajñānam / etāni tamasi pravṛddhe jāyante / etais tamaḥ pravṛddham iti vidyāt //
body.translated_text: Darkness (<s>aprakāśa</s>) — the non-arising of knowledge. Non-activity (<s>apravṛtti</s>) — torpor. Heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>) — inattentiveness resulting in engagement in improper activities. Delusion (<s>moha</s>) — erroneous knowledge. These arise when <s>tamas</s> has increased. By these, one should know that <s>tamas</s> has increased. //

children.text: aprakāśaḥ jñāna-anudayaḥ; apravṛttiś ca stabdhatā; pramādaḥ akārya-pravṛtti-phalam anavadhānam; mohaḥ viparīta-jñānam / etāni tamasi pravṛddhe jāyante / etais tamaḥ pravṛddham iti vidyāt //
yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti dehabhṛt /
children.translated_text: 'When the embodied one meets dissolution while <s>sattva</s> has increased,'

children.text: tadottamavidāṃ lokān amalān pratipadyate //
children.translated_text: 'then he attains the pure worlds of the knowers of the highest.' ||

children.text: yadā sattve pravṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti deha-bhṛt /
tada ūttama-vidāṃ lokān amalān pratipadyate //

body.text: yadā sattvaṃ pravṛddhaṃ tadā, sattve pravṛddhe dehabhṛt pralayaṃ maraṇaṃ yāti cet, uttamavidām uttamatattvavidām ātmayāthātmyavidām lokān samūhān amalān malarahitān -- ajñānarahitān, pratipadyate prāpnoti / sattve pravṛddhe tu mṛtaḥ ātmavidāṃ kuleṣu janitvā ātmayāthātmyajñānasādhaneṣu puṇyakarmasv adhikarotīty uktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: When <s>sattva</s> has increased at that time — if the embodied one meets dissolution, i.e., death, while <s>sattva</s> has increased — he attains the worlds, the communities, of the knowers of the highest — of those who know the highest truth, who know the true nature of the self — the pure [worlds], free from impurity, free from ignorance. What is stated is: one who dies while <s>sattva</s> has increased is born in the families of those who know the true nature of the self, and therein engages in the meritorious actions that serve as means for the knowledge of the self's true nature. //

children.text: yadā sattvaṃ pravṛddhaṃ tadā, sattve pravṛddhe deha-bhṛt pralayaṃ maraṇaṃ yāti cet, uttama-vidām uttama-tattva-vidām ātma-yāthātmya-vidām lokān samūhān amalān mala-rahitān --- ajñāna-rahitān, pratipadyate prāpnoti / sattve pravṛddhe tu mṛtaḥ ātma-vidāṃ kuleṣu janitvā ātma-yāthātmya-jñāna-sādhaneṣu puṇya-karmasv adhikaroti ity uktaṃ bhavati //

body.text: rajasi pralayaṃ gatvā karmasaṅgiṣu jāyate /
body.translated_text: 'Having met dissolution in <s>rajas</s>, one is born among those attached to action.'

children.text: rajasi pralayaṃ gatvā karma-saṅgiṣu jāyate /

body.text: rajasi pravṛddhe maraṇaṃ prāpya phalārthaṃ karma kurvatāṃ kuleṣu jāyate; tatra janitvā svargādiphalasādhanakarmasv adhikarotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Having died while <s>rajas</s> has increased, one is born in the families of those who perform actions for the sake of results. Having been born there, one engages in the actions that are the means for results such as heaven and the like — this is the meaning. //

children.text: rajasi pravṛddhe maraṇaṃ prāpya phala-arthaṃ karma kurvatāṃ kuleṣu jāyate; tatra janitvā svarga-ādi-phala-sādhana-karmasv adhikaroti ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: tathā pralīnas tamasi mūḍhayoniṣu jāyate //
body.translated_text: 'Likewise, one who dies in <s>tamas</s> is born in the wombs of the deluded.' ||

children.text: tathā pralīnas tamasi mūḍha-yoniṣu jāyate //

body.text: tathā tamasi pravṛddhe mṛtā mūḍhayoniṣu śvasūkarādiyoniṣu jāyate / sakalapuruṣārthārambhānarho jāyata ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Likewise, one who has died while <s>tamas</s> has increased is born in the wombs of the deluded — in the wombs of dogs, pigs, and the like. The meaning is: one is born unworthy of undertaking any human goal whatsoever. //

children.text: tathā tamasi pravṛddhe mṛtā mūḍha-yoniṣu śva-sūkara-ādi-yoniṣu jāyate / sakala-puruṣa-artha-ārambha-anarho jāyata ity-arthaḥ //
karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyāhuḥ sāttvikaṃ nirmalaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: 'The fruit of good action, they say, is <s>sāttvika</s> — pure.'

children.text: rajasas tu phalaṃ duḥkham ajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam //
children.translated_text: 'The fruit of <s>rajas</s> is suffering; the fruit of <s>tamas</s> is ignorance.' ||

children.text: karmaṇaḥ sukṛtasyā ahuḥ sāttvikaṃ nirmalaṃ phalam /
rajasas tu phalaṃ duḥkham ajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam //

body.text: evaṃ sattvapravṛddhau maraṇam upagamyātmavidāṃ kule jātenānuṣṭhitasya sukṛtasya phalābhisandhirahitasya madārādhanarūpasya karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ punar api tato 'dhikasattvajanitaṃ nirmalaṃ duḥkhagandharahitaṃ bhavatīty āhuḥ sattvaguṇapariṇāmavidaḥ / antyakālapravṛddhasya rajasas tu phalaṃ phalasādhanakarmasaṅgikulajanmaphalābhisandhipūrvakakarmārambhatatphalānubhavapunarjanmarajovṛddhiphalābhisandhipūrvaka karmārambhaparamparārūpaṃ sāṃsārikaduḥkhaprāyam evety āhuḥ tadguṇayāthātmyavidaḥ / ajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam -- evam antyakālapravṛddhasya tamasaḥ phalam ajñānaparamparārūpam //
body.translated_text: Thus, one who dies while <s>sattva</s> has increased, having been born in the family of knowers of the self and having performed good action — action free from desire for results and in the form of worshipping Me — its fruit, they say, the knowers of the transformations of the <s>sattva guṇa</s> say, is further increased <s>sattva</s>, pure, devoid of even a trace of suffering. But the fruit of <s>rajas</s> that has increased at the time of death — [is a chain of]: birth in the family of those attached to action as the means for results, undertaking of action preceded by desire for results, experiencing those fruits, rebirth, increase of <s>rajas</s>, undertaking of action preceded by desire for results — this perpetual cycle is predominantly <s>saṃsāric</s> suffering, say the knowers of the true nature of that <s>guṇa</s>. The fruit of <s>tamas</s> is ignorance — thus the fruit of <s>tamas</s> that has increased at the time of death is a perpetual chain of ignorance. //

children.text: evaṃ sattva-pravṛddhau maraṇam upagamyā atma-vidāṃ kule jātena anuṣṭhitasya sukṛtasya phala-abhisandhi-rahitasya mad-ārādhana-rūpasya karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ punar api tato 'dhika-sattva-janitaṃ nirmalaṃ duḥkha-gandha-rahitaṃ bhavati ity āhuḥ sattva-guṇa-pariṇāma-vidaḥ / antya-kāla-pravṛddhasya rajasas tu phalaṃ phala-sādhana-karma-saṅgi-kula-janma-phala-abhisandhi-pūrvaka-karma-ārambha-tat-phala-anubhava-punar-janma-rajo-vṛddhi-phala-abhisandhi-pūrvaka karma-ārambha-paramparā-rūpaṃ sāṃsārika-duḥkha-prāyam eva ity āhuḥ tad-guṇa-yāthātmya-vidaḥ / ajñānaṃ tamasaḥ phalam --- evam antya-kāla-pravṛddhasya tamasaḥ phalam ajñāna-paramparā-rūpam //

body.text: tad adhikasattvādijanitaṃ nirmalādiphalaṃ kim ity atrāha --
body.translated_text: As to what is the pure and other fruits generated by increased <s>sattva</s> and the rest — to this he says —

children.text: tad adhika-sattva-ādi-janitaṃ nirmala-ādi-phalaṃ kim ity atrā aha ---
sattvāt saṃjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca /
children.translated_text: 'From <s>sattva</s> arises knowledge, and from <s>rajas</s>, greed indeed;'

children.text: pramādamohau tamaso bhavato 'jñānam eva ca //
children.translated_text: 'from <s>tamas</s> arise heedlessness and delusion, and ignorance too.' ||

children.text: sattvāt saṃjāyate jñānaṃ rajaso lobha eva ca /
pramāda-mohau tamaso bhavato 'jñānam eva ca //

body.text: evaṃ paramparayā jātād adhikasattvād ātmayāthātmyāparokṣyarūpaṃ jñānaṃ jāyate / tathā pravṛddhād rajasaḥ svargādiphalalobho jāyate / tathā pravṛddhāc ca tamasaḥ pramādaḥ anavadhānanimittā asatkarmaṇi pravṛttiḥ; tataś ca mohaḥ viparītajñānam; tataś cādhikataraṃ tamaḥ; tataś cājñānam -- jñānābhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, from the increased <s>sattva</s> generated through [this] chain, knowledge in the form of direct realization of the true nature of the self arises. Likewise, from increased <s>rajas</s>, greed — the desire for results such as heaven and the like — arises. And from increased <s>tamas</s>, heedlessness — engagement in improper actions caused by inattentiveness; and from that, delusion — erroneous knowledge; from that, greater <s>tamas</s>; and from that, ignorance — the complete absence of knowledge. //

children.text: evaṃ paramparayā jātād adhika-sattvād ātma-yāthātmya-aparokṣya-rūpaṃ jñānaṃ jāyate / tathā pravṛddhād rajasaḥ svarga-ādi-phala-lobho jāyate / tathā pravṛddhāc ca tamasaḥ pramādaḥ anavadhāna-nimittā asat-karmaṇi pravṛttiḥ; tataś ca mohaḥ viparīta-jñānam; tataś ca adhikataraṃ tamaḥ; tataś ca ajñānam --- jñāna-abhāvaḥ //
ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattvasthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Those established in <s>sattva</s> go upward; the <s>rājasa</s> ones dwell in the middle;'

children.text: jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ //
children.translated_text: 'those established in the activity of the lowest <s>guṇa</s> — the <s>tāmasa</s> ones — go downward.' ||

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti sattva-sthā madhye tiṣṭhanti rājasāḥ /
jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtti-sthā adho gacchanti tāmasāḥ //

body.text: evam uktena prakāreṇa sattvasthā ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti -- krameṇa saṃsārabandhān mokṣaṃ gacchanti / rajasaḥ svargādiphalalobhakaratvād rājasāḥ phalasādhanabhutaṃ karmānuṣṭhāya tatphalam anubhūya punar api janitvā tad eva karmānutiṣṭhantīti madhye tiṣṭhanti / punarāvṛttirūpatayā duḥkhaprāyam eva tat / tāmasās tu jaghanyaguṇavṛttisthā uttarottaranikṛṣṭatamoguṇavṛttiṣu sthitā adho gacchanti -- antyatvam, tatas tiryaktvam, tataḥ krimikīṭādijanma, sthāvaratvam, tato 'pi gulmalatātvam, tataś ca śilākāṣṭhaloṣṭatṛṇāditvaṃ gacchantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the manner described, those established in <s>sattva</s> go upward — gradually they go toward liberation from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Because <s>rajas</s> causes greed for results such as heaven and the like, the <s>rājasa</s> ones, having performed the actions that serve as means for results, having experienced those results, being born again and performing those very same actions — thus they remain in the middle. That is predominantly suffering because of the nature of repeated return. But the <s>tāmasa</s> ones, established in the activity of the lowest <s>guṇa</s> — established in the activities of progressively inferior <s>tamas guṇa</s> — go downward: [they become] outcastes, from that animals, from that worms and insects, from that immobile beings, from that further bushes and creepers, and from that stones, wood, clods, grass, and the like — this is the meaning. //

children.text: evam uktena prakāreṇa sattva-sthā ūrdhvaṃ gacchanti --- krameṇa saṃsāra-bandhān mokṣaṃ gacchanti / rajasaḥ svarga-ādi-phala-lobha-karatvād rājasāḥ phala-sādhana-bhutaṃ karma-anuṣṭhāya tat-phalam anubhūya punar api janitvā tad eva karma-anutiṣṭhanti iti madhye tiṣṭhanti / punar-āvṛtti-rūpatayā duḥkha-prāyam eva tat / tāmasās tu jaghanya-guṇa-vṛtti-sthā uttara-uttara-nikṛṣṭa-tamo-guṇa-vṛttiṣu sthitā adho gacchanti --- antyatvam, tatas tiryaktvam, tataḥ krimi-kīṭa-ādi-janma, sthāvaratvam, tato 'pi gulma-latātvam, tataś ca śilā-kāṣṭha-loṣṭa-tṛṇa-āditvaṃ gacchanti ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: āhāraviśeṣaiḥ phalābhisandhirahitasukṛtaviśeṣaiś ca paramparayā pravardhitasattvānāṃ guṇātyayadvāreṇa ūrdhvagamanaprakāram āha --
body.translated_text: He states the manner of going upward — through the transcendence of the <s>guṇas</s> — for those whose <s>sattva</s> has been progressively increased through special food and meritorious actions free from desire for results —

children.text: āhāra-viśeṣaiḥ phala-abhisandhi-rahita-sukṛta-viśeṣaiś ca paramparayā pravardhita-sattvānāṃ guṇa-atyaya-dvāreṇa ūrdhva-gamana-prakāram āha ---
nānyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṃ yadā draṣṭānupaśyati /
children.translated_text: 'When the seer perceives no author other than the <s>guṇas</s>,'

children.text: guṇebhyaś ca paraṃ vetti madbhāvaṃ so 'dhigacchati //
children.translated_text: 'and knows that which is beyond the <s>guṇas</s> — he attains My state.' ||

children.text: na anyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāraṃ yadā draṣṭa ānupaśyati /
guṇebhyaś ca paraṃ vetti mad-bhāvaṃ so 'dhigacchati //

body.text: evaṃ sāttvikāhārasevayā phalābhisandhirahitabhagavadārādhanarūpakarmānuṣṭhānaiś ca rajastamasī sarvātmanābhibhūya utkṛṣṭasattvaniṣṭho yadāyaṃ guṇebhyo 'nyaṃ kartāraṃ nānupaśyati -- guṇā eva svānuguṇapravṛttiṣu kartāra iti paśyati; guṇebhyaś ca paraṃ vetti kartṛbhyo guṇebhyaś ca param anyam ātmānam akartāraṃ vetti -- sa madbhāvam adhigacchati mama yo bhāvas tam adhigacchati / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- "ātmanaḥ svataḥ pariśuddhasvabhāvasya pūrvapūrvakarmamūlaguṇasaṅganimittaṃ vividhakarmasu kartṛtvam; ātmā svatas tv akartā aparicchinnajñānaikākāraḥ" ity evam ātmānaṃ yadā paśyati, tadā madbhāvam adhigacchatīti //
body.translated_text: Thus, when this person, established in the highest <s>sattva</s> — through the cultivation of <s>sāttvika</s> food and the performance of worship of the Lord free from desire for results — having completely overpowered <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> in every way, sees no author other than the <s>guṇas</s> — perceives that the <s>guṇas</s> alone are the authors in their respective activities; and knows that which is beyond the <s>guṇas</s> — knows the self as other than the <s>guṇas</s> which are the authors, as a non-author — he attains My state, he attains that state which is Mine. What is being said is this: when he sees the self thus — 'For the self, whose nature is intrinsically pure, agency in the various actions is caused by the contact with the <s>guṇas</s> rooted in prior <s>karma</s>; the self, by its own nature, is a non-agent, of the single form of unlimited knowledge' — then he attains My state. //

children.text: evaṃ sāttvika-āhāra-sevayā phala-abhisandhi-rahita-bhagavad-ārādhana-rūpa-karma-anuṣṭhānaiś ca rajas-tamasī sarva-ātmana ābhibhūya utkṛṣṭa-sattva-niṣṭho yada āyaṃ guṇebhyo 'nyaṃ kartāraṃ na anupaśyati --- guṇā eva sva-anuguṇa-pravṛttiṣu kartāra iti paśyati; guṇebhyaś ca paraṃ vetti kartṛbhyo guṇebhyaś ca param anyam ātmānam akartāraṃ vetti --- sa mad-bhāvam adhigacchati mama yo bhāvas tam adhigacchati / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- "ātmanaḥ svataḥ pariśuddha-sva-bhāvasya pūrva-pūrva-karma-mūla-guṇa-saṅga-nimittaṃ vividha-karmasu kartṛtvam; ātmā svatas tv akartā aparicchinna-jñāna-eka-ākāraḥ" ity evam ātmānaṃ yadā paśyati, tadā mad-bhāvam adhigacchati iti //

body.text: kartṛbhyo guṇebhyo 'nyam akartāram ātmānaṃ paśyan bhagavadbhāvam adhigacchatīty uktam; sa bhagavadbhāvaḥ kīdṛśa ity ata āha --
body.translated_text: It was said that one who sees the self as a non-agent, other than the <s>guṇas</s> which are the agents, attains the Lord's state. What is that Lord's state like? To this he says —

children.text: kartṛbhyo guṇebhyo 'nyam akartāram ātmānaṃ paśyan bhagavad-bhāvam adhigacchati ity uktam; sa bhagavad-bhāvaḥ kīdṛśa ity ata āha ---
guṇān etān atītya trīn dehī dehasamudbhavān /
children.translated_text: 'The embodied one, having transcended these three <s>guṇas</s> that are the source of the body,'

children.text: janmamṛtyujarāduḥkhair vimukto 'mṛtam aśnute //
children.translated_text: 'freed from birth, death, old age, and suffering, attains immortality.' ||

children.text: guṇān etān atītya trīn dehī deha-samudbhavān /
janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duḥkhair vimukto 'mṛtam aśnute //

body.text: ayaṃ dehī dehasamudbhavān dehākārapariṇataprakṛtisamudbhavān etān sattvādīn trīn guṇān atītya tebhyo 'nyaṃ jñānaikākāram ātmānaṃ paśyan janmamṛtyujarāduhkhair vimuktaḥ amṛtam ātmānam anubhavati / eṣa madbhāva ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: This embodied one, having transcended these three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the others — that are the source of the body, arising from <s>Prakṛti</s> which has transformed into the form of the body, seeing the self as other than them, of the single form of knowledge — freed from the sufferings of birth, death, and old age, experiences the self which is immortal. This is the meaning of 'My state.' //

children.text: ayaṃ dehī deha-samudbhavān deha-ākāra-pariṇata-prakṛti-samudbhavān etān sattva-ādīn trīn guṇān atītya tebhyo 'nyaṃ jñāna-eka-ākāram ātmānaṃ paśyan janma-mṛtyu-jarā-duhkhair vimuktaḥ amṛtam ātmānam anubhavati / eṣa mad-bhāva ity-arthaḥ //

attributes.n: atha guṇā1tītasya sva-rūpa-sūcanā3cāra-prakāraṃ guṇā1tyaya-hetuṃ ca pṛcchan arjuna uvāca ---

children.text: kair liṅgais triguṇān etān atīto bhavati prabho /
children.translated_text: 'By what marks is one known who has transcended these three <s>guṇas</s>, O Lord?'

children.text: kim ācāraḥ kathaṃ caitāṃs trīn guṇān ativartate //
children.translated_text: 'What is his conduct, and how does he transcend these three <s>guṇas</s>?' //

children.text: kair liṅgais tri-guṇān etān atīto bhavati prabho /
kim ācāraḥ kathaṃ ca etāṃs trīn guṇān ativartate //

body.text: sattvādīn trīn guṇān etān atītaḥ kair liṅgaiḥ kair lakṣaṇaiḥ upalakṣito bhavati? kim ācāraḥ kenācāreṇa yukto 'sau? asya svarūpāvagatiliṅgabhūtācāraḥ kīdṛśa ityarthaḥ / kathaṃ caitān kenopāyena sattvādīṃs trīn guṇān ativartate? //
body.translated_text: One who has transcended these three <s>guṇas</s> beginning with <s>sattva</s> — by what marks, by what characteristics is he recognized? What is his conduct — with what behavior is he endowed? What is the conduct that serves as the mark for understanding his essential nature? — this is the meaning. And how — by what means — does he transcend these three <s>guṇas</s> beginning with <s>sattva</s>? //

children.text: sattva-ādīn trīn guṇān etān atītaḥ kair liṅgaiḥ kair lakṣaṇaiḥ upalakṣito bhavati? kim ācāraḥ kenā acāreṇa yukto 'sau? asya sva-rūpa-avagati-liṅga-bhūta-ācāraḥ kīdṛśa ity-arthaḥ / kathaṃ ca etān kena upāyena sattva-ādīṃs trīn guṇān ativartate? //
prakāśaṃ ca pravṛttiṃ ca moham eva ca pāṇḍava /
children.translated_text: 'Illumination, activity, and delusion, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>,' |

children.text: na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati //
children.translated_text: 'he does not hate when they arise, nor long for them when they cease.' ||

children.text: prakāśaṃ ca pravṛttiṃ ca moham eva ca pāṇḍava /
na dveṣṭi saṃpravṛttāni na nivṛttāni kāṅkṣati //

body.text: ātmavyatirikteṣu vastvaniṣṭeṣu saṃpravṛttāni sattvarajastamasāṃ kāryāṇi prakāśapravṛttimohākhyāni yo na dveṣṭi, tathā ātmavyatirikteṣv iṣṭeṣu vastuṣu tāny eva nivṛttāni na kāṅkṣati //
body.translated_text: He who does not hate the effects of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> — called illumination, activity, and delusion — when they arise in undesirable objects external to the self; and likewise does not long for those very [effects] when they have ceased in desirable objects external to the self. //

children.text: ātma-vyatirikteṣu vastv-aniṣṭeṣu saṃpravṛttāni sattva-rajas-tamasāṃ kāryāṇi prakāśa-pravṛtti-moha-ākhyāni yo na dveṣṭi, tathā ātma-vyatirikteṣv iṣṭeṣu vastuṣu tāny eva nivṛttāni na kāṅkṣati //
udāsīnavad āsīno guṇair yo na vicālyate /
children.translated_text: 'Seated as if indifferent, undisturbed by the <s>guṇas</s>,' |

children.text: guṇā vartanta ity eva yo 'vatiṣṭhati neṅgate //
children.translated_text: 'who remains [thinking] "the <s>guṇas</s> operate" and does not waver.' ||

children.text: udāsīnavad āsīno guṇair yo na vicālyate /
guṇā vartanta ity eva yo 'vatiṣṭhati na iṅgate //

body.text: udāsīnavad āsīnaḥ guṇavyatiriktātmāvalokanatṛptyā anyatrodāsīnavad āsīnaḥ, guṇair dveṣākāṅkṣādvāreṇe yo na vicālyate -- guṇāḥ sveṣu kāryeṣu prakāśādiṣu vartanta ity anusandhāya yas tūṣṇīm avatiṣṭhate / neṅgate na guṇakāryānuguṇaṃ ceṣṭate //
body.translated_text: 'Seated as if indifferent' — seated as if indifferent toward everything else, due to the contentment derived from contemplating the self that is distinct from the <s>guṇas</s>; who is not disturbed by the <s>guṇas</s> through the avenue of aversion and longing — reflecting that the <s>guṇas</s> operate in their own effects such as illumination and the like, he remains silent. 'Does not waver' — he does not act in conformity with the effects of the <s>guṇas</s>. //

children.text: udāsīnavad āsīnaḥ guṇa-vyatirikta-ātma-avalokana-tṛptyā anyatra udāsīnavad āsīnaḥ, guṇair dveṣa-ākāṅkṣā-dvāreṇe yo na vicālyate --- guṇāḥ sveṣu kāryeṣu prakāśa-ādiṣu vartanta ity anusandhāya yas tu uṣṇīm avatiṣṭhate / na iṅgate na guṇa-kārya-anuguṇaṃ ceṣṭate //
samaduḥkhasukhaḥ svasthaḥ samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Equal in pain and pleasure, self-abiding, regarding a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as equal,' |

children.text: tulyapriyāpriyo dhīras tulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'equal toward the pleasant and the unpleasant, wise, equal toward blame and praise of himself,' ||

children.text: sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ sva-sthaḥ sama-loṣṭa-aśma-kāñcanaḥ /
tulya-priya-apriyo dhīras tulya-nindā-ātma-saṃstutiḥ //
mānāvamānayos tulyas tulyo mitrāripakṣayoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward the sides of friend and foe,' |

children.text: sarvārambhaparityāgī guṇātītaḥ sa ucyate //
children.translated_text: 'renouncing all undertakings — he is said to have transcended the <s>guṇas</s>.' ||

children.text: māna-avamānayos tulyas tulyo mitra-ari-pakṣayoḥ /
sarva-ārambha-parityāgī guṇa-atītaḥ sa ucyate //

body.text: samaduḥkhasukhaḥ sukhaduḥkhayos samacittaḥ, svasthaḥ svasmin sthitaḥ / svātmaikapriyatvena tadvyatiriktaputrādijanmamaraṇādisukhaduḥkhayos samacitta ityarthaḥ / tata eva samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ / tata eva tulyapriyāpriyaḥ tulyapriyāpriyaviṣayaḥ / dhīraḥ prakṛtyātmavivekakuśalaḥ / tata eva tulyanindātmasaṃstutiḥ ātmani manuṣyādyabhimānakṛtaguṇāguṇanimittastutinindayoḥ svāsaṃbandhānusandhānena tulyacittaḥ / tatprayuktamānāvamānayoḥ tatprayuktamitrāripakṣayor api svasaṃbandhābhāvād eva tulyacittaḥ / tathā dehitvaprayuktasarvārambhaparityāgī / ya evaṃbhūtaḥ, sa guṇātīta ucyate //
body.translated_text: 'Equal in pain and pleasure' — of equal mind in pleasure and pain. 'Self-abiding' — established in oneself. The meaning is: having the self alone as dear, he is of equal mind toward the pleasures and pains of birth, death, and the like pertaining to sons and others external to the self. For that very reason, he regards a clod, a stone, and gold as equal. For that very reason, 'equal toward the pleasant and unpleasant' — equal with respect to pleasant and unpleasant objects. 'Wise' (<s>dhīra</s>) — skilled in discriminating between <s>Prakṛti</s> and the self. For that very reason, 'equal toward blame and praise of himself' — of equal mind toward praise and blame occasioned by virtues and faults attributed to himself through the false identification with human and other [forms], by reflecting on his own non-connection [with them]. Of equal mind toward honor and dishonor occasioned by that, and toward the sides of friend and foe occasioned by that as well, precisely because of the absence of any connection of his [true self with them]. Likewise, renouncing all undertakings occasioned by embodiment. He who is of such a nature is said to have transcended the <s>guṇas</s>. //

children.text: sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ sukha-duḥkhayos sama-cittaḥ, sva-sthaḥ svasmin sthitaḥ / sva-ātma-eka-priyatvena tad-vyatirikta-putra-ādi-janma-maraṇa-ādi-sukha-duḥkhayos sama-citta ity-arthaḥ / tata eva sama-loṣṭa-aśma-kāñcanaḥ / tata eva tulya-priya-apriyaḥ tulya-priya-apriya-viṣayaḥ / dhīraḥ prakṛty-ātma-viveka-kuśalaḥ / tata eva tulya-nindā-ātma-saṃstutiḥ ātmani manuṣya-ādy-abhimāna-kṛta-guṇa-aguṇa-nimitta-stuti-nindayoḥ sva-asaṃbandha-anusandhānena tulya-cittaḥ / tat-prayukta-māna-avamānayoḥ tat-prayukta-mitra-ari-pakṣayor api sva-saṃbandha-abhāvād eva tulya-cittaḥ / tathā dehitva-prayukta-sarva-ārambha-parityāgī / ya evaṃ-bhūtaḥ, sa guṇa-atīta ucyate //

body.text: athaivaṃrūpaguṇātyaye pradhānahetum āha --
body.translated_text: Now He states the principal means for transcending the <s>guṇas</s> in the manner described:

children.text: atha evaṃ-rūpa-guṇa-atyaye pradhāna-hetum āha ---
māṃ ca yo 'vyabhicāreṇa bhaktiyogena sevate /
children.translated_text: 'And he who serves Me with unswerving <s>bhaktiyoga</s>,' |

children.text: sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate //
children.translated_text: 'having fully transcended these <s>guṇas</s>, he becomes fit for the state of <s>Brahman</s>.' ||

children.text: māṃ ca yo 'vyabhicāreṇa bhakti-yogena sevate /
sa guṇān samatītya etān brahma-bhūyāya kalpate //

body.text: "nānyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāram" ityādinoktena prakṛtyātmavivekānusandhānamātreṇa na guṇātyayaḥ saṃpatsyate; tasyānādikālapravṛttiviparītavāsanābādhyatvasaṃbhavāt / mām satyasaṅkalpaṃ paramakāruṇikam āśritavātsalyajaladhim, avyabhicārena aikāntyaviśiṣṭena bhaktiyogena ca yaḥ sevate, sa etān sattvādīn guṇān duratyayān atītya brahmabhūyāya brahmatvāya kalpate; brahmabhāvayogyo bhavati / yathāvasthitam ātmānam amṛtam avyayaṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ // BhGR_14.26 //
body.translated_text: Merely by the contemplative discrimination of <s>Prakṛti</s> and self as stated in 'there is no agent other than the <s>guṇas</s>' and the like, the transcendence of the <s>guṇas</s> will not be accomplished — because of the possibility of being overpowered by the contrary impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) accumulated since beginningless time. But he who serves Me — who am of true resolve, supremely compassionate, an ocean of affection toward those who have taken refuge — with unswerving, that is, exclusively devoted <s>bhaktiyoga</s> — he, having transcended these <s>guṇas</s> beginning with <s>sattva</s> that are so difficult to overcome, becomes fit for the state of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmabhūya</s>), that is, becomes worthy of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>. The meaning is: he attains the self as it truly is — immortal and imperishable. //

children.text: "na anyaṃ guṇebhyaḥ kartāram" ity-ādina ūktena prakṛty-ātma-viveka-anusandhāna-mātreṇa na guṇa-atyayaḥ saṃpatsyate; tasya anādi-kāla-pravṛtti-viparīta-vāsanā-bādhyatva-saṃbhavāt / mām satya-saṅkalpaṃ parama-kāruṇikam āśrita-vātsalya-jaladhim, avyabhicārena aikāntya-viśiṣṭena bhakti-yogena ca yaḥ sevate, sa etān sattva-ādīn guṇān duratyayān atītya brahma-bhūyāya brahmatvāya kalpate; brahma-bhāva-yogyo bhavati / yathā-avasthitam ātmānam amṛtam avyayaṃ prāpnoti ity-arthaḥ // BhGR_14.26 //
brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham amṛtasyāvyayasya ca /
children.translated_text: 'For I am the foundation of <s>Brahman</s>, the immortal and the imperishable,' |

children.text: śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca //
children.translated_text: 'and of the eternal <s>dharma</s>, and of absolute bliss.' ||

children.text: brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭha āham amṛtasya avyayasya ca /
śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasya ekāntikasya ca //

body.text: hiśabdo hetau; yasmād aham avyabhicāribhaktiyogena sevito 'mṛtasyāvyayasya ca brahmaṇaḥ pratiṣṭhā, tathā śāśvatasya ca dharmasya atiśayitanityāiśvaryasya; eikāntikasya ca sukhasya "vāsudevaḥ sarvam" ityādinā nirdiṣṭasya jñāninaḥ prāpyasya sukhasyetyarthaḥ / yady api śāśvatadharmaśabdaḥ prāpakavacanaḥ, tathāpi pūrvottarayoḥ prāpyarūpatvena tatsāhacaryādayam api prāpyalakṣakaḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- pūrvatra "daivī hy eṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā / mām eva ye prapadyante" ity ārabhya guṇātyayasya tatpūrvakākṣarair bhagavatprāptīnāṃ ca bhagavatprapattyekopāyatāyāḥ pratipāditatvād ekāntabhagavatprapattyekopāyo guṇātyayaḥ tatpūrvakabrahmabhāvaś ceti //
body.translated_text: The word 'for' (<s>hi</s>) indicates the reason. Because I, when served with unswerving <s>bhaktiyoga</s>, am the foundation of <s>Brahman</s> — the immortal and the imperishable — and likewise of the eternal <s>dharma</s>, that is, the surpassingly eternal sovereignty; and of absolute bliss — meaning the bliss that is to be attained by the <s>jñānin</s> (knower) as described in '<s>Vāsudeva</s> is all' and the like. Although the term 'eternal <s>dharma</s>' denotes the means of attainment, yet due to its proximity to the objects of attainment mentioned before and after, it too indicates what is to be attained. What is stated amounts to this: since previously, beginning with 'For this divine <s>māyā</s> of Mine, constituted of the <s>guṇas</s>, is difficult to overcome; but those who take refuge in Me alone' — the transcendence of the <s>guṇas</s> and the attainments of the imperishable and of the Lord that follow from it have been established as having sole surrender to the Lord as their means, the transcendence of the <s>guṇas</s> and the subsequent attainment of the state of <s>Brahman</s> have exclusive surrender to the Lord as their sole means. //

children.text: hi-śabdo hetau; yasmād aham avyabhicāri-bhakti-yogena sevito 'mṛtasya avyayasya ca brahmaṇaḥ pratiṣṭhā, tathā śāśvatasya ca dharmasya atiśayita-nitya-aiśvaryasya; eikāntikasya ca sukhasya "vāsu-devaḥ sarvam" ity-ādinā nirdiṣṭasya jñāninaḥ prāpyasya sukhasya ity-arthaḥ / yady api śāśvata-dharma-śabdaḥ prāpaka-vacanaḥ, tatha āpi pūrva-uttarayoḥ prāpya-rūpatvena tat-sāhacarya-ādayam api prāpya-lakṣakaḥ / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- pūrvatra "daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī mama māyā duratyayā / mām eva ye prapadyante" ity ārabhya guṇa-atyayasya tat-pūrvaka-akṣarair bhagavat-prāptīnāṃ ca bhagavat-prapatty-eka-upāyatāyāḥ pratipāditatvād eka-anta-bhagavat-prapatty-eka-upāyo guṇa-atyayaḥ tat-pūrvaka-brahma-bhāvaś ca iti //

body.text:
kṣetrādhyāye kṣetrakṣetrajñabhūtayoḥ prakṛtipuruṣayoḥ svarūpaṃ viśodhya viśuddhasyāparicchinnajñānaikākārasyaiva puruṣasya prākṛtaguṇasaṅgapravāhanimitto devādyākārapariṇataprakṛtisaṃbandho 'nādir ity uktam / anantare cādhyāye puruṣasya kāryakāraṇobhayāvasthaprakṛtisaṃbandho guṇasaṅgamūlo bhagavataiva kṛta ity uktvā guṇasaṅgaprakāraṃ savistaraṃ pratipādya guṇasaṅganivṛttipūrvakātmayāthātmyāvāptiś ca bhagavadbhaktimūlety uktam / idānīṃ bhajanīyasya bhagavataḥ kṣarākṣarātmakabaddhamuktavibhūtimattām, vibhūtibhūtāt kṣarākṣarapuruṣadvayān nikhilaheyapratyanīkakalyāṇaiktānatayā atyantotkarṣeṇa visajātīyasya bhagavataḥ puruṣottamatvaṃ ca vaktum ārabhate / tatra tāvad asaṅgarūpaśastracchinnabandhām
akṣarākhyavibhūtiṃ vaktuṃ chedyarūpabandhākāreṇa vitatam acitpariṇāmaviśeṣam aśvatthavṛkṣākāram kalpayan --
body.translated_text: In the chapter on the field, having purified the essential natures of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> — which are the field and the knower of the field — it was stated that the <s>Puruṣa</s>, whose sole form when purified is unlimited consciousness, has a beginningless connection with <s>Prakṛti</s> that has transformed into the forms of gods and the like, caused by the stream of attachment to the <s>guṇas</s>. And in the subsequent chapter, having stated that the <s>Puruṣa</s>'s connection with <s>Prakṛti</s> in both its causal and effectual states is rooted in attachment to the <s>guṇas</s> and is brought about by the Lord Himself, and having expounded in detail the mode of attachment to the <s>guṇas</s>, it was stated that the attainment of the true nature of the self, preceded by the cessation of attachment to the <s>guṇas</s>, is rooted in devotion to the Lord. Now, He begins to state the supreme sovereignty of the Lord who is to be worshipped — His possession of the twofold <s>vibhūti</s> (glory) consisting of the bound and the liberated, characterized as the perishable (<s>kṣara</s>) and the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) — and the Lord's being <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person), utterly different in kind from the twofold <s>Puruṣa</s> — the perishable and the imperishable — that constitutes His <s>vibhūti</s>, by virtue of being exclusively a repository of auspicious qualities opposed to all that is defective. To that end, in order to describe the <s>vibhūti</s> called the imperishable whose bondage has been severed by the weapon of non-attachment, He first conceives of the particular transformation of non-conscious matter, spread out in the form of bondage that is to be severed, as having the form of an <s>aśvattha</s> (fig) tree:

children.text:
kṣetra-adhyāye kṣetra-kṣetra-jña-bhūtayoḥ prakṛti-puruṣayoḥ sva-rūpaṃ viśodhya viśuddhasya aparicchinna-jñāna-eka-ākārasya eva puruṣasya prākṛta-guṇa-saṅga-pravāha-nimitto deva-ādy-ākāra-pariṇata-prakṛti-saṃbandho 'nādir ity uktam / anantare ca adhyāye puruṣasya kārya-kāraṇa-ubhaya-avastha-prakṛti-saṃbandho guṇa-saṅga-mūlo bhagavata aiva kṛta ity uktvā guṇa-saṅga-prakāraṃ sa-vistaraṃ pratipādya guṇa-saṅga-nivṛtti-pūrvaka-ātma-yāthātmya-avāptiś ca bhagavad-bhakti-mūla īty uktam / idānīṃ bhajanīyasya bhagavataḥ kṣara-akṣara-ātmaka-baddha-mukta-vibhūtimattām, vibhūti-bhūtāt kṣara-akṣara-puruṣa-dvayān nikhila-heya-pratyanīka-kalyāṇa-ektānatayā atyanta-utkarṣeṇa visajātīyasya bhagavataḥ puruṣa-uttamatvaṃ ca vaktum ārabhate / tatra tāvad asaṅga-rūpa-śastra-cchinna-bandhām
akṣara-ākhya-vibhūtiṃ vaktuṃ chedya-rūpa-bandha-ākāreṇa vitatam acit-pariṇāma-viśeṣam aśvattha-vṛkṣa-ākāram kalpayan ---
ūrdhvamūlam adhaśśākham aśvatthaṃ prāhur avyayam |
children.translated_text: 'With roots above and branches below, they speak of the <s>aśvattha</s> as imperishable,' |

children.text: chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yas taṃ veda sa vedavit ||
children.translated_text: 'whose leaves are the <s>Vedas</s> — he who knows it is a knower of the <s>Vedas</s>.' ||

children.text: ūrdhva-mūlam adhaś-śākham aśvatthaṃ prāhur avyayam |
chandāṃsi yasya parṇāni yas taṃ veda sa veda-vit ||

body.text:
yaṃ saṃsārākhyam aśvatham ūrdhvamūlam adhaś śākham avyayaṃ prāhuḥ śrutayaḥ, "ūrdhvamūlo 'vākchākha eṣo 'śvatthas sanātanaḥ", "ūrdhvamūlam avākchākhaṃ vṛkṣaṃ yo veda saṃprti" ityādyāḥ / saptalokopariniviṣṭacaturmukhāditvena tasyordhvamūlatvam / pṛthivīnivāsisakalanarapaśumṛgakrimikīṭapataṅgasthāvarāntatayā adhaś śākhatvam / asaṅgahetubhūtād a samyagjñanodayāt pravāharūpeṇācchedyatvenāvyayatvam / yasya cāśvatthasya chandāṃsi parṇāny āhuḥ / chandāṃsi -- śrutayaḥ, "vāyavyaṃ śvetam ālabheta bhūtikāmaḥ", "aindrāgnam ekādaśa kapālaṃ nirvapet prajākāmaḥ" ityādiśrutipratipāditaiḥ kāmyakarmabhir vardhate 'yaṃ saṃsāravṛkṣa iti chandāṃsy evāsya parṇāni / parṇair hi vṛkṣo vardhate / yas tam evaṃbhūtam
aśvatthaṃ veda, sa vedavit / vedo hi saṃsāravṛkṣacchedopāyaṃ vadati; chedyavṛkṣasvarūpajñānaṃ chedanopāyajñanopayogīti vedavid ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: The <s>śrutis</s> speak of this <s>aśvattha</s> called <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of birth and death) as having its roots above and branches below, and as imperishable: 'This eternal <s>aśvattha</s> has its roots above and branches below,' 'He who knows the tree with roots above and branches below' — and so on. Its having roots above is due to the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>] established in the seven worlds [being its root]. Its having branches below is due to its extending down to all humans, animals, deer, worms, insects, moths, and immovable things dwelling on earth. Its imperishability is in the sense that it cannot be severed in its flow-like form, until the arising of right knowledge that is the cause of non-attachment. And the <s>śrutis</s> declare that the leaves of this <s>aśvattha</s> are the <s>chandas</s> (Vedic hymns). The <s>chandas</s> — the <s>śrutis</s> — [are its leaves because] this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> grows through the desire-motivated rites taught in <s>śruti</s> passages such as 'One desiring prosperity should offer a white [animal] to <s>Vāyu</s>,' 'One desiring progeny should prepare an eleven-potsherds offering to <s>Indrāgni</s>,' and the like — thus the <s>chandas</s> are indeed its leaves. For a tree grows by its leaves. He who knows this <s>aśvattha</s> as being of such a nature — he is a knower of the <s>Veda</s>. For the <s>Veda</s> teaches the means of severing this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s>; and knowledge of the nature of the tree to be severed is useful for knowledge of the means of severing — hence he is called a knower of the <s>Veda</s>. //

children.text:
yaṃ saṃsāra-ākhyam aśvatham ūrdhva-mūlam adhaś śākham avyayaṃ prāhuḥ śrutayaḥ, "ūrdhva-mūlo 'vāk-chākha eṣo 'śvatthas sanātanaḥ", "ūrdhva-mūlam avāk-chākhaṃ vṛkṣaṃ yo veda saṃprti" ity-ādyāḥ / sapta-loka-upari-niviṣṭa-catur-mukha-āditvena tasyā urdhva-mūlatvam / pṛthivī-nivāsi-sakala-nara-paśu-mṛga-krimi-kīṭa-pataṅga-sthāvara-antatayā adhaś śākhatvam / asaṅga-hetu-bhūtād a samyagjñana-udayāt pravāha-rūpeṇa acchedyatvena avyayatvam / yasya ca aśvatthasya chandāṃsi parṇāny āhuḥ / chandāṃsi --- śrutayaḥ, "vāyavyaṃ śvetam ālabheta bhūti-kāmaḥ", "aindrāgnam ekādaśa kapālaṃ nirvapet prajā-kāmaḥ" ity-ādi-śruti-pratipāditaiḥ kāmya-karmabhir vardhate 'yaṃ saṃsāra-vṛkṣa iti chandāṃsy eva asya parṇāni / parṇair hi vṛkṣo vardhate / yas tam evaṃ-bhūtam
aśvatthaṃ veda, sa veda-vit / vedo hi saṃsāra-vṛkṣa-ccheda-upāyaṃ vadati; chedya-vṛkṣa-sva-rūpa-jñānaṃ chedana-upāya-jñana-upayogi iti veda-vid ity ucyate //
adhaś cordhvaṃ ca prasṛtās tasya śākhā guṇapravṛddhā viṣayapravālāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Its branches spread below and above, nourished by the <s>guṇas</s>, with sense-objects as sprouts.' |

children.text: adhaś cā urdhvaṃ ca prasṛtās tasya śākhā guṇa-pravṛddhā viṣaya-pravālāḥ |

body.text: tasya manuṣyādiśākhasya vṛkṣasya tattatkarmakṛtā aparāś ca adhaḥ śākhāḥ punar api manuṣyapaśvādirūpeṇa prasṛtā bhavanti; ūrdhvaṃ ca gandharvayakṣadevādirūpeṇa prasṛtā bhavanti / tāś ca guṇapravṛddhāḥ guṇaiḥ sattvādibhiḥ pravṛddhāḥ, viṣayapravālāḥ śabdādiviṣayapallavāḥ / katham ity atrāha --
body.translated_text: Of that tree whose [primary] branches are humans and the like, other branches too, produced by their respective <s>karmas</s>, spread downward again in the form of humans, animals, and the like; and upward in the form of <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, gods, and the like. And they are 'nourished by the <s>guṇas</s>' — nourished by <s>sattva</s> and the other <s>guṇas</s>; 'with sense-objects as sprouts' — having the sense-objects such as sound and the like as their tender shoots. How so? — to this he says:

children.text: tasya manuṣya-ādi-śākhasya vṛkṣasya tat-tat-karma-kṛtā aparāś ca adhaḥ śākhāḥ punar api manuṣya-paśv-ādi-rūpeṇa prasṛtā bhavanti; ūrdhvaṃ ca gandharva-yakṣa-deva-ādi-rūpeṇa prasṛtā bhavanti / tāś ca guṇa-pravṛddhāḥ guṇaiḥ sattva-ādibhiḥ pravṛddhāḥ, viṣaya-pravālāḥ śabda-ādi-viṣaya-pallavāḥ / katham ity atrā aha ---
adhaś ca mūlāny anusaṃtatāni karmānubandhīni manuṣyaloke ||
children.translated_text: 'And below, the roots extend continuously, bound to <s>karma</s>, in the world of humans.' ||

children.text: adhaś ca mūlāny anusaṃtatāni karma-anubandhīni manuṣya-loke ||

body.text: brahmalokamūlasyāsya vṛkṣasya manuṣyāgrasya, adho manuṣyaloke mūlāny anusantatāni; tāni ca karmānubandhīni karmāṇy evānubandhīni mūlāni adho manuṣyaloke ca bhavantītyarthaḥ / manuṣyatvāvasthāyāṃ kṛtair hi karmabhiḥ adho manuṣyapaśvādayaḥ, ūrdhvaṃ ca devādayo bhavanti //
body.translated_text: Of this tree whose root is the world of <s>Brahmā</s> and whose tips are humans, the roots extend continuously downward in the world of humans. And those roots are 'bound to <s>karma</s>' — <s>karmas</s> themselves are the roots that are bound [to the tree], and they exist below in the world of humans — this is the meaning. For it is by <s>karmas</s> performed in the state of being human that [beings become] humans, animals, and the like below, and gods and the like above. //

children.text: brahma-loka-mūlasya asya vṛkṣasya manuṣya-agrasya, adho manuṣya-loke mūlāny anusantatāni; tāni ca karma-anubandhīni karmāṇy eva anubandhīni mūlāni adho manuṣya-loke ca bhavanti ity-arthaḥ / manuṣyatva-avasthāyāṃ kṛtair hi karmabhiḥ adho manuṣya-paśv-ādayaḥ, ūrdhvaṃ ca deva-ādayo bhavanti //
na rūpam asyeha tathopalabhyate nānto na cādir na ca saṃpratiṣṭhā |
children.translated_text: 'The form of this [tree] is not perceived here as such, nor its end, nor its beginning, nor its foundation.' |

children.text: na rūpam asya iha tatha ūpalabhyate na anto na cā adir na ca saṃpratiṣṭhā |

body.text: asya vṛkṣasya caturmukhāditvenordhvamūlatvam, tatsantānaparamparayā manuṣyāgratvenādhaś śākhatvam, manuṣyatve kṛtaiḥ karmabhir mūlabhūtaiḥ punar apy adhaś cordhvaṃ ca prasṛtaśākhatvam iti yathedaṃ rūpaṃ nirdiṣṭam, na tathā saṃsāribhir upalabhyate / manuṣyo 'haṃ devadattasya putro yajñadattasya pitā tadanurūpaprigrahaś cety etāvanmātram upalabhyate / tathā asya vṛkṣasya antaḥ vināśo 'pi guṇamayabhogeṣv asaṅgakṛta iti nopalabhyate / tathā asya guṇasaṅga evādir iti nopalabhyate / tasya pratiṣṭhā ca anātmani ātmābhimānarūpam ajñānam iti nopalabhyate; pratitiṣṭhaty asminn+eveti hy ajñānam evāsya pratiṣṭhā //
body.translated_text: The form of this tree as described — having its roots above due to [<s>Brahmā</s>] being the four-faced one, having its branches below due to humans being at the tips through the continuous succession of his lineage, having branches spreading further below and above through <s>karmas</s> that serve as roots performed in the human state — this form is not perceived as such by those in <s>saṃsāra</s>. They perceive only this much: 'I am a human, the son of <s>Devadatta</s>, the father of <s>Yajñadatta</s>, with possessions befitting that.' Likewise, the end of this tree — its destruction through non-attachment to the enjoyments constituted of the <s>guṇas</s> — is not perceived. Likewise, that the beginning of this [tree] is attachment to the <s>guṇas</s> is not perceived. And its foundation — which is ignorance in the form of the false identification of the self with what is not the self — is not perceived; for that on which it stands firmly — that is, ignorance itself is its foundation. //

children.text: asya vṛkṣasya catur-mukha-āditvenā urdhva-mūlatvam, tat-santāna-paramparayā manuṣya-agratvena adhaś śākhatvam, manuṣyatve kṛtaiḥ karmabhir mūla-bhūtaiḥ punar apy adhaś cā urdhvaṃ ca prasṛta-śākhatvam iti yatha īdaṃ rūpaṃ nirdiṣṭam, na tathā saṃsāribhir upalabhyate / manuṣyo 'haṃ deva-dattasya putro yajña-dattasya pitā tad-anurūpa-prigrahaś ca ity etāvan-mātram upalabhyate / tathā asya vṛkṣasya antaḥ vināśo 'pi guṇa-maya-bhogeṣv asaṅga-kṛta iti na upalabhyate / tathā asya guṇa-saṅga evā adir iti na upalabhyate / tasya pratiṣṭhā ca anātmani ātma-abhimāna-rūpam ajñānam iti na upalabhyate; pratitiṣṭhaty asminn+eva iti hy ajñānam eva asya pratiṣṭhā //
aśvattham enaṃ suvirūḍhamūlam asaṅgaśastreṇa dṛḍhena chitvā ||
children.translated_text: 'Having cut this <s>aśvattha</s> with its deeply grown roots, with the strong weapon of non-attachment,' ||

children.text: aśvattham enaṃ su-virūḍha-mūlam asaṅga-śastreṇa dṛḍhena chitvā ||
tataḥ padaṃ tat parimārgitavyam yasmin gatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'then that goal is to be sought, reaching which they do not return again.' |

children.text: tataḥ padaṃ tat parimārgitavyam yasmin gatā na nivartanti bhūyaḥ |

body.text: enam uktaprakāraṃ suvirūḍhamūlam suṣṭhu vividhaṃ rūḍhamūlam aśvatthaṃ samyagjñānamūlena dṛḍhena guṇamayabhogāsaṃgākhyena śastreṇa chitvā, tataḥ viṣayāsaṃgād dhetoḥ tat padaṃ parimārgitavyam anveṣaṇīyam, yasmin gatā bhūyo na nivartante //
body.translated_text: This <s>aśvattha</s> of the nature described, 'with deeply grown roots' — with roots that have grown in manifold and firm ways — having cut it with the strong weapon called non-attachment to the enjoyments constituted of the <s>guṇas</s>, rooted in right knowledge, then, because of non-attachment to sense-objects, that goal is to be sought, is to be investigated — reaching which, they do not return again. //

children.text: enam ukta-prakāraṃ suvirūḍha-mūlam suṣṭhu vividhaṃ rūḍha-mūlam aśvatthaṃ samyagjñāna-mūlena dṛḍhena guṇa-maya-bhoga-asaṃga-ākhyena śastreṇa chitvā, tataḥ viṣaya-asaṃgād dhetoḥ tat padaṃ parimārgitavyam anveṣaṇīyam, yasmin gatā bhūyo na nivartante //

body.text: katham anādikālapravṛtto guṇamayabhogasaṃgaḥ tanmūlaṃ ca viparītajñānaṃ nivartata ity ata āha --
body.translated_text: How can the attachment to the enjoyments constituted of the <s>guṇas</s>, which has been operating since beginningless time, and the contrary knowledge that is its root, be brought to cessation? — to this He says:

children.text: katham anādi-kāla-pravṛtto guṇa-maya-bhoga-saṃgaḥ tan-mūlaṃ ca viparīta-jñānaṃ nivartata ity ata āha ---
tam eva cādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadyed yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī ||
children.translated_text: 'One should take refuge in that very primeval Person from whom the ancient activity has issued forth.' ||

children.text: tam eva cā adyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadyed yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī ||

body.text:
ajñānādinivṛttaye tam eva ca ādyam kṛtsnasyādibhūtam, "mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram", "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate", "mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyat kiñcid asti dhanañjaya" ityādiṣūktam ādyaṃ puruṣam eva śaraṇaṃ prapadyet tam eva śaraṇaṃ prapadyeta / yataḥ yasmāt kṛtsnasya sraṣṭur iyaṃ guṇamayabhogasaṅgapravṛttiḥ, purāṇī purātanī prasṛtā / uktaṃ hi mayaitatpūrvam eva, "daivī hy eṣā guṇamayī mam māyā dūratyayā / mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṃ taranti te" iti / prapadyeyataḥ pravṛttir iti vā pāṭhaḥ; tam eva cādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prpadya śaraṇam upagamya, iyataḥ ajñānanivṛttyādeḥ kṛstnasyaitasya sādhanabhūtā pravṛttiḥ purāṇī purātanī praṛtā / purātanānāṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ pravṛttiḥ
purāṇī / purātanā hi mumukṣavo mām eva śaraṇam upagamya nirmuktabandhās saṃjātā ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: For the cessation of ignorance and the like, one should take refuge in — surrender to — that very primeval Person who is the origin of everything, as stated in 'Under My supervision <s>Prakṛti</s> gives birth to the moving and the unmoving,' 'I am the origin of all; from Me everything proceeds,' 'There is nothing else whatsoever higher than Me, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>' — that primeval Person alone. Because from Him, the creator of all, this activity of attachment to the enjoyments constituted of the <s>guṇas</s>, ancient and primordial, has issued forth. For this has been stated by Me previously: 'For this divine <s>māyā</s> of Mine, constituted of the <s>guṇas</s>, is difficult to overcome; but those who take refuge in Me alone cross beyond this <s>māyā</s>.' Alternatively, the reading is '<s>prapadyeyataḥ pravṛttiḥ</s>': having taken refuge in, having surrendered to, that very primeval Person, from [Him comes] the activity — the ancient, primordial practice — that is the means for all of this, beginning with the cessation of ignorance. 'Ancient activity' — the practice of the ancient seekers of liberation. For the ancient seekers of liberation, having taken refuge in Me alone, became freed from bondage — this is the meaning. //

children.text:
ajñāna-ādi-nivṛttaye tam eva ca ādyam kṛtsnasyā adi-bhūtam, "maya ādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacara-acaram", "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate", "mattaḥ parataraṃ na anyat kiñcid asti dhanañjaya" ity-ādiṣu uktam ādyaṃ puruṣam eva śaraṇaṃ prapadyet tam eva śaraṇaṃ prapadyeta / yataḥ yasmāt kṛtsnasya sraṣṭur iyaṃ guṇa-maya-bhoga-saṅga-pravṛttiḥ, purāṇī purātanī prasṛtā / uktaṃ hi maya aitat-pūrvam eva, "daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī mam māyā dūratyayā / mām eva ye prapadyante māyām etāṃ taranti te" iti / prapadyeyataḥ pravṛttir iti vā pāṭhaḥ; tam eva cā adyaṃ puruṣaṃ prpadya śaraṇam upagamya, iyataḥ ajñāna-nivṛtty-ādeḥ kṛstnasya etasya sādhana-bhūtā pravṛttiḥ purāṇī purātanī praṛtā / purātanānāṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ pravṛttiḥ
purāṇī / purātanā hi mumukṣavo mām eva śaraṇam upagamya nirmukta-bandhās saṃjātā ity-arthaḥ //
nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Free from pride and delusion, having conquered the fault of attachment, ever devoted to the self, with desires completely ceased,' |

children.text: dvandvair vimuktās sukhaduḥkhasaṃjñair gacchanty amūḍhāḥ padam avyayaṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: 'liberated from the dualities known as pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that imperishable goal.' ||

children.text: nirmāna-mohā jita-saṅga-doṣā adhyātma-nityā vinivṛtta-kāmāḥ |
dvandvair vimuktās sukha-duḥkha-saṃjñair gacchanty amūḍhāḥ padam avyayaṃ tat ||

body.text: evaṃ māṃ śaraṇam upagamya nirmānamohāḥ nirgatānātmātmābhimānarūpamohāḥ, jitasaṅgadoṣā jitaguṇamayabhogasaṅgākhyadoṣāḥ / adhyātmanityāḥ ātmani yaj jñānaṃ tad adhyātmam, ātmajñānaniratāḥ / vinivṛttakāmāḥ vinivṛttataditarakāmāḥ sukhaduḥkhasajñair dvandvaiś ca vimuktāḥ, amūḍhāḥ ātmānātmasvabhavajñāḥ, tad avyayaṃ padaṃ gacchanti anavacchinnajñānākāram ātmānaṃ yathāvasthitaṃ prāpnuvanti; māṃ śaraṇam upagatānāṃ matprasādāder evaitāḥ sarvāḥ pravṛttayaḥ suśakāḥ siddhiparyantā bhavantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, having taken refuge in Me: 'free from pride and delusion' — free from the delusion that is the false identification of what is not the self with the self; 'having conquered the fault of attachment' — having conquered the fault called attachment to the enjoyments constituted of the <s>guṇas</s>. 'Ever devoted to the self' — <s>adhyātma</s> is the knowledge pertaining to the self; [they are] devoted to self-knowledge. 'With desires completely ceased' — with all other desires having completely ceased; 'liberated from the dualities known as pleasure and pain'; 'undeluded' — knowing the true natures of the self and the non-self; they reach that imperishable goal — they attain the self as it truly is, in its form of unlimited consciousness. The meaning is: for those who have taken refuge in Me, all these activities, from the grace of the Lord onward, become easy and reach their consummation. //

children.text: evaṃ māṃ śaraṇam upagamya nirmāna-mohāḥ nirgata-anātma-ātma-abhimāna-rūpa-mohāḥ, jita-saṅga-doṣā jita-guṇa-maya-bhoga-saṅga-ākhya-doṣāḥ / adhyātma-nityāḥ ātmani yaj jñānaṃ tad adhyātmam, ātma-jñāna-niratāḥ / vinivṛtta-kāmāḥ vinivṛtta-tad-itara-kāmāḥ sukha-duḥkha-sajñair dvandvaiś ca vimuktāḥ, amūḍhāḥ ātma-anātma-sva-bhava-jñāḥ, tad avyayaṃ padaṃ gacchanti anavacchinna-jñāna-akāram ātmānaṃ yathā-avasthitaṃ prāpnuvanti; māṃ śaraṇam upagatānāṃ mat-prasāda-āder eva etāḥ sarvāḥ pravṛttayaḥ suśakāḥ siddhi-paryantā bhavanti ity-arthaḥ //
na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Neither the sun illuminates it, nor the moon, nor fire. |

children.text: yad gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: Having gone where they do not return — that is My supreme abode. ||

children.text: na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śaśa-aṅko na pāvakaḥ |
yad gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṃ mama ||

body.text: tad atmajyotir na sūryo bhāsayate, na śaśāṅkaḥ, na pāvakaś ca / jñānam eva hi sarvasya prakāśakam; bāhyāni tu jyotīṃṣi viṣayendriyasaṃbandhavirodhitamonirasanadvāreṇopakārakāṇi / asya ca prakāśako yogaḥ / tadvirodhi cānādikarma / tannivartanaṃ coktaṃ bhagavatprapattimūlam asaṅgādi / yad gatvā punar na nivartante, tat paramaṃ dhāma paraṃ jyotiḥ mama madīyam; madvibhūtibhūtaḥ mamāṃśa ityarthaḥ / ādityādīnām api prakāśakatvena tasya paramatvam / ādityādīni hi jyotīṃṣi na jñānajyotiṣaḥ prakāśakāni; jñānam eva sarvasya prakāśakam //
body.translated_text: That self-luminous [self] — the sun does not illuminate it, nor the moon, nor fire. For knowledge alone is the illuminator of everything; external lights merely assist by removing the darkness that obstructs the contact between the sense-organs and their objects. And the illuminator of this [self] is <s>yoga</s>. What obstructs it is beginningless <s>karma</s>. And the removal of that [<s>karma</s>] has been stated [to be] non-attachment and the like, rooted in taking refuge in the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having gone where they do not return again — that is My supreme abode (<s>dhāma</s>), My supreme light; it is Mine — it is a <s>vibhūti</s> (glorious manifestation) of Mine, a portion (<s>aṃśa</s>) of Mine, is the meaning. Its supremacy as light consists in being the illuminator even of the sun and the like. For the lights such as the sun and the like do not illuminate the light of knowledge; knowledge alone is the illuminator of everything. //

children.text: tad atma-jyotir na sūryo bhāsayate, na śaśa-aṅkaḥ, na pāvakaś ca / jñānam eva hi sarvasya prakāśakam; bāhyāni tu jyotīṃṣi viṣaya-indriya-saṃbandha-virodhi-tamo-nirasana-dvāreṇa upakārakāṇi / asya ca prakāśako yogaḥ / tad-virodhi ca anādi-karma / tan-nivartanaṃ ca uktaṃ bhagavat-prapatti-mūlam asaṅga-ādi / yad gatvā punar na nivartante, tat paramaṃ dhāma paraṃ jyotiḥ mama madīyam; mad-vibhūti-bhūtaḥ mama aṃśa ity-arthaḥ / āditya-ādīnām api prakāśakatvena tasya paramatvam / āditya-ādīni hi jyotīṃṣi na jñāna-jyotiṣaḥ prakāśakāni; jñānam eva sarvasya prakāśakam //
mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ |
children.translated_text: An eternal fragment of Mine alone, having become a living being in the world of the living, |

children.text: manaṣṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthitāni karṣati ||
children.translated_text: draws to itself the sense-organs, with the mind as the sixth, that are established in <s>Prakṛti</s>. ||

children.text: mama eva aṃśo jīva-loke jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ |
manaṣ-ṣaṣṭhāni indriyāṇi prakṛti-sthitāni karṣati ||

body.text: ittham uktasvarūpaḥ sanātano mamāṃśa eva san kaścid anādikarmarūpāvidyāveṣṭito jīvabhūto jīvaloke vartamāno devamanuṣyādiprakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣaśarīrasthāni manaṣṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi karṣati / kaścic ca pūrvoktena mārgeṇāsyā avidyāyāḥ muktaḥ svena rūpeṇāvatiṣṭhate / jīvabhūtas tv atisaṃkucitajñānāiśvaryaḥ karmalabdhaprakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣarūpaśarīrasthānām indriyāṇāṃ manaṣṣaṣṭhānām īśvaraḥ tāni karmānuguṇam itas tataḥ karṣati //
body.translated_text: Being of the nature described above, being eternal, being indeed a fragment (<s>aṃśa</s>) of Mine — a certain [self], enveloped by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) in the form of beginningless <s>karma</s>, having become a living being (<s>jīvabhūta</s>), existing in the world of the living, draws to itself the sense-organs with the mind as the sixth, which are established in the body that is a particular modification of <s>Prakṛti</s> in the forms of gods, humans, and the like. And another [self], liberated from this <s>avidyā</s> by the path described earlier, abides in its own form. But the one who has become a living being, with its knowledge and lordship extremely contracted, being the lord (<s>īśvara</s>) of the sense-organs with the mind as the sixth that are established in the body — a particular modification of <s>Prakṛti</s> obtained through <s>karma</s> — draws them hither and thither in accordance with [its] <s>karma</s>. //

children.text: ittham ukta-sva-rūpaḥ sanātano mama aṃśa eva san kaścid anādi-karma-rūpa-avidyā-veṣṭito jīva-bhūto jīva-loke vartamāno deva-manuṣya-ādi-prakṛti-pariṇāma-viśeṣa-śarīra-sthāni manaṣ-ṣaṣṭhāni indriyāṇi karṣati / kaścic ca pūrva-uktena mārgeṇa asyā avidyāyāḥ muktaḥ svena rūpeṇa avatiṣṭhate / jīva-bhūtas tv atisaṃkucita-jñāna-aiśvaryaḥ karma-labdha-prakṛti-pariṇāma-viśeṣa-rūpa-śarīra-sthānām indriyāṇāṃ manaṣ-ṣaṣṭhānām īśvaraḥ tāni karma-anuguṇam itas tataḥ karṣati //
śarīraṃ yad avāpnoti yac cāpy utkrāmatīśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever body the lord (<s>īśvara</s>) obtains, and from whatever [body] he also departs,

children.text: gṛhītvaitāni saṃyāti vāyur gandhān ivāśayāt ||
children.translated_text: taking these [senses] he goes, as the wind carries fragrances from their source. ||

children.text: śarīraṃ yad avāpnoti yac ca apy utkrāmatī iśvaraḥ |
gṛhītva aitāni saṃyāti vāyur gandhān ivā aśayāt ||

body.text: yac śarīram avāpnoti, yamāc charīrād utkrāmati, tatrāyam indriyāṇām īśvaraḥ etāni indriyāṇi bhūtasūkṣmais saha gṛhītvā saṃyāti vāyur gandhān ivāśayāt / yathā vāyuḥ srakcandanakastūrikādyāśayāt tatsthānāt sūkṣmāvayavais saha gandhān gṛhītvānyatra saṃyāti, tadvad ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Whatever body he obtains, and from whatever body he departs — there, this lord of the sense-organs, taking these sense-organs together with the subtle elements, goes — as the wind carries fragrances from their source. Just as the wind, taking fragrances together with subtle particles from their source — a garland, sandal, musk, and the like — goes elsewhere, so is it, is the meaning. //

children.text: yac śarīram avāpnoti, yamāc charīrād utkrāmati, tatra ayam indriyāṇām īśvaraḥ etāni indriyāṇi bhūta-sūkṣmais saha gṛhītvā saṃyāti vāyur gandhān ivā aśayāt / yathā vāyuḥ srak-candana-kastūrika-ādy-āśayāt tat-sthānāt sūkṣma-avayavais saha gandhān gṛhītva ānyatra saṃyāti, tadvad ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: kāni punas tānīndriyāṇīty atrāha --
body.translated_text: What then are those sense-organs? — to this He says —

children.text: kāni punas tāni indriyāṇi ity atrā aha ---
śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Hearing, sight, touch, taste, and smell,

children.text: adhiṣṭhāya manaś cāyaṃ viṣayān upasevate ||
children.translated_text: and presiding over the mind — he experiences the objects [of the senses]. ||

children.text: śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇam eva ca |
adhiṣṭhāya manaś ca ayaṃ viṣayān upasevate ||

body.text: etāni manaṣṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi adhiṣṭhāya svasvaviṣayavṛttyanuguṇāni kṛtvā, tān śabdādīn viṣayān upasevate upabhuṅkte //
body.translated_text: Presiding over these sense-organs with the mind as the sixth, i.e., making them function in accordance with their respective object-activities, he experiences — he enjoys — those objects such as sound and the like. //

children.text: etāni manaṣ-ṣaṣṭhāni indriyāṇi adhiṣṭhāya sva-sva-viṣaya-vṛtty-anuguṇāni kṛtvā, tān śabda-ādīn viṣayān upasevate upabhuṅkte //
utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ vāpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇānvitam |
children.translated_text: The deluded do not see him departing, or remaining, or experiencing, endowed with the <s>guṇas</s>;

children.text: vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those with the eye of knowledge see. ||

children.text: utkrāmantaṃ sthitaṃ va āpi bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇa-anvitam |
vimūḍhā na anupaśyanti paśyanti jñāna-cakṣuṣaḥ ||

body.text: evaṃ guṇānvitaṃ sattvādiguṇamayaprakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣamanuṣyatvādisaṃsthānapiṇḍasaṃsṛṣṭam, piṇḍaviśeṣād utkrāmantaṃ piṇḍaviśeṣe 'vathitaṃ vā, guṇamayān viṣayān bhuñjānaṃ vā kadācid api prakṛtipariṇāmaviśeṣamanuṣyatvādipiṇḍād vilakṣaṇaṃ jñānaikākāraṃ vimūḍhā nānupaśyanti / vimūḍhāḥ manuṣyatvādipiṇḍātmatvābhimāninaḥ / jñānacakṣuṣas tu piṇḍātmavivekaviṣayajñānavantaḥ sarvāvastham apy enaṃ viviktākāram eva paśyanti //
body.translated_text: Thus, this [self], endowed with the <s>guṇas</s> — conjoined with the particular modification of <s>Prakṛti</s> constituted by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like, in the bodily mass (<s>piṇḍa</s>) configured as humanhood and the like — whether departing from a particular bodily mass, or remaining in a particular bodily mass, or experiencing objects constituted by the <s>guṇas</s> — the deluded never see [him] as distinct from the bodily mass in the form of the particular modification of <s>Prakṛti</s> such as humanhood and the like, as having the sole form of knowledge. The deluded are those who identify the self with the bodily mass of humanhood and the like. But those with the eye of knowledge — those who possess knowledge pertaining to the discrimination of the bodily mass and the self — see him as having a distinct form [from the body] in all states. //

children.text: evaṃ guṇa-anvitaṃ sattva-ādi-guṇa-maya-prakṛti-pariṇāma-viśeṣa-manuṣyatva-ādi-saṃsthāna-piṇḍa-saṃsṛṣṭam, piṇḍa-viśeṣād utkrāmantaṃ piṇḍa-viśeṣe 'vathitaṃ vā, guṇa-mayān viṣayān bhuñjānaṃ vā kadācid api prakṛti-pariṇāma-viśeṣa-manuṣyatva-ādi-piṇḍād vilakṣaṇaṃ jñāna-eka-ākāraṃ vimūḍhā na anupaśyanti / vimūḍhāḥ manuṣyatva-ādi-piṇḍa-ātmatva-abhimāninaḥ / jñāna-cakṣuṣas tu piṇḍa-ātma-viveka-viṣaya-jñānavantaḥ sarva-avastham apy enaṃ vivikta-ākāram eva paśyanti //
yatanto yoginaś cainaṃ paśyanty ātmany avasthitam |
children.translated_text: The striving <s>yogins</s> also see this [self] as established in themselves;

children.text: yatanto 'py akṛtātmāno nainaṃ paśyanty acetasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but those who have not refined themselves, though striving, do not see this [self] — being without discernment. ||

children.text: yatanto yoginaś ca enaṃ paśyanty ātmany avasthitam |
yatanto 'py akṛta-ātmāno na enaṃ paśyanty acetasaḥ ||

body.text: matprapattipūrvakaṃ karmayogādiṣu yatamānās tair nirmalāntaḥkaraṇā yogino yogākhyena cakṣuṣā ātmani śarīre 'vasthitam api śarīrād viviktaṃ svena rūpeṇāvasthitam enaṃ paśyanti / yatamānā apy akṛtātmānaḥ matprapattivirahiṇaḥ tata evāsaṃskṛtamanasaḥ, tata eva acetasaḥ ātmāvalokanasamarthacetorahitāḥ nainaṃ paśyanti //
body.translated_text: Those who strive in <s>Karmayoga</s> and the like preceded by taking refuge in Me — <s>yogins</s> whose inner faculties have been purified by those [practices] — see this [self] with the eye called <s>yoga</s>, as established in the self, i.e., in the body, yet as distinct from the body, abiding in its own form. But those who strive yet have not refined themselves (<s>akṛtātmānas</s>) — who lack taking refuge in Me and therefore have unrefined minds, and therefore are without discernment (<s>acetas</s>), i.e., devoid of the mental capacity to perceive the self — they do not see this [self]. //

children.text: mat-prapatti-pūrvakaṃ karma-yoga-ādiṣu yatamānās tair nirmala-antaḥkaraṇā yogino yoga-ākhyena cakṣuṣā ātmani śarīre 'vasthitam api śarīrād viviktaṃ svena rūpeṇa avasthitam enaṃ paśyanti / yatamānā apy akṛta-ātmānaḥ mat-prapatti-virahiṇaḥ tata eva asaṃskṛta-manasaḥ, tata eva acetasaḥ ātma-avalokana-samartha-ceto-rahitāḥ na enaṃ paśyanti //

body.text: evaṃ ravicandrāgnīnām indriyasannikarṣavirodhisaṃtamasanirasanamukhenendriyānugrāhakatayā prakāśakānāṃ jyotiṣmatām api prakāśakajñānajyotir ātmā muktāvastho jīvāvasthaś ca bhagavadvibhūtir ity uktam, "tad dhāma pramaṃ mama", "mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtas sanātanaḥ" iti / idānīm acitpariṇāmaviśeṣabhūtam ādityādīnāṃ jyotiṣmatāṃ jyotir api bhagavad vibhūtir ity āha --
body.translated_text: Thus it has been stated that the self — the light of knowledge that illuminates even the luminous bodies such as the sun, moon, and fire, which are illuminators by removing the darkness that obstructs the contact of sense-organs [with objects] — is a <s>vibhūti</s> (glorious manifestation) of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, both in the liberated state and in the state of being a living being: 'that is My supreme abode' and 'an eternal fragment of Mine alone, having become a living being in the world of the living.' Now He says that the light of the luminous bodies such as the sun and the like, which are particular modifications of non-conscious [<s>Prakṛti</s>], is also a <s>vibhūti</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s> —

children.text: evaṃ ravi-candra-agnīnām indriya-sannikarṣa-virodhi-saṃtamasa-nirasana-mukhena indriya-anugrāhakatayā prakāśakānāṃ jyotiṣmatām api prakāśaka-jñāna-jyotir ātmā mukta-avastho jīva-avasthaś ca bhagavad-vibhūtir ity uktam, "tad dhāma pramaṃ mama", "mama eva aṃśo jīva-loke jīva-bhūtas sanātanaḥ" iti / idānīm acit-pariṇāma-viśeṣa-bhūtam āditya-ādīnāṃ jyotiṣmatāṃ jyotir api bhagavad vibhūtir ity āha ---
yad ādityagataṃ tejo jagad bhāsayate 'khilam |
children.translated_text: That splendor which, residing in the sun, illuminates the entire world,

children.text: yac candramasi yac cāgnau tat tejo viddhi māmakam ||
children.translated_text: which is in the moon, and which is in fire — know that splendor to be Mine. ||

children.text: yad āditya-gataṃ tejo jagad bhāsayate 'khilam |
yac candra-masi yac ca agnau tat tejo viddhi māmakam ||

body.text: akhilasya jagato bhāsakam eteṣām ādityādīnāṃ yat tejaḥ, tan madīyaṃ tejaḥ tais tair ārādhitena mayā tebhyo dattam iti viddhi //
body.translated_text: The splendor of the sun and the like, which illuminates the entire world — know that to be My splendor, given by Me — who was propitiated by them through various acts of worship — to them. //

children.text: akhilasya jagato bhāsakam eteṣām āditya-ādīnāṃ yat tejaḥ, tan madīyaṃ tejaḥ tais tair ārādhitena mayā tebhyo dattam iti viddhi //

body.text: pṛthivyāś ca bhūtadhāriṇyā dhārakatvaśaktir madīyety āha --
body.translated_text: And the sustaining power of the earth, which supports all beings, is also Mine — He says —

children.text: pṛthivyāś ca bhūta-dhāriṇyā dhārakatva-śaktir madīya īty āha ---
gām āviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmy aham ojasā //
children.translated_text: And entering the earth, I sustain all beings by [My] energy. ||

children.text: puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvās somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And having become the nectareous <s>Soma</s>, full of sap, I nourish all the herbs. ||

children.text: gām āviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmy aham ojasā //
puṣṇāmi ca oṣadhīḥ sarvās somo bhūtvā rasa-ātmakaḥ ||

body.text: ahaṃ pṛthivīm āviśya sarvāṇi bhūtāni ojasā mamāpratihatasāmarthyena dhārayāmi / tathāham amṛtarasamayas somo bhūtvā sarvauṣadhīḥ puṣṇāmi //
body.translated_text: I, entering the earth, sustain all beings by [My] energy — by My irresistible power. Likewise, I, having become the <s>Soma</s> (moon), full of nectareous sap, nourish all the herbs. //

children.text: ahaṃ pṛthivīm āviśya sarvāṇi bhūtāni ojasā mama apratihata-sāmarthyena dhārayāmi / tatha āham amṛta-rasa-mayas somo bhūtvā sarva-oṣadhīḥ puṣṇāmi //
ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ deham āśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: I, having become the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (digestive fire), dwelling in the bodies of living beings, |

children.text: prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmy annaṃ caturvidham //
children.translated_text: joined with the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> breaths, I digest the fourfold food. ||

children.text: ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ deham āśritaḥ /
prāṇa-apāna-samāyuktaḥ pacāmy annaṃ catur-vidham //

body.text: ahaṃ vaiśvānaro jāṭharānalo bhūtvā sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ deham āśritaḥ tair bhuktaṃ khādyacūṣyalehyapeyātmakaṃ caturvidham annaṃ prāṇāpānavṛttibhedasamāyuktaḥ pacāmi //
body.translated_text: I, having become the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> — the gastric fire — dwelling in the bodies of all living beings, joined with the activities of the <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> breaths, I digest the fourfold food — consisting of what is chewed, sucked, licked, and drunk — that has been eaten by them. //

children.text: ahaṃ vaiśvānaro jāṭhara-analo bhūtvā sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ deham āśritaḥ tair bhuktaṃ khādya-cūṣya-lehya-peya-ātmakaṃ catur-vidham annaṃ prāṇa-apāna-vṛtti-bheda-samāyuktaḥ pacāmi //

body.text: atra paramapuruṣavibhūtibhūtau somavaiśvānarau ahaṃ somo bhūtvā, vaiśvānaro bhūtvā iti tatsāmānādhikaraṇyena nirdiṣṭau / tayoś ca sarvasya bhūtajātasya ca paramapuruṣasāmānādhikaraṇyanirdeśahetum āha --
body.translated_text: Here, <s>Soma</s> and <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, which are <s>vibhūtis</s> (glorious manifestations) of the Supreme Person, are designated in co-referential predication with Him as 'I, having become <s>Soma</s>' and 'having become <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.' He states the reason for the co-referential predication (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of them and of all classes of beings with the Supreme Person —

children.text: atra parama-puruṣa-vibhūti-bhūtau soma-vaiśvānarau ahaṃ somo bhūtvā, vaiśvānaro bhūtvā iti tat-sāmānādhikaraṇyena nirdiṣṭau / tayoś ca sarvasya bhūta-jātasya ca parama-puruṣa-sāmānādhikaraṇya-nirdeśa-hetum āha ---
sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtijñānam apohanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me come memory, knowledge, and their removal. |

children.text: vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyo vedāntakṛd vedavid eva cāham //
children.translated_text: By all the <s>Vedas</s> I alone am to be known; I am the author of <s>Vedānta</s> and the knower of the <s>Vedas</s>. ||

children.text: sarvasya ca ahaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛti-jñānam apohanaṃ ca /
vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyo veda-anta-kṛd veda-vid eva ca aham //

body.text:
