tayoḥ somavaiśvānarayoḥ sarvasya ca bhūtajātasya sakalapravṛttinivṛttimūlajñānodayadeśe hṛdi sarvaṃ matsaṃkalpena niyacchan aham ātmatayā sanniviṣṭaḥ / tathāhuḥ śrutayaḥ, "antaḥ praviṣṭaś śāstā janānāṃ sarvātmā", "yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan", "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro ..... yamayati", "padmakośapratīkāśaṃ hṛdayaṃ cāpy adhomukham", "atha yad idam asmin brahmapure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma" ityādyāḥ / smṛtayaś ca, "śāstā viṣṇur aśeṣasya jagato yo jaganmayaḥ", "praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām aṇīyāṃsam aṇīyasām", "yamo vaivasvato rājā yas tavaiṣa hṛdi sthitaḥ" ityādyāḥ / ato matta eva sarveṣāṃ smṛtir jāyate / smṛtiḥ pūrvānubhūtiviṣayam anubhavasaṃskāramātrajaṃ jñānam / jñānam indriyaliṅgāgamayogajo
vastuniścayaḥ; so 'pi mattaḥ / apohanaṃ ca / apohanam -- jñānanivṛttiḥ / apohanam ūhanaṃ vā; ūhanam ūhaḥ; ūho nāma idaṃ pramāṇam itthaṃ pravartitum arhatīti pramāṇapravṛttyarhatāviṣayaṃ sāmagryādinirūpaṇajanyaṃ pramāṇānugrāhakaṃ jñānam; sa coho matta eva / vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ / ato 'gnisūryavāyusomendrādīnāṃ madantaryāmikatvena madātmakatvāt tatpratipādanaparair api sarvair vedair aham eva vedyaḥ, devamanuṣyādiśabdair jīvātmaiva / vedāntakṛd vedānām -- "indraṃ yajeta", "varuṇaṃ yajeta" ity evam ādīnām antaḥ phalam; phale hi te sarve vedāḥ paryavasyanti; antakṛt phalakṛt; vedoditaphalasya pradātā cāham evetyarthaḥ / tad uktaṃ pūrvam eva, "yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitum icchati" ity ārabhya "labhate
ca tataḥ kāmān mayaiva vihitān hi tān" iti, "ahaṃ hi sarvayajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca" iti ca / vedavid eva cāham -- vedavic cāham eva / evaṃ madabhidhāyinaṃ vedam aham eva veda; ito 'nyathā yo vedārthaṃ
brūte na sa vedavid ity abhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: I am seated as the self in the hearts — the locus of the arising of knowledge that is the root of all activity and cessation — of <s>Soma</s>, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, and the entire class of beings, governing all by My will. Thus the <s>śruti</s> passages say: 'Having entered within, the ruler of all beings, the Self of all'; 'He who stands in the earth'; 'He who stands in the self, who is interior to the self... who controls'; 'The heart, resembling a lotus bud, facing downward'; 'Now, in this city of <s>Brahman</s> there is a small lotus dwelling' — and so on. And the <s>smṛti</s> passages say: 'The ruler <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who pervades the universe, is the Lord of the entire world'; 'The ruler of all, smaller than the smallest of the small'; '<s>Yama</s>, the king, son of <s>Vivasvat</s>, who is established in your heart' — and so on. Therefore, memory arises from Me alone for all beings. Memory (<s>smṛti</s>) is knowledge born solely from the latent impressions of previous experience, having previous experience as its object. Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is the ascertainment of an object born from sense-perception, inference, scripture, and <s>yoga</s>; that too is from Me. And removal (<s>apohana</s>) too — <s>apohana</s> means the cessation of knowledge. Or <s>apohana</s> means reasoning (<s>ūhana</s>); reasoning (<s>ūha</s>) is the knowledge that assists a means of valid knowledge, generated by the examination of conditions and the like, pertaining to the fitness of a given means of valid knowledge to operate in a given manner; that reasoning too is from Me alone. And by all the <s>Vedas</s> I alone am to be known — therefore, even by all the <s>Vedas</s> whose purpose is to expound [deities like] <s>Agni</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the like, I alone am to be known, because of their having Me as their inner controller and therefore being ensouled by Me, while [words like] 'god,' 'human,' and the like denote the individual self alone. I am the author of <s>Vedānta</s> (<s>vedāntakṛt</s>) — the 'end' (<s>anta</s>) of the <s>Vedas</s>, i.e., [the statements] such as 'Let one sacrifice to <s>Indra</s>,' 'Let one sacrifice to <s>Varuṇa</s>,' and the like — their 'end' is the fruit; for all those <s>Vedic</s> [injunctions] culminate in their fruit; 'the maker of the end' means 'the maker of the fruit'; meaning: I alone am the bestower of the fruits enjoined by the <s>Vedas</s>. This was stated earlier, beginning with 'Whatever form each devotee wishes to worship with faith' and concluding with 'And he obtains from that the desires that are indeed ordained by Me alone,' and also 'For I alone am the enjoyer and the Lord of all sacrifices.' And I am the knower of the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>vedavit</s>) — I alone know the <s>Vedas</s> that speak of Me. The meaning is: whoever states the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> otherwise than this does not know the <s>Vedas</s>. //

children.text:
tayoḥ soma-vaiśvānarayoḥ sarvasya ca bhūta-jātasya sakala-pravṛtti-nivṛtti-mūla-jñāna-udaya-deśe hṛdi sarvaṃ mat-saṃkalpena niyacchan aham ātmatayā sanniviṣṭaḥ / tathā āhuḥ śrutayaḥ, "antaḥ praviṣṭaś śāstā janānāṃ sarva-ātmā", "yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan", "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro ..... yamayati", "padma-kośa-pratīkāśaṃ hṛdayaṃ ca apy adho-mukham", "atha yad idam asmin brahma-pure daharaṃ puṇḍarīkaṃ veśma" ity-ādyāḥ / smṛtayaś ca, "śāstā viṣṇur aśeṣasya jagato yo jagan-mayaḥ", "praśāsitāraṃ sarveṣām aṇīyāṃsam aṇīyasām", "yamo vaivasvato rājā yas tava eṣa hṛdi sthitaḥ" ity-ādyāḥ / ato matta eva sarveṣāṃ smṛtir jāyate / smṛtiḥ pūrva-anubhūti-viṣayam anubhava-saṃskāra-mātra-jaṃ jñānam / jñānam indriya-liṅga-āgama-yoga-jo
vastu-niścayaḥ; so 'pi mattaḥ / apohanaṃ ca / apohanam --- jñāna-nivṛttiḥ / apohanam ūhanaṃ vā; ūhanam ūhaḥ; ūho nāma idaṃ pramāṇam itthaṃ pravartitum arhati iti pramāṇa-pravṛtty-arhatā-viṣayaṃ sāmagry-ādi-nirūpaṇa-janyaṃ pramāṇa-anugrāhakaṃ jñānam; sa cā uho matta eva / vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ / ato 'gni-sūrya-vāyu-soma-indra-ādīnāṃ mad-antaryāmikatvena mad-ātmakatvāt tat-pratipādana-parair api sarvair vedair aham eva vedyaḥ, deva-manuṣya-ādi-śabdair jīva-ātma aiva / veda-anta-kṛd vedānām --- "indraṃ yajeta", "varuṇaṃ yajeta" ity evam ādīnām antaḥ phalam; phale hi te sarve vedāḥ paryavasyanti; anta-kṛt phala-kṛt; veda-udita-phalasya pradātā ca aham eva ity-arthaḥ / tad uktaṃ pūrvam eva, "yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhaya ārcitum icchati" ity ārabhya "labhate
ca tataḥ kāmān maya aiva vihitān hi tān" iti, "ahaṃ hi sarva-yajñānāṃ bhoktā ca prabhur eva ca" iti ca / veda-vid eva ca aham --- veda-vic ca aham eva / evaṃ mad-abhidhāyinaṃ vedam aham eva veda; ito 'nyathā yo veda-arthaṃ
brūte na sa veda-vid ity abhiprāyaḥ //

body.text: ato matta eva sarvavedānāṃ sārabhūtam artham śṛṇu --
body.translated_text: Therefore, hear from Me alone the essential meaning of all the <s>Vedas</s> —

children.text: ato matta eva sarva-vedānāṃ sāra-bhūtam artham śṛṇu ---
dvāv imau puruṣau loke kṣaraś cākṣara eva ca /
children.translated_text: There are these two <s>Puruṣas</s> in the world: the perishable and the imperishable. |

children.text: kṣaras sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate //
children.translated_text: The perishable is all beings; the immutable is called the imperishable. ||

children.text: dvāv imau puruṣau loke kṣaraś ca akṣara eva ca /
kṣaras sarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭa-stho 'kṣara ucyate //

body.text: kṣaraś cākṣaraś ceti dvāv imau puruṣau loke prathitau / tatra kṣaraśabdanirdiṣṭaḥ puruṣo jīvaśabdābhilapanīyabrahmādistambaparyantakṣaraṇasvabhāvācitsaṃsṛṣṭasarvabhūtāni / atrācitsaṃsargarūpaikopādhinā puruṣa ity ekatvanirdeśaḥ / akṣaraśabdanirdiṣṭaḥ kūṭasthaḥ acitsaṃsargaviyuktaḥ svena rūpeṇāvasthito muktātmā / sa tv acitsaṃsargābhavād acitpariṇāmaviśeṣabrahmādidehāsādhāraṇo na bhavatīti kūṭastha ity ucyate / atrāpy ekatvanirdeśo 'cidviyogarūpaikopādhinābhihitaḥ / na hi itaḥ pūrvam anādau kāle mukta eka eva / yathoktam, "bahavo jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvam āgatāḥ", "sarge 'pi nopajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca" iti //
body.translated_text: These two <s>Puruṣas</s> designated as the perishable (<s>kṣara</s>) and the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>) are well-known in the world. Therein, the <s>Puruṣa</s> designated by the word 'perishable' — to be denoted by the word <s>jīva</s> (living being) — is all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, conjoined with non-conscious [<s>Prakṛti</s>] whose nature is to perish. Here, the singular designation '<s>Puruṣa</s>' [for all of them] is due to the single limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>) of conjunction with non-conscious [<s>Prakṛti</s>]. The <s>Puruṣa</s> designated by the word 'imperishable' is the immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>) — the liberated self (<s>muktātman</s>), separated from conjunction with non-conscious [<s>Prakṛti</s>], abiding in its own form. Since it is free from conjunction with non-conscious [<s>Prakṛti</s>], it does not share in the bodies of <s>Brahmā</s> and the like that are particular modifications of non-conscious [<s>Prakṛti</s>] — hence it is called 'immutable' (<s>kūṭastha</s>). Here too the singular designation is used due to the single limiting condition of separation from non-conscious [<s>Prakṛti</s>]. For it is not that from time immemorial there has been only one single liberated [self]. As stated: 'Many, purified by knowledge and austerity, have attained My state'; 'Even at creation they are not born, nor do they suffer at dissolution.' //

children.text: kṣaraś ca akṣaraś ca iti dvāv imau puruṣau loke prathitau / tatra kṣara-śabda-nirdiṣṭaḥ puruṣo jīva-śabda-abhilapanīya-brahmā-ādi-stamba-paryanta-kṣaraṇa-sva-bhāva-acit-saṃsṛṣṭa-sarva-bhūtāni / atra acit-saṃsarga-rūpa-eka-upādhinā puruṣa ity ekatva-nirdeśaḥ / akṣara-śabda-nirdiṣṭaḥ kūṭa-sthaḥ acit-saṃsarga-viyuktaḥ svena rūpeṇa avasthito mukta-ātmā / sa tv acit-saṃsarga-abhavād acit-pariṇāma-viśeṣa-brahmā-ādi-deha-asādhāraṇo na bhavati iti kūṭa-stha ity ucyate / atra apy ekatva-nirdeśo 'cid-viyoga-rūpa-eka-upādhina ābhihitaḥ / na hi itaḥ pūrvam anādau kāle mukta eka eva / yatha ūktam, "bahavo jñāna-tapasā pūtā mad-bhāvam āgatāḥ", "sarge 'pi na upajāyante pralaye na vyathanti ca" iti //
uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ paramātmety udāhṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> is other [than these two], called the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), |

children.text: yo lokatrayam āviśya bibharty avyaya īśvaraḥ //
children.translated_text: who, entering the three worlds, sustains them — the imperishable Lord. ||

children.text: uttamaḥ puruṣas tv anyaḥ parama-ātma īty udāhṛtaḥ /
yo loka-trayam āviśya bibharty avyaya īśvaraḥ //

body.text:
uttamaḥ puruṣas tu tābhyāṃ kṣarākṣaraśabdanirdiṣṭābhyāṃ baddhamuktapuruṣābhyām anyaḥ arthāntarabhūtaḥ paramātmety udāhṛtaḥ sarvāsu śrutiṣu / paramātmeti nirdeśād eva hy uttamaḥ puruṣo baddhamuktapuruṣābhyāṃ arthāntarabhūta ity avagamyate / katham? yo lokatrayam āviśya bibharti / lokyata iti lokaḥ; tattrayaṃ lokatrayam / acetanaṃ tatsaṃsṛṣṭaś cetano muktaś ceti pramāṇāvagamyam etat trayaṃ ya ātmatayā āviśya bibharti, sa tasmād vyāpyād bhartavyāc cārthāntarabhūtaḥ / itaś coktāl lokatrayād arthāntarabhūtaḥ; yataḥ so 'vyayaḥ, īśvaraś ca; avyayasvabhāvo hi vyayasvabhāvād acetanāt tatsaṃbandhena tadanusāriṇaś ca cetanād acitsaṃbandhayogyatayā pūrvasaṃbandhino muktāc cārthāntarabhūta eva / tathaitasya lokatrayasyeśvaraḥ,
īśitavyāt tasmād arthāntarabhūtaḥ //
body.translated_text: But the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (<s>Uttamaḥ Puruṣaḥ</s>) is other than — is a distinct reality from — these two, the bound and liberated <s>Puruṣas</s> designated by the words 'perishable' and 'imperishable'; He is spoken of as the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) in all the <s>śrutis</s>. By the very designation 'Supreme Self,' it is understood that the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> is a distinct reality from the bound and liberated <s>Puruṣas</s>. How so? He who, entering the three worlds, sustains them. That which is experienced (<s>lokyate</s>) is a world (<s>loka</s>); these three are the three worlds: the non-conscious, the conscious conjoined with it, and the liberated — this triad is to be known through the means of valid knowledge. He who, entering them as their self, sustains them — He is a distinct reality from that which is pervaded and sustained. And further, He is a distinct reality from the stated three worlds because He is imperishable (<s>avyaya</s>) and the Lord (<s>īśvara</s>). For one whose nature is imperishable is indeed a distinct reality from the non-conscious, whose nature is perishable, from the conscious who follows it [<s>Prakṛti</s>] due to conjunction with it, and even from the liberated self who is fit for conjunction with non-conscious [<s>Prakṛti</s>] by virtue of prior conjunction. Likewise, being the Lord of this triad of worlds — He is a distinct reality from what is to be ruled. //

children.text:
uttamaḥ puruṣas tu tābhyāṃ kṣara-akṣara-śabda-nirdiṣṭābhyāṃ baddha-mukta-puruṣābhyām anyaḥ artha-antara-bhūtaḥ parama-ātma īty udāhṛtaḥ sarvāsu śrutiṣu / parama-ātma īti nirdeśād eva hy uttamaḥ puruṣo baddha-mukta-puruṣābhyāṃ artha-antara-bhūta ity avagamyate / katham? yo loka-trayam āviśya bibharti / lokyata iti lokaḥ; tat-trayaṃ loka-trayam / acetanaṃ tat-saṃsṛṣṭaś cetano muktaś ca iti pramāṇa-avagamyam etat trayaṃ ya ātmatayā āviśya bibharti, sa tasmād vyāpyād bhartavyāc ca artha-antara-bhūtaḥ / itaś ca uktāl loka-trayād artha-antara-bhūtaḥ; yataḥ so 'vyayaḥ, īśvaraś ca; avyaya-sva-bhāvo hi vyaya-sva-bhāvād acetanāt tat-saṃbandhena tad-anusāriṇaś ca cetanād acit-saṃbandha-yogyatayā pūrva-saṃbandhino muktāc ca artha-antara-bhūta eva / tatha aitasya loka-trayasyā iśvaraḥ,
īśitavyāt tasmād artha-antara-bhūtaḥ //
yasmāt kṣaram atīto 'ham akṣarād api cottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since I transcend the perishable and am superior even to the imperishable, |

children.text: ato 'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ //
children.translated_text: therefore I am celebrated in the world and in the <s>Vedas</s> as <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person). ||

children.text: yasmāt kṣaram atīto 'ham akṣarād api ca uttamaḥ /
ato 'smi loke vede ca prathitaḥ puruṣa-uttamaḥ //

body.text: yasmād evam uktaiḥ svabhāvaiḥ kṣaraṃ puruṣam atīto 'ham, akṣarān muktād apy uktair hetubhir utkṛṣṭatamaḥ, ato 'haṃ loke vede ca puruṣottama iti prathito 'smi / vedārthāvalokanāl loka iti smṛtir ihocyate / śrutau smṛtau cety arthaḥ / śrutau tāvat, "paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇābhiniṣpadyate, sa uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ" ityādau / smṛtav api, "aṃśāvatāraṃ puruṣottamasya hy anādimadhyāntam ajasya viṣṇoḥ" ityādau //
body.translated_text: Since by the attributes described I transcend the perishable <s>Puruṣa</s>, and since by the reasons stated I am the most excellent even beyond the imperishable, i.e., the liberated [self] — therefore I am celebrated in the world and in the <s>Vedas</s> as <s>Puruṣottama</s>. Since 'world' (<s>loka</s>) is mentioned in juxtaposition with 'the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>,' the word <s>loka</s> here refers to <s>smṛti</s> (traditional literature). The meaning is: in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. In <s>śruti</s>, for instance: 'Approaching the supreme light, he manifests in his own form — he is the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>' and the like. In <s>smṛti</s> also: 'A partial incarnation of <s>Puruṣottama</s>, the beginningless, middleless, and endless <s>Viṣṇu</s>' and the like. //

children.text: yasmād evam uktaiḥ sva-bhāvaiḥ kṣaraṃ puruṣam atīto 'ham, akṣarān muktād apy uktair hetubhir utkṛṣṭatamaḥ, ato 'haṃ loke vede ca puruṣa-uttama iti prathito 'smi / veda-artha-avalokanāl loka iti smṛtir iha ucyate / śrutau smṛtau ca ity arthaḥ / śrutau tāvat, "paraṃ jyotir upasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇa abhiniṣpadyate, sa uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ" ity-ādau / smṛtav api, "aṃśa-avatāraṃ puruṣa-uttamasya hy anādi-madhya-antam ajasya viṣṇoḥ" ity-ādau //
yo mām evam asaṃmūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam /
children.translated_text: He who, thus undeluded, knows Me as the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>) —

children.text: sa sarvavid bhajati māṃ sarvabhāvena bhārata //
children.translated_text: he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being, O <s>Bhārata</s>. ||

children.text: yo mām evam asaṃmūḍho jānāti puruṣa-uttamam /
sa sarva-vid bhajati māṃ sarva-bhāvena bhārata //

body.text: ya evam uktena prakāreṇa puruṣottamaṃ mām asaṃmūḍho jānāti kṣarākṣarapuruṣābhyām, avyayasvabhāvatayā vyāpanabharaṇāiśvaryādiyogena ca visajātīyaṃ jānāti, sa sarvavin matprāptyupāyatayā yad veditavyaṃ tat sarvaṃ veda; bhajati māṃ sarvabhāvena -- ye ca matprāptyupāyatayā madbhajanaprakārā nirdiṣṭāḥ taiś ca sarvair bhajanaprakārair māṃ bhajate / sarvair madviṣayair vedanair mama yā prītiḥ, yā ca mama sarvair madviṣayair bhajanaiḥ, ubhayavidhā sā prītir anena vedanena mama jāyate // ity etat puruṣottamatvavedanaṃ pūjayati --
body.translated_text: He who, in the manner described, knows Me as the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), undeluded — who knows [Me] as dissimilar from the perishable and imperishable <s>puruṣas</s>, by virtue of the imperishable nature, the pervasion, sustenance, sovereignty, and the like — he is all-knowing: he knows everything that is to be known as the means to attaining Me. He worships Me with his whole being — with all the modes of worship that have been prescribed as means to attaining Me, he worships Me. Whatever pleasure I derive from all forms of knowledge directed toward Me, and whatever [pleasure I derive] from all forms of worship directed toward Me — both kinds of that pleasure arise for Me from this knowledge [of My Puruṣottama nature]. // He thus extols this knowledge of the Puruṣottama doctrine:

children.text: ya evam uktena prakāreṇa puruṣa-uttamaṃ mām asaṃmūḍho jānāti kṣara-akṣara-puruṣābhyām, avyaya-sva-bhāvatayā vyāpana-bharaṇa-aiśvarya-ādi-yogena ca visajātīyaṃ jānāti, sa sarva-vin mat-prāpty-upāyatayā yad veditavyaṃ tat sarvaṃ veda; bhajati māṃ sarva-bhāvena --- ye ca mat-prāpty-upāyatayā mad-bhajana-prakārā nirdiṣṭāḥ taiś ca sarvair bhajana-prakārair māṃ bhajate / sarvair mad-viṣayair vedanair mama yā prītiḥ, yā ca mama sarvair mad-viṣayair bhajanaiḥ, ubhaya-vidhā sā prītir anena vedanena mama jāyate // ity etat puruṣa-uttamatva-vedanaṃ pūjayati ---
iti guhyatamaṃ śāstram idam uktaṃ mayānagha /
children.translated_text: Thus this most secret teaching has been imparted by Me, O sinless one.

children.text: etad buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛtakṛtyaś ca bhārata //
children.translated_text: Having understood this, one would become wise and would have accomplished all that is to be accomplished, O <s>Bhārata</s>. ||

children.text: iti guhyatamaṃ śāstram idam uktaṃ maya ānagha /
etad buddhvā buddhimān syāt kṛta-kṛtyaś ca bhārata //

body.text: itthaṃ mama puruṣottamatvapratipādanaṃ sarveṣāṃ guhyānāṃ guhyatamam idaṃ śāstram, "tvam anaghatayā yogyatamaḥ" iti kṛtvā mayā tavoktam / etad buddhvā buddhimāṃs syāt kṛtakṛtyaś ca -- māṃ prepsunā upādeyā yā buddhiḥ sā sarvā upāttā syāt: yac ca tena kartavyam, tat sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ syād ityarthaḥ / anena ślokena, anantaroktaṃ puruṣottamaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ śāstrajanyam evaitat sarvaṃ karoti, na tatsākṣātkārarūpam ity ucyate //
body.translated_text: This teaching that establishes My <s>Puruṣottama</s> nature — the most secret of all secrets — has been imparted by Me to you, since 'you, being sinless, are the most worthy.' Having understood this, one would become wise — all the understanding that is to be attained by one who seeks Me would be attained; and all that is to be done by him would be done — this is the meaning. By this verse it is stated that the knowledge concerning the <s>Puruṣottama</s> that was just described is produced entirely by scripture, and is not of the nature of direct realization [at this stage]. //

children.text: itthaṃ mama puruṣa-uttamatva-pratipādanaṃ sarveṣāṃ guhyānāṃ guhyatamam idaṃ śāstram, "tvam anaghatayā yogyatamaḥ" iti kṛtvā mayā tava uktam / etad buddhvā buddhimāṃs syāt kṛta-kṛtyaś ca --- māṃ prepsunā upādeyā yā buddhiḥ sā sarvā upāttā syāt: yac ca tena kartavyam, tat sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ syād ity-arthaḥ / anena ślokena, anantara-uktaṃ puruṣa-uttama-viṣayaṃ jñānaṃ śāstra-janyam eva etat sarvaṃ karoti, na tat-sākṣāt-kāra-rūpam ity ucyate //

body.text: atītenādhyāyatrayeṇa prakṛtipuruṣayor viviktayoḥ saṃsṛṣṭayoś ca yāthātmyaṃ tatsaṃsargaviyogayoś ca guṇasaṅgatadviparyayahetutvam, sarvaprakāreṇāvasthitayoḥ prakṛtipuruṣayor bhagavadvibhūtitvam, vibhūtimato bhagavato vibhūtibhūtād acidvastunaś cidvastunaś ca baddhamuktobhayarūpād avyayatvavyāpanabharaṇasvāmyair arthāntaratayā puruṣottamatvena yāthātmyañ ca varṇitam / anantaram, uktasya kṛtsnasyārthasya sthemne śāstravaśyatāṃ vaktuṃ śāstravaśyatadviparītayor devāsurasargayor vibhāgaṃ
body.translated_text: In the preceding three chapters, the true nature of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> when differentiated and when conjoined has been described; the attachment to the <s>guṇas</s> and its opposite as the respective causes of bondage and liberation have been stated; the fact that <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> in all their states are the <s>vibhūti</s> (glorious manifestation) of the Lord; and the true nature of the Lord as <s>Puruṣottama</s> — who, by virtue of His imperishable nature, pervasion, sustenance, and sovereignty, is of an utterly different kind from the non-conscious substance and the conscious substance in both its bound and liberated forms that constitute His <s>vibhūti</s> — all this has been described. Next, in order to establish the firmness of all that has been stated by [showing] its dependence on scripture, the division between the divine and demonic creations — which represent conformity to and contravention of scripture —

children.text: atītena adhyāya-trayeṇa prakṛti-puruṣayor viviktayoḥ saṃsṛṣṭayoś ca yāthātmyaṃ tat-saṃsarga-viyogayoś ca guṇa-saṅga-tad-viparyaya-hetutvam, sarva-prakāreṇa avasthitayoḥ prakṛti-puruṣayor bhagavad-vibhūtitvam, vibhūtimato bhagavato vibhūti-bhūtād acid-vastunaś cid-vastunaś ca baddha-mukta-ubhaya-rūpād avyayatva-vyāpana-bharaṇa-svāmyair artha-antaratayā puruṣa-uttamatvena yāthātmyañ ca varṇitam / anantaram, uktasya kṛtsnasya arthasya sthemne śāstra-vaśyatāṃ vaktuṃ śāstra-vaśya-tad-viparītayor deva-asura-sargayor vibhāgaṃ
abhayaṃ sattvasaṃśuddhir jñānayogavyavasthitiḥ |
children.translated_text: Fearlessness, purity of <s>sattva</s>, steadfastness in the <s>yoga</s> of knowledge,

children.text: dānaṃ damaś ca yajñaś ca svādhyāyas tapa ārjavam ||
children.translated_text: charity, self-control, sacrifice, study of the <s>Vedas</s>, austerity, and uprightness,

children.text: abhayaṃ sattva-saṃśuddhir jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitiḥ |
dānaṃ damaś ca yajñaś ca sva-adhyāyas tapa ārjavam ||
ahiṃsā satyam akrodhas tyāgaḥ śāntir apaiśunam |
children.translated_text: non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, tranquility, absence of calumny,

children.text: dayā bhūteṣv aloluptvaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīr acāpalam ||
children.translated_text: compassion toward beings, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and steadiness,

children.text: ahiṃsā satyam akrodhas tyāgaḥ śāntir apaiśunam |
dayā bhūteṣv aloluptvaṃ mārdavaṃ hrīr acāpalam ||
tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucam adroho nātimānitā |
children.translated_text: vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, freedom from malice, and absence of excessive pride —

children.text: bhavanti saṃpadaṃ daivīm abhi jātasya bhārata ||
children.translated_text: these belong to one born to the divine endowment, O <s>Bhārata</s>. ||

children.text: tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ śaucam adroho na atimānitā |
bhavanti saṃpadaṃ daivīm abhi jātasya bhārata ||

body.text:
iṣṭāniṣṭaviyogasaṃyogarūpasya duḥkhasya hetudarśanajaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhayam, tannivṛttir abhayam / sattvasaṃśuddhiḥ sattvasyāntaḥkaraṇasya rajastamobhyām aspṛṣṭatvam / jñānayogavyavasthitiḥ prakṛtiviyuktātmasvarūpavivekaniṣṭhā / dānam nyāyārjitadhanasya pātre pratipādanam / damaḥ manaso viṣayonmukhyanivṛttisaṃśīlanam / yajñaḥ phalābhisandhirahitabhagavadārādhanarūpamahāyajñādyanuṣṭhānam / svādhyāyaḥ savibhūter bhagavatas tadārādhanaprakārasya ca pratipādakaḥ kṛtsno veda ityanusandhāya vedābhyāsaniṣṭhā / tapaḥ kṛcchracāndrāyaṇadvādaśyupavāsāder bhagavatprīṇanakarmayogyatāpādanasya karaṇam / ārjavam manovākkāyavṛttīnām ekaniṣṭhatā pareṣu / ahiṃsā parapīḍāvarjanam / satyam
yathādṛṣṭārthagocarabhūtahitavākyam / akrodhaḥ parapīḍāphalacittavikārarahitatvam / tyāgaḥ ātmahitapratyanīkaparigrahavimocanam / śāntiḥ indriyāṇāṃ viṣayaprāvaṇyanirodhasaṃśīlanam / apaiśunam parānarthakaravākyanivedanākaraṇam / dayā bhūteṣu -- sarvabhūteṣu duḥkhāsahiṣṇutvam / aloluptvam alolupatvam / alolutvam iti vā pāṭhaḥ; viṣayeṣu nisspṛhatvam ityarthaḥ / mārdavam akāṭhinyam, sādhujanasaṃśleṣārhatetyarthaḥ / hrīḥ akāryakaraṇe vrīḍā / acāpalam spṛhaṇīyaviṣayasannidhau acañcalatvam / tejaḥ durjanair anabhibhavanīyatvam / kṣamā paranimittapīḍānubhave 'pi pareṣu taṃ prati cittavikārarahitatā / dhṛtiḥ mahatyām apy āpadi kṛtyakartavyatāvadhāraṇam / śaucam bāhyāntarakaraṇānāṃ kṛtyayogyatā
śāstrīyā / adrohaḥ pareṣv anuparodhaḥ; pareṣu svacchandavṛttinirodharahitatvam ityarthaḥ / nātimānitā -- asthāne garvo 'timānitvam; tadrahitatā / ete guṇāḥ daivīṃ saṃpadam abhijātasya bhavanti / devasaṃbandhinī saṃpad daivī; devā bhagavadājñānuvṛttiśīlāḥ; teṣāṃ saṃpat / sā ca bhagavadājñānuvṛttir eva / tām abhijātasya tām abhimukhīkṛtya jātasya, tāṃ nivartayituṃ jātasya bhavantītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text:
Fear is the suffering born of perceiving the cause of sorrow in the form of separation from the desired and conjunction with the undesired; its cessation is fearlessness. Purity of <s>sattva</s> is the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) being untouched by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>. Steadfastness in the <s>yoga</s> of knowledge is being established in the discrimination of the essential nature of the self as distinct from <s>Prakṛti</s>. Charity is the giving of righteously acquired wealth to a worthy recipient. Self-control (<s>dama</s>) is the habitual practice of turning the mind away from inclination toward sense-objects. Sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>) is the performance of the great sacrifices and the like as worship of the Lord, without desire for the fruit. Study of the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>svādhyāya</s>) is being established in the study of the <s>Vedas</s>, contemplating that the entire <s>Veda</s> teaches the Lord together with His sovereignty and the mode of worshipping Him. Austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is the performance of fasts such as <s>Kṛcchra</s>, <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s>, <s>Dvādaśī</s> observances and the like, which produce fitness for acts that please the Lord. Uprightness (<s>ārjava</s>) is the uniformity of mental, verbal, and bodily dispositions toward others. Non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) is avoidance of causing suffering to others. Truthfulness (<s>satya</s>)
is speech that accords with what is perceived, concerns real objects, and is conducive to the welfare of beings. Freedom from anger (<s>akrodha</s>) is being free from the mental disturbance whose fruit is causing suffering to others. Renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>) is releasing possessions that are opposed to one's own highest good. Tranquility (<s>śānti</s>) is the habitual practice of restraining the senses from their inclination toward objects. Absence of calumny (<s>apaiśuna</s>) is not reporting speech that causes harm to others. Compassion toward beings — being unable to tolerate the suffering of all beings. Non-covetousness (<s>aloluptva</s>) — or <s>alolutva</s> as another reading — means being free from craving toward objects. Gentleness (<s>mārdava</s>) is absence of hardness, meaning fitness for association with virtuous people. Modesty (<s>hrī</s>) is shame in doing what ought not to be done. Steadiness (<s>acāpala</s>) is not being agitated in the proximity of desirable objects. Vigor (<s>tejas</s>) is being incapable of being overwhelmed by the wicked. Forgiveness (<s>kṣamā</s>) is freedom from mental disturbance toward the one who caused suffering, even when experiencing suffering caused by another. Fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>) is maintaining one's course of duty even in great calamity.
Purity (<s>śauca</s>) is the fitness of the external and internal organs for the performance of duties, as prescribed by scripture. Freedom from malice (<s>adroha</s>) is non-obstruction of others; meaning: not restraining others' free conduct. Absence of excessive pride (<s>nātimānitā</s>) — excessive pride is pride in an inappropriate context; freedom from that. These qualities belong to one born to the divine endowment. The endowment connected with the <s>devas</s> is divine; the <s>devas</s> are those whose disposition is to follow the Lord's commands; this is their endowment. And that [endowment] is nothing but following the Lord's commands. One 'born to' it means one born in its direction — meaning: one born to carry it out. //

children.text:
iṣṭa-aniṣṭa-viyoga-saṃyoga-rūpasya duḥkhasya hetu-darśana-jaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhayam, tan-nivṛttir abhayam / sattva-saṃśuddhiḥ sattvasya antaḥ-karaṇasya rajas-tamobhyām aspṛṣṭatvam / jñāna-yoga-vyavasthitiḥ prakṛti-viyukta-ātma-sva-rūpa-viveka-niṣṭhā / dānam nyāya-arjita-dhanasya pātre pratipādanam / damaḥ manaso viṣaya-unmukhya-nivṛtti-saṃśīlanam / yajñaḥ phala-abhisandhi-rahita-bhagavad-ārādhana-rūpa-mahā-yajña-ādy-anuṣṭhānam / sva-adhyāyaḥ sa-vibhūter bhagavatas tad-ārādhana-prakārasya ca pratipādakaḥ kṛtsno veda ity-anusandhāya veda-abhyāsa-niṣṭhā / tapaḥ kṛcchra-cāndrāyaṇa-dvādaśy-upavāsa-āder bhagavat-prīṇana-karma-yogyatā-āpādanasya karaṇam / ārjavam mano-vāk-kāya-vṛttīnām eka-niṣṭhatā pareṣu / ahiṃsā para-pīḍā-varjanam / satyam
yathā-dṛṣṭa-artha-gocara-bhūta-hita-vākyam / akrodhaḥ para-pīḍā-phala-citta-vikāra-rahitatvam / tyāgaḥ ātma-hita-pratyanīka-parigraha-vimocanam / śāntiḥ indriyāṇāṃ viṣaya-prāvaṇya-nirodha-saṃśīlanam / apaiśunam para-anartha-kara-vākya-nivedana-akaraṇam / dayā bhūteṣu --- sarva-bhūteṣu duḥkha-asahiṣṇutvam / aloluptvam alolupatvam / alolutvam iti vā pāṭhaḥ; viṣayeṣu nisspṛhatvam ity-arthaḥ / mārdavam akāṭhinyam, sādhu-jana-saṃśleṣa-arhata īty-arthaḥ / hrīḥ akārya-karaṇe vrīḍā / acāpalam spṛhaṇīya-viṣaya-sannidhau acañcalatvam / tejaḥ durjanair anabhibhavanīyatvam / kṣamā para-nimitta-pīḍā-anubhave 'pi pareṣu taṃ prati citta-vikāra-rahitatā / dhṛtiḥ mahatyām apy āpadi kṛtya-kartavyatā-avadhāraṇam / śaucam bāhya-antara-karaṇānāṃ kṛtya-yogyatā
śāstrīyā / adrohaḥ pareṣv anuparodhaḥ; pareṣu svacchanda-vṛtti-nirodha-rahitatvam ity-arthaḥ / na atimānitā --- asthāne garvo 'timānitvam; tad-rahitatā / ete guṇāḥ daivīṃ saṃpadam abhijātasya bhavanti / deva-saṃbandhinī saṃpad daivī; devā bhagavad-ājñā-anuvṛtti-śīlāḥ; teṣāṃ saṃpat / sā ca bhagavad-ājñā-anuvṛttir eva / tām abhijātasya tām abhimukhī-kṛtya jātasya, tāṃ nivartayituṃ jātasya bhavanti ity-arthaḥ //
dambho darpo 'timānaś ca krodhaḥ pāruṣyam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Ostentation, arrogance, excessive pride, anger, and harshness,

children.text: ajñānaṃ cābhijātasya pārtha sampadam asurīm ||
children.translated_text: and ignorance — these belong to one born to the demonic endowment, O <s>Pārtha</s>. ||

children.text: dambho darpo 'timānaś ca krodhaḥ pāruṣyam eva ca |
ajñānaṃ ca abhijātasya pārtha sampadam asurīm ||

body.text: dambhaḥ dhārmikatvakhyāpanāya dharmānuṣṭhānam / darpaḥ kṛtyākṛtyāvivekakaro viṣayānubhavanimitto harṣaḥ / atimānaś ca svavidyābhijanān anuguṇo 'bhimānaḥ / krodhaḥ parapiḍāphalacittavikāraḥ / pāruṣyam sādhūnām udvegakaraḥ svabhāvaḥ / ajñānam parāvaratattvakṛtyākṛtyāvivekaḥ / ete svabhāvāḥ āsurīṃ saṃpadam abhijātasya bhavanti / asurāḥ bhagavadājñātivṛttiśīlāḥ //
body.translated_text: Ostentation (<s>dambha</s>) is performing <s>dharma</s> for the purpose of proclaiming one's righteousness. Arrogance (<s>darpa</s>) is the elation caused by sense-experience that produces inability to discriminate between what should and should not be done. Excessive pride (<s>atimāna</s>) is self-esteem corresponding to one's own learning and lineage. Anger (<s>krodha</s>) is the mental disturbance whose fruit is causing suffering to others. Harshness (<s>pāruṣya</s>) is a disposition that causes agitation in virtuous people. Ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) is the inability to discriminate between higher and lower realities and between what should and should not be done. These dispositions belong to one born to the demonic endowment. Demons (<s>asuras</s>) are those whose disposition is to transgress the Lord's commands. //

children.text: dambhaḥ dhārmikatva-khyāpanāya dharma-anuṣṭhānam / darpaḥ kṛtya-akṛtya-aviveka-karo viṣaya-anubhava-nimitto harṣaḥ / atimānaś ca sva-vidyā-abhijanān anuguṇo 'bhimānaḥ / krodhaḥ para-piḍā-phala-citta-vikāraḥ / pāruṣyam sādhūnām udvega-karaḥ sva-bhāvaḥ / ajñānam para-avara-tattva-kṛtya-akṛtya-avivekaḥ / ete sva-bhāvāḥ āsurīṃ saṃpadam abhijātasya bhavanti / asurāḥ bhagavad-ājñā-ativṛtti-śīlāḥ //
daivī saṃpad vimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā |
children.translated_text: The divine endowment is deemed to lead to liberation; the demonic [endowment leads] to bondage.

children.text: daivī saṃpad vimokṣāya nibandhāyā asurī matā |

body.text: daivī madājñānuvṛttirūpā saṃpad vimokṣāya bandhān muktaye bhavati / krameṇa matprāptaye bhavatītyarthaḥ / āsurī madājñātivṛttirūpā saṃpan nibandhāya bhavati adhogatiprāptaye bhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The divine endowment, whose form is following My commands, leads to liberation — to freedom from bondage. The meaning is: gradually it leads to attaining Me. The demonic endowment, whose form is transgressing My commands, leads to bondage — the meaning is: it leads to attaining a downward course. //

children.text: daivī mad-ājñā-anuvṛtti-rūpā saṃpad vimokṣāya bandhān muktaye bhavati / krameṇa mat-prāptaye bhavati ity-arthaḥ / āsurī mad-ājñā-ativṛtti-rūpā saṃpan nibandhāya bhavati adho-gati-prāptaye bhavati ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: etac chrutvā svaprakṛtyanirdhāraṇād atibhītāyārjunāyaivam āha --
body.translated_text: Hearing this, to <s>Arjuna</s> who was exceedingly frightened due to being unable to determine his own nature, He spoke thus:

children.text: etac chrutvā sva-prakṛty-anirdhāraṇād atibhītāya arjunāya evam āha ---
mā śucas saṃpadaṃ daivīm abhijāto 'si pāṇḍava ||
children.translated_text: Do not grieve — you are born to the divine endowment, O <s>Pāṇḍava</s>. ||

children.text: mā śucas saṃpadaṃ daivīm abhijāto 'si pāṇḍava ||

body.text: śokaṃ mā kṛthāḥ; tvaṃ tu daivīṃ saṃpadam abhijāto 'si / pāṇḍava / dhārmikāgresarasya hi pāṇḍos tanayas tvam ityabhiprāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Do not grieve; you are born to the divine endowment. O <s>Pāṇḍava</s> — the intent is: for you are the son of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, who was foremost among the righteous. //

children.text: śokaṃ mā kṛthāḥ; tvaṃ tu daivīṃ saṃpadam abhijāto 'si / pāṇḍava / dhārmika-agresarasya hi pāṇḍos tanayas tvam ity-abhiprāyaḥ //
dvau bhūtasargau loke 'smin daiva āsura eva ca |
children.translated_text: There are two types of created beings in this world — the divine and the demonic.

children.text: daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: The divine has been described at length; hear from Me of the demonic, O <s>Pārtha</s>. ||

children.text: dvau bhūta-sargau loke 'smin daiva āsura eva ca |
daivo vistaraśaḥ prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu ||

body.text: asmin karmaloke karmakarāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ sargo dvividhau daivaś cāsuraś ceti / sargaḥ utpattiḥ, prācīnapuṇyapāparūpakarmavaśād bhagavadājñānuvṛttitadviparītakaraṇāyotpattikāla eva vibhāgena bhūtāny utpadyanta ityarthaḥ / tatra daivaḥ sargo vistaraśaḥ proktaḥ -- devānāṃ madājñānuvṛttiśīlānām utpattir yadācārakaraṇārthā, sa ācāraḥ karmayogajñānayogabhaktiyogarūpo vistaraśaḥ proktaḥ / asurāṇāṃ sargaś ca yadācārārthaḥ, tam ācāraṃ me śṛṇu -- mama sakāśāc chṛṇu //
body.translated_text: In this world of action, the creation — the birth — of beings who perform actions is of two kinds: divine and demonic. Creation means birth; meaning: by the force of prior <s>karma</s> in the form of merit and demerit, beings are born at the very time of creation with the division [into those born] for following the Lord's commands and for doing the opposite. Therein, the divine creation has been described at length — the birth of the <s>devas</s>, those whose disposition is to follow My commands, is for the purpose of performing certain conduct; that conduct, in the form of <s>karmayoga</s>, <s>jñānayoga</s>, and <s>bhaktiyoga</s>, has been described at length. And the creation of the demons — the conduct for whose performance [they are born] — hear that from Me. //

children.text: asmin karma-loke karma-karāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ sargo dvi-vidhau daivaś cā asuraś ca iti / sargaḥ utpattiḥ, prācīna-puṇya-pāpa-rūpa-karma-vaśād bhagavad-ājñā-anuvṛtti-tad-viparīta-karaṇāya utpatti-kāla eva vibhāgena bhūtāny utpadyanta ity-arthaḥ / tatra daivaḥ sargo vistaraśaḥ proktaḥ --- devānāṃ mad-ājñā-anuvṛtti-śīlānām utpattir yad-ācāra-karaṇa-arthā, sa ācāraḥ karma-yoga-jñāna-yoga-bhakti-yoga-rūpo vistaraśaḥ proktaḥ / asurāṇāṃ sargaś ca yad-ācāra-arthaḥ, tam ācāraṃ me śṛṇu --- mama sakāśāc chṛṇu //
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidur āsurāḥ |
children.translated_text: Demonic people know neither the path of activity nor the path of cessation;

children.text: na śaucaṃ nāpi cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate ||
children.translated_text: neither purity, nor good conduct, nor truth is found in them. ||

children.text: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidur āsurāḥ |
na śaucaṃ na api cā acāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate ||

body.text: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca abhyudayasādhanaṃ mokṣasādhanaṃ ca vaidikaṃ dharmam āsurā na viduḥ na jānanti / śaucam vaidikakarmayogyatvaṃ śāstrasiddham; tad bāhyam āntaraṃ cāsureṣu na vidyate / nāpi cācāraḥ tad bāhyāntaraśaucaṃ yena sandhyāvandanādinā ācāreṇa jāyate, so 'py ācāras teṣu na vidyate / yathoktam, "saṃdhyāhīno 'śucir nityam anarhas sarvakarmasu" iti / tathā satyaṃ ca teṣu na vidyate yathājñātabhūtahitarūpabhāṣaṇaṃ teṣu na vidyate //
body.translated_text: Demonic people do not know the path of activity and the path of cessation — the Vedic <s>dharma</s> that is the means to prosperity and the means to liberation. Purity — the fitness for Vedic rites as established by scripture — both external and internal, is not found in the demonic. Nor good conduct — that conduct, such as <s>sandhyā</s>-worship and the like, by which both external and internal purity arises — that conduct too is not found in them. As it is stated: 'One who is devoid of <s>sandhyā</s>-worship is always impure, unfit for all [ritual] actions.' Likewise, truth is not found in them — speech that accords with what is known and is in the form of [stating] the welfare of beings is not found in them. //

children.text: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca abhyudaya-sādhanaṃ mokṣa-sādhanaṃ ca vaidikaṃ dharmam āsurā na viduḥ na jānanti / śaucam vaidika-karma-yogyatvaṃ śāstra-siddham; tad bāhyam āntaraṃ cā asureṣu na vidyate / na api cā acāraḥ tad bāhya-antara-śaucaṃ yena sandhyā-vandana-ādinā ācāreṇa jāyate, so 'py ācāras teṣu na vidyate / yathā-uktam, "saṃdhyā-hīno 'śucir nityam anarhas sarva-karmasu" iti / tathā satyaṃ ca teṣu na vidyate yathā-jñāta-bhūta-hita-rūpa-bhāṣaṇaṃ teṣu na vidyate //

body.text: kiṃ ca --
body.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: kiṃ ca ---
asatyam apratiṣṭhaṃ te jagad āhur anīśvaram |
children.translated_text: They say: 'The world is devoid of truth, without a foundation, without a Lord,

children.text: aparasparasaṃbhūtaṃ kim anyat kāmahetukam ||
children.translated_text: not produced by mutual causation — what else? It has desire as its cause.' ||

children.text: asatyam apratiṣṭhaṃ te jagad āhur anīśvaram |
a-paraspara-saṃbhūtaṃ kim anyat kāma-hetukam ||

body.text: asatyam jagad etat satyaśabdanirdiṣṭabrahmakāryatayā brahmātmakam iti nāhuḥ / apratiṣṭham tathā brahmaṇi pratiṣṭhitam iti na vadanti / brahmaṇānantena dhṛtā hi pṛthivī sarvān lokān bibharti / yathoktam, "teneyaṃ nāgavaryeṇa śirasā vidhṛtā mahī / bibharti mālāṃ lokānāṃ sad evāsuramānuṣām" iti / anīśvaram / satyasaṃkalpena pareṇa brahmaṇā sarveśvareṇa mayaitanniyamitam iti ca na vadanti / "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" iti hy uktam / vadanti caivam aparas parasaṃbhūtam; kim anyat / yoṣitpuruṣayoḥ parasparasaṃbandhena jātam idaṃ manuṣyapaśvādikam upalabhyate; anevaṃbhūtaṃ kim anyad upalabhyate ? kiṃcid api nopalabhyata ityarthaḥ / ataḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat kāmahetukam iti //
body.translated_text: 'The world is devoid of truth' — they do not say that this world, being the effect of <s>Brahman</s> designated by the word 'truth' (<s>satya</s>), has <s>Brahman</s> as its self. 'Without a foundation' — likewise they do not say that it is established in <s>Brahman</s>. For the earth, upheld by the infinite <s>Brahman</s>, bears all the worlds. As stated: 'The great earth, upheld on his head by that foremost of serpents, bears the garland of worlds — gods, <s>asuras</s>, and humans.' 'Without a Lord' — they do not say that this is governed by Me, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the Lord of all, whose will is true. For it has been stated: 'I am the source of all; from Me everything proceeds.' And they declare thus: 'produced by mutual [causation]' — what else [could it be]? The world of humans, animals, and the like that is observed is born from the mutual union of female and male; is anything observed that is not of this kind? Nothing else whatsoever is observed — this is the meaning. Therefore, this entire world has desire as its cause. //

children.text: asatyam jagad etat satya-śabda-nirdiṣṭa-brahma-kāryatayā brahma-ātmakam iti nā ahuḥ / apratiṣṭham tathā brahmaṇi pratiṣṭhitam iti na vadanti / brahmaṇa ānantena dhṛtā hi pṛthivī sarvān lokān bibharti / yathā-uktam, "tena iyaṃ nāga-varyeṇa śirasā vidhṛtā mahī / bibharti mālāṃ lokānāṃ sad eva asura-mānuṣām" iti / anīśvaram / satya-saṃkalpena pareṇa brahmaṇā sarva-īśvareṇa maya aitan-niyamitam iti ca na vadanti / "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" iti hy uktam / vadanti ca evam aparas para-saṃbhūtam; kim anyat / yoṣit-puruṣayoḥ paraspara-saṃbandhena jātam idaṃ manuṣya-paśv-ādikam upalabhyate; anevaṃ-bhūtaṃ kim anyad upalabhyate ? kiṃcid api na upalabhyata ity-arthaḥ / ataḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat kāma-hetukam iti //
etāṃ dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno 'lpabuddhayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Holding to this view, [these] lost souls of meager understanding,

children.text: prabhavanty ugrakarmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato 'śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: come forth as doers of cruel deeds, for the destruction of the world, [these] impure ones. ||

children.text: etāṃ dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya naṣṭa-ātmāno 'lpa-buddhayaḥ |
prabhavanty ugra-karmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato 'śubhāḥ ||

body.text: etāṃ dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya avalambya, naṣṭātmānaḥ adṛṣṭadehātiriktātmānaḥ, alpabuddhayaḥ ghaṭādivaj jñeyabhūte dehe jñātṛtvena dehavyatirikta ātmopalabhyata iti vivekākuśalāḥ, ugrakarmāṇaḥ sarveṣāṃ hiṃsakā jagataḥ kṣayāya prabhavanti //
body.translated_text: Holding to this view — clinging to it; lost souls — those who have not perceived the self as distinct from the body; of meager understanding — unskilled in the discrimination that 'the knower is perceived as distinct from the body, which is an object of knowledge like a pot'; doers of cruel deeds — harmful to all; they come forth for the destruction of the world. //

children.text: etāṃ dṛṣṭim avaṣṭabhya avalambya, naṣṭa-ātmānaḥ adṛṣṭa-deha-atirikta-ātmānaḥ, alpa-buddhayaḥ ghaṭa-ādivaj jñeya-bhūte dehe jñātṛtvena deha-vyatirikta ātma upalabhyata iti viveka-akuśalāḥ, ugra-karmāṇaḥ sarveṣāṃ hiṃsakā jagataḥ kṣayāya prabhavanti //
kāmam āśritya duṣpūraṃ dambhamānamadānvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Resorting to insatiable desire, filled with ostentation, vanity, and intoxication,

children.text: mohād gṛhītvāsadgrāhān pravartante 'śucivratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: grasping false tenets through delusion, they operate with impure vows. ||

children.text: kāmam āśritya duṣpūraṃ dambha-māna-mada-anvitāḥ |
mohād gṛhītva āsad-grāhān pravartante 'śuci-vratāḥ ||

body.text: duṣpūram duṣprāpaviṣayaṃ kāmam āśritya tatsisādhayiṣayā mohād ajñānāt, asadgrāhān anyāyagṛhītaparigrahān gṛhītvā, aśucivratāḥ aśāstravihitavratayuktāḥ dambhamānamadānvitāḥ pravartante //
body.translated_text: Resorting to insatiable desire — desire whose objects are difficult to attain — with the wish to accomplish those [desires], through delusion, through ignorance, having grasped false tenets — possessions acquired by unjust means — with impure vows — vows not prescribed by scripture — filled with ostentation, vanity, and intoxication, they operate. //

children.text: duṣpūram duṣprāpa-viṣayaṃ kāmam āśritya tat-sisādhayiṣayā mohād ajñānāt, asad-grāhān a-nyāya-gṛhīta-parigrahān gṛhītvā, aśuci-vratāḥ a-śāstra-vihita-vrata-yuktāḥ dambhamāna-mada-anvitāḥ pravartante //
cintām aparimeyāṃ ca pralayāntām upāśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: Given over to immeasurable anxiety that ends only at death,

children.text: kāmopabhogaparamā etāvad iti niścitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: considering the enjoyment of desires as the highest [goal], convinced that 'this is all there is,' ||

children.text: cintām aparimeyāṃ ca pralaya-antām upāśritāḥ |
kāma-upabhoga-paramā etāvad iti niścitāḥ ||

body.text: adya śvo vā mumūrṣavaḥ cintām aparimeyām -- aparicchedyāṃ pralayāntāṃ prākṛtapralayāvadhikālasādhyaviṣayām upāśritāḥ, tathā kāmopabhogaparamāḥ kāmopabhoga eva paramapuruṣārtha iti manvānāḥ, etāvad iti niścitāḥ ito 'dhikaḥ puruṣārtho na vidyata iti saṃjātaniścayāḥ //
body.translated_text: About to die today or tomorrow, given over to immeasurable anxiety — anxiety that is incalculable, whose object requires time lasting until the cosmic dissolution — and considering the enjoyment of desires as the highest — thinking that the enjoyment of desires alone is the supreme human goal — and convinced that 'this is all there is' — having arrived at the firm conviction that no higher human goal exists. //

children.text: adya śvo vā mumūrṣavaḥ cintām aparimeyām --- aparicchedyāṃ pralaya-antāṃ prākṛta-pralaya-avadhi-kāla-sādhya-viṣayām upāśritāḥ, tathā kāma-upabhoga-paramāḥ kāma-upabhoga eva parama-puruṣa-artha iti manvānāḥ, etāvad iti niścitāḥ ito 'dhikaḥ puruṣa-artho na vidyata iti saṃjāta-niścayāḥ //
āśāpāśaśatair baddhāḥ kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Bound by hundreds of fetters of expectation, devoted to desire and anger,

children.text: īhante kāmabhogārtham anyāyenārthasañcayān ||
children.translated_text: they strive for the accumulation of wealth by unjust means, for the enjoyment of desires. ||

children.text: āśā-pāśa-śatair baddhāḥ kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ |
īhante kāma-bhoga-artham a-nyāyena artha-sañcayān ||

body.text: āśāpāśaśataiḥ āśākhyapāśaśatair baddhāḥ, kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ kāmakrodhaikaniṣṭhāḥ, kāmabhogārtham anyāyenārthasaṃcayān prati īhante //
body.translated_text: Bound by hundreds of fetters called expectations, devoted solely to desire and anger, they strive for the accumulation of wealth by unjust means for the enjoyment of desires. //

children.text: āśa-apāśa-śataiḥ āśa-ākhya-pāśa-śatair baddhāḥ, kāma-krodha-parāyaṇāḥ kāma-krodha-eka-niṣṭhāḥ, kāma-bhoga-artham a-nyāyena artha-saṃcayān prati īhante //
idam adya mayā labdham imaṃ prāpsye manoratham |
children.translated_text: 'This has been obtained by me today; this desire I shall fulfill;

children.text: idam astīdam api me bhaviṣyati punar dhanam ||
children.translated_text: this wealth is mine, and this too shall be mine again.' ||

children.text: idam adya mayā labdham imaṃ prāpsye mano-ratham |
idam asti idam api me bhaviṣyati punar dhanam ||

body.text: idam kṣetraputrādikaṃ sarvaṃ mayā matsāmarthyenaiva labdham, nādṛṣṭādinā; imaṃ ca manoratham aham eva prāpsye, nādṛṣṭādisahitaḥ / idaṃ dhanaṃ matsāmarthyena labdhaṃ me asti, idam api punar me matsāmarthyenaiva bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: 'This — fields, sons, and the like — has all been obtained by me through my own ability alone, not through unseen [merit] and the like. And this desire I alone shall fulfill, not aided by unseen [merit] and the like. This wealth, obtained through my ability, is mine; and this too shall again be mine through my own ability alone.' //

children.text: idam kṣetra-putra-ādikaṃ sarvaṃ mayā mat-sāmarthyena eva labdham, na adṛṣṭa-ādinā; imaṃ ca mano-ratham aham eva prāpsye, na adṛṣṭa-ādi-sahitaḥ / idaṃ dhanaṃ mat-sāmarthyena labdhaṃ me asti, idam api punar me mat-sāmarthyena eva bhaviṣyati //
asau mayā hataḥ śatrur haniṣye cāparān api |
children.translated_text: 'That enemy has been slain by me, and I shall slay others too.' |

children.text: asau mayā hataḥ śatrur haniṣye ca aparān api |

body.text: asau mayā balavatā hataḥ śatruḥ / aparān api śatrūn ahaṃ śūro dhīraś ca haniṣye / kim atra mandadhībhir durbalaiḥ parikalpitenādṛṣṭaparikareṇa //
body.translated_text: 'That enemy has been slain by me, the powerful one. And I, the hero, the steadfast one, shall slay other enemies too. What can these weak-minded, feeble ones accomplish with their imaginary unseen [merit] and its accessories?' ||

children.text: asau mayā balavatā hataḥ śatruḥ / aparān api śatrūn ahaṃ śūro dhīraś ca haniṣye / kim atra manda-dhībhir durbalaiḥ parikalpitena adṛṣṭa-parikareṇa //

body.text: tathā ca --
body.translated_text: And likewise:

children.text: tathā ca ---
īśvaro 'ham ahaṃ bhogī siddho 'haṃ balavān sukhī ||
children.translated_text: 'I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am the accomplished one, I am the powerful and happy one.' ||

children.text: īśvaro 'ham ahaṃ bhogī siddho 'haṃ balavān sukhī ||

body.text: īśvaro 'ham svādhīno 'ham; anyeṣāṃ cāham eva niyantā / ahaṃ bhogī svata evāhaṃ bhogī; nādṛṣṭādibhiḥ / siddho 'ham svatassiddho 'ham; na kasmāccid adṛṣṭādeḥ / tathā svata eva balavān; svata eva sukhī //
body.translated_text: 'I am the lord' — I am self-dependent; and I alone am the controller of others. 'I am the enjoyer' — I am the enjoyer by my own power; not through unseen [merit] and the like. 'I am the accomplished one' — I am self-accomplished; not through any unseen [merit] or the like. Likewise, I am powerful by my own nature; happy by my own nature. ||

children.text: īśvaro 'ham sva-adhīno 'ham; anyeṣāṃ ca aham eva niyantā / ahaṃ bhogī svata eva ahaṃ bhogī; na adṛṣṭa-ādibhiḥ / siddho 'ham svatas-siddho 'ham; na kasmāc-cid adṛṣṭa-ādeḥ / tathā svata eva balavān; svata eva sukhī //
āḍhyo 'bhijanavān asmi ko 'nyo 'sti sadṛśo mayā |
children.translated_text: 'I am wealthy and of noble birth; who else is equal to me?' |

children.text: yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ityajñānavimohitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'I shall sacrifice, I shall give, I shall rejoice' — thus deluded by ignorance. ||

children.text: āḍhyo 'bhijanavān asmi ko 'nyo 'sti sa-dṛśo mayā |
yakṣye dāsyāmi modiṣya ity-ajñāna-vimohitāḥ ||

body.text: ahaṃ svataś cāḍhyo 'smi; abhijanavān asmi svata evottamakule prasūto 'smi; asmin loke mayā sadṛśaḥ ko 'nyaḥ svasāmarthyalabdhasarvavibhavo vidyate? ahaṃ svayam eva yakṣye dāsyāmi, modiṣye ityajñānavimohitāḥ īśvarānugrahanirapekṣeṇa svenaiva yāgadānādikaṃ kartuṃ śakyam ityajñānavimohitā manyante //
body.translated_text: I am wealthy by my own power; I am of noble birth — born of the highest lineage by my own nature. In this world, who else exists equal to me, one who has acquired all splendor by his own prowess? I myself shall sacrifice, I shall give — thus deluded by ignorance, they think that sacrifice, charity, and the like can be accomplished by oneself alone, without dependence on the grace of the Lord. ||

children.text: ahaṃ svataś cā aḍhyo 'smi; abhijanavān asmi svata eva uttama-kule prasūto 'smi; asmin loke mayā sadṛśaḥ ko 'nyaḥ sva-sāmarthya-labdha-sarva-vibhavo vidyate? ahaṃ svayam eva yakṣye dāsyāmi, modiṣye ity-ajñāna-vimohitāḥ īśvara-anugraha-nirapekṣeṇa svena eva yāga-dāna-ādikaṃ kartuṃ śakyam ity-ajñāna-vimohitā manyante //
anekacittavibhrāntā mohajālasamāvṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Bewildered by manifold fancies, enveloped in a net of delusion,' |

children.text: prasaktāḥ kāmabhogeṣu patanti narake 'śucau ||
children.translated_text: 'attached to the enjoyment of desires, they fall into an impure hell.' ||

children.text: aneka-citta-vibhrāntā moha-jāla-samāvṛtāḥ |
prasaktāḥ kāma-bhogeṣu patanti narake 'śucau ||

body.text: adṛṣṭeśvarādisahakāram ṛte svenaiva sarvaṃ kartuṃ śakyam iti kṛtvā, evaṃ kuryām, tac ca kuryām, anyac ca kuryām ity anekacittavibhrāntāḥ, evaṃrūpeṇa mohajālena samāvṛtāḥ, kāmabhogeṣu prakarṣeṇa saktāḥ, madhye mṛtāḥ aśucau narake patanti //
body.translated_text: Thinking that everything can be accomplished by oneself alone without the cooperation of unseen [merit], the Lord, and the like — [thinking] 'I shall do this, and I shall do that, and I shall do yet another thing' — thus bewildered by manifold fancies, enveloped in a net of delusion of such a kind, excessively attached to the enjoyment of desires — dying in the midst [of their pursuits], they fall into an impure hell. ||

children.text: adṛṣṭa-īśvara-ādi-saha-kāram ṛte svena eva sarvaṃ kartuṃ śakyam iti kṛtvā, evaṃ kuryām, tac ca kuryām, anyac ca kuryām ity aneka-citta-vibhrāntāḥ, evaṃ-rūpeṇa moha-jālena samāvṛtāḥ, kāma-bhogeṣu prakarṣeṇa saktāḥ, madhye mṛtāḥ aśucau narake patanti //
ātmasaṃbhāvitāḥ stabdhāḥ dhanamānamadānvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the intoxication of wealth and pride,' |

children.text: yajante nāmayajñais te dambhenāvidhipūrvakam ||
children.translated_text: 'they perform sacrifices in name only, with ostentation, not according to scriptural injunction.' ||

children.text: ātma-saṃbhāvitāḥ stabdhāḥ dhana-māna-mada-anvitāḥ |
yajante nāma-yajñais te dambhena avidhi-pūrvakam ||

body.text: ātmanaiva saṃbhāvitāḥ / ātmanaivātmānaṃ saṃbhāvayantītyarthaḥ / stabdhāḥ paripūrṇaṃ manyamānā na kiṃcitkurvāṇāḥ / katham ? dhanamānamadānvitāḥ dhanena vidyābhijanābhimānena ca janitamadānvitāḥ, nāmayajñaiḥ nāmaprayojanaiḥ yaṣṭetināmamātraprayojanair yajñaiḥ yajante / tad api dambhena hetunā yaṣṭṛtvakhyāpanāya, avidhipūrvakam ayathācodanaṃ yajante //
body.translated_text: Self-conceited — they esteem themselves by themselves; the meaning is: they honor themselves by themselves. Stubborn — considering themselves complete, they do nothing [for self-improvement]. How so? Filled with the intoxication of wealth and pride — intoxicated by the pride generated from wealth and the conceit of learning and noble birth. They perform sacrifices that are in name only — sacrifices whose sole purpose is merely the name, i.e., the designation 'sacrificer.' And even that is performed with ostentation as the motive — for the purpose of advertising themselves as sacrificers — not according to scriptural injunction, not in conformity with the commandments. ||

children.text: ātmana aiva saṃbhāvitāḥ / ātmana aivā atmānaṃ saṃbhāvayanti ity-arthaḥ / stabdhāḥ paripūrṇaṃ manyamānā na kiṃcit-kurvāṇāḥ / katham ? dhana-māna-mada-anvitāḥ dhanena vidyā-abhijana-abhimānena ca janita-mada-anvitāḥ, nāma-yajñaiḥ nāma-prayojanaiḥ yaṣṭa-iti-nāma-mātra-prayojanair yajñaiḥ yajante / tad api dambhena hetunā yaṣṭṛtva-khyāpanāya, avidhi-pūrvakam ayathā-codanaṃ yajante //

body.text: te cedṛgbhūtā yajanta ity āha --
body.translated_text: As to how they, being of such a nature, sacrifice — he says:

children.text: te cā idṛg-bhūtā yajanta ity āha ---
ahaṃkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Resorting to egoism, force, arrogance, desire, and anger,' |

children.text: mām ātmaparadeheṣu pradviṣanto 'bhyasūyakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'envious, they despise Me who dwell in their own and others' bodies.' ||

children.text: ahaṃ-kāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ |
mām ātma-para-deheṣu pradviṣanto 'bhyasūyakāḥ ||

body.text: ananyāpekṣo 'ham eva sarvaṃ karomītyevaṃrūpam ahaṃkāram āśritāḥ, tathā sarvasya karaṇe madbalam eva paryāptam iti ca balam, ato matsadṛśo na kaścid astīti ca darpam, evaṃbhūtasya mama kāmamātreṇa sarvaṃ saṃpatsyata iti kāmam, mama ye aniṣṭakāriṇas tān sarvān haniṣyāmīti ca krodham, evam etān saṃśritāḥ, svadeheṣu paradeheṣu cāvasthitaṃ sarvasya kārayitāraṃ puruṣottamaṃ mām abhyasūyakāḥ pradviṣantaḥ, kuyuktibhir matsthitau doṣam āviṣkurvanto mām asahamānāḥ / ahaṃkārādikān saṃśritā yāgādikaṃ sarvaṃ kriyājātaṃ kurvata ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Resorting to egoism of such a form as 'I alone, depending on no one else, do everything'; and likewise [resorting to] force — 'my strength alone is sufficient for accomplishing everything'; and arrogance — 'therefore no one exists equal to me'; and desire — 'for one such as me, everything will be accomplished by mere wish'; and anger — 'I shall slay all those who act against my wishes' — thus resorting to these, being envious, they despise Me, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), the impeller of all, who abides in their own bodies and in the bodies of others. Being envious — through perverse reasoning, they reveal faults in My existence, they are unable to bear Me. The meaning is: resorting to egoism and the like, they perform all kinds of activities such as sacrifice and the like. ||

children.text: ananya-apekṣo 'ham eva sarvaṃ karomi ity-evaṃ-rūpam ahaṃ-kāram āśritāḥ, tathā sarvasya karaṇe mad-balam eva paryāptam iti ca balam, ato mat-sadṛśo na kaścid asti iti ca darpam, evaṃ-bhūtasya mama kāma-mātreṇa sarvaṃ saṃpatsyata iti kāmam, mama ye aniṣṭa-kāriṇas tān sarvān haniṣyāmi iti ca krodham, evam etān saṃśritāḥ, sva-deheṣu para-deheṣu ca avasthitaṃ sarvasya kārayitāraṃ puruṣa-uttamaṃ mām abhyasūyakāḥ pradviṣantaḥ, ku-yuktibhir mat-sthitau doṣam āviṣkurvanto mām asahamānāḥ / ahaṃ-kāra-ādikān saṃśritā yāga-ādikaṃ sarvaṃ kriyā-jātaṃ kurvata ity-arthaḥ //
tān ahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrān saṃsāreṣu narādhamān |
children.translated_text: 'Those haters, cruel and lowest of humanity, I hurl' |

children.text: kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu ||
children.translated_text: 'perpetually into inauspicious, demonic wombs in the cycles of <s>saṃsāra</s>.' ||

children.text: tān ahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrān saṃsāreṣu nara-adhamān |
kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu ||

body.text: ya evaṃ māṃ dviṣanti, tān krūrān narādhamān aśubhān aham ajasraṃ saṃsāreṣu janmajarāmaraṇādirūpeṇa parivartamāneṣu saṃtāneṣu, tatrāpy āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu kṣipāmi madānukūlyapratyanīkeṣv eva janmasu kṣipāmi / tattajjanmaprāptyanuguṇapravṛttihetubhūtabuddhiṣu krūrāsv aham eva saṃyojayāmītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Those who thus despise Me — those cruel, lowest of humanity, inauspicious ones — I hurl perpetually into the cycles of <s>saṃsāra</s>, revolving in the form of birth, old age, death, and the like, and even there into demonic wombs alone — into births that are opposed to being favorable to Me. The meaning is: I conjoin them with cruel dispositions that generate activities leading to the attainment of those respective births. ||

children.text: ya evaṃ māṃ dviṣanti, tān krūrān nara-adhamān aśubhān aham ajasraṃ saṃsāreṣu janma-jarā-maraṇa-ādi-rūpeṇa parivartamāneṣu saṃtāneṣu, tatra apy āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu kṣipāmi mad-ānukūlya-pratyanīkeṣv eva janmasu kṣipāmi / tat-taj-janma-prāpty-anuguṇa-pravṛtti-hetu-bhūta-buddhiṣu krūrāsv aham eva saṃyojayāmi ity-arthaḥ //
āsurīṃ yonim āpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani |
children.translated_text: 'Having entered demonic wombs, deluded in birth after birth,' |

children.text: mām aprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yānty adhamāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: 'without ever attaining Me, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, they go thence to the lowest destination.' ||

children.text: āsurīṃ yonim āpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani |
mām aprāpya eva kaunteya tato yānty adhamāṃ gatim ||

body.text: madānukūlyapratyanīkajanmāpannāḥ punar api janmani janmani mūḍhāḥ madviparītajñānā mām aprāpyaiva "asti bhagavān sarveśvaro vāsudevaḥ" iti jñānam aprāpya tataḥ tato janmano 'dhamām eva gatiṃ yānti /20//
body.translated_text: Having entered births that are opposed to being favorable to Me, further deluded in birth after birth — possessing knowledge that is the opposite of knowledge about Me — without ever attaining Me, without ever gaining the knowledge that 'the Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the sovereign of all, exists' — from birth after birth, they go to an ever lower destination. ||

children.text: mad-ānukūlya-pratyanīka-janma-āpannāḥ punar api janmani janmani mūḍhāḥ mad-viparīta-jñānā mām aprāpya eva "asti bhagavān sarva-īśvaro vāsudevaḥ" iti jñānam aprāpya tataḥ tato janmano 'dhamām eva gatiṃ yānti /20//

body.text: asyāsurasvabhāvasyātmanāśasya mūlahetum āha --
body.translated_text: He states the root cause of this demonic disposition that is the destruction of the self:

children.text: asya asura-sva-bhāvasyā atma-nāśasya mūla-hetum āha ---
trividhaṃ narakasyaitad dvāraṃ nāśanam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'This threefold gate of hell, destructive of the self:' |

children.text: kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etattrayaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: 'desire, anger, and greed — therefore one should abandon these three.' ||

children.text: tri-vidhaṃ narakasya etad dvāraṃ nāśanam ātmanaḥ |
kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat-trayaṃ tyajet ||

body.text: asyāsurasvabhāvarūpasya narakasyaitat trividhaṃ dvāram, tac cātmano nāśanam; kāmaḥ krodho lobha iti trayāṇāṃ svarūpaṃ pūrvam eva vyākhyātam / dvāram mārgaḥ; hetur ityarthaḥ / tasmād etattrayaṃ tyajet; tasmād atighoranarakahetutvāt kāmakrodhalobhānām, etattritayaṃ dūrataḥ parityajet //
body.translated_text: Of this hell that consists of the demonic disposition — this is the threefold gate, and it is destructive of the self: desire, anger, and greed — their essential nature has been explained previously. 'Gate' means 'path'; the meaning is: 'cause.' Therefore one should abandon these three — therefore, because desire, anger, and greed are the cause of the most terrible hell, one should completely abandon these three from afar. ||

children.text: asya asura-sva-bhāva-rūpasya narakasya etat tri-vidhaṃ dvāram, tac cā atmano nāśanam; kāmaḥ krodho lobha iti trayāṇāṃ sva-rūpaṃ pūrvam eva vyākhyātam / dvāram mārgaḥ; hetur ity-arthaḥ / tasmād etat-trayaṃ tyajet; tasmād atighora-naraka-hetutvāt kāma-krodha-lobhānām, etat-tritayaṃ dūrataḥ parityajet //
etair vimuktaḥ kaunteya tamodvārais tribhir naraḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Released from these three gates of darkness, a person' |

children.text: ācaraty ātmanaḥ śreyas tato yāti parāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: 'practices what is good for the self; thence he goes to the supreme goal.' ||

children.text: etair vimuktaḥ kaunteya tamo-dvārais tribhir naraḥ |
ācaraty ātmanaḥ śreyas tato yāti parāṃ gatim ||

body.text: etaiḥ kāmakrodhalobhaiḥ tamodvāraiḥ madviparītajñānahetubhiḥ vimuko naraḥ ātmanaḥ śreya ācarati labdhamadviṣayajñāno madānukūlye prayatate / tato mām eva parāṃ gatiṃ yāti //
body.translated_text: A person released from these three gates of darkness — desire, anger, and greed, which are the causes of knowledge opposed to Me — practices what is good for the self: having gained knowledge concerning Me, he strives for what is favorable to Me. Thence he goes to Me alone as the supreme goal. ||

children.text: etaiḥ kāma-krodha-lobhaiḥ tamo-dvāraiḥ mad-viparīta-jñāna-hetubhiḥ vimuko naraḥ ātmanaḥ śreya ācarati labdha-mad-viṣaya-jñāno mad-ānukūlye prayatate / tato mām eva parāṃ gatiṃ yāti //

body.text: śāstrānādaro 'sya narakasya pradhānahetur ity āha --
body.translated_text: He says that disregard for scripture is the principal cause of this hell:

children.text: śāstra-anādaro 'sya narakasya pradhāna-hetur ity āha ---
yaḥ śāstravidhim utsṛjya vartate kāmakārataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He who, having cast aside the injunctions of scripture, acts according to his own desire,' |

children.text: na sa siddhim avāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: 'he attains neither perfection, nor happiness, nor the supreme goal.' ||

children.text: yaḥ śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya vartate kāma-kārataḥ |
na sa siddhim avāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim ||

body.text: śāstraṃ vedāḥ; vidhiḥ anuśāsanam / vedākhyaṃ madanuśāsanam utsṛjya yaḥ kāmakārato vartate svacchandānuguṇamārgeṇa vartate, na sa siddhim avāpnoti na kām apy āmuṣmikīṃ siddhim avāpnoti; na sukhaṃ kiṃcid avāpnoti / na parāṃ gatim / kutaḥ parāṃ gatiṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Scripture (<s>śāstra</s>) means the <s>Vedas</s>; injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) means commandment. He who, having cast aside My commandment in the form of the <s>Vedas</s>, acts according to his own desire — follows a path conforming to his own whim — he does not attain perfection: he does not attain any perfection pertaining to the other world; nor any happiness; nor the supreme goal. How indeed could he attain the supreme goal? — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: śāstraṃ vedāḥ; vidhiḥ anuśāsanam / veda-ākhyaṃ mad-anuśāsanam utsṛjya yaḥ kāma-kārato vartate svacchanda-anuguṇa-mārgeṇa vartate, na sa siddhim avāpnoti na kām apy āmuṣmikīṃ siddhim avāpnoti; na sukhaṃ kiṃcid avāpnoti / na parāṃ gatim / kutaḥ parāṃ gatiṃ prāpnoti ity-arthaḥ //
tasmāc chāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te kāryākāryavyavasthitau |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore let scripture be your authority in determining what should and should not be done.' |

children.text: jñātvā śāstravidhānoktaṃ karma kartum ihārhasi ||
children.translated_text: 'Having known what is declared by scriptural injunction, you should act accordingly here.' ||

children.text: tasmāc chāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te kārya-akārya-vyavasthitau |
jñātvā śāstra-vidhāna-uktaṃ karma kartum iha arhasi ||

body.text: tasmāt kāryākāryavyvasthitau upādeyānupādeyavyavasthāyāṃ śāstram eva tava pramāṇam / dharmaśāstretihāsapurāṇādyupabṛṃhitā vedāḥ yad eva puruṣottamākhyaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ tatprīṇanarūpaṃ tatprāptyupāyabhūtaṃ ca karmāvabodhayanti, tac śāstravidhānoktaṃ tattvaṃ karma ca jñātvā yathāvad anyūnātiriktaṃ vijñāya, kartuṃ tvam arhasi -- tad evopādātum arhasi //
body.translated_text: Therefore, in determining what should and should not be done — what is to be adopted and what is not to be adopted — scripture alone is your authority. The <s>Vedas</s>, supplemented by the <s>Dharmaśāstras</s>, <s>Itihāsas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the like — whatever they reveal as the supreme reality named <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person), and whatever action is in the form of propitiating Him and serving as the means for attaining Him — having known that reality and action declared by scriptural injunction properly, completely, neither deficiently nor excessively — you should act: you should adopt that very [practice]. ||

children.text: tasmāt kārya-akārya-vyvasthitau upādeya-anupādeya-vyavasthāyāṃ śāstram eva tava pramāṇam / dharma-śāstra-itihāsa-purāṇa-ādy-upabṛṃhitā vedāḥ yad eva puruṣa-uttama-ākhyaṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ tat-prīṇana-rūpaṃ tat-prāpty-upāya-bhūtaṃ ca karma avabodhayanti, tac śāstra-vidhāna-uktaṃ tattvaṃ karma ca jñātvā yathāvad anyūna-atiriktaṃ vijñāya, kartuṃ tvam arhasi --- tad eva upādātum arhasi //

body.text: devāsuravibhāgoktimukhena prāpyatattvajñānaṃ tatprāptyupāyajñānaṃ ca vedaikamūlam ityuktam / idānīm aśāstravihitasyāsuratvenāphalatvam, śāstravihitasya ca guṇatas traividhyam, śāstrasiddhasya lakṣaṇaṃ cocyate / tatrāśāstravihitasya niṣphalatvam ajānan aśāstravihite śraddhāsaṃyukte yāgādau sattvādinimittaphalabhedabubhutsayā arjunaḥ pṛcchati --
body.translated_text: Through the discourse distinguishing the divine and demonic natures, it has been stated that the knowledge of the truth to be attained and the knowledge of the means for attaining it have the <s>Vedas</s> alone as their root. Now it is stated that what is not enjoined by scripture is fruitless because of its demonic character, and that what is enjoined by scripture is of three kinds according to [the predominance of] the <s>guṇas</s>, and the characteristic of what is established by scripture. Therein, not knowing the fruitlessness of what is not enjoined by scripture, <s>Arjuna</s> asks — with the desire to know the distinction of fruits according to the <s>guṇas</s> (<s>sattva</s> and the rest) in sacrifice and the like that are performed with faith but without scriptural injunction:

children.text: deva-asura-vibhāga-ukti-mukhena prāpya-tattva-jñānaṃ tat-prāpty-upāya-jñānaṃ ca veda-eka-mūlam ity-uktam / idānīm aśāstra-vihitasyā asuratvena aphalatvam, śāstra-vihitasya ca guṇatas traividhyam, śāstra-siddhasya lakṣaṇaṃ ca ucyate / tatra aśāstra-vihitasya niṣphalatvam ajānan aśāstra-vihite śraddhā-saṃyukte yāga-ādau sattva-ādi-nimitta-phala-bheda-bubhutsayā arjunaḥ pṛcchati ---
ye śāstravidhim utsṛjya yajante śraddhayānvitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those who, having set aside the injunctions of scripture, sacrifice with faith —' |

children.text: teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvam āho rajas tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'what is their standing, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? Is it <s>sattva</s>, or <s>rajas</s>, or <s>tamas</s>?' ||

children.text: ye śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya yajante śraddhaya ānvitāḥ |
teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvam āho rajas tamaḥ ||

body.text: śāstravidhim utsṛjya śraddhayānvitā ye yajante, teṣāṃ niṣṭhā kā ? kiṃ sattvam ? āhosvid rajaḥ ? atha tamaḥ ? niṣṭhā sthitiḥ; sthīyate 'sminn iti sthitiḥ sattvādir eva niṣṭhety ucyate / teṣāṃ kiṃ sattve sthitiḥ ? kiṃ vā rajasi ? kiṃ vā tamasītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Those who, having set aside the injunction of scripture, sacrifice endowed with faith — what is their standing? Is it <s>sattva</s>? Or <s>rajas</s>? Or <s>tamas</s>? Standing (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) means 'state'; that in which one is established is the standing — <s>sattva</s> and the like themselves are called the standing. The meaning is: is their establishment in <s>sattva</s>? Or in <s>rajas</s>? Or in <s>tamas</s>? ||

children.text: śāstra-vidhim utsṛjya śraddhaya ānvitā ye yajante, teṣāṃ niṣṭhā kā ? kiṃ sattvam ? āhosvid rajaḥ ? atha tamaḥ ? niṣṭhā sthitiḥ; sthīyate 'sminn iti sthitiḥ sattva-ādir eva niṣṭha īty ucyate / teṣāṃ kiṃ sattve sthitiḥ ? kiṃ vā rajasi ? kiṃ vā tamasi ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭo bhagavān aśāstravihitaśraddhāyās tatpūrvakasya ca yāgāder niṣphalatvaṃ hṛdi nidhāya śāstrīyasyaiva yāgāder guṇatas traividhyaṃ pratipādayituṃ śāstrīyaśraddhāyāḥ traividhyaṃ tāvad āha --
body.translated_text: The Lord, being thus questioned, keeping in mind the fruitlessness of faith not based on scripture and of sacrifice and the like preceded by it, in order to set forth the threefold division according to the <s>guṇas</s> of sacrifice and the like that are scriptural alone — first states the threefold division of scriptural faith:

children.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭo bhagavān aśāstra-vihita-śraddhāyās tat-pūrvakasya ca yāga-āder niṣphalatvaṃ hṛdi nidhāya śāstrīyasya eva yāga-āder guṇatas traividhyaṃ pratipādayituṃ śāstrīya-śraddhāyāḥ traividhyaṃ tāvad āha ---
trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāvajā |
children.translated_text: 'The faith of embodied beings is of three kinds, born of their own nature:' |

children.text: sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: '<s>sāttvika</s>, <s>rājasa</s>, and <s>tāmasa</s> — hear of it.' ||

children.text: tri-vidhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā sva-bhāva-jā |
sāttvikī rājasī ca eva tāmasī ca iti tāṃ śṛṇu ||

body.text: sarveṣāṃ dehināṃ śraddhā trividhā bhavati / sā ca svabhāvajā svabhāvaḥ svāsādhāraṇo bhāvaḥ, prācīnavāsanānimittaḥ tattadruciviśeṣaḥ / yatra ruciḥ tatra śraddhā jāyate / śraddhā hi svābhimataṃ sādhayaty etad iti viśvāsapūrvikā sādhane tvarā / vāsanā ruciś ca śraddhā cātmadharmāḥ guṇasaṃsargajāḥ; teṣām ātmadharmāṇāṃ vāsanādīnāṃ janakāḥ dehendriyāntaḥkaraṇaviṣayagatā dharmāḥ kāryaikanirūpaṇīyāḥ sattvādayo guṇāḥ sattvādiguṇayuktadehādyanubhavajā ityarthaḥ / tataś ceyaṃ śraddhā sāttvikī rājasī tāmasī ceti trividhā / tām imāṃ śraddhāṃ śṛṇu; sā śraddhā yat svabhāvā, taṃ svabhāvaṃ śṛṇv ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The faith of all embodied beings is of three kinds. And it is born of one's own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). One's own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is one's unique disposition — it is the specific taste or inclination caused by latent impressions from previous [births]. Where there is inclination, there faith arises. For faith is eagerness in pursuing the means, preceded by the trust that 'this will accomplish what I consider desirable.' Latent impressions, inclinations, and faith are all properties of the self, born from the conjunction with the <s>guṇas</s>. The causes that generate these properties of the self — latent impressions and the like — are the properties inhering in the body, senses, inner instrument, and sense-objects, definable solely through their effects — these are the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the rest. The meaning is: [these properties are] born from the experience of a body and the like endowed with <s>sattva</s> and the other <s>guṇas</s>. Therefore, this faith is of three kinds: <s>sāttvika</s>, <s>rājasa</s>, and <s>tāmasa</s>. Hear of this faith; the meaning is: hear of the nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of this faith — what nature it has. ||

children.text: sarveṣāṃ dehināṃ śraddhā tri-vidhā bhavati / sā ca sva-bhāva-jā sva-bhāvaḥ sva-asādhāraṇo bhāvaḥ, prācīna-vāsanā-nimittaḥ tat-tad-ruci-viśeṣaḥ / yatra ruciḥ tatra śraddhā jāyate / śraddhā hi sva-abhimataṃ sādhayaty etad iti viśvāsa-pūrvikā sādhane tvarā / vāsanā ruciś ca śraddhā cā atma-dharmāḥ guṇa-saṃsarga-jāḥ; teṣām ātma-dharmāṇāṃ vāsanā-ādīnāṃ janakāḥ deha-indriya-antaḥkaraṇa-viṣaya-gatā dharmāḥ kārya-eka-nirūpaṇīyāḥ sattva-ādayo guṇāḥ sattva-ādi-guṇa-yukta-deha-ādy-anubhava-jā ity-arthaḥ / tataś ca iyaṃ śraddhā sāttvikī rājasī tāmasī ca iti tri-vidhā / tām imāṃ śraddhāṃ śṛṇu; sā śraddhā yat sva-bhāvā, taṃ sva-bhāvaṃ śṛṇv ity-arthaḥ //
sattvānurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata |
children.translated_text: 'The faith of everyone corresponds to his inner nature (<s>sattva</s>), O <s>Bhārata</s>.' |

children.text: śraddhāmayo 'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'This person is constituted of faith; whatever faith one has, that indeed is what one is.' ||

children.text: sattva-anurūpā sarvasya śraddhā bhavati bhārata |
śraddhā-mayo 'yaṃ puruṣo yo yac-chraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ ||

body.text: sattvam antaḥkaraṇam / sarvasya puruṣasyāntaḥkaraṇānurūpā śraddhā bhavati / antaḥkaraṇaṃ yādṛśaguṇayuktam, tadviṣayā śraddhā jāyata ityarthaḥ / sattvaśabdaḥ pūrvoktānāṃ dehendriyādīnāṃ pradarśanārthaḥ / śraddhāmayo 'yaṃ puruṣaḥ / śraddhāmayaḥ śraddhāpariṇāmaḥ / yo yacchraddhaḥ yaḥ puruṣo yādṛśyā śraddhayā yuktaḥ, sa eva saḥ sa tādṛśaśraddhāpariṇāmaḥ / puṇyakarmaviṣaye śraddhāyuktaś cet, puṇyakarmaphalasaṃyukto bhavatīti śraddhāpradhānaḥ phalasaṃyoga ityuktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> [here] means the inner instrument (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>). The faith of every person corresponds to his inner instrument. The meaning is: whatever <s>guṇa</s> the inner instrument possesses, faith directed toward those [corresponding objects] arises. The word <s>sattva</s> here is representative of the previously mentioned body, senses, and the like. 'This person is constituted of faith' — constituted of faith means: he is a transformation of faith. 'Whatever faith one has, that indeed is what one is' — whatever kind of faith a person possesses, he is a transformation of that very kind of faith. If endowed with faith directed toward meritorious action, he becomes conjoined with the fruits of meritorious action — thus it is said that the conjunction with fruits is predominantly [determined] by faith. ||

children.text: sattvam antaḥkaraṇam / sarvasya puruṣasya antaḥkaraṇa-anurūpā śraddhā bhavati / antaḥkaraṇaṃ yādṛśa-guṇa-yuktam, tad-viṣayā śraddhā jāyata ity-arthaḥ / sattva-śabdaḥ pūrva-uktānāṃ deha-indriya-ādīnāṃ pradarśana-arthaḥ / śraddhā-mayo 'yaṃ puruṣaḥ / śraddhā-mayaḥ śraddhā-pariṇāmaḥ / yo yac-chraddhaḥ yaḥ puruṣo yādṛśyā śraddhayā yuktaḥ, sa eva saḥ sa tādṛśa-śraddhā-pariṇāmaḥ / puṇya-karma-viṣaye śraddhā-ayuktaś cet, puṇya-karma-phala-saṃyukto bhavati iti śraddhā-pradhānaḥ phala-saṃyoga ity-uktaṃ bhavati //

body.text: tad eva vivṛṇoti --
body.translated_text: He elaborates on this very [point]:

children.text: tad eva vivṛṇoti ---
yajante sāttvikā devān yakṣarakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The <s>sāttvika</s> ones worship the gods; the <s>rājasa</s> ones, <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>.' |

children.text: pretān bhūtagaṇāṃś cānye yajante tāmasā janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The <s>tāmasa</s> people worship ghosts and hosts of spirits.' ||

children.text: yajante sāttvikā devān yakṣa-rakṣāṃsi rājasāḥ |
pretān bhūta-gaṇāṃś ca anye yajante tāmasā janāḥ ||

body.text: sattvaguṇapracurāḥ sāttvikyā śraddhayā yuktāḥ devān yajante / duḥkhāsaṃbhinnotkṛṣṭasukhahetubhūtadevayāgaviṣayā śraddhā sāttvikītyuktaṃ bhavati / rājasā yakṣarakṣāṃsi yajante / anye tu tāmasā janāḥ pretān bhūtagaṇān yajante / duḥkhasaṃbhinnālpasukhajananī rājasī śraddhā; duḥkhaprāyātyalpasukhajananī tāmasītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Those abundant in the <s>sattva guṇa</s>, endowed with <s>sāttvika</s> faith, worship the gods. What is stated is: faith directed toward the worship of gods, which produces exalted happiness unmixed with suffering, is <s>sāttvika</s>. The <s>rājasa</s> ones worship <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>. Other <s>tāmasa</s> people worship ghosts and hosts of spirits. <s>Rājasa</s> faith generates meager happiness mixed with suffering; <s>tāmasa</s> [faith] generates very meager happiness that is predominantly suffering — this is the meaning. ||

children.text: sattva-guṇa-pracurāḥ sāttvikyā śraddhayā yuktāḥ devān yajante / duḥkha-asaṃbhinna-utkṛṣṭa-sukha-hetu-bhūta-deva-yāga-viṣayā śraddhā sāttviki īty-uktaṃ bhavati / rājasā yakṣa-rakṣāṃsi yajante / anye tu tāmasā janāḥ pretān bhūta-gaṇān yajante / duḥkha-saṃbhinna-alpa-sukha-jananī rājasī śraddhā; duḥkha-prāya ātyalpa-sukha-jananī tāmasi īty-arthaḥ //

body.text: evaṃ śāstrīyeṣv eva yāgādiṣu śraddhāyukteṣu guṇataḥ phalaviśeṣaḥ. aśāstrīyeṣu tapoyāgaprabhṛtiṣu madanuśāsanaviparītatvena na kaścid api sukhalavaḥ, api tv anartha eveti hṛdi nihitaṃ vyañjayan āha --
body.translated_text: Thus, there is a distinction of fruits according to the <s>guṇas</s> only in sacrifice and the like that are scriptural and endowed with faith. In austerity, sacrifice, and the like that are non-scriptural, because they are opposed to My commandment, there is not even a trace of happiness; rather, [there is] only harm. Making clear what has been kept in mind, He says:

children.text: evaṃ śāstrīyeṣv eva yāga-ādiṣu śraddhā-yukteṣu guṇataḥ phala-viśeṣaḥ. aśāstrīyeṣu tapo-yāga-prabhṛtiṣu mad-anuśāsana-viparītatvena na kaścid api sukha-lavaḥ, api tv anartha eva iti hṛdi nihitaṃ vyañjayan āha ---
aśāstravihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those persons who practice austerity that is fierce, not enjoined by scripture,' |

children.text: dambhāhaṅkārasaṃyuktāḥ kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'joined with ostentation and egoism, impelled by desire, passion, and force,' ||

children.text: aśāstra-vihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ |
dambha-ahaṅkāra-saṃyuktāḥ kāma-rāga-bala-anvitāḥ ||
karśayantaḥ śarīrasthaṃ bhūtagrāmam acetasaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'senselessly tormenting the aggregate of elements dwelling in the body,' |

children.text: māṃ caivāntaśśarīrasthaṃ tān viddhy āsuraniścayān ||
children.translated_text: 'and Me also, dwelling within the body — know them to be of demonic resolve.' ||

children.text: karśayantaḥ śarīra-sthaṃ bhūta-grāmam acetasaḥ |
māṃ ca eva antaś-śarīra-sthaṃ tān viddhy āsura-niścayān ||

body.text: aśāstravihitam atighoram api tapo ye janāḥ tapyante / pradarśanārtham idam / aśāstravihitaṃ bahvāyāsaṃ yāgādikaṃ ye kurvate, dambhāhaṃkārasaṃyuktāḥ kāmarāgabalānvitāḥ śarīrasthaṃ pṛthivyādibhūtasamūhaṃ karśayantaḥ, madaṃśabhūtaṃ jīvaṃ cāntaśśarīrasthaṃ karśayanto ye tapyante, yāgādikaṃ ca kurvate; tān āsuraniścayān viddhi / asurāṇāṃ niścaya āsuro niścayaḥ; asurā hi madājñāviparītakāriṇaḥ; madājñāviparītakāritvāt teṣāṃ sukhalavasaṃbandho na vidyate; api tvananarthavrāte patantīti pūrvam evoktam, "patanti narake 'ścau" iti //
