body.translated_text: Those persons who practice austerity that is exceedingly severe yet not prescribed by scripture — this is by way of illustration — who perform sacrifices and the like that are not prescribed by scripture and involve great exertion, who are endowed with hypocrisy and ego, impelled by the force of desire and passion, who mortify the aggregate of elements such as earth and the like which constitute the body, and who mortify the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) — which is a portion of Me — situated within the body: know those who practice such austerities and perform such sacrifices as being of demonic resolve. The resolve of the demons (<s>asuras</s>) is demonic resolve. For the demons act contrary to My commands. Because they act contrary to My commands, they have no connection with even the slightest happiness; rather, they fall into a multitude of calamities — as was stated earlier: 'They fall into foul hell.' //

children.text: aśāstra-vihitam atighoram api tapo ye janāḥ tapyante / pradarśana-artham idam / aśāstra-vihitaṃ bahv-āyāsaṃ yāga-ādikaṃ ye kurvate, dambha-ahaṃkāra-saṃyuktāḥ kāma-rāga-bala-anvitāḥ śarīra-sthaṃ pṛthivy-ādi-bhūta-samūhaṃ karśayantaḥ, mad-aṃśa-bhūtaṃ jīvaṃ ca antaś-śarīra-sthaṃ karśayanto ye tapyante, yāga-ādikaṃ ca kurvate; tān āsura-niścayān viddhi / asurāṇāṃ niścaya āsuro niścayaḥ; asurā hi mad-ājñā-viparīta-kāriṇaḥ; mad-ājñā-viparīta-kāritvāt teṣāṃ sukha-lava-saṃbandho na vidyate; api tvan-anartha-vrāte patanti iti pūrvam eva uktam, "patanti narake 'ścau" iti //

body.text: atha prakṛtam eva śāstrīyeṣu yajñādiṣu guṇato viśeṣaṃ prapañcayati / tatrāhāramūlatvāt sattvādivṛddher āhāratraividhyaṃ prathamam ucyate / "annamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ", "āhāraśuddhau sattvaśuddhiḥ" iti hi śrūyate --
body.translated_text: Now He elaborates on the distinctions based on the <s>guṇas</s> in the very topic at hand — scriptural sacrifices and the like. Since the increase of <s>sattva</s> and the other [<s>guṇas</s>] is rooted in food, the threefold nature of food is stated first. For it is heard in <s>śruti</s>: 'The mind, O dear one, is made of food,' 'When the food is pure, <s>sattva</s> is purified' —

children.text: atha prakṛtam eva śāstrīyeṣu yajña-ādiṣu guṇato viśeṣaṃ prapañcayati / tatrā ahāra-mūlatvāt sattva-ādi-vṛddher āhāra-traividhyaṃ prathamam ucyate / "anna-mayaṃ hi somya manaḥ", "āhāra-śuddhau sattva-śuddhiḥ" iti hi śrūyate ---
āhāras tv api sarvasya trividho bhavati priyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Food too is of three kinds, dear to each person.'

children.text: yajñas tapas tathā dānaṃ teṣāṃ bhedam imaṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: 'Likewise sacrifice, austerity, and charity — hear this distinction of theirs.' ||

children.text: āhāras tv api sarvasya tri-vidho bhavati priyaḥ |
yajñas tapas tathā dānaṃ teṣāṃ bhedam imaṃ śṛṇu ||

body.text: āhāro 'pi sarvasya prāṇijātasya sattvādiguṇatrayānvayena trividhaḥ priyo bhavati / tathaiva yajño 'pi trividhaḥ, tathā tapaḥ dānaṃ ca / teṣām bhedam imaṃ śṛṇu -- teṣām āhārayajñatapodānānāṃ sattvādibhedenemam ucyamānaṃ bhedaṃ śṛṇu //
body.translated_text: Food too, for every class of living beings, becomes dear in three kinds according to its connection with the three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the others. Likewise, sacrifice is also threefold, and so are austerity and charity. Hear this distinction of theirs — hear the distinction of food, sacrifice, austerity, and charity based on [their being] <s>sāttvika</s> and the rest, which is now being stated. //

children.text: āhāro 'pi sarvasya prāṇi-jātasya sattva-ādi-guṇa-traya-anvayena tri-vidhaḥ priyo bhavati / tatha aiva yajño 'pi tri-vidhaḥ, tathā tapaḥ dānaṃ ca / teṣām bhedam imaṃ śṛṇu --- teṣām āhāra-yajña-tapo-dānānāṃ sattva-ādi-bhedena imam ucyamānaṃ bhedaṃ śṛṇu //
āyussattvabalārogyasukhaprītivivardhanāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Foods that increase life, <s>sattva</s>, strength, health, happiness, and contentment,'

children.text: rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'that are savory, unctuous, substantial, and agreeable — are dear to the <s>sāttvika</s> person.' ||

children.text: āyus-sattva-bala-ārogya-sukha-prīti-vivardhanāḥ |
rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvika-priyaḥ ||

body.text: sattvaguṇopetasya sattvamayā āhārāḥ priyā bhavanti / sattvamayāś cāhārā āyurvivardhanāḥ; punar api sattvasya vivardhanāḥ / sattvam antaḥkaraṇam; antaḥkaraṇakāryaṃ jñānam iha sattvaśabdenocyate / "sattvāt saṃjāyate jñānam" iti sattvasya jñānavivṛddhihetutvāt, āhāro 'pi sattvamayo jñānavivṛddhihetuḥ / tathā balārogyayor api vivardhanāḥ / sukhaprītyor api vivardhanāḥ -- pariṇāmakāle svayam eva sukhasya vivardhanāḥ ;tathā prītihetubhūtakarmārambhadvāreṇa prītivardhanāḥ / rasyāḥ madhurarasopetāḥ / snigdhāḥ snehayuktāḥ / sthirāḥ sthirapariṇāmāḥ / hṛdyāḥ ramaṇīyaveṣāḥ / evaṃvidhāḥ sattvamayā āhārāḥ sāttvikasya puruṣasya priyāḥ //
body.translated_text: For a person endowed with the <s>sattva guṇa</s>, foods made of <s>sattva</s> are dear. And foods made of <s>sattva</s> are those that increase life; and further, that increase <s>sattva</s>. <s>Sattva</s> [here] means the inner faculty (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>); the word <s>sattva</s> here refers to knowledge, which is the effect of the inner faculty. Since 'from <s>sattva</s> arises knowledge' — <s>sattva</s> being the cause of the increase of knowledge — food made of <s>sattva</s> too is a cause for the increase of knowledge. Likewise, they increase strength and health. They also increase happiness and contentment — at the time of digestion, they spontaneously increase happiness; and they increase contentment through being the cause of engaging in actions that produce joy. Savory (<s>rasya</s>) — endowed with sweet flavor. Unctuous (<s>snigdha</s>) — possessing oiliness. Substantial (<s>sthira</s>) — producing stable effects upon digestion. Agreeable (<s>hṛdya</s>) — of pleasing appearance. Foods of such a kind, made of <s>sattva</s>, are dear to the <s>sāttvika</s> person. //

children.text: sattva-guṇa-upetasya sattva-mayā āhārāḥ priyā bhavanti / sattva-mayāś cā ahārā āyur-vivardhanāḥ; punar api sattvasya vivardhanāḥ / sattvam antaḥkaraṇam; antaḥkaraṇa-kāryaṃ jñānam iha sattva-śabdena ucyate / "sattvāt saṃjāyate jñānam" iti sattvasya jñāna-vivṛddhi-hetutvāt, āhāro 'pi sattva-mayo jñāna-vivṛddhi-hetuḥ / tathā bala-ārogyayor api vivardhanāḥ / sukha-prītyor api vivardhanāḥ --- pariṇāma-kāle svayam eva sukhasya vivardhanāḥ ;tathā prīti-hetu-bhūta-karma-ārambha-dvāreṇa prīti-vardhanāḥ / rasyāḥ madhura-rasa-upetāḥ / snigdhāḥ sneha-yuktāḥ / sthirāḥ sthira-pariṇāmāḥ / hṛdyāḥ ramaṇīya-veṣāḥ / evaṃ-vidhāḥ sattva-mayā āhārāḥ sāttvikasya puruṣasya priyāḥ //
kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, excessively hot, pungent, dry, and burning'

children.text: āhārā rājasasyeṣṭā duḥkhaśokāmayapradāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'are desired by the <s>rājasa</s> person — they cause pain, grief, and disease.' ||

children.text: kaṭv-amla-lavaṇa-atyuṣṇa-tīkṣṇa-rūkṣa-vidāhinaḥ |
āhārā rājasasya iṣṭā duḥkha-śoka-āmaya-pradāḥ ||

body.text: kaṭurasāḥ, amlarasāḥ, lavaṇotkaṭāḥ, atyuṣṇāḥ, atitīkṣaṇāḥ, rūkṣāḥ, vidāhinaś ceti kaṭvamlalavaṇātyuṣṇatīkṣṇarūkṣavidāhinaḥ / atiśaityātitaikṣṇyādinā durupayogās tīkṣṇāḥ; śoṣakarā rūkṣāḥ; tāpakarā vidāhinaḥ / evaṃvidhā āhārā rājasasyeṣṭāḥ / te ca rajomayatvād duḥkhaśokāmayavardhanāḥ rajovardhanāś ca //
body.translated_text: Bitter in taste, sour in taste, excessively salty, excessively hot, excessively pungent, dry, and burning — these are the foods that are bitter, sour, salty, excessively hot, pungent, dry, and burning. Pungent (<s>tīkṣṇa</s>) — difficult to consume due to excessive coldness, excessive sharpness, and the like. Dry (<s>rūkṣa</s>) — causing desiccation. Burning (<s>vidāhin</s>) — causing a burning sensation. Foods of such a kind are desired by the <s>rājasa</s> person. And they, being made of <s>rajas</s>, increase pain, grief, and disease, and also increase <s>rajas</s>. //

children.text: kaṭu-rasāḥ, amla-rasāḥ, lavaṇa-utkaṭāḥ, atyuṣṇāḥ, atitīkṣaṇāḥ, rūkṣāḥ, vidāhinaś ca iti kaṭv-amla-lavaṇa-atyuṣṇa-tīkṣṇa-rūkṣa-vidāhinaḥ / atiśaitya-atitaikṣṇya-ādinā durupayogās tīkṣṇāḥ; śoṣa-karā rūkṣāḥ; tāpa-karā vidāhinaḥ / evaṃ-vidhā āhārā rājasasya iṣṭāḥ / te ca rajo-mayatvād duḥkha-śoka-āmaya-vardhanāḥ rajo-vardhanāś ca //
yātayāmaṃ gatarasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: 'Food that is stale, tasteless, putrid, leftover,'

children.text: ucchiṣṭam api cāmedhyaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasapriyam ||
children.translated_text: 'as well as leavings and impure — is the food dear to the <s>tāmasa</s> person.' ||

children.text: yāta-yāmaṃ gata-rasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat |
ucchiṣṭam api ca amedhyaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasa-priyam ||

body.text: yātayāmam cirakālāvasthitam; gatarasam tyaktasvābhāvikarasam; pūti durgandhopetam, paryuṣitam kālātipattyā rasāntarāpannam; ucchiṣṭam gurvādibhyo 'nyeṣāṃ bhuktaśiṣṭam; amedhyam ayajñārham; ayajñaśiṣṭam ityarthaḥ / evaṃvidhaṃ tamomayaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasapriyaṃ bhavati / bhujyata iti āhāra eva bhojanam / punaś ca tamaso vardhanam / ato hitaiṣibhiḥ sattvavivṛddhaye sāttvikāhāra eva sevyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Stale (<s>yātayāma</s>) — kept for a long time. Tasteless (<s>gatarasa</s>) — having lost its natural flavor. Putrid (<s>pūti</s>) — having acquired a foul odor. Leftover (<s>paryuṣita</s>) — having, through lapse of time, acquired a different taste. Leavings (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>) — the remnants of the meal of persons other than one's guru and the like. Impure (<s>amedhya</s>) — unfit for sacrifice — meaning: not the remnant of sacrifice. Food of such a kind, made of <s>tamas</s>, is dear to the <s>tāmasa</s> person. And it further increases <s>tamas</s>. Therefore, those who desire their own welfare should consume only <s>sāttvika</s> food for the increase of <s>sattva</s>. //

children.text: yāta-yāmam cira-kāla-avasthitam; gata-rasam tyakta-svābhāvika-rasam; pūti durgandha-upetam, paryuṣitam kāla-atipattyā rasa-antara-āpannam; ucchiṣṭam gurv-ādibhyo 'nyeṣāṃ bhukta-śiṣṭam; amedhyam ayajña-arham; ayajña-śiṣṭam ity-arthaḥ / evaṃ-vidhaṃ tamo-mayaṃ bhojanaṃ tāmasa-priyaṃ bhavati / bhujyata iti āhāra eva bhojanam / punaś ca tamaso vardhanam / ato hita-eṣibhiḥ sattva-vivṛddhaye sāttvika-āhāra eva sevyaḥ //
aphalākāṅkṣibhir yajño vidhidṛṣṭo ya ijyate |
children.translated_text: 'The sacrifice that is offered in accordance with injunction, by those who do not desire the fruit,'

children.text: yaṣṭavyam eveti manas samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'with the mind focused [on the thought] "this must be sacrificed" — that is <s>sāttvika</s>.' ||

children.text: aphala-ākāṅkṣibhir yajño vidhi-dṛṣṭo ya ijyate |
yaṣṭavyam eva iti manas samādhāya sa sāttvikaḥ ||

body.text: phalākāṅkṣārahitaiḥ puruṣaiḥ vidhidṛṣṭaḥ śāstradṛṣṭaḥ mantradravyakriyādibhir yuktaḥ, yaṣṭavyam eveti bhagavadārādhanatvena svayaṃprayojanatayā yaṣṭavyam iti manas samādhāya yo yajña ijyate, sa sāttvikaḥ //
body.translated_text: The sacrifice that is performed by persons free from desire for results, in accordance with injunction — as prescribed by scripture, equipped with proper mantras, materials, rituals, and the like — with the mind focused [on the thought] 'this must be sacrificed,' [considering it] as worship of the Lord and thus an end in itself — that sacrifice is <s>sāttvika</s>. //

children.text: phala-ākāṅkṣā-rahitaiḥ puruṣaiḥ vidhi-dṛṣṭaḥ śāstra-dṛṣṭaḥ mantra-dravya-kriyā-ādibhir yuktaḥ, yaṣṭavyam eva iti bhagavad-ārādhanatvena svayaṃ-prayojanatayā yaṣṭavyam iti manas samādhāya yo yajña ijyate, sa sāttvikaḥ //
abhisandhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārtham api caiva yaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'But that which is offered aiming at the fruit, and also for the sake of ostentation,'

children.text: ijyate bharataśreṣtha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam ||
children.translated_text: 'know that sacrifice to be <s>rājasa</s>, O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>.' ||

children.text: abhisandhāya tu phalaṃ dambha-artham api ca eva yaḥ |
ijyate bharata-śreṣtha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam ||

body.text: phalābhisandhiyuktair dambhagarbho yaśaḥphalaś ca yo yajña ijyate, taṃ yajñaṃ rājasaṃ viddhi //
body.translated_text: The sacrifice that is offered by those with desire for results, containing ostentation at its core, and having fame as its fruit — know that sacrifice to be <s>rājasa</s>. //

children.text: phala-abhisandhi-yuktair dambha-garbho yaśaḥ-phalaś ca yo yajña ijyate, taṃ yajñaṃ rājasaṃ viddhi //
vidhihīnam asṛṣṭānnaṃ mantrahīnam adakṣiṇam |
children.translated_text: 'The sacrifice devoid of scriptural sanction, without food distribution, without mantras, without gifts [to priests],'

children.text: śraddhāvirahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate ||
children.translated_text: 'devoid of faith — they call that sacrifice <s>tāmasa</s>.' ||

children.text: vidhi-hīnam asṛṣṭa-annaṃ mantra-hīnam adakṣiṇam |
śraddhā-virahitaṃ yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate ||

body.text: vidhihīnam brāhmaṇoktihīnam; sadācārayuktair vidvadbhir brāhmaṇair yajasvetyuktihīnam ityarthaḥ; asṛṣṭānnaṃ acoditadravyam, mantrahīnam adakṣiṇaṃ śraddhāvirahitaṃ ca yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate //
body.translated_text: Devoid of scriptural sanction (<s>vidhihīna</s>) — without the authorization of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>; meaning: without the instruction 'sacrifice!' from learned <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who are endowed with good conduct. Without food distribution — with materials that have not been properly dedicated. Without mantras, without gifts [to priests], and devoid of faith — they call that sacrifice <s>tāmasa</s>. //

children.text: vidhi-hīnam brāhmaṇa-ukti-hīnam; sad-ācāra-yuktair vidvadbhir brāhmaṇair yajasva ity-ukti-hīnam ity-arthaḥ; asṛṣṭa-annaṃ acodita-dravyam, mantra-hīnam adakṣiṇaṃ śraddhā-virahitaṃ ca yajñaṃ tāmasaṃ paricakṣate //

body.text: atha tapaso guṇatas traividhyaṃ vaktuṃ tasya śarīravāṅmanoniṣpādyatayā svarūpabhedaṃ tāvad āha --
body.translated_text: Now, in order to state the threefold nature of austerity based on the <s>guṇas</s>, He first states the essential types of austerity, since it is accomplished through body, speech, and mind —

children.text: atha tapaso guṇatas traividhyaṃ vaktuṃ tasya śarīra-vāṅ-mano-niṣpādyatayā sva-rūpa-bhedaṃ tāvad āha ---
devadvijaguruprājñapūjanaṃ śaucam ārjavam |
children.translated_text: 'Worship of the gods, the twice-born, teachers, and the wise; purity, uprightness,'

children.text: brahmacaryam ahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: 'celibacy, and non-violence — this is called bodily austerity.' ||

children.text: deva-dvi-ja-guru-prājña-pūjanaṃ śaucam ārjavam |
brahma-caryam ahiṃsā ca śārīraṃ tapa ucyate ||

body.text: devadvijaguruprājñānāṃ pūjanam, śaucam tīrthasnānādikam, ārjavam yathāmanaḥśarīravṛttam, brahmacaryam yoṣitsu bhogyatābuddhiyuktekṣaṇādirahitatvam, ahiṃsā aprāṇipīḍā; etac charīraṃ tapa ucyate //
body.translated_text: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, teachers, and the wise. Purity — bathing at sacred waters and the like. Uprightness — conduct of body that conforms to the mind. Celibacy — freedom from looking at women with the attitude of enjoyment and the like. Non-violence — not causing suffering to living beings. This is called bodily austerity. //

children.text: deva-dvi-ja-guru-prājñānāṃ pūjanam, śaucam tīrtha-snāna-ādikam, ārjavam yathā-manaḥ-śarīra-vṛttam, brahma-caryam yoṣitsu bhogyatā-buddhi-yukta-īkṣaṇa-ādi-rahitatvam, ahiṃsā aprāṇi-pīḍā; etac charīraṃ tapa ucyate //
anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: 'Speech that causes no agitation, that is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial,'

children.text: svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ caiva vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: 'and the practice of <s>svādhyāya</s> (sacred study) — this is called austerity of speech.' ||

children.text: anudvega-karaṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priya-hitaṃ ca yat |
sva-adhyāya-abhyasanaṃ ca eva vāṅ-mayaṃ tapa ucyate ||

body.text: pareṣām anudvegakaraṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yad vākyaṃ svādhyāyābhyasanaṃ cety etad vāṅmayaṃ tapa ucyate //
body.translated_text: Speech that causes no agitation to others, that is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial; and the practice of <s>svādhyāya</s> — this is called austerity of speech. //

children.text: pareṣām anudvega-karaṃ satyaṃ priya-hitaṃ ca yad vākyaṃ sva-adhyāya-abhyasanaṃ ca ity etad vāṅ-mayaṃ tapa ucyate //
manaḥprasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ maunam ātmavinigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-restraint,'

children.text: bhāvasaṃśuddhir ity etat tapo mānasam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: 'purity of disposition — this is called mental austerity.' ||

children.text: manaḥ-prasādaḥ saumyatvaṃ maunam ātma-vinigrahaḥ |
bhāva-saṃśuddhir ity etat tapo mānasam ucyate ||

body.text: manaḥprasādaḥ manasaḥ krodhādirahitatvam, saumyatvam manasaḥ pareṣām abhyudayaprāvaṇyam, maunaṃ -- manasā vākpravṛttiniyamanam, ātmavinigrahaḥ manovṛtter dhyeyaviṣaye 'vasthāpanam, bhāvaśuddhiḥ ātmavyatiriktaviṣayacintārahitatvam; etan mānasaṃ tapaḥ //
body.translated_text: Serenity of mind — the mind's freedom from anger and the like. Gentleness (<s>saumyatva</s>) — the mind's inclination toward the welfare of others. Silence (<s>mauna</s>) — the restraint of speech-activity by the mind. Self-restraint (<s>ātmavinigraha</s>) — establishing the activity of the mind on the object of meditation. Purity of disposition (<s>bhāvaśuddhi</s>) — freedom from thoughts concerning objects other than the self. This is mental austerity. //

children.text: manaḥ-prasādaḥ manasaḥ krodha-ādi-rahitatvam, saumyatvam manasaḥ pareṣām abhyudaya-prāvaṇyam, maunaṃ --- manasā vāk-pravṛtti-niyamanam, ātma-vinigrahaḥ mano-vṛtter dhyeya-viṣaye 'vasthāpanam, bhāva-śuddhiḥ ātma-vyatirikta-viṣaya-cintā-rahitatvam; etan mānasaṃ tapaḥ //
śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapas tat trividhaṃ naraiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'This threefold austerity, practiced with supreme faith by people'

children.text: aphalākāṅkṣibhir yuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate ||
children.translated_text: 'who do not desire the fruit, who are disciplined — they call it <s>sāttvika</s>.' ||

children.text: śraddhayā parayā taptaṃ tapas tat tri-vidhaṃ naraiḥ |
aphala-ākāṅkṣibhir yuktaiḥ sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate ||

body.text: aphalākāṅkṣibhiḥ phalākāṅkṣārahitaiḥ, yuktaiḥ paramapuruṣārādhanarūpam idam iti cintāyuktaiḥ naraiḥ parayā śraddhayā yat trividhaṃ tapaḥ kāyavāṅmanobhis taptam, tat sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate //
body.translated_text: The threefold austerity — performed by body, speech, and mind — that is practiced by persons free from desire for results, who are disciplined — contemplating that 'this is in the form of worship of the Supreme Person' — with supreme faith: that they call <s>sāttvika</s>. //

children.text: aphala-ākāṅkṣibhiḥ phala-ākāṅkṣā-rahitaiḥ, yuktaiḥ parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-rūpam idam iti cintā-yuktaiḥ naraiḥ parayā śraddhayā yat tri-vidhaṃ tapaḥ kāya-vāṅ-manobhis taptam, tat sāttvikaṃ paricakṣate //
satkāramānapūjārthaṃ tapo dambhena caiva yat |
children.translated_text: 'The austerity that is practiced for the sake of honor, respect, and reverence,'

children.text: kriyate tad iha proktaṃ rājasaṃ calam adhruvam ||
children.translated_text: 'and with ostentation — that is declared here to be <s>rājasa</s>, unstable, and impermanent.' ||

children.text: sat-kāra-māna-pūjā-arthaṃ tapo dambhena ca eva yat |
kriyate tad iha proktaṃ rājasaṃ calam adhruvam ||

body.text: manasā ādaraḥ satkāraḥ, vācā praśaṃsā mānaḥ, śarīro namaskārādiḥ pūjā / phalābhisandhipūrvakaṃ satkārādyarthaṃ ca dambhena hetunā yat tapaḥ kriyate, tad iha rājasaṃ proktam; svargādiphalasādhanatvenāsthiratvāc calam adhruvam / calatvam pātabhayena calanahetutvam, adhruvatvam kṣayiṣṇutvam //
body.translated_text: Honor (<s>satkāra</s>) is regard in the mind; respect (<s>māna</s>) is verbal praise; reverence (<s>pūjā</s>) is bodily [gesture] such as salutation and the like. The austerity that is practiced preceded by desire for results, for the sake of honor and the like, and with ostentation as its motive — that is declared here to be <s>rājasa</s>. Being unstable and impermanent because it is the means for results like heaven and the like. Unstable (<s>cala</s>) — causing unsteadiness due to fear of falling [from attainment]. Impermanent (<s>adhruva</s>) — subject to decay. //

children.text: manasā ādaraḥ sat-kāraḥ, vācā praśaṃsā mānaḥ, śarīro namaskāra-ādiḥ pūjā / phala-abhisandhi-pūrvakaṃ sat-kāra-ādy-arthaṃ ca dambhena hetunā yat tapaḥ kriyate, tad iha rājasaṃ proktam; svarga-ādi-phala-sādhanatvena asthiratvāc calam adhruvam / calatvam pāta-bhayena calana-hetutvam, adhruvatvam kṣayiṣṇutvam //
mūḍhagrāheṇātmano yat pīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The austerity that is practiced with deluded obstinacy, with self-torture,'

children.text: parasyotsādanārthaṃ vā tat tāmasam udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'or for the purpose of destroying another — that is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>.' ||

children.text: mūḍha-grāheṇā atmano yat pīḍayā kriyate tapaḥ |
parasya utsādana-arthaṃ vā tat tāmasam udāhṛtam ||

body.text: mūḍhāḥ avivekinaḥ, mūḍhagrāheṇa mūḍhaiḥ kṛtenābhiniveśena ātmanaḥ śaktyādikam aparīkṣya ātmapīḍayā yat tapaḥ kriyate, parasyotsādanārthaṃ ca yat kriyate, tat tāmasam udāhṛtam //
body.translated_text: The deluded (<s>mūḍha</s>) are the undiscriminating. With deluded obstinacy — with the obstinate fixation adopted by the deluded, without examining one's own capacity and the like — the austerity that is practiced with self-torture, or that is practiced for the purpose of destroying another — that is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>. //

children.text: mūḍhāḥ avivekinaḥ, mūḍha-grāheṇa mūḍhaiḥ kṛtena abhiniveśena ātmanaḥ śakty-ādikam aparīkṣya ātma-pīḍayā yat tapaḥ kriyate, parasya utsādana-arthaṃ ca yat kriyate, tat tāmasam udāhṛtam //
dātavyam iti yad dānaṃ dīyate 'nupakāriṇe |
children.translated_text: 'That gift which is given with the thought "it is to be given," to one who has done no prior service,'

children.text: deśe kāle ca pātre ca tad dānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'at the right place and time, and to a worthy person — that gift is considered <s>sāttvika</s>.' ||

children.text: dātavyam iti yad dānaṃ dīyate 'nupakāriṇe |
deśe kāle ca pātre ca tad dānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam ||

body.text: phalābhisandhirahitaṃ dātavyam iti deśe kāle pātre cānupakāriṇe yad dānaṃ dīyate, tad dānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam //
body.translated_text: Free from desire for results, with the thought 'it is to be given,' at the right place and time, and to a worthy person who has done no prior service — the gift that is given [thus] is considered <s>sāttvika</s>. //

children.text: phala-abhisandhi-rahitaṃ dātavyam iti deśe kāle pātre ca anupakāriṇe yad dānaṃ dīyate, tad dānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam //
yat tu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalam uddiśya vā punaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'But that which is given with an eye to reciprocation, or aiming at the fruit,'

children.text: dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ tad rājasam udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'and given grudgingly — that is declared to be <s>rājasa</s>.' ||

children.text: yat tu pratyupakāra-arthaṃ phalam uddiśya vā punaḥ |
dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ tad rājasam udāhṛtam ||

body.text: pratyupakārakaṭākṣagarbhaṃ phalam uddiśya ca, parikliṣṭam akalyāṇadravyakaṃ yad dānaṃ dīyate, tad rājasam udāhṛtam //
body.translated_text: The gift that is given containing a glance toward reciprocation at its core, aiming at [some] fruit, and grudgingly — with inauspicious materials — that is declared to be <s>rājasa</s>. //

children.text: pratyupakāra-kaṭa-akṣa-garbhaṃ phalam uddiśya ca, parikliṣṭam akalyāṇa-dravyakaṃ yad dānaṃ dīyate, tad rājasam udāhṛtam //
adeśakāle yad dānam apātrebhyaś ca dīyate |
children.translated_text: 'The gift given at the wrong place and time, to unworthy persons,'

children.text: asatkṛtam avajñātaṃ tat tāmasam udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'without respect and with contempt — that is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>.' ||

children.text: adeśa-kāle yad dānam apātrebhyaś ca dīyate |
a-satkṛtam avajñātaṃ tat tāmasam udāhṛtam ||

body.text: adeśakāle apātrebhyaś ca yad dānaṃ dīyate, asatkṛtam pādaprakṣālanādigauravarahitam, avajñātaṃ sāvajñam anupacārayuktaṃ yad dīyate, tat tāmasam udāhṛtam /22//
body.translated_text: The gift given at the wrong place and time, to unworthy persons, without respect — without the honor of washing the feet and the like — and with contempt, given disdainfully, without proper courtesy — that is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>. //

children.text: adeśa-kāle apātrebhyaś ca yad dānaṃ dīyate, a-satkṛtam pāda-prakṣālana-ādi-gaurava-rahitam, avajñātaṃ sa-avajñam anupacāra-yuktaṃ yad dīyate, tat tāmasam udāhṛtam /22//

body.text: evaṃ vaidikānāṃ yajñatapodānānāṃ sattvādiguṇabhedena bheda uktaḥ; idānīṃ tasyaiva vaidikasya yajñādeḥ praṇavasaṃyogena tatsacchabdavyapadeśytayā ca lakṣaṇam ucyate --
body.translated_text: Thus, the distinction of Vedic sacrifices, austerities, and charities based on the division of the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the others — has been stated. Now, the defining characteristic of that very Vedic sacrifice and the like, through its connection with the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> and through its being designated by the words <s>Tat</s> and <s>Sat</s>, is stated —

children.text: evaṃ vaidikānāṃ yajña-tapo-dānānāṃ sattva-ādi-guṇa-bhedena bheda uktaḥ; idānīṃ tasya eva vaidikasya yajña-ādeḥ praṇava-saṃyogena tat-sac-chabda-vyapadeśytayā ca lakṣaṇam ucyate ---
oṃ tat sad iti nirdeśo brahmaṇas trividhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ Tat Sat</s> — this is remembered as the threefold designation of <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: brāhmaṇās tena vedāś ca yajñāś ca vihitāḥ purā ||
children.translated_text: 'By that, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the <s>Vedas</s>, and the sacrifices were ordained of old.' ||

children.text: oṃ tat sad iti nirdeśo brahmaṇas tri-vidhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
brāhmaṇās tena vedāś ca yajñāś ca vihitāḥ purā ||

body.text: oṃ tat sad iti trividho 'yaṃ nirdeśaḥ śabdaḥ brahmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ brahmaṇo 'nvayī bhavati / brahma ca vedaḥ / vedaśabdena vaidikaṃ karmocyate / vaidikaṃ yajñādikam / yajñādikaṃ karma oṃ tat sad iti śabdānvitaṃ bhavati / om iti śabdasyānvayo vaidikakarmāṅgatvena prayogādau prayujyamānatayā; tat sad iti śabdayor anvayaḥ pūjyatvāya vācakatayā / tena trividhena śabdenānvitā brāhmaṇāḥ vedānvayinas traivarṇikāḥ vedāś ca yajñāś ca purā vihitāḥ purā mayaiva nirmitā ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ Tat Sat</s> — this threefold designation, this set of words, is remembered as being connected with <s>Brahman</s> — associated with <s>Brahman</s>. And <s>Brahman</s> is the <s>Veda</s>. By the word '<s>Veda</s>,' Vedic action is meant — Vedic sacrifices and the like. Vedic sacrifices and the like are connected with the words <s>Oṃ Tat Sat</s>. The connection of the word <s>Oṃ</s> is by being employed at the commencement of performance, as an auxiliary of Vedic action. The connection of the words <s>Tat</s> and <s>Sat</s> is by being expressive of veneration. By that threefold set of words, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — the twice-born of the three <s>varṇas</s> who are connected with the <s>Vedas</s> — and the <s>Vedas</s> and the sacrifices were ordained of old — meaning: they were created by Me alone of old. //

children.text: oṃ tat sad iti tri-vidho 'yaṃ nirdeśaḥ śabdaḥ brahmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ brahmaṇo 'nvayī bhavati / brahma ca vedaḥ / veda-śabdena vaidikaṃ karma ucyate / vaidikaṃ yajña-ādikam / yajña-ādikaṃ karma oṃ tat sad iti śabda-anvitaṃ bhavati / om iti śabdasya anvayo vaidika-karma-aṅgatvena prayoga-ādau prayujyamānatayā; tat sad iti śabdayor anvayaḥ pūjyatvāya vācakatayā / tena tri-vidhena śabdena anvitā brāhmaṇāḥ veda-anvayinas traivarṇikāḥ vedāś ca yajñāś ca purā vihitāḥ purā maya aiva nirmitā ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: trayāṇām oṃ tat sad iti śabdānām anvayaprakāro varṇyate; prathamam om iti śabdasyānvayaprakāram āha --
body.translated_text: The manner of connection of the three words — <s>Oṃ</s>, <s>Tat</s>, and <s>Sat</s> — is described. First, He states the manner of connection of the word <s>Oṃ</s> —

children.text: trayāṇām oṃ tat sad iti śabdānām anvaya-prakāro varṇyate; prathamam om iti śabdasya anvaya-prakāram āha ---
tasmād om ity udāhṛtya yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, having uttered <s>Oṃ</s>, the acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity'

children.text: pravartante vidhānoktāḥ satataṃ brahmavādinām ||
children.translated_text: 'of the expounders of <s>Brahman</s> always commence as prescribed by ordinance.' ||

children.text: tasmād om ity udāhṛtya yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ |
pravartante vidhāna-uktāḥ satataṃ brahma-vādinām ||

body.text: tasmād brahmavādinām vedādināṃ traivarṇikānāṃ yajñadānatapaḥkriyāḥ vidhānoktāḥ vedavidhānoktāḥ ādau om ity udāhṛtya satataṃ sarvadā pravartante / vedāś ca om ity udāhṛtyārabhyante / evaṃ vedānāṃ vaidikānāṃ ca yajñādīnāṃ karmaṇām om iti śabdānvayo varṇitaḥ / om itiśabdānvitavedadhāraṇāt tadanvitayajñādikarmakaraṇāc ca brāhmaṇaśabdanirdiṣṭānāṃ traivarṇikānām api om iti śabdānvayo varṇitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore, the acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity of the expounders of <s>Brahman</s> — the twice-born of the three <s>varṇas</s> — as prescribed by Vedic ordinance, always commence having first uttered <s>Oṃ</s>. The <s>Vedas</s> too are commenced having uttered <s>Oṃ</s>. Thus, the connection of the word <s>Oṃ</s> with the <s>Vedas</s> and with the Vedic actions such as sacrifices and the like has been described. And since the twice-born designated by the word <s>brāhmaṇa</s> bear the <s>Vedas</s> connected with the word <s>Oṃ</s> and perform sacrificial actions connected with it, their connection with the word <s>Oṃ</s> too has been described. //

children.text: tasmād brahma-vādinām veda-ādināṃ traivarṇikānāṃ yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ vidhāna-uktāḥ veda-vidhāna-uktāḥ ādau om ity udāhṛtya satataṃ sarvadā pravartante / vedāś ca om ity udāhṛtyā arabhyante / evaṃ vedānāṃ vaidikānāṃ ca yajña-ādīnāṃ karmaṇām om iti śabda-anvayo varṇitaḥ / om iti-śabda-anvita-veda-dhāraṇāt tad-anvita-yajña-ādi-karma-karaṇāc ca brāhmaṇa-śabda-nirdiṣṭānāṃ traivarṇikānām api om iti śabda-anvayo varṇitaḥ //

body.text: athaiteṣāṃ tad iti śabdānvayaprakāram āha --
body.translated_text: Now He states the manner of connection of the word <s>Tat</s> with these —

children.text: atha eteṣāṃ tad iti śabda-anvaya-prakāram āha ---
tad ity anabhisandhāya phalaṃ yajñatapaḥkriyāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Uttering <s>Tat</s>, without aiming at the fruit, the acts of sacrifice and austerity'

children.text: dānakriyāś ca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣakāṅkṣibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'and the various acts of charity are performed by the seekers of liberation.' ||

children.text: tad ity anabhisandhāya phalaṃ yajña-tapaḥ-kriyāḥ |
dāna-kriyāś ca vividhāḥ kriyante mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhiḥ ||

body.text: phalam anabhisandhāya vedādhyayanayajñatapodānakriyāḥ mokṣakāṅkṣibhis traivarṇikair yāḥ kriyante, tāḥ brahmaprāptisādhanatayā brahmavācinā tad iti śabdena nirdeśyāḥ; "sa vaḥ kaḥ kiṃ yat tat padam anuttamam" iti tacchabdo hi brahmavācī prasiddhaḥ / evaṃ vedādhyayanayajñādīnāṃ mokṣasādhanabhūtānāṃ tacchabdanirdeśyatayā tad iti śabdānvaya uktaḥ / traivarṇikānām api tathāvidhavedādhyayanādyanuṣṭhānād eva tacchabdānvaya upapannaḥ //
body.translated_text: The acts of Vedic study, sacrifice, austerity, and charity that are performed by the seekers of liberation — the twice-born of the three <s>varṇas</s> — without aiming at the fruit: those are to be designated by the word <s>Tat</s>, which denotes <s>Brahman</s>, because they are the means of attaining <s>Brahman</s>. For the word <s>Tat</s> is well-known as denoting <s>Brahman</s>: 'What is He — what, which — that is the unsurpassed abode.' Thus, the connection of the word <s>Tat</s> with Vedic study, sacrifice, and the like that serve as the means of liberation, by being designated by it, is stated. And the connection of the twice-born too, through their performance of such Vedic study and the like, with the word <s>Tat</s> is established. //

children.text: phalam anabhisandhāya veda-adhyayana-yajña-tapo-dāna-kriyāḥ mokṣa-kāṅkṣibhis traivarṇikair yāḥ kriyante, tāḥ brahma-prāpti-sādhanatayā brahma-vācinā tad iti śabdena nirdeśyāḥ; "sa vaḥ kaḥ kiṃ yat tat padam anuttamam" iti tac-chabdo hi brahma-vācī prasiddhaḥ / evaṃ veda-adhyayana-yajña-ādīnāṃ mokṣa-sādhana-bhūtānāṃ tac-chabda-nirdeśyatayā tad iti śabda-anvaya uktaḥ / traivarṇikānām api tathā-vidha-veda-adhyayana-ādy-anuṣṭhānād eva tac-chabda-anvaya upapannaḥ //

body.text: athaiṣāṃ sacchabdānvayaprakāraṃ vaktuṃ loke sacchabdasya vyutpattiprakāram āha --
body.translated_text: Now, to state the manner of connection of the word <s>Sat</s> with these, He states the manner of usage of the word <s>Sat</s> in common parlance —

children.text: atha eṣāṃ sac-chabda-anvaya-prakāraṃ vaktuṃ loke sac-chabdasya vyutpatti-prakāram āha ---
sadbhāve sādhubhāve ca sad ity etat prayujyate |
children.translated_text: 'In the sense of existence and in the sense of goodness, the word <s>sat</s> is used.' |

children.text: praśaste karmaṇi tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate ||
children.translated_text: 'And likewise, the word <s>sat</s> is applied to praiseworthy action, O <s>Pārtha</s>.' ||

children.text: sad-bhāve sādhu-bhāve ca sad ity etat prayujyate |
praśaste karmaṇi tathā sac-chabdaḥ pārtha yujyate ||

body.text: sadbhāve vidyamānatāyām, sādhubhāve kalyāṇabhāve ca sarvavastuṣu sad ity etat padaṃ prayujyate lokavedayoḥ / tathā kenacit puruṣeṇānuṣṭhite laukike praśaste kalyāṇe karmaṇi satkarmedam iti sacchabdo yujyate prayujyate ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'In the sense of existence' — regarding existing reality; 'and in the sense of goodness' — in the sense of being auspicious — the word <s>sat</s> is used with respect to all things, both in common usage and in the <s>Vedas</s>. Likewise, when a praiseworthy, auspicious worldly action has been performed by someone, the word <s>sat</s> is applied, used, as in 'this is a good (<s>sat</s>) action' — this is the meaning. //

children.text: sad-bhāve vidyamānatāyām, sādhu-bhāve kalyāṇa-bhāve ca sarva-vastuṣu sad ity etat padaṃ prayujyate loka-vedayoḥ / tathā kenacit puruṣeṇa anuṣṭhite laukike praśaste kalyāṇe karmaṇi sat-karma idam iti sac-chabdo yujyate prayujyate ity-arthaḥ //
yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ sad iti cocyate |
children.translated_text: 'Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and charity is also called <s>sat</s>.' |

children.text: karma caiva tadarthīyaṃ sad ity evābhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: 'And action undertaken for those purposes is likewise declared as <s>sat</s>.' ||

children.text: yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ sad iti ca ucyate |
karma ca eva tad-arthīyaṃ sad ity eva abhidhīyate ||

body.text: ato vaidikānāṃ traivarṇikānāṃ yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ kalyāṇatayā sad ity ucyate / karma ca tadarthīyam traivarṇikārthīyaṃ yajñadānādikaṃ sad ity evābhidhīyate / tasmād vedāḥ vaidikāni karmāṇi brāhmaṇaśabdanirdiṣṭās traivarṇikāś ca oṃ tat sad iti śabdānvayarūpalakṣaṇena avedebhyaś cāvaidikebhyaś ca vyāvṛttā veditavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: Therefore, for the Vedic adherents of the three <s>varṇas</s>, steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and charity is called <s>sat</s> on account of being auspicious. And action undertaken for their sake — sacrifice, charity, and the like pertaining to the three <s>varṇas</s> — is likewise declared as <s>sat</s>. Therefore, the <s>Vedas</s>, Vedic rites, and the members of the three <s>varṇas</s> designated by the word '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' are to be known as distinguished from non-Vedic [texts] and non-Vedic [persons] by the characteristic of being connected with the words <s>Om Tat Sat</s>. //

children.text: ato vaidikānāṃ traivarṇikānāṃ yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ kalyāṇatayā sad ity ucyate / karma ca tad-arthīyam traivarṇika-arthīyaṃ yajña-dāna-ādikaṃ sad ity eva abhidhīyate / tasmād vedāḥ vaidikāni karmāṇi brāhmaṇa-śabda-nirdiṣṭās traivarṇikāś ca oṃ tat sad iti śabda-anvaya-rūpa-lakṣaṇena avedebhyaś ca avaidikebhyaś ca vyāvṛttā veditavyāḥ //
aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapas taptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: 'Whatever is offered, given, or practiced as austerity without faith,' |

children.text: asad ity ucyate pārtha na ca tat pretya no iha ||
children.translated_text: 'is called <s>asat</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>, and it is of no avail after death or here.' ||

children.text: aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapas taptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat |
asad ity ucyate pārtha na ca tat pretya no iha ||

body.text: aśraddhayā kṛtaṃ śāstrīyam api homādikam asad ity ucyate / kutaḥ ? na ca tat pretya, no iha na mokṣāya, na sāṃsārikāya ca phalāyeti //
body.translated_text: Even a scriptural act such as oblation and the like, when performed without faith, is called <s>asat</s>. Why? Because it is of no avail after death — not for liberation — nor here — not for any worldly result either. //

children.text: aśraddhayā kṛtaṃ śāstrīyam api homa-ādikam asad ity ucyate / kutaḥ ? na ca tat pretya, no iha na mokṣāya, na sāṃsārikāya ca phalāya iti //

body.text:
atītenādhyāyadvayena -- abhyudayaniśśreyasasādhanabhūtaṃ vaidikam eva yajñatapodānādikaṃ karma, nānyat; vaidikasya ca karmaṇas sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ praṇavānvayaḥ; tatra mokṣābhyudayasādhanayor bhedaḥ tatsacchabdanirdeśyatvena; mokṣasādhanaṃ ca karma phalābhisandhirahitaṃ yajñādikam; tadārambhaś ca sattvodrekād bhavati; sattvavṛddhiś ca sāttvikāhārasevayā ityuktam / anantaraṃ mokṣasādhanatayā nirdiṣṭayos tyāgasaṃnyāsayor aikyam, tyāgasya ca svarūpam, bhagavati sarveśvare ca sarvakarmaṇāṃ kartṛtvānusandhānam, sattvarajastamasāṃ kāryavarṇanena sattvaguṇasyāvaśyopādeyatvam, svavarṇocitānāṃ karmaṇāṃ paramapuruṣārādhanabhūtānāṃ paramapuruṣaprāptinirvartanaprakāraḥ, kṛtsnasya gītāśāstrasya sārārtho bhaktiyoga ity ete
pratipādyante / tatra tāvat tyāgasaṃnyāsayor pṛthaktvaikatvanirṇayāya svarūpanirṇayāya cārjunaḥ pṛcchati --
body.translated_text: In the preceding two chapters [it was established]: only Vedic action in the form of sacrifice, austerity, charity, and the like is the means to worldly prosperity and to the supreme good — nothing else; and the general characteristic of Vedic action is its connection with the syllable <s>Om</s>; therein, the distinction between the means to liberation and the means to worldly prosperity is indicated by their being designable by the word <s>sat</s>; and the action that is a means to liberation consists of sacrifice and the like performed without attachment to results; and the commencement of such [action] arises from the predominance of <s>sattva</s>; and the increase of <s>sattva</s> comes through the cultivation of <s>sāttvika</s> food — [all this] has been stated. Next, the following topics will be expounded: the identity of <s>tyāga</s> (relinquishment) and <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation), which have been prescribed as means to liberation; the essential nature of <s>tyāga</s>; the contemplation of the agency of all actions in the Lord who is the ruler of all; the necessity of adopting the <s>sattva guṇa</s>, [shown] by describing the effects of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>; the manner in which actions proper to one's own <s>varṇa</s>, being worship of the Supreme Person, bring about the attainment of the Supreme Person; and that <s>bhaktiyoga</s> is the quintessential meaning of the entire teaching of the <s>Gītā</s>. To begin with, <s>Arjuna</s> asks, in order to determine whether <s>tyāga</s> and <s>saṃnyāsa</s> are distinct or identical, and to ascertain their essential nature:

children.text:
atītena adhyāya-dvayena --- abhyudaya-niśśreyasa-sādhana-bhūtaṃ vaidikam eva yajña-tapo-dāna-ādikaṃ karma, na anyat; vaidikasya ca karmaṇas sāmānya-lakṣaṇaṃ praṇava-anvayaḥ; tatra mokṣa-abhyudaya-sādhanayor bhedaḥ tat-sac-chabda-nirdeśyatvena; mokṣa-sādhanaṃ ca karma phala-abhisandhi-rahitaṃ yajña-ādikam; tad-ārambhaś ca sattva-udrekād bhavati; sattva-vṛddhiś ca sāttvika-āhāra-sevayā ity-uktam / anantaraṃ mokṣa-sādhanatayā nirdiṣṭayos tyāga-saṃnyāsayor aikyam, tyāgasya ca sva-rūpam, bhagavati sarva-īśvare ca sarva-karmaṇāṃ kartṛtva-anusandhānam, sattva-rajas-tamasāṃ kārya-varṇanena sattva-guṇasya avaśya-upādeyatvam, sva-varṇa-ucitānāṃ karmaṇāṃ parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-bhūtānāṃ parama-puruṣa-prāpti-nirvartana-prakāraḥ, kṛtsnasya gītā-śāstrasya sāra-artho bhakti-yoga ity ete
pratipādyante / tatra tāvat tyāga-saṃnyāsayor pṛthaktva-ekatva-nirṇayāya sva-rūpa-nirṇayāya ca arjunaḥ pṛcchati ---
saṃnyāsasya mahābāho tattvam icchāmi veditum |
children.translated_text: 'Of <s>saṃnyāsa</s>, O mighty-armed one, I wish to know the truth,' |

children.text: tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthak keśiniṣūdana ||
children.translated_text: 'and of <s>tyāga</s> separately, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, O slayer of <s>Keśin</s>.' ||

children.text: saṃnyāsasya mahābāho tattvam icchāmi veditum |
tyāgasya ca hṛṣīkeśa pṛthak keśi-niṣūdana ||

body.text: tyāgasaṃnyāsau hi mokṣasādhanatayā vihitau, "na karmaṇā na prajayā dhanena tyāgenaike amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ -- vedāntavijñānasuniścitārthās saṃnyāsayogād yatayaś śuddhasattvāḥ / te brahmaloke tu parāntakāle parāmṛtāt parimucyanti sarve" ityādiṣu / asya saṃnyāsasya tyāgasya ca tattvam yāthātmyaṃ pṛthak veditum icchāmi / ayam abhiprāyaḥ -- kim etau saṃnyāsatyāgaśabdau pṛthagarthau, utaikārthav eva yadā pṛthagarthau, tadā anayoḥ pṛthaktvena svarūpaṃ veditum icchāmi; ekatve 'pi tasya svarūpaṃ vaktavyam iti //
body.translated_text: For <s>tyāga</s> and <s>saṃnyāsa</s> are prescribed as means to liberation in [passages such as]: 'Not by action, not by progeny, not by wealth — by renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>) alone some have attained immortality — those whose conviction is firmly established through the knowledge of <s>Vedānta</s>, the ascetics of purified nature, through the practice of renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>), at the end of time, in the world of <s>Brahman</s>, they are completely liberated by the supreme immortal' — and the like. I wish to know the truth — the real nature — of this <s>saṃnyāsa</s> and this <s>tyāga</s> separately. The intent is: are these two words <s>saṃnyāsa</s> and <s>tyāga</s> of different meaning, or of the same meaning? If of different meaning, I wish to know their essential natures as distinct; and even if they are of the same meaning, their essential nature should be stated. //

children.text: tyāga-saṃnyāsau hi mokṣa-sādhanatayā vihitau, "na karmaṇā na prajayā dhanena tyāgena eke amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ --- veda-anta-vijñāna-suniścita-arthās saṃnyāsa-yogād yatayaś śuddha-sattvāḥ / te brahma-loke tu para-anta-kāle parā-mṛtāt parimucyanti sarve" ity-ādiṣu / asya saṃnyāsasya tyāgasya ca tattvam yāthātmyaṃ pṛthak veditum icchāmi / ayam abhiprāyaḥ --- kim etau saṃnyāsa-tyāga-śabdau pṛthag-arthau, uta eka-arthav eva yadā pṛthag-arthau, tadā anayoḥ pṛthaktvena sva-rūpaṃ veditum icchāmi; ekatve 'pi tasya sva-rūpaṃ vaktavyam iti //

attributes.n: athā7nayor ekam eva sva-rūpam, tac ce8dṛśam iti nirṇetuṃ vādi-vipratipattiṃ darśayan śrī-bhagavān uvāca ---

children.text: kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The abandonment of desire-motivated actions is understood as <s>saṃnyāsa</s> by the wise.' |

children.text: sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ prāhus tyāgaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The relinquishment of the results of all actions is declared as <s>tyāga</s> by the discerning.' ||

children.text: kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ kavayo viduḥ |
sarva-karma-phala-tyāgaṃ prāhus tyāgaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ ||

body.text:
kecana vidvāṃsaḥ kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ svarūpatyāgaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ viduḥ / kecic ca vicakṣaṇāḥ nityānāṃ naimittikānāṃ ca kāmyānāṃ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalatyāga eva mokṣaśāstreṣu tyāgaśabdārtha iti prāhuḥ / tatra śāstrīyatyāgaḥ kāmyakarmasvarūpaviṣayaḥ; sarvakarmaphalaviṣaya iti vivādaṃ pradarśayan ekatra saṃnyāsaśabdam itaratra tyāgaśabdaṃ prayuktavān / atas tyāgasaṃnyāsaśabdayor ekārthatvam aṅgīkṛtam iti jñāyate / tathā "niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama" iti tyāgaśabdenaiva nirṇayavacanāt, "niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate / mohāt tasya parityāgaḥ tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // BhGR_18.", "aniṣṭam iṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam / bhavaty atyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ
kvacit" iti parasparaparyāyatādarśanāc ca tayor ekārthatvam aṅgīkṛtam iti niścīyate //
body.translated_text: Certain learned ones understand <s>saṃnyāsa</s> as the abandonment — the giving up of the very form — of desire-motivated actions. And certain other discerning ones declare that in the scriptures on liberation, the meaning of the word <s>tyāga</s> is the relinquishment of results alone, with respect to all actions — obligatory, occasional, and desire-motivated. Herein, showing the dispute as to whether scriptural <s>tyāga</s> pertains to the form of desire-motivated actions or pertains to the results of all actions, He used the word <s>saṃnyāsa</s> for the one [view] and the word <s>tyāga</s> for the other. From this it is known that the identity of meaning of the words <s>tyāga</s> and <s>saṃnyāsa</s> is accepted. Likewise, since the determination is made using only the word <s>tyāga</s> — 'Hear My definitive view on <s>tyāga</s>, O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>' — and since their interchangeability is shown in: 'The renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) of obligatory action is not appropriate; its abandonment (<s>parityāga</s>) through delusion is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>,' and 'The threefold fruit of action — undesirable, desirable, and mixed — accrues after death to those who do not relinquish (<s>atyāgin</s>), but never to the renouncers (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>)' — the identity of meaning of the two is definitively established. //

children.text:
kecana vidvāṃsaḥ kāmyānāṃ karmaṇāṃ nyāsaṃ sva-rūpa-tyāgaṃ saṃnyāsaṃ viduḥ / kecic ca vicakṣaṇāḥ nityānāṃ naimittikānāṃ ca kāmyānāṃ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ phala-tyāga eva mokṣa-śāstreṣu tyāga-śabda-artha iti prāhuḥ / tatra śāstrīya-tyāgaḥ kāmya-karma-sva-rūpa-viṣayaḥ; sarva-karma-phala-viṣaya iti vivādaṃ pradarśayan ekatra saṃnyāsa-śabdam itaratra tyāga-śabdaṃ prayuktavān / atas tyāga-saṃnyāsa-śabdayor eka-arthatvam aṅgīkṛtam iti jñāyate / tathā "niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharata-sattama" iti tyāga-śabdena eva nirṇaya-vacanāt, "niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo na upapadyate / mohāt tasya parityāgaḥ tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // BhGR_18.", "aniṣṭam iṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca tri-vidhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam / bhavaty atyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ
kvacit" iti paraspara-paryāyatā-darśanāc ca tayor eka-arthatvam aṅgīkṛtam iti niścīyate //
tyājyaṃ doṣavad ity eke karma prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Some wise men declare that all action should be abandoned as defective.' |

children.text: yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyam iti cāpare ||
children.translated_text: 'And others [say] that acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should not be abandoned.' ||

children.text: tyājyaṃ doṣavad ity eke karma prāhur manīṣiṇaḥ |
yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma na tyājyam iti ca apare ||

body.text: eke manīṣiṇaḥ kāpilāḥ vaidikāś ca tanmatānusāriṇaḥ rāgādidoṣavad bandhakatvāt sarvaṃ yajñādikaṃ karma mumukṣuṇā tyājyam iti prāhuḥ; apare paṇḍitāḥ yajñādikaṃ karma na tyājyam iti prāhuḥ //
body.translated_text: Some wise men — the <s>Kāpilas</s> (followers of <s>Sāṃkhya</s>) and those Vedic thinkers who follow their doctrine — declare that all action including sacrifice and the like should be abandoned by the seeker of liberation, since like attachment and the like it is defective by virtue of being a cause of bondage. Others, the learned, declare that acts of sacrifice and the like should not be abandoned. //

children.text: eke manīṣiṇaḥ kāpilāḥ vaidikāś ca tan-mata-anusāriṇaḥ rāga-ādi-doṣavad bandhakatvāt sarvaṃ yajña-ādikaṃ karma mumukṣuṇā tyājyam iti prāhuḥ; apare paṇḍitāḥ yajña-ādikaṃ karma na tyājyam iti prāhuḥ //
niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama |
children.translated_text: 'Hear My definitive view on <s>tyāga</s>, O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>.' |

children.text: tyāgo hi puruṣavyāghra trividhas saṃprakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'For <s>tyāga</s>, O tiger among men, is declared to be of three kinds.' ||

children.text: niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharata-sattama |
tyāgo hi puruṣa-vyāghra tri-vidhas saṃprakīrtitaḥ ||

body.text: tatra evaṃ vādivipratipanne tyāge tyāgaviṣayaṃ niścayaṃ mattaś śṛṇu; tyāgaḥ kriyamāṇeṣv eva vaidikeṣu karmasu phalaviṣayatayā, karmaviṣayatayā, kartṛtvaviṣayatayā ca pūrvam eva hi mayā trividhas saṃprakīrtitaḥ, "mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā / nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā yuddhyasva vigatajvaraḥ" iti / karmajanyaṃ svargādikaṃ phalaṃ mama na syād iti phalatyāgaḥ; madīyaphalasādhanatayā madīyam idaṃ karmeti karmaṇi mamatāyāḥ parityāgaḥ karmaviṣayas tyāgaḥ; sarveśvare kartṛtvānusaṃdhānenātmanaḥ kartṛtātyāgaḥ kartṛtvaviṣayas tyāgaḥ //
body.translated_text: In this matter of <s>tyāga</s>, where the disputants are thus at variance, hear from Me the definitive view concerning the object of <s>tyāga</s>. <s>Tyāga</s>, as [practiced] within Vedic actions being performed, has been previously declared by Me as threefold — pertaining to results, pertaining to action, and pertaining to agency — in: 'Offering all actions to Me, with mind focused on the self, free from expectation, free from possessiveness, fight without distress.' The relinquishment of results pertaining to action — 'May the fruit of action such as heaven and the like not be mine' — is relinquishment pertaining to results. Giving up possessiveness regarding action — [thinking] 'this action is the Lord's, being a means to His results' — is relinquishment pertaining to action. Giving up one's own agency through contemplating the agency of the Lord of all is relinquishment pertaining to agency. //

children.text: tatra evaṃ vādi-vipratipanne tyāge tyāga-viṣayaṃ niścayaṃ mattaś śṛṇu; tyāgaḥ kriyamāṇeṣv eva vaidikeṣu karmasu phala-viṣayatayā, karma-viṣayatayā, kartṛtva-viṣayatayā ca pūrvam eva hi mayā tri-vidhas saṃprakīrtitaḥ, "mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya adhyātma-cetasā / nirāśīr nirmamo bhūtvā yuddhyasva vigata-jvaraḥ" iti / karma-janyaṃ svarga-ādikaṃ phalaṃ mama na syād iti phala-tyāgaḥ; madīya-phala-sādhanatayā madīyam idaṃ karma iti karmaṇi mamatāyāḥ parityāgaḥ karma-viṣayas tyāgaḥ; sarva-īśvare kartṛtva-anusaṃdhānenā atmanaḥ kartṛtā-tyāgaḥ kartṛtva-viṣayas tyāgaḥ //
yajñadānatapaḥkarma na tyājyaṃ kāryam eva tat |
children.translated_text: 'Acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should not be abandoned; they are indeed to be performed.' |

children.text: yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-karma na tyājyaṃ kāryam eva tat |

body.text: yajñadānatapaḥprabhṛti vaidikaṃ karma mumukṣuṇā na kadācid api tyājyam, api tu ā prayāṇād aharahaḥ kāryam eva //
body.translated_text: Vedic action beginning with sacrifice, charity, and austerity should never be abandoned by the seeker of liberation; rather, it is to be performed every day until the time of departure. //

children.text: yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-prabhṛti vaidikaṃ karma mumukṣuṇā na kadācid api tyājyam, api tu ā prayāṇād ahar-ahaḥ kāryam eva //

body.text: kutaḥ ?
body.translated_text: Why?

children.text: kutaḥ ?
yajño dānaṃ tapaś caiva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: 'Sacrifice, charity, and austerity are purifiers for the wise.' ||

children.text: yajño dānaṃ tapaś ca eva pāvanāni manīṣiṇām ||

body.text: yajñadānatapaḥprabhṛtīni varṇāśramasaṃbandhīni karmāṇi manīṣiṇāṃ mananaśīlānāṃ pāvanāni / mananam upāsanam; mumukṣūṇāṃ yāvajjīvam upāsanaṃ kurvatām upāsananiṣpattivirodhiprācīnakarmavināśanānītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Actions related to one's <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, beginning with sacrifice, charity, and austerity, are purifiers for the wise — for those given to contemplation (<s>manana</s>). Contemplation means meditation (<s>upāsana</s>); the meaning is: for seekers of liberation who practice meditation throughout their lives, [these actions] destroy the accumulated prior <s>karma</s> that obstructs the fruition of meditation. //

children.text: yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-prabhṛtīni varṇa-āśrama-saṃbandhīni karmāṇi manīṣiṇāṃ manana-śīlānāṃ pāvanāni / mananam upāsanam; mumukṣūṇāṃ yāvaj-jīvam upāsanaṃ kurvatām upāsana-niṣpatti-virodhi-prācīna-karma-vināśanāni ity-arthaḥ //
etāny api tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca |
children.translated_text: 'But even these actions are to be performed, having abandoned attachment and results.' |

children.text: kartavyānīti me pārtha niścitaṃ matam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: 'This is My definitive and supreme view, O <s>Pārtha</s>.' ||

children.text: etāny api tu karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalāni ca |
kartavyāni iti me pārtha niścitaṃ matam uttamam ||

body.text: yasmān manīṣiṇāṃ yajñadānatapaḥprabhṛtīni pāvanāni, tasmād upāsanavad etāny api yajñādikarmāṇi madārādhanarūpāṇi, saṅgam -- karmaṇi mamatāṃ phalāni ca tyaktvā aharahar āprayāṇād upāsananivṛttaye mumukṣuṇā kartavyānīti mama niścitam uttamaṃ matam //
body.translated_text: Since sacrifice, charity, austerity, and the like are purifiers for the wise, therefore even these sacrificial and other actions, being in the form of worship of Me, are to be performed — having abandoned attachment, that is, possessiveness regarding the action, and results — every day until the time of departure, for the purpose of bringing meditation to fruition, by the seeker of liberation. This is My definitive and supreme view. //

children.text: yasmān manīṣiṇāṃ yajña-dāna-tapaḥ-prabhṛtīni pāvanāni, tasmād upāsanavad etāny api yajña-ādi-karmāṇi mad-ārādhana-rūpāṇi, saṅgam --- karmaṇi mamatāṃ phalāni ca tyaktvā ahar-ahar āprayāṇād upāsana-nivṛttaye mumukṣuṇā kartavyāni iti mama niścitam uttamaṃ matam //
niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nopapadyate |
children.translated_text: 'The renunciation of obligatory action is not appropriate.' |

children.text: mohāt tasya parityāgas tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Its abandonment through delusion is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>.' ||

children.text: niyatasya tu saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo na upapadyate |
mohāt tasya parityāgas tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ||

body.text:
niyatasya nityanaimittikasya mahāyajñādeḥ karmaṇaḥ saṃnyāsaḥ tyāgo nopapadyate, "śarīrayātrāpi ca tena prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ" iti śarīrayātrāyā evāsiddheḥ, śarīrayātrā hi yajñaśiṣṭāśanena nirvartyamānā samyagjñānāya prabhavati; anyathā, "te tv aghaṃ bhuñjate pāpāḥ" ity ayajñaśiṣṭāgharūpāśanāpyāyanaṃ manaso viparītajñānāya bhavati / "annamayaṃ hi somya manaḥ" ity annena hi mana āpyāyate / "āhāraśuddhau sattvaśuddhis sattvaśuddhau dhruvā smṛtiḥ / smṛtilambhe sarvagranthīnāṃ vipramokṣaḥ // BhGR_18." iti brahmasākṣātkārarūpaṃ jñānam āhāraśuddhyāyattaṃ śrūyate / tasmān mahāyajñādinityanaimittikaṃ karma ā prayāṇād brahmajñānāyaivopādeyam iti tasya tyāgo nopapadyate / evaṃ jñānotpādinaḥ karmaṇo
bandhakatvamohāt parityāgas tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ / tamomūlas tyāgas tāmasaḥ / tamaḥkāryājñānamūlatvena tyāgasya tamomūlatvam / tamo hy ajñānasya mūlaṃ, "pramādamohau tamaso bhavato 'jñānam eva ca" ity atroktam / ajñānaṃ tu jñānavirodhi viparītajñānam; tathā ca vakṣyate, "adharmaṃ dharmam iti yā manyate tamasāvṛtā / sarvārthān viparītāṃś ca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī" iti / ato nityanaimittikādeḥ karmaṇas tyāgo viparītajñānamūla evetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The renunciation, the giving up, of obligatory action — the regular and occasional rites beginning with the great sacrifices (<s>mahāyajñas</s>) — is not appropriate, since as stated in 'even the sustenance of the body would not be accomplished for the inactive one,' the very sustenance of the body would not be accomplished. For the sustenance of the body, carried on by eating the remnants of sacrifice, is conducive to right knowledge; otherwise, as stated in 'Those sinners eat their own sin,' eating that is sinful, consisting of what is not the remnant of sacrifice, nourishes the mind toward wrong knowledge. 'For the mind, dear one, is made of food' — for the mind is nourished by food. 'When food is pure, <s>sattva</s> is pure; when <s>sattva</s> is pure, memory is firm; upon the attainment of memory, there is the release of all knots' — thus it is heard in <s>śruti</s> that knowledge in the form of direct realization of <s>Brahman</s> depends on the purity of food. Therefore, the regular and occasional action beginning with the great sacrifices is to be adopted until the time of departure for the very purpose of knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, and hence its abandonment is not appropriate. Thus, the abandonment of action that generates knowledge, out of the delusion that it causes bondage, is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>. The <s>tāmasa</s> renunciation is one rooted in <s>tamas</s>. The renunciation is rooted in <s>tamas</s> because it is rooted in ignorance which is the effect of <s>tamas</s>. For <s>tamas</s> is the root of ignorance, as stated here: 'Heedlessness and delusion arise from <s>tamas</s>, as does ignorance.' And ignorance means wrong knowledge that is opposed to right knowledge; and thus it will be stated: 'That understanding which, enveloped by <s>tamas</s>, considers <s>adharma</s> to be <s>dharma</s> and sees all things as the reverse — that understanding, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is <s>tāmasa</s>.' Therefore, the abandonment of regular, occasional, and other action is rooted in wrong knowledge alone — this is the meaning. //

children.text:
niyatasya nitya-naimittikasya mahā-yajña-ādeḥ karmaṇaḥ saṃnyāsaḥ tyāgo na upapadyate, "śarīra-yātra āpi ca tena prasiddhyed akarmaṇaḥ" iti śarīra-yātrāyā eva asiddheḥ, śarīra-yātrā hi yajña-śiṣṭa-āśanena nirvartyamānā samyag-jñānāya prabhavati; anyathā, "te tv aghaṃ bhuñjate pāpāḥ" ity ayajña-śiṣṭa-agha-rūpa-āśana-āpyāyanaṃ manaso viparīta-jñānāya bhavati / "anna-mayaṃ hi somya manaḥ" ity annena hi mana āpyāyate / "āhāra-śuddhau sattva-śuddhis sattva-śuddhau dhruvā smṛtiḥ / smṛti-lambhe sarva-granthīnāṃ vipramokṣaḥ // BhGR_18." iti brahma-sākṣāt-kāra-rūpaṃ jñānam āhāra-śuddhy-āyattaṃ śrūyate / tasmān mahā-yajña-ādi-nitya-naimittikaṃ karma ā prayāṇād brahma-jñānāya eva upādeyam iti tasya tyāgo na upapadyate / evaṃ jñāna-utpādinaḥ karmaṇo
bandhakatva-mohāt parityāgas tāmasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ / tamo-mūlas tyāgas tāmasaḥ / tamaḥ-kārya-ajñāna-mūlatvena tyāgasya tamo-mūlatvam / tamo hy ajñānasya mūlaṃ, "pramāda-mohau tamaso bhavato 'jñānam eva ca" ity atra uktam / ajñānaṃ tu jñāna-virodhi viparīta-jñānam; tathā ca vakṣyate, "adharmaṃ dharmam iti yā manyate tamasā āvṛtā / sarva-arthān viparītāṃś ca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī" iti / ato nitya-naimittika-ādeḥ karmaṇas tyāgo viparīta-jñāna-mūla eva ity-arthaḥ //
duḥkham ity eva yaḥ karma kāyakleśabhayāt tyajet |
children.translated_text: 'He who abandons action merely because it is painful, out of fear of bodily discomfort,' |

children.text: sa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ naiva tyāgaphalaṃ labhet ||
children.translated_text: 'having performed <s>rājasa</s> renunciation, he does not obtain the fruit of renunciation at all.' ||

children.text: duḥkham ity eva yaḥ karma kāya-kleśa-bhayāt tyajet |
sa kṛtvā rājasaṃ tyāgaṃ na eva tyāga-phalaṃ labhet ||

body.text: yady api paraṃparayā mokṣasādhanabhūtaṃ karma, tathāpi duḥkhātmakadravyārjanasādhyatvād bahvāyāsarūpatayā kāyakleśakaratvāc ca manaso 'vasādakaram iti tadbhītyā yoganiṣpattaye jñānābhyāsa eva yatanīya iti / yo mahāyajñādyāśramakarma parityajet, sa rājasaṃ rajomūlaṃ tyāgaṃ kṛtvā tad ayathāvasthitaśāstrārtharūpam iti jñānotpattirūpaṃ tyāgaphalaṃ na labhate; "ayathāvat prajānāti buddhis sā pārtha rājasī" iti hi vakṣyate / na hi karma dṛṣṭadvāreṇa manaḥprasādahetuḥ, api tu bhavagatprasādadvāreṇa //
body.translated_text: Although action is indirectly a means to liberation, still, since it requires the acquisition of material resources that are of the nature of suffering, since it involves much exertion and thus causes bodily discomfort, it depresses the mind — therefore, out of fear of that, one should strive for the practice of knowledge alone for the accomplishment of <s>yoga</s>. He who on this [reasoning] abandons the <s>āśrama</s> duties beginning with the great sacrifices — he, having performed <s>rājasa</s> renunciation, that is, renunciation rooted in <s>rajas</s>, does not obtain the fruit of renunciation in the form of the arising of knowledge, since that [reasoning] is a misunderstanding of the true meaning of scripture. For it will be stated: 'That understanding which grasps things wrongly is <s>rājasa</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s>.' For action is not a cause of mental clarity through the direct path, but rather through the path of the Lord's grace. //

children.text: yady api paraṃparayā mokṣa-sādhana-bhūtaṃ karma, tatha āpi duḥkha-ātmaka-dravya-arjana-sādhyatvād bahv-āyāsa-rūpatayā kāya-kleśa-karatvāc ca manaso 'vasāda-karam iti tad-bhītyā yoga-niṣpattaye jñāna-abhyāsa eva yatanīya iti / yo mahā-yajña-ādy-āśrama-karma parityajet, sa rājasaṃ rajo-mūlaṃ tyāgaṃ kṛtvā tad ayathā-avasthita-śāstra-artha-rūpam iti jñāna-utpatti-rūpaṃ tyāga-phalaṃ na labhate; "ayathāvat prajānāti buddhis sā pārtha rājasī" iti hi vakṣyate / na hi karma dṛṣṭa-dvāreṇa manaḥ-prasāda-hetuḥ, api tu bhavagat-prasāda-dvāreṇa //
kāryam ity eva yat karma niyataṃ kriyate 'rjuna |
children.translated_text: 'When obligatory action is performed, O <s>Arjuna</s>, thinking "it must be done,"' |

children.text: saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva, sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'having abandoned attachment and the fruit as well — that renunciation is considered <s>sāttvika</s>.' ||

children.text: kāryam ity eva yat karma niyataṃ kriyate 'rjuna |
saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ ca eva, sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ ||

body.text: nityanaimittikamahāyajñādivarṇāśramavihitaṃ karma madārādhanarūpatayā kāryaṃ svayaṃprayojanam iti matvā saṅgam karmaṇi mamatāṃ phalaṃ ca tyaktvā yat kriyate, sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ, sa sattvamūlaḥ, yathāvasthitaśāstrārthajñānamūla ityarthaḥ / sattvaṃ hi yathāvasthitavastujñānam utpādayatīty uktam, "sattvāt saṃjāyate jñānam" iti / vakṣyate ca, "pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākāryaṃ bhayābhaye / bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī// " iti //
body.translated_text: When the action prescribed for one's <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s> — the regular and occasional great sacrifices and the like — is performed with the understanding that it must be done as being in the form of worship of Me, as having its own purpose [independent of worldly results], having abandoned attachment — possessiveness regarding the action — and the fruit as well — that renunciation is considered <s>sāttvika</s>, that is, rooted in <s>sattva</s>, meaning rooted in knowledge of the true meaning of scripture. For <s>sattva</s> produces knowledge of things as they truly are, as was stated: 'From <s>sattva</s> knowledge arises.' And it will be stated: 'That understanding which knows activity and inactivity, what should and should not be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation — that understanding, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is <s>sāttvika</s>.' //

children.text: nitya-naimittika-mahā-yajña-ādi-varṇa-āśrama-vihitaṃ karma mad-ārādhana-rūpatayā kāryaṃ svayaṃ-prayojanam iti matvā saṅgam karmaṇi mamatāṃ phalaṃ ca tyaktvā yat kriyate, sa tyāgaḥ sāttviko mataḥ, sa sattva-mūlaḥ, yathā-avasthita-śāstra-artha-jñāna-mūla ity-arthaḥ / sattvaṃ hi yathā-avasthita-vastu-jñānam utpādayati ity uktam, "sattvāt saṃjāyate jñānam" iti / vakṣyate ca, "pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kārya-akāryaṃ bhaya-abhaye / bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī// " iti //
na dveṣṭy akuśalaṃ karma kuśale nānuṣajjate |
children.translated_text: 'He does not hate unwholesome action, nor is he attached to wholesome action.' |

children.text: tyāgī sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī cchinnasaṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'The relinquisher, pervaded by <s>sattva</s>, wise, with doubts severed,' ||

children.text: na dveṣṭy akuśalaṃ karma kuśale na anuṣajjate |
tyāgī sattva-samāviṣṭo medhāvī cchinna-saṃśayaḥ ||

body.text: evaṃ sattvasamāviṣṭo medhāvī yathāvasthitatattvajñānaḥ, tata eva cchinnasaṃśayaḥ, karmaṇi saṅgaphalakartṛtvatyāgī, na dveṣṭy akuśalaṃ karma; śukale ca karmaṇi nānuṣajjate / akuśalaṃ karma aniṣṭaphalam, kuśalaṃ ca karma iṣṭarūpasvargaputrapaśvannādyādiphalam / sarvasmin karmaṇi mamatārahitatvāt, tyaktabrahmavyatiriktasarvaphalatvāt, tyaktakartṛtvāc ca tayoḥ kriyamāṇayoḥ prītidveṣau na karoti / aniṣṭaphalaṃ pāpaṃ karmātra prāmādikam abhipretam; "nāvirato duścaritān nāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ / nāśāntamānaso vāpi prajñānenainam āpnuyāt // BhGR_18." iti duścaritāvirater jñānotpattivirodhitvaśravaṇāt / ataḥ karmaṇi kartṛtvasaṅgaphalānāṃ tyāgaḥ śāstrīyatyāgaḥ, na karmasvarūpatyāgaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus one who is pervaded by <s>sattva</s>, being intelligent, possessing knowledge of reality as it truly is, and therefore with doubts severed, renouncing attachment, fruits, and the sense of agency in action — he does not hate disagreeable (<s>akuśala</s>) action, nor is he attached to agreeable (<s>śukla</s>) action. Disagreeable action is that which bears undesirable fruits; agreeable action is that which bears desirable fruits such as heaven, sons, cattle, food, and the like. Since in all actions he is free from the sense of 'mine,' since he has renounced all fruits other than <s>Brahman</s>, and since he has renounced the sense of agency — he feels neither delight nor aversion toward these two [types of action] when they are performed. The sinful action bearing undesirable fruits that is intended here is inadvertent (<s>prāmādika</s>) action, since it is heard that non-cessation from evil conduct obstructs the arising of knowledge: 'One who has not ceased from evil conduct, who is not tranquil, who is not concentrated, whose mind is not at peace — cannot attain Him through wisdom.' Therefore, the renunciation in action is the renunciation of agency, attachment, and fruits — it is scriptural renunciation, not the renunciation of the action itself. //

children.text: evaṃ sattva-samāviṣṭo medhāvī yathā-avasthita-tattva-jñānaḥ, tata eva cchinna-saṃśayaḥ, karmaṇi saṅga-phala-kartṛtva-tyāgī, na dveṣṭy akuśalaṃ karma; śukale ca karmaṇi na anuṣajjate / akuśalaṃ karma aniṣṭa-phalam, kuśalaṃ ca karma iṣṭa-rūpa-svarga-putra-paśv-anna-adya-ādi-phalam / sarvasmin karmaṇi mamatā-rahitatvāt, tyakta-brahma-vyatirikta-sarva-phalatvāt, tyakta-kartṛtvāc ca tayoḥ kriyamāṇayoḥ prīti-dveṣau na karoti / aniṣṭa-phalaṃ pāpaṃ karma atra prāmādikam abhipretam; "na avirato duścaritān na aśānto na asamāhitaḥ / na aśānta-mānaso va āpi prajñānena enam āpnuyāt // BhGR_18." iti duścarita-avirater jñāna-utpatti-virodhitva-śravaṇāt / ataḥ karmaṇi kartṛtva-saṅga-phalānāṃ tyāgaḥ śāstrīya-tyāgaḥ, na karma-sva-rūpa-tyāgaḥ //

body.text: tad āha --
body.translated_text: This He states —

children.text: tad āha ---
na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇy aśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: For it is not possible for an embodied being to abandon actions entirely. |

children.text: yas tu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgīty abhidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: But he who renounces the fruit of action — he is called the renouncer. ||

children.text: na hi deha-bhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇy aśeṣataḥ |
yas tu karma-phala-tyāgī sa tyāgi īty abhidhīyate ||

body.text: na hi dehabhṛtā dhriyamāṇaśarīreṇa karmāṇy aśeṣatas tyaktuṃ śakyam; dehadhāraṇārthānām aśanapānādīnāṃ tadanubandhināṃ ca karmaṇām avarjanīyatvāt / tad arthaṃ ca mahāyajñādyanuṣṭhānam avarjanīyam / yas tu teṣu mahāyajñādikarmasu phalatyāgī sa eva, "tyāgenaike amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ" ityādiśāstreṣu tyāgīty abhidhīyate / phalatyāgīti pradarśanārthaṃ phalakartṛtvakarmasaṅgānāṃ tyāgīti; "trividhaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ" iti prakramāt //
body.translated_text: For it is not possible for an embodied being — one who maintains a body — to abandon actions entirely, since actions such as eating, drinking, and the like that serve to maintain the body, and actions connected with those, are unavoidable. And the performance of the great sacrifices (<s>mahāyajña</s>) and the like for that purpose is also unavoidable. He who renounces the fruit in those actions such as the great sacrifices and the like — he alone is called the 'renouncer' (<s>tyāgin</s>) in the scriptures such as 'By renunciation alone some have attained immortality' and the like. 'The renouncer of the fruit' is stated as illustrative — [it means] the renouncer of the fruit, the sense of agency, and attachment to action, since [the verse] proceeds from the earlier [statement] 'threefold it has been declared.' //

children.text: na hi deha-bhṛtā dhriyamāṇa-śarīreṇa karmāṇy aśeṣatas tyaktuṃ śakyam; deha-dhāraṇa-arthānām aśana-pāna-ādīnāṃ tad-anubandhināṃ ca karmaṇām avarjanīyatvāt / tad arthaṃ ca mahā-yajña-ādy-anuṣṭhānam avarjanīyam / yas tu teṣu mahā-yajña-ādi-karmasu phala-tyāgī sa eva, "tyāgena eke amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ" ity-ādi-śāstreṣu tyāgi īty abhidhīyate / phala-tyāgi īti pradarśana-arthaṃ phala-kartṛtva-karma-saṅgānāṃ tyāgi īti; "tri-vidhaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ" iti prakramāt //

body.text: nanu karmāṇy agnihotradarśapūrṇamāsajyotiṣṭomādīni, mahāyajñādīni ca svargādiphalasaṃbandhitayā śāstrair vidhīyante; nityanaimittikānām api "prājāpatyaṃ gṛhasthānām" ityādiphalasaṃbandhitayaiva hi codanā / ataḥ tattatphalasādhanasvabhāvatayāvagatānāṃ karmaṇām anuṣṭhāne, bījāvāpādīnām iva, anabhisaṃhitaphalasyāpi iṣṭāniṣṭarūpaphalasaṃbandhaḥ avarjanīyaḥ / ato mokṣavirodhiphalatvena mumukṣuṇā na karmānuṣṭheyam ity ata uttaram āha --
body.translated_text: Now, actions such as <s>Agnihotra</s>, <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>, <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>, and the like, as well as the great sacrifices and the like, are enjoined by the scriptures as connected with fruits such as heaven and the like. Even for the obligatory and occasional [rites], the injunction is connected with a fruit: 'The <s>Prājāpatya</s> [rite] is for householders' and the like. Therefore, when performing actions that are known to be by nature the means to their respective fruits — like the sowing of seeds and the like — even for one who does not intend the fruit, the connection with the fruit, whether desirable or undesirable, is unavoidable. Therefore, since they produce fruits that obstruct liberation, a seeker of liberation should not perform actions — to this He replies —

children.text: nanu karmāṇy agni-hotra-darśa-pūrṇa-māsa-jyotiṣṭoma-ādīni, mahā-yajña-ādīni ca svarga-ādi-phala-saṃbandhitayā śāstrair vidhīyante; nitya-naimittikānām api "prājāpatyaṃ gṛha-sthānām" ity-ādi-phala-saṃbandhitaya aiva hi codanā / ataḥ tat-tat-phala-sādhana-sva-bhāvataya āvagatānāṃ karmaṇām anuṣṭhāne, bīja-āvāpa-ādīnām iva, anabhisaṃhita-phalasya api iṣṭa-aniṣṭa-rūpa-phala-saṃbandhaḥ avarjanīyaḥ / ato mokṣa-virodhi-phalatvena mumukṣuṇā na karma-anuṣṭheyam ity ata uttaram āha ---
aniṣṭam iṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam |
children.translated_text: Undesirable, desirable, and mixed — the threefold fruit of action |

children.text: bhavaty atyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: accrues after death to those who have not renounced, but never to the renouncers. ||

children.text: aniṣṭam iṣṭaṃ miśraṃ ca tri-vidhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam |
bhavaty atyāgināṃ pretya na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit ||

body.text:
aniṣṭam narakādiphalam, iṣṭam svargādi, miśram aniṣṭasaṃbhinnaṃ putrapaśvannādyādi; etat trividhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam, atyāginām kartṛtvamamatāphalatyāgarahitānāṃ pretya bhavati / pretya karmānuṣṭhānottarakālam ityarthaḥ / na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit -- na tu kartṛtvādiparityāgināṃ kvacid api mokṣavirodhi phalaṃ bhavati / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- yady apy agnihotramahāyajñādīni tāny eva, tathāpi jīvanādhikārakāmādhikārayor iva mokṣādhikāre ca viniyogapṛthaktvena parihriyate / mokṣaviniyogaś ca, "tam etaṃ vedānuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena dānena tapasānāśakena" ityādibhir iti / tad evaṃ kriyamāṇeṣv eva karmasu
kartṛtvādiparityāgaḥ śāstrasiddhiḥ saṃnyāsaḥ; sa eva ca tyāga ity uktaḥ //
body.translated_text: Undesirable — fruit such as hell and the like; desirable — heaven and the like; mixed — that which is mixed with suffering, such as sons, cattle, food, and the like. This threefold fruit of action accrues after death — meaning: after the time of performing the action — to those who have not renounced, i.e., those who lack the renunciation of agency, the sense of 'mine,' and the fruit. But never to the renouncers — but for those who have renounced agency and the like, no fruit that obstructs liberation ever accrues. What is being said is this: although the very same <s>Agnihotra</s>, great sacrifices, and the like [are performed], still, just as [the same ritual has] different purposes (<s>viniyoga</s>) for livelihood, for [fulfillment of] desire, and for liberation, the conflict is resolved by the difference of purpose. And the purpose connected with liberation is [established by passages such as]: 'By <s>Vedic</s> recitation, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know Him — by sacrifice, by charity, by austerity, by fasting' and the like. Thus, the renunciation of agency and the like in the very actions being performed is what is established by scripture as <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation); and that alone is what has been called <s>tyāga</s> (relinquishment). //

children.text:
aniṣṭam naraka-ādi-phalam, iṣṭam svarga-ādi, miśram aniṣṭa-saṃbhinnaṃ putra-paśv-anna-adya-ādi; etat tri-vidhaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam, atyāginām kartṛtva-mamatā-phala-tyāga-rahitānāṃ pretya bhavati / pretya karma-anuṣṭhāna-uttara-kālam ity-arthaḥ / na tu saṃnyāsināṃ kvacit --- na tu kartṛtva-ādi-parityāgināṃ kvacid api mokṣa-virodhi phalaṃ bhavati / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- yady apy agni-hotra-mahā-yajña-ādīni tāny eva, tatha āpi jīvana-adhikāra-kāma-adhikārayor iva mokṣa-adhikāre ca viniyoga-pṛthaktvena parihriyate / mokṣa-viniyogaś ca, "tam etaṃ veda-anuvacanena brāhmaṇā vividiṣanti yajñena dānena tapasa ānāśakena" ity-ādibhir iti / tad evaṃ kriyamāṇeṣv eva karmasu
kartṛtva-ādi-parityāgaḥ śāstra-siddhiḥ saṃnyāsaḥ; sa eva ca tyāga ity uktaḥ //

body.text: idānīṃ bhagavati puruṣottame antaryāmiṇi kartṛtvānusaṃdhānena ātmani akartṛtvānusaṃdhānaprakāram āha, tata eva phalakarmaṇor api mamatāparityāgo bhavatīti / paramapuruṣo hi svakīyena jīvātmanā svakīyaiś ca karaṇakalevaraprāṇaiḥ svalīlāprayojanāya karmāṇy ārabhate / ato jīvātmagataṃ kṣunnivṛttyādikam api phalam, tatsādhanabhūtaṃ ca karma paramapuruṣasyaiva /
body.translated_text: Now He states the manner of contemplating non-agency in oneself through contemplating the agency in the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>), the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) — since from that very [contemplation] the renunciation of the sense of 'mine' with respect to fruits and actions also follows. For the Supreme Person initiates actions through His own individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) and through His own instruments, body, and vital breaths, for the purpose of His own sport (<s>līlā</s>). Therefore, even the fruit pertaining to the individual self, such as the cessation of hunger and the like, and the action that is the means thereto, belong to the Supreme Person alone —

children.text: idānīṃ bhagavati puruṣa-uttame antaryāmiṇi kartṛtva-anusaṃdhānena ātmani akartṛtva-anusaṃdhāna-prakāram āha, tata eva phala-karmaṇor api mamatā-parityāgo bhavati iti / parama-puruṣo hi svakīyena jīva-ātmanā svakīyaiś ca karaṇa-kalevara-prāṇaiḥ sva-līlā-prayojanāya karmāṇy ārabhate / ato jīva-ātma-gataṃ kṣun-nivṛtty-ādikam api phalam, tat-sādhana-bhūtaṃ ca karma parama-puruṣasya eva /
pañcaitāni mahābāho kāraṇāni nibodhe me /
children.translated_text: Learn from Me, O mighty-armed, these five causes |

children.text: sāṃkhye kṛtānte proktāni siddhaye sarvakarmaṇām ||
children.translated_text: declared in the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> doctrine for the accomplishment of all actions. ||

children.text: pañca etāni mahā-bāho kāraṇāni nibodhe me /
sāṃkhye kṛta-ante proktāni siddhaye sarva-karmaṇām ||

body.text: sāṃkhyā buddhiḥ, sāṃkhye kṛtānte yathāvasthitatattvaviṣayayā vaidikyā buddhyā anusaṃhite nirṇaye sarvakarmaṇāṃ siddhaye utpattaye, proktāni pañcaitāni kāraṇāni nibodhe me -- mama sakāśād anusaṃdhatsva / vaidikī hi buddhiḥ śarīrendriyaprāṇajīvātmopakaraṇaṃ paramātmānam eva kartāram avadhārayati, "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyātmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati sa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ", "antaḥpraviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānāṃ sarvātmā" ityādiṣu //
body.translated_text: <s>Sāṅkhya</s> means intellect (<s>buddhi</s>). In the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> doctrine — in the determination (<s>kṛtānta</s>) arrived at by the <s>Vedic</s> intellect whose object is reality as it truly is — declared for the accomplishment, i.e., origination, of all actions — learn these five causes from Me, i.e., contemplate [them] from My teaching. For the <s>Vedic</s> intellect ascertains the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) alone as the [true] agent, who uses the body, senses, vital breaths, and individual self as His instruments — [as stated in <s>śruti</s>]: 'He who stands in the self, who is interior to the self, whom the self does not know, whose body is the self, who controls the self from within — He is your Self, the inner controller, the immortal'; 'Having entered within, the ruler of all beings, the Self of all' — and so on. //

children.text: sāṃkhyā buddhiḥ, sāṃkhye kṛta-ante yathā-avasthita-tattva-viṣayayā vaidikyā buddhyā anusaṃhite nirṇaye sarva-karmaṇāṃ siddhaye utpattaye, proktāni pañca etāni kāraṇāni nibodhe me --- mama sakāśād anusaṃdhatsva / vaidikī hi buddhiḥ śarīra-indriya-prāṇa-jīva-ātma-upakaraṇaṃ parama-ātmānam eva kartāram avadhārayati, "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan ātmano 'ntaro yam ātmā na veda yasyā atmā śarīraṃ ya ātmānam antaro yamayati sa ta ātma āntaryāmy amṛtaḥ", "antaḥ-praviṣṭaḥ śāstā janānāṃ sarva-ātmā" ity-ādiṣu //

body.text: tad idam āha --
body.translated_text: This He states —

children.text: tad idam āha ---
adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham /
children.translated_text: The locus (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), the agent, the instruments of various kinds, |

children.text: vividhā ca pṛthakceṣṭā daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam //
children.translated_text: the manifold distinct activities, and providence (<s>daiva</s>) as the fifth. ||

children.text: adhiṣṭhānaṃ tathā kartā karaṇaṃ ca pṛthag-vidham /
vividhā ca pṛthak-ceṣṭā daivaṃ ca eva atra pañcamam //
śarīravāṅmanobhir yat karma prārabhate naraḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever action a person initiates with body, speech, and mind — |

children.text: nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañcaite tasya hetavaḥ //
children.translated_text: whether right or wrong — these five are its causes. ||

children.text: śarīra-vāṅ-manobhir yat karma prārabhate naraḥ /
nyāyyaṃ vā viparītaṃ vā pañca ete tasya hetavaḥ //

body.text:
nyāyye śāstrasiddhe, viparīte pratiṣiddhe vā sarvasmin karmaṇi śarīre, vācike, mānase ca pañcaite hetavaḥ / adhiṣṭhānam śarīram; adhiṣṭhīyate jīvātmaneti mahābhūtasaṃghātarūpaṃ śarīram adhiṣṭhānam / tathā kartā jīvātmā; asya jīvātmano jñātṛtvaṃ kartṛtvaṃ ca, "jño 'ta eva", "kartā śāstrārthavattvāt " iti ca sūtropapāditam / karaṇaṃ ca pṛthagvidham -- vākpāṇipādādipañcakaṃ samanaskaṃ karmendriyaṃ pṛthagvidham karmaniṣpattau pṛthagvyāpāram / vividhā ca pṛthakceṣṭā / ceṣṭāśabdena pañcātmā vāyur abhidhīyate tadvṛttivācinā; śarīrendriyadhāraṇasya prāṇāpānādibhedabhinnasya vāyoḥ pañcātmano vividhā ca ceṣṭā vividhā vṛttiḥ / daivaṃ caivātra pañcamam -- atra karmahetukalāpe daivaṃ pañcamam -- paramātmā
