antaryāmī karmaniṣpattau pradhānahetur ityarthaḥ / uktaṃ hi, "sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca" iti / vakṣyati ca, "īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati / bhrāmayan sarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā" iti / paramātmāyattaṃ ca jīvātmanaḥ kartṛtvam, "parāt tu tacchruteḥ" ityādyupapāditam / nanv evaṃ paramātmāyatte jīvātmanaḥ kartṛtve jīvātmā karmaṇy aniyojyo bhavatīti vidhiniṣedhaśāstrāṇy anarthakāni syuḥ // idam api codyaṃ sūtrakāreṇa parihṛtam, "kṛtaprayatnāpekṣas tu vihitapratiṣiddhāvaiyārthyādibhyaḥ" iti / etad uktaṃ bhavati -- paramātmanā dattais tadādhāraiś ca karaṇakalebarādibhis tadāhitaśaktibhiḥ svayaṃ ca jīvātmā tadādhāras tadāhitaśaktis san karmaniṣpattaye svecchayā
karaṇādyadhiṣṭhānākāraṃ prayatnaṃ cārabhate; tadantaravasthitaḥ paramātmā svānumatidānena taṃ pravartayatīti jīvasyāpi svabuddhyaiva pravṛttihetutvam asti; yathā gurutaraśilāmahīruhādicalanādiphalapravṛttiṣu bahupuruṣasādhyāsu bahūnāṃ hetutvaṃ vidhiniṣedhabhāktvaṃ ceti //
body.translated_text: In every action — whether right, i.e., established by scripture, or wrong, i.e., prohibited — whether bodily, vocal, or mental — these five are the causes. The locus (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) is the body; the body, an aggregate of the great elements, is the locus because the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>) presides over it. The agent (<s>kartā</s>) is the individual self; the individual self's nature as knower and as agent is demonstrated in the <s>Sūtras</s>: 'The knower, for that very reason' and 'The agent, because of the purposefulness of scripture.' The instruments of various kinds — the five action-organs (<s>karmendriyas</s>) such as speech, hands, feet, and the like, together with the mind, are of various kinds, i.e., having distinct functions in the accomplishment of action. And the manifold distinct activities — by the word 'activity' (<s>ceṣṭā</s>), the fivefold vital air (<s>vāyu</s>) is denoted, by a term referring to its functions; the manifold activities, i.e., the manifold functions, of the fivefold vital air — differentiated as <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the like — which sustains the body and the senses. And providence (<s>daiva</s>) as the fifth — in this aggregate of causes of action, <s>daiva</s> as the fifth is the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>), who is the principal cause in the accomplishment of action — this is the meaning. For it has been stated: 'And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me come memory, knowledge, and their removal.' And it will be stated: 'The Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings, O <s>Arjuna</s>, causing all beings to revolve, mounted on the machine, by [His] <s>māyā</s>.' And the agency of the individual self is dependent on the Supreme Self — as demonstrated [in the <s>Sūtra</s>]: 'But [it is] from the Supreme, because of the <s>śruti</s>.' Now, if the individual self's agency is dependent on the Supreme Self, then the individual self would not be enjoinable with respect to action, and the scriptures of injunction and prohibition would become purposeless. This objection too has been resolved by the author of the <s>Sūtras</s>: 'But [the Supreme Self acts] in dependence on the effort initiated [by the individual self], because of the non-purposelessness of injunction and prohibition.' What is being said is this: with the instruments, body, and the like given by the Supreme Self, established on Him, and endowed with powers placed by Him — and the individual self too, being established on Him and endowed with powers placed by Him — initiates by its own will the effort in the form of presiding over the instruments and the like for the accomplishment of action; the Supreme Self, abiding within, sets him in motion by granting His permission. Thus, the individual self too has causality through its own volition; just as in activities requiring many persons — such as moving a very heavy rock or tree and the like — many have causality and are subjects of injunction and prohibition. //

children.text:
nyāyye śāstra-siddhe, viparīte pratiṣiddhe vā sarvasmin karmaṇi śarīre, vācike, mānase ca pañca ete hetavaḥ / adhiṣṭhānam śarīram; adhiṣṭhīyate jīva-ātmana īti mahā-bhūta-saṃghāta-rūpaṃ śarīram adhiṣṭhānam / tathā kartā jīva-ātmā; asya jīva-ātmano jñātṛtvaṃ kartṛtvaṃ ca, "jño 'ta eva", "kartā śāstra-arthavattvāt " iti ca sūtra-upapāditam / karaṇaṃ ca pṛthag-vidham --- vāk-pāṇi-pāda-ādi-pañcakaṃ samanaskaṃ karma-indriyaṃ pṛthag-vidham karma-niṣpattau pṛthag-vyāpāram / vividhā ca pṛthak-ceṣṭā / ceṣṭā-śabdena pañca-ātmā vāyur abhidhīyate tad-vṛtti-vācinā; śarīra-indriya-dhāraṇasya prāṇa-apāna-ādi-bheda-bhinnasya vāyoḥ pañca-ātmano vividhā ca ceṣṭā vividhā vṛttiḥ / daivaṃ ca eva atra pañcamam --- atra karma-hetu-kalāpe daivaṃ pañcamam --- parama-ātmā
antaryāmī karma-niṣpattau pradhāna-hetur ity-arthaḥ / uktaṃ hi, "sarvasya ca ahaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca" iti / vakṣyati ca, "īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati / bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantra-ārūḍhāni māyayā" iti / parama-ātma-āyattaṃ ca jīva-ātmanaḥ kartṛtvam, "parāt tu tac-chruteḥ" ity-ādy-upapāditam / nanv evaṃ parama-ātma-āyatte jīva-ātmanaḥ kartṛtve jīva-ātmā karmaṇy aniyojyo bhavati iti vidhi-niṣedha-śāstrāṇy anarthakāni syuḥ // idam api codyaṃ sūtra-kāreṇa parihṛtam, "kṛta-prayatna-apekṣas tu vihita-pratiṣiddha-avaiyārthya-ādibhyaḥ" iti / etad uktaṃ bhavati --- parama-ātmanā dattais tad-ādhāraiś ca karaṇa-kalebara-ādibhis tad-āhita-śaktibhiḥ svayaṃ ca jīva-ātmā tad-ādhāras tad-āhita-śaktis san karma-niṣpattaye sva-icchayā
karaṇa-ādy-adhiṣṭhāna-ākāraṃ prayatnaṃ cā arabhate; tad-antar-avasthitaḥ parama-ātmā sva-anumati-dānena taṃ pravartayati iti jīvasya api sva-buddhya aiva pravṛtti-hetutvam asti; yathā gurutara-śilā-mahī-ruha-ādi-calana-ādi-phala-pravṛttiṣu bahu-puruṣa-sādhyāsu bahūnāṃ hetutvaṃ vidhi-niṣedha-bhāktvaṃ ca iti //
tatraivaṃ sati kartāram ātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ /
children.translated_text: This being the case, he who sees the self alone as the agent — |

children.text: paśyaty akṛtabuddhitvān na sa paśyati durmatiḥ //
children.translated_text: that person of wicked mind, due to undeveloped intellect, does not see. ||

children.text: tatra evaṃ sati kartāram ātmānaṃ kevalaṃ tu yaḥ /
paśyaty akṛta-buddhitvān na sa paśyati durmatiḥ //

body.text: evaṃ vastutaḥ paramātmānumatipūrvake jīvātmanaḥ kartṛtve sati, tatra karmaṇi kevalam ātmānam eva kartāraṃ yaḥ paśyati, sa durmatiḥ viparītamatiḥ akṛtabuddhitvād aniṣpannayathāvasthitavastubuddhitvān na paśyati na yathāvasthitaṃ kartāraṃ paśyati //
body.translated_text: Since, in reality, the individual self's agency is preceded by the permission of the Supreme Self, in that action, he who sees the self alone as the agent — that person of wicked mind, i.e., of perverted understanding, due to undeveloped intellect, i.e., due to his understanding of reality as it truly is being unaccomplished — does not see: he does not see the agent as he truly is. //

children.text: evaṃ vastutaḥ parama-ātma-anumati-pūrvake jīva-ātmanaḥ kartṛtve sati, tatra karmaṇi kevalam ātmānam eva kartāraṃ yaḥ paśyati, sa durmatiḥ viparīta-matiḥ akṛta-buddhitvād aniṣpanna-yathā-avasthita-vastu-buddhitvān na paśyati na yathā-avasthitaṃ kartāraṃ paśyati //
yasya nāhaṃkṛto bhāvo buddhir yasya na lipyate /
children.translated_text: He whose sense of being (<s>bhāva</s>) is not egoistic, whose intellect is not tainted — |

children.text: hatvāpi sa imāṃl lokān na hanti na nibadhyate //
children.translated_text: even though he slays these worlds, he does not slay, nor is he bound. ||

children.text: yasya na ahaṃ-kṛto bhāvo buddhir yasya na lipyate /
hatva āpi sa imāṃl lokān na hanti na nibadhyate //

body.text: paramapuruṣakartṛtvānusaṃdhānena yasya bhāvaḥ kartṛtvaviṣayo manovṛttiviśeṣaḥ nāhaṃkṛtaḥ nāhamabhimānakṛtaḥ / ahaṃ karomīti jñānaṃ yasya na vidyata ityarthaḥ / buddhir yasya na lipyate asmin karmaṇi mama kartṛtvābhāvād etatphalaṃ na mayā saṃbadhyate, na ca madīyaṃ karmeti yasya buddhir jāyata ityarthaḥ / sa imān lokān yuddhe hatvāpi tān na nihanti; na kevalaṃ bhīṣmādīn ityarthaḥ / tatas tena yuddhākhyena karmaṇā na nibadhyate / tatphalaṃ nānubhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Through the contemplation of the Supreme Person's agency, he whose <s>bhāva</s> — the specific mental disposition pertaining to agency — is not egoistic (<s>nāhaṃkṛta</s>), i.e., not produced by the I-notion; the meaning is: he in whom the cognition 'I am the doer' does not exist. He whose intellect is not tainted — the meaning is: he in whom the understanding arises that 'since I have no agency in this action, its fruit is not connected with me, nor is this action mine.' He, even though he slays these worlds in battle, does not slay them; not just <s>Bhīṣma</s> and the like — this is the meaning. Consequently, he is not bound by that action called battle — he does not experience its fruit, is the meaning. //

children.text: parama-puruṣa-kartṛtva-anusaṃdhānena yasya bhāvaḥ kartṛtva-viṣayo mano-vṛtti-viśeṣaḥ na ahaṃ-kṛtaḥ na aham-abhimāna-kṛtaḥ / ahaṃ karomi iti jñānaṃ yasya na vidyata ity-arthaḥ / buddhir yasya na lipyate asmin karmaṇi mama kartṛtva-abhāvād etat-phalaṃ na mayā saṃbadhyate, na ca madīyaṃ karma iti yasya buddhir jāyata ity-arthaḥ / sa imān lokān yuddhe hatva āpi tān na nihanti; na kevalaṃ bhīṣma-ādīn ity-arthaḥ / tatas tena yuddha-ākhyena karmaṇā na nibadhyate / tat-phalaṃ na anubhavati ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: sarvam idam akartṛtvādyanusandhānaṃ sattvaguṇavṛddhyaiva bhavatīti sattvasyopādeyatājñāpanāya karmaṇi sattvādiguṇakṛtaṃ vaiṣamyaṃ prapañcayiṣyan karmacodanāprakāraṃ tāvad āha --
body.translated_text: All this contemplation of non-agency and the like arises only through the increase of the <s>sattva guṇa</s>. In order to make known the desirability of <s>sattva</s>, intending to elaborate on the differences produced by the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like in action, He first states the manner of the incitement to action —

children.text: sarvam idam akartṛtva-ādy-anusandhānaṃ sattva-guṇa-vṛddhya aiva bhavati iti sattvasya upādeyatā-jñāpanāya karmaṇi sattva-ādi-guṇa-kṛtaṃ vaiṣamyaṃ prapañcayiṣyan karma-codanā-prakāraṃ tāvad āha ---
jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā trividhā karmacodanā /
children.translated_text: Knowledge, the knowable, and the knower — [this is] the threefold incitement to action. |

children.text: kāraṇaṃ karma karteti trividhaḥ karmasaṃgrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: The instrument, the action, and the agent — [this is] the threefold aggregate of action. ||

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ parijñātā tri-vidhā karma-codanā /
kāraṇaṃ karma karta īti tri-vidhaḥ karma-saṃgrahaḥ //

body.text: jñānam kartavyakarmaviṣayaṃ jñānam, jñeyaṃ ca kartavyaṃ karma, parijñātā tasya boddheti trividhā karmacodanā / bodhaboddhavyaboddhṛyukto jyotiṣṭomādikarmavidhir ityarthaḥ / tatra boddhavyarūpaṃ karma trividhaṃ saṃgṛhyate karaṇaṃ karma karteti / karaṇam sādhanabhūtaṃ dravyādikam; karma yāgādikam; kartā anuṣṭhāteti //
body.translated_text: Knowledge — the knowledge pertaining to the action to be performed; the knowable — the action to be performed; the knower (<s>parijñātā</s>) — the one who understands it. This is the threefold incitement to action. The meaning is: the injunction of action such as <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like is accompanied by the knowledge, the knowable, and the knower. Therein, the action in the form of the knowable is subsumed under three categories: the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>), the action (<s>karma</s>), and the agent (<s>kartā</s>). The instrument — the materials such as substances and the like that serve as means; the action — the sacrificial rite and the like; the agent — the performer. //

children.text: jñānam kartavya-karma-viṣayaṃ jñānam, jñeyaṃ ca kartavyaṃ karma, parijñātā tasya boddha īti tri-vidhā karma-codanā / bodha-boddhavya-boddhṛ-yukto jyotiṣṭoma-ādi-karma-vidhir ity-arthaḥ / tatra boddhavya-rūpaṃ karma tri-vidhaṃ saṃgṛhyate karaṇaṃ karma karta īti / karaṇam sādhana-bhūtaṃ dravya-ādikam; karma yāga-ādikam; kartā anuṣṭhāta īti //
jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridhaiva guṇabhedataḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowledge, action, and the agent are declared to be of three kinds alone, according to the distinction of <s>guṇas</s>, |

children.text: procyate guṇasaṃkhyāne yathāvac chṛṇu tāny api //
children.translated_text: in the enumeration of the <s>guṇas</s>. Hear of these as well, properly. ||

children.text: jñānaṃ karma ca kartā ca tridha aiva guṇa-bhedataḥ /
procyate guṇa-saṃkhyāne yathāvac chṛṇu tāny api //

body.text: kartavyakarmaviṣayaṃ jñānam, anuṣṭhīyamānaṃ ca karma, tasyānuṣṭhātā ca sattvādiguṇabhedatas trividhaiva procyate guṇasaṃkhyāne guṇakāryagaṇane / yathāvac chṛṇu tāny api tāni guṇato bhinnāni jñānādīni yathāvac chṛṇu //
body.translated_text: Knowledge pertaining to the action to be performed, the action being performed, and its performer are declared to be of three kinds alone, according to the distinction of the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the like, in the enumeration of the <s>guṇas</s>, i.e., in the counting of the effects of the <s>guṇas</s>. Hear properly of these as well — of knowledge and the like that are differentiated by the <s>guṇas</s>. //

children.text: kartavya-karma-viṣayaṃ jñānam, anuṣṭhīyamānaṃ ca karma, tasya anuṣṭhātā ca sattva-ādi-guṇa-bhedatas tri-vidha aiva procyate guṇa-saṃkhyāne guṇa-kārya-gaṇane / yathāvac chṛṇu tāny api tāni guṇato bhinnāni jñāna-ādīni yathāvac chṛṇu //
sarvabhūteṣu yenaikaṃ bhāvam avyayam īkṣate /
children.translated_text: That knowledge by which one sees a single, imperishable reality |

children.text: avibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu taj jñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam //
children.translated_text: in all beings — undivided among the divided — know that knowledge to be <s>sāttvika</s>. ||

children.text: sarva-bhūteṣu yena ekaṃ bhāvam avyayam īkṣate /
avibhaktaṃ vibhakteṣu taj jñānaṃ viddhi sāttvikam //

body.text: brāhmaṇakṣatriyabrahmacārigṛhasthādirūpeṇa vibhakteṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu karmādhikāriṣu yena jñānenaikam ātmākhyaṃ bhāvaṃ, tatrāpy avibhaktam brāhmaṇatvādyanekākāreṣv api bhūteṣu sitadīrghādivibhāgavatsu jñānākāre ātmani vibhāgarahitam, avyayaṃ vyayasvabhāveṣv api brāhmaṇādiśarīreṣu avyayam avikṛtaṃ phalādisaṅgānarhaṃ ca karmādhikāravelāyām īkṣate, taj jñānaṃ sāttvikaṃ viddhi //
body.translated_text: Among all beings — those qualified for action, differentiated in the forms of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Brahmacārin</s>, householder, and the like — the knowledge by which one sees a single reality called the self; and therein, undivided — among beings that are of many forms such as <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood and the like, and that possess differentiations such as white, tall, and the like — [one sees that the self] in the form of knowledge is devoid of differentiation; imperishable — even though the bodies of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like are by nature subject to decay — [one sees that] it is imperishable, unmodified, and unfit for connection with fruits and the like, at the time of being qualified for action — know that knowledge to be <s>sāttvika</s>. //

children.text: brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-brahma-cāri-gṛha-stha-ādi-rūpeṇa vibhakteṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu karma-adhikāriṣu yena jñānena ekam ātma-ākhyaṃ bhāvaṃ, tatra apy avibhaktam brāhmaṇatva-ādy-aneka-ākāreṣv api bhūteṣu sita-dīrgha-ādi-vibhāga-vatsu jñāna-ākāre ātmani vibhāga-rahitam, avyayaṃ vyaya-sva-bhāveṣv api brāhmaṇa-ādi-śarīreṣu avyayam avikṛtaṃ phala-ādi-saṅga-anarhaṃ ca karma-adhikāra-velāyām īkṣate, taj jñānaṃ sāttvikaṃ viddhi //
pṛthaktvena tu yaj jñānaṃ nānābhāvān pṛthagvidhān /
children.translated_text: But that knowledge which, through separateness, |

children.text: vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu taj jñānaṃ viddhi rājasam //
children.translated_text: cognizes manifold and diverse entities in all beings — know that knowledge to be <s>rājasa</s>. ||

children.text: pṛthaktvena tu yaj jñānaṃ nānā-bhāvān pṛthag-vidhān /
vetti sarveṣu bhūteṣu taj jñānaṃ viddhi rājasam //

body.text: sarveṣu bhūteṣu brāhmaṇādiṣu brāhmaṇādyākārapṛthaktvenātmākhyān api bhāvān nānābhūtān sitadīrghādipṛthaktvena ca pṛthagvidhān phalādisaṃyogayogyān karmādhikāravelāyāṃ yaj jñānaṃ vetti, taj jñānaṃ rājasaṃ viddhi //
body.translated_text: That knowledge which, at the time of being qualified for action, cognizes in all beings such as <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like, the entities called selves too as manifold through the separateness of [their being] <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like, and as diverse — as differentiated by the distinctions of white, tall, and the like, and as fit for connection with fruits and the like — know that knowledge to be <s>rājasa</s>. //

children.text: sarveṣu bhūteṣu brāhmaṇa-ādiṣu brāhmaṇa-ādy-ākāra-pṛthaktvenā atma-ākhyān api bhāvān nānā-bhūtān sita-dīrgha-ādi-pṛthaktvena ca pṛthag-vidhān phala-ādi-saṃyoga-yogyān karma-adhikāra-velāyāṃ yaj jñānaṃ vetti, taj jñānaṃ rājasaṃ viddhi //
yat tu kṛtsnavad ekasmin kārye saktam ahetukam /
children.translated_text: But that [knowledge] which clings to a single effect as if it were the whole, which is irrational, |

children.text: atattvārthavad alpaṃ ca tat tāmasam udāhṛtam //
children.translated_text: which does not grasp the true nature of things, and which is trivial — that is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>. //

children.text: yat tu kṛtsnavad ekasmin kārye saktam ahetukam /
atattva-arthavad alpaṃ ca tat tāmasam udāhṛtam //

body.text: yat tu jñānam, ekasmin kārye ekasmin kartavye karmaṇi pretabhūtagaṇādyārādhanarūpe atyalpaphale kṛtsnaphalavat saktam, ahetukam vastutas tv akṛtsnaphalavattayā tathāvidhasaṅgaheturahitam atattvārthavat pūrvavad evātmani pṛthaktvādiyuktatayā mithyābhūtārthaviṣayam, atyalpaphalaṃ ca pretabhūtādyārādhanaviṣayatvād alpaṃ ca, taj jñānaṃ tāmasam udāhṛtam //
body.translated_text: But that knowledge which, regarding a single action to be performed — an action in the form of propitiation of ghosts, spirits, and the like, producing very meager fruit — is attached [to it] as if it were the whole fruit; which is without [rational] cause, since in reality it lacks a basis for such attachment due to not yielding complete fruit; which has an object that is unreal — as before, [regarding] the self as possessing separateness and the like that are false; and which pertains to very meager fruit, since it concerns the propitiation of ghosts, spirits, and the like, and is therefore meager — that knowledge is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>. ||

children.text: yat tu jñānam, ekasmin kārye ekasmin kartavye karmaṇi preta-bhūta-gaṇa-ādy-ārādhana-rūpe atyalpa-phale kṛtsna-phalavat saktam, ahetukam vastutas tv akṛtsna-phalavattayā tathā-vidha-saṅga-hetu-rahitam atattva-arthavat pūrvavad evā atmani pṛthaktva-ādi-yuktatayā mithyā-bhūta-artha-viṣayam, atyalpa-phalaṃ ca preta-bhūta-ādy-ārādhana-viṣayatvād alpaṃ ca, taj jñānaṃ tāmasam udāhṛtam //

body.text: evaṃ kartavyakarmaviṣayajñānasyādhikāravelāyām adhikāryaṃśena guṇatas traividhyam uktvā anuṣṭheyasya karmaṇo guṇatas traividhyam āha --
body.translated_text: Having thus stated the threefold division according to the <s>guṇas</s> of knowledge concerning action to be performed — [a division] from the standpoint of the qualified person at the time of qualification — He now states the threefold division according to the <s>guṇas</s> of the action to be performed:

children.text: evaṃ kartavya-karma-viṣaya-jñānasya adhikāra-velāyām adhikāry-aṃśena guṇatas traividhyam uktvā anuṣṭheyasya karmaṇo guṇatas traividhyam āha ---
niyataṃ saṅgarahitam arāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'Obligatory, free from attachment, done without passion or hatred,' |

children.text: aphalaprepsunā karma yat tat sāttvikam ucyate //
children.translated_text: 'by one who does not desire the fruit — such action is called <s>sāttvika</s>.' ||

children.text: niyataṃ saṅga-rahitam arāga-dveṣataḥ kṛtam /
aphala-prepsunā karma yat tat sāttvikam ucyate //

body.text: niyatam svavarṇāśramocitam, saṅgarahitam kartṛtvādisaṅgarahitam, arāgadveṣataḥ kṛtam kīrtirāgād akīrtidveṣāc ca na kṛtam; adambhena kṛtam ityarthaḥ; aphalaprepsunā aphalābhisandhinā kāryam ity eva kṛtaṃ yat karma, tat sāttvikam ucyate //
body.translated_text: Obligatory (<s>niyata</s>) — suited to one's <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>; free from attachment — free from attachment in the form of [the sense of] agency and the like; done without passion or hatred — not done out of passion for fame or hatred of infamy; meaning: done without ostentation. Done by one who does not desire the fruit — done by one without attachment to the fruit, [thinking] 'this is [simply] duty' — such action is called <s>sāttvika</s>. ||

children.text: niyatam sva-varṇa-āśrama-ucitam, saṅga-rahitam kartṛtva-ādi-saṅga-rahitam, arāga-dveṣataḥ kṛtam kīrti-rāgād akīrti-dveṣāc ca na kṛtam; adambhena kṛtam ity-arthaḥ; aphala-prepsunā aphala-abhisandhinā kāryam ity eva kṛtaṃ yat karma, tat sāttvikam ucyate //
yat tu kāmepsunā karma sāhaṅkāreṇa vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'But action that is done by one desiring the fruit, or again with egoism,' |

children.text: kriyate bahulāyāsaṃ tad rājasam udāhṛtam //
children.translated_text: 'involving much exertion — that is declared to be <s>rājasa</s>.' ||

children.text: yat tu kāma-īpsunā karma sa-ahaṅ-kāreṇa vā punaḥ /
kriyate bahula-āyāsaṃ tad rājasam udāhṛtam //

body.text: yat tu punaḥ kāmepsunā phalaprepsunā sāhaṃkāreṇa vā vāśabdaś cārthe kartṛtvābhimānayuktena ca, bahulāyāsaṃ yat karma kriyate, tad rājasam bahulāyāsam idaṃ karma mayaiva kriyata ity evaṃrūpābhimānayuktena yat karma kriyate, tad rājasam ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: But action that is done by one desiring the fruit — seeking the fruit — or with egoism (the word 'or' is used in the conjunctive sense), i.e., conjoined with the conceit of being the agent, involving much exertion — that action which is performed with the conceit of the form 'this action involving much exertion is accomplished by me alone' — that is declared to be <s>rājasa</s>. This is the meaning. ||

children.text: yat tu punaḥ kāma-īpsunā phala-prepsunā sa-ahaṃ-kāreṇa vā vā-śabdaś ca arthe kartṛtva-abhimāna-yuktena ca, bahula-āyāsaṃ yat karma kriyate, tad rājasam bahula-āyāsam idaṃ karma maya aiva kriyata ity evaṃ-rūpa-abhimāna-yuktena yat karma kriyate, tad rājasam ity-arthaḥ //
anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsām anavekṣya ca pauruṣam /
children.translated_text: 'Without considering the consequence, the loss, the injury, or one's own capacity,' |

children.text: mohād ārabhyate karma yat tat tāmasam ucyate //
children.translated_text: 'action that is undertaken out of delusion — that is called <s>tāmasa</s>.' ||

children.text: anubandhaṃ kṣayaṃ hiṃsām anavekṣya ca pauruṣam /
mohād ārabhyate karma yat tat tāmasam ucyate //

body.text: kṛte karmaṇy anubadhyamānaṃ duḥkham anubandhaḥ; kṣayaḥ karmaṇi kriyamāṇe arthavināśaḥ; hiṃsā tatra prāṇipīḍā; pauruṣam ātmanaḥ karmasamāpanasāmarthyam; etāni anavekṣya avimṛśya, mohāt paramapuruṣakartṛtvājñānād yat karmārabhyate, tat tāmasam ucyate //
body.translated_text: Consequence (<s>anubandha</s>) is the suffering that attaches to the performed action. Loss (<s>kṣaya</s>) is the destruction of resources in the course of performing the action. Injury (<s>hiṃsā</s>) is the harming of living beings therein. Capacity (<s>pauruṣa</s>) is one's own ability to complete the action. Without considering these — without deliberating upon them — action that is undertaken out of delusion, out of ignorance of the fact that the Supreme Person is the [true] agent — that is called <s>tāmasa</s>. ||

children.text: kṛte karmaṇy anubadhyamānaṃ duḥkham anubandhaḥ; kṣayaḥ karmaṇi kriyamāṇe artha-vināśaḥ; hiṃsā tatra prāṇi-pīḍā; pauruṣam ātmanaḥ karma-samāpana-sāmarthyam; etāni anavekṣya avimṛśya, mohāt parama-puruṣa-kartṛtva-ajñānād yat karmā arabhyate, tat tāmasam ucyate //
muktasaṅgo 'nahaṃvādī dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Free from attachment, without self-reference, endowed with steadfastness and enthusiasm,' |

children.text: siddhyasiddhyor nirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate //
children.translated_text: 'unaffected by success or failure — such an agent is called <s>sāttvika</s>.' ||

children.text: mukta-saṅgo 'nahaṃvādī dhṛty-utsāha-samanvitaḥ /
siddhy-asiddhyor nirvikāraḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate //

body.text: muktasaṅgaḥ phalasaṅgarahitaḥ anahaṃvādī kartṛtvābhimānarahitaḥ, dhṛtyutsāhasamanvitaḥ ārabdhe karmaṇi yāvatkarmasamāptyavarjanīyaduḥkhadhāraṇaṃ dhṛtiḥ; utsāhaḥ udyuktacetastvam; tābhyāṃ samanvitaḥ, siddhyasiddhyor nirvikāraḥ yuddhādau karmaṇi tadupakaraṇabhūtadravyārjanādiṣu ca siddhyasiddhyor avikṛtacittaḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate //
body.translated_text: Free from attachment — devoid of attachment to the fruit; without self-reference — devoid of the conceit of agency; endowed with steadfastness and enthusiasm — steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>) is the endurance of unavoidable suffering until the completion of the action that has been undertaken; enthusiasm (<s>utsāha</s>) is eagerness of mind; endowed with both of these. Unaffected by success or failure — of unperturbed mind regarding success and failure in action such as battle and the like, and in the acquisition of materials and other things subsidiary to it. Such an agent is called <s>sāttvika</s>. ||

children.text: mukta-saṅgaḥ phala-saṅga-rahitaḥ anahaṃvādī kartṛtva-abhimāna-rahitaḥ, dhṛty-utsāha-samanvitaḥ ārabdhe karmaṇi yāvat-karma-samāpty-avarjanīya-duḥkha-dhāraṇaṃ dhṛtiḥ; utsāhaḥ udyukta-cetastvam; tābhyāṃ samanvitaḥ, siddhy-asiddhyor nirvikāraḥ yuddha-ādau karmaṇi tad-upakaraṇa-bhūta-dravya-arjana-ādiṣu ca siddhy-asiddhyor avikṛta-cittaḥ kartā sāttvika ucyate //
ragī karmaphalaprepsur lubdho hiṃsātmako 'śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Passionate, desiring the fruits of action, greedy, of a harmful nature, impure,' |

children.text: harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'subject to elation and grief — such an agent is proclaimed <s>rājasa</s>.' ||

children.text: ragī karma-phala-prepsur lubdho hiṃsā-ātmako 'śuciḥ /
harṣa-śoka-anvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //

body.text: rāgī yaśo'rthī, karmaphalaprepsuḥ karmaphalārthī; lubdhaḥ karmāpekṣitadravyavyayasvabhāvarahitaḥ, hiṃsātmakaḥ parān pīḍayitvā taiḥ karma kurvāṇaḥ, aśuciḥ karmāpekṣitaśuddhirahitaḥ, harṣaśokānvitaḥ yuddhādau karmaṇi jayādisiddhyasiddhyor harṣaśokānvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Passionate (<s>rāgī</s>) — seeking fame; desiring the fruits of action — seeking the fruits of action; greedy (<s>lubdha</s>) — of a nature that does not expend resources needed for the action; of a harmful nature — one who performs action by oppressing others and making them work; impure — devoid of the purity required for the action; subject to elation and grief — subject to elation and grief at the success and failure of victory and the like in action such as battle. Such an agent is proclaimed <s>rājasa</s>. ||

children.text: rāgī yaśo-'rthī, karma-phala-prepsuḥ karma-phala-arthī; lubdhaḥ karma-apekṣita-dravya-vyaya-sva-bhāva-rahitaḥ, hiṃsā-ātmakaḥ parān pīḍayitvā taiḥ karma kurvāṇaḥ, aśuciḥ karma-apekṣita-śuddhi-rahitaḥ, harṣa-śoka-anvitaḥ yuddha-ādau karmaṇi jaya-ādi-siddhy-asiddhyor harṣa-śoka-anvitaḥ kartā rājasaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naikṛtiko 'lasaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Undisciplined, vulgar, stubborn, deceitful, dishonest, lazy,' |

children.text: viṣādī dīrghasūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate //
children.translated_text: 'despondent, and procrastinating — such an agent is called <s>tāmasa</s>.' ||

children.text: ayuktaḥ prākṛtaḥ stabdhaḥ śaṭho naikṛtiko 'lasaḥ /
viṣādī dīrgha-sūtrī ca kartā tāmasa ucyate //

body.text: ayuktaḥ śāstrīyakarmāyogyaḥ, vikarmasthaḥ, prākṛtaḥ anadhigatavidyaḥ, stabdhaḥ anārambhaśīlaḥ, śaṭhaḥ abhicārādikarmaruciḥ, naikṛtikaḥ vañcanaparaḥ, alasaḥ ārabdheṣv api karmasu mandapravṛttiḥ, viṣādī atimātrāvasādaśīlaḥ dīrghasūtrī abhicārādikarma kurvan pareṣu dīrghakālavartyanarthaparyālocanaśīlaḥ, evaṃbhūto yaḥ kartā, sa tāmasaḥ //
body.translated_text: Undisciplined (<s>ayukta</s>) — unfit for scriptural action, established in improper action; vulgar (<s>prākṛta</s>) — uneducated; stubborn (<s>stabdha</s>) — of a nature that does not undertake [good works]; deceitful (<s>śaṭha</s>) — having a taste for sorcery and the like; dishonest (<s>naikṛtika</s>) — devoted to cheating; lazy (<s>alasa</s>) — slow in effort even in actions already undertaken; despondent (<s>viṣādī</s>) — of a nature given to excessive dejection; procrastinating (<s>dīrghasūtrī</s>) — when performing sorcery and the like, of a disposition to contemplate harm to others over a long period. An agent who is of such a nature — he is <s>tāmasa</s>. ||

children.text: ayuktaḥ śāstrīya-karma-ayogyaḥ, vikarma-sthaḥ, prākṛtaḥ anadhigata-vidyaḥ, stabdhaḥ anārambha-śīlaḥ, śaṭhaḥ abhicāra-ādi-karma-ruciḥ, naikṛtikaḥ vañcana-paraḥ, alasaḥ ārabdheṣv api karmasu manda-pravṛttiḥ, viṣādī atimātra-avasāda-śīlaḥ dīrgha-sūtrī abhicāra-ādi-karma kurvan pareṣu dīrgha-kāla-varty-anartha-paryālocana-śīlaḥ, evaṃ-bhūto yaḥ kartā, sa tāmasaḥ //

body.text: evaṃ kartavyakarmaviṣayajñāne kartavye ca karmaṇi anuṣṭhātari ca guṇatas traividhyam uktam; idānīṃ sarvatattvasarvapuruṣārthaniścayarūpāyā buddher dhṛteś ca guṇatas traividhyam āha --
body.translated_text: Thus, the threefold division according to the <s>guṇas</s> of knowledge concerning action to be performed, of the action to be performed, and of the performer has been stated. Now He states the threefold division according to the <s>guṇas</s> of understanding (<s>buddhi</s>), which has the form of discerning determination regarding all realities and all human goals, and of steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>):

children.text: evaṃ kartavya-karma-viṣaya-jñāne kartavye ca karmaṇi anuṣṭhātari ca guṇatas traividhyam uktam; idānīṃ sarva-tattva-sarva-puruṣa-artha-niścaya-rūpāyā buddher dhṛteś ca guṇatas traividhyam āha ---
buddher bhedaṃ dhṛteś caiva guṇatas trividhaṃ śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: 'Hear the threefold distinction of understanding and also of steadfastness,' |

children.text: procyamānam aśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanaṃjaya //
children.translated_text: 'as declared separately according to the <s>guṇas</s>, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>.' ||

children.text: buddher bhedaṃ dhṛteś ca eva guṇatas tri-vidhaṃ śṛṇu /
procyamānam aśeṣeṇa pṛthaktvena dhanaṃjaya //

body.text: buddhiḥ vivekapūrvakaṃ niścayarūpaṃ jñānam; dhṛtiḥ ārabdhāyāḥ kriyāyā vighnopanipāte 'pi dhāraṇam, tayos sattvādiguṇatas trividhaṃ bhedaṃ pṛthaktvena procyamānaṃ yathāvac chṛṇu //
body.translated_text: Understanding (<s>buddhi</s>) is knowledge in the form of determination preceded by discernment. Steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>) is the maintenance of an activity that has been undertaken, even when obstacles arise. Hear properly the threefold distinction of these two according to the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>sattva</s> and the rest, as declared separately. ||

children.text: buddhiḥ viveka-pūrvakaṃ niścaya-rūpaṃ jñānam; dhṛtiḥ ārabdhāyāḥ kriyāyā vighna-upanipāte 'pi dhāraṇam, tayos sattva-ādi-guṇatas tri-vidhaṃ bhedaṃ pṛthaktvena procyamānaṃ yathāvac chṛṇu //
pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kāryākārye bhayābhaye /
children.translated_text: 'That which knows activity and cessation, what should and should not be done, fear and fearlessness,' |

children.text: bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī //
children.translated_text: 'bondage and liberation — that understanding, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is <s>sāttvika</s>.' ||

children.text: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kārya-akārye bhaya-abhaye /
bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yā vetti buddhiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī //

body.text: pravṛttiḥ abhyudayasādhanabhūto dharmaḥ, nivṛttiḥ mokṣasādhanabhūtaḥ, tav ubhau yathāvasthitau yā buddhir vetti; kāryākārye sarvavarṇānāṃ pravṛttinivṛttidharmayor anyataraniṣṭhānāṃ deśakālāvasthāviśeṣeṣu "idaṃ kāryam, idam akāryam" iti yā vetti; bhayābhaye -- śāstrātivṛttir bhayasthānaṃ tadanuvṛttir abhayasthānam, bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca saṃsārayāthātmyaṃ tadvigamayāthātmyaṃ ca yā vetti; sā sāttvikī buddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is <s>dharma</s> that is the means to worldly prosperity; cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>) is [<s>dharma</s>] that is the means to liberation — the understanding (<s>buddhi</s>) that knows both of these as they truly are. What should and should not be done — for persons of all <s>varṇas</s> established in either the path of activity or the path of cessation, in specific times, places, and circumstances, [the understanding] that knows 'this should be done, this should not be done.' Fear and fearlessness — transgression of scripture is the ground for fear; conformity to it is the ground for fearlessness. Bondage and liberation — the true nature of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the true nature of its cessation — the understanding that knows [all] these: that is <s>sāttvika</s> understanding. ||

children.text: pravṛttiḥ abhyudaya-sādhana-bhūto dharmaḥ, nivṛttiḥ mokṣa-sādhana-bhūtaḥ, tav ubhau yathā-avasthitau yā buddhir vetti; kārya-akārye sarva-varṇānāṃ pravṛtti-nivṛtti-dharmayor anyatara-niṣṭhānāṃ deśa-kāla-avasthā-viśeṣeṣu "idaṃ kāryam, idam akāryam" iti yā vetti; bhaya-abhaye --- śāstra-ativṛttir bhaya-sthānaṃ tad-anuvṛttir abhaya-sthānam, bandhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca saṃsāra-yāthātmyaṃ tad-vigama-yāthātmyaṃ ca yā vetti; sā sāttvikī buddhiḥ //
yathā dharmam adharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ cākāryam eva ca /
children.translated_text: 'That by which one knows <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, what should be done and what should not,' |

children.text: ayathāvat prajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī //
children.translated_text: 'incorrectly — that understanding, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is <s>rājasa</s>.' ||

children.text: yathā dharmam adharmaṃ ca kāryaṃ ca akāryam eva ca /
ayathāvat prajānāti buddhiḥ sā pārtha rājasī //

body.text: yathā pūrvoktaṃ dvividhaṃ dharmaṃ tadviparītaṃ ca tanniṣṭhānāṃ deśakālāvasthādiṣu kāryaṃ cākāryaṃ ca yathāvan na jānāti, sā rājasī buddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: That [understanding] which does not correctly know the twofold <s>dharma</s> as previously stated, and its opposite [<s>adharma</s>], and what should and should not be done in specific times, places, and circumstances for those established [in either path] — that is <s>rājasa</s> understanding. ||

children.text: yathā pūrva-uktaṃ dvi-vidhaṃ dharmaṃ tad-viparītaṃ ca tan-niṣṭhānāṃ deśa-kāla-avasthā-ādiṣu kāryaṃ ca akāryaṃ ca yathāvan na jānāti, sā rājasī buddhiḥ //
adharmaṃ dharmam iti yā manyate tamasāvṛtā /
children.translated_text: 'That which, enveloped in darkness, considers <s>adharma</s> to be <s>dharma</s>,' |

children.text: sarvārthān viparītāṃś ca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī //
children.translated_text: 'and [sees] all things in a perverted way — that understanding, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is <s>tāmasa</s>.' ||

children.text: adharmaṃ dharmam iti yā manyate tamasā āvṛtā /
sarva-arthān viparītāṃś ca buddhiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī //

body.text: tāmasī tu buddhiḥ tamasāvṛtā satī sarvārthān viparītān manyate / adharmaṃ dharmaṃ, dharmaṃ cādharmaṃ, santaṃ cārtham asantam, asantam cārthaṃ santaṃ, paraṃ ca tattvam aparam, aparaṃ ca tattvaṃ param / evaṃ sarvaṃ viparītaṃ manyata ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: But <s>tāmasa</s> understanding, being enveloped in darkness, considers all things in a perverted way: <s>adharma</s> to be <s>dharma</s>, and <s>dharma</s> to be <s>adharma</s>; an existing thing to be non-existent, and a non-existent thing to be existing; the supreme reality to be the non-supreme, and the non-supreme reality to be the supreme. The meaning is: it considers everything in a perverted way. ||

children.text: tāmasī tu buddhiḥ tamasā āvṛtā satī sarva-arthān viparītān manyate / adharmaṃ dharmaṃ, dharmaṃ ca adharmaṃ, santaṃ ca artham asantam, asantam ca arthaṃ santaṃ, paraṃ ca tattvam aparam, aparaṃ ca tattvaṃ param / evaṃ sarvaṃ viparītaṃ manyata ity-arthaḥ //
dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥprāṇendriyakriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The steadfastness by which one sustains the activities of the mind, vital breath, and senses,' |

children.text: yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī //
children.translated_text: 'through unfailing <s>yoga</s> — that steadfastness, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is <s>sāttvika</s>.' ||

children.text: dhṛtyā yayā dhārayate manaḥ-prāṇa-indriya-kriyāḥ /
yogena avyabhicāriṇyā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha sāttvikī //

body.text: yayā dhṛtyā yogenāvyabhicāriṇyā manaḥprāṇendriyāṇāṃ kriyāḥ puruṣo dhārayate; yogaḥ mokṣasādhanabhūtaṃ bhagavadupāsanam; yogena prayojanabhūtenāvyabhicāriṇyā yogoddeśena pravṛttās tatsādhanabhūtā manaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ kriyāḥ yayā dhṛtyā dhārayate, sā sāttvikītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: The steadfastness by which a person sustains the activities of the mind, vital breath, and senses through unfailing <s>yoga</s>. <s>Yoga</s> is the worship of the Lord that serves as the means to liberation. Through <s>yoga</s> as its purpose — with unfailing [commitment] — the activities of the mind and the rest, which are undertaken for and serve as means to that [<s>yoga</s>], are sustained by that steadfastness: that is <s>sāttvika</s>. This is the meaning. ||

children.text: yayā dhṛtyā yogena avyabhicāriṇyā manaḥ-prāṇa-indriyāṇāṃ kriyāḥ puruṣo dhārayate; yogaḥ mokṣa-sādhana-bhūtaṃ bhagavad-upāsanam; yogena prayojana-bhūtena avyabhicāriṇyā yoga-uddeśena pravṛttās tat-sādhana-bhūtā manaḥ-prabhṛtīnāṃ kriyāḥ yayā dhṛtyā dhārayate, sā sāttviki īty-arthaḥ //
yayā tu dharmakāmārthān dhṛtyā dhārayate 'rjuna /
children.translated_text: 'But the steadfastness by which one holds to <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth, O <s>Arjuna</s>,' |

children.text: prasaṅgena phalākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī //
children.translated_text: 'with attachment, desiring the fruit — that steadfastness, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is <s>rājasa</s>.' ||

children.text: yayā tu dharma-kāma-arthān dhṛtyā dhārayate 'rjuna /
prasaṅgena phala-ākāṅkṣī dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha rājasī //

body.text: phalākāṅkṣī puruṣaḥ prakṛṣṭasaṅgena dharmakāmārthān yayā dhṛtyā dhārayate, sā rājasī / dharmakāmārthaśabdena tatsādhanabhūtā manaḥprāṇendriyakriyā lakṣyante / phalākāṅkṣīty atrāpi phalaśabdena rājasatvād dharmakāmārthā eva vivakṣitāḥ / ato dharmakāmārthāpekṣayā manaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ kriyā yayā dhṛtyā dhārayate, sā rājasīty uktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: The steadfastness by which a person who desires the fruit holds to <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth with intense attachment — that is <s>rājasa</s>. By the words <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth, the activities of the mind, vital breath, and senses that serve as their means are intended. Here too, by the word 'fruit,' since it is <s>rājasa</s>, <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth themselves are what is intended. Therefore, the steadfastness by which the activities of the mind and the rest are sustained with a view to <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth — that is stated to be <s>rājasa</s>. ||

children.text: phala-ākāṅkṣī puruṣaḥ prakṛṣṭa-saṅgena dharma-kāma-arthān yayā dhṛtyā dhārayate, sā rājasī / dharma-kāma-artha-śabdena tat-sādhana-bhūtā manaḥ-prāṇa-indriya-kriyā lakṣyante / phala-ākāṅkṣi īty atra api phala-śabdena rājasatvād dharma-kāma-arthā eva vivakṣitāḥ / ato dharma-kāma-artha-apekṣayā manaḥ-prabhṛtīnāṃ kriyā yayā dhṛtyā dhārayate, sā rājasi īty uktaṃ bhavati //
yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madam eva ca /
children.translated_text: 'That by which a person of poor understanding does not abandon sleep, fear, grief,' |

children.text: na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī //
children.translated_text: 'despondency, and also intoxication — that steadfastness, O <s>Pārtha</s>, is <s>tāmasa</s>.' ||

children.text: yayā svapnaṃ bhayaṃ śokaṃ viṣādaṃ madam eva ca /
na vimuñcati durmedhā dhṛtiḥ sā pārtha tāmasī //

body.text: yayā dhṛtyā /svapnaṃ nidrām / madaṃ viṣayānubhavajanitaṃ madam / svapnamadav uddiśya pravṛttā manaḥprāṇādīnāṃ kriyāḥ durmedhā na vimuñcati dhārayati / bhayaśokaviṣādaśabdāś ca bhayaśokādidāyiviṣayaparāḥ; tatsādhanabhūtāś ca manaḥprāṇādikriyā yayā dhārayate, sā dhṛtis tāmasī //
body.translated_text: The steadfastness by which — sleep means slumber; intoxication means the intoxication produced by the experience of sense-objects — a person of poor understanding does not abandon, [i.e.,] sustains, the activities of the mind, vital breath, and the rest that are directed toward sleep and intoxication. The words fear, grief, and despondency refer to sense-objects that produce fear, grief, and the like; and the activities of the mind, vital breath, and the rest that serve as means to those — the steadfastness by which one sustains them: that is <s>tāmasa</s> steadfastness. ||

children.text: yayā dhṛtyā /svapnaṃ nidrām / madaṃ viṣaya-anubhava-janitaṃ madam / svapna-madav uddiśya pravṛttā manaḥ-prāṇa-ādīnāṃ kriyāḥ durmedhā na vimuñcati dhārayati / bhaya-śoka-viṣāda-śabdāś ca bhaya-śoka-ādi-dāyi-viṣaya-parāḥ; tat-sādhana-bhūtāś ca manaḥ-prāṇa-ādi-kriyā yayā dhārayate, sā dhṛtis tāmasī //

body.text: sukhaṃ tv idānīṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha /
body.translated_text: 'But now hear from Me of the threefold happiness, O best of <s>Bhāratas</s>.' |

children.text: sukhaṃ tv idānīṃ tri-vidhaṃ śṛṇu me bharata-rṣabha /

body.text: pūrvoktāḥ sarve jñānakarmakartrādayo yac cheṣabhūtāḥ, tac ca sukhaṃ guṇatas trividham idānīṃ śṛṇu //
body.translated_text: All the previously stated [categories] — knowledge, action, agent, and the like — are subservient to that [happiness]; and that happiness too is threefold according to the <s>guṇas</s> — now hear. ||

children.text: pūrva-uktāḥ sarve jñāna-karma-kartr-ādayo yac cheṣa-bhūtāḥ, tac ca sukhaṃ guṇatas tri-vidham idānīṃ śṛṇu //

body.text: abhyāsād ramate yatra duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati //
body.translated_text: 'In which one delights through practice, and reaches the end of suffering,' ||

children.text: abhyāsād ramate yatra duḥkha-antaṃ ca nigacchati //
yat tad agre viṣam iva pariṇāme 'mṛtopamam /
children.translated_text: 'that which is like poison at first but like nectar in its maturation,' |

children.text: tat sukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktam ātmabuddhiprasādajam //
children.translated_text: 'that happiness is declared to be <s>sāttvika</s>, born of the serenity of self-knowledge.' ||

children.text: yat tad agre viṣam iva pariṇāme 'mṛta-upamam /
tat sukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktam ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam //

body.text: yasmin sukhe cirakālābhyāsāt krameṇa niratiśayāṃ ratiṃ prāpnoti, duḥkhāntaṃ ca nigacchati nikhilasya sāṃsārikasya duḥkhasyāntaṃ nigacchati // tad eva viśinaṣṭi -- yat tat sukham, agre yogopakramavelāyāṃ bahvāyāsasādhyatvād viviktasvarūpasyānanubhūtatvāc ca viṣam iva duḥkham iva bhavati, pariṇāme 'mṛtopamam / pariṇāme vipāke abhyāsabalena viviktātmasvarūpāvirbhāve amṛtopamaṃ bhavati, tac ca ātmabuddhiprasādajam ātmaviṣayā buddhiḥ ātmabuddhiḥ, tasyāḥ nivṛttasakaletaraviṣayatvaṃ prasādaḥ, nivṛttasakaletaraviṣayabuddhyā viviktasvabhāvātmānubhavajanitaṃ sukham amṛtopamaṃ bhavati; tat sukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktam //
body.translated_text: The happiness in which, through long-continued practice, one gradually attains unsurpassed delight, and reaches the end of suffering — reaches the end of all <s>saṃsāric</s> suffering. He further specifies it: that happiness which, at the beginning — at the time of commencing <s>yoga</s> — is like poison, i.e., like suffering, because it requires much exertion and because the distinct essential nature [of the self] has not been experienced; but in its maturation, is like nectar — in its ripening, when the distinct essential nature of the self becomes manifest through the force of practice, it becomes like nectar. And it is born of the serenity of self-knowledge: understanding directed toward the self is self-knowledge; its serenity is the withdrawal from all other objects. The happiness born of the experience of the self in its distinct nature, through understanding that has been withdrawn from all other objects — that becomes like nectar. That happiness is declared to be <s>sāttvika</s>. ||

children.text: yasmin sukhe cira-kāla-abhyāsāt krameṇa niratiśayāṃ ratiṃ prāpnoti, duḥkha-antaṃ ca nigacchati nikhilasya sāṃsārikasya duḥkhasya antaṃ nigacchati // tad eva viśinaṣṭi --- yat tat sukham, agre yoga-upakrama-velāyāṃ bahv-āyāsa-sādhyatvād vivikta-sva-rūpasya ananubhūtatvāc ca viṣam iva duḥkham iva bhavati, pariṇāme 'mṛta-upamam / pariṇāme vipāke abhyāsa-balena vivikta-ātma-sva-rūpa-āvirbhāve amṛta-upamaṃ bhavati, tac ca ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam ātma-viṣayā buddhiḥ ātma-buddhiḥ, tasyāḥ nivṛtta-sakala-itara-viṣayatvaṃ prasādaḥ, nivṛtta-sakala-itara-viṣaya-buddhyā vivikta-sva-bhāva-ātma-anubhava-janitaṃ sukham amṛta-upamaṃ bhavati; tat sukhaṃ sāttvikaṃ proktam //
viṣayendriyasaṃyogād yat tad agre 'mṛtopamam /
children.translated_text: 'That which arises from the contact of the senses with their objects — like nectar at first,' |

children.text: pariṇāme viṣam iva tat sukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam //
children.translated_text: 'but like poison in its maturation — that happiness is regarded as <s>rājasa</s>.' ||

children.text: viṣaya-indriya-saṃyogād yat tad agre 'mṛta-upamam /
pariṇāme viṣam iva tat sukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam //

body.text: agre anubhavavelāyāṃ viṣayendriyasaṃyogād yat tad amṛtam iva bhavati, pariṇāme vipāke viṣayāṇāṃ sukhatānimittakṣudādau nivṛtte tasya ca sukhasya nirayādinimittatvād viṣam iva pītaṃ bhavati, tat sukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam //
body.translated_text: At first — at the time of experience — arising from the contact of the senses with their objects, that which is like nectar; but in its maturation — in its ripening, when the causes of pleasure such as hunger and the like that made the objects pleasurable have ceased, and when that pleasure itself becomes the cause of hell and the like — it becomes like swallowed poison. That happiness is regarded as <s>rājasa</s>. ||

children.text: agre anubhava-velāyāṃ viṣaya-indriya-saṃyogād yat tad amṛtam iva bhavati, pariṇāme vipāke viṣayāṇāṃ sukhatā-nimitta-kṣud-ādau nivṛtte tasya ca sukhasya niraya-ādi-nimittatvād viṣam iva pītaṃ bhavati, tat sukhaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam //
yad agre cānubandhe ca sukhaṃ mohanam ātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That happiness which both at first and in its consequence is deluding to the self,' |

children.text: nidrālasyapramādotthaṃ tat tāmasam udāhṛtam //
children.translated_text: 'arising from sleep, laziness, and heedlessness — that is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>.' ||

children.text: yad agre ca anubandhe ca sukhaṃ mohanam ātmanaḥ /
nidrā-ālasya-pramāda-utthaṃ tat tāmasam udāhṛtam //

body.text: yat sukham agre cānubandhe ca anubhavavelāyāṃ vipāke ca ātmano mohanaṃ mohahetur bhavati; moho 'tra yathāvasthitavastvaprakāśo 'bhipretaḥ; nidrālasyapramādottham nidrālasyapramādajanitam, nidrādayo hy anubhavavelāyām api mohahetavaḥ / nidrāyā mohahetutvaṃ spṛṣṭam / ālasyam indriyavyāpāram āndyam / indriyavyāpāram āndye ca jñānam āndyaṃ bhavaty eva / pramādaḥ kṛtyānavadhānarūpa iti tatrāpi jñānam āndyaṃ bhavati / tataś ca tayor api mohahetutvam / tat sukhaṃ tāmasam udāhṛtam / ato mumukṣuṇā rajastamasī abhibhūya sattvam evopādeyam ity uktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: That happiness which both at first and in its consequence — both at the time of experience and in its ripening — is deluding to the self, is the cause of delusion; delusion here means the non-manifestation of things as they truly are. Arising from sleep, laziness, and heedlessness — generated by sleep, laziness, and heedlessness. For sleep and the rest are causes of delusion even at the time of experience. The delusion-causing nature of sleep is self-evident. Laziness is the dullness of sensory activity; and when sensory activity is dulled, knowledge too becomes dulled. Heedlessness is inattentiveness regarding what ought to be done — therein too knowledge becomes dulled. Therefore those two also are causes of delusion. That happiness is declared to be <s>tāmasa</s>. Hence, the seeker of liberation should overcome <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> and adopt <s>sattva</s> alone — this is what is stated. ||

children.text: yat sukham agre ca anubandhe ca anubhava-velāyāṃ vipāke ca ātmano mohanaṃ moha-hetur bhavati; moho 'tra yathā-avasthita-vastv-aprakāśo 'bhipretaḥ; nidrā-ālasya-pramāda-uttham nidrā-ālasya-pramāda-janitam, nidrā-ādayo hy anubhava-velāyām api moha-hetavaḥ / nidrāyā moha-hetutvaṃ spṛṣṭam / ālasyam indriya-vyāpāram āndyam / indriya-vyāpāram āndye ca jñānam āndyaṃ bhavaty eva / pramādaḥ kṛtya-anavadhāna-rūpa iti tatra api jñānam āndyaṃ bhavati / tataś ca tayor api moha-hetutvam / tat sukhaṃ tāmasam udāhṛtam / ato mumukṣuṇā rajas-tamasī abhibhūya sattvam eva upādeyam ity uktaṃ bhavati //
na tad asti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There is no being on earth, or in heaven among the gods,' |

children.text: sattvaṃ prakṛtijair muktaṃ yad ebhiḥ syāt tribhir guṇaiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'that is free from these three <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s>.' ||

children.text: na tad asti pṛthivyāṃ vā divi deveṣu vā punaḥ /
sattvaṃ prakṛti-jair muktaṃ yad ebhiḥ syāt tribhir guṇaiḥ //

body.text: pṛthivyāṃ manuṣyādiṣu divi deveṣu vā prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭeṣu brahmādiṣu sthāvarānteṣu prakṛtijair ebhis tribhir guṇair muktaṃ yat sattvaṃ prāṇijātam, na tad asti //
body.translated_text: On earth — among humans and the like; or in heaven, among the gods — among beings conjoined with <s>Prakṛti</s>, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to immobile beings, there is no living being that is free from these three <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s>. ||

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ manuṣya-ādiṣu divi deveṣu vā prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭeṣu brahmā-ādiṣu sthāvara-anteṣu prakṛti-jair ebhis tribhir guṇair muktaṃ yat sattvaṃ prāṇi-jātam, na tad asti //

body.text: "tyāgenaike amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ" ityādiṣu mokṣasādhanatayā nirdiṣṭas tyāgaḥ saṃnyāsaśabdārthād ananyaḥ; sa ca kriyamāṇeṣv eva karmasu kartṛtvatyāgamūlaḥ phalakarmaṇos tyāgaḥ; kartṛtvatyāgaś ca paramapuruṣe kartṛtvānusaṃdhānenety uktam / etat sarvaṃ sattvaguṇavṛddhikāryam iti sattvopādeyatājñāpanāya sattvarajastamasāṃ kāryabhedāḥ prapañcitāḥ / idānīm evaṃbhūtasya mokṣasādhanatayā kriyamāṇasya karmaṇaḥ paramapuruṣārādhanaveṣatāṃ tathānuṣṭhitasya ca karmaṇas tatprāptilakṣaṇaṃ phalaṃ pratipādayituṃ brāhmaṇādyadhikāriṇāṃ svabhāvānubandhisattvādiguṇabhedabhinnaṃ vṛttyā saha kartavyakarmasvarūpam āha --
body.translated_text: 'By renunciation alone some have attained immortality' — in such [<s>śrutis</s>], the renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>) prescribed as a means to liberation is not different from what is meant by the word <s>saṃnyāsa</s>; and that [renunciation], while actions are being performed, is the renunciation of the fruit and the agency, rooted in the renunciation of agency; and the renunciation of agency is through the contemplation of agency in the Supreme Person — this has been stated. All of this is the effect of the increase of the <s>sattva</s>-quality; to establish the desirability of <s>sattva</s>, the different effects of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> have been elaborated. Now, to establish that action performed in this manner as a means to liberation has the character of worship of the Supreme Person, and that the fruit of action so performed is the attainment of that [Supreme Person], He states the nature of the duties to be performed — differentiated by the distinction of <s>guṇas</s> such as <s>sattva</s> and the like that are connected with the innate nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — together with the livelihood, of the qualified persons beginning with <s>brāhmaṇas</s>:

children.text: "tyāgena eke amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ" ity-ādiṣu mokṣa-sādhanatayā nirdiṣṭas tyāgaḥ saṃnyāsa-śabda-arthād ananyaḥ; sa ca kriyamāṇeṣv eva karmasu kartṛtva-tyāga-mūlaḥ phala-karmaṇos tyāgaḥ; kartṛtva-tyāgaś ca parama-puruṣe kartṛtva-anusaṃdhānena ity uktam / etat sarvaṃ sattva-guṇa-vṛddhi-kāryam iti sattva-upādeyatā-jñāpanāya sattva-rajas-tamasāṃ kārya-bhedāḥ prapañcitāḥ / idānīm evaṃ-bhūtasya mokṣa-sādhanatayā kriyamāṇasya karmaṇaḥ parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-veṣatāṃ tathā-anuṣṭhitasya ca karmaṇas tat-prāpti-lakṣaṇaṃ phalaṃ pratipādayituṃ brāhmaṇa-ādy-adhikāriṇāṃ sva-bhāva-anubandhi-sattva-ādi-guṇa-bheda-bhinnaṃ vṛttyā saha kartavya-karma-sva-rūpam āha ---
brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca paraṃtapa /
children.translated_text: Of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>śūdras</s>, O scorcher of foes,

children.text: karmāṇi pravibhaktāni svabhāvaprabhavair guṇaiḥ //
children.translated_text: the duties are distributed according to the <s>guṇas</s> arising from [their respective] innate natures. ||

children.text: brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-viśāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ ca paraṃtapa /
karmāṇi pravibhaktāni sva-bhāva-prabhavair guṇaiḥ //

body.text: brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviśāṃ svakīyo bhāvaḥ svabhāvaḥ brāhmaṇādijanmahetubhūtaṃ prācīnakarmety arthaḥ; tatprabhavāḥ sattvādayo guṇāḥ / brāhmaṇasya svabhāvaprabhavo rajastamo'bhibhavenodbhūtaḥ sattvaguṇaḥ; kṣatriyasya svabhāvaprabhavaḥ tamassattvābhibhavenodbhūto rajoguṇaḥ; vaiśyasya svabhāvaprabhavaḥ sattvarajo'bhibhavenālpodriktas tamoguṇaḥ; śūdrasya svabhāvaprabhavas tu rajassattvābhibhavenātyudriktas tamoguṇaḥ / ebhiḥ svabhāvaprabhavair guṇaiḥ saha pravibhaktāni karmāṇi śāstraiḥ pratipāditāni / brāhmaṇādaya evaṃguṇakāḥ, teṣāṃ caitāni karmāṇi, vṛttayaś caitā iti hi vibhajya pratipādayanti śāstrāṇi //
body.translated_text: The innate nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>vaiśyas</s> is one's own characteristic disposition — meaning: the prior <s>karma</s> that is the cause of birth as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the like. The <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the like — arise from that. For the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the <s>guṇa</s> arising from innate nature is <s>sattva</s>, emerged through the suppression of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>. For the <s>kṣatriya</s>, the <s>guṇa</s> arising from innate nature is <s>rajas</s>, emerged through the suppression of <s>tamas</s> and <s>sattva</s>. For the <s>vaiśya</s>, the <s>guṇa</s> arising from innate nature is <s>tamas</s>, slightly predominant through the suppression of <s>sattva</s> and <s>rajas</s>. For the <s>śūdra</s>, the <s>guṇa</s> arising from innate nature is <s>tamas</s>, greatly predominant through the suppression of <s>rajas</s> and <s>sattva</s>. According to these <s>guṇas</s> arising from innate nature, the duties are distributed — established by the scriptures. For <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and the others are of such <s>guṇa</s>-constitutions, and these are their duties, and these are their livelihoods — the scriptures establish this by way of distribution. //

children.text: brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-viśāṃ svakīyo bhāvaḥ sva-bhāvaḥ brāhmaṇa-ādi-janma-hetu-bhūtaṃ prācīna-karma ity arthaḥ; tat-prabhavāḥ sattva-ādayo guṇāḥ / brāhmaṇasya sva-bhāva-prabhavo rajas-tamo-'bhibhavena udbhūtaḥ sattva-guṇaḥ; kṣatriyasya sva-bhāva-prabhavaḥ tamas-sattva-abhibhavena udbhūto rajo-guṇaḥ; vaiśyasya sva-bhāva-prabhavaḥ sattva-rajo-'bhibhavena alpa-udriktas tamo-guṇaḥ; śūdrasya sva-bhāva-prabhavas tu rajas-sattva-abhibhavena atyudriktas tamo-guṇaḥ / ebhiḥ sva-bhāva-prabhavair guṇaiḥ saha pravibhaktāni karmāṇi śāstraiḥ pratipāditāni / brāhmaṇa-ādaya evaṃ-guṇakāḥ, teṣāṃ ca etāni karmāṇi, vṛttayaś ca etā iti hi vibhajya pratipādayanti śāstrāṇi //
śamo damas tapaś śaucaṃ kṣāntir ārjavam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Tranquility, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forbearance, and uprightness,

children.text: jñānaṃ vijñānam āstikyaṃ brāhmaṃ karma svabhāvajam //
children.translated_text: knowledge, discernment, and faith — these are the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s duties, born of [his] innate nature. ||

children.text: śamo damas tapaś śaucaṃ kṣāntir ārjavam eva ca /
jñānaṃ vijñānam āstikyaṃ brāhmaṃ karma sva-bhāva-jam //

body.text:
śamaḥ bāhyendriyaniyamanam; damaḥ antaḥkaraṇaniyamanam; tapaḥ bhoganiyamanarūpaḥ śāstrasiddhaḥ kāyakleśaḥ; śaucaṃ śāstrīyakarmayogyatā; kṣāntiḥ paraiḥ pīḍyamānasyāpy avikṛtacittatā; ārjavaṃ pareṣu mano'nurūpaṃ bāhyaceṣṭāprakāśanam; jñānaṃ parāvaratattvayāthātmyajñānam; vijñānaṃ paratattvagatāsādhāraṇaviśeṣaviṣayaṃ jñānam; āstikyaṃ vaidikasya kṛtsnasya satyatāniścayaḥ prakṛṣṭaḥ; kenāpi hetunā cālayitum aśakya ityarthaḥ / bhagavān puruṣottamo vāsudevaḥ parabrahmaśabdābhideyo nirastanikhiladoṣagandhaḥ svābhāvikānavadhikātiśayajñānaśaktyādyasaṅkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇo nikhilavedavedāntavedyaḥ; sa eva nikhilajagadekakāraṇaṃ nikhilajagadādhārabhūtaḥ; nikhilasya sa eva
pravartayitā; tadārādhanabhūtaṃ ca vaidikaṃ kṛtsnaṃ karma; tais tair ārādhito dharmārthakāmamokṣākhyaṃ phalaṃ prayacchatīty asyārthasya satyatāniścaya āstikyam; "vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ", "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate ", "mayi sarvam idaṃ protam", "bhoktāraṃ yajñatapasāṃ ..... jñātvā māṃ śāntim ṛcchati", "mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyat kiñcid asti dhanañjaya", "yataḥ pravṛttir bhūtānāṃ yena sarvam idaṃ tatam / svakarmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ", "yo mām ajam anādiṃ ca vetti lokamaheśvaram" iti hy ucyate / tad etad brāhmaṇasya svabhāvajaṃ karma //
body.translated_text:
Tranquility (<s>śama</s>) is the restraint of the external senses. Self-restraint (<s>dama</s>) is the restraint of the internal organ. Austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is bodily mortification in the form of curtailment of enjoyment, as established by scripture. Purity (<s>śauca</s>) is fitness for the performance of scripturally enjoined duties. Forbearance (<s>kṣānti</s>) is having an undisturbed mind even when caused suffering by others. Uprightness (<s>ārjava</s>) is the manifestation of outward conduct that conforms to the mind, toward others. Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is the knowledge of the true nature of the higher and lower realities. Discernment (<s>vijñāna</s>) is the knowledge concerning the distinctive characteristics unique to the supreme reality. Faith (<s>āstikya</s>) is the firm and eminent conviction of the truth of everything Vedic; meaning: [such conviction] that cannot be shaken by any reason whatsoever. The Lord, the Supreme Person, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, is the one denoted by the word Supreme <s>Brahman</s>; He is devoid of even the slightest trace of all defects; He possesses innumerable hosts of auspicious qualities — knowledge, power, and the like — that are natural, unsurpassed, and of surpassing excellence; He is knowable through all the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāntas</s>. He alone is the sole cause of the entire universe;
He is the support of the entire universe; He alone is the impeller of everything; all Vedic action is of the nature of worship of Him; worshipped through those respective [actions], He bestows the fruits known as <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> — the firm conviction of the truth of this meaning is <s>āstikya</s> (faith). 'By all the <s>Vedas</s>, I alone am to be known'; 'I am the source of all; from Me everything proceeds'; 'All this is strung on Me'; 'The enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities... knowing Me, one attains peace'; 'There is nothing higher than Me, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>'; 'From whom the activity of beings [proceeds], by whom all this is pervaded — by worshipping Him through one's own duty, a person attains perfection'; 'He who knows Me as unborn and beginningless, the great Lord of the world' — thus it is stated. This is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s duty born of [his] innate nature. //

children.text:
śamaḥ bāhya-indriya-niyamanam; damaḥ antaḥkaraṇa-niyamanam; tapaḥ bhoga-niyamana-rūpaḥ śāstra-siddhaḥ kāya-kleśaḥ; śaucaṃ śāstrīya-karma-yogyatā; kṣāntiḥ paraiḥ pīḍyamānasya apy avikṛta-cittatā; ārjavaṃ pareṣu mano-'nurūpaṃ bāhya-ceṣṭā-prakāśanam; jñānaṃ para-avara-tattva-yāthātmya-jñānam; vijñānaṃ para-tattva-gata-asādhāraṇa-viśeṣa-viṣayaṃ jñānam; āstikyaṃ vaidikasya kṛtsnasya satyatā-niścayaḥ prakṛṣṭaḥ; kena api hetunā cālayitum aśakya ity-arthaḥ / bhagavān puruṣa-uttamo vāsudevaḥ para-brahma-śabda-abhideyo nirasta-nikhila-doṣa-gandhaḥ svābhāvika-anavadhika-atiśaya-jñāna-śakty-ādy-asaṅkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇo nikhila-veda-veda-anta-vedyaḥ; sa eva nikhila-jagad-eka-kāraṇaṃ nikhila-jagad-ādhāra-bhūtaḥ; nikhilasya sa eva
pravartayitā; tad-ārādhana-bhūtaṃ ca vaidikaṃ kṛtsnaṃ karma; tais tair ārādhito dharma-artha-kāma-mokṣa-ākhyaṃ phalaṃ prayacchati ity asya arthasya satyatā-niścaya āstikyam; "vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ", "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate ", "mayi sarvam idaṃ protam", "bhoktāraṃ yajña-tapasāṃ ..... jñātvā māṃ śāntim ṛcchati", "mattaḥ parataraṃ na anyat kiñcid asti dhanañjaya", "yataḥ pravṛttir bhūtānāṃ yena sarvam idaṃ tatam / sva-karmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ", "yo mām ajam anādiṃ ca vetti loka-mahā-īśvaram" iti hy ucyate / tad etad brāhmaṇasya sva-bhāva-jaṃ karma //
śairyaṃ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṃ yuddhe cāpy apalāyanam /
children.translated_text: Heroism, vigor, fortitude, skill, and also not fleeing from battle,

children.text: dānam īśvarabhāvaś ca kṣātraṃ karma svabhāvajam //
children.translated_text: generosity, and the disposition of a ruler — these are the <s>kṣatriya</s>'s duties, born of [his] innate nature. ||

children.text: śairyaṃ tejo dhṛtir dākṣyaṃ yuddhe ca apy apalāyanam /
dānam īśvara-bhāvaś ca kṣātraṃ karma sva-bhāva-jam //

body.text: śairyaṃ yuddhe nirbhayapraveśasāmarthyam, tejaḥ parair anabhibhavanīyatā, dhṛtiḥ ārabdhe karmaṇi vighnopanipāte 'pi tatsamāpanasāmarthyam, dākṣyaṃ sarvakriyānirvṛttisāmarthyam, yuddhe cāpy apalāyanam yuddhe cātmamaraṇaniścaye 'py anirvartanam; dānaṃ ātmīyasya dhanasya parasvatvāpādanaparyantas tyāgaḥ īśvarabhāvaḥ svavyatiriktasakalajananiyamanasāmarthyam; etat kṣatriyasya svabhāvajaṃ karma //
body.translated_text: Heroism (<s>śaurya</s>) is the capacity for fearless entry into battle. Vigor (<s>tejas</s>) is the incapacity to be overwhelmed by others. Fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>) is the capacity to complete an undertaking even when obstacles arise. Skill (<s>dākṣya</s>) is the capacity to accomplish all kinds of activities. Not fleeing from battle — not retreating even when the certainty of one's own death is present in battle. Generosity (<s>dāna</s>) is the giving away of one's own wealth to the point of making it another's property. The disposition of a ruler (<s>īśvarabhāva</s>) is the capacity to govern all people other than oneself. This is the <s>kṣatriya</s>'s duty born of [his] innate nature. //

children.text: śairyaṃ yuddhe nirbhaya-praveśa-sāmarthyam, tejaḥ parair anabhibhavanīyatā, dhṛtiḥ ārabdhe karmaṇi vighna-upanipāte 'pi tat-samāpana-sāmarthyam, dākṣyaṃ sarva-kriyā-nirvṛtti-sāmarthyam, yuddhe ca apy apalāyanam yuddhe cā atma-maraṇa-niścaye 'py anirvartanam; dānaṃ ātmīyasya dhanasya para-svatva-āpādana-paryantas tyāgaḥ īśvara-bhāvaḥ sva-vyatirikta-sakala-jana-niyamana-sāmarthyam; etat kṣatriyasya sva-bhāva-jaṃ karma //

body.text: kṛṣigorakṣyavāṇijyaṃ vaiśyaṃ karma svabhāvajam /
body.translated_text: Agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade — these are the <s>vaiśya</s>'s duties, born of [his] innate nature.

children.text: kṛṣi-gorakṣya-vāṇijyaṃ vaiśyaṃ karma sva-bhāva-jam /

body.text: kṛṣiḥ satyotpādanaṃ karṣaṇam / gorakṣyam paśupālanam ityarthaḥ / vāṇijyam dhanasañcayahetubhūtaṃ krayavikrayātmakaṃ karma / etad vaiśyasya svabhāvajaṃ karma //
body.translated_text: Agriculture (<s>kṛṣi</s>) is cultivation — the production of grain through ploughing. Cattle-rearing (<s>gorakṣya</s>) means the tending of livestock. Trade (<s>vāṇijya</s>) is the activity of buying and selling that serves as the means for the accumulation of wealth. This is the <s>vaiśya</s>'s duty born of [his] innate nature. //

children.text: kṛṣiḥ satya-utpādanaṃ karṣaṇam / gorakṣyam paśu-pālanam ity-arthaḥ / vāṇijyam dhana-sañcaya-hetu-bhūtaṃ kraya-vikraya-ātmakaṃ karma / etad vaiśyasya sva-bhāva-jaṃ karma //

body.text: paricaryātmakaṃ karma śūdrasyāpi svabhāvajam //
body.translated_text: Service is the <s>śūdra</s>'s duty, born of [his] innate nature. ||

children.text: paricaryā-ātmakaṃ karma śūdrasya api sva-bhāva-jam //

body.text: pūrvavarṇatrayaparicaryārūpaṃ śūdrasya svabhāvajaṃ karma / tad etac caturṇā varṇānāṃ vṛttibhis saha kartavyānāṃ śāstravihitānāṃ yajñādikarmaṇāṃ pradarśanārtham uktam / yajñādayo hi trayāṇāṃ varṇānāṃ sādhāraṇāḥ / śamādayo 'pi trayāṇāṃ varṇānāṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ sādhāraṇāḥ / brāhmaṇasya tu sattvodrekasya svābhāvikatvena śamadamādayaḥ sukhopādānā iti kṛtvā tasya śamādaya svabhāvajaṃ karmety uktam / kṣatriyavaiśyayos tu svato rajastamaḥpradhānatvena śamadamādayo duḥkhopādānā iti kṛtvā na tat karmety uktam / brāhmaṇasya vṛttir yājanādhyāpanapratigrahāḥ; kṣatriyasya janapadaparipālanam; vaiśyasya ca kṛṣyādayo yathoktāḥ; śūdrasya tu kartavyaṃ vṛttiś ca pūrvavarṇatrayaparicaryaiva //
body.translated_text: Service to the preceding three <s>varṇas</s> is the <s>śūdra</s>'s duty born of [his] innate nature. This has been stated as an illustration of the scripturally enjoined duties such as sacrifices and the like, together with the livelihoods, of the four <s>varṇas</s>. For sacrifices and the like are common to [all] three <s>varṇas</s>. Tranquility and the like are also common to the three <s>varṇas</s> when they seek liberation. However, since for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> the predominance of <s>sattva</s> is natural, tranquility, self-restraint, and the like are easy to adopt; therefore, tranquility and the like are stated as the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s duty born of innate nature. But for the <s>kṣatriya</s> and <s>vaiśya</s>, since <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> are naturally predominant, tranquility, self-restraint, and the like are adopted with difficulty; therefore they are not stated as their duty. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s livelihood consists of officiating at sacrifices, teaching, and accepting gifts. The <s>kṣatriya</s>'s is the protection of the people. The <s>vaiśya</s>'s consists of agriculture and the like as stated. For the <s>śūdra</s>, both the duty and the livelihood are service to the preceding three <s>varṇas</s> alone. //

children.text: pūrva-varṇa-traya-paricaryā-rūpaṃ śūdrasya sva-bhāva-jaṃ karma / tad etac caturṇā varṇānāṃ vṛttibhis saha kartavyānāṃ śāstra-vihitānāṃ yajña-ādi-karmaṇāṃ pradarśana-artham uktam / yajña-ādayo hi trayāṇāṃ varṇānāṃ sādhāraṇāḥ / śama-ādayo 'pi trayāṇāṃ varṇānāṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ sādhāraṇāḥ / brāhmaṇasya tu sattva-udrekasya svābhāvikatvena śama-dama-ādayaḥ sukha-upādānā iti kṛtvā tasya śama-ādaya sva-bhāva-jaṃ karma ity uktam / kṣatriya-vaiśyayos tu svato rajas-tamaḥ-pradhānatvena śama-dama-ādayo duḥkha-upādānā iti kṛtvā na tat karma ity uktam / brāhmaṇasya vṛttir yājana-adhyāpana-pratigrahāḥ; kṣatriyasya jana-pada-paripālanam; vaiśyasya ca kṛṣy-ādayo yathā-uktāḥ; śūdrasya tu kartavyaṃ vṛttiś ca pūrva-varṇa-traya-paricarya aiva //
sve sve karmaṇy abhiratas saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ /
children.translated_text: Devoted to his own respective duty, a person attains perfection.

children.text: svakarmaniratas siddhiṃ yathā vindati tac chṛṇu //
children.translated_text: How one who is devoted to his own duty attains perfection — hear that. ||

children.text: sve sve karmaṇy abhiratas saṃsiddhiṃ labhate naraḥ /
sva-karma-niratas siddhiṃ yathā vindati tac chṛṇu //

body.text: sve sve yathodite karmaṇy abhirato naraḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramapadaprāptiṃ labhate / svakarmanirato yathā siddhiṃ vindati paramapadaṃ prāpnoti, tathā śṛṇu //
body.translated_text: A person devoted to his own respective duty as described attains perfection — the attainment of the supreme abode. How one devoted to his own duty attains perfection — attains the supreme abode — hear that. //

children.text: sve sve yathā-udite karmaṇy abhirato naraḥ saṃsiddhiṃ parama-pada-prāptiṃ labhate / sva-karma-nirato yathā siddhiṃ vindati parama-padaṃ prāpnoti, tathā śṛṇu //
yataḥ pravṛttir bhūtānāṃ yena sarvam idaṃ tatam /
children.translated_text: From whom the activity of beings [proceeds], by whom all this is pervaded —

children.text: svakarmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ //
children.translated_text: by worshipping Him through one's own duty, a person attains perfection. ||

children.text: yataḥ pravṛttir bhūtānāṃ yena sarvam idaṃ tatam /
sva-karmaṇā tam abhyarcya siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ //

body.text: yato bhūtānām utpattyādikā pravṛttiḥ, yena ca sarvam idaṃ tatam, svakarmaṇā taṃ mām indrādyantarātmatayāvasthitam abhyarcya matprasādān matprāptirūpāṃ siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ / matta eva sarvam utpadyate, mayā ca sarvam idaṃ tatam iti pūrvam evoktam, "ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā / mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyat kiṃcid asti dhanañjaya", "mayā tatam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagad avyaktamūrtinā", "mayādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacarācaram", "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" ityādiṣu //
body.translated_text: From whom the activity of beings — such as origination and the like — proceeds, and by whom all this is pervaded — by worshipping Him, Me, who am established as the inner self of <s>Indra</s> and the others, through one's own duty, and by My grace, a person attains perfection in the form of attaining Me. That everything originates from Me alone and that all this is pervaded by Me has been stated earlier: 'I am the source and likewise the dissolution of the entire universe; there is nothing higher than Me, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>'; 'All this universe is pervaded by Me in unmanifest form'; 'Under My supervision, <s>Prakṛti</s> gives birth to the moving and unmoving'; 'I am the source of all; from Me everything proceeds' — and so on. //

children.text: yato bhūtānām utpatty-ādikā pravṛttiḥ, yena ca sarvam idaṃ tatam, sva-karmaṇā taṃ mām indra-ādy-antara-ātmataya āvasthitam abhyarcya mat-prasādān mat-prāpti-rūpāṃ siddhiṃ vindati mānavaḥ / matta eva sarvam utpadyate, mayā ca sarvam idaṃ tatam iti pūrvam eva uktam, "ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayas tathā / mattaḥ parataraṃ na anyat kiṃcid asti dhanañjaya", "mayā tatam idaṃ sarvaṃ jagad avyakta-mūrtinā", "maya ādhyakṣeṇa prakṛtiḥ sūyate sacara-acaram", "ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" ity-ādiṣu //

body.text: śreyān svadharmo viguṇaḥ paradharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt /
body.translated_text: One's own <s>dharma</s>, though defective, is better than another's <s>dharma</s> well-performed. |

children.text: śreyān sva-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣṭhitāt /

body.text: evaṃ tyaktakartṛtvādiko madārādhanarūpaḥ svadharmaḥ / svenaivopādātuṃ yogyo dharmaḥ; prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭena hi puruṣeṇendriyavyāpārarūpaḥ karmayogātmako dharmaḥ sukaro bhavati / ataḥ karmayogākhyaḥ svadharmo viguṇo 'pi paradharmāt -- indriyajayanipuṇapuruṣadharmāj jñānayogāt sakalendriyaniyamanarūpatayā sapramādāt kadācit svanuṣṭhitāc śreyān / tad evopapādayati --
body.translated_text: Thus, one's own <s>dharma</s> in the form of worship of Me, performed with the renunciation of agency and the like, is one's own <s>dharma</s> — the <s>dharma</s> fit to be undertaken by oneself alone. For a person associated with <s>Prakṛti</s>, the <s>dharma</s> in the form of <s>karmayoga</s>, consisting of the activity of the senses, is easy to perform. Therefore, one's own <s>dharma</s> called <s>karmayoga</s>, even though defective, is better than another's <s>dharma</s> — <s>jñānayoga</s>, which is the <s>dharma</s> of one who is skilled in conquering the senses — which, being in the form of the restraint of all the senses, is attended by heedlessness, [and] even if at times well-performed. He substantiates this very point:

children.text: evaṃ tyakta-kartṛtva-ādiko mad-ārādhana-rūpaḥ sva-dharmaḥ / svena eva upādātuṃ yogyo dharmaḥ; prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭena hi puruṣeṇa indriya-vyāpāra-rūpaḥ karma-yoga-ātmako dharmaḥ sukaro bhavati / ataḥ karma-yoga-ākhyaḥ sva-dharmo viguṇo 'pi para-dharmāt --- indriya-jaya-nipuṇa-puruṣa-dharmāj jñāna-yogāt sakala-indriya-niyamana-rūpatayā sa-pramādāt kadācit sv-anuṣṭhitāc śreyān / tad eva upapādayati ---

body.text: svabhāvaniyataṃ karma kurvan nāpnoti kilbiṣam //
body.translated_text: Performing action that is determined by [one's] innate nature, one incurs no sin. ||

children.text: sva-bhāva-niyataṃ karma kurvan nā apnoti kilbiṣam //

body.text: prakṛtisaṃsṛṣṭasya puruṣasya indriyavyāpārarūpatayā svabhāvata eva niyatatvāt karmaṇaḥ, karma kurvan kilbiṣaṃ saṃsāraṃ na prāpnoti; apramādatvāt karmaṇaḥ / jñānayogasya sakalendriyaniyamanasādhyatayā sapramādatvāt tanniṣṭhas tu pramādāt kilbiṣaṃ pratipadyetāpi //
body.translated_text: Since, for a person associated with <s>Prakṛti</s>, action is naturally determined by its being in the form of sense-activity, one who performs [such] action incurs no sin — no <s>saṃsāra</s>; because such action is free from heedlessness. But one who is established in <s>jñānayoga</s>, because it is achievable only by the restraint of all the senses and is therefore attended by heedlessness, might through heedlessness incur sin. //

children.text: prakṛti-saṃsṛṣṭasya puruṣasya indriya-vyāpāra-rūpatayā sva-bhāvata eva niyatatvāt karmaṇaḥ, karma kurvan kilbiṣaṃ saṃsāraṃ na prāpnoti; apramādatvāt karmaṇaḥ / jñāna-yogasya sakala-indriya-niyamana-sādhyatayā sa-pramādatvāt tan-niṣṭhas tu pramādāt kilbiṣaṃ pratipadyeta api //

body.text: ataḥ karmaniṣṭhaiva jyāyasīti tṛtīyādhyāyoktaṃ smārayati --
body.translated_text: He reminds [<s>Arjuna</s>] of what was stated in the third chapter — that devotion to action alone is superior:

children.text: ataḥ karma-niṣṭha aiva jyāyasi īti tṛtīya-adhyāya-uktaṃ smārayati ---
sahajaṃ karma kaunteya sadoṣam api na tyajet /
children.translated_text: One should not abandon action born of one's nature, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, even though it be defective;

children.text: sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnir ivāvṛtāḥ //
children.translated_text: for all undertakings are enveloped by defect, as fire by smoke. ||

children.text: saha-jaṃ karma kaunteya sa-doṣam api na tyajet /
sarva-ārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmena agnir ivā avṛtāḥ //

body.text: ataḥ sahajatvena sukaram apramādaṃ ca karma sadoṣaṃ saduḥkham api na tyajet; jñānayogayogyo 'pi karmayogam eva kurvītetyarthaḥ / sarvārambhāḥ, -- karmārambhāḥ jñānārambhāś ca hi doṣeṇa duḥkhena dhūmenāgnir ivāvṛtāḥ / iyāṃs tu viśeṣaḥ -- karmayogaḥ sukaro 'pramādaś ca, jñānayogas tadviparītaḥ iti //
body.translated_text: Therefore, one should not abandon action that, being innate, is easy and free from heedlessness, even though it be defective — even though it involves suffering. Even one who is qualified for <s>jñānayoga</s> should perform <s>karmayoga</s> alone — this is the meaning. All undertakings — undertakings of action and undertakings of knowledge — are enveloped by defect, by suffering, as fire by smoke. The distinction, however, is this: <s>karmayoga</s> is easy and free from heedlessness, while <s>jñānayoga</s> is the opposite of that. //

children.text: ataḥ sahajatvena sukaram apramādaṃ ca karma sa-doṣaṃ sa-duḥkham api na tyajet; jñāna-yoga-yogyo 'pi karma-yogam eva kurvīta ity-arthaḥ / sarva-ārambhāḥ, --- karma-ārambhāḥ jñāna-ārambhāś ca hi doṣeṇa duḥkhena dhūmena agnir ivā avṛtāḥ / iyāṃs tu viśeṣaḥ --- karma-yogaḥ sukaro 'pramādaś ca, jñāna-yogas tad-viparītaḥ iti //
asaktabuddhis sarvatra jitātmā vigataspṛhaḥ /
children.translated_text: With intellect unattached everywhere, with self conquered, free from longing,

children.text: naiṣkarmyasiddhiṃ paramāṃ saṃnyāsenādhigacchati //
children.translated_text: through renunciation one attains the supreme perfection of freedom from action. ||

children.text: asakta-buddhis sarvatra jita-ātmā vigata-spṛhaḥ /
naiṣkarmya-siddhiṃ paramāṃ saṃnyāsena adhigacchati //

body.text: sarvatra phalādiṣu asaktabuddhiḥ, jitātmā -- jitamanāḥ, paramapuruṣakartṛtvānusaṃdhānenātmakartṛtve vigataspṛhaḥ, evaṃ tyāgād ananyatvena nirṇītena saṃnyāsena yuktaḥ karma kurvan paramāṃ naiṣkarmyasiddhim adhigacchati -- paramāṃ dhyānaniṣṭhāṃ jñānayogasyāpi phalabhūtam adhigacchatītyarthaḥ / vakṣyamāṇadhyānayogāvāptiṃ sarvendriyakarmoparatirūpām adhigacchati //
body.translated_text: With intellect unattached everywhere — to fruits and the like; with self conquered — with mind conquered; free from longing — with longing for one's own agency removed through the contemplation of agency in the Supreme Person; thus endowed with renunciation that has been determined to be identical [with <s>tyāga</s>], performing action, one attains the supreme perfection of freedom from action — the supreme establishment in contemplation (<s>dhyāna-niṣṭhā</s>), which is the fruit even of <s>jñānayoga</s> — this is the meaning. One attains the cessation of all sense-activity, in the form of the attainment of the <s>dhyānayoga</s> that will be described. //

children.text: sarvatra phala-ādiṣu asakta-buddhiḥ, jita-ātmā --- jita-manāḥ, parama-puruṣa-kartṛtva-anusaṃdhānenā atma-kartṛtve vigata-spṛhaḥ, evaṃ tyāgād ananyatvena nirṇītena saṃnyāsena yuktaḥ karma kurvan paramāṃ naiṣkarmya-siddhim adhigacchati --- paramāṃ dhyāna-niṣṭhāṃ jñāna-yogasya api phala-bhūtam adhigacchati ity-arthaḥ / vakṣyamāṇa-dhyāna-yoga-avāptiṃ sarva-indriya-karma-uparati-rūpām adhigacchati //
siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathāpnoti nibodha me /
children.translated_text: How one who has attained perfection then attains <s>Brahman</s> — learn that from Me,

children.text: samāsenaiva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā //
children.translated_text: in brief, O son of <s>Kuntī</s> — [it is] the supreme culmination of knowledge. ||

children.text: siddhiṃ prāpto yathā brahma tathā āpnoti nibodha me /
samāsena eva kaunteya niṣṭhā jñānasya yā parā //

body.text: siddhiṃ prāptaḥ āprayāṇādaharaharanuṣṭhīyamānakarmayoganiṣpādyadhyānasidddhiṃ prāptaḥ, yathā yena prakāreṇa vartamāno brahma prāpnoti, tathā samāsena me nibodha / tad eva brahma viśeṣyate niṣṭhā jñānasya yā pareti / jñānasya dhyānātmakasya yā parā niṣṭhā -- paramaprāpyam ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: One who has attained perfection — who has attained the perfection in the form of contemplation (<s>dhyāna</s>) brought about by <s>karmayoga</s> performed daily until the time of departure — how, by what mode of being, he attains <s>Brahman</s> — learn that from Me in brief. That very <s>Brahman</s> is further specified: 'the supreme culmination of knowledge' — the supreme object to be attained by knowledge in the form of contemplation — this is the meaning. //

children.text: siddhiṃ prāptaḥ ā-prayāṇād-ahar-ahar-anuṣṭhīyamāna-karma-yoga-niṣpādya-dhyāna-sidddhiṃ prāptaḥ, yathā yena prakāreṇa vartamāno brahma prāpnoti, tathā samāsena me nibodha / tad eva brahma viśeṣyate niṣṭhā jñānasya yā para īti / jñānasya dhyāna-ātmakasya yā parā niṣṭhā --- parama-prāpyam ity-arthaḥ //
buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyātmānaṃ niyamya ca /
children.translated_text: Endowed with a purified intellect, restraining the self with firmness,

children.text: śabdādīn viṣayāṃs tyaktvā rāgadveṣau vyudasya ca //
children.translated_text: having abandoned sound and other sense-objects, and having cast aside attachment and aversion,

children.text: buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto dhṛtyā ātmānaṃ niyamya ca /
śabda-ādīn viṣayāṃs tyaktvā rāga-dveṣau vyudasya ca //
viviktasevī laghvāśī yatavākkāyamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: resorting to solitude, eating lightly, with speech, body, and mind controlled,

children.text: dhyānayogaparo nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ //
children.translated_text: ever devoted to the <s>yoga</s> of meditation, having resorted to dispassion,

children.text: vivikta-sevī laghv-āśī yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ /
dhyāna-yoga-paro nityaṃ vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ //
ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham /
children.translated_text: having relinquished egoism, force, arrogance, desire, anger, and possessiveness,

children.text: vimucya nirmamaś śānto brahmabhūyāya kalpate //
children.translated_text: free from the sense of 'mine,' serene — one becomes fit for becoming <s>Brahman</s>. ||

children.text: ahaṅ-kāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham /
vimucya nirmamaś śānto brahma-bhūyāya kalpate //

body.text:
