buddhyā viśuddhayā yathāvasthitātmatattvaviṣayayā yuktaḥ, dhṛtyā ātmānaṃ niyamya ca viṣayavimukhīkaraṇena yogayogyaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā, śabdādīn viṣayān tyaktvā -- asannihitān kṛtvā, tannimittau ca rāgadveṣau vyudasya, viviktasevī -- sarvair dhyānavirodhibhir vivikte deśe vartamānaḥ, laghvāśī -- atyaśanānaśanarahitaḥ, yatavākkāyamānasaḥ -- dhyānābhimukhīkṛtakāyavāṅmanovṛttiḥ, dhyānayogaparo nityam -- evaṃbhūtas san ā prāyāṇād aharahardhyānayogaparaḥ, vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ -- dhyeyatattvavyatiriktaviṣayadoṣāvamarśena tatra tatra virāgatāṃ vardhayan, ahaṃkāram -- anātmani ātmābhimānaṃ, balaṃ -- tadvṛddhihetubhūtavāsanabalaṃ, tannimittaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigrahaṃ vimucya, nirmamaḥ sarveṣv anātmīyeṣv
ātmīyabuddhirahitaḥ, śāntaḥ -- ātmānubhavaikasukhaḥ, evaṃbhūto dhyānayogaṃ kurvan brahmabhūyāya kalpate -- sarvabandhavinirmukto yathāvasthitam ātmānam anubhavatītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Endowed with pure understanding — understanding whose object is the true nature of the self as it really is — and restraining the self with firmness by turning it away from sense-objects, thereby making the mind fit for <s>yoga</s>; having abandoned sense-objects such as sound and the like — having removed them from proximity; and having cast aside attachment and aversion caused by them; dwelling in solitude — staying in a place free from all impediments to meditation; eating lightly — free from both excessive eating and fasting; with speech, body, and mind controlled — with the activities of body, speech, and mind directed toward meditation; constantly devoted to the <s>yoga</s> of meditation — being of such a nature, devoted to the <s>yoga</s> of meditation day by day until death; having resorted to dispassion — increasing detachment toward all objects other than the reality to be meditated upon by contemplating their defects; having released ego — the false identification of the self with the non-self; strength (<s>bala</s>) — the force of the latent impressions that cause the growth of [ego]; and the pride, desire, anger, and possessiveness caused by those [impressions]; free from the sense of 'mine' — devoid of the notion of ownership regarding all things that are not the self; peaceful — whose sole happiness is the experience of the self — one who is of such a nature, practicing the <s>yoga</s> of meditation, becomes fit for becoming <s>Brahman</s> — meaning: being freed from all bondage, he experiences the self as it truly is. //

children.text:
buddhyā viśuddhayā yathā-avasthita-ātma-tattva-viṣayayā yuktaḥ, dhṛtyā ātmānaṃ niyamya ca viṣaya-vimukhīkaraṇena yoga-yogyaṃ manaḥ kṛtvā, śabda-ādīn viṣayān tyaktvā --- asannihitān kṛtvā, tan-nimittau ca rāga-dveṣau vyudasya, vivikta-sevī --- sarvair dhyāna-virodhibhir vivikte deśe vartamānaḥ, laghv-āśī --- atyaśana-anaśana-rahitaḥ, yata-vāk-kāya-mānasaḥ --- dhyāna-abhimukhīkṛta-kāya-vāṅ-mano-vṛttiḥ, dhyāna-yoga-paro nityam --- evaṃ-bhūtas san ā prāyāṇād ahar-ahar-dhyāna-yoga-paraḥ, vairāgyaṃ samupāśritaḥ --- dhyeya-tattva-vyatirikta-viṣaya-doṣa-avamarśena tatra tatra virāgatāṃ vardhayan, ahaṃ-kāram --- anātmani ātma-abhimānaṃ, balaṃ --- tad-vṛddhi-hetu-bhūta-vāsana-balaṃ, tan-nimittaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigrahaṃ vimucya, nirmamaḥ sarveṣv anātmīyeṣv
ātmīya-buddhi-rahitaḥ, śāntaḥ --- ātma-anubhava-eka-sukhaḥ, evaṃ-bhūto dhyāna-yogaṃ kurvan brahma-bhūyāya kalpate --- sarva-bandha-vinirmukto yathā-avasthitam ātmānam anubhavati ity-arthaḥ //
brahmabhūtaḥ prasannātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati /
children.translated_text: 'Having become <s>Brahman</s>, serene in self, he neither grieves nor desires.'

children.text: samas sarveṣu bhūteṣu madbhaktiṃ labhate parām //
children.translated_text: 'Equal toward all beings, he attains supreme devotion to Me.' ||

children.text: brahma-bhūtaḥ prasanna-ātmā na śocati na kāṅkṣati /
samas sarveṣu bhūteṣu mad-bhaktiṃ labhate parām //

body.text: brahmabhūtaḥ -- āvirbhūtāparicchinnajñānaikākāramaccheṣataikasvabhāvātmasvarūpaḥ, "itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām" iti hi svaśeṣatoktā / prasannātmā -- kleśakarmādibhir akaluṣasvarūpo madvyatiriktaṃ na kaṃcana bhūtaviśeṣaṃ prati śocati; na kiṃcana kāṅkṣati; api tu madvyatirikteṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu anādaraṇīyatāyāṃ samo nikhilaṃ vastujātaṃ tṛṇavan manyamāno madbhaktiṃ labhate parām mayi sarveśvare nikhilajagadudbhavasthitipralayalīle nirastasamastaheyagandhe 'navadhikātiśayāsaṃkhyeyakalyāṇaguṇagaṇaikatāne lāvaṇyāmṛtasāgare śrīmati puṇḍarīkanayane svasvāmini atyarthapriyānubhavarūpāṃ parāṃ bhaktiṃ labhate //
body.translated_text: Having become <s>Brahman</s> — his essential nature as the self has manifested: of the single form of unlimited knowledge, whose sole essential nature is being a dependent (<s>śeṣa</s>) of Me; for it was said 'know My higher <s>Prakṛti</s> — which has become the individual souls' — that its nature as His dependent was stated. Serene in self — whose essential nature is free from impurities of <s>kleśa</s>, <s>karma</s>, and the like — he neither grieves regarding any particular being other than Me, nor desires anything at all. Rather, being equal toward all beings other than Me in their being unworthy of regard — considering the entire class of things as [worthless as] grass — he attains supreme devotion to Me: toward Me, the Lord of all, whose sport is the origination, sustenance, and dissolution of the entire universe, in whom every trace of everything undesirable is negated, who is a single thread of innumerable and immeasurable auspicious qualities, an ocean of the nectar of beauty, the glorious one with lotus eyes, his own Lord — he attains supreme devotion in the form of the experience of exceedingly beloved [communion]. //

children.text: brahma-bhūtaḥ --- āvirbhūta-aparicchinna-jñāna-eka-ākāra-mac-cheṣatā-eka-sva-bhāva-ātma-sva-rūpaḥ, "itas tv anyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām" iti hi sva-śeṣata ūktā / prasanna-ātmā --- kleśa-karma-ādibhir akaluṣa-sva-rūpo mad-vyatiriktaṃ na kaṃcana bhūta-viśeṣaṃ prati śocati; na kiṃcana kāṅkṣati; api tu mad-vyatirikteṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu anādaraṇīyatāyāṃ samo nikhilaṃ vastu-jātaṃ tṛṇavan manyamāno mad-bhaktiṃ labhate parām mayi sarva-īśvare nikhila-jagad-udbhava-sthiti-pralaya-līle nirasta-samasta-heya-gandhe 'navadhika-atiśaya-asaṃkhyeya-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-eka-tāne lāvaṇya-amṛta-sāgare śrīmati puṇḍarīka-nayane sva-svāmini atyartha-priya-anubhava-rūpāṃ parāṃ bhaktiṃ labhate //

body.text: tatphalam āha --
body.translated_text: He states the fruit of that —

children.text: tat-phalam āha ---
bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś cāsmi tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Through devotion he comes to know Me — how great I am and who I am, in truth.'

children.text: tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tadanantaram //
children.translated_text: 'Then, having known Me in truth, he enters [into Me] immediately thereafter.' ||

children.text: bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaś ca asmi tattvataḥ /
tato māṃ tattvato jñātvā viśate tad-anantaram //

body.text: svarūpataḥ svabhāvataś ca yo 'ham; guṇato vibhūtito 'pi yāvāṃś cāham, taṃ mām evaṃrūpayā bhaktyā tattvato 'bhijānāti; māṃ tattvato jñātvā tadanantaram -- tattvajñānānantaraṃ tataḥ bhaktitaḥ māṃ viśate praviśati / tattvatas svarūpasvabhāvaguṇavibhūtidarśanottarakālabhāvinyā anavadhikātiśayabhaktyā māṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ / atra tata iti prāptihetutayā, nirdiṣṭā bhaktir evābhidhīyate; "bhaktyā tv ananyayā śakyaḥ" iti tasya eva tattvataḥ praveśahetutvābhidhānāt //
body.translated_text: Who I am in terms of essential nature and characteristics, and how great I am in terms of qualities and manifestations — that Me he comes to know in truth through devotion of such a form. Having known Me in truth, immediately thereafter — immediately after that true knowledge — through devotion, he enters into Me. The meaning is: through devotion of immeasurable and unsurpassable intensity that arises after the realization of [My] true essential nature, characteristics, qualities, and manifestations — he attains Me. Here, the word 'then' (<s>tataḥ</s>) refers to devotion itself as the cause of attainment; for it was stated that [devotion] alone is the cause of entering in truth: 'By exclusive devotion alone can [I] be [known].' //

children.text: sva-rūpataḥ sva-bhāvataś ca yo 'ham; guṇato vibhūtito 'pi yāvāṃś ca aham, taṃ mām evaṃ-rūpayā bhaktyā tattvato 'bhijānāti; māṃ tattvato jñātvā tad-anantaram --- tattva-jñāna-anantaraṃ tataḥ bhaktitaḥ māṃ viśate praviśati / tattvatas sva-rūpa-sva-bhāva-guṇa-vibhūti-darśana-uttara-kāla-bhāvinyā anavadhika-atiśaya-bhaktyā māṃ prāpnoti ity-arthaḥ / atra tata iti prāpti-hetutayā, nirdiṣṭā bhaktir eva abhidhīyate; "bhaktyā tv ananyayā śakyaḥ" iti tasya eva tattvataḥ praveśa-hetutva-abhidhānāt //

body.text: evaṃ varṇāśramocitanityanaimittikakarmaṇāṃ parityaktaphalādikānāṃ paramapuruṣārādhanarūpeṇānuṣṭhitānāṃ vipāka uktaḥ / idānīṃ kāmyānām api karmaṇām uktenaiva prakāreṇānuṣṭhitānāṃ sa eva vipāka ity āha --
body.translated_text: Thus, the ripening of obligatory and occasional actions appropriate to one's <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, performed as worship of the Supreme Person with abandonment of their fruits and the like, has been stated. Now He says that even desire-motivated actions, when performed in the very same manner, yield the same result —

children.text: evaṃ varṇa-āśrama-ucita-nitya-naimittika-karmaṇāṃ parityakta-phala-ādikānāṃ parama-puruṣa-ārādhana-rūpeṇa anuṣṭhitānāṃ vipāka uktaḥ / idānīṃ kāmyānām api karmaṇām uktena eva prakāreṇa anuṣṭhitānāṃ sa eva vipāka ity āha ---
sarvakarmāṇy api sadā kurvāṇo madvyapāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Even while always performing all actions, one who takes refuge in Me'

children.text: matprasādād avāpnoti śāśvataṃ padam avyayam //
children.translated_text: 'attains, by My grace, the eternal, imperishable abode.' ||

children.text: sarva-karmāṇy api sadā kurvāṇo mad-vyapāśrayaḥ /
mat-prasādād avāpnoti śāśvataṃ padam avyayam //

body.text: na kevalaṃ nityanaimittikāni karmāṇi, api tu sarvāṇi kāmyāny api karmāṇi, madvyāśrayaḥ mayi saṃnyastakartṛtvādikaḥ kurvāṇo matprasādāc chāśvataṃ padam avyayam avikalaṃ prāpnoti / padyate gamyata iti padam; māṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Not only the obligatory and occasional actions, but all actions — even the desire-motivated ones — when performed by one who takes refuge in Me, having surrendered agency and the like unto Me, he attains by My grace the eternal, imperishable — undiminished — abode. 'That which is reached' is the abode (<s>pada</s>); the meaning is: he attains Me. //

children.text: na kevalaṃ nitya-naimittikāni karmāṇi, api tu sarvāṇi kāmyāny api karmāṇi, mad-vyāśrayaḥ mayi saṃnyasta-kartṛtva-ādikaḥ kurvāṇo mat-prasādāc chāśvataṃ padam avyayam avikalaṃ prāpnoti / padyate gamyata iti padam; māṃ prāpnoti ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: yasmād evam, tasmāt --
body.translated_text: Since this is so, therefore —

children.text: yasmād evam, tasmāt ---
cetasā sarvakarmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Surrendering all actions to Me with [your] mind, devoted to Me as the supreme [goal],'

children.text: buddhiyogam upāśritya maccittas satataṃ bhava //
children.translated_text: 'having resorted to the <s>yoga</s> of understanding, be constantly minded on Me.' ||

children.text: cetasā sarva-karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya mat-paraḥ /
buddhi-yogam upāśritya mac-cittas satataṃ bhava //

body.text: cetasā - ātmano madīyatvamanniyāmyatvabuddhyā / uktaṃ hi, "mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasyādhyātmacetasā" iti / sarvakarmāṇi sakartṛkāṇi sārādhyāni mayi saṃnyasya, matparaḥ -- aham eva phalatayā prāpya ity anusaṃdhānaḥ, karmāṇi kurvan imam eva buddhiyogam upāśritya satataṃ maccitto bhava //
body.translated_text: With the mind (<s>cetasā</s>) — with the understanding that one belongs to Me and is governed by Me. For it was said: 'Surrendering all actions to Me with the mind directed toward the self.' Surrender all actions together with their agent and their object of worship unto Me, being devoted to Me as the supreme [goal] — with the conviction that 'I alone am to be attained as the fruit.' While performing actions, having resorted to this very <s>yoga</s> of understanding, be constantly minded on Me. //

children.text: cetasā -- ātmano madīyatva-man-niyāmyatva-buddhyā / uktaṃ hi, "mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya adhyātma-cetasā" iti / sarva-karmāṇi sa-kartṛkāṇi sa-ārādhyāni mayi saṃnyasya, mat-paraḥ --- aham eva phalatayā prāpya ity anusaṃdhānaḥ, karmāṇi kurvan imam eva buddhi-yogam upāśritya satataṃ mac-citto bhava //
maccittaḥ sarvadurgāṇi matprasādāt tariṣyasi /
children.translated_text: 'With mind fixed on Me, you shall cross over all difficulties by My grace.'

children.text: atha cet tvam ahaṃkārān na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi //
children.translated_text: 'But if, out of ego, you will not listen, you shall perish.' ||

children.text: mac-cittaḥ sarva-durgāṇi mat-prasādāt tariṣyasi /
atha cet tvam ahaṃ-kārān na śroṣyasi vinaṅkṣyasi //

body.text: evaṃ maccittaḥ sarvakarmāṇi kurvan sarvāṇi sāṃsārikāṇi durgāṇi matprasādād eva tariṣyasi / atha tvam ahaṃkārād aham eva kṛtyākṛtyaviṣayaṃ sarvaṃ jānāmīti bhāvān maduktaṃ na śroṣyasi cet, vinaṅkṣyasi -- vinaṣṭo bhaviṣyasi / na hi kaścin madvyatiriktaḥ kṛtsnasya prāṇijātasya kṛtyākṛtyayor jñātā praśāsitā vāsti //
body.translated_text: Thus, with your mind fixed on Me, performing all actions, you shall cross over all the difficulties of <s>saṃsāra</s> by My grace alone. But if you, out of ego — thinking 'I myself know everything about what is to be done and what is not to be done' — will not listen to what I have said, you shall perish — you shall be destroyed. For there is no one other than Me who knows and governs what is to be done and what is not to be done for the entire class of living beings. //

children.text: evaṃ mac-cittaḥ sarva-karmāṇi kurvan sarvāṇi sāṃsārikāṇi durgāṇi mat-prasādād eva tariṣyasi / atha tvam ahaṃ-kārād aham eva kṛtya-akṛtya-viṣayaṃ sarvaṃ jānāmi iti bhāvān mad-uktaṃ na śroṣyasi cet, vinaṅkṣyasi --- vinaṣṭo bhaviṣyasi / na hi kaścin mad-vyatiriktaḥ kṛtsnasya prāṇi-jātasya kṛtya-akṛtyayor jñātā praśāsitā va āsti //
yady ahaṅkāram āśritya na yotsya iti manyase /
children.translated_text: 'If, resorting to ego, you think "I shall not fight,"'

children.text: mithyaiṣa vyavasāyas te prakṛtis tvāṃ niyokṣyati //
children.translated_text: 'this resolve of yours is vain — [your own] nature will compel you.' ||

children.text: yady ahaṅ-kāram āśritya na yotsya iti manyase /
mithya aiṣa vyavasāyas te prakṛtis tvāṃ niyokṣyati //

body.text: yadi ahaṃkāram ātmani hitāhitajñāne svātantryābhimānam āśritya manniyogam anādṛtya na yotsya iti manyase, eṣa te svātantryavyavasāyo mithyā bhaviṣyati; yataḥ prakṛtis tvāṃ yuddhe niyokṣyati matsvātantryodvignaṃ tvām ajñaṃ prakṛtir niyokṣati //
body.translated_text: If, resorting to ego — the claim of independence in knowing what is beneficial and harmful for yourself — and disregarding My command, you think 'I shall not fight,' this resolve of independence of yours will be in vain. Because [your own] nature will compel you to fight — your own nature will compel you, who are ignorant and unsettled by [the claim of] independence from Me. //

children.text: yadi ahaṃ-kāram ātmani hita-ahita-jñāne svātantrya-abhimānam āśritya man-niyogam anādṛtya na yotsya iti manyase, eṣa te svātantrya-vyavasāyo mithyā bhaviṣyati; yataḥ prakṛtis tvāṃ yuddhe niyokṣyati mat-svātantrya-udvignaṃ tvām ajñaṃ prakṛtir niyokṣati //

body.text: tad upapādayati --
body.translated_text: He explains this —

children.text: tad upapādayati ---
svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: 'Bound by your own action, born of your own nature, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>,'

children.text: kartuṃ necchasi yan mohāt kariṣyasy avaśo 'pi tat //
children.translated_text: 'what you do not wish to do out of delusion, you shall do even against your will.' ||

children.text: sva-bhāva-jena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā /
kartuṃ na icchasi yan mohāt kariṣyasy avaśo 'pi tat //

body.text: svabhāvajaṃ hi kṣatriyasya karma śauryam / svabhāvajena śauryākhyena svena karmaṇā nibaddhaḥ, tad evāvaśaḥ, parair dharṣaṇam asahamānas tvam eva tad yuddhaṃ kariṣyasi, yad idānīṃ mohād ajñānāt kartuṃ necchasi //
body.translated_text: For the action born of one's nature for a <s>kṣatriya</s> is valor. Bound by your own action called valor, which is born of your nature, you yourself, unable to endure being overpowered by others, will helplessly perform that very battle which you now, out of delusion — out of ignorance — do not wish to perform. //

children.text: sva-bhāva-jaṃ hi kṣatriyasya karma śauryam / sva-bhāva-jena śaurya-ākhyena svena karmaṇā nibaddhaḥ, tad eva avaśaḥ, parair dharṣaṇam a-sahamānas tvam eva tad yuddhaṃ kariṣyasi, yad idānīṃ mohād ajñānāt kartuṃ na icchasi //

body.text: sarvaṃ hi bhūtajātaṃ sarveśvareṇa mayā pūrvakarmānuguṇyena prakṛtyanuvartane niyamitam; tac chṛṇu /
body.translated_text: For the entire class of beings is governed by Me, the Lord of all, in conformity with prior <s>karma</s>, in following <s>Prakṛti</s>. Hear this:

children.text: sarvaṃ hi bhūta-jātaṃ sarva-īśvareṇa mayā pūrva-karma-anuguṇyena prakṛty-anuvartane niyamitam; tac chṛṇu /
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: 'The Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings, O <s>Arjuna</s>,'

children.text: bhrāmayan sarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā //
children.translated_text: 'causing all beings, mounted on a machine, to revolve by [His] <s>māyā</s>.' ||

children.text: īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati /
bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantra-ārūḍhāni māyayā //

body.text: īśvaraḥ sarvaniyamanaśīlo vāsudevaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe sakalapravṛttimūlajñānodayapradeśe tiṣṭhati / kathaṃ kiṃ kurvaṃs tiṣṭhati ? yantrārūḍhāni sarvabhūtāni māyayā bhrāmayan / svenaiva nirmitaṃ dehendriyāvasthaṃ prakṛtyākhyaṃ yantram ārūḍhāni sarvabhūtāni svakīyayā sattvādiguṇamayyā māyayā guṇānuguṇaṃ pravartayaṃs tiṣṭhatītyarthaḥ / pūrvam apy etad uktam, "sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca" iti; "mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" iti ca / "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan" ityādikā śrutiś ca //
body.translated_text: The Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) — <s>Vāsudeva</s>, whose nature is to govern all — dwells in the heart-region of all beings, in the region where knowledge arises that is the root of all activity. How, and doing what, does He dwell? Causing all beings, mounted on a machine, to revolve by [His] <s>māyā</s>. All beings, mounted on the machine called <s>Prakṛti</s> — the configuration of body and senses created by Him — He sets in motion by His own <s>māyā</s>, which consists of the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the others — in accordance with their <s>guṇas</s>; thus He dwells — this is the meaning. This too was stated earlier: 'I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me come memory, knowledge, and their removal,' and 'from Me everything proceeds.' And the <s>śruti</s>: 'He who dwells in the self,' and so on. //

children.text: īśvaraḥ sarva-niyamana-śīlo vāsudevaḥ sarva-bhūtānāṃ hṛd-deśe sakala-pravṛtti-mūla-jñāna-udaya-pradeśe tiṣṭhati / kathaṃ kiṃ kurvaṃs tiṣṭhati ? yantra-ārūḍhāni sarva-bhūtāni māyayā bhrāmayan / svena eva nirmitaṃ deha-indriya-avasthaṃ prakṛty-ākhyaṃ yantram ārūḍhāni sarva-bhūtāni svakīyayā sattva-ādi-guṇa-mayyā māyayā guṇa-anuguṇaṃ pravartayaṃs tiṣṭhati ity-arthaḥ / pūrvam apy etad uktam, "sarvasya ca ahaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtir jñānam apohanaṃ ca" iti; "mattas sarvaṃ pravartate" iti ca / "ya ātmani tiṣṭhan" ity-ādikā śrutiś ca //

body.text: etan māyānivṛttihetum āha --
body.translated_text: He states the means for the cessation of this <s>māyā</s> —

children.text: etan māyā-nivṛtti-hetum āha ---
tam eva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhārata /
children.translated_text: 'Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, O <s>Bhārata</s>.'

children.text: tatprasādāt parāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam //
children.translated_text: 'By His grace, you shall attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.' ||

children.text: tam eva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarva-bhāvena bhārata /
tat-prasādāt parāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam //

body.text:
yasmād evam, tasmāt tam eva sarvasya praśāsitāram, āśritavātsalyena tvatsārathye 'vasthitam, "itthaṃ kuru " iti ca śāsitāraṃ sarvabhāvena sarvātmanā śaraṇaṃ gaccha / sarvātmanānuvartasva / anyathāpi tanmāyāpreritenājñena tvayā yuddhādikaraṇam avarjanīyam / tathā sati naṣṭo bhaviṣyasi / atas taduktaprakāreṇa yuddhādikaṃ kurv ityarthaḥ / evaṃ kurvāṇas tatprasādāt parāṃ śāntiṃ sarvakarmabandhopaśamaṃ śāśvataṃ ca sthānam prāpsyasi / yad abhidhīyate śrutiśataiḥ, "tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ, "te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacante yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ", "yatra ṛṣayaḥ prathamajā ye purāṇāḥ", "pareṇa nākaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyām", "yo 'syādhyakṣaḥ parame vyoman", "atha yad ataḥ paro divo jyotir dīpyate", "so 'dhvanaḥ
pāram āpnoti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam" ityādibhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Since this is so, therefore — in Him alone, the governor of all, who out of affection for those who have taken refuge [in Him] is stationed in the role of your charioteer, and who commands you 'do thus' — take refuge with your whole being, with your entire self. Follow Him in every way. Even otherwise, the performance of battle and the like is unavoidable for you, who are ignorant and impelled by His <s>māyā</s>. In that case, you will be destroyed. Therefore, perform the battle and the like in the manner instructed by Him — this is the meaning. Thus doing, by His grace you shall attain supreme peace — the cessation of all bondage of <s>karma</s> — and the eternal abode. That which is spoken of in hundreds of <s>śruti</s> passages: 'The wise ones always behold that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,' 'They of great glory attain the heaven where the ancient <s>Sādhyas</s> and gods dwell,' 'Where the sages are, the first-born, the ancient ones,' 'The heaven deposited beyond, in the cave,' 'He who is its overseer in the supreme space,' 'Now that light which shines beyond this sky,' 'He reaches the end of the road — that is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,' and the like. //

children.text:
yasmād evam, tasmāt tam eva sarvasya praśāsitāram, āśrita-vātsalyena tvat-sārathye 'vasthitam, "itthaṃ kuru " iti ca śāsitāraṃ sarva-bhāvena sarva-ātmanā śaraṇaṃ gaccha / sarva-ātmana ānuvartasva / anyatha āpi tan-māyā-preritena ajñena tvayā yuddha-ādi-karaṇam avarjanīyam / tathā sati naṣṭo bhaviṣyasi / atas tad-ukta-prakāreṇa yuddha-ādikaṃ kurv ity-arthaḥ / evaṃ kurvāṇas tat-prasādāt parāṃ śāntiṃ sarva-karma-bandha-upaśamaṃ śāśvataṃ ca sthānam prāpsyasi / yad abhidhīyate śruti-śataiḥ, "tad-viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ, "te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacante yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ", "yatra ṛṣayaḥ prathama-jā ye purāṇāḥ", "pareṇa nākaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyām", "yo 'sya adhyakṣaḥ parame vyoman", "atha yad ataḥ paro divo jyotir dīpyate", "so 'dhvanaḥ
pāram āpnoti tad-viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam" ity-ādibhiḥ //
iti te jñānam ākhyātaṃ guhyād guhyataraṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: 'Thus has knowledge been declared to you by Me — more secret than all secrets.'

children.text: vimṛśyaitad aśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru //
children.translated_text: 'Reflecting on this fully, do as you wish.' ||

children.text: iti te jñānam ākhyātaṃ guhyād guhyataraṃ mayā /
vimṛśya etad aśeṣeṇa yatha īcchasi tathā kuru //

body.text: iti -- evaṃ te mumukṣubhir adhigantavyaṃ jñānaṃ sarvasmād guhyād guhyataraṃ karmayogaviṣayaṃ jñānayogaviṣayaṃ bhaktiyogaviṣayaṃ ca sarvam ākhyātam / etadaśeṣeṇa vimṛśya svādhikārānurūpaṃ yathecchasi, tathā kuru karmayogaṃ jñānayogaṃ bhaktiyogaṃ vā yatheṣṭam ātiṣṭhetyarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus — in this manner — all the knowledge to be understood by seekers of liberation, more secret than all secrets — concerning <s>karmayoga</s>, concerning <s>jñānayoga</s>, and concerning <s>bhaktiyoga</s> — has been declared to you by Me. Having reflected on all of this fully, do as you wish in accordance with your own qualification — meaning: adopt <s>karmayoga</s>, <s>jñānayoga</s>, or <s>bhaktiyoga</s> as you wish. //

children.text: iti --- evaṃ te mumukṣubhir adhigantavyaṃ jñānaṃ sarvasmād guhyād guhyataraṃ karma-yoga-viṣayaṃ jñāna-yoga-viṣayaṃ bhakti-yoga-viṣayaṃ ca sarvam ākhyātam / etad-aśeṣeṇa vimṛśya sva-adhikāra-anurūpaṃ yatha īcchasi, tathā kuru karma-yogaṃ jñāna-yogaṃ bhakti-yogaṃ vā yatha īṣṭam ātiṣṭha ity-arthaḥ //
sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Hear again My supreme word, the most secret of all.'

children.text: iṣṭo 'si me dṛḍham iti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam //
children.translated_text: 'You are firmly beloved to Me — therefore I shall speak what is for your benefit.' ||

children.text: sarva-guhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ /
iṣṭo 'si me dṛḍham iti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam //

body.text: sarveṣv eteṣu guhyeṣu bhaktiyogasya śraiṣṭhyād guhyatamam iti pūrvam evoktam "idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmy anasūyave" ityādau / bhūyo 'pi tadviṣayaṃ paramaṃ me vacaḥ śṛṇu / iṣṭo 'si me dṛḍham iti tatas te hitaṃ vakṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: Among all these secrets, since <s>bhaktiyoga</s> is supreme, it was already called 'the most secret' — stated earlier in 'I shall declare to you, who are without envy, this most secret [teaching]' and so on. Hear again My supreme word concerning that very subject. You are firmly beloved to Me — therefore I shall speak to you what is for your benefit. //

children.text: sarveṣv eteṣu guhyeṣu bhakti-yogasya śraiṣṭhyād guhyatamam iti pūrvam eva uktam "idaṃ tu te guhyatamaṃ pravakṣyāmy anasūyave" ity-ādau / bhūyo 'pi tad-viṣayaṃ paramaṃ me vacaḥ śṛṇu / iṣṭo 'si me dṛḍham iti tatas te hitaṃ vakṣyāmi //
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru /
children.translated_text: 'Be minded on Me, be devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, bow to Me.'

children.text: mām evaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo 'si me //
children.translated_text: 'You shall come to Me alone — truly I promise you, for you are dear to Me.' ||

children.text: man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṃ namaskuru /
mām eva eṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo 'si me //

body.text:
vedānteṣu, "vedāham etaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntam ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt / tam evaṃ vidvān amṛta iha bhavati nānyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya" ityādiṣu vihitaṃ vedanaṃ dhyānopāsanādiśabdavācyaṃ darśanasamānākāraṃ smṛtisaṃtānam atyarthapriyam iha manmanā bhaveti vidhīyate / madbhaktaḥ atyarthamatpriyaḥ / atyarthamatpriyatvena niratiśayapriyāṃ smṛtisaṃtatiṃ kuruṣvetyarthaḥ / madyājī / tatrāpi madbhakta ity anuṣajyate / yajanaṃ pūjanam / atyarthapriyamadārādhanaparo bhava / ārādhanaṃ hi paripūrṇaśeṣavṛttiḥ / māṃ namaskuru / namaḥ -- namanam / mayy atimātraprahvībhāvam atyarthapriyaṃ kurv ityarthaḥ / evaṃ vartamāno mām evaiṣyasi / etat satyaṃ te pratijāne -- tava pratijñāṃ karomi; nopacchandanamātram; yatas tvaṃ priyo 'si me / "priyo
hi jñānino 'tyartham ahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ" iti pūrvam evoktam / yasya mayy atimātratā prītir vartate, mamāpi tasmin atimātrā prītir bhavatīti tadviyogam asahamāno 'haṃ taṃ māṃ prāpayāmi / ataḥ satyam eva pratijñātam, mām evaiṣyasīti //
body.translated_text: The knowing (<s>vedana</s>) prescribed in <s>Vedānta</s> [texts] such as 'I know this great Person, sun-colored, beyond darkness; knowing Him thus, one becomes immortal here — there is no other path to go' and the like, which is expressed by the words 'meditation,' 'worship,' and the like, which is of the same form as direct vision, which is a continuous stream of remembrance (<s>smṛti</s>) that is exceedingly dear — that is prescribed here as 'be minded on Me.' 'Be devoted to Me' — be one for whom I am exceedingly dear. The meaning is: by virtue of your exceedingly great love for Me, maintain a continuous stream of remembrance that is supremely dear. 'Sacrifice to Me' — here too 'devoted to Me' carries over. Sacrifice (<s>yajana</s>) is worship. Be devoted to My worship, which is exceedingly dear. For worship is the complete expression of the relation of dependence (<s>śeṣavṛtti</s>). 'Bow to Me' — <s>namaḥ</s> means bowing (<s>namana</s>). Make your exceedingly dear prostration before Me, with excessive humility. Conducting yourself thus, you shall come to Me alone. This I truly promise you — I make a promise to you; it is not mere persuasion. Because you are dear to Me. As was said earlier: 'I am exceedingly dear to the <s>jñānī</s>, and he is dear to Me.' One who has exceedingly great love for Me — toward him too I have exceedingly great love; and being unable to bear separation from him, I cause him to attain Me. Therefore, what was promised — 'you shall come to Me alone' — is the truth indeed. //

children.text:
veda-anteṣu, "veda aham etaṃ puruṣaṃ mahā-antam āditya-varṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt / tam evaṃ vidvān amṛta iha bhavati na anyaḥ panthā vidyate 'yanāya" ity-ādiṣu vihitaṃ vedanaṃ dhyāna-upāsana-ādi-śabda-vācyaṃ darśana-samāna-ākāraṃ smṛti-saṃtānam atyartha-priyam iha man-manā bhava iti vidhīyate / mad-bhaktaḥ atyartha-mat-priyaḥ / atyartha-mat-priyatvena niratiśaya-priyāṃ smṛti-saṃtatiṃ kuruṣva ity-arthaḥ / mad-yājī / tatra api mad-bhakta ity anuṣajyate / yajanaṃ pūjanam / atyartha-priya-mad-ārādhana-paro bhava / ārādhanaṃ hi paripūrṇa-śeṣa-vṛttiḥ / māṃ namaskuru / namaḥ --- namanam / mayy atimātra-prahvībhāvam atyartha-priyaṃ kurv ity-arthaḥ / evaṃ vartamāno mām eva eṣyasi / etat satyaṃ te pratijāne --- tava pratijñāṃ karomi; na upacchandana-mātram; yatas tvaṃ priyo 'si me / "priyo
hi jñānino 'tyartham ahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ" iti pūrvam eva uktam / yasya mayy atimātratā prītir vartate, mama api tasmin atimātrā prītir bhavati iti tad-viyogam asahamāno 'haṃ taṃ māṃ prāpayāmi / ataḥ satyam eva pratijñātam, mām eva eṣyasi iti //
sarvadharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja /
children.translated_text: 'Abandoning all <s>dharmas</s>, take refuge in Me alone.'

children.text: ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'I shall liberate you from all sins — do not grieve.' //

children.text: sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja /
ahaṃ tvā sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ //

body.text:
karmayogajñānayogabhaktiyogarūpān sarvān dharmān paramaniśśreyasasādhanabhūtān, madārādhanatvena atimātraprītyā yathādhikāraṃ kurvāṇa eva, uktarītyā phalakarmakartṛtvādiparityāgena parityajya, mām ekam eva kartāram ārādhyaṃ prāpyam upāyaṃ cānusaṃdhatsva / eṣa eva sarvadharmāṇāṃ śastrīyaḥ parityāga iti, "niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharatasattama / tyāgo hi puruṣavyāghra trividhaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ // BhGR_18." ityārabhya, "saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ caiva sa tyāgas sāttiviko mataḥ // ... na hi dehabhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇy aśeṣataḥ / yas tu karmaphalatyāgī sa tyāgīty abhidhīyate // BhGR_18." iti adhyāyādau sudṛḍham upapāditam / ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi -- evaṃ vartamānaṃ tvām matprāptivirodhibhyo
'nādikālasaṃcitānantākṛtyakaraṇakṛtyākaraṇarūpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi / mā śucaḥ -- śokaṃ mā kṛthāḥ / atha vā, sarvapāpavinirmuktātyarthabhagavatpriyapuruṣanirvartyatvād bhaktiyogasya, tadārambhavirodhipāpānām ānantyāt tatprāyaścittarūpair dharmaiḥ parimitakālakṛtais teṣāṃ dustaratayā ātmano bhaktiyogārambhānarhatām ālocya śocato 'rjunasya śokam apanudan śrībhagavān uvāca -- sarvadharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajeti / bhaktiyogārambhavirodhyanādikālasaṃcitanānāvidhānantapāpānuguṇān tattatprāyaścittarūpān kṛcchracāndrāyaṇakūśmāṇḍavaiśvānaravrātapatipavitreṣṭitrivṛdagniṣṭomādikān nānāvidhān anantāṃs tvayā parimitakālavartinā dūranuṣṭhānān sarvān
dharmān parityajya bhaktiyogārambhasiddhaye mām ekaṃ paramakāruṇikam anālocitaviśeṣāśeṣalokaśaraṇyam āśritavātsalyajaladhiṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadyasva / ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyaḥ yathoditasvarūpabhaktyārambhavirodhibhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpebhyaḥ mokṣayiṣyāmi; mā śucaḥ //
body.translated_text: Abandoning all <s>dharmas</s> in the form of <s>karmayoga</s>, <s>jñānayoga</s>, and <s>bhaktiyoga</s> — which are the means to the supreme good — while continuing to perform them according to one's qualification with supreme love as worship of Me, relinquish [them] in the manner described — by giving up [attachment to] results, possessiveness regarding action, and agency — and contemplate Me alone as the agent, the object of worship, the goal to be attained, and the means. This alone is the scriptural relinquishment of all <s>dharmas</s>, as was firmly established at the beginning of the chapter, from 'Hear My definitive view on <s>tyāga</s>, O best of the <s>Bhāratas</s>; for <s>tyāga</s>, O tiger among men, is declared to be of three kinds' up to 'Having abandoned attachment and the fruit as well — that renunciation is considered <s>sāttvika</s>... For an embodied being cannot abandon actions entirely; but he who abandons the fruit of action — he is called a relinquisher.' 'I shall release you from all sins' — you who conduct yourself thus, I shall release from all sins — the innumerable [sins] accumulated since beginningless time, in the form of prohibited acts committed and obligatory acts omitted, which obstruct the attainment of Me. Do not grieve. Alternatively: since <s>bhaktiyoga</s> is to be accomplished only by one completely free of all sins, and since the sins obstructing its commencement are infinite, and since the expiatory <s>dharmas</s> proportionate to those sins, being performed in a limited time, cannot overcome them due to their being insurmountable, <s>Arjuna</s>, reflecting on his own unworthiness to commence <s>bhaktiyoga</s>, was grieving. Dispelling his grief, the Lord said: 'Abandon all <s>dharmas</s> and take refuge in Me alone' — abandoning all the manifold, innumerable expiatory rites proportionate to the diverse, infinite sins accumulated since beginningless time that obstruct the commencement of <s>bhaktiyoga</s> — such as <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, <s>kūśmāṇḍa</s>, <s>vaiśvānara</s>, <s>vrātapati</s>, <s>pavitresti</s>, <s>trivṛt</s>, <s>agniṣṭoma</s>, and the like — all of which are impossible for you to perform being limited in time, for the success of commencing <s>bhaktiyoga</s>, take refuge in Me alone — the supremely compassionate one, the refuge of all the world without distinction, an ocean of affection toward those who have taken refuge. 'I shall release you from all sins' — from all sins that obstruct the commencement of devotion in its proper form as described. Do not grieve. //

children.text:
karma-yoga-jñāna-yoga-bhakti-yoga-rūpān sarvān dharmān parama-niśśreyasa-sādhana-bhūtān, mad-ārādhanatvena atimātra-prītyā yathā-adhikāraṃ kurvāṇa eva, ukta-rītyā phala-karma-kartṛtva-ādi-parityāgena parityajya, mām ekam eva kartāram ārādhyaṃ prāpyam upāyaṃ ca anusaṃdhatsva / eṣa eva sarva-dharmāṇāṃ śastrīyaḥ parityāga iti, "niścayaṃ śṛṇu me tatra tyāge bharata-sattama / tyāgo hi puruṣa-vyāghra tri-vidhaḥ saṃprakīrtitaḥ // BhGR_18." ity-ārabhya, "saṅgaṃ tyaktvā phalaṃ ca eva sa tyāgas sāttiviko mataḥ // ... na hi deha-bhṛtā śakyaṃ tyaktuṃ karmāṇy aśeṣataḥ / yas tu karma-phala-tyāgī sa tyāgi īty abhidhīyate // BhGR_18." iti adhyāya-ādau sudṛḍham upapāditam / ahaṃ tvā sarva-pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi --- evaṃ vartamānaṃ tvām mat-prāpti-virodhibhyo
'nādi-kāla-saṃcita-ananta-akṛtya-karaṇa-kṛtya-akaraṇa-rūpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi / mā śucaḥ --- śokaṃ mā kṛthāḥ / atha vā, sarva-pāpa-vinirmukta-atyartha-bhagavat-priya-puruṣa-nirvartyatvād bhakti-yogasya, tad-ārambha-virodhi-pāpānām ānantyāt tat-prāyaścitta-rūpair dharmaiḥ parimita-kāla-kṛtais teṣāṃ dustaratayā ātmano bhakti-yoga-ārambha-anarhatām ālocya śocato 'rjunasya śokam apanudan śrī-bhagavān uvāca --- sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja iti / bhakti-yoga-ārambha-virodhy-anādi-kāla-saṃcita-nānā-vidha-ananta-pāpa-anuguṇān tat-tat-prāyaścitta-rūpān kṛcchra-cāndrāyaṇa-kūśmāṇḍa-vaiśvānara-vrāta-pati-pavitra-iṣṭi-tri-vṛd-agniṣṭoma-ādikān nānā-vidhān anantāṃs tvayā parimita-kāla-vartinā dūranuṣṭhānān sarvān
dharmān parityajya bhakti-yoga-ārambha-siddhaye mām ekaṃ parama-kāruṇikam anālocita-viśeṣa-aśeṣa-loka-śaraṇyam āśrita-vātsalya-jala-dhiṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadyasva / ahaṃ tvā sarva-pāpebhyaḥ yathā-udita-sva-rūpa-bhakty-ārambha-virodhibhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpebhyaḥ mokṣayiṣyāmi; mā śucaḥ //
idaṃ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācana /
children.translated_text: 'This is not to be told to one who is without austerity, nor to one who is without devotion, ever,' |

children.text: na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo 'bhyasūyati //
children.translated_text: 'nor to one who does not wish to hear, nor to one who speaks ill of Me.' ||

children.text: idaṃ te na atapaskāya na abhaktāya kadācana /
na ca aśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo 'bhyasūyati //

body.text: idaṃ te paramaṃ guhyaṃ śāstraṃ mayākhyātam atapaskāya ataptatapase tvayā na vācyam; tvayi vaktari, mayi cābhaktāya kadācana na vācyam / taptatapase cābhaktāya na vācyam ityarthaḥ / na cāśuśrūṣave / bhaktāyāpy aśuśrūṣave na vācyam / na ca māṃ yo 'bhyasūyati / matsvarūpe madaiśvarye madguṇeṣu ca kathiteṣu yo doṣam āviṣkaroti, na tasmai vācyam / asamānavibhaktinirdeśaḥ tasyātyantapariharaṇīyatājñāpanāya //
body.translated_text: This supreme secret teaching, told to you by Me, is not to be told by you to one who has not performed austerity — to one who has not undergone austerities. When you are the speaker, [it is] never to be told to one who is without devotion to Me. Even to one who has performed austerity but is without devotion, it is not to be told — this is the meaning. 'Nor to one who does not wish to hear' — even to a devotee who does not wish to hear, it is not to be told. 'Nor to one who speaks ill of Me' — whoever finds fault when My essential nature, My sovereignty, and My qualities are described — to him it is not to be told. The use of a different case-ending [in the last phrase] is to indicate that such a person is to be most thoroughly avoided. //

children.text: idaṃ te paramaṃ guhyaṃ śāstraṃ mayā ākhyātam atapaskāya atapta-tapase tvayā na vācyam; tvayi vaktari, mayi ca abhaktāya kadācana na vācyam / tapta-tapase ca abhaktāya na vācyam ity-arthaḥ / na ca aśuśrūṣave / bhaktāya apy aśuśrūṣave na vācyam / na ca māṃ yo 'bhyasūyati / mat-sva-rūpe mad-aiśvarye mad-guṇeṣu ca kathiteṣu yo doṣam āviṣkaroti, na tasmai vācyam / asamāna-vibhakti-nirdeśaḥ tasya atyanta-pariharaṇīyatā-jñāpanāya //
ya idaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣv abhidhāsyati /
children.translated_text: 'He who will expound this supreme secret to My devotees,' |

children.text: bhaktiṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā mām evaiṣyaty asaṃśayaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'having offered supreme devotion to Me, shall come to Me alone, without doubt.' ||

children.text: ya idaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ mad-bhakteṣv abhidhāsyati /
bhaktiṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā mām eva eṣyaty asaṃśayaḥ //

body.text: idaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣu yaḥ abhidhāsyati vyākhyāsyati, saḥ mayi paramāṃ bhaktiṃ kṛtvā mām evaiṣyati; na tatra saṃśayaḥ //
body.translated_text: He who will expound — will teach — this supreme secret to My devotees, he, having offered supreme devotion to Me, shall come to Me alone; there is no doubt about this. //

children.text: idaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ mad-bhakteṣu yaḥ abhidhāsyati vyākhyāsyati, saḥ mayi paramāṃ bhaktiṃ kṛtvā mām eva eṣyati; na tatra saṃśayaḥ //
na ca tasmān manuṣyeṣu kaścin me priyakṛttamaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And no one among humans does Me a greater kindness than he.' |

children.text: bhavitā na ca me tasmād anyaḥ priyataro bhuvi //
children.translated_text: 'Nor shall there be another dearer to Me on earth than he.' ||

children.text: na ca tasmān manuṣyeṣu kaścin me priya-kṛt-tamaḥ /
bhavitā na ca me tasmād anyaḥ priyataro bhuvi //

body.text: sarveṣu manuṣyeṣv itaḥ pūrvaṃ tasmād anyo manuṣyo me na kaścit priyakṛttamo 'bhūt; ita uttaraṃ ca na bhavitā / ayogyānāṃ prathamam upādānaṃ yogyānām akathanād api tatkathanasyāniṣṭatamatvāt //
body.translated_text: Among all human beings, before this time, no other human has done Me a greater kindness than he; nor shall there be [such a one] hereafter. [This is so because] the initial mention of the unworthy [as those to whom the teaching should not be given] implies that not teaching it even to the worthy is most displeasing [to the Lord]. //

children.text: sarveṣu manuṣyeṣv itaḥ pūrvaṃ tasmād anyo manuṣyo me na kaścit priya-kṛt-tamo 'bhūt; ita uttaraṃ ca na bhavitā / ayogyānāṃ prathamam upādānaṃ yogyānām akathanād api tat-kathanasya aniṣṭa-tamatvāt //
adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādam āvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And he who will study this righteous dialogue of ours,' |

children.text: jñānayajñena tenāham iṣṭaḥ syām iti me matiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'by him I would be worshipped through a sacrifice of knowledge — such is My view.' ||

children.text: adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādam āvayoḥ /
jñāna-yajñena tena aham iṣṭaḥ syām iti me matiḥ //

body.text: ya imam āvayor dharmyaṃ saṃvādam adhyeṣyate, tena jñānayajñenāham iṣṭas syām iti me matiḥ -- asmin yo jñānayajño 'bhidhīyate, tenāham etad adhyayanamātreṇeṣṭaḥ syām ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: He who will study this righteous dialogue of ours — by that sacrifice of knowledge I would be worshipped — such is My view. The meaning is: by the sacrifice of knowledge described herein, I would be worshipped through the mere study of this alone. //

children.text: ya imam āvayor dharmyaṃ saṃvādam adhyeṣyate, tena jñāna-yajñena aham iṣṭas syām iti me matiḥ --- asmin yo jñāna-yajño 'bhidhīyate, tena aham etad adhyayana-mātreṇa iṣṭaḥ syām ity-arthaḥ //
śraddhāvān anasūyuś ca śṛṇuyād api yo naraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And the man who, full of faith and free from envy, would even hear [this],' |

children.text: so 'pi muktaḥ śubhāṃl lokān prāpnuyāt puṇyakarmaṇām //
children.translated_text: 'he too, liberated, would attain the auspicious worlds of those of meritorious deeds.' ||

children.text: śraddhāvān anasūyuś ca śṛṇuyād api yo naraḥ /
so 'pi muktaḥ śubhāṃl lokān prāpnuyāt puṇya-karmaṇām //

body.text: śraddhāvān anasūyuś ca yo naraḥ śṛṇuyād api, tena śravaṇamātreṇa so 'pi bhaktivirodhipāpebhyo muktaḥ puṇyakarmaṇāṃ madbhaktānāṃ lokān samūhan prāpnuyāt //
body.translated_text: Even the man who, full of faith and free from envy, would merely hear [this] — by that mere hearing, he too, liberated from the sins that obstruct devotion, would attain the worlds — the communities — of those of meritorious deeds, My devotees. //

children.text: śraddhāvān anasūyuś ca yo naraḥ śṛṇuyād api, tena śravaṇa-mātreṇa so 'pi bhakti-virodhi-pāpebhyo muktaḥ puṇya-karmaṇāṃ mad-bhaktānāṃ lokān samūhan prāpnuyāt //
kaścid etacchrutaṃ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā /
children.translated_text: 'Has this been heard by you, O <s>Pārtha</s>, with single-pointed mind?' |

children.text: kaccid ajñānasaṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭas te dhanañjaya //
children.translated_text: 'Has the delusion born of ignorance been destroyed for you, O <s>Dhanañjaya</s>?' ||

children.text: kaścid etac-chrutaṃ pārtha tvaya aika-agreṇa cetasā /
kaccid ajñāna-saṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭas te dhanañjaya //

body.text: mayā kathitam etat pārtha tvayā avahitena cetasā kaccic śrutam, tavājñānasaṃmohaḥ kaccit pranaṣṭaḥ, yenājñānena mūḍho na yotsyāmītyuktavān //
body.translated_text: Has this that was spoken by Me been heard by you, O <s>Pārtha</s>, with attentive mind? Has the delusion born of your ignorance been destroyed — the ignorance deluded by which you had said 'I shall not fight'? //

children.text: mayā kathitam etat pārtha tvayā avahitena cetasā kaccic śrutam, tava ajñāna-saṃmohaḥ kaccit pranaṣṭaḥ, yena ajñānena mūḍho na yotsyāmi ity-uktavān //
naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtir labdhā tvatprasādān mayācyuta /
children.translated_text: 'Delusion is destroyed, and recollection has been gained, by Your grace, O <s>Acyuta</s>.' |

children.text: sthito 'smi gatasaṃdehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava //
children.translated_text: 'I stand firm, free from doubt. I shall carry out Your word.' ||

children.text: naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtir labdhā tvat-prasādān maya ācyuta /
sthito 'smi gata-saṃdehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava //

body.text:
mohaḥ viparītajñānam / tvatprasādān mama tad vinaṣṭam / smṛtiḥ yathāvasthitatattvajñānam / tvatprasādād eva tac ca labdham / anātmani prakṛtau ātmābhimānarūpo mohaḥ, paramapuruṣaśarīratayā tadātmakasya kṛtsnasya cidacidvastunaḥ atadātmābhimānarūpaś ca, nityanaimittikarūpasya karmaṇaḥ paramapuruṣārādhanatayā tatprāptyupāyabhūtasya bandhakatvabuddhirūpaś ca sarvo vinaṣṭaḥ / ātmanaḥ prakṛtivilakṣaṇatvatatsvabhāvarahitatājñātṛtvaikasvabhāvatāparamapuruṣaśeṣatātanniyāmyatvaikasvarūpatājñānam,
nikhilajagadudbhavasthitipralayalīlāśeṣadoṣapratyanīkakalyāṇaikasvarūpasvābhāvikānavadhikātiśayajñānabalāiśvaryavīryaśaktitejaḥprabhṛtisamastakalyāṇaguṇagaṇamahārṇavaparabrahmaśabdābhidheyaparamapuruṣayāthātmyajñānaṃ ca, evaṃrūpaparāvaratattvayāthātmyavijñānatadabhyāsapūrvakāharaharupacīyamānaparamapuruṣaprītyekaphalanityanaimittikakarmaniṣiddhaparihāraśamadamādyātmaguṇanivartyabhaktirūpatāpannaparamapuruṣopāsanaikalabhyo vedāntavedyaḥ paramapuruṣo vāsudevas tvam iti jñānaṃ ca labdham / tataś ca bandhasnehakāruṇyapravṛddhaviparītajñānamūlāt sarvasmād avasādād vimukto gatasaṃdehaḥ svasthaḥ sthito 'smi / idānīm eva yuddhādikartavyatāviṣayam tava vacanaṃ kariṣyati -- yathoktaṃ
yuddhādikaṃ kariṣyati ityarthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Delusion means wrong knowledge. By Your grace, that has been destroyed for me. Recollection (<s>smṛti</s>) means knowledge of reality as it truly is. By Your grace alone, that too has been gained. The delusion that is the false identification of the self with <s>Prakṛti</s>, which is not the self; the [delusion] that is the false identification of the entire conscious and non-conscious reality — which has the Supreme Person as its self by virtue of being His body — as not having Him as its self; and the [delusion] that is the notion of bondage regarding obligatory and occasional action, which is the means of attaining the Supreme Person by being worship of Him — all this has been destroyed. The knowledge of the self as different from <s>Prakṛti</s>, devoid of its characteristics, having the sole nature of being a knower, having the sole essential nature of being a subordinate (<s>śeṣa</s>) of the Supreme Person and being governed by Him; and the knowledge of the true nature of the Supreme Person — who is denoted by the word <s>parabrahman</s>, an immense ocean of all auspicious qualities such as knowledge, strength, sovereignty, power, might, splendor, and the like, all natural and immeasurably surpassing, whose sole essential nature is auspiciousness that is opposed to all that is defective, whose sport is the origination, sustenance, and dissolution of the entire universe — [the knowledge] that He, the Supreme Person <s>Vāsudeva</s>, is You, attainable solely through the worship of the Supreme Person reached through the practice of knowledge of the true nature of the higher and lower realities of such a nature, preceded by the performance of obligatory and occasional duties with ever-increasing love for the Supreme Person as their sole fruit, accompanied by the abandonment of prohibited acts and the cultivation of qualities of the self such as tranquility, self-control, and the like, taking the form of devotion — this knowledge too has been gained. And therefore, freed from all despondency rooted in the wrong knowledge swelled by affection and compassion arising from familial bonds, free from doubt, self-possessed, I stand firm. I shall carry out Your word regarding the duty of fighting and the like — meaning he will perform battle and the like as instructed. //

children.text:
mohaḥ viparīta-jñānam / tvat-prasādān mama tad vinaṣṭam / smṛtiḥ yathā-avasthita-tattva-jñānam / tvat-prasādād eva tac ca labdham / anātmani prakṛtau ātma-abhimāna-rūpo mohaḥ, parama-puruṣa-śarīratayā tad-ātmakasya kṛtsnasya cid-acid-vastunaḥ atad-ātma-abhimāna-rūpaś ca, nitya-naimittika-rūpasya karmaṇaḥ parama-puruṣa-ārādhanatayā tat-prāpty-upāya-bhūtasya bandhakatva-buddhi-rūpaś ca sarvo vinaṣṭaḥ / ātmanaḥ prakṛti-vilakṣaṇatva-tat-sva-bhāva-rahitatā-jñātṛtva-eka-sva-bhāvatā-parama-puruṣa-śeṣatā-tan-niyāmyatva-eka-sva-rūpatā-jñānam,
nikhila-jagad-udbhava-sthiti-pralaya-līla-aśeṣa-doṣa-pratyanīka-kalyāṇa-eka-sva-rūpa-svābhāvika-anavadhika-atiśaya-jñāna-bala-aiśvarya-vīrya-śakti-tejaḥ-prabhṛti-samasta-kalyāṇa-guṇa-gaṇa-mahā-arṇava-para-brahma-śabda-abhidheya-parama-puruṣa-yāthātmya-jñānaṃ ca, evaṃ-rūpa-para-avara-tattva-yāthātmya-vijñāna-tad-abhyāsa-pūrvaka-ahar-ahar-upacīyamāna-parama-puruṣa-prīty-eka-phala-nitya-naimittika-karma-niṣiddha-parihāra-śama-dama-ādy-ātma-guṇa-nivartya-bhakti-rūpatā-āpanna-parama-puruṣa-upāsana-eka-labhyo veda-anta-vedyaḥ parama-puruṣo vāsudevas tvam iti jñānaṃ ca labdham / tataś ca bandha-sneha-kāruṇya-pravṛddha-viparīta-jñāna-mūlāt sarvasmād avasādād vimukto gata-saṃdehaḥ sva-sthaḥ sthito 'smi / idānīm eva yuddha-ādi-kartavyatā-viṣayam tava vacanaṃ kariṣyati --- yathā-uktaṃ
yuddha-ādikaṃ kariṣyati ity-arthaḥ //

body.text: dhṛtarāṣṭrāya svaputrāḥ pāṇḍavāś ca yuddhe kiṃ kariṣyantīti pṛcchate
body.translated_text: To <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, who asked what his sons and the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> would do in battle,

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭrāya sva-putrāḥ pāṇḍavāś ca yuddhe kiṃ kariṣyanti iti pṛcchate
ity ahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Thus I have heard this dialogue of <s>Vāsudeva</s> and of the great-souled <s>Pārtha</s>,' |

children.text: saṃvādam imam aśrauṣam adbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: 'wondrous and causing the hair to stand on end.' ||

children.text: ity ahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahā-ātmanaḥ /
saṃvādam imam aśrauṣam adbhutaṃ roma-harṣaṇam //

body.text: iti evaṃ vāsudevasya vasudevasūnoḥ, pārthasya ca tatpitṛṣvasuḥ putrasya ca mahātmanaḥ mahābuddhes tatpadadvandvam āśritasyemaṃ romaharṣaṇam adbhutaṃ saṃvādam ahaṃ yathoktam aśrauṣam śrutavān aham //
body.translated_text: 'Thus' — in this manner. Of <s>Vāsudeva</s> — the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>; and of the great-souled <s>Pārtha</s> — the son of his father's sister, of great intellect, who had taken refuge at His two feet — I have heard this wondrous dialogue that causes the hair to stand on end, as narrated. //

children.text: iti evaṃ vāsudevasya vasu-deva-sūnoḥ, pārthasya ca tat-pitṛ-ṣvasuḥ putrasya ca mahā-ātmanaḥ mahā-buddhes tat-pada-dvandvam āśritasya imaṃ roma-harṣaṇam adbhutaṃ saṃvādam ahaṃ yathā-uktam aśrauṣam śrutavān aham //
vyāsaprasādāc chrutavān etad guhyam ahaṃ param /
children.translated_text: 'By the grace of <s>Vyāsa</s>, I have heard this supreme secret,' |

children.text: yogaṃ yogeśvarāt kṛṣṇāt sākṣāt kathayataḥ svayam //
children.translated_text: 'this <s>yoga</s>, from the Lord of <s>Yoga</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself, as He directly spoke it.' ||

children.text: vyāsa-prasādāc chrutavān etad guhyam ahaṃ param /
yogaṃ yoga-īśvarāt kṛṣṇāt sākṣāt kathayataḥ svayam //

body.text: vyāsaprasādād vyāsānugraheṇa divyacakṣuśśrotralābhād etat paraṃ yogākhyaṃ guhyaṃ yogeśvarāj jñānabalāiśvaryavīryaśaktitejasāṃ nidher bhagavataḥ kṛṣṇāt svayam eva kathayataḥ sākṣāc śrutavān aham //
body.translated_text: By the grace of <s>Vyāsa</s> — through <s>Vyāsa</s>'s favor, by obtaining divine sight and hearing — I have directly heard this supreme secret called <s>yoga</s>, from the Lord of <s>Yoga</s> — the treasure-house of knowledge, strength, sovereignty, power, might, and splendor — from the Lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself, as He was directly speaking it. //

children.text: vyāsa-prasādād vyāsa-anugraheṇa divya-cakṣuś-śrotra-lābhād etat paraṃ yoga-ākhyaṃ guhyaṃ yoga-īśvarāj jñāna-bala-aiśvarya-vīrya-śakti-tejasāṃ nidher bhagavataḥ kṛṣṇāt svayam eva kathayataḥ sākṣāc śrutavān aham //
rājan saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādam imam adbhutam /
children.translated_text: 'O King, remembering again and again this wondrous,' |

children.text: keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca muhur muhuḥ //
children.translated_text: 'holy dialogue of <s>Keśava</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, I rejoice again and again.' ||

children.text: rājan saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādam imam adbhutam /
keśava-arjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca muhur muhuḥ //

body.text: keśavārjunayor imaṃ puṇyam adbhutaṃ saṃvādaṃ sākṣāc chrutaṃ smṛtvā muhur muhur hṛṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: Remembering this holy, wondrous dialogue of <s>Keśava</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, directly heard, I rejoice again and again. //

children.text: keśava-arjunayor imaṃ puṇyam adbhutaṃ saṃvādaṃ sākṣāc chrutaṃ smṛtvā muhur muhur hṛṣyāmi //
tac ca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpam atyadbhutaṃ hareḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And remembering again and again that supremely wondrous form of <s>Hari</s>,' |

children.text: vismayo me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'great is my amazement, O King, and I rejoice again and again.' ||

children.text: tac ca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpam atyadbhutaṃ hareḥ /
vismayo me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ //

body.text: tac cārjunāya prakāśitam aiśvaraṃ harer atyadbhutaṃ rūpaṃ mayā sākṣātkṛtaṃ saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya hṛṣyato me mahān vismayo jāyate; punaḥ punaś ca hṛṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: And remembering again and again that supremely wondrous lordly form of <s>Hari</s>, which was revealed to <s>Arjuna</s> and directly perceived by me — great amazement arises in me as I rejoice; and I rejoice again and again. //

children.text: tac ca arjunāya prakāśitam aiśvaraṃ harer atyadbhutaṃ rūpaṃ mayā sākṣāt-kṛtaṃ saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya hṛṣyato me mahān vismayo jāyate; punaḥ punaś ca hṛṣyāmi //

body.text: kim atra bahunoktena ?
body.translated_text: What more need be said?

children.text: kim atra bahuna ūktena ?
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Lord of <s>Yoga</s>, is, and where <s>Pārtha</s>, the bearer of the bow, is,' |

children.text: tatra śrīr vijayo bhūtir dhruvā nītir matir mama //
children.translated_text: 'there are fortune, victory, prosperity, and unfailing righteousness — such is my conviction.' ||

children.text: yatra yoga-īśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanur-dharaḥ /
tatra śrīr vijayo bhūtir dhruvā nītir matir mama //

body.text: yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛtsnasyoccāvacarūpeṇāvasthitasya cetanasyācetanasya ca vastuno ye ye svabhāvayogāḥ, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ yogānām īśvaraḥ, svasaṃkalpāyattasvetarasamastavastusvarūpasthitipravṛttibhedaḥ, kṛṣṇaḥ vasudevasūnuḥ, yatra ca pārtho dhanurdharaḥ tatpitṛṣvasuḥ putraḥ tatpadadvandvaikāśrayaḥ, tatra śrīr vijayo bhūtir nītiś ca dhruvā niścalā iti matir mameti //
body.translated_text: Where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Lord of <s>Yoga</s> — the lord of all the <s>yogas</s> (attributes and powers) belonging to every conscious and non-conscious entity subsisting in all higher and lower forms, whose will alone determines the differences in the essential nature, existence, and activity of all other entities — the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>, is present; and where <s>Pārtha</s> the bearer of the bow — the son of his father's sister, whose sole refuge is His two feet — is present; there are fortune, victory, prosperity, and unfailing, unshakeable righteousness — such is my conviction. //

children.text: yatra yoga-īśvaraḥ kṛtsnasya ucca-avaca-rūpeṇa avasthitasya cetanasya acetanasya ca vastuno ye ye sva-bhāva-yogāḥ, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ yogānām īśvaraḥ, sva-saṃkalpa-āyatta-sva-itara-samasta-vastu-sva-rūpa-sthiti-pravṛtti-bhedaḥ, kṛṣṇaḥ vasu-deva-sūnuḥ, yatra ca pārtho dhanur-dharaḥ tat-pitṛ-ṣvasuḥ putraḥ tat-pada-dvandva-eka-āśrayaḥ, tatra śrīr vijayo bhūtir nītiś ca dhruvā niścalā iti matir mama iti //
